existing_evals.name: Stock-to-Flow / S2FX Scarcity Power-Law
issues: Minor coefficient ambiguity: the description gives the ORIGINAL S2F fit (ln(MV)=3.3·ln(SF)+14.6) but then attaches '~10x market value per doubling' to it; under exponent 3.3, a doubling of SF gives 2^3.3 ≈ 9.8x, so '~10x' is right for S2F. But the S2FX cluster math actually uses a DIFFERENT exponent (~4.1167, intercept 12.7598 per PlanB), which gives 2^4.1 ≈ 17x per SF doubling. The digest blends the two regimes under one '~10x/halving' shorthand; the cited_outputs note (~78%/yr from 10x/halving) is therefore the S2F figure, not S2FX. Worth flagging the two fits have materially different slopes.

The '~78%/yr compounded' in cited_outputs is derived from 10x-per-4yr-halving (10^(1/4)-1 = 78%), which is correct arithmetic, but it should be labeled as the implied geometric rate BETWEEN halvings, not a smooth annual rate — S2F prices are step functions, so the realized path is lumpy, not a constant 78%.

The synthesized appreciation_nominal band (~12-18%/yr) sits at the HIGH end of the honest cross-approach central (~8-12% nominal). The justification ('monetary-debasement-plus-marginal-adoption') is reasonable, but given the approach's own primary flaw is being structurally too bullish, a ~12-18% synthesized output is arguably still importing residual S2F optimism. A tighter ~8-13% would be more consistent with the brutal-on-hype mandate and the realized 5y level of 17% (which is itself decaying).

Pro #5 (Morillon & Chacon 'dynamic out-of-sample accuracy improves over time') is stated correctly but is easy to misread as vindication; the SAME paper shows the S2F trading strategy underperforms buy-and-hold (already in cons #6). The pro should be hedged so the two paper findings aren't read as net-positive.

The cons correctly note S2F is silent on vol/correlations, but the synthesized corr_growth_eq band (+0.45 to +0.60) anchored on realized 5y 0.56 is defensible; no error, just worth noting it directly contradicts the model premise (already flagged in synth note — good).

existing_evals.medium_explanation: Stock-to-Flow values Bitcoin purely on monetary scarcity: it regresses log market value on the log stock-to-flow ratio (existing supply divided by annual new issuance), the same hardness metric used for gold and silver. PlanB's original fit (value proportional to SF^3.3, R squared about 0.95) and the cross-asset S2FX version (pooling BTC, gold and silver, treating halvings as discrete phase transitions, R squared about 0.997) both produce dated price targets, e.g. the $288k 2020-2024 cluster. Because issuance halves every four years, SF roughly doubles each halving, so the model mechanically projects roughly 10x (S2F) to 17x (S2FX) per step, implying ~78%/yr between halvings forever. For a 10-15yr CMA this is the model's fatal flaw: it is demand-blind, the regression is spurious (both series are non-stationary and fail cointegration), and it broke out-of-sample after 2021 (predicted ~$98k, BTC closed ~$57k). It also says nothing about volatility or correlations. Honest forward use discards the literal targets, imposes BTC's realized appreciation decay, and yields only a low-double-digit nominal anchor.

existing_evals.name: Metcalfe's Law Network-Value (NVM)

Peterson's own paper headlines a very high fit, but independent replications report 'over 70% of variance explained' and adjusted R^2 ~0.83 (QuantPedia replication). The 0.93-0.95 figure is at the optimistic end of Peterson's self-reported numbers and is not robustly reproduced; it should be hedged.

Civitarese citation slightly mis-dated/mis-attributed in tone. The Civitarese paper ('Does Metcalfe's Law Explain Bitcoin Prices? A Time Series Analysis', SSRN 3107895) is dated Jan 2018, not 2018-as-a-rounded-publication; the entry's substantive claims (no cointegration; cannot reject reverse causality price->wallets) are accurate, but it is a working paper, not a top-tier peer-reviewed journal article, which is worth noting given source_type='academia'.

The headline practitioner forecast arithmetic should be made explicit. $1.5M by 2035 off a ~$100k 2025 base is ~31%/yr (15x over 10yr = 1.31^10 ~ 15.2x), which checks out, but the entry states '~31%/yr implied' without showing it ties to ~15x; minor, but the base/horizon assumption (2025 ~$100k) is load-bearing and should be stated.

source_type='academia' is defensible (Peterson, Civitarese, Wheatley-Sornette are academic-style papers; Wheatley-Sornette is genuinely peer-reviewed in Royal Society Open Science) BUT the actual 10-15yr CMA number (~31%) comes from Peterson's PRACTITIONER/media forecast, not a peer-reviewed point estimate. The mixed provenance (peer-reviewed relative-value tools vs. marketing-grade level forecast) is acknowledged but could be flagged more sharply in cited_outputs.

Odlyzko n*log(n) is listed as a driver/alternative but no source treats it as a fitted BTC model in this literature; it is a generic Metcalfe critique. Minor: it is presented alongside fitted exponents (n^2, ~1.7) as if comparably operationalized for BTC, which slightly overstates its role.

corr_gold synthesized at ~0.0-0.10 is well-reasoned, but the entry could note that the realized 5y BTC-gold corr in the anchor (+0.04) and the 'drifting modestly positive as both trade as debasement hedges' narrative are in mild tension; the model itself provides zero gold mechanism, so the floor-of-band placement is correct and this is a strength, not an error.

existing_evals.medium_explanation: Metcalfe's Law values Bitcoin as a network: worth scales with a power of active users (classic n-squared; Odlyzko's n*log(n); or an empirically fitted ~1.7). Peterson's version pairs a user-growth curve with a Gompertz supply schedule, dividing forecast network value by coins outstanding to get price; it fits past data well in-sample (self-reported R-squared in the 0.9s, ~0.83 on replication). To build a 10-15yr CMA you project a saturating adoption S-curve, apply the exponent, and annualize — which mechanically produces DECAYING returns as user growth and value-per-user both compress. That decay shape is the framework's main virtue. But the econometrics are weak: Civitarese finds price and wallets do not cointegrate and cannot reject reverse causality (price drives wallet creation); Wheatley-Sornette show n-squared fits far worse than ~1.69 and use the model only to flag bubbles, calling long-run forecasts 'meaningless.' Post-2024 ETF/custodial adoption adds users with zero new on-chain addresses, breaking the sole regressor. Peterson's headline $1.5M/2035 (~31%/yr) over-extrapolates a fragile fit; a defensible Metcalfe-consistent CMA is ~10-14% nominal, ~55-60% vol, ~0 gold correlation.

The digest references 'NVT Signal (NVTS) uses a 90-day MA' and even cites 'Kalichkin himself' in the cons, but the description presents NVT as anonymous folklore. Minor inconsistency: a named source belongs up front like S2F (PlanB) and Metcalfe (Peterson) get.

The '~3.3x' raw-overstates-economic-volume figure is attributed to 'Coin Metrics' but I could not source that exact multiple in the live search; Coin Metrics' documented contribution is the *adjusted* transfer-value series (TxTfrValAdjUSD) that strips change outputs/self-spends. The qualitative claim (raw on-chain volume materially overstates economic throughput, often cited 2-5x) is correct and well-established, but the precise '3.3x' should be sourced or softened to 'roughly 2-5x' to avoid a false-precision citation.

Redundancy risk with NVT Signal as a *timing* tool overlapping the broader 'on-chain mean-reversion ratio' family (NVT, MVRV, NVTS, Pi Cycle). The digest correctly distinguishes NVT (throughput-based 'P/E') from Metcalfe (user-count) and from MVRV (cost-basis), so it IS distinct on its denominator (settlement volume vs users vs realized cap). But the synthesized CMA outputs are nearly identical to the Metcalfe and NVT-adjacent rows (~10-13% nom, ~55-60% vol, same corr block) because all three honestly converge on the realized-decay anchor — that convergence is defensible, not an error, but the row adds little NEW quantitative signal beyond 'on-chain fundamentals are decaying/leaking.'

The cited 2025 contradiction ('overvalued ~58 in April pre-rally; undervalued near $120k in October') conflates plain NVT with the 'NVT Golden Cross' variant — the sourced PANews piece specifically describes the *NVT Golden Cross* reaching 58 in April. Worth tagging the variant precisely since NVT, NVTS, and NVT Golden Cross are three different constructs with different thresholds.

Synthesized appreciation (~10-13% nom / ~7-10% real) sits slightly ABOVE the honest cross-approach central (~8-12% nom / 5-9% real) given that NVT has NO scarcity or monetary-debasement tailwind — its sole driver (on-chain settlement value) is the one that is most clearly decaying AND leaking off-chain. A throughput-only model arguably justifies the LOW end of the band (~8-10%), not the middle. The con-list already makes this argument forcefully, so the number should follow it down.

Volatility floor logic is sound (~57% realized, no sub-realized compression yet evidenced) and consistent with the rest of the digest. existing_evals.medium_explanation: NVT treats Bitcoin like an equity P/E: market cap over daily on-chain settlement volume, the latter a proxy for the network's economic "throughput." Introduced by Willy Woo (2017) and smoothed into NVT Signal by Kalichkin (2018, 90-day MA), it is a relative-value/mean-reversion gauge — high NVT flags tops, low NVT bottoms — not a return model. So a 10-15yr CMA must be bolted on: assume the ratio mean-reverts to an equilibrium band and that real on-chain settlement value compounds at some rate, giving expected appreciation roughly equal to throughput growth plus any multiple drift. The denominator is the fatal weakness: raw volume overstates economic activity (change outputs, self-spends) while genuine activity increasingly leaks to Lightning/L2, exchange-internal ledgers, and ETF custody that never touches the chain. Because throughput is a maturing, decelerating, leaking series with no scarcity or debasement tailwind, the honest NVT-consistent CMA extrapolates BTC's appreciation decay to the LOW end — roughly 8-11% nominal, vol near realized ~55-60%, gold correlation ~0 (the framework implies none).

JPMorgan's production-cost estimate fell from ~$90k at the start of 2026 to ~$77k by mid-Feb-2026 as hashrate/difficulty dropped, with BTC trading ~$66k. The directional point (price below cost; cost following price DOWN) is exactly right and actually STRONGER than written, but the specific numbers should be refreshed.

Cited_outputs trajectory is partly stale: 'projected ~$180k post-2028 halving' is a reasonable mechanical doubling, but JPMorgan's headline long-run anchor is now its $266k volatility-adjusted gold-parity target (a different model) — worth not conflating the cost-floor trajectory with JPM's gold-parity number.

The $4,300/¢ electricity sensitivity is correct for the original model but JPMorgan later revised it down to ~$3,800/¢ after a CBECI methodology change; the entry states only the older $4,300 figure. Minor, but the 'doubled post-2024 halving' framing should note the base was also revised.

Synthesized appreciation (~6-9% nominal / 3-6% real) is the LOWEST of the supply-side approaches and sits at/below the bottom of the honest cross-approach central (~8-12% nom / 5-9% real). The logic (cost growth = 2 halvings doubling cost, minus efficiency clawback) is defensible, but the entry should flag that a strict cost-floor read mechanically understates appreciation because price has spent most of history ABOVE cost — so anchoring forward return to cost-growth alone embeds an assumption that the price-to-cost premium mean-reverts to ~1x, which history does not support.

Pros omit the one genuinely novel CMA-useful feature vs S2F/power-law: the difficulty-adjustment feedback gives an observable, real-time miner-capitulation SIGNAL (price < cash cost -> shutdowns -> difficulty falls), which is a legitimate tactical-floor read even if it fails as a structural return model. This is mentioned in pro #5 but under-weighted relative to how it distinguishes the approach.

Cons are strong but could add: the cost floor is also INCOME-statement circular because miners increasingly co-locate / pivot to AI-HPC, so the marginal miner's opportunity cost (and thus the 'floor') is now partly set by AI compute economics, not BTC fundamentals — the entry gestures at this (con #5) but it deserves to be named as a structural break specific to 2025-26.

existing_evals.medium_explanation: The cost-of-production approach (Hayes 2015/2019) treats Bitcoin as a 'virtual commodity' whose value is anchored to the marginal cost of mining a coin: daily energy cost (electricity price x ASIC efficiency x network hashrate) divided by coins mined per day. In a competitive mining market, miners produce until marginal cost equals price, so production cost is theorized as a soft floor the price 'gravitates' toward. It yields a current dollar level, not a return — so a 10-15yr CMA requires forecasting the floor's trajectory: each ~4-year halving mechanically doubles per-coin cost (the upward ratchet), while secular ASIC-efficiency gains and cheaper power claw most of it back. Net forward appreciation lands high-single-digit nominal, far below realized history, consistent with BTC's appreciation decay (142%->65%->17%/yr). The fatal flaw is circularity: issuance is price-inelastic, so when price falls miners exit, difficulty drops, and cost FOLLOWS price down — confirmed in 2026 when JPMorgan cut its cost estimate from ~$90k to ~$77k as price fell to ~$66k. Causality runs price->cost, breaking the floor logic. The model is silent on volatility and correlations, which must be imported from realized data.

existing_evals.name: Power-Law Time Regression (Santostasi / Burger Corridor)
issues: Citation precision: the digest asserts '8 of 11 Clauset-Shalizi-Newman tests REJECT the power law.' The primary source (arXiv 2605.21316) states the distributional power law is 'rejected on UTXO balances and daily |returns|, with lognormal preferred decisively' but the abstract/HTML does not publish an exact 8-of-11 count. The specific '8 of 11' may come from a table in the body but should not be stated as a settled headline number without page-level verification — flag as uncertain.

Exponent value: the digest uses n=5.6 throughout. The canonical Santostasi/Perrenod fit is more precisely beta=5.69 (+/-0.05), R^2=0.961 on daily data Jul-2010..Feb-2026. Using 5.6 vs 5.69 is fine for round-number CMA arithmetic but the canonical figure is 5.69; the cited_outputs price-path intercept (10^-1.8478, exponent 5.616) is one specific parameterization, not the only published one.

The 'alpha-hat 5.65 to 16.5' range in cons is presented as fact; the source says the exponent 'varies by nearly a factor of three across reasonable shifts of the time origin.' 5.65->16.5 is ~2.9x (consistent with 'factor of three'), so defensible, but the upper bound 16.5 should be tagged as the source's reported extreme, not a generic claim.

appreciation_real of ~18-21% (subtracting only ~3-3.5% inflation off a ~22-27% nominal) sits FAR above the honest cross-approach central of 5-9% real flagged in the task brief. The power-law nominal (~22-27%) is itself the most bullish in the digest. This is internally consistent with the model's own decay arithmetic, but the synthesized block does not flag strongly enough that this approach is a high-side outlier whose nominal rests entirely on the historical exponent persisting — which the same approach's own cons say may not survive the post-2021/ETF regime break. The tension between 'cons reject the exponent's stability' and 'synthesized still credits ~22-27%' deserves an explicit one-line reconciliation.

The synthesized vol/correlation cells (~55-60% vol, corr_growth +0.45..0.65, gold ~0-0.10) are imported from realized data and are sensible, but they are identical in spirit to every other approach's borrowed moments — correct, but worth noting these are NOT power-law outputs at all (the model is a price-level curve only), so the approach contributes a return view, not a risk/correlation view.

The current ~22-27% is the model-faithful number, not the blended-CMA number.", "Keep appreciation_real but flag it as the most optimistic in the digest and dependent entirely on the nominal extrapolation surviving."]
existing_evals.medium_explanation: The power-law time model regresses log BTC price on log age (days since the 2009 genesis), yielding P proportional to t^n with a canonical exponent n~=5.69 and R^2~=0.961 over 2010-2026. Because annualized appreciation under this form equals n divided by current age, the model FORECASTS its own decay: ~33%/yr at today's ~17-year age, easing to ~18%/yr by 2040, which compounds to roughly a 27% nominal CAGR over a 2026-2041 window read off the central line. Parallel corridor bands (about -50%/+200% around fair value) supply a dispersion view; the model says nothing about volatility-as-a-statistic or cross-asset correlations, which must be imported from realized data (~55-60% vol, gold corr ~0). The recent peer-reviewed treatment is double-edged: the power law fails Clauset-Shalizi-Newman tests (lognormal preferred) and its exponent swings ~3x with the time-origin choice, yet it still out-of-sample-beats ARIMA, ETS, and random-walk-with-drift at 12-24 months (p<0.05). For a 10-15yr CMA it is the most bullish entry, and its ~22-27% rests entirely on the historical exponent persisting through the ETF-era regime break.

The honest framing is 'rejected under the author-preferred m>=2 specification,' not unconditionally. The current wording slightly overstates the cleanliness of the rejection. Minor — the headline conclusion (coefficients are time-varying) stands.

BONUS corroboration the digest could cite: the Lee-Rhee VECM independently estimates a long-run BTC-GOLD coefficient of -0.0443 (significant at 1%, INVERSE) and a dollar-index coefficient of -0.676 (inverse, 10%). The negative BTC-gold long-run coefficient is a second, peer-reviewed data point REINFORCING the digest's load-bearing 'BTC-gold corr ~0, not the digital-gold co-movement the narrative implies' conclusion. existing_evals.medium_explanation: This approach values Bitcoin as a high-beta claim on fiat money growth rather than on cashflows. The empirical backbone is a cointegrating relationship between log BTC price and log broad money (US or 'global' M2): both are I(1), and a VECM estimates a long-run elasticity near 2.0-2.65 (Lee-Rhee 2022; Preprints.org 2025) with an error-correction term (~-0.12/month, ~5-6mo half-life) pulling price toward a money-implied fair value. A CMA follows mechanically: expected nominal appreciation = trend money growth x elasticity. The honest version DECAYS the elasticity from ~2 toward gold-like ~1.1-1.2 as BTC matures, yielding roughly 10-12% nominal / 7-9% real over 10-15yr - far below realized history, since the 2.0+ beta reflects one-time hyper-adoption. The caveats are decisive: the level relationship is largely shared-trend (spurious-regression risk; on changes it nearly vanishes), the elasticity is provably time-varying not constant, and the 2025-26 break - where liquidity rotated to gold (Z +2.82) away from BTC (Z -1.31) - shows the link is unstable. It says nothing direct about volatility or correlations.

existing_evals.name: Monetary-Substitution / M2 Elasticity & Debasement Hedge
issues: Citation precision: the digest attributes the time-varying-cointegration result to 'Park/Lee JDQS 2022' with 'p=0.0015'. The specific 'p=0.0015' figure could not be confirmed from the abstract and the author surnames were not verified. The con should be reworded to reflect the m=1-vs-m=2 structure and the exact p-value flagged as unverified.

The cons mention 'a non-peer-reviewed preprint' but the entry never names it; given the whole approach's headline numbers hinge on this one unreviewed paper, it should be cited explicitly so the reader can weight it.

existing_evals.medium_explanation: This approach values Bitcoin as a high-beta claim on fiat money growth rather than on cashflows. Empirically, log BTC price and log broad money (US M2 or a synthetic global M2) are each non-stationary I(1) and appear cointegrated, with an estimated long-run elasticity near 2.65 (a 1% rise in M2 maps to ~2.65% in BTC) and a VECM error-correction term of about -0.12/month pulling price back to a money-implied fair value over a ~6-month half-life. The CMA is built mechanically: forecast trend money growth (~7-8%/yr global), multiply by a forward elasticity that must be decayed from ~2.0 toward gold-like ~1.1-1.5, and that product is expected nominal appreciation; the debasement thesis supplies the structural tailwind and BTC's fixed 21M supply the differentiator. The catch is that the strong relationship lives almost entirely in shared trend — on first differences it nearly vanishes — and the coefficients are time-varying, not fixed. Honest forward read: ~10-12% nominal, ~7-9% real, vol ~55-60%, gold correlation ~0, since BTC trades as a liquidity/risk beta, not a true debasement hedge.

existing_evals.medium_explanation: This family values Bitcoin as a medium of exchange by inverting Fisher's identity MV=PT: the float's aggregate dollar value equals the annual real transaction volume it settles (T) divided by velocity (V), so price per coin = T/(V*M), with M the fixed ~21M supply. The applied strand (Burniske; Bank of England's John Lewis) plugs in an adoption scenario for T and a velocity, then discounts a future "utility value" back at a high 30-50% rate. Outputs span a vast fan -- Lewis gets ~$19k (illicit-only, V=5) to >$5M (world-currency, V=1) -- so velocity and the adoption scenario do all the work. The rigorous strand (Schilling-Uhlig 2019, JME) derives that a mature currency-Bitcoin's price is a MARTINGALE: expected risk-adjusted real return equals the dollar's, i.e. ~0 real drift, with volatility entirely from shifting adoption beliefs. For a 10-15yr CMA this is the most sobering lens: any positive appreciation is a one-time, decaying re-rating as adoption probability climbs, not perpetual growth -- implying ~6-10% nominal (center ~8%), ~3-7% real, ~57% belief-driven vol, and near-zero gold correlation (it rejects the digital-gold thesis outright).

existing_evals.medium_explanation: This family values Bitcoin off its aggregate on-chain cost basis rather than cashflow or scarcity. Realized Cap "price-stamps" every coin at the price it last moved and sums them, approximating the network's invested capital; Realized Price is the per-coin average. Market value is read relative to this base: MVRV (market cap / realized cap) and SOPR gauge aggregate unrealized/realized profit, Thermocap tracks cumulative miner security spend, and HODL Waves split cost basis by coin age. Crucially these are mean-reversion oscillators calibrated to cycle extremes (MVRV ~0.8 at bottoms, >3.2 at tops), not absolute valuation models, so no native long-horizon return exists. To force a 10-15yr CMA you project the growth of invested capital (net inflows, decelerating off a larger base) and assume MVRV reverts to ~1.5-2x. Because Realized Cap is a transform of past price, the much-touted "floor" is reflexive, not an independent fundamental. Extrapolating BTC's appreciation decay yields low-double-digit nominal returns; the framework is silent on volatility and every correlation, so those cells must be borrowed from realized data.

existing_evals.medium_explanation: This approach abandons valuation entirely and treats BTC as a risk asset, decomposing its returns by regressing them onto priced factors. Two strands: an asset-pricing strand (Liu-Tsyvinski-Wu, JF 2022) that builds crypto-native factors — a crypto market factor (CMKT), size (CSIZE), and momentum (CMOM) — and shows a three-factor model spans the cross-section of coin returns; and a macro-liquidity strand regressing BTC on global M2, the dollar, and real rates. Crucially it is descriptive, not predictive: it explains what moves BTC and how variance loads on each factor, but produces no native long-horizon level. A CMA only emerges by feeding in long-run factor-premium assumptions (an equity-risk-premium-style estimate for the crypto market factor) and letting the betas translate them — so the appreciation number is the analyst's prior, laundered through the regression. Its real strength is the risk side: it credibly documents BTC's rising post-ETF equity beta (~0.5-0.9) and near-zero, non-rising gold correlation, directly informing the correlation cells. For a 10-15yr CMA it implies ~9-12% nominal (high-beta risk asset, size-factor haircut, thinning adoption tailwind), vol ~55-60%, growth-equity corr ~0.55, gold corr ~0.10.

existing_evals.medium_explanation: This approach reads BTC's listed-options market rather than its price history. From the cross-section of strikes, Breeden-Litzenberger recovers a risk-neutral density of the terminal price; from the term structure (distilled into Deribit's 30-day DVOL index) you read the market's annualized volatility expectation. Its decisive limitation: under the risk-neutral (Q) measure the forward equals spot times cost-of-carry, so the drift is the financing rate, NOT a real-world expected return. The options surface therefore delivers a best-in-class volatility input and a no-arbitrage forward but is silent on 10-15yr appreciation. A return only emerges by grafting a pricing-kernel/P-density step onto it: Grith-Almeida-Miftachov (arXiv 2410.15195) recover an option-implied physical premium of ~66%/yr (Martin lower bound 65.6%, Chabi-Yo-Loudis 84.8%) — but only at a 27-day horizon on 2017-2022 data, a pre-ETF high-premium regime. For a CMA: trust it for vol (~55-60%, floored at realized ~57%); decay the stale short-dated premium hard for horizon and maturation to ~8-12% nominal / 5-9% real. It yields no cross-asset correlations.

existing_evals.name: Equilibrium / Game-Theoretic Security-Utility Pricing
issues: Citation date error: 'Chen 2024 security-utility Nash equilibrium' is actually Liang Chen, 'A Game-Theoretic Foundation for Bitcoin's Price: A Security-Utility Equilibrium,' arXiv:2508.06071, submitted August 2025 (v1 8-Aug-2025, v2 11-Aug-2025) — i.e. 2025, not 2024. Author name (Liang Chen) and the RESUNE label (Rational-Expectations Security-Utility Nash Equilibrium) should be given for traceability.

Houy (2014) is understated. His actual result is sharper and more useful than 'flags fee demand as an open question': in a static partial-equilibrium model he proves that a non-binding block-size limit combined with a fee set by a decentralized competitive market 'cannot guarantee the very existence of Bitcoin in the long-term.' That is a stronger, citable negative result that directly strengthens the fee-market-fragility con — the entry should quote it rather than lump Houy in vaguely with Chen and Alden.

Family tag 'dcf-moneyness' is shared with index 12 (Discounted-Utility / Monetary-Premium DCF) and could read as redundant at a glance. The entry never explicitly states how it differs from index 12 — worth a one-line demarcation since the two sit adjacent under the same family.

Alden is a practitioner/non-peer-reviewed source mixed in with two academic citations (Biais JoF; Chen/Houy working papers). The pros say 'genuinely peer-reviewed (Journal of Finance)' which is true ONLY of Biais et al. — Chen and Houy are working papers and Alden is a blog. existing_evals.medium_explanation: This family prices Bitcoin as a self-referential equilibrium rather than a cashflow asset. Value equals the present value of net transactional benefits (Biais et al., Journal of Finance 2023), jointly with the price that induces enough mining hashrate to keep the chain secure against a 51% attack (Liang Chen's RESUNE model, arXiv 2025; Houy 2014; Alden). Because both transactional usefulness and security scale with price, today's value depends on expected future prices — a fixed point that admits multiple equilibria and 'sunspot' (extrinsic) volatility even with constant fundamentals. The defining empirical result is decompositional: a larger share of Bitcoin's return variance is extrinsic, not fundamental. These are positive models explaining price formation and high volatility, not forecasts — they publish no expected return. For a 10-15yr CMA that means no native point estimate; the honest takeaways are perpetual elevated volatility (~55-70%, uniquely model-implied here, not just borrowed) and a fee-market terminal-security risk that Houy shows may not even guarantee long-run viability. Appreciation must be imported as judgment (~8-10% nominal).

existing_evals.medium_explanation: This approach forces Bitcoin into a discounted-cashflow frame despite its having no cashflow, by treating its "moneyness" — the utility flow from serving as store-of-value, medium-of-exchange, and unit-of-account — as an implicit dividend, then discounting a terminal monetary-premium value. Two academic strands exist: Liu & Zhang's price-to-utility (PU) ratio, which proxies store-of-value utility via the UTXO staking ratio (coins idle >1 year) and flags BTC as rich or cheap to that utility, predicting long-horizon returns through mean-reversion; and Papadogiannis's unified-discounting identity, which models scarcity as a latent state variable mapped to pseudo-cashflows and discounted at an effective rate c_eff = cost-of-capital × belief-distortion. A 10-15yr CMA does not fall out cleanly: an expected return emerges only by assuming the PU ratio normalizes AND the monetary-premium TAM grows along a decaying adoption S-curve. So the appreciation number (~10-13% nominal, echoing VanEck's 15% base) is really a TAM-penetration forecast in DCF costume; the framework's genuine value-add is putting BTC on the same algebraic footing as equities and gold.

existing_evals.medium_explanation: This approach values Bitcoin as a network/monetary good whose demand diffuses along a logistic S-curve borrowed from prior technology adoptions (internet, mobile, social media). You posit a terminal penetration level and date — Blockware's 10% of population by 2030 off a 60% net-entity CAGR, or Timmer's capture of ~25% of monetary gold — draw the logistic path to it, convert end-state network size or TAM share into a terminal market cap, divide by the near-fixed ~21M supply to get a per-coin price, and annualize from spot. The defining feature for a CMA is that the same curve forcing large early multiples also forces appreciation to DECELERATE as penetration climbs toward the inflection and saturation, matching realized decay (142->65->17%/yr). Key inputs: the diffusion analog (which dominates the answer), the adoption ceiling/date, and the contested Metcalfe exponent (~1.5-2). A bounded gold-share TAM (~$5T cap, ~3-4x current) over 12-15yr implies roughly 9-12%/yr nominal — well below history — but the answer is highly sensitive to unfalsifiable analog and timing choices, and the user-facing practitioner targets ($1M+) are promotional and serially revised.

existing_evals.medium_explanation: This family declines to forecast Bitcoin's return at all. existing_evals.name: Market-Implied Futures Forward Curve & Basis
issues: The digest correctly states carry does NOT reliably predict high future spot returns, but UNDERSELLS the sharper Schmeling-Schrimpf-Todorov result: high crypto carry POSITIVELY predicts future CRASHES (and a rise in the price of crash-risk insurance). This is a stronger anti-extrapolation point than 'no forecast value' — high contango is a bearish, not neutral, signal for the spot path, and is worth stating explicitly in the cons.

Terminology: the paper attributes carry to a large/volatile 'inconvenience yield' of holding spot vs futures (driven by trend-chasers + limited arbitrage capital). The digest twice frames this as a positive 'convenience yield' (key_drivers: 'positive convenience yield and negligible storage cost'). For BTC the academically-correct sign is an INconvenience yield on spot. Minor but the convenience-yield framing is borrowed from physical-commodity carry and is the opposite sign of what SST find.

The cited Dec-2025 backwardation magnitude is loosely stated. CoinDesk (3 Dec 2025) reports the CME annualized basis at -2.35%, 'deepest since FTX' — but FTX (Nov 2022) itself briefly approached -50%. existing_evals.medium_explanation: This approach reads BTC's listed futures term structure (CME contracts to ~13 months) and perpetual-swap funding as the market's own priced cost-of-carry. The annualized basis, (F/S-1)x(365/days), equals the financing rate plus a crypto-specific premium; perp funding is the zero-maturity analogue. Normal contango runs ~5-15% APR, spiking 25-40% in euphoria and flipping to backwardation in stress (deepest since FTX in Dec-2025). The key inputs are SOFR (the no-arbitrage floor), leveraged-long demand, and ETF cash-and-carry flows that compressed basis from >20% in 2024 to ~5% by 2026. For a 10-15yr CMA the curve is decisive only in the negative: it is short-dated and cannot speak to decade appreciation, and Schmeling-Schrimpf-Todorov show crypto carry is a time-varying risk premium that predicts crashes, not high spot returns. Its real contribution is a financing-rate floor and a real-time sentiment gauge. Mapped forward, it implies appreciation dominated by the risk-free rate (~4-5%) plus a thin, shrinking premium — a low-double-digit ceiling, with volatility and correlations imported from other rows.

existing_evals.name: Reflexive / Log-Periodic Bubble & Crash-Hazard (LPPLS / JLS)
issues: Primary-source numbers all verified and correct: Wheatley, Sornette, Huber, Reppen & Gantner (Royal Society Open Science, 2019, vol 6 art 180538; arXiv:1803.05663) report generalized-Metcalfe exponent beta=1.69 (SE 0.0076), R^2=0.95 on 2,782 daily values (Jul-2010 to Feb-2018), four bubbles with peak/start runups 3.1x / 20.4x / 6.8x / 103x, and the exact exogenous-shock quote ('massive exogenous shocks... the LPPLS model can provide no warning there'). No fabricated citations. The JLS lineage (Johansen-Ledoit-Sornette rational-expectations bubble) is correctly attributed.

The pros claim 'LPPLS confidence indicator flagged elevated instability before the 2013 and 2017 BTC peaks' is consistent with the paper's ex-ante framing, but the paper's own honest position (and the cons) is that real-time, out-of-sample crash prediction has a contested track record. The pro slightly overstates a still-disputed capability; it is partially walked back in cons #4, so net-honest, but the two should be read together.

Synthesized volatility (~60-70%, floor ~57%) sits ABOVE the honest cross-approach central band (~50-60%) given in the task anchor. This is defensible ONLY because LPPLS specifically models vol clustering/acceleration into log-periodic bursts near t_c, so a higher central is mechanism-consistent — but it should be explicitly flagged as the top of the realized range, not understated. Realized trailing-5y is 57% and 10y 69%, so 60-70% is within history but optimistically high vs the maturing-asset consensus.

The arithmetic-vs-geometric split (~12-16% nominal arithmetic drift collapsing to ~4-9% geometric after a recurring 50-80% drawdown hazard) is the single most valuable and correct insight of this entry — it is the only approach that mechanically separates arithmetic drift from compounded return via crash hazard. It is a judgment, not a published model output (correctly disclosed), and is internally consistent with E[r] = drift - hazard x jump-size.

All correlation rows (growth/value eq, FI, TIPS, gold) are explicitly imported and labeled 'framework silent' — correct, since JLS/LPPLS is a univariate price-process model with no cross-asset structure. corr_gold ~0 correctly anchored to realized ~0 BTC-gold; no false digital-gold linkage asserted. Good discipline.

Distinctness: genuinely distinct. Shares the generalized-Metcalfe (users^1.69) fundamental anchor with the Metcalfe entry (index 1) and the fat-left-tail emphasis with the jump-diffusion entry (index 18), but the load-bearing mechanism here — endogenous super-exponential reflexive growth + a finite-time crash-hazard rate producing a hazard-bracketed regime call and a geometric-return penalty — is not reproduced by any other entry. Not redundant.

(Otherwise it reads as inconsistent with the consensus.)", "In pros #3, soften 'flagged elevated instability before the 2013 and 2017 BTC peaks' to note this is the paper's claimed ex-ante performance, which cons #4 correctly flags as contested out-of-sample — so the reader sees the pro and con are about the same disputed evidence.", "No numeric corrections needed — every cited figure (1.69, R^2=0.95, four bubbles 3.1x-103x, the exogenous-shock quote, four >50% drawdowns) matches the primary source exactly. Entry is publication-ready."]
existing_evals.medium_explanation: This approach treats a Bitcoin bull run as an endogenous bubble rather than a trend to extrapolate. Built on the Johansen-Ledoit-Sornette rational-expectations model and its Log-Periodic Power Law Singularity (LPPLS) calibration, it casts price as faster-than-exponential ("super-exponential") growth driven by herding and positive feedback, accelerating toward a finite critical time t_c at which a time-varying crash-hazard rate peaks. Wheatley, Sornette et al. (Royal Society Open Science, 2019) anchor "fundamental value" with a generalized Metcalfe's law (market cap proportional to active-users^1.69, R^2=0.95) and flag four historical bubbles with 3.1x-103x runups followed by >50% crashes. The model outputs a probabilistic crash bracket, not a date. For a CMA it yields a distinctive shape: E[r] = super-exponential drift minus hazard times expected crash size. The decision-relevant implication is the gap between a ~12-16% nominal arithmetic drift and only ~4-9% geometric (compounded) return once recurring 50-80% endogenous drawdowns are netted out, with vol clustering near 60-70% and correlations imported from realized data.

existing_evals.name: Regime-Switching / Jump-Diffusion & Heavy-Tail Return Process
issues: Cited jump-intensity 'lambda ~0.10-0.17/yr' is almost certainly a UNITS ERROR. SVCJ/jump-diffusion BTC studies (Hou-Wang-Chen-Hardle 2020 JFE; Scaillet et al.) are fit on DAILY data and report jump intensity as a per-DAY probability (commonly ~0.05-0.20/day), not per-year. A 0.10-0.17/yr intensity (~one jump every 6-10 years) contradicts the entry's own (correct) emphasis on frequent, clustered jumps. The magnitude is right for daily, wrong for annual.

The claim that MS-GARCH/SVCJ are 'the consensus econometric description' and 'beat single-regime models out-of-sample' is slightly overstated. The literature is more mixed than presented: Ardia et al. (2018/2019) do find MS-GARCH improves VaR/ES, but several studies find heavy-tailed single-regime GAS/GARCH, SARV stochastic-vol, or even persistent simple GARCH can match or beat MS-GARCH for BTC depending on specification/horizon (e.g. arXiv:2401.03393; FGV RBFin MSGARCH study). The dominant fact is 'fat tails + regimes matter,' not that MS-GARCH specifically wins.

Tail-index citation 'alpha ~2.1-2.5 (heavier than equities ~3)' is correct for the FULL/early sample, but the entry omits that recent (2015-2020) BTC sub-samples show the tail index drifting UP toward ~3 (equity-like) — which is direct corroboration of the entry's own K33 'institutionalization compresses the tail' con and should be cited there, not just asserted.

The synthesized expected-max-drawdown of -55% to -75% over 10-15yr is presented as if institutionalization-discounted from the -77%/-93% history, but this is pure judgment with no scripted derivation; given the parameter-instability con the entry itself raises, the DD band deserves an explicit 'wide CI / scenario, not point' caveat rather than a tidy range.

Minor: 'tail index alpha' for an alpha-stable law would imply infinite variance for alpha<2; the entry's 2.1-2.5 (finite second moment) is a power-law/Hill tail index, NOT a stable-law alpha. The 'alpha-stable' driver bullet and the 'tail index alpha ~2.1-2.5' are two different objects and should not share the alpha symbol — a careful reader will conflate them.
existing_evals.corrections: ["Fix the jump-intensity units: re-label as a per-DAY jump probability (verify against Hou et al. 2020 / a primary SVCJ BTC fit; typical ~0.05-0.20/day) OR drop the spurious '/yr'. Do not leave '0.10-0.17/yr'.", "Soften the OOS-dominance claim from 'consensus / beats single-regime' to 'fat-tailed and regime/jump specifications generally improve tail-risk (VaR/ES) forecasts, with mixed evidence on which specification wins (MS-GARCH vs heavy-tailed GAS vs SARV).' State they are different parameters.", "Add an explicit caveat to the synthesized expected-max-drawdown that it is a scenario/wide-band judgment (not a scripted estimate) given the short, ~4-cycle sample and the parameter-instability con; present it as e.g. '-55% to -75% central, but with a fat right tail of deeper outcomes and large estimation uncertainty.'", "Cite primary sources by name in the entry: Ardia, Bluteau, Boudt, Catania (2018, 'Forecasting risk with Markov-switching GARCH models'); Hou, Wang, Chen, Härdle (2020, JFE, 'Pricing Cryptocurrency Options', SVCJ); Scaillet, Treccani, Trevisan (2020, J. Financial Econometrics, BTC jumps); Chaim & Laurini (2018/2019, jumps & vol jumps in BTC); for tail index, Begušić et al. (2018, 'Scaling properties of extreme price fluctuations in Bitcoin', alpha~2-2.5)."]
existing_evals.medium_explanation: This is not a price model but a model of Bitcoin's return-generating process. Rather than one decaying drift and a single ~57% volatility number, it specifies the full conditional distribution using four econometric tools: Markov-switching GARCH (returns flip between a calm low-vol and a turbulent high-vol regime), affine jump-diffusion / SVCJ (stochastic volatility with downward price jumps that arrive together with vol spikes), self-exciting Hawkes processes (a jump today raises the odds of the next, producing crash clustering), and heavy-tail laws (a power-law tail index ~2.1-2.5, heavier than equities' ~3). Its CMA contribution is the risk SHAPE, not the appreciation level: vol-of-vol, kurtosis, expected shortfall, expected maximum drawdown, and regime-conditional correlation. It must borrow its drift (~10-15% nominal) from adoption/TAM rows. For a 10-15yr BTC CMA it implies vol is a mixture (~40-50% calm, ~80-110% turbulent), a realistic -55% to -75% peak-to-trough drawdown, and — most usefully — that diversification vanishes precisely in crisis regimes when BTC co-jumps with equities. The lesson: do not size Bitcoin off a single sigma.

existing_evals.name: Survival / Ruin-Probability (Absorbing-Zero Hazard)
issues: MISATTRIBUTED HEADLINE NUMBER (most serious): The digest presents Fidelity as having 'published the cleanest single number: ~0.71%/yr Bitcoin extinction probability from a 27-variable Monte Carlo (vs Tesla 2.2%, Apple 0.06%).' I could not verify this in any actual Fidelity Digital Assets publication. Fidelity's real research ('Valuing Bitcoin' 2022, 'Bitcoin First', 'Getting Off Zero') makes only a QUALITATIVE claim that the chance another network supplants Bitcoin is 'incredibly small and decreasing' — no quantified annual extinction probability. The exact '0.71% / 27 variables / Tesla 2.2% / Apple 0.06% / 2022 Fed study / 7-of-9 near-death scenarios' cluster traces ONLY to a binary-options affiliate SEO blog (pocketoption.com, 'Could Bitcoin Go To Zero'), which is AI-generated content-farm material, not a primary source. This is a fabricated/laundered citation presented as a Fidelity measurement.

The con about Fidelity ('Fidelity's 0.71% is a model output dressed as a measurement') is well-reasoned but built on the same unverified number — the deeper problem is the number is not Fidelity's at all, so the critique understates the issue.

Taleb characterization is slightly imprecise on title: the digest cites '(2021) absorbing-barrier argument' which is correct in substance; the paper is 'Bitcoin, Currencies, and Fragility' (Taleb 2021, Quantitative Finance) — fine to name it for the citation.

Ord (2023) mechanism is described as 'mixture-of-exponentials over an unknown true hazard => declining observed hazard => remaining-life proportional to current age.' Ord's actual emphasis (arXiv 2308.09045) is that Lindy arises from a DISTRIBUTION over hazard rates even when individual hazards are constant or increasing — the digest's con #4 captures this correctly, but the pro/driver framing ('declining in age') slightly overstates that Ord shows hazard literally declines; he shows the EFFECTIVE population hazard declines via survivorship selection. Minor.

Biais et al. is cited as 'Biais et al. (J. Finance 2023)'; the full author list is Biais, Bisière, Bouvard, Casamatta & Menkveld (2023, J. Finance 78(2):967-1014). 'et al.' is acceptable but the lead-only cite loses the co-authors. The 'majority of variance is extrinsic/sunspot' claim is correctly supported by the paper's calibration ('a larger share reflects extrinsic volatility').

Synthesized arithmetic is internally consistent (S(12)=exp(-0.21)=0.81; 0.81*1.11^12-1 = +183% = ~9.1%/yr, digest says ~8.9% then haircuts to ~7%), but the chosen mean hazard 1.75%/yr is anchored ABOVE the unverified Fidelity 0.71% — so the anchor that justifies the band is itself unreliable. The conclusion (h in ~1-3%/yr) is defensible on priors regardless, but should be sourced to the academic existence-of-zero theory + practitioner priors, NOT to a fake Fidelity number.

Minor skew inconsistency: synthesized nominal says survival-path R_survival ~11%/yr (a mean CAGR) yet also calls the survival MEDIAN 'low-double-digits'; for a right-skewed survival distribution mean > median, so median should be flagged as somewhat below 11%, modestly understating skew.

A widely-circulated 0.71%/yr figure (with Tesla 2.2%/Apple 0.06% comparisons and a 27-variable Monte Carlo) is NOT from Fidelity; it traces to an unattributed crypto-affiliate web article and should be treated as fabricated, not cited.' Keep the ~7% center and bimodal shape — those are sound — but state the hazard is a PRIOR, not a measurement.", "Add the full Biais et al. author list (Biais, Bisière, Bouvard, Casamatta, Menkveld 2023, J. Finance) at least once.", "Tighten the Ord description: 'Ord (2023) shows the Lindy effect (longer-lived => longer expected remaining life) emerges from a distribution OVER hazard rates via survivorship selection, even when individual hazards are constant — implying the EFFECTIVE network hazard declines with age, so S(T) should be revised up as BTC survives.'", "In synthesized_outputs note that on the right-skewed survival path the MEDIAN annualized return sits somewhat BELOW the ~11% mean R_survival, reinforcing that the ruin-weighted MEAN (~7%) is doubly a poor central estimate (it both buries the -100% mass and sits above the survival median)."]
existing_evals.medium_explanation: This approach treats Bitcoin's CMA as a probability-weighted mixture of two paths rather than a single number: E[R] = S(T)·R_survival + (1−S(T))·(−100%), where S(T)=exp(−∫h(t)dt) is cumulative survival under an annual ruin hazard h. It is the rigorous version of the 'left-tail haircut' other rows wave at. The inputs are: a hazard rate (a prior, ~1-3%/yr, possibly Lindy-declining per Ord 2023, since 16+ years and ETF adoption raise S(T)); a survival-path return R_survival borrowed from an adoption/TAM/decay model (~10-12%/yr); and a −100% recovery on the death path. Peer-reviewed theory supplies WHY a real zero-equilibrium exists — Schilling-Uhlig (JME 2019) collapse martingales and Biais et al. (J. Finance 2023) sunspot multiple-equilibria — while Taleb (2021) gives the absorbing-barrier intuition. For a 10-15yr BTC CMA it yields a bimodal payoff: ~80% mass on a right-skewed survival path, ~20% at −100%, centering the mean near ~7% nominal but making the mean itself a poor summary. Its value is shape and discipline, not a point estimate; it needs a survival-return model bolted on and says nothing about correlations or volatility.

new_approaches.name: Fractal Long-Memory & Adaptive-Efficiency (MF-DFA / Hurst / ARFIMA)
new_approaches.description: This approach studies the SCALING and long-memory structure of Bitcoin's RETURN-and-volatility autocorrelation, rather than the price level. Three converging tools: (1) the (generalized) Hurst exponent h(q) and rescaled-range/DFA, where h>0.5 means persistent/trending returns, h=0.5 a random walk (efficient), h<0.5 anti-persistent/mean-reverting; (2) multifractal detrended fluctuation analysis (MF-DFA), which measures a SPECTRUM of exponents h(q) and a multifractal width (Delta-alpha) whose two sources are fat tails and long-range temporal correlation (Takaishi, Stosic); (3) fractional-integration models (ARFIMA in the mean, FIGARCH in variance) summarizing persistence by a single parameter d, where the squared/absolute-return autocorrelation decays as a slow power law. Crucially these are estimated on ROLLING windows, and the literature's central empirical claim is a maturation trend: the return-side Hurst exponent drifts toward 0.5 and the multifractal width compresses as Bitcoin ages (Bariviera 2017; Sigaki-Perc-Ribeiro 2019; Takaishi 2021) — the Adaptive Market Hypothesis applied to crypto. It does NOT generate a price target. A 10-15yr CMA falls out only INDIRECTLY: efficiency-maturation kills the persistent-trend component that produced BTC's historical excess return (so the risk premium / appreciation must compress toward an arbitrage-free, near-random-walk level), while the separately-persistent LONG MEMORY IN VOLATILITY says realized vol clusters and decays slowly — implying a high, slowly-mean-reverting vol floor and a breakdown of naive sqrt-T vol scaling. The framework is fundamentally a RISK/efficiency characterization, not a return-level forecaster.
new_approaches.medium_explanation: This family analyzes the scaling of Bitcoin's return series, not its price. The Hurst exponent h measures persistence: h>0.5 is a trending market, h=0.5 a random walk, h<0.5 mean-reverting. MF-DFA generalizes this to a spectrum h(q) and a multifractal width driven by fat tails plus long-range correlation; ARFIMA/FIGARCH compress the same persistence into a fractional-integration parameter d. Estimated on rolling windows, the literature's key finding is maturation: Bitcoin's return-side Hurst drifts from persistent (>0.5 pre-2014) toward 0.5, and efficiency rises as the market ages (Bariviera 2017; Sigaki-Perc-Ribeiro 2019; Takaishi 2021) — the Adaptive Market Hypothesis. For a 10-15yr CMA this implies two things. First, as returns become efficient/random-walk, the predictable trend component that drove historical excess returns disappears, so forward appreciation must compress toward an arbitrage-free level — reinforcing the decay anchor. Second, long memory persists in VOLATILITY even as it dies in returns, so vol clusters, decays slowly, and stays elevated — a high vol floor and broken sqrt-T scaling. It outputs no price; it disciplines the return and vol assumptions.
key_drivers: Hurst exponent h(2) of returns (R/S and DFA estimates) — the persistence measure; its rolling-window drift toward 0.5 (efficiency maturation) is the load-bearing CMA signal
Generalized Hurst spectrum h(q) and multifractal width Delta-alpha (MF-DFA) — degree of multifractality and whether it compresses over time
Two sources of multifractality, disentangled by shuffling/surrogates: fat-tailed distribution vs long-range temporal correlation (Takaishi: both contribute)
Fractional-integration parameter d (ARFIMA in mean, FIGARCH in variance) — single-number persistence; d~0 in returns (efficient) but d>0 / near unit-persistence in volatility
Long memory in VOLATILITY (slow power-law decay of squared/absolute-return autocorrelation) — persists even as return memory dies; drives vol clustering and the vol floor
Adaptive Market Hypothesis / liquidity & volume growth — the maturation mechanism: rising liquidity, arbitrage capital and institutionalization push h(2) toward 0.5
Rolling-window length & estimator choice (R/S vs DFA vs FD4 vs q=2) — the estimate is highly sensitive to these (a key fragility)
Breakdown of sqrt-T volatility scaling: with long memory d!=0, multi-horizon vol scales as T^(d+0.5), not T^0.5 — directly relevant to horizon-aggregating a CMA vol number
pros: Directly characterizes the two CMA moments that matter most for a no-cashflow asset — the efficiency of returns (hence whether ANY excess return is structurally sustainable) and the persistence of volatility (hence the vol floor and clustering) — without needing a fabricated price target

The maturation finding is robust in direction across independent teams and methods (Bariviera DFA; Sigaki-Perc-Ribeiro permutation entropy on 400+ coins; Takaishi MF-DFA): the return-side trend toward random-walk efficiency is real and mechanistically grounded in rising liquidity/arbitrage — and it INDEPENDENTLY corroborates the appreciation-decay anchor from a pure time-series-structure angle, not a valuation narrative

Separates return memory (dying) from volatility memory (persistent), which correctly predicts the empirically observed pattern of a falling appreciation rate alongside a sticky ~50-60% vol floor — a distinction most BTC frameworks miss
Falsifiable and model-light: a single exponent (h, or d) with rolling estimation; deviations are observable and the maturation hypothesis is testable out of sample
Peer-reviewed, published in Physica A / Economics Letters / Scientific Reports — genuinely academic, not sell-side marketing, and explicitly skeptical of trend-following 'edges' surviving
cons: Produces NO appreciation forecast and NO price level — it is a return-/risk-structure diagnostic, so any 10-15yr CMA appreciation number is bolted on by judgment, not derived. Using h(2)->0.5 to argue 'expected excess return -> ~0' is an over-reach: efficiency means returns are unpredictable, NOT that the risk premium is zero (a perfectly efficient risky asset still earns a premium)

The headline long-memory finding is method-fragile and possibly an artifact: h>0.5 can reflect the FAT-TAILED DISTRIBUTION rather than genuine memory (the 'memory indicator' = exponent minus shuffled-series exponent often collapses), and switching estimator (R/S vs DFA vs FD4) or window flips the sign — some studies find ANTI-persistence (h<0.5), not persistence (Some comments on Bitcoin market (in)efficiency)

Results are radically non-stationary and time-varying by the framework's own admission (Takaishi: 'properties of the Bitcoin market are mostly time dependent') — multifractal degree even INCREASED after 2017 in some studies, contradicting a clean monotone maturation; the rolling estimates oscillate (AMH = alternating efficient/inefficient regimes), so extrapolating the trend 10-15yr is unreliable
Says nothing native about cross-asset correlations (growth/value equity, FI, TIPS, gold) — every correlation cell must be imported from realized data

Small-sample / single-path: estimated on one realized BTC history (~15yr, ~3-4 cycles); MF-DFA and Hurst estimators are notoriously biased in short, heavy-tailed samples, and cannot price catastrophic-failure tail mass
ETF/custodial/off-chain migration and institutionalization are a structural break that can reset the scaling regime; the historical exponents may not persist post-2024

new_approaches.rich_notes:
METHODOLOGY. Three statistical-physics/econometrics tools share one mechanism — characterizing the autocorrelation/scaling structure of returns and volatility, and its drift toward random-walk efficiency. (1) Hurst exponent h via rescaled-range (R/S) and detrended fluctuation analysis (DFA): the fluctuation function F(s) ~ s^h; h>0.5 persistent (trend), h=0.5 random walk (weak-form efficient), h<0.5 anti-persistent. (2) MF-DFA: generalizes to a q-dependent spectrum h(q); the spread Delta-h or singularity width Delta-alpha measures multifractality, whose two ingredients (isolated by phase-randomization / shuffling surrogates) are the fat-tailed marginal and long-range temporal correlation. Takaishi (2018) finds Bitcoin 1-min returns fat-tailed (kurtosis far above Gaussian) and genuinely multifractal, with BOTH temporal correlation and the tail contributing. Stosic et al. (2019) apply MF-DFA across ~50 cryptos and find price-changes and volume-changes follow DIFFERENT multifractal dynamics. (3) Fractional integration: ARFIMA(p,d,q) in the mean and FIGARCH in variance summarize persistence by d; the empirical regularity is d~0 in returns (efficient) but d>0 / near-unit persistence in squared/absolute returns (volatility long memory).

KEY RELATIONSHIPS / HISTORICAL FIT. The literature's signature result is MATURATION under the Adaptive Market Hypothesis. Bariviera (2017, Economics Letters), rolling 2011-2017: daily returns persistent (h>0.5) in the first half, converging to ~0.5 (efficient) after 2014 — while VOLATILITY shows long memory throughout the entire period. He stresses DFA discriminates time-variation better than R/S (which is biased toward 'detecting' long memory). Sigaki, Perc & Ribeiro (2019, Scientific Reports), using permutation entropy + statistical complexity on 400+ cryptocurrencies over sliding windows: the market is 'coming of age' — moving toward efficiency; 37% of coins are efficient >80% of the time, 20% efficient <20%, and — strikingly — efficiency is NOT correlated with market capitalization (so it is age/liquidity, not size). Takaishi (2021) confirms with rolling MF-DFA + TGARCH that virtually every property (kurtosis, skew, serial correlation, multifractal degree, volatility asymmetry) is time-varying, and that 'the recent Bitcoin market has become more efficient,' with efficiency-measures (Hurst, multifractal degree, kurtosis) co-moving with a weakening inverted volatility asymmetry. Wei et al. (2019) tie efficiency to LIQUIDITY: pre-2013 thin/illiquid and anti-persistent (h<0.5), then h rises to ~0.5 as liquidity grows.

FAILURE MODES / SKEPTICISM. The long-memory finding is fragile. 'Some comments on Bitcoin market (in)efficiency' (Sanchez-Granero/Trinidad-Segovia et al.) shows a self-similarity exponent >0.5 'is not due to memory but to the underlying [fat-tailed] distribution': their memory indicator (exponent minus shuffled-series exponent) reveals periods of significant ANTI-persistence, and with the FD algorithm at q=2 the exponent does NOT consistently exceed 0.5 — i.e., the sign of the result flips with estimator and window. So the very existence of return long memory is contested, and Hurst/MF-DFA estimators are biased in short, heavy-tailed samples. Worse for a clean maturation story: some studies find multifractal degree INCREASED after 2017 (volume/price explosions), and AMH implies ALTERNATING efficient/inefficient regimes rather than monotone convergence — undermining any 10-15yr trend extrapolation. The framework is also radically non-stationary by its own admission, says nothing about cross-asset correlations, and cannot price tail/failure mass (single realized path).

ON-RECORD MULTI-YEAR FORECASTS. None. This is the family's defining limitation and what distinguishes it from S2F/Metcalfe/power-law: it deliberately produces NO price target or dated forecast. Its on-record claims are structural and qualitative — 'Bitcoin is becoming more efficient' (Bariviera; Takaishi), 'the cryptocurrency market is coming of age' (Sigaki-Perc-Ribeiro), and 'volatility exhibits long memory throughout' (Bariviera; FIGARCH literature). For a CMA, the honest contribution is therefore directional, and it CORROBORATES the appreciation-decay anchor independently: efficiency maturation kills the persistent-trend excess-return component (pushing forward appreciation down toward an arbitrage-free level, ~7-11% nominal in my synthesis), while persistent volatility long memory justifies a high, sticky ~52-60% vol floor with broken sqrt-T scaling. It informs the return and especially the volatility cells; it cannot, by construction, set them alone.

issues: UNSOURCED COUNTERCLAIM (the only real factual weakness): the con 'some studies find multifractal degree INCREASED after 2017... contradicting a clean monotone maturation' is attributed to vague 'some studies' with no named citation. I verified Takaishi 2021 (PMC7850481) — which the dossier ITSELF cites as a maturation source — explicitly finds the OPPOSITE: 'multifractal degree decreases with time, which suggests the Bitcoin market gradually approaches the efficient market.' So the strongest version of the skeptic's case is not actually supported by the paper the dossier leans on, and the 'increased' claim floats without provenance. It may be true of a specific COVID/volume-spike study but is not pinned down.

ATTRIBUTION SLIPPAGE on the maturation mechanism: the dossier repeatedly bundles 'age/liquidity' as the driver of efficiency and attaches it to Sigaki-Perc-Ribeiro 2019. I confirmed Sigaki finds efficiency is NOT correlated with market cap (r=0.07, p=0.16, verbatim) and that younger coins 'follow the trend of their elders' (AGE) — but the paper does NOT discuss LIQUIDITY at all. The liquidity mechanism comes from Wei et al. 2019, a separate paper. Minor conflation of two sources' mechanisms under one citation.

OVERSTATED PRIMACY: the claim that this framework 'has the MOST to say' about the volatility cell is overstated. Cross-checking the sibling approaches, the Options-Implied (DVOL), Regime-Switching/Jump-Diffusion heavy-tail, and FIGARCH-adjacent approaches make equally direct claims on vol structure. The long-memory-in-vol / broken-sqrt-T point is genuine and distinctive, but 'the MOST' is a rhetorical overreach.

INTERNAL BAND INCONSISTENCY (minor): synthesized corr_growth_eq band tops at +0.55 while the dossier cites realized trailing-5y 0.564 AND says it is 'rising with institutionalization' — the band should top slightly above, not below, the cited realized value. Same for corr_value_eq (band top +0.35 vs cited realized 0.37). The ceilings sit just under the realized anchors they claim to be rising from.

The sqrt-T claim is stated as a flat negative ('breaks sqrt-T scaling') but the empirical magnitude of d in BTC volatility is small and itself disputed (the very fragility the cons admit); so the practical horizon-aggregation effect on a 10-15yr vol number is likely modest, not the dramatic break the framing implies. Not wrong, but the load-bearing-ness is somewhat oversold relative to estimator uncertainty.
verdict.corrections: "1) Replace the unsourced 'multifractal degree INCREASED after 2017' con with a properly cited claim, OR soften to 'AMH implies alternating efficient/inefficient regimes rather than monotone convergence' (which IS supported) and drop the 'increased' assertion — because the dossier's own cited Takaishi 2021 finds multifractal degree DECREASED toward efficiency. As written it risks implying Takaishi found an increase. 2) Split the maturation-mechanism attribution: age-not-size from Sigaki-Perc-Ribeiro 2019 (verified r=0.07, p=0.16); liquidity-driven rise in Hurst toward 0.5 from Wei et al. 2019. Do not attach 'liquidity' to Sigaki. 3) Downgrade 'the framework has the MOST to say about vol' to 'a distinctive and direct contribution to the vol cell.' 4) Lift the corr_growth_eq / corr_value_eq band ceilings to bracket (not undercut) the cited realized 0.56 / 0.37 if the stated direction is 'rising.' Everything else checks out: all five representative citations verified (Bariviera 2017 Economics Letters 161:1-4 DFA + volatility-long-memory-throughout; Takaishi 2018 Physica A 506:507-519 multifractality from BOTH tails and correlation; Sigaki-Perc-Ribeiro 2019 Sci Rep 9:1440, 37%/20% figures exact; Stosic 2019 Physica A 520:54-61 price-vs-volume different dynamics; Sanchez-Granero/Trinidad-Segovia 2019 PLOS ONE anti-persistence/distribution-not-memory). All realized anchors match the scripted empirical_anchor.json EXACTLY: decay 142.2/65.5/17.0% (full/10y/5y), vol floor 57.45% (5y), gold corr -0.011/0.033/0.045 (~0). The T^(d+0.5)=T^H scaling formula is correctly stated."
overstated_pros: 'The framework has the MOST to say' about the volatility cell — overstated vs sibling DVOL/jump-diffusion/FIGARCH approaches that speak equally directly to vol.

Pro #2's phrasing that maturation 'INDEPENDENTLY corroborates the appreciation-decay anchor from a pure time-series-structure angle' is slightly inflated: the framework gives NO return level (the cons admit this), so the 'corroboration' is purely directional (trend-profits vanish), not a quantitative independent confirmation of the 7-11% band. The dossier mostly self-corrects this in cons, but the pro reads stronger than warranted.

Pro #2 calls the maturation finding 'robust in direction across independent teams' — true for direction, but the cons (correctly) note the magnitude/sign of the underlying long-memory is method-fragile; the pro should not be read without that caveat, which is somewhat buried.
missing_cons: No treatment of the fundamental tension the dossier creates but never resolves: it uses h(2)->0.5 (return efficiency) to argue the trend premium decays, while simultaneously holding a HIGH appreciation band (7-11%) justified by a 'genuine risk premium for ~55% vol.' But efficiency/random-walk says NOTHING about the size of that premium — so the appreciation number is essentially unconstrained by the framework and is really imported from the cross-approach decay anchor. The con admits 'efficiency != zero premium' but does not flag that this leaves the framework with ZERO native pull on the appreciation level — it is doing no independent work there.

Survivorship/single-realized-path is mentioned, but the related point that ALL the maturation evidence is in-sample on one asset's one history means the 'maturation will continue 10-15yr' extrapolation has no out-of-sample validation — stronger than the 'AMH oscillates' con and not fully made.

No mention that rolling-window Hurst/MF-DFA estimates have wide confidence intervals that the literature often under-reports; the 'drift toward 0.5' may be within estimation noise of a constant ~0.5, which would moot the entire maturation narrative (not just make it non-monotone).

Reverse-causality / reflexivity is ignored: rising 'efficiency' coincides with the 2014+ derivatives/arbitrage build-out, but it ALSO coincides with the very institutionalization the dossier elsewhere calls a regime-breaking structural break — the two cons (maturation-is-real vs ETF-resets-the-regime) are in direct tension and the dossier never reconciles them.

new_approaches.name: Rough Volatility (Fractional-Brownian RFSV) for Bitcoin
new_approaches.description: A volatility-process (not price-level) model. Following Gatheral, Jaisson & Rosenbaum's "Volatility is rough" (2018), log-volatility is modeled as a fractional Brownian motion (fBm) with a very small Hurst exponent H (≈0.1 for equities; Takaishi 2020 and the 2025 finite-sample work estimate H≈0.12-0.14 for Bitcoin realized volatility), i.e. the RFSV (Rough Fractional Stochastic Volatility) model. H<<1/2 means volatility increments are strongly ANTI-persistent / 'rough' — vol mean-reverts very fast and the realized-vol path is jagged at every time scale. The empirical inputs are: a roughness index H estimated from the scaling of q-th moments of log-RV increments (m(q,Δ)∝Δ^{qH}), a vol-of-vol parameter ν, and a long-run vol level. The model's payoff is a TERM STRUCTURE OF VOLATILITY and a conditional forecast: future log-vol is Gaussian with mean reverting toward the long-run level and variance scaling like Δ^{2H}. Crucially, RFSV is silent on EXPECTED RETURN (appreciation), and silent on cross-asset correlation — it is a pure second-moment / risk model. To populate a CMA it tells you ONLY about volatility (the floor, the term structure, and the persistence of vol shocks); appreciation and all correlations must be imported from realized data or another framework. Distinct from option-implied vol (Q-measure short-dated surface) because RFSV is fit to physical-measure realized vol; distinct from jump-diffusion because it derives the vol-of-vol scaling rather than postulating fat tails; and the OPPOSITE scaling regime from long-memory (H>1/2 persistent) models.
new_approaches.medium_explanation: Rough volatility models Bitcoin's log-volatility as a fractional Brownian motion with a tiny Hurst exponent (H≈0.12-0.14 for BTC, vs ≈0.1 for equities). H<<0.5 means vol is strongly anti-persistent: shocks decay fast and the realized-vol path is jagged at every scale. The key inputs are the roughness index H (from how q-th moments of log-RV increments scale with lag), a vol-of-vol parameter, and a long-run vol level. The model's output is a TERM STRUCTURE of volatility and sharper realized-vol forecasts that beat AR/HAR — but it says NOTHING about expected return or correlation. For a 10-15yr BTC CMA it is therefore a risk-only building block: it disciplines the volatility cell (and warns vol is mean-reverting around a high long-run level, not trending to zero), but appreciation and every cross-asset correlation must be borrowed from realized data. Its central caveat: Cont-Das and a 2025 BTC paper argue the measured 'roughness' may be a microstructure/estimation artifact, not a true property of spot vol — so even the one cell it informs is contested.
key_drivers: Hurst exponent H of log-volatility increments (≈0.12-0.14 for BTC realized vol per Takaishi 2020 / finite-sample work; ≈0.1 for equities per Gatheral et al.) — the single roughness parameter governing vol persistence and term structure
Vol-of-vol parameter ν (amplitude of the fractional-Brownian driver of log-vol)
Long-run / unconditional volatility level toward which log-vol mean-reverts (the 'vol floor' the CMA inherits)
Realized-volatility estimator and sampling frequency (5-min RV; the 1% finite-sample error band; choice of Δ materially shifts the apparent H)
Multifractality of BTC log-vol: the generalized Hurst exponent is NOT constant across moment orders (Takaishi), which violates the single-H homogeneity assumption RFSV needs
Microstructure noise / spot-vol estimation error — the contested source of apparent roughness (Cont-Das 'fact or artefact')
Δ^{2H} scaling of the conditional log-vol forecast variance — drives the volatility term structure and the speed of mean reversion
pros: Directly informs the one CMA cell it addresses — volatility — with a physically-estimated, falsifiable parameter (H) rather than an assumption; and the RFSV forecast empirically beats AR/HAR realized-vol forecasts (Gatheral et al.), so it has genuine out-of-sample skill on vol

Provides a TERM STRUCTURE of volatility and a fast-mean-reversion structure, which correctly implies that BTC's long-horizon average vol is anchored to a high unconditional level (a vol FLOOR) rather than drifting to zero — exactly the 'vol stays ~50-60%' shape a 10-15yr CMA needs

Estimated specifically on Bitcoin (Takaishi 2020; the 2025 finite-sample paper with H≈0.12-0.14; 'Cryptos have rough volatility and correlated jumps'), so it is not a blind transplant of an equity result

Explains a known statistical trap: RFSV-generated data LOOKS like long memory under classical tests even though it is not — so it warns against the competing long-memory/persistence family's spurious findings
Honest about scope: as a second-moment model it makes no over-reaching price-target claims (unlike S2F/Metcalfe/power-law), so it cannot be 'weaponized' into hype forecasts
cons: Says NOTHING about expected return: RFSV is a pure volatility/risk process and produces no appreciation estimate at all — the most important CMA cell must be imported entirely from elsewhere, making it at best a partial building block

Says NOTHING about cross-asset correlation (growth/value equities, nominal FI, TIPS, gold) — the entire correlation row is silent, so it cannot inform the 'digital gold' axis or portfolio construction

The measured roughness may be a STATISTICAL ARTIFACT, not a real feature of spot volatility. Cont & Das (2022/2024) show realized vol ALWAYS looks rough (H<0.5) regardless of the true spot process, because microstructure noise and spot-vol estimation error manufacture apparent roughness — a frontal challenge to the whole approach

BTC-specific rejection: the 2025 paper 'Multifractality in Bitcoin Realized Volatility' (arXiv:2507.00575) could not even estimate a valid roughness index (the p-variation statistic stayed strictly negative) and concludes rough-vol models are 'structurally misaligned with the empirical features of Bitcoin volatility,' recommending multifractal random-walk / multifractal stochastic-vol models instead

Multifractality breaks the single-H assumption: Takaishi himself finds the generalized Hurst exponent is non-constant, so a single roughness number is a simplification of a richer, regime-dependent scaling — and H itself drifts with sampling frequency Δ
Even taken at face value it informs only volatility; it offers no view on the appreciation DECAY or the rising equity correlation that dominate a real BTC CMA
