new_approaches.rich_notes:
METHODOLOGY. Rough volatility begins with Gatheral, Jaisson & Rosenbaum (2018, Quantitative Finance; arXiv:1410.3394). Their empirical claim: across thousands of equity/index realized-vol series, the q-th absolute moments of log-vol increments scale as m(q,Δ)∝Δ^{qH} with H≈0.1 — far below the H=1/2 of a standard diffusion. They model log-volatility as a fractional Brownian motion with this small H (the RFSV model), where H<1/2 makes vol 'rough' / anti-persistent: it mean-reverts extremely fast and the path is jagged at every scale. Two consequences matter for a CMA. First, RFSV produces a TERM STRUCTURE of volatility: the conditional variance of future log-vol scales like Δ^{2H}, giving sharper realized-vol forecasts that beat AR and HAR benchmarks. Second — and decisively — RFSV is a model of the SECOND MOMENT only. It contains no drift on price, no expected-return parameter, and no cross-asset structure. It can populate the volatility cell of a CMA and nothing else.

BITCOIN ESTIMATES. Takaishi (2020, Finance Research Letters; arXiv:1904.12346) applies multifractal detrended fluctuation analysis (MF-DFA) to Bitcoin log-volatility increments and finds the generalized Hurst exponent is below 1/2 — confirming rough, anti-persistent BTC vol. He adds a crucial wrinkle: the generalized Hurst exponent is NOT constant across moment orders, i.e. BTC log-vol is MULTIFRACTAL, with part of the multifractality coming from the fat-tailed distribution (revealed by shuffling). A 2025 finite-sample follow-up (arXiv:2511.03314, 'Multifractality and sample size influence on Bitcoin volatility patterns') sharpens the number: estimating H as Δ→0 via the ansatz H(Δ)=H₀·n/(n+a), it obtains H₀≈0.1262-0.1379 across three periods, with the parameter a≈3, and finds the 5-minute RV carries only ~1% relative error — concluding 5-min RV is adequate for H estimation. So the on-record BTC roughness index is H≈0.12-0.14, slightly above the equity ~0.1 but firmly 'rough.' The Digital Finance paper 'Cryptos have rough volatility and correlated jumps' (2025) corroborates roughness using 3+ years of 5-min data and adds that daily vol is best explained by roughness PLUS correlated jumps across cryptos.

KEY RELATIONSHIP TO A CMA. The model's honest contribution is the VOL FLOOR. Because rough vol mean-reverts very fast around a high unconditional level, the multi-year AVERAGE volatility is governed by that long-run level, not by the latest (possibly low) print. This is the cleanest theoretical case AGAINST the optimistic vol-compression theses (e.g. CF Benchmarks' ~28% terminal vol): fast anti-persistent reversion does not let vol drift to equity-like levels and stay there. It supports a 10-15yr vol band around realized ~55-60%. The model gives NO appreciation and NO correlation, which must be imported from the realized-decay baseline (nom 142%→65%→17%/yr; vol floor ~57%; equity corr rising to ~0.56; BTC-gold ~0).

FAILURE MODES / CRITIQUES (represented faithfully). (1) Roughness may be an ARTIFACT. Cont & Das, 'Rough volatility: fact or artefact?' (2022; arXiv:2203.13820) show via simulation that realized vol ALWAYS exhibits apparent H<0.5 regardless of the true spot-vol roughness — microstructure noise and spot-vol estimation error manufacture spurious roughness. Their follow-up filtering work (2024) reinforces that estimation error, not the volatility process, drives the H<0.5 finding. If true, the BTC H≈0.13 is measuring noise, not vol dynamics. (2) BTC-SPECIFIC REJECTION. The seed paper 'Multifractality in Bitcoin Realized Volatility: Implications for Rough Volatility Modelling' (2025; arXiv:2507.00575), using Bitstamp 1-min data 2017-2024, could NOT estimate a valid roughness index at all — the normalized p-variation statistic stayed strictly negative (max < -0.009) across all years and frequencies — and concludes rough-vol models are 'structurally misaligned with the empirical features of Bitcoin volatility,' recommending Multifractal Random Walk / Multifractal Stochastic Volatility instead. (3) MULTIFRACTALITY breaks the single-H homogeneity assumption RFSV needs (Takaishi's own non-constant generalized-Hurst result; the 2025 paper's spectral widths 0.06-0.42). (4) H drifts with sampling frequency, so the 'law' is not shift-invariant.

ON-RECORD MULTI-YEAR FORECASTS. None. This is a defining feature: the rough-volatility literature publishes NO multi-year price forecasts, NO appreciation targets, and NO correlation projections. It is exclusively a second-moment estimation exercise. Any practitioner who attaches a return path to it is bolting an external assumption onto a pure vol model. For our CMA the appropriate use is narrow and defensible: cite rough vol as theoretical support for a HIGH, MEAN-REVERTING volatility floor (~55-60% over 10-15yr, arguing against rapid compression), discount that support modestly for the artifact critique, and import every other cell from the realized-decay baseline.

issues: Citation-date inconsistency on Gatheral et al.: the doc dates it 2018, but the arXiv preprint is 2014 (1410.3394) and the Quantitative Finance publication is 2018. Both 'years' appear in the doc (header says 2018, rich_notes says '2018, Quantitative Finance; arXiv:1410.3394'). Minor but the bare '2018' for an arXiv:1410 link is loose. Defensible since journal year is 2018.
Takaishi 2020 vs 2019: doc cites '2020 (Finance Research Letters)' with arXiv:1904.12346. The arXiv preprint is 2019; FRL publication 2020. Correctly attributed to the journal year. No error.

H0=0.1262-0.1379 for arXiv:2511.03314 could NOT be confirmed from the abstract (only 'H<1/2, rough' and the 1% 5-min error were verifiable). The precise three-period H0 band and the ansatz form H(D)=H0*n/(n+a) with a~3 are body-level claims I could not independently verify. The doc states them as specific facts. They are plausible and consistent with the abstract's direction, but the headline numeric band is unverified at the source-text level. The doc should flag these as body-extracted, not abstract-confirmed.

Apparent internal tension in the volatility synthesis: the doc cites realized trailing-5y ~57% AND 10y ~69%, then anchors the 10-15yr CMA at ~55-60% — i.e. at/below the LOWER (5y) realized figure and well below the 10y. But its central rough-vol argument is that the LONG-RUN unconditional level (not the recent print) governs the multi-year average, and that vol should NOT compress. If the 10y realized is 69% and 5y is 57%, the realized series is itself DECLINING, and picking 55-60% implicitly bets on continued mild compression toward the recent low - which partially contradicts the 'long-run level dominates, reject compression' thesis. The doc rejects CF-Benchmarks 28-40% but lands closer to the 5y low than the 10y level. This is a mild framing inconsistency, not a fatal one (institutionalization/maturation is a reasonable reason vol trends down), but it is not fully reconciled.

The single concrete CMA contribution (vol floor) rests on a parameter (H) the doc itself concedes may be a statistical artifact (Cont-Das) AND that a BTC-specific paper says is not even estimable for Bitcoin (2507.00575). The doc handles this honestly by saying it leans only on the QUALITATIVE floor, not a precise H - but logically, if rough-vol is 'structurally misaligned with BTC' (2507.00575's conclusion, which the doc endorses), then the model provides essentially ZERO genuine support even for the vol cell. The doc's framing ('the one cell it genuinely informs') overstates how much survives its own cited rejections. The fast-mean-reversion-implies-floor argument does not strictly require rough-vol; any mean-reverting vol model gives a floor.

Mechanism gap: the claim 'fast anti-persistent mean reversion means the long-run level dominates the multi-year average, arguing AGAINST vol compression' conflates two different things. Roughness (H<<0.5, jaggedness at all scales) is about the PATH texture and short-horizon forecast variance scaling, not about the LEVEL or trend of the long-run mean. Rough-vol is fully compatible with a long-run vol level that DECLINES over a decade (e.g. via institutionalization); H says nothing about whether the unconditional level itself drifts down. So rough-vol does not actually rule out the CF-Benchmarks compression thesis - that thesis is about the long-run LEVEL falling, which is orthogonal to roughness. This is the most substantive analytical overstatement.
verdict.corrections: ["Reframe the central pro: rough-vol does NOT 'argue against vol compression.' Roughness (small H) governs path texture and the Delta^{2H} scaling of short-horizon forecast variance - it is silent on whether the long-run unconditional vol LEVEL drifts down over 10-15yr. The CF-Benchmarks compression thesis is a claim about the long-run level falling (via institutionalization/liquidity), which is orthogonal to H. So rough-vol cannot adjudicate the vol-floor-vs-compression debate; only a mean-reversion model with an assumed long-run level can, and that long-run level is an IMPORTED assumption, not a rough-vol output. The doc currently credits rough-vol with supporting the floor; it should credit only generic mean-reversion + a separately-justified long-run-level assumption.", "Soften 'the one cell it genuinely informs.' Given the doc endorses 2507.00575's conclusion that rough-vol is 'structurally misaligned with the empirical features of Bitcoin volatility' AND Cont-Das that the H<0.5 finding is a microstructure artifact, the honest net is that rough-vol's contribution to the BTC CMA is close to nil even for volatility - it is at most a weak prior for 'vol is mean-reverting, not trending to zero,' a conclusion obtainable from far simpler/uncontested models (HAR, GARCH). State this net explicitly rather than calling vol 'the one cell it genuinely informs.'", "Flag the H0=0.1262-0.1379 band and the H(Delta)=H0*n/(n+a), a~3 ansatz as body-extracted from arXiv:2511.03314 (not abstract-confirmed in my check); keep them but mark provenance. The 1% 5-min RV error and H<1/2 direction ARE abstract-confirmed.", "Reconcile the 55-60% pick vs realized 57% (5y) / 69% (10y): either (a) justify the mild downward path explicitly via maturation/institutionalization (which then concedes the long-run level CAN fall, weakening the anti-compression framing), or (b) raise the band toward the 10y 69% if the thesis is truly 'long-run level dominates.' As written the number leans on the recent low while the prose argues the opposite.", "Standardize the Gatheral citation year (journal 2018 vs arXiv 2014); keep 2018 but note the link is the 2014 preprint."]
overstated_pros: 'Provides theoretical support for a high, mean-reverting vol FLOOR / argues against compression' - overstated. H governs path roughness and short-horizon forecast-variance scaling, NOT the level or secular trend of the long-run mean. Rough-vol is fully compatible with a declining long-run vol level, so it does not actually argue against the CF-Benchmarks compression thesis. The anti-compression conclusion comes from an imported long-run-level assumption, not from roughness.

'The one CMA cell it genuinely informs (volatility)' - overstated given the doc's own cited rejections (2507.00575 'structurally misaligned'; Cont-Das 'artifact'). If those critiques are taken seriously (and the doc endorses them), rough-vol informs essentially nothing for BTC beyond a generic mean-reversion prior available from simpler uncontested models.

'RFSV forecast empirically beats AR/HAR' is true in the Gatheral equity setting but is presented as a pro FOR THE BTC CMA; the BTC-specific evidence (2507.00575) says the roughness index is not even estimable for Bitcoin, so the forecast-skill pro does not transfer cleanly to BTC and is mildly overstated in this context.
missing_cons: Roughness is orthogonal to the long-run vol LEVEL: even taken at face value, rough-vol cannot distinguish a 28% terminal-vol world from a 60% one - it constrains path texture, not the unconditional level. This is the single most important limitation for CMA use and is not stated; the doc instead (incorrectly) claims rough-vol supports the high floor.

No out-of-sample multi-horizon validation cited for BTC: rough-vol's forecast edge is documented at short horizons (days/weeks) in equities; there is no evidence it improves 10-15yr average-vol estimation for any asset, let alone BTC. The horizon mismatch (short-dated vol-surface tool vs decade CMA) is under-emphasized.

Survivorship/maturation of the BTC vol series itself: the realized 10y 69% -> 5y 57% decline suggests a non-stationary vol level (regime change with institutionalization), which directly undermines the 'single unconditional long-run level' assumption rough-vol/RFSV needs - a stronger structural objection than the multifractality point already listed, and not separately called out.

The crypto-jumps source ('Cryptos have rough volatility and correlated jumps', Krain/Zuo/Haerdle) implies JUMPS are a first-order feature of BTC vol; a pure rough-vol (continuous fBm) model omits jumps, so even the second-moment characterization is incomplete without a jump component - the doc mentions jumps in passing but does not list 'ignores jumps' as a con of the rough-vol building block.

new_approaches.name: Agent-Based / Sociophysics Generative Market (Chartist-Fundamentalist, Percolation, Ising/SOC)
new_approaches.description: A bottom-up, generative family in which the macro return distribution — fat tails, volatility clustering, and crashes — EMERGES from interacting heterogeneous micro-agents rather than being fitted by a reduced-form equation. It is the opposite epistemology to the other 20 BTC-CMA approaches: instead of regressing price on a driver (S2F, M2, addresses) it simulates many traders (random/noise traders, chartists/trend-followers, fundamentalists) on an order book — or binary opinion 'spins' on a lattice/network (Ising/Bornholdt/Sznajd) — or percolation clusters of co-trading herds (Cont-Bouchaud) — or a self-organized-critical (SOC) sandpile of avalanching liquidations (Bak-Tang-Wiesenfeld), and reads the emergent price path. A single control parameter — social coupling strength, per-cluster trade probability near the percolation threshold p_c, or an Ising 'temperature' — tunes the system toward criticality, where power-law tails and bubble/crash onset appear endogenously. Crucially these models are calibrated to reproduce the SHAPE of the return distribution (higher moments: vol level, excess kurtosis, tail exponent, vol-clustering autocorrelation), NOT the drift. They generate no native long-horizon expected-return forecast. For a 10-15yr BTC CMA they are therefore a vol/tail/crash-structure engine — informing the realistic ~50-60% vol floor, the heavy left tail, and crash hazard — while being essentially silent on appreciation and on cross-asset correlations (single-asset, closed-economy simulations).
new_approaches.medium_explanation: This family asks the opposite question from every reduced-form BTC model: not "what equation fits price?" but "what minimal set of interacting agents makes the real return distribution appear by itself?" You simulate noise traders, chartists, and fundamentalists on an order book (Cocco-Marchesi for Bitcoin), or binary buy/sell 'spins' coupled locally and to global sentiment (Bornholdt's Ising market), or random percolation clusters of agents who trade as a herd (Cont-Bouchaud), and the macro stylized facts — truncated power-law tails (cumulative exponent ~2.9-3, the empirical "inverse-cubic" range), volatility clustering, and crashes — emerge endogenously. A single control parameter (social-coupling strength, per-cluster trade probability near the percolation threshold, or Ising temperature) tunes the system toward criticality, where bubbles and crashes self-organize. For a BTC CMA the key implication is humbling: these models target the distribution's higher moments (vol, kurtosis, tail, crash hazard), not its drift. They robustly justify a high vol floor and a fat left tail, but produce no native appreciation number and, being single-asset, no cross-asset correlations.
key_drivers: Social-coupling / herding strength — the master control parameter (Ising coupling J, Cont-Bouchaud cluster trade probability a, sentiment-feedback gain) that tunes proximity to a critical point where power-law tails and crashes emerge

Agent-type mix and switching: relative populations of random/noise traders, chartists (trend-followers/momentum) and fundamentalists, and the endogenous switching between them that drives alternating-dominance cycles, bubbles and reversals
Network/lattice topology of who-influences-whom (regular lattice, scale-free, random percolation graph) — sets cluster-size distribution and how herds form

Proximity to the percolation threshold p_c / critical temperature T_c — the order parameter governing whether the market is in a disordered (Gaussian-ish) or ordered (herded, fat-tailed, crash-prone) phase
Self-organized-criticality feedback (margin calls / forced liquidations / leverage avalanches) that drives the system back to the critical state, producing scale-invariant avalanche (drawdown) sizes
Order-book / market-clearing microstructure and finite agent wealth/inventory constraints, which truncate the power law and shape realized volatility
Exogenous supply schedule (issuance/mining) entered only as a slow drift in coin count — NOT as a fitted appreciation driver
pros: Only family in the set that DERIVES BTC's stylized facts endogenously — fat tails, volatility clustering, and crashes fall out of micro-interaction rather than being assumed or curve-fit, giving a genuine mechanism for the ~50-60% vol floor and heavy left tail a CMA needs

Provides a principled, mechanistic account of crash/bubble hazard via a tunable criticality parameter — directly relevant to sizing the drawdown risk a 10-15yr BTC holder must survive, which most reduced-form models ignore

Cocco-Marchesi (2017) demonstrably reproduces real Bitcoin statistical properties (autocorrelation of absolute returns, the return CDF) from a simple two-agent design — a real, peer-reviewed validation on BTC specifically, not just equities

Falsifiable on distributional grounds: the emergent tail exponent, vol-clustering decay, and crash-size distribution can be checked against realized BTC data (Cont-Bouchaud cumulative tail ~2.9-3 matches the empirical inverse-cubic law)
Naturally accommodates regime change / structural breaks (ETF entry, leverage build-up) by changing agent populations or coupling — more flexible than a single fixed regression coefficient
cons: Silent on appreciation — the CMA's single most important cell. These models target the return-distribution SHAPE (higher moments), not the drift; Cocco-Marchesi enters supply growth but does not output an expected-return path. Any 10-15yr appreciation number is bolted on from outside the framework.

Silent on cross-asset correlations — they are single-asset, closed-economy simulations of one order book / one lattice, so they say nothing about BTC vs growth equities, value, nominal FI, TIPS or gold. All correlation cells are n/a.

Severe calibration/identification problem: many free parameters (agent counts, coupling, switching rates, network topology) map to the same handful of stylized facts, so the model is badly under-identified — multiple very different parameter sets reproduce the same fat tails. INET-Oxford/PLOS work flags the absence of reliable operational calibration and weak out-of-sample validation as the field's central methodological weakness.

Stylized-fact matching is necessary but not sufficient: reproducing fat tails and vol clustering does NOT validate a model's forward predictions; some literature finds even those facts are hard to recover robustly under calibration, and the models are routinely critiqued as flexible enough to be near-unfalsifiable on dynamics.

Essentially never used to produce on-record multi-year BTC price/return forecasts — the family is explanatory/generative, not a desk forecasting tool. Repurposing it as a CMA point estimate is a category error.

Criticality/SOC claims for markets are contested: 'scale-invariant avalanche' findings are sensitive to estimation choices and have been challenged (the general critique that financial criticality is partly a fitting artifact), so the crash-hazard mechanism, while suggestive, is not settled science.

cited_outputs.appreciation_nominal: n/a (source silent) — the family models the return-distribution SHAPE, not the drift. Cocco-Marchesi grows BTC supply at the real issuance rate but does not output an appreciation forecast; no ABM/sociophysics BTC paper publishes a multi-year expected-return figure.
cited_outputs.appreciation_real: n/a (source silent — nominal price path is itself not a forecast output; no inflation treatment)
cited_outputs.volatility: Not published as an annualized % CMA input, but volatility level and (critically) volatility CLUSTERING are core emergent outputs — Bornholdt and Cont-Bouchaud both produce clustered volatility endogenously; Cocco-Marchesi reproduces the autocorrelation of BTC absolute returns. The models reproduce, rather than predict, realized BTC vol.
cited_outputs.corr_growth_eq: n/a (source silent — single-asset simulation)
cited_outputs.corr_gold: n/a (source silent — single-asset simulation; no digital-gold/cross-asset axis modeled)
cited_outputs.notes: Distributional outputs ARE published: Cont-Bouchaud produces an exponentially-truncated power-law return tail with cumulative exponent ~2.9-3 (matching the empirical 'inverse-cubic law'), tuned by per-cluster trade probability near the percolation threshold p_c. Bornholdt's Ising/spin market reproduces power-law-distributed returns and clustered volatility from local+global frustrated coupling. Bak-Tang-Wiesenfeld SOC yields power-law avalanche (drawdown) sizes. Cocco-Marchesi (2017/2019) reproduces BTC's absolute-return autocorrelation and return CDF. None of these are appreciation or correlation forecasts.

synthesized_outputs.appreciation_nominal: ~8-12%/yr (JUDGMENT — imported, not a model output). The framework is silent on drift, so I anchor to the cross-approach central and BTC's realized appreciation DECAY (full 142% -> 10y 65% -> 5y 17%/yr): a maturing asset whose excess return compresses toward a monetary-debasement-plus-residual-adoption pace. The ABM contribution is to insist this mean sits atop a heavy-tailed, crash-prone distribution, so the MEDIAN realized 10-15yr return is likely well below the mean.
synthesized_outputs.appreciation_real: ~5-9%/yr real (subtract ~2.5-3% long-run US inflation). Judgment, consistent with the honest cross-approach band; the family adds no scarcity tailwind of its own.
synthesized_outputs.volatility: ~55-60%/yr (JUDGMENT, but the cell this family most legitimately informs). Generative models endogenously produce fat tails and persistent volatility clustering, which argues AGAINST clean compression to equity-like vol: the critical/herding dynamics that drive BTC's vol do not switch off as the asset matures. I hold the floor AT realized trailing-5y ~57% with a decade band of ~50-60%, and flag that the left tail / crash hazard is fatter than a lognormal CMA assumes.
synthesized_outputs.corr_growth_eq: +0.40 to +0.55 (JUDGMENT — framework silent, single-asset). Anchored to realized trailing-5y 0.56; rising as BTC institutionalizes into risk-asset portfolios. An ABM with shared liquidity/sentiment coupling across markets would predict positive co-movement in herding/crash regimes specifically.
synthesized_outputs.corr_value_eq: +0.25 to +0.40 (JUDGMENT; realized 5y 0.37). Lower than growth equities.
synthesized_outputs.corr_fi_nominal: +0.10 to +0.25 (JUDGMENT; realized 5y 0.19). Mild positive via shared liquidity/discount-rate sensitivity; not a duration asset.
synthesized_outputs.corr_tips: +0.20 to +0.30 (JUDGMENT; realized 5y 0.30). Modest real-rate/liquidity sensitivity.
synthesized_outputs.corr_gold: ~0.0-0.15 (JUDGMENT). The family provides NO mechanism forcing gold co-movement (single-asset), and realized BTC-gold correlation is ~0 (full -0.01, 5y +0.04). I hold the bottom of the band and explicitly reject any digital-gold linkage — nothing in a generative micro-model implies it. The one nuance: in synchronized cross-market herding/de-risking events, BTC and gold could briefly co-move via shared sentiment, but this is episodic, not a structural correlation.
synthesized_outputs.notes: This family's honest CMA role is to supply the VOL FLOOR, FAT LEFT TAIL and CRASH-HAZARD assumptions — not the central appreciation or correlation numbers, which are imported. Key cross-cutting caveat: it is the only approach that mechanistically justifies refusing to compress BTC vol toward equity levels (herding/criticality dynamics persist through maturation), and it implies the median 10-15yr outcome materially trails the mean because of the heavy left tail / crash mass that a lognormal CMA understates.

new_approaches.rich_notes:
EPISTEMOLOGY (why this is genuinely distinct). The other 20 BTC-CMA approaches are reduced-form: they posit a driver (stock-to-flow, M2, active addresses, mining cost, time-since-genesis, an option surface) and fit price to it. This family inverts the logic. It specifies the MICRO rules of heterogeneous interacting agents and lets the MACRO return distribution — fat tails, volatility clustering, bubbles, crashes — emerge as a collective phenomenon. None of the reduced-form models derive the stylized facts; here they are the output. The unifying thread across the four canonical lineages is a tunable social-coupling control parameter that pushes the system toward a critical point, at which power-law tails and crash onset appear endogenously.

THE FOUR LINEAGES. (1) Order-book ABM — Cocco, Concas & Marchesi (2017, J. Econ. Interaction & Coordination), the first ABM built specifically for Bitcoin: random traders + chartists on an order book, supply growing at the real issuance rate. It reproduces BTC's autocorrelation of absolute returns and the return CDF. The 2019 IEEE Access extension adds mining and a fundamentalist class. (2) Percolation/herd — Cont & Bouchaud (2000, Macroeconomic Dynamics): random communication clusters of agents trade together; at/near the percolation threshold p_c the return distribution becomes an exponentially-truncated power law with cumulative tail exponent ~2.9-3, squarely in the empirical 'inverse-cubic' range, with the per-cluster trade probability a as control knob. (3) Ising/spin opinion dynamics — Bornholdt (2001, IJMPC): binary buy/sell spins with ferromagnetic local coupling FRUSTRATED against an anti-ferromagnetic coupling to global magnetization; this frustration produces metastable states, intermittency, power-law returns and clustered volatility. Sznajd and scale-free-network variants extend it. (4) Self-organized criticality — Bak, Tang & Wiesenfeld (1987, PRL): the sandpile that self-tunes to a critical state emitting power-law avalanches; applied to markets, leverage/margin-call cascades give scale-invariant drawdown sizes.

WHAT IT DELIVERS FOR A BTC CMA — AND WHAT IT DOES NOT. The honest, load-bearing point: this family is a DISTRIBUTION-SHAPE engine, not a drift engine. It legitimately informs the higher moments a CMA needs — a high, persistent volatility (vol clustering does not switch off with maturity), a fat LEFT tail, and an explicit crash/bubble hazard mechanism via criticality. It is the best mechanistic justification in the whole survey for refusing to compress BTC vol to equity-like levels and for treating the median 10-15yr outcome as well below the mean. But it is SILENT on appreciation (Cocco-Marchesi enters supply growth without forecasting return) and, being single-asset closed-economy simulations, SILENT on every cross-asset correlation. So appreciation (~8-12% nominal / 5-9% real) and correlations are imported from the realized-decay baseline and cross-approach central, NOT derived here.

FAILURE MODES / SKEPTICAL READ. Calibration and identification are the Achilles heel: many free parameters (agent counts, coupling strength, switching rates, topology) collapse onto the same few stylized facts, so the models are badly under-identified — wildly different parameter sets reproduce the same tails. The INET-Oxford calibration-methods survey and the PLOS One 'Calibrating emergent phenomena' work both flag the absence of reliable operational calibration and weak out-of-sample validation as the field's defining weakness; some find even fat tails / sufficient kurtosis hard to recover robustly under calibration. Reproducing stylized facts is necessary but not sufficient — it does not validate forward dynamics, and critics reasonably call the family near-unfalsifiable on dynamics. The SOC/criticality-in-markets claim is itself contested ('scale-invariant avalanche' findings are estimation-sensitive and have been challenged as partly artifactual). ON-RECORD MULTI-YEAR FORECASTS: essentially NONE. Unlike S2F ($288k-$500k+), Metcalfe ($1.5M/2035) or power-law-time ($1M/2037), the ABM/sociophysics literature does not publish dated multi-year BTC price targets — it is explanatory/generative, not a forecasting desk. That absence is itself the verdict: this family belongs in a BTC CMA as the source of the vol floor, fat-tail, and crash-hazard assumptions, NOT as the source of the central appreciation or correlation numbers.

verdict.corrections:
["Fix representative source #6 author to 'Lucas Fievet, Didier Sornette' (ETH Zurich), PLOS One 2018, DOI 10.1371/journal.pone.0193290. Remove 'Donald Robertson / Platt & Gebbie lineage.'",
"Add the INET-Oxford calibration survey as a SEPARATE source where rich_notes invokes it: Donovan Platt, 'A Comparison of Economic Agent-Based Model Calibration Methods,' arXiv 1902.05938, J. Economic Dynamics & Control 113 (2020). Do not merge it with the Fievet-Sornette PLOS One paper.",
"State Cont-Bouchaud as 'arXiv 1997 / Macroeconomic Dynamics 2000' so the year on the arXiv link (1997) and the journal year (2000) are not silently contradictory.",
"Where the inverse-cubic law is mentioned, attribute the empirical law itself to Gopikrishnan et al. / Gabaix-Plerou-Stanley, keeping Cont-Bouchaud as the model that reproduces it.",
"Soften pro #4 from 'matches' to 'is broadly consistent with (in some calibrations)' to avoid implying the ~2.9 exponent is a robust, calibration-independent output — consistent with the doc's own under-identification con."]
overstated_pros: Pro #4 ('Cont-Bouchaud cumulative tail ~2.9-3 matches the empirical inverse-cubic law') overstates robustness — the exponent is calibration/finite-size sensitive, not an invariant; it should read 'broadly consistent in some specifications.'

Pro #3 ('Cocco-Marchesi demonstrably reproduces real Bitcoin statistical properties... a real peer-reviewed validation on BTC specifically') is fair but slightly oversells. The 2017 J. Econ. Interaction & Coordination paper reproduces autocorrelation of absolute returns and the return CDF shape from a Random-Trader + Chartist design; it is a qualitative stylized-fact match, not a quantitative fit to BTC's actual tail exponent or vol level, and the model long predates the current BTC regime (ETF era). 'Demonstrably reproduces' should be 'qualitatively reproduces select stylized facts of early-era Bitcoin.'

Pro #2's 'principled, mechanistic account of crash/bubble hazard via a tunable criticality parameter' rests on the SOC-in-markets claim, which the doc itself (correctly) lists as contested in con #6. So the pro is somewhat self-undercut: the mechanism is suggestive, not established. The doc is internally honest about this, but the pro as worded reads stronger than the con allows.
missing_cons: No-drift is not just 'silent on appreciation' — it is a hard ceiling on usefulness for a CMA whose single most important cell IS appreciation. The doc flags this, but does not state the corollary: the synthesized 8-12% nominal / 5-9% real numbers carry ZERO information content from this family; they are 100% imported from the realized-decay baseline. So this approach's marginal contribution to the CMA's central estimate is literally nil — it only colors the distribution around a number it cannot produce. That is a stronger indictment than 'bolted on from outside.'

Stationarity / regime-transfer problem specific to BTC is missing. Cocco-Marchesi was calibrated to pre-2017 Bitcoin (thin, retail-dominated, no derivatives, no ETF, no institutional market-makers). The microstructure that generated those stylized facts has been structurally replaced (CME futures, spot ETFs, perp-swap basis, MM inventory). Using a 2017-era ABM to justify a 2026-2041 vol floor assumes the generative micro-rules are invariant across exactly the regime change the doc elsewhere says ABMs 'naturally accommodate.' That is an unargued assumption, and it cuts against the vol-floor claim (institutionalization historically compresses vol).

The realized vol-decay trend itself argues against a hard 50-60% floor. The doc cites 103% (full) -> 69% (10y) -> 57% (5y) vol but then asserts the floor sits at the latest 57% reading with no compression. A monotone-declining series is weak evidence for a floor; it is at least as consistent with continued decay toward 40-45%. The ABM 'criticality persists' argument is asserted, not demonstrated, and is exactly the kind of unfalsifiable-on-dynamics claim con #4 warns about — applied here it would caution AGAINST confidence in the floor.

Survivorship / single-realization caveat absent. These models are stochastic and produce wildly dispersed paths; reading 'the' emergent vol or tail off them requires ensemble averaging, and the realized BTC series is a single draw. The doc treats realized 57% as if it pins the model, but a generative model with fat tails is consistent with a very wide range of realized 5y vols — so the empirical anchor under-constrains the model far more than the doc implies.

new_approaches.name: Information-Entropy / Complexity-Plane Efficiency Valuation
new_approaches.description: A model-free, information-theoretic family that measures the residual exploitable structure (predictable, non-random pattern) in Bitcoin's price series using ordinal/symbolic measures — Bandt-Pompe permutation entropy, statistical (Jensen-Shannon) complexity, and their joint position on the complexity-entropy causality plane (CECP), plus approximate/Shannon entropy of intraday returns. An efficient, unforecastable series sits at the random-walk corner: normalized permutation entropy H→1 and statistical complexity C→0; deviations from that corner quantify inefficiency (exploitable memory/arbitrage). The empirical core finding is a SECULAR DRIFT of Bitcoin toward that corner: it was strongly inefficient in 2010-2014, and by 2021-2024 sits near maximum efficiency (Sigaki et al. 2019; Cryptocurrency Binary CECP 2025 report BTC H≈0.983, C≈0.036, inefficiency score ≈0.040 — 4th most efficient of 47 coins). This is used NOT to produce a price level but as a direct MATURATION argument: as exploitable structure vanishes, the excess return that compensated early arbitrage/risk premium compresses — i.e., appreciation decays. A second, orthogonal channel (Pele & Mazurencu-Marinescu-Pele 2019) uses the entropy of the intraday return distribution as a high-frequency predictor of daily Value-at-Risk: low entropy (ordered, one-sided days) forecasts fatter left tails. A 10-15yr CMA does not fall out mechanically; it is built by reading the efficiency drift as evidence that the alpha/risk-premium term must keep shrinking, while the VaR channel pins the (still-high, slowly-falling) volatility/tail regime.
new_approaches.medium_explanation: This approach treats Bitcoin's price series purely as information and asks: how much exploitable, non-random structure remains? Using permutation entropy and statistical complexity, it places BTC on the complexity-entropy plane, where a perfectly efficient (unpredictable) asset sits at the random-walk corner — entropy ≈1, complexity ≈0. The signature empirical result is a secular drift: BTC was highly inefficient in its early years and by 2021-2024 sits essentially AT the efficient corner (H≈0.98, C≈0.04). The CMA logic is maturation: the abnormal early returns compensated exploitable inefficiency/arbitrage and a thin-market risk premium; as that structure disappears, the excess-return term must compress toward whatever pure risk premium survives. This directly endorses appreciation DECAY (the realized 142%→65%→17% path) rather than its level. Separately, intraday-return entropy forecasts daily VaR: low-entropy, one-sided days predict fatter left tails, anchoring a high but slowly-falling volatility view. The method produces no price target and is silent on cross-asset correlations.
key_drivers: Normalized permutation (Bandt-Pompe) entropy of ordinal patterns in the return series — proximity to 1 measures randomness/efficiency
Statistical (Jensen-Shannon) complexity — distance from 0 measures residual exploitable structure; jointly defines position on the complexity-entropy causality plane
Secular drift toward the random-walk corner as the maturation signal (BTC 2010-2014 inefficient → 2021-2024 H≈0.98, C≈0.04)
Asset age and market capitalization / liquidity / institutional participation as the empirical drivers of rising efficiency (2023 7000-coin study)
Intraday log-return distribution entropy (Shannon, via symbolic time-series analysis) as a high-frequency predictor of daily Value-at-Risk and left-tail risk
Embedding dimension and time-window length (sliding window, e.g. 500-day) — tunable parameters that set the timescale at which 'efficiency' is judged
Compression of the alpha/excess-return term as exploitable structure vanishes (the CMA bridge, not a native model output)
pros: Model-free and assumption-light: requires no functional form (no power law, no cointegration, no DCF), only ordinal pattern counting — sidesteps the spurious-regression trap that sinks S2F/Metcalfe/M2 (those regress non-stationary trends; permutation entropy reads stationary ordinal structure)

Orthogonal information content: measures disorder of ordinal patterns, not fluctuation scaling (distinct from the Hurst/fractal family) — adds a genuinely independent maturation lens to a CMA committee

Empirically robust and peer-reviewed: the rising-efficiency / 'coming-of-age' finding replicates across Sigaki et al. (2019, >400 coins), the 2025 binary-CECP study (47 coins), and a 2023 >7000-coin study — all agree BTC has drifted to near the efficient corner

Directly supports appreciation DECAY on first principles: an asset approaching the random-walk corner cannot sustain large abnormal returns, which is exactly the realized 142%→65%→17% pattern a credible forward CMA must extrapolate

The Pele entropy-VaR channel is genuinely useful and validated: the entropy-AR model was the ONLY VaR spec to pass all three Christoffersen backtests at 99%, beating Normal-GARCH, t-GARCH and historical sim — a real, falsifiable risk-forecasting contribution
Cheap, transparent, refreshable from public price data; tunable timescale via embedding dimension and window length
cons: Produces NO price level and NO native expected return — efficiency is a property of the residual, not a valuation. Any appreciation number is an external bridge ('efficient ⇒ premium compresses'), not a model output; the framework cannot tell you WHAT the surviving risk premium is, only that exploitable structure is gone

Silent on cross-asset correlations entirely — permutation entropy is univariate (single-series ordinal patterns); it offers zero mechanism for BTC-vs-equities/FI/TIPS/gold co-movement, so every correlation cell must be borrowed from realized data

Efficiency ≠ low risk: a series can be perfectly random-walk-like (H≈1, C≈0) AND extremely volatile with fat tails. Reaching the efficient corner says nothing about vol falling — BTC sits at the corner yet still realizes ~57% vol. Conflating 'efficient' with 'mature/safe' is a category error the maturation narrative invites

Window/embedding sensitivity: the verdict on whether a period is 'efficient' depends on the chosen window length, embedding dimension and timescale; the same series flips between efficient and inefficient across reasonable parameter choices — and on-record studies disagree on which sub-periods were efficient

Survivorship and single-path: like all BTC fits it reads the one realized history; near-corner efficiency today is partly a consequence of the very institutionalization that could also break (it cannot price catastrophic-failure tail mass)

The maturation-⇒-decay link is qualitatively right but quantitatively unpinned: the literature never states how much premium compression corresponds to a given efficiency gain, so the CMA must impute the magnitude entirely from realized decay — the entropy framework only confirms the SIGN

new_approaches.rich_notes:
METHODOLOGY. The family rests on three information-theoretic objects. (1) Bandt-Pompe permutation entropy: map overlapping windows of the return series to ordinal patterns (which of d! orderings the d consecutive values take), build the pattern-frequency distribution, and compute its normalized Shannon entropy H. A random walk visits all orderings equally → H→1; structured/predictable series have 'forbidden' or rare patterns → H<1. (2) Statistical (Jensen-Shannon / Lopez-Ruiz-Mancini-Calbet) complexity C: a disequilibrium measure that is zero both for perfect order AND perfect disorder, peaking for structured-but-not-trivial series. The pair (H,C) defines the complexity-entropy causality plane (CECP); the efficient-market corner is (H≈1, C≈0). (3) Symbolic Shannon entropy of the intraday return distribution (Pele 2019), computed by binarizing minute returns (1=down, 0=up) and taking St = -p·log2(p) - (1-p)·log2(1-p).

KEY RELATIONSHIPS / HISTORICAL FIT. The load-bearing empirical fact is a SECULAR DRIFT of Bitcoin toward the efficient corner. Sigaki, Perc & Ribeiro (2019, Scientific Reports, >400 coins, ~April-2013 start, 500-day sliding window) frame this as the market's 'coming-of-age': inefficient in 2010-2014, progressively random-walk-like thereafter; 37% of coins efficient >80% of the time, 20% efficient <20%, and efficiency NOT correlated with market cap cross-sectionally (younger coins 'follow their elders'). The 2025 binary-CECP arXiv study (47 coins, Aug-2021–Nov-2024) puts BTC at H≈0.983, C≈0.036, inefficiency ℐ≈0.040, ranking it 4th-most-efficient of 47 — 'within the top tier,' near the theoretical (1,0) point. A 2023 >7000-coin study confirms asset age AND market cap significantly raise efficiency over time. So three independent peer-reviewed/working studies agree on the direction and on BTC's current near-corner position. The Pele (2019) VaR channel adds a within-the-residual risk result: entropy of intraday returns is a strong, negative, significant predictor of return quantiles (coef ≈ -0.190 at 1%, -0.163 at 5%; logprice~entropy R²≈0.868), and the entropy-AR VaR model was the ONLY specification to pass all three Christoffersen tests at 99% confidence, beating Normal-GARCH, t-GARCH, and historical simulation. That is a genuine, falsifiable, validated contribution to BTC tail-risk forecasting.

CMA BRIDGE (why this maps to appreciation decay). The framework yields no price. The economic argument is: abnormal early BTC returns compensated (a) exploitable serial structure / arbitrage in a thin, immature market and (b) a large illiquidity/novelty risk premium. As permutation entropy → 1 and complexity → 0, channel (a) is mechanically exhausted — there is no longer exploitable memory to harvest — so the excess-return term must compress toward whatever pure, non-arbitrageable risk premium survives. This is a FIRST-PRINCIPLES endorsement of the realized appreciation decay (142%→65%→17%/yr across full/10y/5y windows) and a clean refutation of constant-return models (S2F's ~78%/yr-forever, naive power-law) that ignore the efficiency drift. It does NOT tell you the magnitude of the surviving premium — that must be imputed from the realized decay path — so I synthesize ~8-12% nominal / 5-9% real, sitting below the trailing-5y 17% as decay continues.

FAILURE MODES / SKEPTICISM. The sharpest critique: efficiency is NOT safety. A series at (H≈1, C≈0) is unforecastable but can be wildly volatile and fat-tailed — and BTC is exactly that (near-corner efficiency, ~57% realized vol). Anyone who reads 'mature/efficient' as 'vol converges to equities/gold' commits a category error; I therefore hold vol at the realized ~57% floor, not a step-down. Second, the framework is univariate and silent on every correlation cell — no digital-gold axis, no equity beta — so the cross-asset CMA is entirely borrowed from realized data (the honest upside: it never ASSERTS a gold linkage, so unlike S2F/gold-parity there is no internal contradiction to expose). Third, window/embedding-dimension sensitivity makes the efficient/inefficient verdict parameter-dependent, and on-record studies already disagree on which sub-periods qualified as efficient. Fourth, the maturation reading is reflexive: near-corner efficiency today is partly produced by the institutionalization/ETF flows that could also reverse, and the single realized path cannot price catastrophic-failure tail mass.

ON-RECORD MULTI-YEAR FORECASTS. None. This is the defining honest limitation: no paper in the entropy-complexity family publishes a multi-year BTC price or return forecast — every output is either a descriptive efficiency score (Sigaki; 2025 CECP) or a short-horizon risk/VaR forecast (Pele). The family's value to a 10-15yr CMA is therefore as a CORROBORATING MATURATION LENS — it independently confirms the SIGN of appreciation decay and supplies a validated tail-risk channel — not as a standalone return generator. It belongs in a committee alongside a level/anchor model, never as the sole input.

new_approaches.name: Generalized-Metcalfe x Logistic-Saturation Fundamental Support (Wheatley-Sornette)
new_approaches.description: Values Bitcoin as a network whose FUNDAMENTAL (non-bubble) support value scales with an EMPIRICALLY-ESTIMATED, sub-quadratic Metcalfe exponent applied to active users, where the user base itself follows a saturating S-curve (logistic in Wheatley-Sornette, Gompertz in Peterson) toward a finite carrying capacity. Wheatley, Sornette et al. (2019) fit ln(market cap) = alpha + beta*ln(users) on 2,782 daily values (Jul-2010 to Feb-2018), obtaining beta = 1.69 (s.e. 0.0076), alpha = 1.51 (0.087), R-squared = 0.95, and decisively REJECT the classic n^2 Metcalfe exponent (forcing beta=2 is significantly worse; ANOVA p < 1e-16). Users are modeled as ln(u) = a - b*e^(-c*t^d), projecting growth decelerating from ~35% to ~21% over five years (0.79M users in 2018 to ~2.60M by 2023). Crucially, this combination pins a BOUNDED terminal fundamental value with endogenous appreciation decay as users approach the ceiling -- distinct from the relative-valuation Metcalfe row (which applies an ad-hoc exponent to an unconstrained user series as an over/under-valuation gauge) and from LPPLS (#18), which only treats this fundamental as the baseline a bubble departs from. The fundamental support is explicitly NOT a return forecaster in the authors' hands: they use it to flag four bubbles that exceeded fundamental value and warn long-term predictions are 'effectively meaningless.' A 10-15yr CMA must be reconstructed: forecast saturating user growth, apply the 1.69 exponent, divide by near-fixed supply, and annualize -- which mechanically yields a decaying, finite-terminal appreciation path.
new_approaches.medium_explanation: Wheatley-Sornette regress log market cap on log active users and let the data choose the exponent: beta = 1.69, not Metcalfe's n^2 (forcing beta=2 is rejected at p < 1e-16, R-squared = 0.95). The novel binding is to a SATURATING user model, ln(u) = a - b*e^(-c*t^d), where growth decays (~35% to ~21% over five years) toward a finite carrying capacity. Combining a sub-quadratic exponent with a ceiling on users produces a FINITE terminal fundamental value and endogenous appreciation decay -- the per-user multiple and the user-growth rate both compress as the network matures. In 2018 the fitted support was just 22-44B vs a 170B market cap, flagging ~4x overvaluation; the authors used it to detect four bubbles and (validated out-of-sample) to call the early-2019 bottom near the predicted 40-80B band. For a 10-15yr BTC CMA the mechanism forces appreciation toward saturating user growth times a shrinking multiple -- low-double-digit at most -- but the authors stress carrying-capacity estimates span four orders of magnitude beyond sample, so long-horizon point forecasts are, in their words, 'effectively meaningless.'
key_drivers: Number of active users / non-dormant addresses (network size n), the sole fundamental input
Empirically-estimated Metcalfe exponent beta = 1.69 (sub-quadratic; n^2 statistically rejected, p<1e-16), implying each user connects to ~n^(2/3) others
Logistic/Gompertz user-saturation curve ln(u)=a-b*e^(-c*t^d) with a finite carrying capacity -- the feature that bounds terminal value
User growth-rate decay path (~35% -> ~21% over 5yr in the 2018 fit) driving endogenous appreciation deceleration
Near-fixed coin supply (21M cap, halving issuance) as denominator converting network value to price
Carrying-capacity (saturation ceiling) uncertainty -- spans ~4 orders of magnitude out of sample, dominating long-horizon uncertainty
Mean-reversion of price toward the Metcalfe support line, used to flag bubbles (the LPPLS overlay handles the bubble departures)
pros: Lets the DATA choose the exponent (1.69) rather than imposing n^2, and statistically rejects the naive quadratic law (p<1e-16) -- more honest than crypto-native Metcalfe variants

The saturating user curve produces a FINITE terminal fundamental value and built-in appreciation decay, the correct qualitative shape for a maturing-asset CMA (unlike S2F/power-law, which imply unbounded growth)

Genuine out-of-sample validation: the 2018 fundamental-support call (market cap to fall to 40-80B) was confirmed when BTC fell into the middle of that band in early 2019 -- a real ex-ante success, not just in-sample fit
Peer-reviewed (Royal Society Open Science), with full data deposited (Dryad), and the authors are unusually candid about model uncertainty and the limits of long-term prediction
Grounds value in an observable, hard-to-fake fundamental (on-chain users) and cleanly separates the slow fundamental from fast LPPLS bubble dynamics
cons: The authors THEMSELVES disclaim CMA use: carrying-capacity estimates differ by ~4 orders of magnitude beyond the sample and they call long-term predictions 'effectively meaningless' -- repurposing this as a 10-15yr return forecast is precisely the misuse they warn against

Likely spurious regression: log-price and log-users are non-stationary trending I(1) series; Civitarese (2018) finds they do NOT cointegrate and cannot reject reverse causality (price drives wallet creation, not the reverse), so the 0.95 R-squared may be a trend artifact

Active-user / address metrics are crude and increasingly broken: exchange/ETF/custodial adoption and L2 migration create economic value with ZERO new on-chain active addresses, severing the model's sole driver post-2021/2024

It is a fundamental-SUPPORT and bubble-detection tool, not a return model -- deriving appreciation requires bolting on a forward user-growth assumption the paper does not provide, and the practitioner extrapolations ($1M by 2028, $1.5M by 2035) launder a fragile in-sample fit into precise targets the econometrics cannot support
Tiny structural sample (one BTC history, ~4 bubble episodes) and post-2021 institutionalization regime break leave the exponent and carrying capacity unstable out of sample
Silent on volatility and on cross-asset correlations (growth/value equities, FI, TIPS, gold) -- all distributional CMA cells must be imported from realized data

METHODOLOGY. Two ingredients, bound together. (1) A GENERALIZED Metcalfe law: ln(p) = alpha + beta*ln(u) + epsilon, with p = market cap, u = active users. On 2,782 daily values (17-Jul-2010 to 26-Feb-2018) the fit is beta = 1.69 (s.e. 0.0076), alpha = 1.51 (0.087), R-squared = 0.95. The authors explicitly test and REJECT the classic quadratic Metcalfe exponent: 'Forcing the exponent beta to be equal to 2 would result in an intercept of -2.01 (0.018), but this regression is significantly worse,' with an ANOVA/F-test p-value 'less than 10^-16.' Economically, beta=1.69 implies each user connects on average to ~N^(2/3) others (for N=1M, ~10,000 links), a more realistic density than full pairwise n^2. (2) A SATURATING user-adoption curve: ln(u) = a - b*e^(-c*t^d) + epsilon, fit Jan-2012 to Feb-2018, projecting annual user growth to 'decrease over the next 5 years from 35 to 21%,' with users rising from ~0.79M (2018) to ~2.60M (2023). The combination is what makes this row distinct: a sub-quadratic exponent applied to a CEILINGED user base yields a FINITE terminal fundamental value with endogenous appreciation decay, whereas the existing Metcalfe row (#2) applies an ad-hoc exponent to an unconstrained series purely as a relative over/under-valuation gauge, and LPPLS (#18) merely uses such a fundamental as the baseline a bubble departs from.

KEY RELATIONSHIP / USE. The paper's actual deliverable is a fundamental SUPPORT value, not a return. As of Mar-2018 the OLS support was ~$44B (point fit), with alternative support lines at $22B and $33B, versus an actual market cap of $170B -- i.e. BTC was ~4x above fundamental. The model is then paired with the Log-Periodic Power Law Singularity (LPPLS) model: periods where price runs far above the Metcalfe support are the bubbles, and LPPLS brackets the crash time. Four bubbles were flagged with overvaluation factors: May-Aug 2012 (3.1x), Jan-Apr 2013 (20.4x), Oct-Nov 2013 (6.8x), and Jun-2015-Dec-2017 (103x).

HISTORICAL FIT / VALIDATION. This approach has a rare genuine out-of-sample success. In 2018 the authors predicted Bitcoin's market cap would 'fall several-fold from its peak, to a $40-80 Billion range'; in the 2019 follow-up Wheatley confirms 'the market cap indeed fell into the middle of the predicted range in the new year of 2019,' and by Apr-2019 they re-assessed BTC as 'still 2x overvalued' (down from '10x overvalued' at peak). That is an ex-ante fundamental call that worked -- materially stronger evidence than S2F, which failed catastrophically post-2021.

FAILURE MODES. (a) The authors disclaim long-horizon use: 'beyond the sample, differences explode such that there are 4 orders of magnitude difference between the predicted carrying capacities,' and 'precise inference based on a single model is misleading, and long-term predictions effectively meaningless... model uncertainty dominates uncertainty of estimated parameters.' Any 10-15yr CMA built on this is a reconstruction AGAINST the authors' warning. (b) Likely spurious regression: Civitarese (2018) tests price vs an adjusted wallet-connection series and finds they do NOT cointegrate, rejecting Metcalfe, and cannot reject reverse causality (returns drive new wallets). Both log-price and log-users are non-stationary I(1) trends, so the 0.95 R-squared may be a trend artifact. (c) Metric decay: ETF/custodial/treasury adoption and L2 migration add economic value with zero new on-chain active addresses, breaking the sole driver post-2021/2024.

ON-RECORD MULTI-YEAR FORECASTS PRODUCED THIS WAY. The academic paper deliberately publishes none beyond ~2023 user counts. The practitioner branch (Peterson, same generalized-Metcalfe-plus-Gompertz family, AIAR 2018) does: validated near-term calls of ~$3,500 EOY-2018 (actual $3,782) and ~$7,000 EOY-2019 (actual $7,243), then forward targets of >$500k by the ~2028 halving, ~$1M by March-2028 / ~450 days post-halving, and ~$1.5M by 2035 (~31%/yr off a ~$100k base). These laundered, precise long-horizon targets are exactly what the academic authors caution against; I anchor my synthesized ~9-13%/yr nominal to BTC's realized appreciation DECAY (142%->65%->17%) and the model's own saturating-user logic, not to the practitioner extrapolations. Distributional cells (vol ~55-60%, equity corr +0.35-0.50, gold corr ~0-0.10) are imported from realized data because the framework is silent on them.

issues: PETERSON EXPONENT MISATTRIBUTION (most material framing error). Multiple sources confirm Peterson's 'Metcalfe's Law as a Model for Bitcoin's Value' uses the CLASSIC n^2 quadratic law (value proportional to square of users) + a Gompertz curve, NOT the sub-quadratic 1.69 exponent. Wheatley-Sornette explicitly REJECT n^2 at p<1e-16. So Peterson's >$500k-by-2028 / $1M-post-halving / $1.5M-by-2035 targets are produced by the very quadratic model W-S statistically refuted. The deep-dive repeatedly binds them ('same generalized-Metcalfe-plus-Gompertz family,' 'launder a fragile in-sample fit the academic authors themselves disown') as if Peterson's targets descend from the 1.69 mechanism. They do not -- they descend from a DIFFERENT, mutually-contradictory model. This is the single biggest framing defect: the row treats two opposed exponent choices as one family.

VOLATILITY FLOOR CLAIM IS CONTRADICTED BY ETF-ERA DATA. The synthesized vol of '~55-60%/yr' is justified by 'floor held AT ~57%... sub-2yr ETF sample shows no compression below realized.' But current data shows the opposite: 1-year realized BTC vol has fallen BELOW 50%, 30-day below 40%, and has not exceeded 80% since the Jan-2024 ETF launch (Fidelity Digital Assets, Kaiko, iShares ~54% Jan-2025). The 'no compression' assertion is empirically wrong for the most recent regime; if anything realized vol is structurally compressing toward 40-55%. The 55-60% central case is defensible as a long-run blend but the stated rationale ('no compression') is false.

PETERSON FORECAST-ACCURACY CITATIONS VERIFY but are SELECTION-BIASED. The ~$3,500 (actual $3,782) EOY-2018 and ~$7,000 (actual $7,243) EOY-2019 calls check out exactly. But these are exactly the near-term calls promoters foreground; the same model implied $100k by Jan-2024 (BTC was ~$42k then), a large miss the row omits. Citing only the two hits as 'validated near-term calls' overstates the practitioner branch's reliability.

'GOMPERTZ in Peterson' vs 'LOGISTIC in Wheatley-Sornette' is stated correctly, but the row then merges them mechanically; the user-saturation functional forms differ AND the exponents differ, so 'same family' is doubly loose.
verdict.corrections: All ACADEMIC numbers verify exactly against the open-access paper (PMC6599809) and arXiv:1803.05663: beta=1.69 (s.e.0.0076), alpha=1.51 (0.087), R2=0.95, 2,782 daily obs Jul-17-2010 to Feb-26-2018; beta=2 rejected at p<1e-16 with forced-beta=2 intercept -2.01 (0.018); user growth decay 35%->21% over 5yr, 0.79M->2.60M; support $22B/$33B/$44B vs ~$170B mkt cap; four bubbles 3.1x/20.4x/6.8x/103x; predicted fall to $39-77B (rounded to $40-80B in the row) confirmed early-2019; 'effectively meaningless' and 'model uncertainty dominates' / orders-of-magnitude carrying-capacity quotes all verbatim-accurate. Civitarese (2018) non-cointegration + reverse-causality finding verifies. Peterson EOY-2018 ($3,500 vs $3,782) and EOY-2019 ($7,000 vs $7,243) verify; >$500k-by-2028-halving and ~$1M-~450-days-post-halving and $1.5M-by-2035 all verify against Peterson sourcing. NOTE the $1.5M/2035 implies ~36-38%/yr off a ~$93-100k base (TradingView/article math), slightly above the row's stated '~31%/yr'. FIX NEEDED: (1) stop attributing Peterson's targets to the 1.69 mechanism -- state plainly Peterson uses n^2, which W-S reject, so his targets are not a defensible extension of THIS row's model. (2) Drop or rewrite the 'vol floor held at ~57%, no compression' rationale -- ETF-era 1yr realized is now <50%; keep 55-60% only as a long-horizon blend, not a 'floor.' (3) Add the Peterson $100k-by-Jan-2024 miss when citing his accuracy.
overstated_pros: 'Genuine out-of-sample validation' (the $40-80B early-2019 call): real and verified, but the row leans on it as strong evidence for a 10-15yr CMA. It validates a <1yr bubble-deflation call, not multi-year appreciation forecasting -- the very use the authors disclaim. Strength of evidence is overstated relative to what it supports.

'Lets the DATA choose the exponent (1.69)... more honest than crypto-native Metcalfe variants': true for W-S, but the row simultaneously imports Peterson's n^2-derived targets, undercutting its own honesty claim.

'Finite terminal fundamental value / built-in appreciation decay = correct qualitative shape': fair, but the carrying-capacity uncertainty (4 orders of magnitude, per the authors) means the 'finite terminal value' is unknowable in level -- so the pro is qualitative-only and the row's ~9-13%/yr point estimate borrows precision the mechanism cannot supply.
missing_cons: No mention that the model's appreciation output is structurally near-DEFLATIONARY in late stages: as users saturate toward the ceiling, forward user CAGR -> low single digits, and 1.69 x (low single digit) can fall BELOW inflation, implying the honest central case could be lower than the stated 9-13% nominal -- the row picks the optimistic interior of its own logic.

Active-user count itself is a contested/gameable metric (address != user; one user holds many addresses; exchanges net many users into few addresses) -- the row flags L2/ETF leakage but not the more basic identification problem that 'active addresses' never cleanly equaled 'users' even IN-sample, weakening the 0.95 R2's economic meaning.

Halving/supply denominator is treated as 'near-fixed,' but lost coins, long-term-holder illiquidity, and ETF/treasury lockups mean effective float is far below 21M and time-varying -- the price = networkvalue/supply step is noisier than presented.

Survivorship/single-history problem is mentioned for the exponent but not for the OUT-OF-SAMPLE appreciation path: one realized BTC trajectory cannot distinguish a saturating-network process from a one-off monetization, so the CMA has no genuine cross-sectional support.

No acknowledgment that the rising BTC-Nasdaq correlation (now ~0.5, briefly ~0.8) makes BTC's diversification value time-varying and regime-dependent -- the corr_growth_eq band +0.35-0.50 may be too low for risk-off episodes when it spikes.

new_approaches.name: Global-Liquidity / Collateral-Multiplier Cycle Barometer (Howell / Alden Directional Liquidity-Beta)
new_approaches.description: This approach treats Bitcoin as the purest directional claim on Global Liquidity — defined NOT as a money-supply level but as gross, collateral-augmented flow of funds: central-bank money plus private-sector credit plus a collateral-reuse (repo/shadow-money) multiplier, which Howell/CrossBorder Capital aggregate to a ~$188.8T pool that peaked in Q3 2025. The core empirical object is a DIRECTIONAL liquidity-beta and a recurring ~65-month (5-6yr) debt-refinancing cycle, not a cointegrating level-elasticity. Callahan/Alden show BTC moves in the SAME DIRECTION as global liquidity in 83% of rolling 12-month and 74% of 6-month windows — higher than any other major asset — but that hit rate and the level correlation DECAY at shorter horizons (overall corr 0.94, 12mo rolling 0.51, 6mo 0.36), where idiosyncratic and valuation factors dominate. Howell adds a cycle-PHASE overlay (liquidity leads BTC ~13 weeks) and a driver DECOMPOSITION (~40-45% global liquidity, ~25% gold-like, ~25% pure risk appetite). A 10-15yr CMA does NOT fall out cleanly: the framework's native outputs are a phase-conditioned return + high-amplitude drawdown profile (e.g. -47% peak-to-trough into the 2026-27 downswing), not a perpetual growth rate. To force a CMA you assume the liquidity tide rises secularly (fiscal-dominance money printing to monetize deficits) and BTC retains a >1 liquidity-beta that decays as it matures. Distinct from M2-cointegration (#7, a LEVEL elasticity ~2.0-2.65) and QTM (#8, MV=PT identity): here the driver is collateral-backed GROSS funding and cycle PHASE, and the asset is a barometer/beta, not a fair-value level.
new_approaches.medium_explanation: Bitcoin is framed as the most liquidity-sensitive asset on the planet — a high-beta, demand-pure claim on Global Liquidity. The driver is not money-supply level but gross, collateral-augmented funding: central-bank money + private credit + a repo/shadow-money multiplier (~77-80% of global lending is collateral-backed), aggregating to Howell's ~$189T pool that cycles on a ~65-month debt-refinancing rhythm. The headline evidence is DIRECTIONAL: BTC aligns with global liquidity in 83% of 12-month windows (74% of 6-month), more than equities, gold or bonds, with liquidity leading BTC ~13 weeks. Crucially this beta DECAYS as the horizon shortens (corr 0.94 overall, 0.51 at 12mo, 0.36 at 6mo), where idiosyncratic and valuation forces take over. For a 10-15yr CMA the framework implies appreciation tracks the secular liquidity uptrend (fiscal-dominance money creation) times a liquidity-beta >1 that compresses toward gold's as BTC matures — yielding a decaying return with violent cyclical drawdowns, NOT a perpetual growth rate. Howell decomposes BTC as ~40-45% liquidity, ~25% gold-like, ~25% risk appetite — explicitly NOT pure digital gold.
key_drivers: Global Liquidity as GROSS collateral-augmented funding: central-bank money + private-sector credit + a collateral-reuse/repo/shadow-money multiplier (~$188.8T peak; ~77-80% of global lending collateral-backed) — the level AND its rate-of-change
The ~65-month (5-6yr) debt-refinancing liquidity cycle and its PHASE (peaked Q3 2025, downswing through ~2027) — the recurring driver Howell argues should REPLACE the 4-year halving cycle
Directional liquidity-beta: BTC moves with liquidity 83% of 12mo / 74% of 6mo windows; liquidity LEADS BTC ~13 weeks (a tradable lead, not a level anchor)

Horizon-dependent decay of the relationship: tight over 12mo (corr 0.51) and full-sample (0.94), but eroding to 0.36 at 6mo and toward noise intraday/monthly as idiosyncratic + valuation factors dominate
Driver decomposition (Howell): ~40-45% global liquidity, ~25% gold-like behavior, ~25% pure risk appetite (NASDAQ-correlated) — BTC is a BLEND, not a pure liquidity or pure gold play
Fiscal dominance / sovereign debt refinancing (~$70T+ annual rollovers) forcing central banks to monetize deficits — the secular tailwind under the cyclical wobble (the 'monetary inflation' thesis)
Idiosyncratic break conditions: exchange collapses (Mt.Gox, FTX/Terra), and extreme on-chain valuation (high MVRV-Z) where profit-taking/panic overrides the liquidity signal
The 'global M2' / global-liquidity measurement choice itself (8-economy M2 in USD vs collateral-inclusive gross liquidity) and any lag-shift applied — a load-bearing and contested input
pros: The DIRECTIONAL claim is the most robust empirical finding in BTC macro: an 83%/12mo hit rate with global liquidity, higher than equities/gold/bonds, is a real and replicated signal (Callahan/Alden) — and being directional (sign-of-change) it sidesteps the spurious-level-regression trap that sinks naive M2-elasticity and S2F

The collateral-multiplier lens is conceptually richer than money-supply models: it captures repo/shadow-money creation (~77-80% of lending is collateral-backed) and gross funding conditions that M2 misses, which is genuinely where marginal risk-asset liquidity is set

Honest about HORIZON: the framework explicitly documents its own decay (0.94 → 0.51 → 0.36 as windows shorten), so it does not over-claim short-term precision — and the ~65-month cycle gives a falsifiable PHASE call rather than a perpetual-uptrend assertion

Driver decomposition (~40-45% liquidity / ~25% gold / ~25% risk) is unusually candid for a practitioner thesis — it explicitly REFUSES the pure-digital-gold framing and quantifies BTC as a blend, which matches realized behavior (high equity beta, ~0 gold correlation)

Generates a realistic drawdown/amplitude profile (e.g. the -47% 2025-26 liquidity-downswing call) rather than a smooth compounding path — useful for the tail/loss-given-bear half of a CMA that level models ignore

Practitioner adoption is deep and cross-checkable: CrossBorder Capital, Alden, CF Benchmarks and Onramp all publish liquidity-linked BTC work, and the framework has on-record cycle calls (peak Q3 2025) that can be scored ex-post
cons: DIRECTION ≠ MAGNITUDE: an 83% directional hit rate says nothing about HOW MUCH BTC rises — it cannot, by itself, produce an appreciation number. Any 10-15yr CMA is bolted on by assuming a secular liquidity uptrend AND a liquidity-beta, neither of which the barometer estimates; the headline stat is being repurposed beyond what it supports

The 'global M2 / global liquidity' series is contested as data-tortured: critics (e.g. Sina vs Raoul Pal's model) show the fit relies on arbitrarily lag-shifting M2 forward 10-13 weeks and 'finding great matches between pockets of data' — overfitting with 'no idea about predictive accuracy.' The lead-time is itself a fitted parameter, not structural

REVERSE CAUSALITY is unresolved: in 2025 BTC topped FIRST and liquidity peaked ~145 days later, suggesting BTC may LEAD liquidity (as a risk-appetite barometer) rather than follow it — which inverts the framework's premise that liquidity is the exogenous driver

The collateral multiplier is asserted, not measured: Howell's own interviews give the $189T peak and the ~77-80% collateral-backed-lending stat but do NOT publish an itemized central-bank-vs-private-vs-collateral breakdown or a quantified multiplier coefficient — the mechanism is narrative, the aggregate a black box

Documented post-2021/2025 BREAKDOWN: CF Benchmarks reports the M2-BTC R² collapsing from 0.71-0.90 to ~0.59 with a ~46% (~$66k) fair-value gap as M2 EXPANDED while BTC FELL — exactly the regime where the liquidity bid rotated toward gold (gold liquidity Z-score +2.82 vs BTC -1.31). The barometer can read wrong for quarters at a time

The ~65-month cycle is calibrated on very few realized cycles and is converging with the halving cycle right now (Howell concedes this), making it nearly impossible to attribute BTC moves to liquidity-phase vs halving vs risk appetite — the decomposition (40/25/25) is judgmental, not estimated

Silent on a calibrated covariance matrix: like the other monetary models it gives qualitative correlation views (BTC-gold negative short-run / positive long-run, the 'dog on a leash') but no stable coefficients vs growth eq, value eq, nominal FI, TIPS — all CMA covariance cells must be imported from realized data
