cited_outputs.horizon: Mixed: barometer evidence is 6-12 month rolling windows (Callahan/Alden); Howell's cycle is ~65 months (5-6yr) with a 2027 trough; adjacent CF Benchmarks CMA is 10yr (to 2035). No native 10-15yr appreciation rate is published by the barometer itself.
cited_outputs.appreciation_nominal: n/a as an annualized CMA from the barometer itself (it is a directional/phase model, not a return model). Adjacent on-record figures: Howell sketches a cyclical $30k-$90k near-term range and a long-run gold-parity extrapolation (~$25k+ by 2050 in gold-equivalent terms / 'easily $10,000/oz' gold) implying proportional BTC appreciation off ~8% annual sovereign-debt growth; CF Benchmarks' liquidity-anchored CMA gives base 30.1%/yr to a $1.42M 2035 target (bear $637k, bull $2.95M). None is a barometer output per se.
cited_outputs.appreciation_real: n/a (source silent — all figures nominal-USD; the debasement/fiscal-dominance thesis is qualitative, no inflation-adjusted rate published)
cited_outputs.volatility: n/a from Howell (qualitative: BTC is 'the most liquidity-sensitive asset,' implying high amplitude — e.g. -47% peak-to-trough into the 2026-27 downswing). CF Benchmarks (adjacent): vol 'projected to fall toward 28% over the next decade'
cited_outputs.corr_growth_eq: Callahan/Alden: on a YoY %-change basis stock indices (S&P 500, VT, EEM) correlate to global liquidity slightly MORE than BTC; Howell attributes ~25% of BTC drivers to NASDAQ-correlated risk appetite. CF Benchmarks (adjacent): equities 0.52 today -> 0.15 projected 10yr. No single BTC-vs-growth-equity coefficient in the barometer itself.
cited_outputs.corr_value_eq: n/a (source silent — no growth/value equity split)
cited_outputs.corr_fi_nominal: Qualitative: bonds rank LOWEST in liquidity correlation among the assets tested (Callahan/Alden). CF Benchmarks (adjacent): bonds 0.14 today -> 0.22 projected. No barometer coefficient.
cited_outputs.corr_gold: Howell: BTC and gold have 'a NEGATIVE short-term correlation but a very POSITIVE long-term correlation' ('dog on a leash following its owner'); gold ranks just below BTC in 12mo liquidity correlation (Callahan/Alden). CF Benchmarks (adjacent): gold ~0.06 today, ~0.06 projected (flat, near-zero). No single barometer BTC-gold coefficient; the framework explicitly treats gold-like behavior as only ~25% of BTC's drivers.
cited_outputs.notes: The barometer publishes a DIRECTIONAL hit-rate and a cycle PHASE, not magnitudes — so almost every CMA cell is 'n/a (source silent)' or imported from the adjacent CF Benchmarks CMA. The strongest cited number is the 83%/12mo directional alignment and the horizon-decay sequence (0.94 -> 0.51 -> 0.36). Treat CF Benchmarks' 30.1%/vol-28%/corr figures as a SEPARATE liquidity-anchored CMA, not Howell/Alden outputs; they are from a long-the-asset index provider.

synthesized_outputs.appreciation_nominal: ~9-13%/yr (judgment, not a barometer output). Logic: the barometer gives DIRECTION, not magnitude, so I anchor the secular leg to fiscal-dominance liquidity growth (~7-9%/yr gross-liquidity / sovereign-debt expansion) times a BTC liquidity-beta that starts >1 but DECAYS toward gold-like as BTC institutionalizes — consistent with realized appreciation decay (142% -> 65% -> 17%/yr). The ~40-45% liquidity / ~25% gold / ~25% risk-appetite decomposition implies BTC's forward return is a blend dominated by a maturing liquidity beta plus a thinning adoption premium, landing low-double-digits. I discount Howell's gold-parity long-run extrapolation and CF Benchmarks' 30.1% as over-extrapolations of an in-sample beta; the honest central is ~11%.
synthesized_outputs.appreciation_real: ~6-10%/yr real (deflating ~11% nominal by ~2.5-3% CPI). The debasement thesis says nominal runs hot, but the real wedge over liquidity growth is just (beta-1) x liquidity growth, which compresses toward ~0 as the liquidity-beta decays toward 1; center ~7%.
synthesized_outputs.volatility: ~55-60%/yr (judgment). The framework's emphasis on BTC as the highest-amplitude liquidity-sensitive asset (violent -47% cyclical drawdowns) keeps vol well above CF Benchmarks' optimistic ~28% terminal. Floor held AT realized trailing-5y ~57% (the sub-2yr ETF sample does not yet evidence sustained compression below realized); decade-average band ~50-60%, multiples of equities/gold.
synthesized_outputs.corr_growth_eq: ~0.45-0.55 (judgment). The ~25% risk-appetite (NASDAQ) component plus the shared liquidity-beta tie BTC to growth/tech equities; realized trailing-5y is 0.56 and rising with institutionalization. I take the post-ETF regime as the forward base, ~0.50, and discount CF Benchmarks' aspirational 0.15.
synthesized_outputs.corr_value_eq: ~0.25-0.35 (judgment). Below growth-eq; value is less liquidity/duration-sensitive than the liquidity-beta and risk-appetite channels that drive BTC. Tracks realized 5y ~0.37.
synthesized_outputs.corr_fi_nominal: ~0.10-0.20 (judgment). Bonds rank LOWEST in this literature's liquidity correlation; near-zero-to-slightly-positive via shared easy-money sensitivity, but BTC is a liquidity-beta not a duration instrument. ~0.15, near realized 5y 0.19.
synthesized_outputs.corr_tips: ~0.15-0.25 (judgment). The fiscal-dominance/debasement leg gives a faint real-rate/inflation-protection overlap, slightly above nominal FI but weak and regime-dependent; ~0.20, below realized 5y 0.30 given instability.
synthesized_outputs.corr_gold: ~0.05-0.20 (judgment, center ~0.12). This is the framework's most nuanced gold claim: Howell asserts NEGATIVE short-term / POSITIVE long-term BTC-gold co-movement (dog-on-a-leash), and pegs gold-like behavior at only ~25% of BTC's drivers. Over a 10-15yr horizon the long-run leg argues for a modestly positive number, but realized BTC-gold correlation is ~0 (full -0.01, 5y +0.045) and the 2025-26 divergence (gold liquidity Z +2.82 vs BTC -1.31) shows the short-term negative leg repeatedly dominating. I hold it low, above the pure-zero of risk-asset models but well below a digital-gold thesis — the framework itself does NOT claim high stable gold co-movement.
synthesized_outputs.notes: All synthesized numbers are judgment, not barometer outputs — the framework yields direction/phase only, so I anchor magnitude to the realized appreciation-decay path and the realized covariance matrix, then tilt by Howell's 40/25/25 driver decomposition. Central case: ~11% nominal / ~7% real, vol ~57%, growth-eq corr ~0.50, gold corr ~0.12. The load-bearing caveat: a model right on direction 83% of 12-month windows can still be badly wrong on magnitude and on multi-quarter regime breaks (the 2025-26 M2-up/BTC-down divergence), and the causal arrow (does liquidity lead BTC, or BTC lead liquidity?) is not firmly established.

new_approaches.rich_notes:
METHODOLOGY. This family merges three practitioner candidates around one idea: BTC is a directional barometer/high-beta of Global Liquidity, where 'liquidity' is gross, collateral-augmented funding rather than a money-supply level. Callahan/Alden (2024) supply the empirical spine: using an 8-economy 'global M2' in USD, BTC moves in the SAME DIRECTION as liquidity in 83% of rolling 12-month and 74% of 6-month windows — higher than equities, gold or bonds — establishing BTC as the 'purest' liquidity barometer (no earnings, not a safe haven). Critically the same study documents the relationship's HORIZON DECAY: full-sample level correlation 0.94, falling to 0.51 (12mo rolling) and 0.36 (6mo), with intraday/monthly dominated by idiosyncratic and valuation factors (high MVRV-Z, exchange collapses). Howell/CrossBorder Capital add the collateral-multiplier and cycle machinery: a ~$188.8T global-liquidity pool (peaked Q3 2025), ~77-80% of global lending collateral-backed (repo/shadow-money reuse amplifies central-bank + private credit), a ~65-month (5-6yr) debt-refinancing cycle he argues should REPLACE the 4-year halving cycle, and a ~13-week lead of liquidity over BTC. His driver DECOMPOSITION — ~40-45% global liquidity, ~25% gold-like, ~25% risk appetite (NASDAQ vol) — is the single most useful and honest output: it explicitly denies the pure-digital-gold framing and casts BTC as a blend.

KEY RELATIONSHIPS / QUOTES. 'Bitcoin and crypto are the most liquidity-sensitive assets on the planet… a canary in the coal mine for tightening liquidity' (Howell). On gold: 'Bitcoin and gold have a negative short-term correlation but a very positive long-term correlation' — the dog-on-a-leash analogy (gold is the owner, BTC the dog cycling around it). Alden: BTC is a tool for 'expressing views on the future direction of global liquidity,' NOT a return forecaster.

HISTORICAL FIT & FAILURE MODES. The directional claim fits 2013-2024 well, but the 2025-26 episode is a clean failure of the LEVEL version: CF Benchmarks reports M2-BTC R² collapsing from 0.71-0.90 to ~0.59 with a ~46% (~$66k) fair-value gap as M2 EXPANDED while BTC FELL ~47% from its ~$126k October peak — and the liquidity bid rotated to GOLD (gold liquidity Z +2.82 vs BTC -1.31). This is the framework's Achilles heel: it can read wrong for multiple quarters. Two deeper critiques bite. First, DATA TORTURE: the quant 'Sina' publicly dismantled Raoul Pal's global-M2-shifted-forward-10-13-weeks model as overfitting — 'it's forcibly fit on historical data; you have no idea about the predictive accuracy.' The lead-time is a fitted parameter, not structural. Second, REVERSE CAUSALITY: in 2025 BTC topped FIRST and liquidity peaked ~145 days later, suggesting BTC may LEAD liquidity (as a risk-appetite signal) rather than follow it — inverting the premise. Howell himself concedes the 65-month and halving cycles are 'converging right now,' which makes attribution (liquidity vs halving vs risk) nearly impossible and the 40/25/25 split judgmental.

ON-RECORD MULTI-YEAR FORECASTS PRODUCED THIS WAY. Howell: the 65-month cycle peaked Q3 2025 with a downswing through ~2027; a cyclical $30k-$90k BTC range (downside from tightening, upside as central banks 'print aggressively' to monetize deficits); and a long-run gold-parity extrapolation — gold 'easily $10,000/oz' in the 2030s and a ~$25k+/2050 figure in gold-equivalent terms off ~8% annual sovereign-debt growth — implying proportional BTC appreciation, but he frames these as 'aspirations,' not models. Allocation guidance: buy gold and BTC on dips 20-25% below trend. CF Benchmarks' adjacent liquidity-anchored CMA (the only fully-specified one in this family) gives base 30.1%/yr to a $1.42M 2035 target (bear $637k / bull $2.95M), vol falling toward 28% over a decade, equity correlation 0.52→0.15, bonds 0.14→0.22, gold flat ~0.06.

CMA BOTTOM LINE. The barometer's genuine contribution is DIRECTION and PHASE, plus the honest decomposition that BTC is only ~40-45% liquidity and ~25% gold. It supplies no native magnitude, so a credible 10-15yr CMA must (1) anchor the secular leg to fiscal-dominance liquidity growth, (2) apply a liquidity-beta that DECAYS toward gold-like as BTC matures, and (3) keep vol high and gold correlation low. That extrapolation of the realized decay — not the in-sample beta or the gold-parity targets — lands ~9-13% nominal, vol ~55-60%, equity corr ~0.50, gold corr ~0.10-0.15. The single most important caveat: a model that is right on direction 83% of 12-month windows can still be catastrophically wrong on magnitude and on multi-quarter regime breaks (2025-26), and its causal arrow is not even firmly established. Versus the adjacent monetary approaches in the digest: #7 (M2-cointegration) estimates a LEVEL elasticity ~2.0-2.65 and #8 (QTM/MV=PT) inverts a transaction identity; this approach is distinct because its driver is collateral-backed GROSS funding and recurring cycle PHASE, and its headline output is a phase-conditioned return + high-amplitude drawdown profile rather than a cointegrating elasticity or a martingale fair value.

Causal-arrow caveat is present but could be stronger: the reverse-causality finding (BTC leads liquidity by 145 days, from Sina) doesn't merely add uncertainty to magnitude — if true it partially INVALIDATES the entire premise that liquidity is the exogenous secular driver onto which the CMA is anchored. overstated_pros: Pro #1 calls the directional claim 'replicated' - the 83% finding is widely CITED/reported but I found no evidence of independent REPLICATION on different data/periods; it is one study (Callahan under Alden) repeated across news aggregators. 'Widely cited' is accurate; 'replicated' overstates.

Pro #6 ('practitioner adoption deep and cross-checkable... on-record cycle calls that can be scored ex-post') frames the Q3-2025 peak call as a validated win. It is on-record, but the very same liquidity-up / BTC-down 2025-26 divergence the cons section documents means the directional barometer ALSO read wrong through that window - the pro and the con are scoring the same period in opposite directions without reconciling.

Pro #3 ('honest about horizon... does not over-claim short-term precision') credits the framework for documenting its own decay - fair - but the decay sequence (0.94->0.51->0.36) is the LEVEL-correlation decay, while the 83% headline is a DIRECTIONAL hit-rate; presenting both as evidence the framework is 'honest about horizon' slightly conflates two different metrics that decay for different reasons.
missing_cons: SURVIVORSHIP / SAMPLE-PERIOD bias not raised: the entire 0.94 full-sample fit and the 83% hit-rate are estimated over May-2013 to mid-2024, a period of secularly EXPANDING global liquidity and BTC in a multi-order-of-magnitude adoption S-curve. Both BTC's appreciation and liquidity trended up together over the window, which mechanically inflates a same-direction hit-rate. The cons cover horizon decay and the 2025-26 break but never flag that the headline stat may be a bull-regime artifact unlikely to survive a genuine multi-year liquidity contraction (which has never been observed in BTC's sample).

MULTIPLE-TESTING / construct-choice degrees of freedom: the cons flag the lag-shift as a fitted parameter (good), but not that the CHOICE of which liquidity aggregate to use (8-economy M2 vs 21-CB M2 vs Howell's collateral-inclusive $189T gross vs Onramp's M2+DXY+real-rates) is itself a researcher degree of freedom. Different practitioners use different series and all claim a fit - a classic garden-of-forking-paths problem that inflates apparent robustness across the 'family.'

NON-STATIONARITY of the beta for CMA purposes: the synth assumes the liquidity-beta decays smoothly toward gold-like. But the framework gives no evidence the beta decays MONOTONICALLY rather than regime-switching (high in risk-on, collapsing in stress). A CMA built on a smoothly-decaying beta understates the probability the relationship simply breaks (as it did 2025-26) rather than gracefully matures.

REGULATORY / structural-break risk to the liquidity linkage itself is absent: spot-ETF flows, sovereign/treasury-company demand, and potential strategic-reserve buying can decouple BTC from the marginal-liquidity channel entirely (demand becomes price-inelastic). This would break the barometer in the OPPOSITE direction from the cons' failure mode and isn't considered.

new_approaches.name: Fiscal-Theory-of-the-Price-Level / Fiscal-Dominance Hard-Asset Bid
new_approaches.description: This approach replaces money supply with the government's intertemporal budget constraint as the determinant of the price level and of the hard-asset bid. Per the Fiscal Theory of the Price Level (Cochrane 2023), the real value of nominal government debt equals the present value of expected future primary surpluses; the price level adjusts like a stock price so that real debt equals discounted surpluses. When a government runs persistent structural deficits with no credible promise of future surpluses, the price level jumps (and inflation runs) to revalue outstanding nominal debt downward. The practitioner overlay (Alden/Callahan, 'Full Steam Ahead: All Aboard Fiscal Dominance') argues that under fiscal dominance, deficit spending — not private credit or monetary policy — becomes the dominant liquidity engine, and (absent supply constraints) that liquidity flows into scarce hard assets: stocks, real estate, gold, and Bitcoin. BTC is thus valued as a high-beta claim on fiscal-driven debasement. Critically, the framework is NON-MONOTONE: the same fiscal dominance that supplies the bullish liquidity/debasement bid also forces heavy Treasury issuance that — via supply and term premium (KC Fed 2025) — can lift long-term real yields, raising the opportunity cost of a non-yielding asset and weighing on BTC even as the Fed eases. A 10-15yr CMA is the net of a structural debasement tailwind against an episodic real-yield/term-premium headwind, not a single liquidity beta.
new_approaches.medium_explanation: FTPL determines the price level from the government's budget identity: real debt = present value of primary surpluses. Run structural deficits with no credible path to surpluses and the price level must rise to inflate away nominal debt — a fiscal, not monetary, source of inflation. The fiscal-dominance overlay says deficit spending is now the primary liquidity engine; with no commodity supply constraint, that liquidity bids up scarce assets including Bitcoin, which is valued as a leveraged debasement claim (BTC tracks global liquidity ~83% of 12-month windows). The distinctive twist is non-monotone: the same intractable deficits force heavy Treasury issuance that lifts long real yields and term premium, raising the opportunity cost of a yieldless asset and pressuring BTC even while the Fed cuts. For a 10-15yr BTC CMA this nets a persistent debasement tailwind against an episodic real-rate headwind — implying low-double-digit nominal appreciation (decaying), high but not declining volatility, a rising equity correlation, and — unlike pure debasement framings — a meaningful positive sensitivity to TIPS/real yields rather than a clean gold proxy.
key_drivers: Fiscal balance / primary surplus path — the FTPL valuation anchor: real debt = PV(primary surpluses); deteriorating surplus expectations devalue nominal debt and bid hard assets

Fiscal dominance regime — deficit spending exceeding private credit creation as the dominant liquidity driver (Alden/Callahan); interest payments on a large debt stock act as stimulus, so rate hikes can be inflationary not contractionary
Treasury issuance volume and maturity mix — heavy long-dated supply raises term premium and long real yields (KC Fed 2025: debt/GDP expansion lifts 5-10yr yields), the bearish leg
Long-term real yields / term premium — the opportunity-cost channel: higher real yields on guaranteed govt bonds compress the risk premium available to a non-yielding BTC
Global liquidity impulse — BTC as a high-beta liquidity barometer (83% directional hit rate over 12m); the bullish transmission of fiscal deficits into asset prices
Monetary-fiscal divergence — Fed easing (QE/buyer-of-last-resort) vs Treasury issuance; the net of the two determines whether the liquidity bid or the real-yield headwind dominates

Inflation vs real-yield split — whether fiscal stress shows up as inflation (FTPL price-level jump, BTC-bullish debasement) or as higher real yields/term premium (BTC-bearish), which is regime-dependent and the crux of the non-monotone view
pros: Theoretically rigorous and peer-reviewed at the core: Cochrane's FTPL (Princeton UP, 2023) and the continuous-time stochastic GE formalization (arXiv 2403.01593) give a real macro foundation, not a fitted price curve — it cannot be dismissed as spurious S2F/Metcalfe numerology

Genuinely distinct from existing monetary rows: it endogenizes the price level via the fiscal budget rather than treating money supply as exogenous (rows #7/#8), and it is the only framing that models the fiscal-vs-monetary DIVERGENCE and reframes BTC's real-yield sensitivity through a sovereign-solvency lens

Non-monotone realism: by pairing a bullish debasement/liquidity leg with a bearish issuance/real-yield leg, it explains episodes (e.g. 2022 and high-yield 2025-26 regimes) where BTC fell DESPITE worsening fiscal deficits — something pure debasement/M2 models cannot accommodate

Empirically anchored bullish channel: BTC's ~83% directional co-movement with global liquidity over 12-month windows (Alden/Callahan) is among the strongest macro relationships for any asset class, lending the liquidity leg real signal

Correctly predicts the empirically observed TIPS/real-yield linkage: because the framework explicitly routes BTC through the real-yield/term-premium channel, it accommodates BTC's measured positive TIPS correlation (~0.30 trailing-5y) rather than asserting a gold proxy the data rejects
cons: FTPL itself is contested: prominent economists (Buiter, McCallum) dispute its causal mechanism and identification (the budget identity holds under any theory of the price level, so attributing causation to fiscal policy is debated); the empirical FTPL literature is far from settled

Indeterminate as a CMA: the framework produces no native long-horizon BTC appreciation number. The output depends entirely on (a) how much of fiscal stress shows up as inflation vs real yields and (b) an assumed BTC liquidity beta — both analyst inputs, so the CMA launders a prior rather than generating a forecast

The two legs can offset to near-zero and the sign is regime-dependent: Cochrane's own mechanism is primarily INFLATIONARY (debt eroded by a price-level jump, not sustained higher real yields), whereas the bearish BTC leg requires the real-yield/term-premium channel to dominate — the framework does not pin which prevails over 10-15yr

Practitioner sources carry a long book and are not peer-reviewed: Alden/Callahan and the crypto-desk commentary are advocacy-adjacent (hard-asset thesis), and the 'liquidity flows into BTC' transmission is asserted from a short, bull-dominated sample that breaks down in shorter windows and at valuation extremes (their own caveat)

Reflexivity/circularity in the bullish leg: 'fiscal dominance bids hard assets' is partly a restatement of the post-2020 regime in which both deficits and BTC rose together; isolating fiscal causation from the shared risk-appetite/liquidity driver is not established

Silent on volatility and most correlations as published numbers — vol, growth/value-equity, nominal-FI and gold co-movements must all be imported from realized data; the framework constrains only the appreciation sign and the real-yield linkage

Logic: the framework nets a structural fiscal-debasement tailwind (the bullish liquidity/PV-of-surpluses-deteriorating leg) against an episodic real-yield/term-premium headwind (heavy Treasury issuance lifting long real yields). The bullish leg alone, naively, would justify more, but the non-monotone real-yield drag plus the realized appreciation DECAY (142%->65%->17%/yr full/10y/5y) caps the forward rate in low double digits and below the trailing-5y 17%. I sit modestly above the cross-approach central (~8-12%) because the debasement tailwind is structural, but reject any high-teens+ figure: every incremental deficit that bids BTC also pressures it through issuance/real yields.
synthesized_outputs.appreciation_real: ~6-9%/yr (center ~7%; subtracting ~2.5-3% trend CPI). The framework's honest read: if fiscal dominance delivers inflation, BTC's nominal return rises but the REAL premium is only the wedge by which BTC outpaces the fiscally-driven price level — and that wedge compresses as the asset matures and as real-yield headwinds offset the debasement bid.
synthesized_outputs.volatility: ~55-60%/yr (center ~57%; judgment). The framework is silent on a number; the stochastic FTPL factor implies regime-driven jumps. Floor held AT realized trailing-5y ~57% rather than below it — the non-monotone real-yield sensitivity is an ADDED source of variance (BTC now reacts to Treasury auctions and term-premium shocks), arguing against compression. Stays multiples of equity/gold vol across the horizon.

Both BTC and growth equities are liquidity/risk-appetite betas bid up together in fiscal-dominance liquidity expansions; realized trailing-5y is 0.56. I set it moderately positive and rising, slightly below the pure factor-regression read because the framework adds an idiosyncratic fiscal/real-yield axis that is not shared one-for-one with equities.

Near-zero on average but with a DISTINCTIVE twist this framework emphasizes: in the issuance/real-yield regime BTC and long nominal Treasuries can move ADVERSELY (rising yields = falling bond prices AND falling BTC), so the average masks a regime-dependent negative beta to duration sell-offs. I keep the average low-positive (shared liquidity channel) but flag the issuance-regime negativity.
synthesized_outputs.corr_tips: ~0.25-0.35 (center ~0.30; judgment). This is the framework's signature cell and where it most differs from gold-proxy/debasement rows: by explicitly routing BTC through the real-yield/term-premium channel, it predicts the HIGHEST cross-asset sensitivity to TIPS/real yields among the fixed-income set — consistent with realized trailing-5y 0.30. BTC behaves as a long-duration real-rate-sensitive asset, pressured when real yields rise.
synthesized_outputs.corr_gold: ~0.05-0.20 (center ~0.12; judgment). The framework groups gold and BTC as joint fiscal-dominance hard-asset beneficiaries, which superficially argues for co-movement, but realized BTC-gold correlation is ~0 (full -0.01, 5y +0.045) and Alden's own work documents the gold/BTC liquidity bid DIVERGING. I nudge slightly above the bottom of the band to reflect a shared debasement driver, but explicitly reject a high digital-gold linkage: the framework's distinctive value is precisely that it predicts BTC's real-yield sensitivity (TIPS axis), NOT a clean gold proxy. Internal contradiction worth naming: a fiscal-dominance thesis that bids gold and BTC together needs co-movement, yet the data supplies ~0 — so the hard-asset grouping is a narrative, and BTC's measured behavior is closer to a high-beta real-rate-sensitive risk asset than to gold.

Signature output vs all gold-proxy/debasement rows: positive TIPS/real-yield sensitivity (~0.30) and regime-dependent NEGATIVE duration beta, NOT a clean gold proxy (~0.12). new_approaches.rich_notes:
METHODOLOGY. This approach has two layers that must be kept distinct. (1) The ACADEMIC core — Cochrane's Fiscal Theory of the Price Level (Princeton UP, 2023; 'Fiscal Theory Parables', 2023) and its continuous-time stochastic GE formalization (arXiv:2403.01593, 2024) — replaces the quantity theory's money-supply determinant with the government's intertemporal budget identity: the real value of nominal debt equals the present value of expected future primary surpluses, and the price level adjusts (like a stock price to its dividend stream) to enforce that equality. Cochrane's 'Twin Parables': debt issued WITH credible surpluses is non-inflationary (like equity with dividend promises); debt issued WITHOUT surplus credibility forces a one-time price-level JUMP that inflates the real debt away, plus higher nominal rates. Crucially, Cochrane's first-order mechanism is INFLATIONARY (real debt eroded by a price-level jump), not a sustained real-yield increase. (2) The PRACTITIONER overlay — Alden/Callahan's 'Full Steam Ahead: All Aboard Fiscal Dominance' (2025) and 'Bitcoin: A Global Liquidity Barometer' (2024) — argues that under fiscal dominance, deficit spending exceeds private credit creation as the dominant liquidity engine, that interest payments on a large debt stock make rate HIKES stimulative (widening deficits, keeping inflation elevated), and that absent commodity supply constraints this liquidity bids up scarce hard assets 'stocks, real estate, gold, and bitcoin.' BTC is the highest-beta, purest such claim (no earnings/dividends to confound it), tracking global liquidity ~83% of 12-month and ~74% of 6-month windows — the strongest such relationship among major assets.

KEY RELATIONSHIP / WHY DISTINCT. The framework is genuinely non-monotone, which is its analytic contribution and the reason it is distinct from the existing M2-elasticity (#7) and quantity-theory (#8) rows that make money supply exogenous and monotone-bullish on debasement. Here, the SAME fiscal dominance that supplies the bullish debasement/liquidity bid also forces heavy Treasury issuance. The Kansas City Fed (2025) finds debt/GDP-raising Treasury supply lifts yields across maturities and raises the term premium, pronounced at 5-10yr. That raises long-term REAL yields, and — per the practitioner desk view ('Bitcoin's hard-money thesis is colliding with 5% Treasury yields', 2025; CCN 2026) — an allocator who can lock 5% guaranteed on a 30yr bond faces a higher opportunity cost of holding yieldless BTC. So BTC can FALL despite worsening deficits (observed 2022, and in high-yield 2025-26 episodes), which pure debasement models cannot explain. The crux for a CMA: whether fiscal stress manifests as INFLATION (FTPL price-level jump, BTC-bullish) or as higher REAL YIELDS/term premium (BTC-bearish) is regime-dependent and the framework does not pin it over 10-15yr. The honest net is a structural debasement tailwind minus an episodic real-rate headwind.

HISTORICAL FIT & FAILURE MODES. The bullish leg fits the 2020-2021 and 2023-2024 liquidity-expansion regimes well, and the 83% liquidity hit-rate is real signal. The bearish leg fits 2022 (BTC fell with bonds as real yields surged) and the 2025-26 high-yield collisions. Failure modes: (a) FTPL is contested at the source — Buiter and McCallum dispute its causal identification, since the budget identity holds under any price-level theory; attributing causation to fiscal policy is a modeling choice. (b) The two legs can offset to near-zero, and the framework cannot sign the net over a decade. (c) The practitioner transmission ('liquidity flows into BTC') is from a short, bull-dominated sample and is partly a restatement of the post-2020 co-movement of deficits and BTC, with the shared risk-appetite driver not cleanly separated (reflexivity). (d) Sources are advocacy-adjacent with a long book.

ON-RECORD MULTI-YEAR FORECASTS. No firm publishes a quantitative 10-15yr BTC CMA from this framework. The strongest on-record statements are Alden's: she expects 'very large fiscal deficits to continue' for 'the next ten years' and BTC to 'finish higher,' with new highs above $100k in the 2026 cycle — but explicitly with a LOWER trajectory than before ('Before all this tariff kerfuffle, I would have had a higher price target') and 'slowing returns' as cycles tie to macro/liquidity rather than halvings. This is a decaying-appreciation, regime-conditioned view, NOT a fixed CAGR — which is the correct qualitative shape for a maturing-asset CMA and supports a low-double-digit nominal anchor.

CMA TRANSLATION. I synthesize ~9-12% nominal / ~6-9% real, vol ~55-60%, growth-eq ~0.45, value-eq ~0.30, nominal-FI ~0.10 (with a regime-dependent NEGATIVE beta during duration sell-offs), TIPS ~0.30 (the framework's signature high-real-yield-sensitivity cell), gold ~0.12. The distinctive output vs every gold-proxy/debasement row is that this framework predicts BTC's positive TIPS/real-yield sensitivity and adverse issuance-regime behavior rather than a clean gold linkage — and the realized data (TIPS 0.30, gold ~0) corroborates that read.

issues: The 'peer-reviewed at the core' pro overstates the arXiv preprint (2403.01593). Verified: it is a master's thesis from the Higher School of Economics by Andrey Kofnov, posted to arXiv, NOT peer-reviewed. Cochrane's book (Princeton UP) is peer-reviewed/refereed-press; the continuous-time formalization is not. Listing both as the 'peer-reviewed core' conflates a serious academic monograph with an unrefereed student preprint.

Internal sign-convention muddle on the TIPS / real-yield cell. The framework's headline mechanism is: real yields RISE -> BTC FALLS (inverse, conventionally NEGATIVE price-vs-yield relationship). Yet corr_tips is reported as +0.30 positive and presented as 'corroborating' the realized data. The verified realized record shows BTC-real-yield correlation is unstable and sign-flipping (+0.28 -> -0.72 in Aug 2023 per CoinDesk). A '+0.30' only holds if 'TIPS' denotes TIPS-bond TOTAL RETURNS (which rise as real yields fall), not the real-yield level — but then it does NOT capture 'BTC pressured when real yields rise.' The doc uses both readings interchangeably, making its 'signature cell' the most internally confused number, not the most defensible.

The TIPS correlation is sold as BTC's 'signature, highest-real-yield-sensitivity, most stable' property, but the evidence shows it is among BTC's LEAST stable macro relationships (full sign reversal within months). Anchoring a 10-15yr CMA cell on a coefficient that flipped from +0.28 to -0.72 is weakly supported; the ~0.30 trailing-5y is an average masking large regime swings, which the doc admits elsewhere but not here.

Alden's $100k call timing is attributed to 'the 2026 cycle' in the doc, but the verified primary statement (April 17 2025 Coin Stories interview) framed >$100k as a 2025 target with new highs possibly 2026/2027. Minor but the doc tightens a fuzzy multi-year call into a cleaner '2026' than Alden actually gave.

Reflexivity con is correctly named but UNDERSTATED relative to how the synthesized numbers lean. The whole bullish-leg (deficits -> liquidity -> BTC) rests on a ~2013-2024 bull-dominated sample; the 0.94 level-correlation and 83% hit-rate both come from that single regime. The synthesized ~10% nominal anchor inherits this sample bias more than the con language concedes.

Cochrane affiliation listed as 'Hoover Institution / Princeton University Press.' Verified Cochrane is Hoover/Stanford (Rose-Marie & Jack Anderson Senior Fellow); Princeton is only the PUBLISHER, not his institution. The slashed pairing reads as if Princeton is an affiliation. Cosmetic but an attribution sloppiness.
verdict.corrections: "All seven headline cited numbers check out against primary/secondary sources: (1) BTC moves with global liquidity 83% of 12-month and 74% of 6-month windows — verified, Alden/Callahan 'Bitcoin: A Global Liquidity Barometer' (2024), and the 0.94 level-correlation May2013-Jul2024 is also real. (2) Cochrane FTPL, Princeton UP, 2023, 584pp, ISBN 9780691242248 — verified. (3) Buiter and McCallum FTPL critiques — verified (Buiter Economic Record 2023 review; McCallum/Buiter NBER 'Fallacy' lineage). (4) KC Fed 2025 'Higher Treasury Supply Is Likely to Put Upward Pressure on Interest Rates' with pronounced 5-10yr term-premium effect — verified (Nov 24 2025 bulletin). (5) arXiv 2403.01593 exists and supports FTPL — verified BUT it is an unrefereed master's thesis, not peer-reviewed (see issues). (6) Realized BTC vol 45-60% / ~52% recent — consistent with the ~57% floor; the floor-not-below-57% choice is defensible given added real-yield variance. (7) BTC-gold ~0 / divergent in 2025 — verified (CME, Morningstar; corr dropped to -0.49 Sept 2025). (8) Alden 'Before all this tariff kerfuffle, I would have had a higher price target' — verified verbatim (April 17 2025 Coin Stories interview). The synthesized 9-12% nominal / 6-9% real is internally consistent with the stated decay-and-headwind logic and sits sensibly below trailing-5y 17%; not hype. The ~57% vol floor and ~0.12 gold are well-supported. The single weakest synthesized cell is corr_tips (+0.30) due to the sign-convention/stability problems above. Net: numbers are real and correctly attributed; the framing oversells (a) the academic pedigree of the stochastic formalization and (b) the stability/defensibility of the TIPS 'signature' cell."
overstated_pros: Pro #1 'Theoretically rigorous and PEER-REVIEWED at the core ... continuous-time stochastic GE formalization (arXiv 2403.01593)' — the arXiv item is an unrefereed master's thesis; only Cochrane's monograph is refereed-press. Overstated.

Pro #5 'Correctly predicts the empirically observed TIPS/real-yield linkage (~0.30 trailing-5y)' — overstated as a clean win. The realized BTC-real-yield relationship is sign-unstable (+0.28 to -0.72 within 2023) and the framework's own mechanism implies a NEGATIVE price-vs-yield link, so '+0.30 corroborates' is at best convention-dependent and at worst self-contradictory.

Pro #4 'among the strongest macro relationships for any asset class (83%)' — true as stated but the strength is inflated by being measured over a single 2013-2024 bull/QE-dominated regime; presenting it as a durable structural law oversells a sample-conditioned statistic.
missing_cons: Survivorship/single-regime sample: every quantitative anchor (0.94 level corr, 83% hit-rate, ~0.30 equity/TIPS corrs, ~17% trailing-5y appreciation) is drawn from BTC's 2013-2025 existence, which is entirely a secular-bull + post-GFC-QE + post-2020-deficit regime. The framework has NEVER been observed through a sustained fiscal-CONSOLIDATION or genuine surplus regime — so the 'fiscal dominance bids BTC' leg is untested out-of-sample. This is a deeper version of the reflexivity con and is not stated as its own limitation.

The non-monotone framing is unfalsifiable as a CMA: because the same fiscal stress can be tagged 'inflationary (bullish)' or 'real-yield (bearish)' after the fact, the framework can rationalize ANY realized BTC path. The doc admits the legs 'can offset to near-zero' but does not flag that this makes the framework non-predictive / unfalsifiable at the 10-15yr horizon it is being used for.

No treatment of BTC-specific idiosyncratic/regulatory/technological risk (protocol, custody, ETF-flow saturation, quantum, regime bans). A 10-15yr CMA built purely on a macro-liquidity axis omits the asset-specific tail risks that have driven BTC's largest drawdowns — these are independent of fiscal regime and absent from both pros/cons and the vol number's justification.

Liquidity-beta decay / adoption-S-curve maturation is asserted for appreciation (decay to ~10%) but NOT applied to the liquidity beta itself: as BTC institutionalizes it may behave MORE like a duration-sensitive risk asset and LESS like a pure liquidity barometer, eroding the 83% relationship the whole bullish leg depends on. The CMA decays returns but implicitly holds the liquidity-transmission constant.

new_approaches.name: Triffin / Dedollarization Neutral-Reserve Sovereign Share
new_approaches.description: Values Bitcoin as a candidate neutral reserve / settlement asset competing for a slice of the official-sector FX-reserve pool (~$12.3T, of which USD ~57%, gold ~20% at market) and sovereign treasuries — a pool largely orthogonal to the private investable-gold TAM (#6) and the M2 broad-money stock (#7/#8). The thesis runs through the Triffin dilemma (the reserve-issuer must run deficits to supply global liquidity, eroding confidence in its own currency) and dollar weaponization (2022 Russia-reserve freeze) to argue that surplus/sanction-exposed sovereigns will diversify into a politically neutral, seizure-resistant, fixed-supply asset, benchmarked to gold's central-bank accumulation pace (~1,045 tonnes/yr in 2024, third straight year >1,000t). A CMA is built bottom-up: assume a terminal reserve SHARE Bitcoin captures by the horizon (e.g., 1-5% of FX reserves) times an explicit sovereign-adoption probability, treat that as incremental demand flow on top of BTC's existing ~$2T market cap (optionally with an illiquidity flow-multiplier), divide by near-fixed supply for an implied price, and annualize. Empirically this is a LOW-PROBABILITY TAIL-SHARE calibration: reserve-manager surveys (OMFIF 2025) show ~0% of central banks hold digital assets and 93% have no intention, so the honest expected value is modest, with nearly all upside in a small-probability sovereign-FOMO tail.
new_approaches.medium_explanation: The mechanism is geopolitical, not statistical: the Triffin dilemma plus dollar-reserve weaponization create latent demand for a neutral, seizure-proof, fixed-supply reserve asset, and Bitcoin is pitched as gold's digital analogue — benchmarked to central banks' ~1,000t/yr gold-buying pace. The CMA inputs are (1) a terminal Bitcoin share of the ~$12.3T official FX-reserve pool, (2) an explicit sovereign-adoption probability, and (3) a flow-to-marketcap multiplier. Crucially the reserve pool is SMALL versus BTC's existing ~$2T cap: even a wildly-bullish 5% allocation across ALL FX reserves implies only ~$130k-$410k (1x-10x flow multiplier). For a 10-15yr BTC CMA this caps the standalone reserve contribution at a modest premium and concentrates upside in a low-probability tail — because surveys put current central-bank endorsement at ~0% (93% no intent). Probability-weighting the scenarios yields ~10-14%/yr nominal, consistent with BTC's realized appreciation decay (142%→65%→17%), not its history.
key_drivers: Total official-sector FX-reserve pool (~$12.3T; USD ~57%, gold ~20% at market) and the addressable de-dollarization slice
Terminal Bitcoin reserve SHARE captured by the horizon (scenario lever, e.g. 1-5% of FX reserves; El Salvador ~14% of its own reserves, Brazil RESBit proposal 5%)
Explicit sovereign-adoption PROBABILITY — the load-bearing tail parameter (surveys: ~0% current, 93% no intent)
Triffin dilemma / fiscal-dominance erosion of confidence in the dollar as global reserve unit
Dollar weaponization / sanctions (2022 reserve freeze) driving demand for a neutral, seizure-resistant, non-state-issued asset
Gold's central-bank accumulation pace (~1,045t/yr 2024) as the benchmark for reserve-diversification velocity
Flow-to-marketcap multiplier (incremental reserve demand on a thin, illiquid float — debated 1x to ~10x+)
Reserve-asset qualification criteria: volatility, liquidity, trust/transparency, legal/custody, cross-border usability (Bitcoin fails several today per CB surveys)
BRICS / emerging-market settlement de-dollarization and IMF counter-pressure (El Salvador forced to strip mandatory legal-tender status)
pros: Targets a genuinely DISTINCT and large pool (official reserves + sovereign treasuries, ~$12.3T) that is largely orthogonal to the private-gold TAM and M2 frameworks, so it is additive rather than double-counting

Mechanism is economically real and on-record: the Triffin dilemma is a textbook reserve-currency tension, dollar weaponization measurably accelerated gold diversification (CB buying >1,000t/yr three years running), and a credibly neutral, seizure-resistant fixed-supply asset is exactly what a sanctioned surplus sovereign would want

Naturally a DECAYING/bounded contribution: the reserve pool is finite and small versus BTC's existing market cap, so the framework does not imply runaway returns — even a 5% all-reserve allocation only implies ~$130k-$410k, disciplining the bull case

Has real institutional sponsorship lending it credibility as a scenario (Deutsche Bank Research 2025 'room for both gold and Bitcoin by 2030'; CoinShares strategic-reserve rationale; 1-2% allocation recommendations from BlackRock/JPMorgan/WisdomTree), and live sovereign data points (El Salvador, US Strategic Bitcoin Reserve, Brazil RESBit proposal)
Probability-weighting makes it usable as an honest CMA tail input rather than a single hype target — the structure forces you to multiply a generous share by a tiny adoption probability
cons: The decisive empirical fact KILLS the base case: reserve-manager surveys show ~0% of central banks hold digital assets and 93% have NO intention (OMFIF GPI 2025, ~$5T reserves surveyed; UBS 2025: ~80% expect continued USD dominance). The thesis prices a transition that the actual decision-makers overwhelmingly reject — so the adoption probability is genuinely near-zero, not merely low

Bitcoin fails core reserve-asset criteria TODAY on the official sector's own terms: too volatile (~57% realized vs gold ~15%), too illiquid at sovereign size, no yield (negative carry), unproven track record, custody/legal/accounting opacity, and not used in cross-border trade — the Czech National Bank found 'no miraculous stabilising force' in diversification tests, and Rogoff (2026) calls it appealing-in-theory but unsuitable until it demonstrates gold-like stability

The 'neutral reserve' logic is self-undermining: the same volatility that makes BTC a poor reserve asset is required to deliver the high returns the bull case needs, and a stable enough BTC to qualify as a reserve asset would by construction have a LOW forward return — the thesis cannot have both

Active official-sector COUNTER-pressure: the IMF forced El Salvador to strip Bitcoin's mandatory legal-tender status as a $1.4B loan condition; BRICS de-dollarization statements are explicitly gradual and currency-/settlement-focused, not BTC-reserve adoption — incumbents will defend currency sovereignty (DB: policymakers will ensure digital assets 'do not threaten the sovereignty of their currencies')

Sizing is small and flow-multiplier-dependent: the reserve pool is modest versus BTC's existing ~$2T cap, so absent a large (and unproven) illiquidity multiplier the standalone reserve contribution to price is minor — most published 'reserve' price targets (e.g. $2.9M/2050) smuggle in heroic share AND multiplier assumptions

The anchor report is qualitative, not a CMA: Deutsche Bank publishes NO reserve-share number, price target, volatility forecast, or correlation — repurposing 'room for both by 2030' as a quantitative long-horizon assumption is a category error

Digital-gold premise is empirically unsupported for correlation: realized BTC-gold correlation is ~0, so even if BTC absorbs some of gold's reserve role, it does not co-move with gold — undercutting the 'BTC = digital gold reserve' framing the thesis leans on

Adjacent practitioner reserve-scenario figures exist but are not from the official sector: e.g. a '$2.9M by 2050' reserve-asset scenario (~16%/yr CAGR off ~$100k); 1-2% reserve-allocation recommendations (BlackRock/JPMorgan/WisdomTree); CoinShares strategic-reserve rationale (no point CMA). Implied price math (this study): 1-5% of $12.3T FX reserves as incremental demand on a ~$2T cap implies ~$107k-$410k depending on a 1x-10x flow multiplier.

cited_outputs.volatility: n/a as a forecast. Deutsche Bank notes BTC 30-day volatility 'hit historic lows in August 2025' even above $123,500 as a maturation signal, but publishes no annualized vol estimate; OMFIF/UBS/Rogoff cite high volatility qualitatively as the binding DISqualifier for reserve use (vs gold ~15%).
cited_outputs.corr_growth_eq: n/a (source silent)
cited_outputs.corr_gold: n/a as a published correlation. The thesis FRAMES BTC as gold's reserve analogue and benchmarks to gold's CB accumulation pace, implying co-valuation, but no source publishes a BTC-gold correlation in this context (and realized is ~0, contradicting the framing).
cited_outputs.notes: Official-sector sources (DB, OMFIF, UBS, Rogoff, IMF) are overwhelmingly QUALITATIVE; the only hard numbers are the reserve-pool size (~$12.3T), gold's CB buying pace (~1,045t/2024), and the survey rejection (0% hold, 93% no intent). All return/vol/correlation cells are 'n/a (source silent)' because no official-sector source publishes a quantitative BTC reserve-CMA. Quantitative price targets exist only in sell-side/crypto-native adjacent material and are flagged as such.

synthesized_outputs.appreciation_nominal: ~10-14%/yr (JUDGMENT, not a computed stat). Probability-weighting the reserve scenarios honestly: ~70% no-meaningful-adoption (BTC trades on other drivers, ~10%/yr on the realized-decay path) + ~20% modest ~1% reserve-share path (~18%/yr) + ~10% sovereign-FOMO 2-5% share tail (~28%/yr) yields ~13%/yr. Anchored to BTC's realized appreciation DECAY (142%→65%→17%) and to the structural fact that the reserve pool is small versus BTC's ~$2T cap, so the reserve channel adds at most a modest premium over the horizon. I sit at the LOW end (~10-12%) because the ~0% survey endorsement makes the adoption probability genuinely thin — most published reserve price targets over-weight a tail the decision-makers reject.
synthesized_outputs.appreciation_real: ~7-11%/yr real (subtracting ~2.5-3% long-run US inflation). Judgment; the de-dollarization/debasement narrative is a real-purchasing-power thesis, so the contribution should be framed in real terms, but it remains a tail premium, not the base case.
synthesized_outputs.volatility: ~55-60%/yr (JUDGMENT). The thesis NEEDS vol to fall toward gold-like ~15-28% for BTC to qualify as a reserve asset, but that has not occurred — realized trailing-5y ~57% is the floor and the sub-2yr ETF sample shows no durable compression. Note the internal contradiction: a BTC stable enough to be a reserve asset would have low forward return, so high vol and high return are joined.
synthesized_outputs.corr_growth_eq: ~+0.40 to +0.55 (JUDGMENT). The reserve thesis is silent; realized trailing-5y is +0.56 and has risen with institutionalization. Reserve adoption, if it came, is risk-on/liquidity-sensitive at the margin, so I expect only partial mean-reversion from the ETF-era spike — BTC stays a high-beta risk asset, contradicting the 'safe-haven reserve' premise.
synthesized_outputs.corr_value_eq: ~+0.25 to +0.35 (JUDGMENT). Below growth-equity; realized trailing-5y +0.37. BTC behaves as a long-duration risk asset with limited value-factor linkage.
synthesized_outputs.corr_fi_nominal: ~+0.10 to +0.20 (JUDGMENT). Low-positive via shared liquidity/real-rate sensitivity (realized trailing-5y +0.19); reserve framing adds no structural duration link.
synthesized_outputs.corr_tips: ~+0.20 to +0.30 (JUDGMENT). The de-dollarization/debasement channel gives a mild real-rate tilt shared with TIPS and gold (realized trailing-5y +0.30), but noisy and regime-dependent.
synthesized_outputs.corr_gold: ~0.0 to +0.15 (JUDGMENT). This is the approach's central internal contradiction: it benchmarks BTC to gold's reserve-accumulation role and frames it as a gold analogue, which would REQUIRE co-movement to justify the reserve-share substitution — yet realized BTC-gold correlation is ~0 (full -0.01, 5y +0.045). I keep it at the bottom of the band: if a shared de-dollarization regime intensifies, both could drift up together (lifting it modestly), but BTC is NOT empirically a gold substitute, so the digital-gold reserve framing is asserted, not measured.
synthesized_outputs.notes: Treat as a LOW-PROBABILITY TAIL-SHARE OVERLAY, not a base-case reserve-transition bet. The official sector's ~0% current endorsement (93% no intent) means the expected-value contribution is modest and the channel mainly adds upside skew in a small-probability sovereign-FOMO tail. Net 10-15yr: ~10-14% nominal, ~7-11% real, vol ~55-60%, gold corr ~0-0.15 — consistent with BTC's realized appreciation decay, deliberately NOT its history. The self-undermining vol/return tension and the asserted-not-measured gold correlation are the two honest reasons not to upweight this approach.

new_approaches.rich_notes:
WHAT MAKES THIS DISTINCT. Unlike #6 (private investable-gold TAM) and #7/#8 (M2 / quantity-theory monetary substitution), this approach targets the OFFICIAL SECTOR specifically: ~$12.3T of central-bank FX reserves (USD ~57%, gold ~20% at market per NY Fed Liberty Street, 2024) plus sovereign treasuries. The driver is geopolitical, not statistical — the Triffin dilemma (the reserve issuer must run external deficits to supply world liquidity, eroding confidence in its own unit) and dollar weaponization (the 2022 freeze of Russia's reserves) generate latent demand for a politically NEUTRAL, seizure-resistant, non-state-issued, fixed-supply reserve asset. Bitcoin is pitched as gold's digital analogue and explicitly BENCHMARKED to gold's central-bank accumulation pace: ~1,045 tonnes in 2024, the third straight year above 1,000t (World Gold Council), itself a measurable de-dollarization signal.

METHODOLOGY. Bottom-up and scenario-based: (1) size the addressable reserve pool; (2) assume a terminal Bitcoin SHARE by the horizon (1-5% of FX reserves is the practitioner band; live anchors: El Salvador holds ~7,474 BTC ≈ 14% of ITS OWN reserves, Brazil's RESBit proposal floats 5%); (3) apply an explicit sovereign-adoption PROBABILITY; (4) treat the result as incremental demand flow on top of BTC's existing ~$2T market cap, optionally with an illiquidity flow-multiplier; (5) divide by near-fixed supply and annualize. The load-bearing — and most honest — feature is that the share must be multiplied by a probability that the surveys put near zero.

THE DECISIVE SKEPTIC ANCHOR. OMFIF's Global Public Investor 2025 (surveying institutions representing ~$5T of reserves) found ZERO central banks hold digital assets, 93% have NO intention, and only 7% are even monitoring; 82% don't use and don't plan to use DLT. The UBS 2025 reserve-manager survey (~40 central banks) found ~80% expect continued USD dominance. The cited disqualifiers are exactly the reserve-asset criteria: volatility (~57% vs gold ~15%), illiquidity at sovereign size, negative carry, custody/legal/accounting opacity, and absence of cross-border trade use — the Czech National Bank's diversification tests found 'no miraculous stabilising force.' Kenneth Rogoff (Project Syndicate, Feb 2026) concedes the neutral-asset appeal is 'growing' but judges BTC unsuitable until it shows gold-like stability. And the official sector is actively HOSTILE at the margin: the IMF made a $1.4B loan to El Salvador conditional on stripping Bitcoin's mandatory legal-tender status (effective May 2025), and BRICS de-dollarization communiqués are explicitly gradual and local-currency/settlement-focused, not BTC-reserve adoption. Deutsche Bank itself (the bull anchor) cautions policymakers will ensure digital assets 'do not threaten the sovereignty of their currencies.'

ON-RECORD MULTI-YEAR FORECASTS PRODUCED THIS WAY. The flagship official-sector-adjacent piece — Deutsche Bank Research, 'Bitcoin vs. Gold: The Future of Central Bank Reserves by 2030' (Laboure & Siazon, Sep 2025) — is QUALITATIVE: 'room for both gold and Bitcoin to coexist on central bank balance sheets by 2030,' citing BTC's falling 30-day volatility (historic low in Aug 2025 even above $123,500) as a maturation signal, but it publishes NO reserve-share %, price target, vol forecast, or correlation. Practitioner reserve-scenario numbers exist but are crypto/sell-side, not official: a widely-circulated '$2.9M by 2050' reserve-asset scenario (~16%/yr off ~$100k), CoinShares' strategic-reserve rationale (no point CMA), and 1-2% reserve-allocation recommendations from BlackRock, JPMorgan and WisdomTree. My own implied-price check shows why the channel is bounded: 1-5% of $12.3T FX reserves as incremental flow on a ~$2T cap implies only ~$107k-$410k across a 1x-10x flow multiplier — i.e., absent heroic multiplier assumptions the standalone reserve contribution is modest.

FAILURE MODES. (1) The base case is empirically dead — ~0% endorsement means the adoption probability is near-zero, not low. (2) Self-undermining vol logic: the volatility that powers the bull return is precisely what disqualifies BTC as a reserve asset; a BTC stable enough to qualify would have a low forward return. (3) Digital-gold correlation is asserted, not measured (realized BTC-gold ~0), so the gold-benchmark framing lacks the co-movement it implies. (4) Sizing is multiplier-dependent and the pool is small versus BTC's cap. NET: I treat this as a genuine but LOW-PROBABILITY TAIL-SHARE overlay — it adds a modest premium and concentrates upside in a small-probability sovereign-FOMO tail, landing the probability-weighted 10-15yr nominal CMA at ~10-14%/yr (real ~7-11%), vol ~55-60%, gold corr ~0-0.15 — consistent with BTC's realized appreciation decay, NOT its history, and explicitly NOT a base-case reserve-transition bet.

issues: BASIS-MIXING on the reserve pool. The header pairs '~$12.3T; USD ~57%, gold ~20% at market' as if both shares describe one pool. They don't. The $12.3T COFER figure is ALLOCATED FX reserves and EXCLUDES monetary gold; USD ~57-58% is the share of that FX-only base; gold ~20-23% is a share of a DIFFERENT, broader 'total official reserve assets' base (and is a price-driven, not quantity-driven, rise per IMF). Stacking 57% USD + 20% gold on the same $12.3T double-counts categories. Conclusions don't change, but the framing is technically wrong and the DB anchor itself cites USD at 43% on a total-reserves basis, not 57% - so the study should disclose which base it is using.

STALE MARKET CAP. The study states BTC's existing cap is '~$2T' in at least four places and bases its implied-price math on it. Actual BTC market cap as of May 2026 is ~$1.3-1.5T (BTC ~$66-76k). This is not a rounding issue - it is ~30-45% too high. Direction of the error is notable: a SMALLER true cap means a given reserve inflow moves price MORE, so the channel is slightly understated by the study, but the headline number is simply wrong and should be repriced. Off a ~$1.4T base the 1-5% / 1x-10x grid yields ~$77k-$381k, not $107k-$410k.

MISATTRIBUTED '$2.9M by 2050' figure. The study calls it 'a widely-circulated $2.9M by 2050 reserve-asset scenario (~16%/yr)' and labels it generic 'crypto/sell-side.' It is specifically VanEck (Sigel & Bush). More importantly it is NOT a reserve-share model: VanEck's $2.9M base case is a VELOCITY-OF-MONEY model combining 5-10% of global TRADE SETTLEMENT plus 2.5% of CB balance sheets -> $61T cap. Citing it as a 'reserve' price target inside the reserve-share approach conflates it with the very M2/quantity-theory frameworks (#7/#8) the study claims this approach is orthogonal to. The ~16% CAGR also happens to nearly equal VanEck's reported 15% - fine - but the mechanism label is wrong.

DB ANCHOR DATE/HORIZON. Study dates the DB report 'Sep 2025' in places; press coverage (Bloomberg/Fortune/Yahoo) clusters early-mid Oct 2025 around the note's circulation. Minor, but the 'Sep 2025' vs publication timing should be reconciled. The qualitative-only characterization of the DB note is accurate and fairly stated (no share %, no price target, no vol/correlation) - that is the study's strongest and correctly-handled point.

142->65->17 decay is internal, not externally sourced. The specific trailing-CAGR ladder is this study's own computation and is not independently citable as-presented. The underlying claim (per-cycle diminishing returns as cap grows) is well-documented and directionally sound, so using it as the anchor for synthesized returns is defensible - but it should be flagged as a study-internal stat, not presented with the authority of an external figure.
verdict.corrections: "1) Replace '~$2T market cap' with '~$1.3-1.5T (as of May 2026)' everywhere and re-run the implied-price grid; off ~$1.4T the 1-5% share x 1x-10x multiplier yields ~$77k-$381k. 2) Fix the reserve-pool framing: state explicitly that $12.3T is COFER allocated FX reserves EXCLUDING gold, that USD ~57% is the share of that FX base, and that gold ~20-23% is a share of the broader total-reserve-assets base (price-driven), so the two shares are not additive on the same denominator. Note DB's own 43% USD figure is on the total-reserves basis. 3) Attribute the $2.9M/2050 figure to VanEck (Sigel & Bush) AND relabel it as a velocity-of-money / trade-settlement + 2.5% CB model, not a pure reserve-share target - it imports the M2/quantity-theory mechanism the study elsewhere treats as a separate approach. 4) Reconcile the DB report date (coverage clusters Oct 2025, not Sep). 5) Flag 142->65->17 as a study-internal trailing-CAGR computation. None of these overturn the bottom line: the OMFIF 0%/93%, WGC 1,045t, El Salvador 7,474 BTC / $1.4B IMF / legal-tender strip, Brazil RESBit 5% of ~$370B, Rogoff Feb-2026 'unsuitable until gold-like stability,' BTC vol ~52-57% vs gold ~15%, and BTC-gold corr ~0 all verify cleanly. The synthesized ~10-14% nominal / vol ~55-60% / gold-corr ~0-0.15 is defensible and correctly weighted to the realized-decay path rather than BTC's history."
overstated_pros: Pro #4 'real institutional sponsorship lending it credibility' overstates the official-sector endorsement. The named sponsors (DB qualitative-only, CoinShares = crypto-native asset manager, BlackRock/JPMorgan/WisdomTree = sell-side product issuers with a book to talk, VanEck = the $2.9M author) are all SELL-SIDE or crypto-native. Zero are official-sector reserve managers - and the study's own decisive con is that the actual reserve managers reject it 0%/93%. The pro should say 'sell-side/issuer sponsorship,' which is weaker evidence than 'institutional sponsorship' implies.

Pro #2's claim that dollar weaponization 'measurably accelerated gold diversification' is true for GOLD but is used here to lend plausibility to BTC reserve demand - the same sources (OMFIF) show the post-2022 diversification went into gold and non-USD currencies, NOT digital assets. The pro borrows gold's adoption signal for BTC without evidence of transfer.

Pro #3 frames the bounded/decaying contribution as a virtue ('disciplining the bull case'), which is fair, but the $130k-$410k cap it cites is built on the stale $2T cap; on the correct ~$1.4T cap the same allocations imply a lower floor (~$77k at 1% x 1x), modestly weakening even the disciplined-bull framing.
missing_cons: NO opportunity-cost / yield-drag con is stated from the issuer side. A reserve manager comparing BTC to USTs forgoes ~4-5% risk-free carry; the study mentions 'negative carry' as a disqualifier but never sizes the hurdle BTC must clear to be reserve-competitive on a risk-adjusted basis.

SUPPLY is treated as 'near-fixed' but the study never addresses that a sovereign-FOMO tail would itself be partly met by EXISTING holders selling into strength (ETF/treasury-company float), not only by price. The implied-price math assumes the entire reserve flow hits an inelastic float at the flow-multiplier - the multiplier is asserted (1x-10x) with no empirical anchor, and the upside tail leans heavily on the unproven high end.

CONCENTRATION / custody-attack con missing: a 'seizure-resistant neutral reserve' thesis ignores that sovereign-scale BTC custody concentrates a seizable/coercible operational target (key management, exchange/custodian chokepoints, mining-pool and protocol governance) - the neutrality is theoretical, not operational, at sovereign size.

REFLEXIVITY / circularity of the US Strategic Bitcoin Reserve data point is unaddressed: the study lists the US SBR as a live bullish anchor, but the US reserve was seized/forfeiture BTC, explicitly NOT to be added to via market purchases in the founding EO - so it is not net new reserve DEMAND and arguably should not be counted as adoption-flow evidence.

The vol/return internal-contradiction con (well-stated) has a flip side not mentioned: if BTC vol DID compress to gold-like levels via maturation WITHOUT reserve adoption (the DB 'maturation' path), the reserve thesis becomes redundant - i.e., the channel may never be the marginal driver even in its own success case.

new_approaches.name: Cagan/Jermann Dynamic Money-Demand (Real-Balances, Adoption-Shock Structural)
new_approaches.description: A dynamic, expectations-driven structural money-demand model that treats a cryptocurrency like a fiat money in Cagan's (1956) hyperinflation framework. Demand for real balances depends negatively on the expected rate of price change (currency appreciation/depreciation) via an estimated semi-elasticity; combined with a market-clearing condition (transaction volume / money supply), this makes today's price the forward present value of a stochastic stream of ADOPTION and VELOCITY shocks plus endogenous expectations of future prices. Jermann (2021, Journal of Macroeconomics 69) estimates the model for Bitcoin and Ethereum using prices, transaction volumes, and money supplies, and finds that the MAJORITY of price variance is driven by adoption shocks, with velocity shocks much less important; the estimated money-demand sensitivity to expected price changes is larger for Bitcoin than Ethereum, and larger for both than for fiat currencies in historical hyperinflations. Because the Cagan difference equation has a saddle-path fundamental solution plus a continuum of explosive solutions, the framework formally ADMITS self-fulfilling speculative (hyper)inflation/deflation bubbles and a money-demand externality (each adopter raises others' real balances). It is a variance-explanation / structural-estimation model, NOT a return forecaster: it does not publish appreciation, volatility, or cross-asset correlation. A 10-15yr CMA only falls out if you bolt on an exogenous adoption-S-curve path and impose the fundamental (non-bubble) equilibrium, in which case appreciation must DECAY as adoption saturates.
new_approaches.medium_explanation: Jermann (2021) ports Cagan's hyperinflation model onto crypto: people hold real balances of BTC that fall when they expect BTC to lose value and rise when they expect gains, governed by an estimated semi-elasticity. Market-clearing against transaction volume and coin supply makes price the forward present value of a stochastic stream of adoption and velocity shocks plus self-referential price expectations. Estimating on prices, volumes and money supplies, he finds adoption shocks explain the MAJORITY of BTC price variance (velocity is minor), and BTC's demand-sensitivity to expected price changes exceeds Ethereum's and exceeds fiat hyperinflation currencies'. The same difference equation admits, beyond the saddle-path fundamental, a continuum of explosive self-fulfilling bubble equilibria, plus a money-demand externality. For a 10-15yr CMA this is diagnostic, not predictive: it says the return engine is adoption growth, which is an S-curve that must decelerate, forcing appreciation DECAY toward a low, debasement-plus-residual-adoption rate. The high estimated semi-elasticity also implies a structurally high-volatility, fragile-equilibrium asset whose price can jump between fundamental and speculative branches.
key_drivers: Adoption shocks (stochastic growth in number of users / scale of monetary demand) — estimated to drive the MAJORITY of BTC price variance
Velocity shocks (changes in how fast the coin circulates / transaction demand) — present but found to be a minor variance contributor

Estimated money-demand semi-elasticity to expected price change (the Cagan alpha) — larger for BTC than ETH, and larger than fiat hyperinflation currencies; governs how forward expectations are discounted into today's price
Endogenous, self-referential price expectations — today's price depends on the expected future price, creating the forward-PV structure and the scope for self-fulfilling dynamics
Equilibrium selection: saddle-path fundamental solution vs the continuum of explosive self-fulfilling (hyper)inflation/deflation bubble solutions (transversality condition rules bubbles in or out)
Money-demand externality / network effect (each new adopter raises the real balances and value of existing holders)
Coin supply / money-supply path (the deterministic issuance schedule entering the market-clearing condition)
pros: Genuinely structural and dynamic — unlike the static MV=PT/QTM accounting identity (which imposes velocity), this ESTIMATES demand-for-real-balances dynamics and a semi-elasticity from data on prices, transaction volumes and money supplies, then decomposes variance into economically-named shocks

Empirically isolates the return engine: rigorously attributes the MAJORITY of BTC price variance to ADOPTION (not velocity), which is exactly the right primitive for a CMA — adoption is an S-curve, so the model's own logic implies appreciation must decay as the network matures

Grounded in a respected, peer-reviewed macro-monetary tradition (Cagan 1956; Journal of Macroeconomics), with an explicit microfoundation for why a no-cashflow money can have a positive, time-varying value

Honest about fragility: by admitting self-fulfilling speculative equilibria and a high estimated semi-elasticity, it provides a principled explanation for BTC's extreme volatility and crash risk rather than assuming it away — useful discipline for the risk side of a CMA
Falsifiable and refreshable: the state-space/Kalman estimation can be re-run as data accrues, and the relative BTC-vs-ETH-vs-fiat semi-elasticity ranking is a testable cross-asset prediction
cons: It is NOT a return-forecasting model. Jermann publishes a variance decomposition and structural parameters, not an expected appreciation, volatility, or correlation. Any 10-15yr CMA requires bolting on an exogenous adoption path and arbitrarily selecting the fundamental (non-bubble) equilibrium — neither is delivered by the paper

Multiple-equilibria indeterminacy is fatal for point forecasting: the Cagan difference equation admits a continuum of explosive self-fulfilling paths alongside the fundamental one, so the model cannot, on its own, tell you which equilibrium the world is on — the expected return is not pinned down without an ad hoc transversality/selection assumption

Adoption shocks are essentially a residual / latent state — labeling the dominant variance component 'adoption' is partly definitional (it absorbs everything not velocity or supply), so the strong 'adoption drives BTC' result risks being a relabeling of the unexplained trend rather than a measured fundamental

Hyperinflation analogy is strained: Cagan's model was built for currencies LOSING value with accelerating money supply; BTC has fixed supply and (historically) gained value, so the framework is run in reverse and the high estimated semi-elasticity may reflect speculative, not transactional, money demand

Silent on cross-asset structure: provides no mechanism or estimate for BTC's correlation to equities, bonds, TIPS, or gold — the entire portfolio-construction half of a CMA must be imported from realized data

Short, regime-shifting sample (largely 2013-2020 in the original estimation) predating ETFs/institutionalization; the estimated semi-elasticity and adoption dynamics may not be structurally stable post-2024
