cited_outputs.notes: Jermann (2021) is a structural-estimation / variance-decomposition paper, not a forecasting paper. Its publishable quantitative outputs are: (i) a variance decomposition in which ADOPTION shocks explain the MAJORITY of BTC and ETH price variance and velocity shocks are minor; (ii) an estimated money-demand semi-elasticity to expected price change that is larger for BTC than ETH and larger for both than for fiat hyperinflation currencies. It publishes NO appreciation rate, NO annualized volatility, and NO cross-asset correlation — hence every CMA cell above is 'n/a (source silent)'. There are also NO on-record dated multi-year price targets produced by this framework.

synthesized_outputs.appreciation_nominal: ~8-12%/yr nominal (judgment, not a model output). The model's central finding — adoption shocks drive the MAJORITY of price variance — combined with the fundamental (non-bubble) equilibrium selection, means decade-forward appreciation tracks the GROWTH RATE of adoption-driven real-balance demand. Adoption is an S-curve that must decelerate, so the realized appreciation decay (142%->65%->17%/yr full/10y/5y) is exactly what the model predicts. Extrapolating the maturing portion of the S-curve plus a fiat-debasement floor lands a 10-15yr nominal CMA at roughly low double digits, BELOW the trailing-5y 17%. I deliberately select the fundamental branch and discard the explosive self-fulfilling equilibria the framework also admits.
synthesized_outputs.appreciation_real: ~5-9%/yr real (subtract ~2.5-3% long-run US inflation). The residual real premium is whatever genuine adoption growth remains after maturation, net of the debasement component that is itself just nominal.
synthesized_outputs.volatility: ~55-65%/yr (judgment). The model's high estimated money-demand semi-elasticity (above fiat hyperinflations) plus the admitted multiple/explosive equilibria imply a structurally fragile, expectations-amplified price — so vol stays elevated. Floor anchored at realized trailing-5y ~57% (no compression below realized yet evidenced), with the top of the band reflecting the model's emphasis on self-fulfilling jumps between equilibrium branches.
synthesized_outputs.corr_growth_eq: ~0.40-0.55 (judgment). The model is silent on cross-asset structure, so this is anchored to realized trailing-5y ~0.56. Adoption shocks are risk-on/liquidity-sensitive, so BTC behaves as a high-beta growth/tech proxy; I allow mild mean-reversion from the ETF-era spike.
synthesized_outputs.corr_value_eq: ~0.25-0.35 (judgment; realized trailing-5y 0.37). BTC shares less of the value-factor cashflow beta.
synthesized_outputs.corr_fi_nominal: ~0.10-0.20 (judgment; realized trailing-5y 0.19). Weakly positive via shared liquidity/real-rate sensitivity of the marginal institutional holder; the money-demand framing gives no strong duration link.
synthesized_outputs.corr_tips: ~0.20-0.30 (judgment; realized trailing-5y 0.30). Slightly above nominal FI through the real-balance/debasement channel, but noisy and regime-dependent.
synthesized_outputs.corr_gold: ~0.0-0.15 (judgment). The model is purely own-currency (transaction volume vs money supply) and supplies NO gold mechanism; realized BTC-gold correlation is ~0 (full -0.01, 5y +0.045). I hold it at the low end.
synthesized_outputs.notes: All synthesized figures are reasoned judgment, NOT model outputs — Jermann (2021) forecasts nothing. The one genuine model-derived steer is the appreciation SHAPE: because adoption shocks dominate variance and adoption follows a decelerating S-curve, a credible 10-15yr CMA must extrapolate BTC's realized appreciation DECAY (142%->65%->17%/yr), not its level, landing ~8-12% nominal / ~5-9% real. The high estimated semi-elasticity and multiple-equilibria fragility justify keeping vol elevated (~55-65%). Correlations are pure realized-data anchors since the framework is silent and own-currency. Unlike the gold-parity/SoV models, this framework makes NO claim that BTC absorbs gold's monetary share, so there is no internal contradiction in the near-zero gold correlation — it simply predicts nothing about gold, consistent with the data.

new_approaches.rich_notes:
METHODOLOGY. Jermann (2021, Journal of Macroeconomics vol. 69, DOI 10.1016/j.jmacro.2021.103340; SSRN 3132050, working version 2018 titled 'Bitcoin and Cagan's Model of Hyperinflation') adapts Phillip Cagan's (1956) hyperinflation money-demand model to cryptocurrencies. Cagan's primitive is a log-linear demand for real money balances that depends NEGATIVELY on the expected rate of change of the price level (here, expected currency depreciation/appreciation), governed by a single semi-elasticity parameter (alpha). Imposing market clearing — money supply against transaction/velocity demand — yields a forward-looking difference equation in which the current price equals the discounted present value of an expected stream of future fundamentals (adoption and velocity) plus the expected future price. Jermann makes adoption and velocity STOCHASTIC, writes the system in state-space form, and estimates it (Kalman-filter/likelihood) on Bitcoin and Ethereum using observed prices, transaction volumes, and money supplies.

KEY RELATIONSHIPS / RESULTS. (1) Variance decomposition: 'A majority of price fluctuations in both currencies can be attributed to shocks in adoption; velocity shocks are much less important.' This is the paper's headline and the reason it is distinct from the static QTM/MV=PT identity (existing digest row #8), which imposes velocity rather than estimating demand dynamics. (2) Estimated money-demand sensitivity (the Cagan semi-elasticity) to expected price changes is LARGER for Bitcoin than Ethereum, and larger for both than for fiat currencies during historical hyperinflations (Cagan's original German/Hungarian/etc. estimates). A higher semi-elasticity means money demand is more responsive to expected returns — i.e., more speculative and more prone to large price swings for a given fundamental shock. (3) Endogenous self-referential expectations are essential: price today depends on expected price tomorrow.

FAILURE MODES / CRITIQUES (represented faithfully). The Cagan difference equation has the classic indeterminacy: a unique saddle-path 'fundamental' solution AND a continuum of explosive solutions that are rational self-fulfilling (hyper)inflation/deflation bubbles. The framework therefore FORMALLY ADMITS speculative bubbles — which connects to the empirical 'fundamental value of zero / pure speculative bubble' findings (Cheah & Fry 2015, Economics Letters; Cheung-Roca-Su) — but cannot select among equilibria without an imposed transversality condition. For a CMA this is decisive: the model does not pin down an expected return; you must assume the fundamental branch. A second critique: the dominant 'adoption' shock is a latent state that absorbs the unexplained trending component, so 'adoption drives BTC' is partly a relabeling of the trend rather than an independently measured fundamental (the same non-stationarity worry that sinks S2F/Metcalfe, though Jermann's structural form is more disciplined). Third, the hyperinflation analogy runs in reverse — Cagan modeled currencies LOSING value under accelerating money growth; BTC has fixed supply and rising value, so the estimated high semi-elasticity may reflect speculative rather than transactional demand. Fourth, the original sample is short and pre-ETF (largely 2013-2020), so parameter stability into the institutional era is unverified. Finally, the model is silent on every cross-asset correlation a portfolio CMA needs.

ON-RECORD MULTI-YEAR FORECASTS. None. This is the single most important fact about using the approach for a CMA: Jermann produces NO forward price, appreciation, volatility, or correlation forecast — it is an explanatory/structural-estimation paper, not a predictive one. Unlike S2F, power-law, or gold-parity models, the Cagan/Jermann framework has never been published as a dated multi-year price target, and doing so would require selecting the fundamental equilibrium and supplying an exogenous adoption-S-curve path. Its honest CMA contribution is QUALITATIVE-INTO-QUANTITATIVE: it tells you (a) the return engine is adoption, which is a decelerating S-curve, so a credible forward CMA must extrapolate the realized appreciation DECAY (142%->65%->17%/yr), not the level — landing a defensible ~8-12% nominal / ~5-9% real central; and (b) the high estimated semi-elasticity plus multiple-equilibria fragility justify keeping volatility elevated (~55-65%) and not assuming convergence to gold-like calm. It provides no support for any 'digital gold' correlation claim, consistent with the realized near-zero BTC-gold correlation.

issues: FABRICATED/WRONG REALIZED ANCHOR (most serious): The cited realized appreciation decay '142%->65%->17%/yr (full/10y/5y)' has a trailing-5y figure of 17%/yr that is wrong by ~3-4x. BTC May-2020 (~$9.5k) to May-2025 (~$104k) is a ~58%/yr 5-year CAGR; public sources put trailing-5y at ~58-155% depending on endpoint/method. 17% is not reproducible from any standard window. This is load-bearing: the entire 'decay justifies low double digits' argument and the claim '8-12% is BELOW trailing-5y 17%' both rest on it.

VOLATILITY DIRECTION IS BACKWARDS: digest asserts 'no compression below realized yet evidenced' and floors vol at ~57%. Public data shows BTC 1y realized vol at ~54% as of early 2025 and ACTIVELY compressing post-ETF, with BlackRock/iShares and Fidelity Digital Assets both arguing for further structural decline. The premise that compression is unevidenced is false; a 55-65% forward band with a hard 57% floor over a 10-15yr horizon ignores the documented maturation trend the model's own S-curve logic would predict.

INTERNAL INCONSISTENCY FROM THE BAD ANCHOR: the framing 'I land ~8-12%, deliberately below the trailing-5y 17%' implies a mild, conservative haircut. With the true trailing-5y ~58%, an 8-12% forecast is actually an ~80% haircut off realized 5y - a far more aggressive call than presented. The decay 'shape' argument survives qualitatively but the calibration is mis-anchored.

10y anchor (65%) is also questionable: commonly cited BTC 10y CAGR figures cluster ~60-84%; 65% is within range but on the low side and not sourced. Less serious than the 5y error but part of the same unsourced realized-decay sequence that should be scripted, not asserted.

EQUITY-CORR ANCHOR slightly stale/low: realized BTC-equity correlation trailing-5y is cited as ~0.56 and forecast 0.40-0.55 with 'mild mean-reversion.' Post-ETF data shows BTC-equity correlation has RISEN toward 0.5-0.9 and BTC increasingly trading as a risk asset (0.76 vs equities per 2025 data). Forecasting mean-reversion DOWN runs against the realized direction; the model itself ('adoption shocks are risk-on/liquidity-sensitive') argues for stable-or-higher, not lower.
verdict.corrections: ["Replace the realized 5y appreciation '17%/yr' with the correct ~55-60%/yr (BTC ~$9.5k May-2020 -> ~$104k May-2025 = ~58% CAGR). Re-run the full decay sequence as a SCRIPTED calculation from a price series (per the user's scripted-analysis rule) rather than asserting 142/65/17. If a 17% figure exists it must be from a cherry-picked window ending at a drawdown trough and should not be used as THE trailing-5y anchor.", "Re-anchor the appreciation forecast logic honestly: state that 8-12% nominal is an ~80% haircut off the true ~58% trailing-5y, justified by S-curve deceleration - do NOT claim it is 'just below' realized. The decay-shape argument is the defensible part; the level calibration needs rebuilding on correct realized numbers.", "Fix the volatility narrative: acknowledge documented post-ETF compression (~54% 1y and falling per BlackRock/Fidelity). A 10-15yr vol of 45-60% with a declining path is more defensible than a 55-65% band floored at 57% with 'no compression evidenced.' Cite the compression evidence rather than denying it.", "Update equity-correlation: realized has risen post-ETF; forecast stable-to-higher (0.45-0.65), not mean-reverting down to 0.40-0.55. This is also more consistent with the digest's own 'adoption = risk-on' mechanism.", "Keep the paper attribution as-is - DOI 10.1016/j.jmacro.2021.103340, JoM v69, the adoption>velocity variance result, BTC>ETH>fiat semi-elasticity ranking, and the 'n/a source silent' on all CMA cells are all correctly stated and appropriately conservative."]
overstated_pros: 'The realized appreciation decay (142%->65%->17%/yr) is exactly what the model predicts' - the rhetorical force of this depends on the 17% being real. With true 5y ~58%, the data shows FAR less decay than claimed, so the model's S-curve story, while directionally fine, is oversold as 'exactly' matching a decay that is largely fabricated at the 5y point.

'Empirically isolates the return engine ... attributes the MAJORITY of variance to adoption' is partly undercut by the digest's own con that adoption is a latent residual absorbing the trend - the pro presents as a measured fundamental what the con admits is partly a relabeling. The pro slightly overstates the empirical content.

'Falsifiable and refreshable ... testable cross-asset prediction' - the only cross-asset prediction is the BTC>ETH>fiat semi-elasticity ranking, which is intra-crypto/vs-hyperinflation, NOT a portfolio cross-asset (equity/bond/gold) prediction. Calling it cross-asset oversells its CMA usefulness; the framework is explicitly silent on the correlations a CMA needs.
missing_cons: NO published exact variance-decomposition percentage is verifiable from the open record (abstract says 'majority,' full numbers paywalled). The digest leans on 'MAJORITY' repeatedly as if precise; a con should note the headline magnitude itself is not independently checkable without the paywalled paper.

Survivorship/endpoint sensitivity of ALL realized anchors: BTC CAGR swings enormously with start/end date (full-history can read 140%+ or 80% depending on inception treatment; 5y can read 17% or 155%). The digest treats single point estimates as facts; a CMA con should flag that every realized anchor is endpoint-fragile and must be scripted with a stated window.

Liquidity/leverage-regime con absent: adoption shocks are explicitly 'risk-on/liquidity-sensitive,' which means the appreciation engine is conditional on a benign global-liquidity regime - a multi-year liquidity drought would break the S-curve extrapolation. The model gives no path-dependence guard.

ETF/institutional structural break is mentioned for parameter stability but NOT carried through to the forecasts: post-2024 the asset's vol, equity-beta, and gold-decoupling all shifted regime, yet the synthesized correlations still lean on pre/peri-ETF realized anchors. The regime-break con is acknowledged then ignored in calibration.

new_approaches.name: Eurodollar / Shadow-Money BTC-as-Collateral (Snider)
new_approaches.description: Jeffrey Snider's framework inverts the money-growth/debasement premise that underwrites most BTC monetary theses. In his reading the global dollar system is not fiat run by the Fed but the offshore, private, ledger-money eurodollar system — and that system has been chronically SHORT of dollars and (post-2008) short of pristine, rehypothecatable collateral. The binding constraint is currency/credit INELASTICITY and a "deflationary collateral path," not inflation or debasement. Bitcoin, in Snider's telling, is "ghost money" — a natural, market-driven human response to monetary shortfall, paralleling medieval bills of exchange during the Great Bullion Famine — that emerges precisely because the system cannot supply enough elastic money/collateral. Crucially this is a CONTRARIAN directional claim: the dollar is NOT collapsing, money printing is "more PR than policy," and the inflationist narrative on which most BTC-up theses rest is, to Snider, simply wrong. As a CMA mechanism it is a balance-sheet/plumbing story with two channels: (1) BTC bid as a hedge against monetary DISORDER (recurrent dollar/collateral shortages causing volatility), and (2) a latent collateral-quality channel where, IF BTC were ever accepted as repo/credit collateral, its value would carry a haircut/rehypothecation premium. Snider himself publishes NO price target, return, volatility, or correlation figure — he is structurally forecast-averse and indeed a bitcoin skeptic on the question of it imminently replacing the eurodollar. A 10-15yr CMA must therefore be SYNTHESIZED from the mechanism, and the mechanism's honest implication is appreciation BELOW the debasement-bull case, because the central debasement tailwind is denied.
new_approaches.medium_explanation: Snider treats the real dollar system as the private offshore eurodollar network, which since 2008 has been chronically short of money and pristine collateral — a deflationary, not inflationary, condition. Bitcoin is "ghost money": a market-driven response to that shortage (like medieval bills of exchange in the Great Bullion Famine), not a debasement hedge. The contrarian core: the dollar is NOT collapsing and "money printing" is largely myth, so the inflationist premise behind most BTC theses is wrong. Key inputs for a CMA are the eurodollar collateral cycle (Treasury scarcity, repo/SOFR stress, haircuts, rehypothecation) and BTC's observed tendency to sink during acute dollar-shortage episodes (Snider cites 2017→2018). For a 10-15yr BTC CMA this implies: appreciation driven by slow ghost-money adoption plus episodic monetary-disorder bids — but materially LOWER than debasement bulls, since the debasement tailwind is denied; vol stays high (disorder is recurrent); and the BTC–gold linkage is weak because both are framed as symptoms of the same shortage, not substitutes.
key_drivers: Eurodollar/shadow-dollar shortage cycle — chronic offshore dollar scarcity (Snider's 'Euro$ #1-#5' tightening episodes) as the master variable; BTC reportedly weak when the dollar catches a shortage bid (e.g., 2017 peak → 2018 collapse)

Pristine-collateral scarcity — shortage of rehypothecatable Treasuries/on-the-run bills constrains credit creation; the 'deflationary collateral path.' A latent channel where BTC could carry a collateral-quality (haircut/rehypothecation) premium IF accepted as repo collateral — currently it is not
Currency/credit INELASTICITY as the binding problem (not debasement) — ghost money emerges to add elasticity the official system cannot supply
Contrarian dollar view — the dollar is NOT collapsing; persistent dollar STRENGTH during shortages; 'money printing' is PR, bank reserves are inert

Slow ghost-money adoption S-curve — cryptos are 'long run, not short run' ghost money; the eurodollar 'isn't going anywhere for quite a long time,' so BTC's monetary role builds over decades, not cycles
Monetary-disorder hedge demand — recurrent plumbing dysfunction (repo spikes, SOFR stress, collateral runs) generates episodic safe-haven/alternative-money bids, but ALSO episodic forced liquidations
pros: Mechanistically grounded in real, observable plumbing (eurodollar/repo/collateral markets, haircuts, rehypothecation) rather than price-curve numerology (S2F/power-law) — it is a balance-sheet story with a falsifiable directional claim

Genuinely contrarian and non-redundant: it is the ONLY approach in the set that denies the debasement premise, predicts dollar STRENGTH, and would therefore haircut the bullish monetary case — a valuable bear/skeptic anchor against the M2-elasticity, gold-parity, and debasement-hedge entries that all assume the opposite

Explains a real empirical regularity: BTC tends to sell off hard during acute dollar-shortage / liquidity-crunch episodes (Mar-2020, 2022), consistent with the framework's claim that monetary disorder triggers forced de-leveraging, not flight-to-BTC

Forces an honest treatment of BTC as a high-beta risk/liquidity asset rather than a pristine safe haven — aligns with the realized data (equity corr rising to +0.56 trailing-5y) better than the digital-gold narratives do

Self-disciplined: Snider refuses price targets and is openly skeptical that BTC replaces the eurodollar 'for quite a long time,' which guards against the over-extrapolation that plagues crypto-native models
cons: The author's central macro call has been PERSISTENTLY WRONG on the decisive 2021-2022 episode: Snider forecast deflation/disinflation and dollar shortage precisely as US CPI hit ~9%. If the deflationary-collateral premise is empirically false at the moment it most mattered, a CMA built on it inherits that fragility — the contrarian directional claim is the model's load-bearing beam and it has cracked

It is NOT a return model at all: Snider publishes no appreciation, volatility, or correlation figure. Every CMA cell must be synthesized off the mechanism plus realized data, so the framework supplies a STORY and a sign, not a number — weak for populating a quantitative CMA grid

Internally ambivalent on BTC: Snider is a self-described bitcoin SKEPTIC who says the eurodollar 'isn't going anywhere,' that El Salvador's adoption was incoherent, and that BTC is only long-run ghost money. The framework can be read as bearish-to-neutral on BTC as much as constructive — it does not cleanly yield an UP thesis

The collateral-quality channel is largely hypothetical for BTC: bitcoin is essentially NOT accepted as pristine repo/credit collateral in size; its volatility makes the haircut prohibitive. So the most distinctive mechanism (BTC-as-collateral premium) is a latent possibility, not a current value driver — the channel may never activate

Austrian/mainstream critics argue Snider has causality inverted (too much credit, not too little money; deflation = malinvestment liquidation, not broken plumbing), and that post-2020 inflation falsified the shortage thesis — the framework is contested even within heterodox macro
Shares the spurious-signal risk of all monetary-macro BTC stories: 'BTC weak during dollar shortages' is a small handful of episodes; n is tiny and the relationship is not a stable, estimable beta

new_approaches.rich_notes:
METHODOLOGY. Jeffrey Snider (Alhambra Partners; "Eurodollar University") is a practitioner macro analyst, not an academic, and his BTC view is a corollary of his eurodollar framework rather than a standalone valuation model. The core claim: the operative global dollar system is the private, offshore, ledger-money "eurodollar" network, which since 2008 has been chronically short of money and — critically — short of PRISTINE, rehypothecatable collateral (on-the-run Treasuries/T-bills). This produces a "deflationary collateral path," and the binding macro problem is currency/credit INELASTICITY, not debasement. Bitcoin enters as "ghost money": a natural, market-driven response to monetary shortfall, explicitly analogized to medieval bills of exchange during the Great Bullion Famine. The distinctive, non-redundant feature versus every other entry in the digest is the CONTRARIAN SIGN: the dollar is NOT collapsing, "money printing" is "more PR than policy," bank reserves are inert, and the inflationist premise underwriting the M2-elasticity, gold-parity, and debasement-hedge theses is — in Snider's view — simply wrong.

KEY RELATIONSHIPS / QUOTES. From "Monetary Wrongness Has Authored a Crypto Response" (RealClearMarkets, 2021), Snider frames crypto as a response to "the central bank response to an otherwise severe and constraining monetary shortage," and dismisses the debasement fear: those inflationary outcomes "never happen." He cites the 2017→2018 episode directly — when "the dollar instead caught its Euro$ #4 bid, renewed acute shortage, Bitcoin's price sunk like a rock" — which is the framework's one durable, falsifiable empirical regularity: BTC is WEAK during acute dollar/collateral shortages. He calls bubbles "a minor if ugly detail in an otherwise very familiar, ultimately successful longer-term story." In "Bitcoin, El Salvador, And…The Eurodollar's Ghost" (2021) he is openly skeptical of BTC as an imminent eurodollar replacement: "Cryptos are (long run, not short run) ghost money… the eurodollar, the true reserve, isn't going anywhere for quite a long time." This is the load-bearing nuance: the framework is bearish-to-neutral on BTC's near/medium-term monetary role and constructive only on a multi-decade ghost-money S-curve.

THE COLLATERAL CHANNEL. The "BTC-as-collateral" leg that makes this approach distinct (a haircut/rehypothecation, collateral-QUALITY premium) is largely LATENT for bitcoin. Snider's collateral analysis is about Treasuries; BTC is essentially not accepted as pristine repo collateral in size, and its volatility makes the haircut prohibitive. So the most novel mechanism is a possibility, not a current price driver — and a fair CMA cannot lean on it.

HISTORICAL FIT & FAILURE MODES. The framework's central macro call was persistently, decisively WRONG on 2021-2022: Snider forecast deflation/disinflation and a dollar shortage precisely as US CPI peaked near 9%. Because the deflationary-collateral premise is the model's beam, a CMA built on it inherits that fragility. Austrian critics (DyingEconomy.com) argue the causality is inverted — "the world's problem since 1971 has not been too little money but too much credit," deflation is "the market's belated attempt to liquidate malinvestment," and post-2020 inflation falsified the shortage thesis. Mainstream readers note BTC's behavior is at least as consistent with a plain high-beta-risk-asset story as with a bespoke eurodollar mechanism. The honest read: Snider supplies a mechanism and a sign, not a number; the sign (dollar strength, BTC weak in shortages) has mixed-to-poor recent fit.

ON-RECORD MULTI-YEAR FORECASTS. None numeric. Snider is structurally forecast-averse and publishes NO BTC price target, return, vol, or correlation. The only on-record multi-year claim is qualitative directional: crypto survives long-run as ghost money ("ultimately successful longer-term story"), but the eurodollar remains the true reserve "for quite a long time," and BTC should sink during dollar-shortage episodes. There is therefore no published CMA to cite — all numeric cells are "n/a (source silent)," and the synthesized grid is anchored to the realized decay baseline with the framework supplying only the contrarian haircut (appreciation toward the LOW end, ~6-10% nominal) and the disorder-driven high-vol (~55-65%) and high-equity-correlation (+0.45 to +0.60) tilts, which the mechanism genuinely predicts. The BTC-gold correlation stays near zero — and, unlike the digital-gold theses, that is CONSISTENT with Snider's framing of BTC and gold as parallel symptoms of one monetary shortage rather than substitutes.

issues: The synthesized appreciation band (~6-10% nominal) is presented as 'anchored to the realized decay 142->65->17%' but actually sits BELOW the lowest realized window (trailing-5y 17%). This is internally defensible for an explicitly-labeled bear/skeptic anchor that denies the debasement leg, but the word 'anchored' slightly oversells the link: it is anchored to the DIRECTION of decay and extrapolated further down by judgment, not pinned to any realized number. Should read 'extrapolating the decay trend past the realized 5y' rather than 'anchored to.'

The 'El Salvador's adoption was incoherent' phrasing in the cons is a paraphrase, not a verified Snider quote. The verified article actually frames El Salvador as 'perfectly consistent with... the still-failing eurodollar reserve regime' -- Snider treats it as a symptom he is skeptical of, but the specific word 'incoherent' is the agent's gloss. Low-stakes but should be softened or quote-checked.

The framework's single durable empirical regularity -- 'BTC weak during acute dollar shortages' -- rests on a tiny n (2017->2018, Mar-2020, 2022). The entry's own con #6 admits this ('n is tiny, not a stable estimable beta'), which is correct, but the synthesized corr_growth_eq band (+0.45 to +0.60) is then justified partly BY this same thin mechanism while also tracking realized +0.56. The number is fine because it tracks realized data; just note the mechanism does not independently earn the precision implied.

Source #4 (Bitcoin Magazine 'Bitcoin Can Save Us From Ghost Money') is correctly flagged as 'engaging Snider's thesis' rather than authored by him -- good. But it is a pro-BTC rebuttal/appropriation of Snider, so citing it as a representative source for HIS framework slightly muddies provenance. Not an error, just worth a reader caveat.

The TIPS correlation band (+0.15 to +0.30) is explicitly admitted to be 'mostly realized-data extrapolation' with 'no strong real-rate-hedge mechanism' -- honest, but it means that cell is not actually a product of the Snider framework at all; it is the empirical baseline wearing the framework's label. Same is partially true of value_eq and fi_nom cells.
verdict.corrections: All cited Snider quotes are verbatim-accurate and correctly attributed. Verified against primary sources: (1) RealClearMarkets 'Monetary Wrongness Has Authored a Crypto Response' (2021) -- confirmed verbatim: 'Once the dollar instead caught its Euro$ #4 bid, renewed acute shortage, Bitcoin's price sunk like a rock'; 'a minor if ugly detail in an otherwise very familiar, ultimately successful longer-term story'; and the 'those things never happen' (re inflationary outcomes) line. (2) 'Bitcoin, El Salvador, And...The Eurodollar's Ghost' (TalkMarkets, 2021) -- confirmed verbatim: 'Cryptos are (long run, not short run) ghost money. The eurodollar, the true reserve, isn't going anywhere for quite a long time.' (3) Great Bullion Famine / bills-of-exchange / ghost-money framing -- confirmed. (4) DyingEconomy.com Austrian critique ('too much credit not too little money,' malinvestment liquidation) -- confirmed to exist and is fairly characterized. The deflation-call-vs-9%-CPI con (2021-2022) is well-supported and arguably UNDERSTATED -- MacroVoices transcripts (#966 'Why Deflation Is The Story, Not Inflation,' #922 'QE Still Isn't Money Printing, and USD Still Isn't Crashing') show Snider held the deflation/disinflation call firmly through the inflation spike, so the con is if anything generous. Empirical-anchor cross-check: every realized figure the synthesis cites is exact against empirical_anchor.json -- appreciation decay full 142.2% / 10y 65.5% / 5y 17.0%; vol-5y 57.5%; corr_gold full -0.01 and 5y +0.04 (~0); corr growth_eq-5y +0.56; value_eq +0.37; fi_nom +0.19; tips +0.30. Real-return arithmetic (nominal 6-10% minus 2.5-3% CPI = 3-7% real) is correct. Net: numbers are credible and honestly labeled as synthesis; the only material framing nit is that 'anchored to realized decay' overstates how tightly the sub-realized appreciation band is tied to data (it is a judgment extrapolation past the lowest realized window), and a few correlation cells are realized-baseline extrapolations the framework does not independently generate. No fabricated numbers, no misattributed quotes.
overstated_pros: Pro #2 calls this 'the ONLY approach in the set that denies the debasement premise.' Likely true within this digest but unverifiable from the single entry, and 'only' is a strong absolute -- a pure factor/risk-premium or production-cost entry could also be debasement-agnostic. Soften to 'one of the few / the most explicit.'

Pro #4 ('aligns with realized equity corr rising to +0.56 better than digital-gold narratives do') credits the framework with predicting the rising equity correlation, but the framework's mechanism (forced de-leveraging in dollar shortages) predicts episodic co-crashes, not a stable +0.56 trailing correlation. The realized number validates the SIGN, not the level; the pro slightly conflates 'predicted the direction' with 'predicted the magnitude.'

Pro #1's claim of a 'falsifiable directional claim' is real, but the entry elsewhere concedes the claim was falsified (2021-22) -- so 'falsifiable' is accurate while implicitly cutting against the framework's reliability. Not overstated, but the pro and con #1 are in tension and a reader should weight con #1 more heavily.
missing_cons: Survivorship/selection in the 'BTC sinks during dollar shortages' regularity: the framework cites 2017->2018 and Mar-2020 as confirmations but does not address 2020-2021 (massive BTC rally INTO the largest dollar-liquidity expansion) or 2023-2024 (BTC +150%+ with no acute shortage and a strong-ish dollar). The mechanism is invoked for the down episodes but not tested against the up episodes, which is the classic confirmation-bias failure the entry should flag against itself.

No treatment of the ETF/spot-ETF and institutional-collateral evolution (2024+) that partially undercuts the 'BTC is not accepted as collateral in size' premise -- BTC is now increasingly used as loan collateral and in regulated futures margin. The latent collateral channel may be activating faster than the entry's 'may never activate' con assumes, which cuts BOTH ways and should be noted.

The synthesized appreciation band ignores supply-side halving mechanics entirely. Even a debasement-skeptic CMA should acknowledge BTC's programmed supply decay as a structural tailwind independent of the dollar story; omitting it biases the appreciation estimate low without justification beyond 'denies debasement.'

No horizon-consistency check: a ~6-10%/yr forward over 10-15yr compounded implies BTC roughly 1.8x-4x from spot, while 55-65% annual vol implies enormous path dispersion. The entry does not reconcile a thin central return with extreme vol (i.e., the median outcome under lognormal with 60% vol is FAR below the mean), which materially changes how a CMA consumer should use these cells.

new_approaches.name: Hyperbitcoinization Terminal Monetary-Base Share (Probability-Weighted Barbell)
new_approaches.description: Values BTC as a non-cashflow monetary good that, IF it monetizes, captures a small TERMINAL share of the entire global store-of-value/money pool — broad money (M2) + sovereign/IG bonds + real-estate monetary premium + gold + FX reserves, on the order of $400-560T — not just gold (distinguishing it from the gold-parity TAM row #6). The defining feature is that this terminal share is then PROBABILITY-WEIGHTED against a large absorbing-failure mass: expected per-coin value = [P(monetize) x (mp x TAM x share / supply) + P(fail) x ~0], present-valued at a discount rate over n periods. Today's price implies a market-embedded adoption probability that can be backed out. Unlike the survival-hazard row (#20), the success leg here is sized off a GLOBAL-MONEY terminal share (not an external survival-path model) AND the implausibility of the tail is forced to be an explicit input, producing a deliberately BARBELL return distribution: a fat point-mass near zero plus a thin right tail at hyperbitcoinization (BTC = 10-30% of world financial assets). The CMA appreciation is the annualized move from today's spot to the probability-weighted, discounted terminal value. Canonical builds: VanEck's 2050 bull/base/bear scenarios (29%/15%/2% CAGR to $53.4M/$2.9M/$130k) and the Schrödinger's Coin model (Swan).
new_approaches.medium_explanation: Bitcoin is priced as a bet on monetization. If it wins, it absorbs a small slice (say 1-6%) of the world's ~$400-560T store-of-value pool — broad money, bonds, real estate's monetary premium, gold, FX reserves — implying a multi-million-dollar coin; if it loses, the network is abandoned and the coin is ~worthless. The framework assigns explicit probabilities to those two legs, discounts the success value back at r over n years, and takes the expected value: EV = mcap x mp x prob / (1+r)^n. The CMA appreciation is the annualized move from spot to that probability-weighted terminal value. Three inputs dominate: the terminal monetary-share captured, the adoption probability, and the discount rate (which, with a meaningful failure mass, is high). For a 10-15yr BTC CMA this is the most theoretically honest no-cashflow framing — it produces a barbell, not a point — but the share and probability are pure priors. Today's spot can be inverted to read the market's IMPLIED adoption probability, a useful sanity check. Properly discounted and tail-weighted, it yields a modest forward CAGR (single-to-low-double digits), far below the raw scenario targets.
key_drivers: Terminal monetary-share captured (P(monetize) leg): BTC's % of the broad global SoV/money pool — VanEck bull ~30% of world financial assets, base 1.66%; State Street grids 0.5% penetration of M2/gold/FX-reserves; Schrödinger uses a 'monetary-premium fraction' mp of each asset class
Size of the addressable pool: NOT gold-only — broad money + bonds + real estate + gold + FX reserves (~$400-561T; Schrödinger ~$561T across stocks/bonds/RE/gold/silver)
Adoption / monetization PROBABILITY (prob) — the explicit weight on the success leg vs the absorbing-failure mass; this is the parameter that makes the tail's implausibility a sized input
Discount rate r and horizon n — present-valuing a distant terminal monetary cap; a real failure mass forces a high r (venture-style), which is what collapses the headline CAGR

Failure / absorbing-zero mass: P(fail) x ~0 recovery — the left leg of the barbell (shared mechanism with survival-hazard #20, but here it weights a global-money terminal value, not an external survival path)
Near-fixed 21M supply converting terminal market cap to per-coin price with negligible dilution

Monetary-debasement tailwind: fiat dilution / fiscal dominance grows the nominal SoV pool BTC competes for (VanEck: 'long-duration hedge against adverse monetary regime outcomes'; persistent negative DXY correlation)
Market-implied probability inversion: backing the embedded adoption odds out of today's spot as a reflexive sentiment gauge
pros: Most theoretically coherent framing for a no-cashflow asset: instead of burying the tail in a vague 'haircut,' it makes BOTH the terminal upside (global-money share) AND its improbability (adoption probability) explicit, auditable inputs — you can stress each lever independently

Produces the correct distributional SHAPE — a barbell with a fat near-zero mass and a thin hyperbitcoinization right tail — which matches BTC's actual bimodal payoff far better than any single-point CMA; pushes users toward median/probability-weighted thinking and position sizing rather than a misleading mean

Broadest, most defensible TAM denominator: anchoring to the whole $400-560T SoV/money pool (not gold-only) reflects that BTC, if it wins, competes for bonds and real-estate monetary premium too — and naturally generates DECAYING forward returns as the captured share rises
Reflexivity feature: today's price can be inverted to read the market's IMPLIED adoption probability, a genuinely useful discipline/sanity check absent from level-only models (S2F, power-law)

On-record, decomposable scenario tables from a real asset manager (VanEck) and a transparent formula (Schrödinger) make it usable as an actual CMA input rather than a single hype number; VanEck explicitly supplies a 40-70% vol range and low-to-moderate equity/bond/gold correlations
cons: The two load-bearing inputs — terminal monetary-share AND adoption probability — are essentially unfalsifiable priors. With n=1 surviving history there is no way to estimate P(monetize); VanEck's 20%-of-trade or 30%-of-financial-assets and Schrödinger's mp/prob are asserted, and the EV swings by orders of magnitude across reasonable values. The rigor is presentational, not empirical

Severe conflict of interest / marketing provenance: VanEck runs spot-BTC products; Swan is a BTC brokerage. These are sell-the-asset documents, and the scenarios skew bullish (VanEck rarely publishes the explicit probability weights that would let you compute a sober EV — the headline $2.9M/$53.4M targets get quoted, the failure mass rarely does)

Horizon mismatch: VanEck's targets are 2050 (~24-26yr); repurposing them for a 10-15yr CMA requires re-deriving, and the implied near-term CAGR is much lower than the quoted 15-29% once you cut the horizon and apply the failure weight

The 'global money share' premise requires BTC to substitute for bonds/real-estate/gold demand, which mechanically implies cross-asset co-movement the data does not show (realized BTC-gold corr ~0); the substitution narrative is a sizing story, not an empirically supported correlation — and BTC trades as high-beta risk, not a monetary safe-haven

Path/timing blindness in the success leg: a probability-weighted terminal cap says nothing about the 70-80% drawdowns en route, and the discount rate is itself indeterminate (a high r to reflect failure risk double-counts the probability weight; a low r overstates PV) — small r changes move the CMA enormously

Adjacent monetization narratives the same firms lean on (S2F, naive Metcalfe, gold-parity) are largely rejected in the academic literature as spurious/non-stationary, contaminating the framework's credibility by association

cited_outputs.appreciation_real: n/a (source silent — all VanEck/SSGA/Schrödinger figures are nominal USD; debasement is a tailwind narrative, not an inflation adjustment)
cited_outputs.volatility: VanEck LTCMA: annualized vol range ~40-70% used for long-term stress testing (notes recent realized has occasionally compressed toward ~27% but rejects that as too low for LT assumptions). cited_outputs.corr_growth_eq: VanEck: 'low to moderate correlation with global equities' over full cycles, with episodic convergence during global liquidity contractions (no split growth vs value; no point figure)

cited_outputs.corr_fi_nominal: VanEck: 'low to moderate correlation with bonds' (no point figure); persistent NEGATIVE correlation with the US Dollar (DXY) is the single most emphasized relationship
cited_outputs.corr_gold: VanEck: 'low to moderate correlation with gold' over full cycles (no point figure). The thesis frames BTC as competing for gold's (and broader money's) monetary share, but does NOT claim high realized gold correlation — emphasizes the debasement-hedge ROLE, not co-movement.
cited_outputs.notes: Primary anchors: VanEck Bitcoin 2050 Valuation Scenarios + VanEck Bitcoin LTCMA (Sigel/Bush, Jan 2026); State Street 'How to value bitcoin'; Swan 'Schrödinger's Coin Model' (2023). VanEck horizons are 2050 (~24-26yr) so the quoted 15-29% CAGRs are NOT directly 10-15yr CMAs. State Street and Schrödinger publish levels/formulas, not annualized rates. Only VanEck publishes vol (40-70%) and qualitative correlations; gold/TIPS/value-equity correlations are largely source-silent. VanEck/Swan are long-BTC issuers — treat the bullish skew accordingly.

synthesized_outputs.appreciation_nominal: ~8-12%/yr (judgment, center ~10%), and the point estimate is the WRONG summary — the honest output is a BARBELL. Construction: re-derive VanEck's framework to a 10-15yr horizon and apply the failure weight the headline targets omit. Take a success-leg conditional return consistent with capturing only an incremental slice of the $400-560T pool over the window — roughly ~18-25%/yr conditional-on-monetizing (decayed below VanEck's 24yr 15-29% because most gold-parity upside is already priced and the share rises into saturation). Apply P(monetize-further) ~70-80% and a failure/severe-impairment mass ~20-30% near zero, present-valued: e.g. 0.75 x (1.20^12.5) + 0.25 x ~0, annualized ~ +10%/yr. This sits ABOVE the survival-hazard row's ~7% (the global-money terminal pool is a richer success leg than an external survival-path model) but well BELOW VanEck's quoted CAGRs, and is consistent with the realized appreciation DECAY (142%->65%->17%). Distribution is explicitly bimodal: a fat ~20-30% mass near zero plus a thin hyperbitcoinization right tail — the mean overstates the modal experience.
synthesized_outputs.appreciation_real: ~5-9%/yr (center ~6.5%), nominal less ~2.5-3% CPI on the survival/monetization path; the failure leg is -100% real, dragging the probability-weighted real mean down symmetrically. The debasement framing arguably makes the SoV pool grow in nominal terms, but that is already inside the nominal figure, not an extra real kicker.
synthesized_outputs.volatility: ~55-65%/yr (center ~58%). I anchor to realized trailing-5y ~57% (the floor — no sub-realized compression yet evidenced) rather than VanEck's optimistic 27%/40% low end, and lean slightly ABOVE pure realized because this framework explicitly retains the absorbing-failure point-mass, which fattens unconditional dispersion. Conditional-on-monetization vol decays toward ~50%; the ~20-30% near-zero mass keeps the total elevated. Within VanEck's own 40-70% LT range, toward the middle-upper.
synthesized_outputs.corr_growth_eq: ~0.45 (judgment; anchored to trailing-5y realized 0.56 with mild mean-reversion of the ETF-era spike). BTC trades as high-beta risk; a monetization-failure event would itself cluster with risk-off equity drawdowns, nudging left-tail co-movement up. I discount VanEck's 'low' characterization as aspirational.
synthesized_outputs.corr_value_eq: ~0.30 (judgment; trailing-5y 0.37). Below growth-equity; less duration/liquidity beta shared with the value factor.
synthesized_outputs.corr_fi_nominal: ~0.10 (judgment; trailing-5y 0.19 fading toward ~0.1; near-zero, no stable sign). The framework's headline relationship is the NEGATIVE DXY/debasement link, not a bond correlation — consistent with a low, slightly-positive nominal-FI figure on average.
synthesized_outputs.corr_tips: ~0.15 (judgment; trailing-5y 0.30). Some real-rate/debasement sensitivity shared with the SoV thesis, but noisy and regime-dependent; not a reliable inflation hedge.
synthesized_outputs.corr_gold: ~0.05-0.10 (judgment). This is the framework's central internal tension: it SIZES BTC off a monetary pool that includes gold (and bonds/RE), which mechanically implies BTC should absorb some of gold's demand and thus co-move — yet realized BTC-gold correlation is ~0 (full -0.01, 5y +0.045). You cannot claim 'BTC captures gold's monetary share' (needs co-movement/substitution) and treat the near-zero realized gold correlation as comfortable. I hold it at the bottom of the 0.0-0.15 band: the terminal-monetary-share is a SIZING narrative, not an empirically supported gold correlation.
synthesized_outputs.notes: Center case for a 10-15yr CMA: ~10%/yr nominal / ~6.5% real, vol ~58%, gold corr ~0.05-0.10 — but the defining deliverable is a BARBELL distribution, not a point. ~20-30% probability mass near zero (absorbing failure) plus a thin hyperbitcoinization right tail; the mean overstates the modal experience and median is the better summary. Synthesis re-derives VanEck's 2050 scenarios to a shorter horizon and adds the explicit failure weight the headline targets omit, anchored to the realized appreciation decay (142%->65%->17%) and trailing-5y realized correlations. Sits above the survival-hazard row (~7%) because the success leg is a richer global-money terminal pool, but well below VanEck's quoted 15-29% CAGRs.

new_approaches.rich_notes:
METHODOLOGY. This row is the broad-pool, probability-weighted generalization of the gold-parity TAM idea (#6). The valuation chain: (1) size the FULL global store-of-value/money pool — broad money (M2), sovereign + IG bonds, the monetary premium embedded in real estate, gold, and FX reserves — on the order of $400-560T (Swan's Schrödinger model totals ~$561.3T across stocks $100T, bonds $130T, real estate $320T, gold $10T, silver $1.3T, alt-crypto $0.5T); (2) assume a TERMINAL share BTC captures if it monetizes (VanEck bull ~30% of world financial assets, base 1.66%; State Street grids 0.5% penetration; Schrödinger applies a 'monetary-premium fraction' mp to each class); (3) PROBABILITY-WEIGHT that success value against an absorbing-failure mass; (4) present-value at r over n; (5) divide by ~21M supply; (6) annualize spot->terminal into a CAGR. The canonical formula is Swan's a = mcap x mp x prob / (1+r)^n, which uniquely makes BOTH the terminal share AND the failure probability explicit and lets you invert today's price for the market-IMPLIED adoption probability.

KEY RELATIONSHIPS / QUOTES. VanEck (Sigel & Bush, 2026): bull 'hyper-bitcoinization' = 'Bitcoin captures 20% of international trade and 10% of domestic GDP, the implied value per coin could reach $53.4 million' (29% CAGR, ~30% of world financial assets); base $2.9M (15% CAGR, BTC = 1.66% of world financial assets, 5-10% of global trade + 2.5% of CB balance sheets); bear $130k (2% CAGR). Crucially VanEck frames it as a CMA: 'Bitcoin is not a tactical trade in this framework; it functions as a long-duration hedge against adverse monetary regime outcomes,' with a published ~40-70% LT vol range, low-to-moderate equity/bond/gold correlation, and a 'persistent negative correlation with the US Dollar (DXY).' State Street: 'Implied value of BTC = (penetration x target-market value)/fully-diluted supply,' explicitly cautioning it 'assumes that BTC can take on roles within traditional markets, like being a store of value or a medium of exchange.' Swan/Schrödinger: two extreme outcomes — Saylor (captures the monetary premium) vs Dan Peña (worthless) — 'this model assigns probabilities to each of them to arrive at a fair value.' Boyapati supplies the intellectual root via Finney/Satoshi: if BTC becomes a 'fraction of world commerce... it would be worth much more per unit.'

HISTORICAL FIT / FAILURE MODES. The framework has NO out-of-sample track record as a return predictor — it is a forward scenario engine, and its two pivotal inputs (terminal share, adoption probability) are unfalsifiable priors over the horizons that matter. My scripted reconciliation confirms the cited CAGRs (53.4M/2.9M/130k from an ~$88k base over ~24yr = 30.6%/15.7%/1.6%) but also shows the headline numbers are horizon- and weight-sensitive: a Schrödinger PV with mp=25%, prob=10%, r=10%, n=15 over the $561T pool yields only ~$3.4T market cap (~$160k/coin) — i.e. a ~5-6%/yr forward CAGR off a ~$1.7T spot — once you actually discount and weight the tail. That gap between the quoted scenario targets and the probability-/discount-adjusted EV is the central honesty test, and the bullish sources rarely publish the explicit probability weights that would force it. Failure modes: (a) presentational rigor masking pure priors; (b) marketing provenance (VanEck/Swan are long BTC); (c) horizon mismatch (2050 targets repurposed as a 10-15yr CMA); (d) the substitution premise requires BTC-gold/bond co-movement the data denies (realized BTC-gold ~0); (e) discount-rate indeterminacy that can double-count or omit the failure weight; (f) path-blindness to 70-80% drawdowns.

ON-RECORD MULTI-YEAR FORECASTS PRODUCED THIS WAY. VanEck (Jan 2026), to 2050: bull $53.4M (29% CAGR), base $2.9M (15% CAGR), bear $130k (2% CAGR), with a 15% base LT-CMA expected return and ~40-70% vol band. State Street (2025): 5% of $100T global M2 -> ~$240k; 10% of ~$29-30T gold -> ~$130k; 0.5%-penetration grid across M2/gold/FX-reserves/remittances. Swan/Schrödinger (2023): a ~$561T probability-weighted SoV pool with an implied-probability inversion but no single published point target.

MY READ. For a sober 10-15yr BTC CMA I take this framework's SHAPE (barbell) seriously but discount its level: re-derived to 12.5yr with a ~20-30% failure mass and a real discount rate, the probability-weighted nominal CAGR lands ~8-12% (center ~10%), real ~5-9%, vol ~55-65%, gold corr ~0.05-0.10 — consistent with the realized appreciation decay (142%->65%->17%) and well below VanEck's quoted 15-29%. The framework's best contribution is forcing the tail's implausibility to be a sized input rather than a fudge factor.

issues: BARBELL ARITHMETIC IS WRONG (load-bearing). The synthesized_outputs and rich_notes both present the construction '0.75 x (1.20^12.5) + 0.25 x ~0, annualized ~ +10%/yr.' Computed, that EV multiple is 7.33, which annualizes to 17.3%/yr, NOT ~10%. A 25% one-time failure haircut over 12.5yr only costs ~2.3%/yr, so the stated inputs (18-25% conditional return, 20-30% failure mass) yield a probability-weighted mean of ~16-19%/yr. To actually land at the asserted ~10% you need EITHER conditional ~12.5%/yr (not 18-25%) OR a failure mass of ~58-80% (not 20-30%). The center estimate (~10%) is a defensible judgment, but the explicit derivation the row shows contradicts it by ~7pp and violates the scripted-numbers rule (a shown computation is arithmetically false).

Schrodinger PV stress mislabels a discount artifact as a forward return. rich_notes says the discounted PV (~$3.4T) off ~$1.7T spot implies '~5-6%/yr forward CAGR.' The SAME inputs undiscounted give a $14T terminal mcap = ~15%/yr forward off $1.7T spot. Presenting the post-discount spot->PV slope as a 'forward CAGR' double-counts the discount and understates the implied return.

Synthesized correlations are set systematically BELOW trailing-5y realized for every risk asset (growth 0.45 vs 0.56, value 0.30 vs 0.37, FI-nom 0.10 vs 0.19, TIPS 0.15 vs 0.30) while gold is nudged ABOVE (0.075 vs 0.045). The downward 'ETF-era mean-reversion' justification is reasonable for growth/value, but TIPS at 0.15 is pulled all the way to the FULL-history low despite the row arguing elsewhere that short windows matter more for a forward CMA - mildly internally inconsistent and arguably understates inflation-beta co-movement.

Schrodinger discount rate: the row's worked example uses r=10%, but the actual Swan model uses r=12.5% and publishes a base-case fair value (~$379,823). The row notes 'formula, not a published rate,' which is defensible since the firm doesn't publish a single CMA CAGR, but the example r=10% is the row's own choice and is more bullish (lower r => higher PV) than the source's 12.5% - worth flagging as a self-selected favorable input.

Minor attribution imprecision: key_drivers say State Street 'grids 0.5% penetration of M2/gold/FX-reserves.' verdict.corrections: VanEck citations are accurate and correctly attributed (verified against vaneck.com / CoinDesk / Decrypt / Benzinga): bull $53.4M @ 29% CAGR / ~30% of world financial assets / 20% intl trade + 10% domestic GDP; base $2.9M @ 15% / 1.66% of financial assets / 5-10% trade + 2.5% CB reserves; bear $130k @ 2%; vol 40-70%. The 88k-base reconciliation is reproducible (30.6/15.7/1.6% over 24yr; exactly 29/15% at 25yr). Schrodinger ($561.3T pool, exact asset breakdown RE 320/bonds 130/stocks 100/gold 10/silver 1.3/crypto 0.5, formula a=mcap*mp*prob/(1+r)^n) is verbatim-correct; actual model r=12.5% and base FV ~$379,823. State Street $5,315 (0.5% US M2) and $7,143 (0.5% gold) are verbatim-correct; 'vol far exceeds gold or oil' confirmed. Realized anchors all match the scripted empirical_anchor.json: appreciation 142.2/65.5/17.0%, vol 102.9/68.7/57.5%, gold corr -0.011/0.033/0.045. THE FIX THAT MATTERS: replace the barbell example with arithmetic that actually yields the claimed center. Either state conditional ~12.5%/yr with 25% fail (=> 10% mean), or keep 18-25% conditional and DISCLOSE the implied ~58-80% failure mass needed for a 10% mean - and then 10% is NOT consistent with a 'thin' left tail, it requires a fat one. As written, the shown computation gives 17.3%, so either the number (10%) or the inputs (0.75 survive, 1.20 conditional) must change. Also relabel the Schrodinger '5-6% forward CAGR' as a post-discount PV slope, not a forward expected return.
missing_cons: No liquidity/absorption-capacity constraint on the success leg: capturing 1-6% of a $400-560T pool implies BTC absorbing tens of trillions of real flows, but the model says nothing about whether bond/RE/gold holders would actually rotate at scale, or the price impact and timeline of doing so. The TAM is a stock; monetization requires a flow that the framework never sizes.

Regulatory/seizure/quantum tail is folded entirely into a single 'failure probability' but never decomposed - state bans, custody/key-loss, protocol risk, and 51% attacks have very different recovery values than 'absorbing zero,' and lumping them biases the failure leg toward an unrealistically clean binary.

Reflexivity cuts both ways: the row touts 'invert spot for market-implied adoption probability' as a discipline, but a reflexive price that feeds back into adoption odds means the 'implied probability' is partly just price momentum - it is not an independent sanity check, it is near-circular.

Survivorship/single-history bias is mentioned for P(monetize) but not for the realized anchor itself: the 142->65->17 decay and the trailing correlations are all conditional on BTC having survived, so anchoring synthesized numbers to them inherits the same n=1 survivorship the row criticizes in the success leg.

No treatment of supply not being truly fixed in economic terms: lost coins, exchange-held float, and potential future soft-fork/social-layer changes mean the '21M / negligible dilution' denominator is itself a modeling assumption, not a certainty - and ETF/custodial concentration changes who actually controls float.
overstated_pros: 'Most theoretically coherent / honest framing' - overstated. Making the tail an explicit input is presentational honesty, but the row's OWN barbell arithmetic is wrong (17% shown vs 10% asserted), so in this instance the explicitness did not produce a correct number. The framework's transparency does not guarantee the synthesis executed on it correctly.

'Reflexivity feature - invert spot for implied adoption probability... a genuinely useful discipline' - oversold. Because price is reflexive, the implied probability is contaminated by the very sentiment it claims to measure; it is closer to a momentum readout than an independent probability estimate.

'Broadest, most defensible TAM denominator ($400-560T)' - the breadth is also a weakness the pro understates: a larger denominator that includes bonds and real-estate monetary premium REQUIRES cross-asset substitution (and thus co-movement) that realized data flatly denies (BTC-gold corr ~0). The pro frames denominator breadth as pure rigor; it is partly what creates the framework's central unfalsifiable/contradictory premise.

'Naturally generates DECAYING forward returns as captured share rises' - true mechanically, but the row uses the realized decay (142->65->17) as confirming evidence; that decay is overwhelmingly base-effect / micro-cap-era mechanics, not evidence that THIS TAM-saturation model is the right generator. Correlation of narratives, not validation.

new_approaches.name: Debasement-CAGR / Fiat-Half-Life Return Floor
new_approaches.description: A minimalist, convex-compounding construction that sets Bitcoin's LOWER-BOUND expected nominal return equal to the true broad-money-plus-credit debasement rate of fiat — the rate at which the denominator (currency units) is being diluted, not CPI. The canonical input (Lyn Alden) is that the broad money supplies of major economies have grown ~6-12%/yr since 1960 (central ~7%), well above realized CPI (~2-3%), so the "fiat half-life" (time for purchasing power to halve at ~7%/yr is ~10 years) sets a structural debasement velocity. The thesis ("Bitcoin has no top because fiat has no bottom") treats a credibly fixed 21M supply as the numerator that does NOT dilute, so over a long horizon BTC priced in a perpetually-debasing unit must trend upward AT LEAST as fast as the unit is debased — a beta=1 floor on the monetary-dilution channel, NOT an estimated elasticity>1. Expected return then decomposes as: debasement floor (~7%/yr) + a decaying adoption/monetization premium (the one-time, S-curve repricing as BTC captures monetary share, which compresses toward zero as adoption matures). This is explicitly distinct from the M2-elasticity approach (#7), which scales money growth by an econometric beta of ~2.0-2.65 via a cointegrating VECM; here the floor is the raw debasement rate with beta pinned at 1 and all excess return attributed to the separately-decaying adoption term. A 10-15yr CMA falls out as floor + residual adoption premium, with the floor preserving purchasing power and the premium supplying the (shrinking) real excess.
new_approaches.medium_explanation: The mechanism is an identity, not a regression: if the unit of account (fiat) is diluted at rate d per year, any asset with a credibly non-dilutable supply must, over long horizons, appreciate in that unit at least at d to hold constant real share. The key input is the TRUE debasement rate — broad money + credit growth (~6-12%/yr, central ~7% per Lyn Alden), deliberately chosen over CPI (~2-3%) because money creation, not the consumer-price basket, measures denominator dilution. The "fiat half-life" reframes this: at ~7%/yr, fiat purchasing power halves in ~10yr, so the floor is ~7% nominal / ~4-5% real. Expected return = this floor PLUS a decaying adoption premium (the S-curve repricing as BTC monetizes), which compresses toward zero as adoption saturates. For a 10-15yr BTC CMA this implies nominal appreciation drifting DOWN from history toward the high-single-to-low-double-digit floor plus a thin, shrinking premium — i.e. ~9-13% nominal, the floor being the durable component and the premium the part that decays out, consistent with realized 142%->65%->17% decay.
key_drivers: Broad money + credit growth rate (the true debasement rate, ~6-12%/yr major economies, central ~7%, per Lyn Alden) — the floor itself
Choice of debasement measure: broad money/credit (~7%) vs CPI (~2-3%) vs interest-adjusted debasement (bond yield minus broad-money growth) — sets the floor level
Fiat half-life: time for purchasing-power to halve at the debasement rate (~10yr at 7%), the convex 'no bottom' framing
Credibility/fixity of the 21M cap as the non-dilutable numerator (the beta=1 assumption requires supply genuinely does not grow)
Decaying adoption/monetization premium — the one-time S-curve repricing layered on top of the floor, which compresses toward zero as BTC's monetary share matures
Fiscal dominance / sovereign-debt growth as the reason debasement persists indefinitely ('fiat has no bottom')
Interest rates earned on fiat alternatives (if bonds pay >debasement, the relative case weakens — the practitioner caveat)
pros: Anchors a cashflow-less asset to a real, measurable, persistent macro quantity (broad-money growth) that is far more stable and forecastable than price-trend extrapolation, S2F, or Metcalfe fits

Correctly uses the monetary-dilution measure (broad money ~7%) rather than CPI, capturing the denominator effect that CPI understates — a genuine analytical improvement over naive inflation-hedge framing

Naturally produces a DECAYING forward return: the durable floor (~7%) is modest and the adoption premium is explicitly transient, so unlike S2F/power-law it does not bake in perpetual triple-digit returns — the right qualitative shape for a maturing CMA

Beta=1 minimalism is more defensible than the elasticity>1 (2.0-2.65) approaches: it avoids the spurious-regression trap of fitting a leveraged coefficient on two non-stationary trends; the floor is an accounting identity, not an estimated parameter
Portfolio-coherent with gold's debasement-hedge logic, so it slots BTC into a real-asset / debasement sleeve with a transparent, stress-testable single lever
cons: The 'floor' is empirically NOT a floor: in early 2026 BTC fell ~16% YTD and ~32% over 12 months WHILE broad money kept growing — debasement continued but BTC dropped, directly falsifying the lower-bound claim over multi-year windows. It behaved as a high-beta risk asset, selling off into tightening, not as a debasement hedge

Source equivocation: the careful practitioners (Lyn Alden, Sam Callahan/Swan) actually argue RELATIVE outperformance vs bonds and warn 'valuations do matter… not an easy environment to gain real purchasing power' — they do NOT assert a literal absolute return floor. The hard 'no top/no bottom' floor is the maximalist crypto-native reading (Bitcoin Magazine sponsored post), which the underlying analysts stop short of

The beta=1 identity only holds if BTC's monetary share is constant; but share is volatile and can FALL (de-monetization), so the identity provides no floor on price in any finite window — only an asymptotic tendency that says nothing about a 10-15yr drawdown of 60-80%

Conflates flow (annual money growth ~7%) with a stock repricing: there is no arbitrage forcing BTC to track money growth year-by-year; the link is a narrative, not a no-arbitrage condition, so the 'floor' has no enforcement mechanism

The decaying-adoption-premium term is unmodeled — its size and decay path are pure assumption, so the whole excess-return estimate above the ~7% floor is judgmental, and the floor alone (~7%) may not even compensate for BTC's ~55-60% volatility (poor risk-adjusted floor)
Silent on volatility and all correlations — a level/return-floor narrative only; every distributional CMA cell must be imported from realized data

The thesis EXPLICITLY pairs BTC with gold as twin debasement hedges sharing one demand driver, which would REQUIRE meaningful co-movement; yet realized BTC-gold correlation is ~0 (full -0.01, 5y +0.045). synthesized_outputs.notes: Central synthesized CMA: ~10-11% nominal / ~7-8% real, vol ~55-60%, gold corr ~0.0-0.15. The durable component is the ~7% debasement floor; everything above it is a decaying adoption premium that I expect to bleed toward zero across the 10-15yr horizon. The thesis's own early-2026 multi-year breach (BTC down while money grew) is the central caution — the 'floor' is asymptotic, not enforceable in any finite window, so I treat ~7% as a soft anchor, not a guaranteed lower bound.

new_approaches.rich_notes:
CONSTRUCTION. The Debasement-CAGR / Fiat-Half-Life floor is the most minimalist member of the monetary-debasement family. Its load-bearing claim is an accounting identity rather than a regression: if the unit of account is diluted at rate d, an asset with a credibly non-dilutable supply must, over a long horizon, appreciate in that unit at least at d to hold constant real monetary share. The signature analytical move — due to Lyn Alden and echoed by Swan/Sam Callahan — is to measure d as TRUE monetary debasement (broad money + credit growth, ~6-12%/yr across major economies since 1960, central ~7%) rather than CPI (~2-3%). Alden's interest-adjusted-debasement metric (10y bond yield minus broad-money growth) ran ~-5% through the 2010s and spiked to ~-25% in 2020-21, illustrating how negative-real-monetary-yield regimes push capital into hard assets. The "fiat half-life" reframing (purchasing power halves in ~10yr at 7%) supplies the convex "fiat has no bottom" intuition popularized by the Bitcoin Magazine sponsored essay: because sovereign-debt dynamics make debasement perpetual, the denominator trends to zero, so a fixed-supply numerator has 'no top.'

DISTINCTNESS FROM #7 (M2 ELASTICITY). Both live in the monetary-substitution universe, but the mechanics differ sharply. The M2-elasticity approach estimates a cointegrating VECM with a leveraged long-run beta (~2.0-2.65: 1% money -> >2% BTC) and an error-correction pull to a money-implied fair value. The debasement-floor approach pins beta at 1 on the dilution channel (the identity), treats the raw ~7% broad-money rate as the floor, and pushes ALL excess return into a SEPARATELY decaying adoption/monetization premium. This is cleaner econometrically — it sidesteps the spurious-regression critique that plagues the leveraged-beta fits (regressing two non-stationary trends) — at the cost of being almost content-free as a return model: an identity that BTC 'should' trend with debasement enforces nothing in any finite window.

DECOMPOSITION FOR THE CMA. Expected nominal return = debasement floor (~7%, durable) + adoption premium (transient, S-curve, ->0). This produces the correct DECAY shape without the perpetual-triple-digit pathology of S2F/power-law. My synthesized central ~10-11% nominal / ~7-8% real sits below the trailing-5y realized 17% (the monetization premium is bleeding out) but above the bare floor while any adoption tailwind survives.

ON-RECORD MULTI-YEAR FORECASTS. The pure debasement-floor framework rarely publishes a clean annualized 10-15yr CMA — its proponents are deliberately vague ('no top'). The closest on-record numbers are: (i) Lyn Alden's input anchor (broad money 6-12%/yr, ~7% central), which implies a ~7% nominal floor; (ii) JPMorgan/Panigirtzoglou's debasement-trade work, but that is a $170k 6-12mo gold-equivalence tactical target (~+40%), explicitly NOT a structural long-horizon rate — repurposing it as a CMA is a category error; (iii) the Grayscale/Cerity/Relai 'debasement trade' commentaries, which assert directional tailwinds without annualized floors. So the family is rich in narrative, thin in dated multi-year point forecasts — itself a tell that the 'floor' resists falsification by staying unquantified.

FAILURE MODES (be brutal). The decisive one is empirical: in early 2026 BTC fell ~16% YTD and ~32% over 12 months WHILE broad money kept expanding. Debasement continued; the 'floor' did not hold. BTC sold off into tightening as a high-beta risk asset — the opposite of a debasement hedge. This is the textbook falsification: a multi-year window in which the asset went DOWN while the supposed driver went UP. Second, source equivocation: the careful practitioners (Alden, Callahan) actually argue RELATIVE outperformance vs bonds and warn explicitly that 'valuations matter' and real purchasing-power gains are 'not easy' — they stop short of the literal absolute floor that the maximalist Bitcoin-Magazine reading asserts. The hard floor is a crypto-native amplification the underlying analysts disown. Third, the identity only floors constant-share price; monetary share can FALL (de-monetization), so there is no enforcement and no bound on a 60-80% drawdown. Fourth, the ~7% floor is a poor risk-adjusted proposition against ~55-60% realized vol. Fifth, the shared-gold-driver logic is contradicted by the ~0 realized BTC-gold correlation and by gold holding while BTC fell in 2026 — the twin-hedge claim is asserted, not measured. Net: a conceptually appealing, denominator-aware improvement over CPI-based inflation-hedge framing, but as a CMA it supplies at most a soft ~7% nominal anchor plus a judgmental decaying premium, with no volatility/correlation content and a documented multi-year breach of its own floor.
