JPM CORRECTION: change 'a $170k 6-12mo tactical target (~+40% from $119k)' to '~+67% from ~$102k (BTC mkt cap ~$2.1T at the Nov-6-2025 CoinDesk write-up; JPM said BTC was ~$68k below the $170k fair value).' The category-error framing (tactical, not CMA) is correct and should stay.

CALLAHAN CORRECTION: do not attribute the 'valuations matter / not easy' warning to Swan/Callahan's 'Digital Benchmark' piece — that source contains no such caveat. Attribute it to Lyn Alden's Dec-2025 newsletter only (verified verbatim). Callahan supports the RELATIVE-value reading but not the explicit valuation warning.

DECAY-TRIPLET CORRECTION: label 142%/65%/17% explicitly as a single dated snapshot (and state the snapshot date and geometric-CAGR basis), since rolling-window CAGRs move materially day-to-day; keep the qualitative decay shape, which is robust.

VOL CORRECTION: soften '~57% vol floor that held' to 'central realized vol ~55-60%, with recent trailing windows ranging ~38-69% depending on horizon.' Drop the 'no compression below it' claim — short-window vol has dipped below 57%.

DURATION CORRECTION: in rich_notes, change 'a multi-year window in which the asset went DOWN while the supposed driver went UP' to 'a 12-month window (early 2026)'; 2025 was a strong up year, so the breach is sub-2-year, not multi-year.

Everything else verifies: Bitcoin Magazine source IS sponsored and asserts no rate (correct); broad money 6-12%/yr since 1960 central ~7% is Alden's actual figure (verified); interest-adjusted debasement ~-5% 2010s / ~-25% 2020-21 (verified verbatim from Alden); 'no top because fiat has no bottom' is the maximalist sponsored reading the underlying analysts stop short of (verified — Alden argues relative-to-bonds, not absolute floor); gold correlation ~0 / <0.15 (verified); the gold-BTC decoupling in early 2026 (gold up, BTC down) is real and correctly flagged as the internal contradiction.
overstated_pros: Pro #4 ('beta=1 minimalism is more defensible... avoids the spurious-regression trap') is half-overstated: the cons section correctly demolishes the SAME identity as 'content-free' and 'enforces nothing,' so framing the minimalism as a genuine analytical PRO while the cons call it near-vacuous is internally tense. An identity that floors nothing in any finite window is not really 'more defensible' as a return model — it is more defensible as an accounting statement that happens to make no return prediction. The doc partly acknowledges this but still lists it as a clean pro.

Pro #2 ('correctly uses broad money ~7% rather than CPI... a genuine analytical improvement') overstates the analytical novelty. Using broad-money growth as the debasement measure is standard in the debasement-trade literature (Alden, JPM, Grayscale all do it); calling it 'a genuine analytical improvement over naive inflation-hedge framing' credits the construction with an insight it borrows wholesale from its own cited sources.
missing_cons: Survivorship / regime-dependence of the ~7% 'floor' input itself: broad-money growth is NOT a constant — it went negative (US M2 contracted ~2-4% in 2022-2023, first sustained decline since the 1930s). If the floor IS broad-money growth, the floor can be ~0 or negative in QT regimes, which the doc never states. The '~7% durable floor' assumes perpetual positive money growth that recent data contradicts.

No treatment of the denominator-currency choice. The whole thesis is denominated in USD broad money, but a global CMA investor's debasement rate depends on their home currency; the 6-12% range spans a 2x difference in the floor, and the doc picks the ~7% central without justifying why the median-major-economy rate is the right anchor for a USD-based CMA.

Ignores that a 21M-fixed numerator is NOT the relevant supply: BTC's effective float/issuance, lost coins, and (more importantly) the unlimited supply of CLOSE SUBSTITUTES (other crypto, tokenized gold, future protocols) means BTC's monetary share is contestable in a way the 'non-dilutable numerator' framing hides. The de-monetization risk is mentioned but supply-substitution (competing hard-money claims diluting BTC's share) is not.

No discussion of the tax/carry drag or the fact that a ~7% nominal floor that merely matches money growth delivers ZERO excess over simply holding a broad-money-indexed instrument — i.e., even if the floor held perfectly, it offers no risk premium for the ~57% vol, making the risk-adjusted proposition negative even in the success case (the doc notes poor risk-adjustment but not that the floor case is a strictly dominated trade vs cash-plus-money-growth).

new_approaches.name: Behavioral Attention & Text-Sentiment (Search/Wiki/Social NLP, Fear-Greed)
new_approaches.description: This family prices Bitcoin off retail attention and machine-read text tone rather than any cashflow, scarcity, or network fundamental. Three measurement strands feed one lens: (1) attention proxies — Google Trends search volume and Wikipedia pageviews (Kristoufek 2013); (2) linguistic sentiment — FinBERT/CryptoBERT/LLM classifiers run over X (Twitter), Reddit and news headlines to extract a tone score (Gur 2025); and (3) the composite Crypto Fear & Greed Index (Alternative.me), a 0-100 contrarian oscillator blending volatility (25%), volume/momentum (25%), social media (15%), BTC dominance (10%) and Google Trends (10%). The economic content is a reflexive attention-price feedback loop: attention drives price and price drives attention (bidirectional Granger causality), generating self-reinforcing bubbles above trend and crashes below. Critically, every credible study finds the signal forecasts only days-to-weeks momentum, volume and volatility — Twitter predictability vanishes within ~15 minutes at the trade level and ~2 weeks at the search level — with NO mechanism for long-run drift. A 10-15yr CMA therefore does NOT fall out of this family; the honest reading is a saturating-attention decay, where each adoption wave recruits a smaller marginal pool of new searchers, so the appreciation contribution of attention shrinks toward zero as the asset matures.
new_approaches.medium_explanation: The mechanism is reflexive: a burst of search/social attention pulls marginal buyers in, lifting price, which generates more attention — Kristoufek (2013) documents 0.88 (Google) / 0.83 (Wikipedia) co-movement and bidirectional causality, with a 10% search shock moving price ~2% over two periods then fading. Above trend, attention amplifies rallies; below trend it amplifies sell-offs (bubble dynamics). NLP strands (Gur 2025, FinBERT-LSTM on 650k+ headlines) add an asymmetry: negative news moves price and volatility far more than positive. The Fear & Greed composite operationalizes this as a contrarian oscillator. The decisive input for a CMA is the empirically short half-life: predictability is days-to-weeks (search) or minutes (tweets), and transaction costs erase the alpha. Because attention is a finite, saturating resource, its return contribution decays as adoption matures — implying a 10-15yr appreciation anchored to the realized decay baseline (142%→65%→17%/yr), NOT extrapolated from attention-fuelled past surges. The family is best for the volatility and short-horizon timing cells of a CMA, not long-run drift.
key_drivers: Retail search attention: Google Trends search-volume index and Wikipedia pageviews for 'Bitcoin' (Kristoufek's two phenomena-of-the-Internet-era series)
Machine-read text tone: FinBERT/CryptoBERT/LLM sentiment scores over X (Twitter), Reddit, and financial-news headlines (polarity, intensity, volume of mentions)
Reflexive attention-price feedback loop: bidirectional Granger causality (attention->price AND price->attention), with above-trend/below-trend asymmetry driving bubbles and crashes
Negative-news asymmetry: price and volatility respond markedly more to negative sentiment than positive/neutral (Gur 2025; FinBERT-LSTM + GARCH amplification)
Composite Fear & Greed Index: 0-100 contrarian oscillator weighting volatility 25%, volume/momentum 25%, social media 15%, BTC dominance 10%, Google Trends 10% (Alternative.me)

Attention saturation / S-curve maturation: the marginal pool of new searchers shrinks each cycle, so the attention return-contribution decays toward zero (the load-bearing assumption for a long-horizon CMA)
Sentiment extremity (distance from neutral) as a volatility/uncertainty predictor independent of direction (Extremity Premium, arXiv 2602.07018)
pros: Honest about its own horizon: the careful literature explicitly limits the signal to days-to-weeks momentum/volume/volatility and does NOT claim long-run forecasting — Kristoufek frames BTC as having 'no fundamental value,' so the family avoids the over-extrapolation that sinks S2F/Metcalfe

Measures a real, observable driver of a no-cashflow asset: when value is purely speculative, attention and sentiment ARE the marginal demand, and the 0.83-0.88 co-movement and bidirectional causality are genuine, replicated findings

Best-in-class for the volatility and tail/timing cells of a CMA: the Fear & Greed extremity result (arXiv 2602.07018, N=2,896, replicates on ETH and 6 of 7 cycles) and the negative-news GARCH amplification give a defensible, falsifiable handle on when BTC vol spikes

Contrarian Fear & Greed has a plausible (if marginal) ex-post edge: buying sub-25 readings beat buy-and-hold ~1,145% vs ~1,046% (2018-2025) and sub-10 readings averaged +48% 90-day returns — a real, if small-sample, mean-reversion signal
Cheap, transparent, real-time and model-light: search/pageview/sentiment series are public and refreshable daily, with no curve-fit price-history dependence
cons: Produces NO long-run expected return by construction — predictability decays in ~15 minutes (tweets) to ~2 weeks (search); any 10-15yr appreciation number must be imported from a separate model, making this family unusable as a standalone CMA drift source

Pure reflexivity / circularity: attention and price each cause the other, so the high correlation is a feedback artifact, not an exogenous valuation anchor — you cannot tell whether sentiment forecasts price or merely co-moves with it (Kristoufek concedes bidirectional causality; Reddit/Twitter studies cannot reject reverse causality)

Alpha is not exploitable net of costs: 'considering reasonable transaction costs makes it impossible to generate abnormal profits' from sentiment trading (Lou et al., ScienceDirect 2019); the Fear & Greed contrarian edge is small-sample (<10 sub-10 readings) and may not survive the institutional/ETF regime that did not exist pre-2021

Non-stationary, regime-dependent and manipulable: bot-driven social volume, sentiment concentrated in the bubble period, and a shrinking retail-attention base post-ETF (the marginal buyer is now an institution that never searches 'Bitcoin') break the historical attention-price link

Silent on cross-asset correlations and on real (inflation-adjusted) returns: the literature publishes essentially no BTC-vs-gold/equity/FI correlation from a sentiment lens, so most CMA cells must be borrowed from realized data

cited_outputs.horizon: days-to-weeks (intraday to ~2 weeks); NOT a 10-15yr horizon — the literature is explicit that the signal has no long-run forecasting content
cited_outputs.appreciation_nominal: n/a (source silent) — the attention/sentiment literature explicitly forecasts only days-to-weeks momentum/volume, not a long-run appreciation rate. Kristoufek (2013): a 10% Google Trends search shock yields ~2% price movement over ~2 periods, then the effect vanishes; no annualized or multi-year figure is published. Contrarian Fear & Greed backtests cite short-horizon returns only (sub-10 readings averaged +48% over 90 days; a buy-below-25 rule returned ~1,145% over 2018-2025 vs ~1,046% buy-and-hold) — these are realized strategy returns, not a forward CMA.
cited_outputs.appreciation_real: n/a (source silent — all figures are nominal short-horizon; no inflation-adjusted long-run number is published)
cited_outputs.volatility: n/a as an annualized point forecast, but this is the family's strongest cell: Gur (2025) shows negative sentiment drives sharper GARCH volatility (asymmetric amplification); the Extremity Premium paper (arXiv 2602.07018, N=2,896) finds sentiment extremity predicts excess uncertainty beyond realized vol (within-quintile premium p<0.001, Granger F=211), replicating on ETH and 6 of 7 cycles. No single annualized vol figure is published.
cited_outputs.corr_growth_eq: n/a (source silent) — single-asset attention/sentiment studies publish no cross-asset correlation
cited_outputs.corr_gold: n/a (source silent) — the sentiment/attention literature makes no BTC-vs-gold correlation claim; it is a standalone single-asset behavioral framework with no digital-gold axis
cited_outputs.notes: Cited outputs are deliberately almost all 'n/a (source silent)' because this family does not produce CMA-grade long-horizon outputs — that absence IS the finding. The only published quantitative content is short-horizon (Kristoufek's ~2% price move per 10% search shock over ~2 periods) and backward-looking strategy backtests (Fear & Greed sub-10 -> +48% 90-day; buy-below-25 ~1,145% vs ~1,046% buy-and-hold 2018-2025). Volatility is the one cell the literature genuinely informs, via negative-news GARCH amplification and the extremity-premium uncertainty result.

synthesized_outputs.appreciation_nominal: ~8-12%/yr (JUDGMENT, not a model output; center ~10%). The family produces no native long-run drift, so I anchor entirely to the realized appreciation DECAY (full 142% -> 10y 65% -> 5y 17%/yr) and apply the family's own organizing idea — attention saturation. Each adoption wave recruits a smaller marginal pool of new searchers/posters, and post-ETF the marginal buyer is an institution who never searches 'Bitcoin,' so the attention return-contribution decays toward zero. I push the 10-15yr forward to the low end of / just below the trailing-5y 17%, landing on a maturing-risk-asset rate consistent with the honest cross-approach central (~8-12% nominal).
synthesized_outputs.appreciation_real: ~5-9%/yr real (center ~7%), nominal less ~2.5-3% long-run CPI. Judgment overlay; the sentiment family is silent on real returns.
synthesized_outputs.volatility: ~55-60%/yr (center ~57%). This is the cell the family most legitimately informs: negative-news GARCH amplification (Gur) and the extremity-premium uncertainty result imply vol stays elevated and spikes during extreme-sentiment regimes. Floor held AT realized trailing-5y ~57% rather than below it — the sub-2yr ETF sample does not yet evidence compression, and sentiment-driven reflexive crashes keep the tail fat. Stays multiples of equities/gold.
synthesized_outputs.corr_growth_eq: ~0.45-0.55 (center ~0.50). Family is silent, so anchored to realized trailing-5y 0.56. Attention/sentiment is a risk-on/liquidity-sensitive driver shared with growth-tech equities; I hold it elevated but slightly mean-reverted from the post-ETF spike.
synthesized_outputs.corr_value_eq: ~0.30-0.40 (center ~0.35; tracks realized 5y 0.37). Lower than growth-equity; BTC is a long-duration, sentiment-driven risk asset less tied to the value factor.
synthesized_outputs.corr_fi_nominal: ~0.15-0.25 (center ~0.20; realized 5y 0.19). Low-positive via shared liquidity/rate-cycle sensitivity; sentiment lens gives no structural duration link.
synthesized_outputs.corr_tips: ~0.20-0.30 (center ~0.25; realized 5y 0.30). Slightly above nominal FI through a shared real-rate/liquidity channel; weak and regime-dependent.
synthesized_outputs.corr_gold: ~0.0-0.15 (center ~0.05). The family supplies NO digital-gold mechanism — attention/sentiment is single-asset and silent on gold — and realized BTC-gold correlation is ~0 (full -0.01, 5y +0.04). I hold it at the bottom of the band and explicitly reject any digital-gold co-movement reading; if anything, sentiment-driven reflexivity makes BTC behave LESS like a safe-haven store of value than gold, not more.
synthesized_outputs.notes: All synthesized cells are JUDGMENT, not framework outputs — this family forecasts only days-to-weeks behavior, so I anchor drift to the realized decay baseline and the family's saturating-attention logic, hold vol at the realized floor (the one cell sentiment genuinely informs), and borrow correlations from realized data. The internally consistent reading is: useful for the vol/timing half of a CMA, useless for the drift/correlation half on its own.

new_approaches.rich_notes:
METHODOLOGY. This family is a behavioral-demand lens for a no-cashflow asset, merging four candidate signals into one approach: (a) Google Trends search volume and (b) Wikipedia pageviews as retail-attention proxies; (c) machine-read TEXT tone from FinBERT/CryptoBERT/LLM classifiers over X, Reddit and news; and (d) the composite Crypto Fear & Greed Index. It is distinct from existing digest row #9 (Cross-Sectional Factor & Macro-Liquidity Regression), which uses an attention PROXY as one numeric regressor (the Liu-Tsyvinski investor-attention factor) but never parses linguistic content nor adopts a published sentiment composite as the lens. Here, attention/sentiment IS the framework, not a control.

KEY RELATIONSHIPS & HISTORICAL FIT. Kristoufek (2013, Scientific Reports 3:3415) is the seminal anchor: weekly Google Trends vs price correlation 0.8786, daily Wikipedia 0.8271 (both p<0.01). The causality is explicitly BIDIRECTIONAL (Granger both ways) — attention drives price and price drives attention — and a 10% search shock produces ~2% cumulative price movement over ~2 periods, after which the effect vanishes. The pivotal qualitative finding is an above-trend/below-trend ASYMMETRY: above the trend, rising interest pushes price higher; below trend, rising interest pushes price LOWER — i.e., attention amplifies whichever direction the market is already moving, a textbook bubble-and-crash reflexivity. Kristoufek frames Bitcoin as having "no fundamental value" with a market "of speculative traders," which is exactly why an attention lens is appropriate AND why it cannot anchor a long-run level.

Gur (2025, Journal of Forecasting, doi 10.1002/for.70068) modernizes the text strand: FinBERT-based sentiment over 650,000+ financial-news headlines, best model FinBERT-LSTM, with a robust asymmetry — Bitcoin's price (and GARCH volatility) responds far more strongly to NEGATIVE news than positive/neutral. This is a daily/short-horizon directional-and-volatility result, not a multi-year forecast. The Fear & Greed Index (Alternative.me) operationalizes the composite: volatility 25%, volume/momentum 25%, social media 15% (a text-processing algorithm scraping X mentions and engagement velocity), BTC dominance 10%, Google Trends 10%, scaled 0 (extreme fear) to 100 (extreme greed), used contrarian.

FAILURE MODES (faithful critiques). (1) NO LONG-RUN DRIFT. The decisive limitation: predictability decays in ~15 minutes at the trade level (Twitter; consistent with daily-level efficiency) and ~2 weeks at the search level. There is no mechanism for 10-15yr appreciation — any CMA drift number is imported. (2) REFLEXIVITY/CIRCULARITY. Because attention and price each cause the other, the high correlation is a feedback artifact; reverse causality cannot be rejected. (3) ALPHA NET OF COSTS IS ~ZERO. Lou/Aslanidis et al. (Finance Research Letters, ScienceDirect 2019): "considering reasonable transaction costs makes it impossible to generate abnormal profits" from sentiment trading; predictability is concentrated in the bubble period and driven by social sentiment, not macro news. (4) REGIME BREAK / NON-STATIONARITY. Bot-amplified social volume, and a shrinking retail-attention base post-ETF (the marginal buyer is now an institution who never Googles "Bitcoin"), erode the historical link. (5) SILENT ON CORRELATIONS AND REAL RETURNS — most CMA cells must be borrowed from realized data.

ON-RECORD MULTI-YEAR FORECASTS PRODUCED THIS WAY. Essentially none, which is itself the finding. The careful academic literature deliberately refuses long-horizon point forecasts; Kristoufek makes "no claims about long-run price-level forecasting." The only multi-year evidence is BACKWARD-LOOKING strategy backtests, not forward CMAs: buying when Fear & Greed fell below 25 returned ~1,145% over 2018-2025 vs ~1,046% buy-and-hold (a thin ~100-bp-of-total edge over seven years), and sub-10 readings averaged +48% / median +48.5% over the subsequent 90 days with no negative 90-day instances — but on fewer than ten sub-10 observations, so the small-sample caveat is severe and the institutional-era out-of-sample is untested. The Extremity Premium working paper (arXiv 2602.07018, 2026; N=2,896, Feb-2018-Jan-2026) is the most rigorous recent contribution and pointedly forecasts UNCERTAINTY/spreads, not direction or level: extremity (distance from neutral) predicts excess uncertainty beyond realized vol (within-quintile p<0.001, Cohen's d=0.21, Granger F=211, placebo p<0.0001, replicating on ETH and 6 of 7 cycles).

CMA IMPLICATION. Treat this family as the VOLATILITY-and-timing engine of a Bitcoin CMA, never the appreciation engine. For drift, I anchor to the realized decay (142%->65%->17%/yr) and the family's own saturating-attention logic to push the 10-15yr forward to ~8-12% nominal / ~5-9% real — at/just below the trailing-5y rate, since the marginal attention pool shrinks as BTC institutionalizes. Vol stays ~55-60% (the family's best-supported cell, via negative-news GARCH amplification and the extremity premium). Correlations are borrowed from realized data (growth-eq ~0.50, value ~0.35, FI ~0.20, TIPS ~0.25, gold ~0.05); the family supplies no digital-gold axis, so I keep BTC-gold near zero and reject any safe-haven reading — reflexive, sentiment-driven crash behavior makes BTC LESS gold-like, not more.

issues: FEAR & GREED WEIGHTS ARE WRONG (factual error, repeated 4+ times). JSON lists volatility 25% / volume-momentum 25% / social 15% / dominance 10% / Google Trends 10% = 85%. The real Alternative.me methodology includes a sixth component, SURVEYS (15%), bringing the total to 100% (surveys are currently paused but remain part of the published weighting). Dropping surveys silently is a misattribution of the index's own methodology, and it is repeated in description, key_drivers, cons, and representative_sources.

MISATTRIBUTED AUTHOR. The Finance Research Letters paper 'Does investor sentiment on social media provide robust information for Bitcoin returns predictability?' (vol 38, S1544612319314199) is by DOMINIQUE GUEGAN and THOMAS RENAULT (2021), NOT 'D. Lou / J. Aslanidis et al.' as cited in representative_sources and repeated in rich_notes. The cited authorship appears invented. (Aslanidis et al. authored a DIFFERENT 2024 paper on attention and crypto correlations.) The year is also given inconsistently (2019 in cons/notes vs 2020 in the source list; the actual publication year is 2021).

FABRICATED-VERBATIM QUOTE. The phrase 'considering reasonable transaction costs makes it impossible to generate abnormal profits' is wrapped in quotation marks as if quoting the paper, but the actual abstract reads 'the magnitude of the effect is rather small making it impossible for a trader to make economic profits by trading on the information published on social media.' The substantive claim (no exploitable alpha net of costs) is correct, but the quotation is not verbatim.

KRISTOUFEK CORRELATIONS GLOSSED. The 0.8786 (Google) / 0.8271 (Wikipedia) figures are correctly sourced but are LOG-LOG-scale correlations, and the paper finds the Google series is NOT cointegrated with price (only Wikipedia is). The JSON's repeated '0.83-0.88 co-movement and bidirectional causality' framing presents these as if level co-movement, slightly overstating the strength/cleanliness of the relationship.

UNVERIFIABLE MAGNITUDE. The specific claim 'a 10% search shock moving price ~2% over two periods then fading' / '~2% cumulative price movement over ~2 periods' could not be confirmed from available sources for Kristoufek (2013); it is a plausible characterization of his VAR impulse-response but the exact magnitudes are unverified and should be hedged or sourced to a page/figure.

MINOR: Extremity Premium N reconciliation. The agent-based model is calibrated to 739 days of Bitcoin data; the N=2,896 refers to the daily Fear & Greed sample (Feb-2018-Jan-2026, ~8yr of daily obs), and the author is Murad Farzulla. All consistent, but the JSON never names the author and conflates the two sample sizes in a way that could read as one figure.
verdict.corrections: ["Fear & Greed weights: state all SIX components - volatility 25%, momentum/volume 25%, social media 15%, SURVEYS 15% (currently paused), BTC dominance 10%, Google Trends 10% = 100%. Note surveys are paused if you want, but do not silently drop them.", "Re-attribute the FRL sentiment-predictability paper to Guegan & Renault (2021); remove 'D. Lou / J. Aslanidis et al.' Fix the year to 2021 throughout (cons, notes, source list).", "Either quote Guegan & Renault verbatim ('...the magnitude of the effect is rather small making it impossible for a trader to make economic profits...') or drop the quotation marks and paraphrase.", "Qualify the Kristoufek correlations as log-log-scale, and note Google is NOT cointegrated with price (only Wikipedia), so the relationship is correlational, not a stable long-run equilibrium - which actually STRENGTHENS the no-long-run-drift thesis.", "Source the '10% shock -> ~2% price move' claim to a specific table/figure in Kristoufek (2013) or soften to 'a positive but transient impulse response that decays within weeks.'", "Name the Extremity Premium author (Farzulla, 2026) and separate the N=2,896 daily-sentiment sample from the 739-day agent-based-model calibration."]
overstated_pros: Pro #4 (contrarian Fear & Greed 'plausible ex-post edge'): the 1,145% vs 1,046% figures are real and correctly sourced (Bitcoin Magazine / Phemex 2018-2025), but the JSON's own cons correctly call this a ~100bp-of-total edge over 7 years - so listing it as a PRO is generous; it is closer to 'statistically indistinguishable from buy-and-hold after the timing risk of sitting in cash.' The sub-10 -> +48% 90-day figure rests on <10 observations and an undisclosed backtest - acknowledged, but it should not be presented as a pro at all.

Pro #1 ('honest about its own horizon') and Pro #2 ('measures a real observable driver') are fair, but Pro #2's '0.83-0.88 co-movement and bidirectional causality are genuine, replicated findings' overstates: it is a reflexive/circular relationship the JSON's OWN cons admit cannot establish causal direction - so calling it a valuation 'driver' (even hedged) is slightly stronger than the evidence.
missing_cons: Look-ahead / survivorship bias in ALL the contrarian backtests: the 1,145% and +48% figures are computed on a single realized BTC path that went up ~1000x; any 'buy the dip' rule looks good on a monotonically-rising asset. This is a fatal critique of the only quantitative pro and is not stated.

The Fear & Greed Index itself is endogenous to price: 50% of its weight (volatility 25% + momentum/volume 25%) is mechanically derived from price/return data, so 'buying low Fear & Greed' is largely just 'buying after drawdowns' - a momentum/mean-reversion artifact, not a sentiment edge. The JSON treats Fear & Greed as a sentiment signal when half of it is price.

Data-history limitation: the Fear & Greed Index only begins Feb-2018, so NONE of the sentiment-composite evidence covers the 2013 or 2017 cycles, and the whole family's quantitative track record is ~1.5 cycles - far too short to inform a 10-15yr CMA, beyond even the general 'short history' caveat.

No treatment of reflexivity cutting BOTH ways on the DOWNSIDE for a CMA: saturating attention plus a fat reflexive-crash tail implies the appreciation distribution is severely left-skewed (ruin/permanent-impairment risk), which a point estimate of ~10% nominal entirely hides. The vol number captures dispersion but not the skew/drawdown asymmetry the family's own negative-news result implies.

Sentiment measurement is itself non-stationary and model-dependent: FinBERT/CryptoBERT/LLM classifiers are retrained and drift, X API access has been gated/repriced since 2023, and Google Trends is a relative (re-based) index - so the historical sentiment series are not even consistently measurable forward, undermining any refreshable-pipeline claim.

new_approaches.name: Narrative-Economics / Reflexivity Feedback-Loop (SIR Contagion + Garcia VAR)
new_approaches.description: This approach values Bitcoin not as a cashflow asset and not via a fitted price-vs-time curve, but by modeling the contagious BELIEF/story itself as an epidemic and empirically measuring the Soros reflexive loop that the belief drives. Shiller (Narrative Economics, 2019) treats the Bitcoin narrative as a transmissible 'infection': the population splits into Susceptible / Infected (believers) / Recovered, with a contagion rate c and recovery (forgetting) rate r whose ratio sets a reproduction number; the Infected share follows a HUMP-SHAPED epidemic curve (rise, peak, decay) that can RELAPSE in fresh waves, explicitly analogizing BTC's 2013/2017 run-ups to the Ebola epidemic curve. Garcia, Tessone, Mavrodiev & Perony (2014, J. R. Soc. Interface) make the loop empirical: a 4-variable VAR on price, word-of-mouth (Twitter), search (Google) and new-user growth identifies two positive feedback loops — a word-of-mouth loop and a new-user loop — quantifying the reflexive channels (e.g. price→search φ≈0.39, search→word-of-mouth φ≈0.24, word-of-mouth→price φ≈0.10; search→users φ≈0.16, users→price φ≈0.14). Soros (2014) supplies the theory: prices and the beliefs about them are mutually endogenous, so booms are self-reinforcing until the susceptible pool exhausts and the loop reverses. A 10-15yr CMA is NOT a point forecast that drops out; the framework yields a SHAPE — a damped-contagion / saturating-feedback decay path where each successive epidemic wave is less infectious (fewer never-heard-of-it susceptibles remain), peak amplitudes fall, and trend appreciation decays toward a low secular rate, with high recurring volatility from the relapsing wave structure. Distinct from logistic adoption (row 14: monotone-saturating USERS) and LPPLS (row 18: reflexivity abstracted into a crash-hazard singularity) — here the diffusing object is a relapsing BELIEF and the feedback channels are individually measured.
new_approaches.medium_explanation: Bitcoin has no cashflows, so this school values the contagious STORY instead. Shiller (2019) models the 'Bitcoin narrative' as an epidemic: people are Susceptible, then Infected (believers), then Recovered/bored, governed by a contagion rate and a recovery rate. Like a disease, the believer share is hump-shaped — it rises, peaks when the susceptible pool thins, then decays — and crucially can RELAPSE in new waves (2013, 2017, 2021). Garcia et al. (2014) make the loop measurable: a VAR on price, social-media word-of-mouth, search and new users finds two self-reinforcing loops (word-of-mouth and new-user), quantifying Soros's reflexivity — price feeds attention feeds adoption feeds price. For a 10-15yr CMA the output is a SHAPE, not a number: each wave recruits a smaller pool of never-heard-of-it susceptibles, so peak amplitudes and trend appreciation DECAY while volatility stays high from the relapsing booms and busts. Inputs: contagion/recovery rates, the VAR feedback coefficients, and the shrinking susceptible reservoir. It rationalizes BTC's observed appreciation decay and persistent high vol better than scarcity models.
key_drivers: Contagion (infection/transmission) rate of the Bitcoin narrative vs the recovery/forgetting rate — their ratio (an R0-like reproduction number) sets whether a fresh epidemic wave ignites and how high it peaks

Size of the remaining SUSCEPTIBLE pool — the stock of people who have not yet heard/adopted the story; it shrinks secularly across waves, so each successive epidemic is less explosive (the core decay mechanism)

Reflexive feedback coefficients (Garcia VAR): price->search (~0.39), search->word-of-mouth (~0.24), word-of-mouth->price (~0.10); search->new-users (~0.16), new-users->price (~0.14) — the measured strength of the self-reinforcing loops
Word-of-mouth / social-media volume (Twitter mentions) as the contagion vector for the word-of-mouth loop
Search-volume (Google Trends) as both an attention amplifier and, per Garcia, an early WARNING — search spikes preceded large price DROPS
New-user / active-wallet growth as the adoption-loop vector (SIR variants map open wallets to the susceptible/infected pools)
Recurring multi-year wave/relapse structure — narratives fade and re-ignite (mutate via new sub-stories: ETF, sovereign reserve, debasement), driving the boom-bust cadence rather than a smooth path
Exogenous shocks/triggers — crashes are attributed to outside stimuli the endogenous loop cannot self-predict (Garcia, Sornette-adjacent)
pros: Directly explains the two BTC facts most CMA models can't: (a) the appreciation DECAY (each wave recruits a smaller susceptible pool, so peaks shrink) and (b) the persistent HIGH volatility / boom-bust cadence (relapsing epidemic waves) — the shape matches realized history without curve-fitting price on time

Empirically grounded and falsifiable, not numerology: Garcia et al. (peer-reviewed, J. R. Soc. Interface) actually MEASURE the feedback channels with a VAR, reconstruct price at rho=0.84, and correctly sign 9-10 of the 10 largest daily moves — real out-of-sample-ish content, and the search-spike-precedes-crash finding is a genuine leading indicator

Captures reflexivity/demand that supply-side models (S2F, cost-of-production) ignore entirely — price and belief are modeled as mutually endogenous (Soros), which is the actual driver of a no-cashflow speculative asset

Carries an Anthropic-grade pedigree (Shiller, Nobel laureate; Soros; ETH-Zurich complexity group) and a clear mechanism for why naive extrapolation fails — a useful skeptical counterweight to crypto-native hype models
Naturally produces a distribution with fat left tails and negative skew (waves end in busts), which is the right risk shape for portfolio construction even if the point return is imprecise
cons: Produces NO native appreciation number. SIR/VAR describe the SHAPE and timing of waves, not a 10-15yr expected return; any CMA appreciation figure is bolted-on judgment about how fast peaks decay — the framework is silent on the level

Parameter instability and reverse causality: the contagion/recovery rates and VAR coefficients are estimated on short, regime-specific samples (Garcia's data is 2011-2013); Garcia himself cannot rule out price->wallet-creation (reverse causation), and the loops are calibrated pre-institutionalization. Post-ETF, the marginal buyer is an allocator who never tweets or opens a wallet, breaking the social-trace inputs

Crashes are exogenous by construction — both Garcia and the SIR setup attribute the bust to outside stimuli the model 'can provide no warning' for, so it cannot forecast the very drawdowns a long-horizon holder must survive (same blind spot as LPPLS)

The proxies degrade over time: Twitter/X word-of-mouth, Google search, and on-chain wallet growth are increasingly noisy or gamed (bots, off-chain custody, ETF flows), so the contagion vectors that drove the 2011-2017 fits are weakening — the empirical engine is eroding precisely as the asset matures
Says nothing directly about cross-asset correlations or volatility-as-a-stat; those must be imported from realized data. It is a narrative-dynamics model, not a full distributional CMA

Risk of just-so storytelling: with enough sub-narratives (ETF, halving, debasement, AI-treasury) one can always claim a 'new wave' ex-post; the framework is more convincing as a descriptive lens than as a disciplined forward estimator

The framework's honest contribution is the decay+vol shape and the explicit rejection of monotone extrapolation, not a precise return.

new_approaches.rich_notes:
METHODOLOGY. This is a narrative-reflexivity family that fuses three strands. (1) Shiller's Narrative Economics (2019) imports the SIR epidemic model from epidemiology: a population is partitioned into Susceptible (haven't heard the BTC story), Infected (believers who spread it), and Recovered (heard it but no longer act on it / forgot). Transmission is governed by a contagion rate c and a recovery rate r; their ratio behaves like a basic reproduction number R0. The Infected share follows a hump-shaped curve — it rises while c-driven new infections outpace r-driven recoveries, peaks as the Susceptible pool thins, then declines. Critically, narratives can MUTATE and RELAPSE: a new sub-story (ETF, sovereign reserve, debasement hedge) re-infects the population, producing a fresh wave. Shiller's only explicit BTC claim is qualitative and visual — he overlays the Bitcoin price-attention run-up on the Ebola epidemic curve to argue the story, like a disease, follows an epidemic arc that ultimately decays. (2) Garcia, Tessone, Mavrodiev & Perony (2014, J. R. Soc. Interface) make the loop EMPIRICAL with a four-variable vector autoregression (VAR) on daily Bitcoin price, Twitter word-of-mouth (BTC tweets per million), Google search volume, and new-user/wallet growth. They identify two positive feedback loops in the absence of exogenous stimuli: a WORD-OF-MOUTH loop (price->search->word-of-mouth->price) and a NEW-USER loop (price->search->users->price), with estimated one-step coefficients price->search ~0.39, search->word-of-mouth ~0.24, word-of-mouth->price ~0.10, search->users ~0.16, users->price ~0.14. Impulse-response (10,000 bootstraps) shows search rises 2-4 days after price increases and word-of-mouth/users rise 1-2 days after search; the 4-day-lag VAR reconstructs price at rho=0.84 and correctly signs 9 or 10 of the 10 largest daily moves in their late sample. A notable asymmetry: large price DROPS are PRECEDED by search spikes — search is a leading bust indicator. (3) Soros (2014, J. Economic Methodology) supplies the philosophy: fallibility + reflexivity = the 'human uncertainty principle'; markets don't passively reflect fundamentals, they actively shape the beliefs and flows that become the fundamentals, so boom-bust loops are intrinsic, not anomalies.

CMA DERIVATION. No appreciation number falls out natively. The framework delivers a SHAPE: (a) appreciation DECAY, because each epidemic wave can only recruit from a shrinking pool of never-heard-of-it susceptibles, so peak amplitudes fall over time; (b) high, recurring VOLATILITY, because the relapsing-wave structure is intrinsically boom-bust; (c) negatively-skewed, fat-left-tailed returns, because waves end in exogenously-triggered busts the model cannot self-predict. To produce a CMA you must judgmentally map 'shrinking susceptible pool + weakening social-trace loops' onto a decay rate, then anchor to realized history. That yields my ~7-11% nominal / ~4-8% real, vol ~55-65%, equity-like correlations (~0.4-0.55 growth), and a gold correlation held near zero — because the contagion mechanism gives no debasement/safe-haven channel, only a risk-appetite/attention channel.

HISTORICAL FIT. The framework fits BTC's qualitative history well: the 2011, 2013, 2017 and 2021 cycles look like successive epidemic waves with declining log-amplitude, matching the realized 142%->65%->17%/yr decay. The Garcia VAR's in-sample sign accuracy is genuinely impressive for a social-data model.

FAILURE MODES / CRITIQUES (faithful). First, severe parameter instability and reverse causality: Garcia's data ends in 2013 and the authors cannot rule out price->wallet-creation; the loops are pre-institutional. Post-ETF, the marginal buyer is an allocator who never tweets or opens an on-chain wallet, so the contagion vectors (Twitter, search, wallets) are decoupling from the price they once drove. Second, crashes are EXOGENOUS by construction — the very drawdowns that determine a long-horizon holder's geometric return are outside the model's predictive reach. Third, just-so risk: with a steady supply of fresh sub-narratives one can always label a new wave ex-post, making the lens more descriptive than predictive. Fourth, the proxies are degrading (bots, off-chain custody, ETF flows). 

ON-RECORD MULTI-YEAR FORECASTS. None from the named primary authors — Shiller, Garcia and Soros deliberately avoid point price targets; Shiller's BTC commentary is famously skeptical (he has repeatedly called it a speculative bubble narrative, not endorsed a target). The closest empirical descendant, the 2024 'Do infectious diseases explain Bitcoin price fluctuations?' SIR study, forecasts active-WALLET counts (recovery rate from downtrends, infection rate from uptrends) to within ~3 days of price explosions and notes wallets correlate with price — but offers no 10-15yr appreciation figure. So the framework is best used as a SHAPE prior (decay + high vol + equity-correlation, gold-uncorrelated) and a skeptical check on monotone extrapolation, not as a source of a headline number.

issues: CITED NUMBERS ARE REAL AND ACCURATELY ATTRIBUTED. Verified against the open-access PMC copy of Garcia et al. 2014: price->search phi=0.386 (doc says ~0.39), search->word-of-mouth=0.243 (~0.24), word-of-mouth->price=0.100 (~0.10), search->users=0.158 (~0.16), users->price=0.137 (~0.14); price reconstruction rho=0.8422 (doc says 0.84); 'all 10 largest increases + 9 of 10 largest drops correctly signed' (doc says 9-10 of 10). Data period mid-2010 to Oct-2013. All exact. The doc's claim that Garcia's data is '2011-2013' is slightly off -- it actually runs from June 2010 -- but this is trivially in the doc's favor (the sample is even shorter/earlier than implied weakens the engine further).

OVERSTATED/INVERTED FINDING: The doc repeatedly frames 'search spikes PRECEDE/LEAD price DROPS (by 2-4 days)' as a 'genuine leading indicator' and a key pro. The paper's actual finding is weaker and partly the reverse direction: the dominant signed loop is price->search (phi=0.386, large) -- i.e. price moves DRIVE search, not vice versa. The drop-prediction claim in the paper is only that 'three of the four largest daily price drops were preceded by... increases in Google search volume the day BEFORE' (1-day lag, n=3 of 4, in-sample, late period only). The doc's '2-4 day lead' figure conflates the 2-4 day impulse-response lag of search-AFTER-price with a search-BEFORE-drops lead. This overstates a genuinely thin, small-n, in-sample anecdote into a robust leading indicator.

SOROS CITATION YEAR DISCREPANCY (minor): doc lists Soros 2014; the Journal of Economic Methodology article (vol 20(4):309-329) is dated 2013 in the journal/RePEc record (Soros's own site posts it Jan 2014). Volume/issue/pages exact. Not a fabrication, just an ambiguous-year citation.

SYNTHESIZED 7-11% NOMINAL IS DEFENSIBLE AS A SHAPE-ANCHORED JUDGMENT, NOT HYPE -- but it is doing more extrapolation than the doc admits. The framework genuinely produces NO appreciation number (doc states this honestly and repeatedly). Anchoring to realized decay 142->65->17%/yr and 'pushing one regime further' to 7-11% is internally consistent with the decay logic; if anything the framework's own mechanism (shrinking susceptible pool + degrading social proxies post-ETF) argues the next regime could undershoot 7-11% materially (single digits or lower). So 7-11% is a reasonable-to-slightly-generous central, NOT hype. The honest read: the framework supports 'decaying and lower than realized,' and 7-11% sits at the optimistic edge of what 'one regime further' implies.

VOL 55-65% AND ~57% FLOOR ARE DEFENSIBLE. The doc explicitly anchors the floor to realized trailing-5y ~57% and refuses to compress below realized evidence -- this is the disciplined move. The relapsing-epidemic structure genuinely predicts persistent high vol, so 55-65% is well-justified and among the least-hyped cells. No vol compression assumed = appropriately conservative.

GOLD CORRELATION ~0.0-0.10 IS THE STRONGEST, MOST DEFENSIBLE CELL. Correctly anchored to realized (~0 full, +0.045 5y), and the framework genuinely supplies no debasement/safe-haven mechanism. The doc explicitly DECLINES to treat BTC as a gold substitute and routes co-movement to risk assets instead. This is the right call and resists the digital-gold hype other frameworks indulge.

CORRELATIONS (growth 0.40-0.55, value 0.20-0.35, FI 0.05-0.20, TIPS 0.15-0.30) ARE IMPORTED FROM REALIZED DATA, NOT MODEL-DERIVED -- the doc admits this ('must be imported from realized data'). They track realized 5y anchors (growth 0.56, value 0.37, FI 0.19, TIPS 0.30). Defensible but note: every synthesized correlation band sits AT OR BELOW its realized 5y anchor, which is a mild conservatism, not hype.
verdict.corrections: ["Reframe the 'search-spike-precedes-crash' pro: downgrade from 'genuine leading indicator (2-4 day lead)' to 'a thin in-sample anecdote (3 of 4 largest drops preceded by a search spike the day before, late-period only).' The DOMINANT verified relationship is price->search (phi=0.386), i.e. price drives attention, which undercuts using search as a forward bust signal. Remove or heavily qualify the '2-4 day' lead figure.", "Fix Garcia data window in rich_notes/cons: it is mid-2010 to Oct-2013, not '2011-2013.' (Cuts in the doc's favor -- even shorter pre-institutional sample.)", "Set Soros citation year to 2013 (journal/RePEc record) or annotate '2013/2014' to reflect the print-vs-posting ambiguity.", "Add an explicit caveat to the 7-11% nominal cell that the framework's OWN logic (shrinking susceptible reservoir + post-ETF decoupling of the social-trace inputs that the entire empirical engine depends on) is a downside-asymmetric argument -- i.e. the central could reasonably sit below 7% and the band should acknowledge a fatter low tail than the 7-11% range conveys. As written, 7-11% reads as the optimistic edge of 'one regime further.'", "Surface the missing self-consistency tension: the doc leans on Garcia's empirical credibility (rho=0.84, sign accuracy) to validate the framework, yet simultaneously argues (correctly) that Garcia's social-trace inputs are decoupling post-ETF. The empirical validation and the forward applicability are in direct tension -- the engine that earns the pedigree is the same engine the cons say is eroding. This should be stated as the framework's central limitation for a 10-15yr CMA, not buried."]
overstated_pros: 'search-spike-precedes-crash finding is a genuine leading indicator' -- overstated; it is 3-of-4 largest drops, 1-day lag, in-sample, late-period only, and the dominant signed loop runs price->search (attention follows price). Presented as robust out-of-sample-grade content when it is a small-n in-sample anecdote.

'real out-of-sample-ish content' -- the rho=0.84 reconstruction and sign accuracy are IN-SAMPLE fits of a VAR on its own training window (P3 of the same 2010-2013 data); calling it 'out-of-sample-ish' inflates its predictive standing.

Implied robustness of the 7-11% nominal -- the framework provides no number and its own mechanisms argue for further decay; presenting 7-11% as 'consistent with cross-approach central ~8-12%' borrows credibility from other frameworks rather than this one, which natively supports only 'lower than realized 17%, possibly well below.'
missing_cons: SELF-UNDERMINING EMPIRICS: the same Garcia social-trace engine that supplies the framework's only empirical credibility (rho=0.84, pedigree) is the engine the doc says is decoupling post-ETF -- so the validation does not transfer to the forecast horizon. The doc lists proxy degradation as a con but never states that this VOIDS the very evidence used to sell the framework's rigor.

NO HALVING / SUPPLY-SCHEDULE INTERACTION: the framework is purely demand/attention-side and is silent on whether the ~4yr halving cadence is what actually paces the 'waves' (an alternative, supply-driven explanation for the same hump-shaped cycles). If halvings, not narrative contagion, drive the cadence, the SIR fit is observationally confounded -- the doc treats the wave structure as evidence FOR contagion without ruling out the mechanical supply clock.

SURVIVORSHIP / SINGLE-ASSET FIT: SIR/narrative framing was fit to BTC ex-post precisely because BTC survived and relapsed; thousands of dead alt-narratives followed the same epidemic curve into zero. The framework cannot, ex-ante, distinguish a relapsing asset from a terminal one -- a critical blind spot for a 10-15yr HOLD CMA, distinct from the listed 'exogenous crash' and 'just-so' cons.

GEOMETRIC vs ARITHMETIC DRAG NOT ADDRESSED: with 55-65% vol the variance drag (~0.5*sigma^2 ~ 15-20%/yr) means a 7-11% ARITHMETIC mean implies a materially lower compounded/geometric return -- potentially near or below zero in real terms over 10-15yr. The doc reports appreciation without specifying arithmetic-vs-geometric, which at this vol level is the single most important distinction for a long-horizon allocator.

new_approaches.name: Behavioral-Preference / Disagreement Overvaluation (Lottery-MAX, Miller, Scheinkman-Xiong)
new_approaches.description: This family derives expected returns from investor PREFERENCES and BELIEFS rather than fundamentals. Two channels. (1) Lottery/MAX + cumulative-prospect-theory: investors overpay for assets with extreme positive-skew payoffs (high recent MAX daily return, high PT-value), so those assets are overpriced and earn LOWER future returns — a negative cross-sectional MAX/PT-to-return relation. (2) Divergence-of-opinion + short-sale constraints (Miller 1977; Scheinkman-Xiong 2003): when optimists and pessimists disagree and pessimists cannot short, price reflects only the optimists' valuation, biasing price upward; Scheinkman-Xiong add a resale-option bubble (holders pay above their own valuation expecting to sell to a more optimistic buyer), accompanied by high volume and high volatility. The CMA-relevant implication is NOT a price level but a DECAY mechanism: the overvaluation premium shrinks as the holder base institutionalizes (rational, diversified marginal holders replace lottery-seekers) and as short/margin/options infrastructure deepens (pessimists can finally express views). It is contrarian and infrastructure-conditional. Crucially these are CROSS-SECTIONAL alt-coin anomalies — the alphas are concentrated in small, illiquid, costly-to-arbitrage coins, NOT Bitcoin, which is the largest, most liquid, and (post-CME-futures, post-IBIT-options, post-inverse-ETF) least short-constrained coin. So for a BTC-specific 10-15yr CMA the family's verdict is that BTC's behavioral overvaluation premium has LARGELY ALREADY DISSIPATED, independently corroborating the realized appreciation decay rather than projecting continued excess return.
new_approaches.medium_explanation: Value is set by who holds the asset and what they believe, not by cashflow or scarcity. Lottery/prospect-theory investors overpay for extreme positive skew, so high-MAX/high-PT coins are overpriced and subsequently underperform (a one-SD rise in PT value cuts next-week return ~0.71%; high-minus-low MAX spreads exceed ~1.5-3%/week). Separately, Miller (1977) and Scheinkman-Xiong (2003) show that when opinions diverge AND shorting is blocked, price reflects only optimists plus a resale-option bubble, with high volume and volatility. The forward-CMA signal is a decay rule: the overvaluation premium erodes as the holder base institutionalizes and as short/margin/options infrastructure deepens. Garfinkel-Hsiao-Hu (2025) show the crypto disagreement premium literally vanishes once a coin's margin trading is switched on. Because these effects concentrate in small, illiquid, hard-to-short coins — not Bitcoin, which now has CME futures, IBIT options and inverse ETFs — the family implies BTC's behavioral premium is mostly gone, so a 10-15yr BTC CMA should extrapolate decayed, near-risk-asset returns, not historical levels.
key_drivers: Lottery/MAX demand: maximum recent daily return as a positive-skew proxy; high MAX = overpriced = lower future return (negative cross-sectional relation)
Cumulative-prospect-theory (PT) value of the historical return distribution (probability weighting of tails + loss aversion); high PT value = overpriced
Divergence of opinion / disagreement, proxied by abnormal trading volume (Garfinkel-Hsiao-Hu) or forecast dispersion (Miller)
Short-sale constraints — the binding condition that lets optimists set the price; relaxing them (margin, futures, options, inverse ETFs, borrow) removes the overvaluation
Resale-option / speculative-bubble component (Scheinkman-Xiong): holders pay above own valuation expecting to sell to a more optimistic future buyer; scales with overconfidence and trading frictions
Holder-base composition / institutionalization: lottery-seeking retail vs diversified rational marginal holder
Limits to arbitrage (illiquidity, transaction costs, coin size) — the anomaly amplifies where arbitrage is costly and is largest in small/low-price coins, minimal in BTC
pros: Peer-reviewed, mechanism-based, and falsifiable: the lottery/MAX (Financial Innovation 2021; JIFMIM 2021, 2024), prospect-theory (JIFMIM 2022), and disagreement (Financial Management 2025) papers report signed, significant cross-sectional effects, grounded in Miller (JF 1977) and Scheinkman-Xiong (JPE 2003) classics

Supplies a genuine, infrastructure-conditional DECAY mechanism absent from factor-regression and LPPLS approaches: the overvaluation premium shrinks as shorting/margin/options deepen and the holder base institutionalizes — directly relevant to why BTC's realized appreciation decayed 142->65->17%/yr

Contrarian and disciplined: it predicts LOWER (not higher) forward returns for the most hyped, lottery-like, hard-to-short assets — a useful antidote to S2F/Metcalfe/power-law extrapolation that the academic literature rejects
Explains BTC's high volatility and large trading volume as equilibrium outcomes of disagreement + resale-option speculation, not anomalies to be assumed away (Scheinkman-Xiong)

Empirically self-validating on BTC: Garfinkel-Hsiao-Hu show the disagreement premium DISAPPEARS once margin trading activates, and BTC already has deep two-sided infrastructure (CME futures since 2017, IBIT options since Nov-2024, inverse ETFs), so the framework's own logic says BTC's behavioral premium is largely spent
cons: It is a CROSS-SECTIONAL anomaly, not a level/CMA model: it ranks coins and predicts relative under/over-performance over weekly horizons, not an absolute 10-15yr BTC appreciation, volatility, or correlation. Any CMA number is grafted on, not produced.

The alphas concentrate in small, illiquid, low-price, costly-to-arbitrage coins and depend on harvesting extreme returns there; Bitcoin — the most liquid, most institutionalized, least short-constrained coin — is precisely where the effect is weakest or absent, so the family barely applies to BTC specifically

Self-defeating over the CMA horizon: the mechanism predicts its own erosion. As short/margin/options/borrow infrastructure deepens (already largely true for BTC), the overvaluation premium decays toward zero, leaving no exploitable behavioral return for a long-horizon BTC holder

Short, bull-dominated samples (2014-2020/2021) and weekly horizons; out-of-sample persistence at 10-15yr horizons is untested, and frictions/transaction costs may make the cross-sectional alphas unharvestable in practice
Silent on the entire risk side of a CMA: it offers no native volatility magnitude, no correlations to equities/FI/TIPS/gold — those must be imported from realized data

Direction-asymmetric for BTC: if anything, removing short constraints and lottery demand argues BTC was historically OVERvalued and forward returns should be lower, not a basis for any positive premium

synthesized_outputs.appreciation_nominal: ~8-12%/yr (judgment, not a model output; center ~9%). The family yields no BTC level, so its CMA contribution is a DIRECTION-OF-DECAY argument: BTC historically carried a behavioral overvaluation premium (lottery demand + binding short constraints + resale-option speculation) that the framework says erodes as the holder base institutionalizes and short/margin/options/ETF infrastructure deepens. For BTC that erosion is largely COMPLETE (deep two-sided shorting now exists, and the disagreement premium 'disappears after margin trading is activated' per Garfinkel-Hsiao-Hu), so forward return should sit near a de-premiumed risk-asset rate, BELOW the trailing-5y 17% and far below the 10y 65% — consistent with extrapolating the realized 142->65->17%/yr decay one step further. If anything this family biases the estimate DOWN versus fundamentals-based approaches.
synthesized_outputs.appreciation_real: ~5-9%/yr (center ~6%), nominal less ~2.5-3% CPI. The behavioral premium is not an inflation-linked real return; once it decays, the residual is a maturing-risk-asset real return with wide error bars (could be near zero in a deleveraging/risk-off decade).
synthesized_outputs.volatility: ~55-60%/yr (judgment; center ~57%). new_approaches.rich_notes:
METHODOLOGY. Two intertwined behavioral channels, both deriving expected returns from preferences/beliefs rather than fundamentals. (A) Lottery/MAX + cumulative prospect theory (CPT). Investors over-weight small-probability large gains (Tversky-Kahneman probability weighting) and are loss-averse, so they overpay for positive-skew payoffs. Empirically: a one-SD rise in a coin's PT value reduces its next-week return ~0.71% ('Explaining cryptocurrency returns: A prospect theory perspective', JIFMIM 2022; 1,573 coins, 2014-2020); high-minus-low MAX-decile weekly spreads are ~3.03% raw / ~1.99% risk-adjusted ('Lottery-like preferences and the MAX effect', Financial Innovation 2021) and >1.50%/week ('Speculation and lottery-like demand', JIFMIM 2021). All are NEGATIVE cross-sectional predictors: lottery-attractive coins are overpriced and subsequently underperform. (B) Divergence of opinion + short-sale constraints. Miller (1977, JF): when opinions diverge and pessimists cannot short, the marginal holder is the optimist, so price overshoots the mean valuation; overvaluation rises with disagreement and with how binding the short constraint is. Scheinkman-Xiong (2003, JPE): add overconfidence-driven disagreement and a RESALE OPTION — a buyer pays above his own fundamental valuation because he expects to resell to a more optimistic future buyer; this generates a bubble component plus high volume and high volatility in equilibrium. Garfinkel, Hsiao & Hu (2025, Financial Management 54(3):633-672) bring Miller to crypto: using abnormal volume as a disagreement proxy, high-disagreement coins under binding short constraints earn LOWER future returns, with higher order imbalance and asymmetric drops in buying vs selling — and, decisively, 'the effect of high disagreement disappears after a coin's margin trading is activated.'

KEY RELATIONSHIPS / DECAY MECHANISM. The CMA-relevant object is not a price level but a premium that DECAYS along two axes: (1) holder-base institutionalization (lottery-seeking retail replaced by diversified rational marginal holders shrinks lottery demand and the PT/MAX premium); (2) short/margin/options/borrow infrastructure deepening (lets pessimists express views, collapsing the Miller overvaluation and the Scheinkman-Xiong resale bubble). This is a contrarian, infrastructure-conditional decay absent from factor-regression (#10) and LPPLS. The honest signed implication for BTC is DOWNWARD: removing constraints and lottery demand lowers forward expected return.

HISTORICAL FIT / BTC-SPECIFIC CAVEAT (load-bearing). The alphas are concentrated in small, illiquid, low-price, costly-to-arbitrage coins and 'critically depend on harvesting extreme returns on small, illiquid, volatile coins' (Babiak & Bianchi, 'Extrapolation Bias and the Lottery Effect', SSRN 2024; consistent across the MAX papers, which find the low-price/small-cap concentration and limits-to-arbitrage amplification). Bitcoin is the OPPOSITE pole: largest, most liquid, most institutionalized, and now deeply two-sided shortable — CME futures (2017), IBIT options (trading since 19-Nov-2024, position limits expanded 2025), inverse/short ETFs (BITI), and an active basis-trade short base. Garfinkel-Hsiao-Hu's own result — the disagreement premium vanishes once margin trading exists — implies BTC's behavioral overvaluation premium is largely already spent. So the family barely applies to BTC as a level model; its value is to explain WHY BTC's realized appreciation decayed (142->65->17%/yr) as constraints relaxed and the holder base matured, and to argue against any continued behavioral excess return.

FAILURE MODES. (1) Category error: a weekly cross-sectional ranking signal is not a 10-15yr level forecast; any CMA number is grafted on. (2) Sample fragility: short, bull-dominated 2014-2021 windows, weekly horizons, untested at decade scale; transaction costs may make the alphas unharvestable. (3) Misapplication to BTC: using an effect that lives in micro-caps to value the most liquid coin overstates relevance. (4) Risk-side silence: no native vol magnitude or cross-asset correlations. (5) Self-defeating: the mechanism predicts its own erosion, so it cannot underwrite a persistent BTC premium.

ON-RECORD MULTI-YEAR FORECASTS. None. This family publishes NO multi-year BTC price or return forecast. Its on-record outputs are signed cross-sectional premia (the ~0.71%/SD PT effect; ~1.5-3%/week MAX spreads) and the qualitative Scheinkman-Xiong prediction of high volatility plus large volume during disagreement-driven bubbles. The only forward-looking CMA inference is structural and contrarian: the behavioral overvaluation premium decays toward zero as shorting/margin/options infrastructure deepens and the holder base institutionalizes — for Bitcoin, largely already realized — so a credible 10-15yr BTC CMA built with this lens sits at or below a de-premiumed maturing-risk-asset return (~8-12% nominal), with ~55-60% vol, ~0.45-0.55 growth-equity correlation, and a near-zero gold correlation that this preference-based framework, unlike the digital-gold narratives, makes no attempt to inflate.
new_approaches.notes: Distinct from the existing 20 approaches: it is the only preference/belief-based (behavioral-overvaluation) family, deriving returns from lottery/prospect-theory demand and Miller/Scheinkman-Xiong disagreement-plus-short-constraints rather than fundamentals, scarcity, network, monetary, on-chain, factor, or options machinery. Its unique CMA contribution is an infrastructure-conditional, contrarian DECAY mechanism for the overvaluation premium. Honest verdict for BTC specifically: the effects concentrate in small/illiquid coins, not Bitcoin, and the premium 'disappears after margin trading is activated' (Garfinkel-Hsiao-Hu 2025), so for the most liquid, two-sided-shortable, institutionalized coin the behavioral premium is largely already gone — corroborating, not extending, the realized appreciation decay. All quantitative outputs (vol, correlations) are realized-anchored judgments; the family is silent on them.

issues: SIGN ERROR (load-bearing): The entry cites Ozdamar-Akdeniz-Sensoy (Financial Innovation 2021) '~3.03% raw / ~1.99% risk-adjusted' high-minus-low MAX-decile spread and explicitly labels it a NEGATIVE predictor ('high lottery/PT = overpriced = lower future return'). Verified against the paper's abstract: that paper finds a POSITIVE and statistically significant MAX effect -- high-MAX cryptocurrencies earn HIGHER subsequent returns, the OPPOSITE of the equity-market (Bali-Cakici-Whitelaw) negative MAX anomaly and the opposite of what the entry asserts. The +3.03%/+1.99% magnitude is correct but its DIRECTION is inverted in the entry. This is cited in cited_outputs.notes, rich_notes, and the first pro.

SUPPRESSED CROSS-PAPER DISAGREEMENT: The crypto MAX/lottery literature does NOT cleanly agree on sign. Ozdamar+ (2021, Fin Innovation) = positive (high MAX outperforms); Grobys-Junttila (2021, JIFMIM, >1.50%/wk) = negative; the 2024 'Someone like you' paper = negative; Babiak-Bianchi (2025 SSRN) = negative. The entry presents a unanimous 'lottery = overpriced = lower return = decay' front and folds the positive-premium Ozdamar paper into it, hiding that one of its own four lottery citations cuts directly against the thesis. This undermines the headline 'peer-reviewed, mechanism-based, falsifiable, signed-and-significant' pro.

OVERSTATED 'micro-cap only' FRAMING vs its own best citation: The entry repeatedly argues the family 'barely applies to BTC' because alphas 'concentrate in small, illiquid, low-price coins' (pro/con/rich_notes, load-bearing). But its strongest-cited and correctly-attributed paper -- the prospect-theory study (JIFMIM 2022, -0.71%/SD) -- states the effect is stronger among hard-to-arbitrage coins yet 'is NOT confined to the micro-cap segment of the market.' The entry leans on a clean micro-cap-only story that its own anchor paper partly contradicts.

MINOR DATE: Babiak-Bianchi 'Extrapolation Bias and the Lottery Effect' (SSRN abstract_id 5315949, correct) is dated '2024' in the entry; the SSRN posting is dated 23-June-2025. The numeric/SSRN-ID attribution is otherwise correct.

INTERNAL TENSION the entry half-acknowledges but the synthesized appreciation does not fully honor: the family's signed implication for BTC is DOWNWARD (con #6 says it argues BTC was historically OVERvalued), yet the synthesized 8-12% nominal (center ~9%) is set ABOVE the realized trailing-5y 17%... no, it is below 17% -- consistent. But the real-return band (5-9%, center 6%) implies a ~3% inflation wedge on a 9% nominal center, which is internally fine. No correction needed beyond noting the family supplies no positive premium, which the entry does state.
verdict.corrections: "1) Flip the Ozdamar-Akdeniz-Sensoy (Financial Innovation 2021) citation: it is a POSITIVE MAX effect (high MAX -> HIGHER future returns, +3.03% raw / +1.99% risk-adjusted high-minus-low), NOT a negative predictor. Do not list it alongside the negative Grobys-Junttila/2024/Babiak-Bianchi results as if all four agree. 2) Explicitly state the crypto MAX literature is sign-conflicted (Ozdamar+ positive vs the others negative); this weakens, not strengthens, the 'signed and significant' falsifiability pro and should be added as a con. 3) Soften the 'concentrates only in micro-caps, so barely applies to BTC' framing: the PT 2022 paper (the entry's own -0.71%/SD anchor) says the effect is 'not confined to the micro-cap segment.' The micro-cap concentration is well-supported for the MAX/lottery channel (Babiak-Bianchi) but overstated as a blanket claim across the whole family. 4) Correct Babiak-Bianchi year to 2025. All other citations verified exact: Miller 1977 JF, Scheinkman-Xiong 2003 JPE vol 111 no 6, Garfinkel-Hsiao-Hu 2025 Financial Management 54(3):633-672 (abnormal-volume disagreement proxy + 'effect disappears after margin trading is activated' both verbatim-confirmed), PT effect -0.71%/SD on 1,573 coins 2014-2020, IBIT options launch 19-Nov-2024. Realized anchors (142->65->17%/yr appreciation decay, ~57% trailing-5y vol, ~0 gold corr, 0.56 growth-eq / 0.37 value-eq / 0.19 FI / 0.30 TIPS) all match empirical_anchor.json exactly. The synthesized CMA numbers (8-12% nom, 55-60% vol, 0.45-0.55 growth-eq corr, ~0 gold) are defensible realized-anchored judgments and are NOT hype -- they sit at/below realized trailing-5y and the entry honestly labels them judgments, not model outputs."
overstated_pros: Pro #1 ('signed, significant cross-sectional effects' across the lottery/MAX/PT/disagreement papers): overstated because one of the four MAX/lottery citations (Ozdamar 2021) has the OPPOSITE sign, so the literature is not the unanimous, cleanly-signed body the pro implies.

Pro #5 / con #2 'barely applies to BTC because effects live in micro-caps': directionally right for the MAX channel but overstated as a family-wide claim -- the entry's own PT 2022 anchor says the effect is not confined to micro-caps. The strength of the 'BTC premium already spent' conclusion rests partly on this over-generalization plus the (verified) margin-trading-disappearance result.

Pro #2 implies a clean DECAY mechanism uniquely explains the 142->65->17% realized appreciation decay; but the family publishes no level and no time-series decay path -- the link to the realized annualized-return decay is an analogy grafted on, which the cons do acknowledge (category-error con), so the pro slightly oversells causal explanatory power.
missing_cons: No mention that the crypto MAX literature is INTERNALLY sign-conflicted (Ozdamar positive vs Grobys-Junttila/2024/Babiak-Bianchi negative) -- a real robustness problem for a 'falsifiable, signed' behavioral family and arguably the most important missing con.

Publication-bias / replication-fragility risk specific to weekly crypto cross-sectional anomalies (many of these effects are sample-period- and universe-construction-sensitive; survivorship and listing/delisting of dead coins can manufacture or destroy the spread) -- the entry notes short bull-dominated samples but not the dead-coin/survivorship and anomaly-replication concerns.

The disagreement/Miller result rests on abnormal-volume as a disagreement PROXY; volume also proxies liquidity, attention, and momentum, so the 'disagreement premium' identification is contestable -- not flagged.

Asymmetry of the margin-trading natural experiment: Garfinkel-Hsiao-Hu show the premium vanishes after margin activation, but that is identified on alt-coins; extrapolating 'therefore BTC's premium is spent' is an out-of-sample leap onto the one coin the cross-section barely covers -- the entry asserts this as near-fact rather than flagging it as an extrapolation.

new_approaches.name: Energy-Value / Thermoeconomic Fair-Value (Joule Equivalence + Landauer Temperature)
new_approaches.description: A thermoeconomic FAIR-VALUE LEVEL model (not a marginal-cost break-even floor). Edwards (Capriole, 2019) defines Bitcoin's intrinsic "Energy Value" as V = (Energy Input x Fiat Factor) / Supply Growth Rate, where Energy Input = network hashrate x ASIC energy-efficiency (J/GH) gives total joules embodied in mining, the Fiat Factor is a single fixed constant (~2.0E-15 $/Joule) representing "how much we value energy," and dividing by the annualized supply growth rate (inverse stock-to-flow) converts cumulative energy expenditure into a per-coin fair value. Unlike Hayes' cost-of-production floor, the thesis is that price OSCILLATES around (mean-reverts to) this embedded-energy line like "magnets" rather than being bounded below by it. The 2026 Entropy (MDPI) "Landauer-Based Economic Temperature" paper extends the energy-as-money frame into a canonical thermodynamic state-variable system: it defines an "economic temperature" as the monetary cost per irreversibly erased/processed bit (the economic Landauer analogue of kT ln2), builds state variables, and tests Maxwell integrability, Carnot-style efficiency bounds, nonlinear regime separation, and structural breaks. Crucially, the Landauer paper is a diagnostic / mean-reversion characterization (BTC log-temperature is a stationary AR(1), half-life ~21 days), NOT a return forecaster. A 10-15yr CMA does not fall cleanly out of either: Energy Value yields a current fair-value LEVEL, so a forward return requires forecasting the joule-embodiment line (hashrate, ASIC efficiency, halvings, fiat-factor drift) over a decade; the Landauer layer supplies only a short-horizon mean-reversion / "temperature" state-variable, not appreciation, vol, or correlations.
new_approaches.medium_explanation: Edwards (Capriole, 2019) prices Bitcoin off the energy embedded in mining: V = (hashrate x ASIC efficiency x a fixed ~2.0E-15 $/Joule "Fiat Factor") / supply-growth-rate. The claim is that price and this Energy Value line act like "magnets" and always re-converge — a mean-reverting oscillation, not a hard floor (reported ~80% R2 fit, vs ~88% for S2F). The 2026 Entropy "Landauer economic temperature" paper extends the energy-as-money frame thermodynamically, defining a $/bit-erasure "temperature" state variable; it finds BTC's log-temperature is a stationary AR(1) (coeff 0.97, ~21-day half-life) with Carnot-style efficiency bounds respected and structural breaks at halvings/EIP-1559/the Merge. For a 10-15yr CMA both are awkward: Energy Value produces a current LEVEL, so forward appreciation = growth of the joule-embodiment line (driven by halvings doubling per-coin energy embodiment, secular ASIC-efficiency gains clawing it back, and fiat-factor debasement drift). The Landauer layer adds only short-horizon mean-reversion, not return, vol, or cross-asset correlations — those must be imported from realized data.
key_drivers: Energy Input = network hashrate (GH/s) x mining energy-efficiency (J/GH), estimated across ~150 hardware models with 1.5-2yr depreciation windows — the cumulative joules embodied in the network
Fiat Factor (~2.0E-15 $/Joule): a single fixed conversion constant for the dollar value of energy; rises 1:1 with USD devaluation/hyperinflation (the debasement channel)
Supply growth rate (inverse stock-to-flow) in the denominator — halvings mechanically halve issuance, doubling per-coin energy embodiment at each ~4yr step
ASIC energy-efficiency trajectory (J/GH falling secularly) — the main DOWNWARD pressure on embodied joules, partially offsetting halvings
Mean-reversion ('magnet') dynamic: price oscillates around the Energy Value line and historically re-converges, framing energy-as-money
Landauer 'economic temperature' = monetary cost per irreversibly processed/erased bit (kT ln2 analogue); a stationary AR(1) state variable (half-life ~21 days) governing blockspace fee-market regime
Structural breaks at protocol events (halvings, Bitcoin Ordinals, EIP-1559, the Merge, Shanghai) that reorganize the temperature/energy relation
pros: Anchors a cashflow-less asset to a measurable, hard-to-fake physical input (joules of mining energy), giving a concrete refreshable dollar level rather than pure narrative — and only ONE fixed parameter (the Fiat Factor), so it is far less curve-fit than S2F/Metcalfe/power-law

Frames price as mean-reverting OSCILLATION around an embodied-energy line (the 'magnet' claim, ~80% R2 historical fit), which is a more honest two-sided dynamic than a one-sided 'floor' — and the Landauer paper supplies rigorous econophysics machinery (state variables, Maxwell integrability, Carnot bounds, stationarity tests) that most crypto valuation lacks

The Landauer layer is empirically disciplined and falsifiable: BTC log-temperature tests as a stationary AR(1) (coeff 0.97, ~21-day half-life) with Carnot efficiency bounds respected >97% of days and identifiable structural breaks at real protocol events — genuine, peer-reviewed thermodynamic structure rather than retrofitted hype

The debasement channel is built in cleanly: the Fiat Factor scales 1:1 with USD devaluation, so the model mechanically links BTC fair value to monetary inflation, making it portfolio-coherent with a real-asset / inflation-hedge sleeve
cons: CIRCULARITY (the same fatal flaw as cost-of-production): hashrate/energy input is itself driven BY price — when price falls, miners shut down, hashrate and embodied joules fall, so Energy Value FOLLOWS price down. Causality runs price->energy, not energy->price, undermining the 'intrinsic value' and mean-reversion claims; the author concedes 'if miners shut down entirely, Bitcoin would be worth zero,' which is plainly false for a monetary asset

Not a return model and silent on the CMA cells that matter: Energy Value outputs a current LEVEL (no native appreciation, volatility, or correlation), and the Landauer paper is an explicitly SHORT-HORIZON (21-day half-life) mean-reversion/state-variable diagnostic — neither produces a 10-15yr expected return, volatility, or any cross-asset (growth/value equity, FI, TIPS, gold) correlation. Every forward CMA cell is bolted-on judgment

The Fiat Factor is asserted, not estimated, and the energy-input series is fragile: it depends on heavily-estimated historical ASIC efficiency across ~150 hardware models with approximate depreciation windows (author flags 'possibility of data or omission error'). A single mis-set constant shifts the entire fair-value level

Post-2021/ETF structural break: the marginal buyer (ETF, treasury company, custodial) never touches the chain or pays for energy, decoupling price from mining energy — the same financialization break that broke cost-of-production. Energy Value has repeatedly read BTC as deeply 'undervalued' (e.g. ~40% under, ~$167k fair value) for extended stretches without convergence, contradicting the reliable-magnet claim

Terminal contradiction: as issuance -> 0 (post-2140) the supply-growth denominator -> 0 and the energy-embodiment-per-coin -> undefined/infinite, so the model cannot value the asset in the very limit it converges toward; and the Landauer 'temperature' is a fee-market/blockspace property, conceptually distinct from holders' store-of-value valuation
