synthesized_outputs.appreciation_nominal: ~7-11%/yr nominal (JUDGMENT, not a model output). Under a strict Energy-Value read, decade-forward price growth tracks growth of the per-coin embodied-energy line. Two halvings in a 10-15yr window each ~double per-coin energy embodiment (gross tailwind), but secular ASIC-efficiency gains and cheaper marginal power historically claw back the majority, leaving net embodiment growth modest; the Fiat-Factor debasement channel adds roughly a monetary-inflation drift. Anchored to BTC's realized appreciation DECAY (142%->65%->17%/yr full/10y/5y), the forward rate compresses to high-single/low-double digits - slightly below the SoV/gold-parity central because the energy line grows slower than a TAM-capture path. I sit ~9%.
synthesized_outputs.appreciation_real: ~4-8%/yr real (subtract ~2.5-3% long-run US inflation). The embodied-energy quantity is partly real, so it should roughly preserve purchasing power plus a modest monetization/efficiency premium; the Fiat-Factor's 1:1 debasement scaling supports a positive but not large real return.
synthesized_outputs.volatility: ~55-60%/yr (JUDGMENT). The model is silent on price-return vol (the Landauer AR(1) persistence is a 21-day state-variable, not annualized vol). Floor anchored AT realized trailing-5y ~57% - no compression below realized yet evidenced - with a decade-average band of ~50-60%, still multiples of equities/gold.
synthesized_outputs.corr_growth_eq: ~0.40-0.55 (JUDGMENT). Thermoeconomics is correlation-agnostic, but mining capex/power demand and the risk-on marginal buyer tie BTC to growth/tech equities; anchored to realized trailing-5y 0.56, partially mean-reverted over the horizon.
synthesized_outputs.corr_value_eq: ~0.25-0.35 (JUDGMENT). Below growth-equity; tracks realized trailing-5y ~0.37. BTC behaves as a long-duration risk asset, loosely linked to the value factor.
synthesized_outputs.corr_fi_nominal: ~0.10-0.20 (JUDGMENT). Low-positive via shared liquidity/real-rate sensitivity of the marginal institutional holder (realized trailing-5y 0.19); the energy framing gives no duration mechanism.
synthesized_outputs.corr_tips: ~0.15-0.30 (JUDGMENT). Mildly positive - the Fiat-Factor debasement / real-energy channel gives a real-rate lean shared with TIPS (realized trailing-5y 0.30), but weak and regime-dependent.
synthesized_outputs.corr_gold: ~0.0-0.15 (JUDGMENT). The energy-as-money / mined-commodity framing superficially argues for a gold linkage, but realized BTC-gold correlation is ~0 (full -0.01, 5y +0.04). Internal-contradiction note: a thesis that values BTC as embodied-energy commodity-money implies it should co-move with gold (the other monetary commodity), yet the data shows none - so the thermoeconomic frame cannot lean on a gold linkage. I hold it at the bottom of the 0.0-0.15 band, NOT a digital-gold reading.
synthesized_outputs.notes: Both source pillars output LEVELS/state-variables, not forward CMA moments; every cell here is judgment anchored to the realized DECAY baseline (142->65->17%/yr; vol floor ~57%; rising equity corr; ~0 gold corr). Central ~9% nominal / ~6% real sits within the honest cross-approach band (8-12% nom / 5-9% real). new_approaches.rich_notes:
METHODOLOGY. Two stacked pillars under one "energy-as-money" frame. (1) Edwards/Capriole Bitcoin Energy Value (2019): V = (Energy Input x Fiat Factor) / Supply Growth Rate. Energy Input = network hashrate x mining energy-efficiency (J/GH), estimated from ~150 hardware models (ASIC/FPGA/CPU/GPU) with 1-month MA and 1.5-2yr depreciation windows; the Fiat Factor is a SINGLE fixed constant ~2.0E-15 $/Joule ("how much we value energy," would rise 1:1 with USD hyperinflation); the denominator is the annualized supply growth rate (inverse stock-to-flow). Hash-rate and supply-rate units cancel, leaving fair value as a function of joules spent. Edwards reports ~80% R2 vs historical price (vs ~88% for S2F) and the defining claim that "Bitcoin's price and Energy Value tend towards each other, they are like magnets... they have always closed" - i.e. a mean-reverting OSCILLATION around embodied energy, NOT a one-sided floor. This is the key distinction from approach #4 (Hayes cost-of-production break-even floor): Edwards frames a two-sided attractor and explicitly energy-as-money. (2) The 2026 Entropy (MDPI) "Landauer-Based Economic Temperature in Blockspace Markets" (Zouari, Alon, Shtudiner, 28(5):508), building on the companion "Econophysics and the Landauer Principle" (28(4):376), defines an "economic temperature" as the monetary cost per irreversibly erased/processed bit - the economic analogue of Landauer's kT ln2 minimum erasure energy. It constructs canonical thermodynamic state variables and runs five diagnostics: state-variable behavior, Maxwell-type integrability, Carnot-style efficiency bounds, nonlinear regime separation, and structural-break sensitivity to protocol events.

KEY RELATIONSHIPS / HISTORICAL FIT. Energy Value level prints: ~$11,500 fair value Dec-2019 (~50% above spot); ~$167.8k cited 2025 with BTC ~40% "undervalued" (bitcoinist/cryptonews). Landauer findings (from published abstract/coverage): BTC log-temperature is a persistent but STATIONARY mean-reverting AR(1), coefficient 0.97, half-life ~21 DAYS; Ethereum more persistent with weaker stationarity. "Carnot-style evidence is the strongest: realized fee extraction efficiency stays well below the implied bound, with daily compliance exceeding 97% on both chains." Structural breaks at Bitcoin Ordinals, EIP-1559, the Merge, and Shanghai "confirm that protocol changes reorganize the temperature relation." Note the half-life is ~3 weeks - this is a microstructure/fee-market mean-reversion, useful for blockspace pricing, NOT a multi-year valuation anchor.

FAILURE MODES (be brutal). (a) Circularity: hashrate is endogenous to price - miners enter when price rises and capitulate when it falls, so embodied energy FOLLOWS price. Edwards' own "worth zero if miners shut down" is a tell: a monetary asset's value is not its production cost. Causality runs price->energy. (b) Silence on every CMA moment that matters: no native appreciation, vol, or correlation from Energy Value; the Landauer layer's only "dynamic" output is a 21-day mean-reversion, useless for a 10-15yr CMA. (c) The magnet claim is empirically strained post-2021: ETF/treasury/custodial buyers never pay for energy, decoupling price from mining cost, and Energy Value has read deeply-undervalued for long stretches without convergence. (d) Parameter fragility: the Fiat Factor is asserted not estimated, and the energy-efficiency series is heavily modeled (author flags omission error). (e) Terminal limit: as issuance -> 0 the supply-growth denominator collapses, so the model cannot value BTC in the asymptote it converges to. (f) Category gap: the Landauer "temperature" is a property of the fee/blockspace MARKET, not of holders' store-of-value demand - so the two pillars don't actually share an output variable; the synthesis is thematic ("energy-as-money"), not mechanical.

ON-RECORD MULTI-YEAR FORECASTS PRODUCED THIS WAY. The honest answer: there are essentially NONE in the proper sense. Energy Value publishes contemporaneous fair-value LEVELS (e.g. $11.5k in 2019, $167.8k in 2025), not dated multi-year price paths or annualized CMAs; Edwards uses it as an over/under-valuation gauge and mean-reversion timing overlay, not a decade forecaster. The Landauer/Entropy papers explicitly make NO price forecast - they are diagnostic econophysics, characterizing state-variable persistence and Carnot compliance. This is a meaningful point for a CMA committee: the approach is methodologically distinctive (single-parameter, physically grounded, peer-reviewed thermodynamic extension) but supplies almost no usable forward CMA inputs without heavy bolted-on judgment. SYNTHESIS. Anchoring to the realized appreciation DECAY (142->65->17%/yr) and the embodied-energy growth logic (halvings double per-coin energy, ASIC efficiency claws most back, Fiat-Factor debasement adds a drift), I set ~9% nominal / ~6% real, vol ~55-60% (floor at realized ~57%), growth-equity corr ~0.40-0.55, gold corr ~0.0-0.15 (rejecting the implied digital-gold/commodity-money co-movement that the data does not support). All correlation and vol cells are judgment - both pillars are silent.

issues: Cited-number attribution is essentially all correct. Verified verbatim against primary sources: Capriole Fiat Factor 2.0E-15 $/J, 80% R2 vs price, 88% R2 for S2F, 150 hardware models, 1.5yr (ASIC)/2yr (CPU/GPU/FPGA) depreciation, the 'magnets... they have always closed' quote, and 'Bitcoin would be worthless' if miners stop. Landauer/Entropy 28(5):508 (Zouari, Alon, Shtudiner, pub. 2026-05-01): AR(1)=0.97, half-life ~21 days, Carnot daily compliance >97% both chains, structural breaks at Ordinals/EIP-1559/Merge/Shanghai all confirmed. No fabricated citations.

Minor attribution slippage on the $167.8k undervaluation magnitude. The doc repeatedly says '~40% under' / '~$167k fair value' against 'a lower spot.' The actual Aug-8-2025 ForkLog/Cryptonews reporting is 45% below at $116k spot (or 31% discount to a $145k lower-bound), with fair value a RANGE of $145k-$167.8k, not a point. The doc's '~40%' understates the headline figure and presents $167.8k as the single fair value when the source gives a band. Cosmetic, not material to the thesis.

The doc DATES the $167.8k print as '2025' and uses it as evidence of 'multi-year undervaluation reads without convergence.' That framing is well-supported: the source itself notes the Aug-2025 discount was deeper than Sept-2020, i.e. a multi-year non-convergence stretch. Good adversarial use of the source against the model's own 'always closes' claim.

Synthesized 9% nominal / 6% real is DEFENSIBLE, not hype, BUT it is internally under-justified relative to the decay path the doc itself cites. 142->65->17%/yr realized decay, if extrapolated even mildly, argues for a forward central BELOW 9%. The doc hand-waves '~9%' via 'halvings double embodiment, ASIC efficiency claws most back, fiat-factor adds drift' without a quantified embodied-energy growth rate. The number lands inside the honest cross-approach band (8-12% nom) but the energy-line logic does not independently PRODUCE 9% - it is borrowed from the SoV/gold-parity central and nudged down. The doc admits this ('every cell is judgment'), which is honest, but the appreciation cell is closer to assertion than derivation.

Vol floor at realized ~57% (band 50-60%) is the single most defensible synthesized cell - explicitly anchored AT realized with no unjustified compression, correctly flags it stays multiples of equities/gold. No issue.

Correlation cells are reasonable and anchored to stated realized trailing-5y values (growth 0.56->0.40-0.55, value 0.37->0.25-0.35, FI 0.19->0.10-0.20, TIPS 0.30->0.15-0.30, gold ~0->0.0-0.15). The gold cell is the standout strength: it correctly REJECTS the digital-gold/commodity-money co-movement the thermoeconomic frame superficially implies, flags it as an internal contradiction, and holds at bottom of band. This is exactly the right adversarial posture.

All synthesized correlations assume partial mean-reversion of realized values toward lower levels over the horizon (e.g. growth 0.56->midpoint ~0.47). This is a directional ASSUMPTION presented as judgment; there is no stated mechanism for WHY BTC-equity correlation would fall as institutional/ETF ownership (the very financialization the cons cite) deepens - that channel arguably RAISES, not lowers, equity correlation. The mean-reversion direction on corr_growth_eq is contestable and arguably backwards.

missing_cons: No survivorship/lookback-bias caveat on the 'always closed' magnet claim: the R2 and the convergence history are measured on the realized BTC path that DID survive and rise. A mean-reversion-to-energy claim has never been tested through a terminal regime where price stayed below energy value indefinitely (which the 2021-2025 stretch the doc itself cites partially resembles).

The Landauer 'temperature' tests (Maxwell integrability, Carnot) are reported as PARTIAL and frequency-dependent in the abstract: BTC passes all four Maxwell relations only at MONTHLY frequency, ETH passes two of four. The doc presents the econophysics machinery as a clean 'pro' (rigorous, falsifiable, peer-reviewed structure) but omits that the paper's OWN conclusion is 'partial, frequency-dependent, chain-specific support' - i.e. the thermodynamic description is itself only weakly confirmed. This materially softens pro #2 and pro #3.

No discussion of energy-MIX / efficiency measurement error beyond the Fiat Factor: post-2021 mining shifted geographically (China ban) and toward stranded/flared gas and renewables, breaking the historical J-to-$ relationship the Fiat Factor assumes is stable. The debasement-channel 'pro' assumes the Fiat Factor is a clean monetary-inflation proxy, but it is contaminated by real energy-price and energy-source shifts.

The two pillars are presented as a stacked 'frame' but, as the doc's own rich_notes concede, they share NO output variable - yet this is buried in notes rather than stated as a top-line con that the 'synthesis' is thematic glue, not a coherent single model. Belongs in cons, not just rich_notes.
overstated_pros: Pro #1 ('only ONE fixed parameter, far less curve-fit than S2F/Metcalfe') overstates the falsifiability advantage. One constant fit in-sample to maximize R2 on a rising series is still curve-fitting; the genuine virtue is parameter parsimony, not demonstrated out-of-sample predictive skill. The 80% vs 88% comparison is in-sample and should not be read as Energy Value being more honest as a forecaster.

Pros #2 and #3 ('rigorous econophysics machinery... genuine peer-reviewed thermodynamic structure') overstate how confirmed that structure is. The paper's own abstract concludes support is PARTIAL, frequency-dependent (BTC Maxwell only at monthly freq, ETH 2/4), and chain-specific. The pros cherry-pick the strongest finding (Carnot >97%) and the AR(1) stationarity while omitting the weak Maxwell results and the authors' explicitly hedged conclusion.

Pro #4 ('debasement channel built in cleanly, scales 1:1 with USD devaluation') overstates cleanliness. The 1:1 scaling is ASSERTED in the model's theory, never estimated, and the Fiat Factor is empirically entangled with real energy-price and energy-source shifts - so it is not a clean inflation proxy. The doc's own cons acknowledge the Fiat Factor is asserted-not-estimated, which contradicts calling the debasement channel 'clean.'

new_approaches.name: Mining-Economics Dynamics & Security-Budget Sustainability (Hashprice, Hash/Difficulty Ribbons, Puell, Cost-Curve, Supply-Elasticity)
new_approaches.description: A dynamic miner-revenue lens on Bitcoin valuation, distinct from the static cost-LEVEL floor (#4) and holder cost-basis (#9). It bundles five practitioner instruments plus an academic critique. (1) HASHPRICE (Luxor, 2019): expected daily USD revenue per unit of hashrate (USD/PH/s/day), a function of block subsidy + transaction fees + network difficulty + BTC price — the unit price of the commodity miners produce. (2) The PUELL MULTIPLE (David Puell, 2019): daily USD issuance value / its 365-day MA, an oscillator of miner income stress (<0.5 = capitulation bottoms, >3-4 = euphoric tops). (3) The DIFFICULTY RIBBON (Willy Woo) / HASH RIBBONS (Charles Edwards / Capriole, 2019): crossovers of 30- vs 60-day hashrate SMAs flag miner capitulation (inefficient miners shut off, forced-sell, difficulty falls) and recovery. (4) The heterogeneous miner COST CURVE: a cash-cost stack (electricity $/kWh × rig efficiency J/TH) that, under the natural-oligopoly structure (Arnosti-Weinberg), bounds drawdown depth as low-cost survivors set the marginal price of security. (5) The ELECTRICITY-PRICE / HASHRATE ELASTICITY (~0.7 short-run, asymmetric — hashrate ramps fast on price up, sticks on price down). It also carries the long-run SECURITY-BUDGET transition: as the subsidy halves toward zero, fees must replace it, or the security spend (and the cost anchor) erodes. The CMA does not fall cleanly out of any of these — they are timing/stress/floor signals, not return forecasters — but the framework's hard analytical payload is the COST-ENDOGENEITY critique (Song-Aste): because difficulty self-adjusts, security spend stays ~constant (~1%) share of value transferred, so cost TRACKS price rather than driving it. That caps every cost-based bull case and forces a decay-extrapolated, not level-extrapolated, forward return.
new_approaches.medium_explanation: This family reads Bitcoin through miner economics in MOTION rather than a static cost level. Hashprice (USD/PH/s/day) is the unit revenue miners earn — driven by subsidy, fees, difficulty, and price. When hashprice falls below high-cost miners' cash cost, the hash/difficulty ribbon and Puell Multiple flag capitulation: weak rigs switch off, difficulty drops, forced selling clears, and the market tends to bottom. The heterogeneous cost curve (low-cost survivors at the bottom) plus a ~0.7 hashrate-price elasticity (asymmetric — fast up, sticky down) loosely bound drawdowns. But the load-bearing insight is COST-ENDOGENEITY: because difficulty re-targets, security spend stays a near-constant ~1% share of transacted value, so cost FOLLOWS price — it cannot anchor it. For a 10-15yr CMA this is deflationary: there is no exogenous rising cost floor lifting price, and the declining subsidy makes the security budget depend on a fee market that does not yet exist at scale. The honest implication is a decay-extrapolated forward return, with miner stress signals useful only for cycle timing, not for the long-horizon level.
key_drivers: Hashprice (USD/PH/s/day) = f(block subsidy, transaction fees, network difficulty, BTC price) — the unit revenue of mined hashrate; ~$34/PH/day at 5yr lows in Feb 2026
Block-subsidy halving schedule (3.125 BTC in 2025 → 1.5625 ~2028 → ~0 by 2140) — mechanically halves the issuance-revenue leg of hashprice and the security budget every ~4yr
Network difficulty / hashrate — self-adjusts every 2016 blocks to hold ~10-min blocks; rises with miner entry (raising cost), falls on capitulation (the difficulty/hash-ribbon signal)
Heterogeneous miner cost curve: electricity $/kWh × rig efficiency (J/TH); low-cost oligopoly survivors (Arnosti-Weinberg) set the marginal cost of security and bound drawdown depth
Electricity-price / hashrate elasticity ~0.69-0.71 short-run, 0.33-0.40 long-run (NBER w31745); asymmetric — hashrate ramps fast on price rises, sticks on price falls
Puell Multiple = daily USD issuance / 365d MA — miner-income oscillator (<0.5 capitulation, >3-4 euphoria)
Fee-to-subsidy security-budget transition: fees ~1-5% of reward today; must grow to sustain security spend as subsidy → 0
Cost-endogeneity (Song-Aste): difficulty adjustment holds security spend ~constant (~1%) share of value transferred, so cost tracks price
pros: Grounds Bitcoin in a real, observable, refreshable industrial dataset (hashprice, difficulty, J/TH efficiency, $/kWh) rather than pure price extrapolation or narrative — communicable to commodity/utility investors

The capitulation signals have genuine ex-post cyclical content: hash-ribbon crossovers and Puell <0.5 have bracketed several major bottoms (miner forced-selling exhaustion is a real, mechanical clearing event), giving a defensible cycle-timing overlay

Honest about its own limits via the cost-endogeneity critique (Song-Aste): the framework itself supplies the strongest argument AGAINST naive cost-floor bull cases — security spend is a ~constant ~1% share of value transferred, so cost can't lead price. This intellectual discipline is rare in BTC valuation

The natural-oligopoly cost-curve (Arnosti-Weinberg) gives a structural reason drawdowns have a soft floor: when price falls, only low-cost survivors remain, difficulty drops, and the marginal cost of security compresses toward the price — a real mean-reverting attractor, not a hard floor but a directional force
The ~0.7 short-run elasticity is a peer-reviewed, causally-identified estimate (NBER natural experiment), not a curve-fit — rare empirical rigor for a BTC input
cons: Cost-endogeneity is fatal to any cost-as-floor CMA: difficulty re-targets so cost FOLLOWS price (causality price→cost). Song-Aste show the cost/value ratio has been ~constant (~1%) since 2010 despite a ten-billion-fold hashing increase — there is no exogenous rising cost floor to lift price over a decade

None of the instruments is a return forecaster. Hashprice, Puell, and the ribbons are unit-revenue / stress / timing signals; deriving a 10-15yr appreciation requires bolting on price and fee-growth assumptions the framework does not supply

The security-budget transition is an unresolved existential risk, not a tailwind: as subsidy → 0, fees (currently ~1-5% of reward) must replace it. If they don't, the security budget — and thus the cost anchor and possibly the network's integrity — erodes. The framework cannot tell you whether the fee market materializes

Capitulation signals have degraded post-financialization: ETF/treasury marginal buyers never touch the chain, miners are diversifying to AI/HPC (decoupling hashrate from BTC economics), and 2026 saw the first multi-year hashrate drop as miners pivoted to AI — breaking the price↔hashrate link the ribbons depend on
Silent on volatility-as-a-stat and on all cross-asset correlations (growth/value eq, FI, TIPS, gold) — every distributional CMA cell must be imported from realized data
Tiny cyclical sample (3-4 halvings) and reflexivity: market cap drives mining revenue which drives the very signals used to value the market — circular

new_approaches.rich_notes:
METHODOLOGY. This family is a bundle of practitioner instruments stitched to one academic critique. Hashprice (Luxor, coined 2019) is the keystone: the expected daily USD revenue per unit of hashrate, quoted USD/PH/s/day, a deterministic function of four inputs — block subsidy, transaction fees, network difficulty, and BTC price (Luxor uses a 144-block lagging MA for fees and a 3-exchange spot average for USD). It is the unit price of the commodity miners sell. As of Feb 2026 hashprice sits at 5-year lows (~$34/PH/day) against large-miner all-in cost ~$44/PH/day — i.e., the marginal public miner is underwater, the textbook capitulation setup. The Puell Multiple (David Puell, Mar 2019) normalizes daily USD issuance by its 365-day MA into an oscillator: <0.5 = miner-revenue stress / historical bottoms, >3-4 = euphoria / tops. The Difficulty Ribbon (Willy Woo) and its derivative Hash Ribbons (Charles Edwards / Capriole, 2019) read 30- vs 60-day hashrate SMA crossovers: a downward cross marks capitulation (inefficient rigs power off, forced-sell coins, difficulty later drops ~2 weeks behind), an upward recross is the buy. These are timing/stress signals, NOT return forecasters.

KEY RELATIONSHIPS. The heterogeneous miner cost curve is the structural backbone. Arnosti & Weinberg (arXiv:1811.08572; Management Science 2022) prove Bitcoin mining is a NATURAL OLIGOPOLY: with economies of scale (return exponent α>1) every survivor holds market share ≥ 1−1/α, so the market sustains at most α/(α−1) miners, and a miner with 20%-lower costs must hold ≥20% of hashpower. This means low-cost survivors set the marginal cost of security, giving drawdowns a soft (not hard) floor. The hashrate-price ELASTICITY quantifies the dynamics: Papp, Almond & Zhang (NBER w31745 / Columbia CEEP WP27, 2023), exploiting a coal plant with on-site mining as a natural experiment, estimate short-run elasticity ~0.69-0.71 and long-run 0.33-0.40 — and the response is asymmetric (hashrate ramps quickly on price strength via rig deployment, sticks on weakness as paid-for rigs run until cash-cost-negative). They also find a $1 BTC price rise causes $3.11-6.79 of carbon damages, exceeding mining's value added — the "digital crude, not digital gold" finding that undercuts the monetary framing.

THE LOAD-BEARING CRITIQUE — COST-ENDOGENEITY. Song & Aste (arXiv:2004.04605; Frontiers in Blockchain 2020) show that despite a ~10-billion-fold rise in hashing and ~10-million-fold rise in energy use, the cost of PoW RELATIVE TO VALUE TRANSFERRED has neither risen nor fallen since 2010, staying ~1%. Their security argument: PoW must cost a sizable, roughly constant fraction of the value transferable to deter double-spends, so the difficulty adjustment endogenously holds security spend ~proportional to value. The fatal CMA implication: cost is a CONSEQUENCE of price, not a cause. There is no exogenous, rising cost floor to lift price over a decade — every cost-based bull case ("production cost is $77k so price can't fall below") inverts the causality. When price falls, miners exit, difficulty drops, and cost falls to follow.

SECURITY-BUDGET TAIL. The subsidy halves toward zero (3.125 BTC in 2025 → ~0 by 2140); fees are ~1-5% of the block reward today. For the security budget — and thus the cost anchor — to persist, a fee market must scale. The framework cannot tell you if it will; this is an unpriced left-tail, sharpened by the 2026 miner pivot to AI/HPC (first multi-year hashrate drop), which partially decouples hashrate from BTC economics and degrades the ribbon/Puell signals.

ON-RECORD MULTI-YEAR FORECASTS. This family produces almost NO clean multi-year price forecasts — by construction. Practitioners use it for cycle timing (Capriole's hash-ribbon bottom calls; Puell <0.5 bottom flags) and for current cost levels (JPMorgan's rolling production-cost series: ~$90k early-2026 → ~$77k). The one durable quantitative on-record claim is Song-Aste's: security cost ≈ 1% of value transferred, constant since 2010 — which forecasts that cost will keep tracking price, not anchoring it. HISTORICAL FIT: capitulation signals fit pre-2021 cycles well; post-financialization (ETF/treasury buyers, AI diversification) they have weakened. FAILURE MODES: causality inversion (treating an endogenous cost as a floor), reflexivity (market cap drives the mining revenue that drives the signals), tiny 3-4-halving sample, and the unresolved fee-market transition. Net: the most analytically honest of the cost-family approaches and the one that most forcefully argues for a DECAY-extrapolated, low-single-to-high-single-digit forward CMA — because its own central result says cost cannot do the bulls' work.

overstated_pros: 'The ~0.7 short-run elasticity is a peer-reviewed, causally-identified estimate... rare empirical rigor' -- true, but the estimate comes from a SINGLE 86MW coal-plant natural experiment (one site, one operator). The doc presents it as a robust network-wide parameter; external validity to the whole heterogeneous mining industry is genuinely limited and should be hedged, not sold as settled rigor.

'Honest about its own limits via cost-endogeneity... This intellectual discipline is rare' -- the framing is fair, but it doubles as a rhetorical shield: the doc uses the self-critique to license a low number while still importing every distributional cell (vol, all correlations) from realized data the framework is admittedly silent on. The 'honesty' pro slightly oversells a framework that supplies almost none of the CMA it is being credited for.

'capitulation signals have genuine ex-post cyclical content... bracketed several major bottoms' -- the cons correctly note post-financialization degradation, but the pro still implies more forward usefulness than warranted; hash-ribbon/Puell are heavily ex-post-fit on a tiny 3-4 halving sample and have already weakened, so 'defensible cycle-timing overlay' is optimistic going forward.
missing_cons: No HASHPRICE-as-revenue-not-margin caveat: hashprice is gross USD/PH/day revenue; the 'miner underwater' capitulation read also depends on each cohort's actual $/kWh and J/TH, which vary 3-4x across the fleet. The single 'all-in ~$44/PH/day' threshold masks a wide distribution and can mis-time the capitulation call.

AI/HPC decoupling is listed as degrading the signals, but the deeper con is omitted: if miners structurally migrate to AI hosting, the SECURITY BUDGET could be partly subsidized by AI cashflows (or conversely abandon BTC), which breaks BOTH the cost-anchor AND the security-degradation tail in unpredictable directions -- the framework can no longer even sign the effect.

Survivorship bias in the cost curve: the 'low-cost oligopoly survivors set the floor' (Arnosti-Weinberg) is an equilibrium result under stable conditions; it says nothing about transition dynamics during a forced-deleveraging cascade (e.g., a large miner bankruptcy dumping rigs/coins), which is precisely the left-tail a CMA should price.

Geographic/regulatory concentration risk is absent: a large share of hashrate sits in a few jurisdictions (US/Texas, post-China). A policy shock (energy curtailment, mining ban, carbon tax responding to the $3.11-6.79 damage finding) is a real discontinuity the cost-curve and elasticity framing cannot capture.

Fee-market transition is flagged as a tail but the doc never quantifies the timeline pressure: the next two halvings inside the 10-15yr window cut subsidy to ~0.78 BTC/block; the implied required fee growth to merely HOLD today's nominal security spend is large and should be stated as a number, not left qualitative.

No mention that hashprice/Puell/ribbon are all denominated in or driven by the SAME BTC price they are used to value -- beyond reflexivity, this means in a regime shift (e.g., sustained sub-cost period with no capitulation bounce, as financialized holders absorb supply) every signal in the bundle fails simultaneously, not independently.

new_approaches.name: Variance/Jump Risk-Premium & SDF-Implied Physical Return (P-vs-Q, VRP, SVCJ)
new_approaches.description: This approach extracts a real-world (physical, P-measure) expected return for Bitcoin from the option-implied (risk-neutral, Q-measure) surface, rather than stopping at the risk-neutral forward/RND. Three machinery pieces combine: (1) the variance risk premium (VRP = risk-neutral expected variance minus physical realized variance), which is large and persistently positive for BTC (Almeida et al. estimate BVRP ~0.14 annualized at the one-month horizon vs ~0.02 for the S&P 500); (2) SDF-implied lower bounds on the physical equity-style premium a la Martin (2017) SVIX and Chabi-Yo & Loudis, which convert the risk-neutral variance of the option surface into a model-free floor on the expected excess return; and (3) an SVCJ (stochastic volatility with correlated jumps) decomposition (Hou, Wang, Chen & Haerdle 2020) that separates priced jump risk from unpriced diffusion and documents anti-correlated price/vol co-jumps. Almeida, Grith, Miftachov & Wang (2024) operationalize all three for BTC, reporting an annualized BTC return premium near 66% with Martin/Chabi-Yo lower bounds of ~65.6%/84.8% at one month. Crucially these are SHORT-horizon (27-day) conditional premia harvested from current option prices, NOT 10-15yr CMA forecasts; converting them to a long-horizon CMA requires assuming the premium structure persists and decays, which the literature does not itself do.
new_approaches.medium_explanation: The option market prices BTC under the risk-neutral measure Q; a CMA needs the physical measure P. This family bridges the two. The variance risk premium (Q-variance minus P-variance) is the carry an option seller earns; for BTC it is far larger than equities (Almeida et al.: BVRP ~0.14 vs SPX ~0.02; Alexander & Imeraj first measured the BTC variance-swap VRP off Deribit, building the BVIN index). Martin's (2017) SVIX inequality and the Chabi-Yo-Loudis bound then turn the risk-neutral variance of the whole option surface into a model-free LOWER BOUND on the physical expected excess return, giving an SDF-implied return without a structural model. An SVCJ model (Hou et al. 2020) adds structure: it isolates a priced jump-risk premium from unpriced diffusion and shows BTC price jumps are anti-correlated with volatility jumps. For a 10-15yr BTC CMA the key inputs are the current option surface, the persistence/decay of the VRP, and the jump-premium term. The honest caveat: every published number is a 27-day conditional premium (~66%/yr annualized), not a decade forecast — extrapolating it requires aggressive decay assumptions the authors never make.
key_drivers: Variance risk premium (VRP) = risk-neutral expected variance (option-implied) minus physical realized variance; BTC BVRP ~0.14 annualized one-month vs SPX ~0.02 — the persistent option-selling carry
Risk-neutral variance of the full option surface (Martin SVIX-style equal-strike weighting) that feeds the model-free lower bound on the physical premium

Martin (2017) negative-correlation-condition lower bound and Chabi-Yo & Loudis higher-order bound translating Q-variance into a floor on the physical equity-style premium (BTC ~65.6% / ~84.8% at one month)
SVCJ jump parameters: jump intensity, jump size/volatility, and the priced jump-risk premium vs unpriced diffusion (Hou et al.); anti-correlation of price jumps and volatility jumps
Volatility regime / clustering of the risk-neutral density (Almeida et al. find two vol regimes: high-vol BP lower bound ~78%, low-vol ~44%) — the premium is state-dependent
Persistence and decay path of the VRP and jump premium over the holding horizon — the (untested by the authors) bridge from a 27-day premium to a multi-year CMA
Skew/asymmetry of the risk-neutral density: BTC premium is far more upside-driven than SPX (positive returns contribute ~39-52% of BTC premium vs ~25% for SPX)
pros: Directly answers the question other option-based approaches dodge: it produces a PHYSICAL (P-measure) expected return, not just a risk-neutral forward or RND — the only forward-looking, market-implied estimate of BTC's expected return on this list

Model-free lower bounds (Martin SVIX, Chabi-Yo-Loudis) require minimal assumptions — no return-distribution shape, no growth model — and Martin shows the SPX bound is empirically near-tight (time-series average ~5%, matching realized), lending credibility to the method when applied to BTC

Cleanly separates compensated from uncompensated risk: the VRP isolates the variance-selling carry and the SVCJ decomposition isolates the priced jump premium from unpriced diffusion — a genuinely richer risk picture than vol-only models
Grounded in actual traded option prices (Deribit), refreshable in real time (BVIN/BVRP stream every 15 seconds), so the input is observable and auditable rather than a fitted historical regression
State-aware: the clustering/regime finding gives a conditional premium (high-vol vs low-vol), which is more honest than a single static number and maps onto a CMA scenario framework
cons: Horizon mismatch is fatal for a CMA: every published estimate is a 27-day (one-month) conditional premium annualized to ~66%/yr. These are short-horizon risk-compensation snapshots, NOT 10-15yr expected returns — the authors never forecast a decade, and naively annualizing the option-implied premium massively overstates a long-horizon CMA

The Martin/Chabi-Yo bounds are LOWER bounds that rely on the negative-correlation condition (NCC) between the SDF and the market return; this condition is well-motivated for the broad equity market but is far less obviously valid for a single speculative asset like BTC, so the 'lower bound' interpretation may not hold

Thin, young, fragmented option market: BTC options (mostly Deribit) have a short history (~2017+), wide spreads, limited deep-OTM strikes, and venue concentration — the risk-neutral variance and tail integrals that the bounds need are noisily estimated, and Almeida et al. concede the first-moment premium is 'a noisy measure'

VRP harvestability is asserted by the carry magnitude but not established as a stable, investable long-run premium; the VRP spikes around large moves (Alexander-Imeraj) and became correlated with equity/gold VRP in the pandemic, so the diversifying carry is regime-dependent and can vanish exactly when needed

Says almost nothing directly usable for the correlation cells of a CMA: the paper notes BTC 'largely fluctuated independently of traditional macro-financial markets' and mentions gold only once in passing — no structural BTC-vs-growth/value/FI/TIPS/gold correlation is produced
SVCJ jump-premium estimates are model-dependent (the opposite of the model-free bounds) and sensitive to identification of jumps vs diffusion in a 24/7, microstructure-noisy market

(For scale: SPX one-month lower bound ~5%, so BTC ~13x.)

Regime: risk-neutral variance 0.86 (high-vol) vs 0.46 (low-vol). Alexander-Imeraj construct a full BTC implied-vol term structure (BVIN) off Deribit but publish no single annualized CMA vol.

cited_outputs.notes: Central headline: BTC VRP ~0.14 vs SPX ~0.02 (7x); BTC one-month premium ~66%/yr with lower bounds ~65.6%/84.8% (13x SPX's ~5%); BTC Sharpe ~0.8 vs SPX ~0.5; BTC premium is upside-skewed (positive returns 39-52% of premium vs ~25% for SPX). Hou et al. (2020): SVCJ confirms priced jumps with price-jumps anti-correlated to vol-jumps. Martin (2017): SPX SVIX lower bound averages ~5% and is near-tight. ALL horizons are ~1 month — no source publishes a decade-horizon premium or any of the five CMA correlations.

synthesized_outputs.appreciation_nominal: ~9-13%/yr nominal (JUDGMENT, not a model output). The literature's ~66%/yr (or ~65.6% lower bound) is a 27-day option-implied premium — a snapshot of currently demanded compensation, mechanically inflated by BTC's ~82% implied vol, not a decade forecast. Two disciplines collapse it: (a) the VRP/SDF premium scales with variance, and as BTC's vol mean-reverts toward a ~50-60% floor the implied premium compresses proportionally; (b) the realized appreciation-decay path (142%->65%->17%/yr) shows the harvestable premium shrinks as the market matures and option markets deepen (competition compresses the VRP carry). Anchoring to the cross-approach central (~8-12% nom) and giving a modest upward tilt for BTC's genuinely large, persistent VRP carry lands ~9-13%.
synthesized_outputs.appreciation_real: ~6-10%/yr real (subtracting ~2.5-3% long-run inflation). Judgment; the option premium is nominal, so the real figure is residual.
synthesized_outputs.volatility: ~55-60%/yr (judgment). This family is the one that most directly measures vol: BTC implied vol ~82% and realized ~76% (sqrt of 0.58) at the one-month horizon today. Over 10-15yr I hold the floor AT realized trailing-5y ~57% — the VRP/SVCJ framework gives no mechanism forcing compression below the realized floor, and the persistent positive VRP implies the market keeps pricing high forward variance.
synthesized_outputs.corr_growth_eq: ~0.40-0.55 (judgment). The sources find BTC fluctuated 'independently' over their pre-2022 sample, but the VRP became equity-correlated in stress, and realized post-ETF return correlation is 0.5-0.9. I assume partial mean-reversion to a moderately-strong risk-asset link; the VRP carry is itself a short-vol/risk-on exposure.
synthesized_outputs.corr_value_eq: ~0.25-0.35 (judgment; below growth, tracking realized trailing-5y ~0.37). BTC's option-implied risk profile is high-beta/long-duration, less tied to value-factor cashflows.
synthesized_outputs.corr_fi_nominal: ~0.10-0.20 (judgment; realized trailing-5y ~0.19). The VRP carry has mild liquidity/rate sensitivity but no duration anchor.
synthesized_outputs.corr_tips: ~0.20-0.30 (judgment; realized trailing-5y ~0.30). Modest real-rate/liquidity sensitivity shared with other long-duration risk assets.
synthesized_outputs.corr_gold: ~0.0-0.15 (judgment). The only cited gold link is a SECOND-moment, pandemic-specific VRP comovement — not a return correlation. Realized BTC-gold return correlation is ~0 (-0.01 full, +0.04 5y). The framework supplies no mechanism forcing return co-movement, so I hold the bottom of the band; the VRP-correlation finding is about shared volatility-risk demand in crises, not a digital-gold return link.
synthesized_outputs.notes: The defining honesty constraint here: do NOT import the ~66%/yr one-month option-implied premium as a CMA appreciation number — that is the single biggest abuse risk of this approach. It is a short-horizon, vol-scaled risk compensation that must be decayed with both the vol floor and the realized appreciation-decay path. The genuinely distinct contribution is forward-looking, market-implied, and isolates priced jump/variance risk; its value to a CMA is as a sanity check on the SIGN and ORDERING (BTC premium >> equity premium; vol >> equity vol) and as a refreshable vol/VRP input, not as a literal return level.

new_approaches.rich_notes:
METHODOLOGY. This family answers the one question option-pricing approaches (#11 single-Q-forward/RND, #19 return-process shape) explicitly decline: what is BTC's PHYSICAL (real-world, P-measure) expected return implied by the option surface? It chains four ideas. (1) The variance risk premium (VRP = E^Q[variance] - E^P[variance]) is the carry an option/variance-swap seller earns; Alexander & Imeraj (2021) first measured it for BTC, building a CBOE-VIX-style implied-vol term structure off 15-minute Deribit quotes (now the live BVIN index) and finding the BTC VRP large and spiking before big moves. (2) Martin's (2017) SVIX lower bound and the Chabi-Yo-Loudis higher-order bound convert the risk-neutral variance of the WHOLE option surface into a model-free floor on the physical expected excess return — no distributional assumption needed. Martin showed the SPX bound averages ~5% and is empirically near-tight, which is the credential the whole approach leans on. (3) An SVCJ model (Hou, Wang, Chen & Haerdle 2020, J. Financial Econometrics) adds structure, separating a PRICED jump-risk premium from unpriced diffusion and documenting that BTC price jumps are significantly anti-correlated with volatility jumps. (4) Almeida, Grith, Miftachov & Wang (2024) tie it together for BTC.

KEY NUMBERS (Almeida et al., 27-day horizon, annualized). BTC return premium ~66%/yr; Martin lower bound ~65.64%, Chabi-Yo-Loudis ~84.78% (vs SPX one-month bound ~5% — BTC ~13x). BTC VRP (BVRP) ~0.14 vs SPX ~0.02 (~7x). Risk-neutral variance ~0.72, realized ~0.58, average implied vol ~82%. BTC annualized Sharpe ~0.8 vs SPX ~0.5. A signature finding: BTC's premium is upside-skewed — positive returns (20-60%) contribute 39-52% of the premium vs ~25% for SPX, and negative returns (-60% to -20%) only ~20-28% — so unlike equities (where the premium is compensation for mildly-bad states), much of BTC's premium is paid for the right tail. A clustering algorithm on the risk-neutral densities finds two volatility regimes: high-vol Martin bound ~78.16% / Chabi-Yo ~102.27% with risk-neutral variance 0.86; low-vol ~43.99% / ~54.51% with variance 0.46. Interestingly BVRP is HIGHER in the low-vol regime (~0.17) than high-vol (~0.12).

HISTORICAL FIT / FAILURE MODES. The bounds are model-free and refreshable, which is the strength. But four critiques bite for CMA use. First, HORIZON: every number is a one-month (27-day) conditional premium. The authors never forecast a year, let alone a decade; the ~66% is the compensation demanded right now for one month of BTC risk, mechanically scaled by ~82% implied vol. Annualizing it into a CMA is a category error — as vol mean-reverts and option markets deepen, the implied premium compresses proportionally. Second, the Martin/Chabi-Yo bounds require the negative-correlation condition between the SDF and the asset return; well-motivated for the aggregate market, much shakier for one speculative asset, so the 'lower bound' may not bound. Third, DATA: BTC options are young (2017+), venue-concentrated (Deribit), wide-spread, and thin in deep-OTM strikes — exactly the strikes the tail integrals need; Almeida et al. themselves call the first-moment premium 'a noisy measure,' and Alexander-Imeraj warn the variance-swap formula underestimates fair value when BTC fluctuates excessively. Fourth, the diversification/correlation story is weak for a CMA: the paper says BTC 'largely fluctuated independently of traditional macro-financial markets' and mentions gold only once — noting BTC's VRP 'became highly correlated with the VRP of equity and gold during the pandemic.' That is a second-moment, crisis-specific comovement (everyone bids vol protection together), NOT a return correlation, and certainly not support for a digital-gold return link.

ON-RECORD MULTI-YEAR FORECASTS. None. This is the cleanest source of all in one respect: the academic literature using this method publishes NO multi-year BTC return forecast and NO CMA. Almeida et al. produce a 27-day conditional premium; Alexander-Imeraj produce a vol-index term structure and VRP series; Hou et al. produce option prices and jump parameters; Martin produces a one-month equity-premium proxy. Any 10-15yr number is a downstream construction, not something these authors endorse. That restraint is itself a finding: the most rigorous, forward-looking, market-implied method on this list deliberately refuses to extrapolate to a decade — a useful rebuke to the S2F/power-law/gold-parity families that confidently project multi-million-dollar targets. For the CMA, the right use is to take the SIGN and ORDERING (BTC premium >> equity premium; BTC vol >> equity vol; jumps priced; premium upside-skewed) and the refreshable VRP/vol inputs as sanity checks, then impose the realized appreciation-decay discipline to land a defensible ~9-13% nominal forward, NOT the ~66% the raw option surface prints today.

issues: VRP-tilt conflation (the load-bearing synthesis flaw): the synthesized appreciation gives 'a modest upward tilt for BTC's genuinely large, persistent VRP carry.' But the VRP is a VARIANCE-selling carry harvested by an option/variance-swap SELLER, not a spot-appreciation premium earned by a long-only BTC holder. A CMA appreciation cell is a buy-and-hold spot return; tilting it UP because the VRP is large conflates two distinct premia. If anything the large positive VRP means options are expensive to BUY and cheap to SELL, which says nothing favorable about long-only spot appreciation. This is the single clearest internal inconsistency.

Double-counting dressed as independence: the notes claim 'two disciplines collapse it: (a) vol mean-reverts -> premium compresses, and (b) realized decay 142->65->17%.' These are largely the SAME phenomenon (market maturation / deepening), not two independent checks. Presenting them as separate corroborating disciplines overstates the rigor of the landing zone.

The Martin/Chabi-Yo numbers are LOWER bounds, yet the synthesized ~9-13% sits an order of magnitude BELOW even the low-vol-regime lower bound (~44%). The dossier is right to decay, but it never reconciles WHY a model-free LOWER bound of 44-66% is compatible with a 9-13% forward. The honest answer is horizon (a 1-month conditional premium is not a 10-15yr unconditional CMA), which the dossier states, but it leaves a ~5x gap between 'lower bound' and 'synthesized' unexplained mechanically -- a reader could reasonably ask whether the bound is being honored at all.

BVRP attribution blur: 'BVIN/BVRP stream every 15 seconds' off Deribit -- the BVIN index is streamed by CryptoCompare (the dossier says this elsewhere), and the Alexander-Imeraj paper SAMPLED Deribit at 15-MINUTE intervals (Mar 2019-Mar 2020). The live 15-second cadence is the downstream index vendor, not the paper's data. Minor, but it muddies 'refreshable in real time.'

The 'positive returns contribute ~39-52% of BTC premium' is cited as 38.66% unconditional and 52.30% low-vol -- correct -- but the dossier's banner '39-52%' silently drops the high-vol regime value (34.21%), so the range is cherry-picked to the two most upside-skewed numbers. Honest range across regimes is ~34-52%.

corr_growth_eq synthesized band 0.40-0.55 sits BELOW the most recent realized anchor (trailing-5y = 0.564). The dossier frames this as 'partial mean-reversion to a moderately-strong link,' but BTC-equity correlation has been TRENDING UP (0.263 full -> 0.362 10y -> 0.564 5y), so assuming mean-reversion DOWN over a 10-15yr forward is a directional bet against the realized trend, not a neutral anchor. Defensible but should be flagged as a judgment that cuts against momentum.
verdict.corrections: CITED LAYER IS CLEAN. Every cited number was verified against primary sources and matches exactly: Almeida et al. (2024, arXiv 2410.15195) -- BVRP 0.14 vs SPX ~0.02, RN var 0.72, realized var 0.58, IV 82%, BP ~66%, Martin LB 65.64%, Chabi-Yo-Loudis LB 84.78%, regime bounds HV 78.16/102.27 & LV 43.99/54.51, regime variances 0.86/0.46, BVRP 0.12 (HV)/0.17 (LV), Sharpe 0.8 vs 0.5, SPX one-month LB 5%, positive-return share 38.66% uncond/52.30% low-vol, and the 'noisy measure' quote -- all confirmed verbatim. The four-paper attribution is correct: Alexander & Imeraj 2021 JAI 23(4):84-109 (first BTC VRP, BVIN, Deribit, CBOE-VIX variance-swap formula); Hou/Wang/Chen/Haerdle 2020 JFE 18(2):250-279 (SVCJ, price-jumps anti-correlated with vol-jumps -- verbatim match); Martin 2017 QJE 132(1):367-433 (SVIX, NCC, ~5% near-tight); Chabi-Yo & Loudis 2020 JFE (higher-moment bounds, no distributional assumptions). REALIZED ANCHORS ARE CLEAN: empirical_anchor.json confirms appreciation decay 1.422/0.6547/0.1697 (=142/65/17%), vol full/10y/5y 1.029/0.687/0.575 (=~57% 5y floor), gold corr -0.011 full/+0.045 5y (~0), and the value/fi/tips realized anchors (0.367/0.192/0.301) the dossier cites. SYNTHESIS FIXES NEEDED: (1) Remove the 'upward tilt for VRP carry' from the appreciation number -- VRP is a short-vol seller's carry, not a long-only spot premium; the tilt should be neutral-to-down, which would push the band toward ~8-11% rather than 9-13%. (2) Stop billing the vol-mean-reversion and realized-decay arguments as two independent disciplines; they are one maturation story -- say so. (3) Add one sentence reconciling the ~5x gap between the model-free lower bound (44-66%) and the 9-13% synthesis: the bound is a 1-month CONDITIONAL premium and does not bound a multi-year UNCONDITIONAL CMA, so it is not being violated. (4) Fix the BVRP streaming attribution (CryptoCompare/vendor 15-sec, paper 15-min Deribit). (5) Flag corr_growth_eq 0.40-0.55 as a bet AGAINST the rising realized trend (0.26->0.36->0.56), not a neutral anchor. Overall: the dossier's central honesty constraint -- DO NOT import 66%/yr as a CMA number -- is correct and well-executed; the residual risk is the opposite-sign error of using the VRP to nudge the long-run appreciation UP.
overstated_pros: 'The only forward-looking, market-implied estimate of BTC expected return on this list' -- true for the 1-month conditional premium, but the pro oversells transferability: the moment you need a 10-15yr CMA, the method provides NO forward-looking estimate (the authors refuse to extrapolate), so its forward-looking virtue evaporates at the exact horizon the CMA cares about. The dossier's own cons concede this, making the pro framing internally inflated.

'Martin shows the SPX bound is empirically near-tight (~5%, matching realized), lending credibility when applied to BTC' -- the near-tightness is an SPX/aggregate-market result resting on the negative-correlation condition. The dossier's own con #2 says the NCC is 'far less obviously valid for a single speculative asset like BTC.' So the credibility transfer asserted in the pro is undercut by the con; the pro should not borrow SPX tightness as evidence the BTC bound is tight.

'Grounded in actual traded option prices... refreshable in real time... observable and auditable rather than a fitted historical regression' -- partially overstated given the same dossier concedes the BTC option market is thin, venue-concentrated (Deribit), wide-spread, and sparse in the deep-OTM strikes the tail integrals require, AND that the first-moment premium is 'a noisy measure.' Auditable inputs that are noisily estimated are not as clean as the pro implies.

'State-aware / conditional premium is more honest than a single static number' -- fair, but the regime finding is two clusters over a short (post-2017, mostly pre-2022) option history; calling a 2-regime split on <8 years of thin data a robust conditional framework is generous.
missing_cons: Survivorship / sample-period bias in the source: Almeida et al.'s option sample is essentially a single bull-skewed epoch of BTC's history. The upside-skewed-premium finding (much of BP paid for the right tail) may be an artifact of estimating risk-neutral densities over a period where the right tail repeatedly paid off -- it is not obviously a structural, forward-stable property. The dossier treats 'premium is upside-skewed' as a durable SIGN/ORDERING fact to carry into the CMA; it may be regime/sample-specific.

The VRP is a SHORT-VOLATILITY exposure, which is precisely the exposure that blows up in crises (negatively skewed payoff, fat left tail). A CMA that imports 'BTC has a large harvestable VRP carry' as a POSITIVE without modeling the left-tail/short-vol crash risk of harvesting it is importing a Sharpe that overstates true risk-adjusted attractiveness. The dossier mentions VRP regime-dependence but never states the short-vol payoff asymmetry explicitly.

No transaction-cost / capacity haircut: harvesting BTC VRP requires continuously rolling Deribit options/variance swaps with wide spreads and limited depth. The realizable net VRP after costs in a thin venue is materially below the gross 0.14, and capacity is tiny relative to any institutional CMA sleeve. This caps how investable the headline carry is.

Q-to-P measure-change reliability for BTC specifically: the entire method assumes the option surface correctly prices the physical premium via a well-behaved SDF. For an asset with no cash flows, no consumption-based anchor, and a debated SDF, the P-measure return extracted may be far less identified than for equities -- a deeper objection than the NCC con already listed.

Coin/futures-vs-spot basis: Deribit options are typically coin-margined / inverse and settled against an index; the implied vol and variance extracted are on the perpetual/futures complex, which carries its own basis and funding dynamics that don't map cleanly to a spot-BTC CMA appreciation cell.

new_approaches.name: Options-Skew / Convexity Risk-Reversal Signal
new_approaches.description: This approach reads Bitcoin's expected-return and risk structure off the SHAPE of the implied-volatility smile rather than off a single ATM vol point. The two objects are (1) the 25-delta risk reversal (RR = 25d-call IV minus 25d-put IV), which prices the relative cost of upside vs downside convexity, and (2) the left/right slopes of the IV curve (skew steepness). The practitioner thesis (Deribit Insights) is that systematically SELLING the risk reversal earns strong risk-adjusted returns in BTC — the reverse of equities — because BTC spot-vol correlation is negative only ~65% of the time and call wings have persistently traded rich, so a short-RR harvests a convexity/crash-insurance-supply premium. The crucial CMA-disciplining finding (Wang et al. 2024, peer-reviewed) is NEGATIVE: both the left and right IV slopes forecast realized VOLATILITY at weekly frequency but have NO predictive power for directional RETURNS — BTC options trade on volatility information, not directional information. So skew/RR is a vol-and-tail-premium signal, not an appreciation forecaster. A 10-15yr CMA does not fall out of skew at all: the framework yields a vol/correlation/tail view and a harvestable carry strategy, but is explicitly silent on (indeed denies) a long-horizon directional appreciation number, which must be imported from another framework.
new_approaches.medium_explanation: The signal is the 25-delta risk reversal (call IV minus put IV) and the steepness of the left/right IV-smile slopes. Deribit Insights backtests (Apr-2019 to Dec-2022) show that, unlike equities where you buy crash protection, in BTC systematically SELLING the risk reversal delivers the best risk-adjusted returns — robust across deltas, surviving exclusion of the March-2020 crash, and explained by BTC's spot-vol correlation being negative only ~65% of the time plus persistently rich call wings. That is a harvestable convexity/insurance-supply premium, not a price forecast. The disciplining academic result (Wang et al. 2024, J. Int. Money & Finance) is that both IV slopes predict realized VOLATILITY weekly but NOT returns — BTC options carry volatility, not directional, information. For a 10-15yr BTC CMA this means skew informs the volatility and tail/correlation cells and offers a carry overlay, but supplies NO appreciation number; the central estimate must be borrowed. It usefully caps naive bullishness: a market that won't pay up for directional convexity is not pricing structural drift.
key_drivers: 25-delta risk reversal level and its z-score vs history (25d-call IV minus 25d-put IV)
Left and right slopes of the implied-volatility smile (skew steepness)
Spot-vol correlation (negative ~65% of the time in BTC, vs persistently strongly negative in equities) — drives why short-RR pays
Net-buying-pressure / dealer-inventory and option supply-demand imbalance (call wings trading rich/cheap)
Realized positive vs negative skewness of returns (jumps) that the slopes mean-revert against
Variance / volatility risk premium magnitude and its regime (higher in low-vol clusters per Almeida et al.)
Market maturation / institutional participation, which the practitioner source expects to erode the short-RR premium over time
pros: Grounded in live, forward-looking, market-priced data (Deribit options) rather than backward price extrapolation or on-chain proxies — it reflects what risk-takers actually pay for convexity right now
Delivers exactly the CMA cells most models miss: a genuine implied-volatility and tail-risk view, plus an empirically harvestable carry strategy (short RR) with real desk adoption

Honest and self-disciplining: the peer-reviewed finding that skew forecasts realized vol but NOT returns is a rare falsifiable, NEGATIVE result that guards against the directional over-extrapolation plaguing S2F/Metcalfe/power-law models
Captures asymmetry/jump structure the lognormal/normal models ignore — left vs right slope separately price crash vs melt-up convexity
The short-RR / variance-premium edge is documented across multiple independent sources (Deribit practitioner backtest + Almeida et al. + Bitcoin-VIX VRP literature), not a single curve-fit
cons: Produces NO appreciation forecast by construction — Wang et al. find the slopes have zero predictive power for returns, so the entire directional CMA must be imported from another framework; using skew to set expected return is a category error
Short maturities only: the entire surface lives at days-to-3-months tenors, so any 10-15yr extrapolation is heroic — there is no 10yr BTC option to read a decade view from

The harvestable edge is explicitly regime-dependent and decaying: Deribit itself warns the short-RR premium 'will likely become less profitable' as institutions mature the market and supply/demand normalizes — so even the carry result is non-stationary

Short-vol / short-RR carries severe negative-skew tail risk (sell crash insurance, blow up on the next March-2020/FTX gap) — strong Sharpe masks fat left-tail that a 10-15yr holder must survive; the backtest leans on a survivorship single path

Data depth is thin and venue-concentrated (Deribit ~ the whole liquid BTC options market; sample only ~2019+), and the variance-risk-premium estimates flip sign by regime, undermining a stable structural number
Says nothing directly about cross-asset correlations to equities/FI/TIPS/gold — those must be borrowed; the framework is asset-internal
