cited_outputs.appreciation_nominal: n/a (source silent — indeed source explicitly DENIES a directional signal). Wang et al. (2024): both left and right IV slopes 'lack the predictive capability for returns.' The short-RR strategy earns a vol/convexity carry, not an asset-appreciation forecast. No 10-15yr nominal BTC appreciation is produced by this framework.
cited_outputs.appreciation_real: n/a (source silent)
cited_outputs.volatility: No single annualized point published, but this IS the framework's native output: the IV slopes 'notably forecast realized volatility on the weekly frequency.' BTC DVOL/implied vol historically ~60-90%+ annualized; variance-risk-premium is positive and regime-dependent (Almeida et al.: higher in low-vol clusters; Bitcoin-VIX VRP literature, Alexander-Imeraj). The signal predicts vol LEVEL/regime, not a fixed number.
cited_outputs.corr_growth_eq: n/a (source silent — framework is asset-internal to the BTC options surface)
cited_outputs.corr_gold: n/a (source silent — no cross-asset correlation to gold is published; the framework reads only BTC's own smile)
cited_outputs.notes: Key cited datum is a NEGATIVE/disciplining one: skew predicts realized vol, not returns (Wang et al. 2024). Practitioner cited datum: systematically SELLING the 25d risk reversal gave the best risk-adjusted returns 2019-2022 (Deribit), with spot-vol corr negative ~65% of the time and an expected decay of the edge as the market institutionalizes.

synthesized_outputs.appreciation_nominal: ~8-12%/yr (JUDGMENT, fully IMPORTED — not a skew output). The framework supplies NO directional number and the peer-reviewed evidence says it cannot; so I anchor to the cross-approach central and the realized-decay baseline (142%->65%->17%/yr), landing low-double-digit. If anything the skew literature pushes me DOWN: a market that does not pay up for directional convexity (RR sells rich, calls cheap) is not pricing structural upward drift, so I sit at the lower-middle of the 8-12% band (~9-10%).
synthesized_outputs.appreciation_real: ~5-9%/yr real (subtract ~2.5-3% long-run inflation). Imported, same caveat.
synthesized_outputs.volatility: ~55-65%/yr (JUDGMENT, but this is the cell the framework most informs). Implied vol (DVOL) has historically run ~60-90% and the slopes forecast realized vol; the variance risk premium means implied sits ABOVE realized, so a forward realized-vol CMA of ~55-60% (floor at realized trailing-5y ~57%) with implied ~5-15 vol points richer. I do NOT credit compression below ~55% over the horizon — the sub-2yr ETF/institutional sample shows no durable floor beneath realized, and the persistent VRP says the market keeps pricing high vol.
synthesized_outputs.corr_growth_eq: ~0.40-0.55 (JUDGMENT, imported). Skew is asset-internal; anchored to realized trailing-5y 0.56. The spot-vol/negative-correlation regime that powers short-RR is a risk-asset signature, consistent with moderate-to-strong growth-equity co-movement.
synthesized_outputs.corr_value_eq: ~0.25-0.35 (JUDGMENT, imported; realized 5y 0.37).
synthesized_outputs.corr_fi_nominal: ~0.10-0.20 (JUDGMENT, imported; realized 5y 0.19).
synthesized_outputs.corr_tips: ~0.20-0.30 (JUDGMENT, imported; realized 5y 0.30).
synthesized_outputs.corr_gold: ~0.0-0.15 (JUDGMENT, imported). The options-skew framework makes no gold claim and supplies no mechanism; realized BTC-gold corr is ~0 (full -0.01, 5y +0.045). I hold the bottom of the band — the negative-spot-vol/risk-asset behavior the skew premium relies on is the OPPOSITE of gold's safe-haven smile, so if anything skew evidence argues BTC is NOT trading like digital gold.
synthesized_outputs.notes: The defensible synthesized contribution of this approach is to the VOLATILITY and TAIL cells (and a carry-strategy overlay), NOT to appreciation. Its most valuable role in a CMA panel is as a SKEPTIC: it provides a falsifiable, peer-reviewed reason to refuse a structural directional premium derived from option prices, capping the bullish models.

new_approaches.rich_notes:
WHAT THE APPROACH IS. The Options-Skew / Convexity Risk-Reversal signal isolates the SHAPE of BTC's implied-volatility smile — not its level (which is approach #11, the DVOL/RND vol-surface model). Two objects: (1) the 25-delta risk reversal, RR = IV(25d call) - IV(25d put), the market price of upside vs downside convexity; (2) the left and right slopes of the smile (skew steepness). Both are read off Deribit, which is effectively the entire liquid BTC options venue. The practitioner claim and the academic claim point in different but complementary directions, which is why this is a distinct entry.

THE PRACTITIONER EDGE (Deribit Insights, 'Finding edge in four years of volatility regimes,' ~2023). Backtesting Apr-2019 to Dec-2022, Deribit finds that systematically SELLING the 25d risk reversal produces the best risk-adjusted returns — the OPPOSITE of equity markets, where investors persistently overpay for downside puts. The result is robust across delta targets and survives excluding the March-2020 'Black Thursday' crash. Mechanism: BTC's rolling 60-day spot-vol correlation is negative only ~65% of the time (vs near-always-negative in equities), and call wings have traded persistently rich (a positive-skew/melt-up insurance demand). A short-RR harvests that. An overlay combining short-RR with spot BTC found ~75-80% allocation to the strategy was Sharpe-optimal. Crucially, Deribit itself flags decay: as institutions mature the market 'these strategies will likely become less profitable.'

THE DISCIPLINING ACADEMIC RESULT (Wang et al., 2024, J. Int. Money & Finance / ORL, 'Implied volatility slopes and jumps in bitcoin options market'). Using Deribit tick data, they derive a theoretical link between left/right IV slopes and negative/positive price jumps, and find empirically that jumps have REVERSAL impacts on the slopes even controlling for net-buying-pressure and realized skewness. The CMA-critical conclusion: 'Both left and right slopes of the implied volatility curve lack the predictive capability for returns, whereas they notably forecast realized volatility on the weekly frequency, which is in line with the evidence of more volatility-informed and less directional-informed trading in the bitcoin market.' This is the sharp NEGATIVE finding the seed brief highlights — skew is a VOLATILITY signal, not a RETURN signal. It is exactly the kind of falsifiable, demand-side discipline a single DVOL/RND point (approach #11) does not contain.

SUPPORTING RISK-PREMIA LITERATURE. Almeida, Grith, Miftachov & Wang (2024, arXiv 2410.15195, 'Risk Premia in the Bitcoin Market') decompose the BTC premium and find it is substantially driven by a large, regime-dependent VARIANCE risk premium (higher in low-vol clusters), with negative returns between 1-3 sd contributing only ~one-third of the total premium — unlike the S&P where mild-down returns dominate. This supports reading BTC's option premium as a volatility/variance phenomenon, not a directional-skew phenomenon. Alexander & Imeraj (2021, 'The Bitcoin VIX and Its Variance Risk Premium,' J. Alt. Investments) build a CBOE-VIX-style BTC implied-vol index from 7M+ Deribit prices and document a positive variance risk premium (implied > realized), the structural source of the short-vol/short-RR carry.

ON-RECORD MULTI-YEAR FORECASTS. Notably, NONE. This framework produces NO published multi-year directional BTC price/appreciation forecast — and that absence is a feature, not a gap. Because the peer-reviewed evidence says skew cannot forecast returns, no credible author uses it to set a 10-15yr appreciation number. The only forward-looking 'forecasts' are (a) realized-volatility predictions at weekly horizon and (b) the practitioner expectation that the short-RR premium itself will compress as the market institutionalizes. Anyone projecting a decade BTC price off the smile is misusing the tool.

FAILURE MODES / SKEPTIC'S READ. (1) Maturity wall: no 10-15yr options exist, so any long-horizon read is extrapolation from <3-month tenors. (2) Negative-skew tail: the short-RR/short-vol edge is selling crash insurance — high Sharpe, fat left tail; a single FTX/March-2020 gap can erase years of carry, and the backtest is one survivorship path. (3) Regime non-stationarity: the variance risk premium flips magnitude by vol regime (Almeida et al.) and Deribit expects the edge to decay — so even the harvestable part is unstable. (4) Venue/sample concentration: Deribit ~= the market; data only ~2019+. (5) Asset-internal: silent on cross-asset correlations, which must be imported.

NET ROLE IN A BTC CMA PANEL. Use this approach to populate the VOLATILITY and TAIL/convexity cells (forward realized vol ~55-60%, implied richer by a positive VRP) and as a carry-strategy overlay — and, most importantly, as a SKEPTIC that refuses to read a structural directional premium out of option prices, thereby capping the over-bullish supply-scarcity and gold-parity models. The appreciation and correlation numbers are imported from the realized-decay baseline (~8-12% nom, gold corr ~0), not generated here.

issues: MISATTRIBUTION (journal): The Wang et al. (2024) paper 'Implied volatility slopes and jumps in bitcoin options market' is published in OPERATIONS RESEARCH LETTERS (DOI 10.1016/j.orl.2024.107135), NOT the Journal of International Money and Finance. The doc repeatedly cites it as 'J. Int. Money & Finance / ORL' (representative_sources, medium_explanation, rich_notes). J. Int. Money & Finance appears to be wrong; ORL is correct. The dual-journal hedge in representative_sources author_firm field papers over an error rather than committing to the verified venue.

The core disciplining quote (slopes 'lack the predictive capability for returns' but 'notably forecast realized volatility on the weekly frequency') could not be directly verified verbatim from the paywalled/403 source pages, though abstract paraphrases from ResearchGate/ScienceDirect corroborate the jump-reversal and vol-forecasting structure. The negative-on-returns finding is plausible and consistent with the cited risk-premia literature, but the doc presents a verbatim quotation whose exact wording I could not confirm — treat as paraphrase-grade, not confirmed quote-grade.

Almeida et al. is an arXiv WORKING PAPER (2410.15195), not peer-reviewed. The doc mostly labels it correctly as 'arXiv working paper,' but the pros list says the short-RR/variance-premium edge is 'documented across multiple independent sources (Deribit practitioner backtest + Almeida et al. + Bitcoin-VIX VRP literature)' — leaning on a non-peer-reviewed preprint as corroboration of robustness slightly overstates the evidentiary weight.

Single-venue / single-path fragility is acknowledged in cons but the synthesized vol floor (~55-65%, 'floor at realized trailing-5y ~57%') leans on a backward-looking realized number while the framework's own thesis is that the surface only reaches ~3-month tenors. Using a trailing-5y realized vol as a 10-15yr forward floor is itself an extrapolation the doc elsewhere calls 'heroic' — mild internal tension between the vol cell's confidence and the maturity-wall caveat.

The synthesized appreciation logic is internally circular as a 'contribution': the doc imports ~8-12% nominal from the cross-approach central / realized-decay baseline, then claims skew evidence 'pushes me DOWN' to 9-10%. But a market not pricing directional convexity is equally consistent with efficient pricing of an unknown drift — the inference that flat RR implies 'not pricing structural upward drift' is a weak directional read the doc's OWN cited result (Wang: skew has zero return information) says cannot be made. Using a 'no return signal' result to nudge the return estimate down is mildly self-contradictory.
verdict.corrections: ["Change the journal attribution for Wang et al. (2024) from 'Journal of International Money and Finance / Operations Research Letters' to 'Operations Research Letters' (vol/DOI 10.1016/j.orl.2024.107135). Drop the J. Int. Money & Finance reference entirely unless a second JIMF paper by the same authors can be cited — the verified venue is ORL.", "Downgrade the Wang verbatim quote to a paraphrase, or flag it as 'per abstract' since the exact sentence could not be confirmed from an open source. The substantive claim (slopes forecast realized vol weekly, not returns) is well-supported; the quotation marks imply a precision not independently verified here.", "In the pros list, qualify Almeida et al. as a working paper (not yet peer-reviewed) when invoking it as corroboration of robustness, so the 'multiple independent sources' claim doesn't over-credit a preprint.", "Resolve the appreciation circularity: state plainly that skew supplies NO directional information (per Wang) and therefore should NOT nudge the imported appreciation number up OR down. The current 9-10% 'skew pushes me down' reasoning contradicts the framework's own central finding. Keep appreciation as a pure import with a neutral, not bearish, skew read.", "For the vol cell, note that the ~57% floor is a trailing-realized anchor, not a skew-surface output — the surface only reaches ~3mo tenors, so the long-horizon vol number is itself imported/extrapolated, same caveat as appreciation. Don't present the vol cell as materially better-grounded than it is."]
missing_cons: NO OUT-OF-SAMPLE / LIVE TRACK RECORD post-2022: the Deribit backtest ends Dec-2022; the short-RR edge has not been shown to persist through the 2023-2025 institutionalization the source itself predicts would erode it. The doc cites the decay warning but omits that the edge may have ALREADY decayed in the unobserved 2023-2026 window — a survivorship/look-ahead concern stronger than 'non-stationary.'

TRANSACTION COSTS / LIQUIDITY: harvesting short-RR requires continuously rolling 25-delta options on a single venue (Deribit); bid-ask, slippage, and margin/funding costs on the wings are material and the cited Sharpe is almost certainly gross. A 10-15yr holder cannot frictionlessly compound this.

COUNTERPARTY / VENUE RISK: Deribit ~= the entire liquid BTC options market. Concentration in one offshore exchange is an existential tail (cf. FTX) that the short-vol carry strategy is maximally exposed to — distinct from the price-gap tail already listed.

REGULATORY / STRUCTURAL BREAK: spot ETF approval (Jan 2024) and institutional market-making explicitly change the supply/demand of convexity the strategy harvests; the doc mentions maturation generically but doesn't flag that the post-ETF regime may invert the sign of the RR carry, not merely shrink it.

The framework cannot distinguish a genuine risk premium from a peso-problem / under-sampled-crash bias: ~6 years of data (2019+) with few tail events means the 'rich call wings / short-RR pays' result may simply reflect tails that haven't fully realized in-sample.
overstated_pros: 'documented across multiple independent sources ... not a single curve-fit' — the three supporting sources are heavily OVERLAPPING, not independent: Zijin Wang is a co-author on BOTH Wang et al. (2024) and Almeida et al. (2024), and all sources draw on the SAME Deribit data. This is closer to one research cluster on one venue than independent confirmation. The 'multiple independent sources' framing is overstated.

'real desk adoption' (pro #2: 'empirically harvestable carry strategy with real desk adoption') — the Deribit piece is a sponsored/practitioner backtest; there is no evidence cited of actual desk AUM or live P&L. 'Real desk adoption' is asserted, not sourced.

'Honest and self-disciplining ... rare falsifiable NEGATIVE result' (pro #3) is fair on substance but slightly self-congratulatory; the negative result is about return-predictability of slopes specifically, and the doc then partially walks it back by letting skew 'push appreciation down,' undercutting the very discipline it praises.

The pro that it 'reflects what risk-takers actually pay for convexity right now' is true only at <3-month tenors — overstated as a forward-looking input for a 10-15yr CMA, since the surface contains no decade-horizon information at all.

new_approaches.name: Derivatives-Microstructure: Perp Funding, Cross-Rail Basis Segmentation & Price Discovery (Crypto Carry)
new_approaches.description: This approach reads three distinct microstructure objects in Bitcoin's derivatives complex rather than treating the dated-futures basis as a simple carry/yield input. (1) The perpetual-swap FUNDING rate — a zero-maturity rebalancing payment (offshore base ~0.01%/8hr ≈ 10.95%/yr, but spiking to 200%+ annualized in bull manias) that proxies leveraged long demand. (2) The cross-rail basis WEDGE — the gap between IBIT-ETF-options-implied carry and matched CME-futures carry, ~2.6%/yr (Mallory 2026), which persists because segmented collateral/margin systems prevent cross-margining and limit arbitrage capital. (3) Price DISCOVERY — Hasbrouck (1995) information share measuring WHERE the efficient price is formed (CME futures vs spot ETFs vs offshore perps), which has been migrating toward CME/Chicago post-ETF. The load-bearing academic result (Schmeling-Schrimpf-Todorov, BIS WP1087 / Management Science 2026) is a non-additive-drift CAVEAT: crypto carry is large and volatile (up to 60%/yr), is NOT compensation for spot risk, and HIGH carry predicts future price CRASHES — so you cannot add the basis/funding yield to BTC's expected spot return. As a CMA tool this framework does not generate a primary appreciation number; it disciplines OTHER models by ruling out a carry-additive-drift error and informs volatility (excess futures vol, forced-liquidation cascades) and the marginal-trader/correlation structure.
new_approaches.medium_explanation: Bitcoin's derivatives complex emits three measurable signals. Perpetual-swap funding (paid every 8 hours to keep the perp pinned to spot) proxies leveraged long demand; its base is ~11%/yr but it spikes to triple digits in manias. The cross-rail wedge is the ~2.6%/yr gap between ETF-option-implied carry and CME-futures carry, persisting because segmented margin/collateral rails block cross-margining and starve arbitrage capital (limits-of-arbitrage). Price discovery — Hasbrouck information share — locates where the efficient price forms; post-ETF it has shifted toward CME. The pivotal academic result (Schmeling-Schrimpf-Todorov) is a warning, not a return: carry reaches 40-60%/yr, is unexplained by fundamentals, reflects a volatile convenience yield from trend-chasers plus scarce arbitrage capital, is NOT a risk premium on spot, and HIGH carry predicts CRASHES (a non-additive drift). For a 10-15yr BTC CMA this framework therefore mainly CONSTRAINS others: it forbids adding basis/funding to expected spot return, raises the volatility/tail estimate via forced-liquidation cascades, and says nothing structural about gold.
key_drivers: Perpetual-swap funding rate (8-hour rebalancing payment): base ~0.01%/8hr ≈ 10.95%/yr, spiking to 200%+ annualized in bull manias; proxies leveraged-long demand and trend-chasing convenience yield
Dated-futures / cash-and-carry basis level (crypto carry): up to 40-60%/yr, highly time-varying, unexplained by observable fundamentals
Cross-rail basis WEDGE: ~2.58% mean / 2.52% median annualized gap between IBIT-ETF-options-implied carry and matched CME-futures carry (Mallory 2026, 386 obs); SD ~4.7%

Limits-of-arbitrage / market segmentation: inability to cross-margin spot BTC, CME futures, and ETF-options across distinct collateral systems; scarcity of arbitrage capital due to regulatory/margin frictions
Marginal-trader composition: small trend-chasing leveraged longs (perp demand) vs. constrained arbitrageurs (cash-and-carry shorts) — the demand/supply imbalance that sets carry
Hasbrouck (1995) information share / Gonzalo-Granger component share: WHERE the efficient price is formed (CME futures vs spot ETFs vs offshore perps); transaction size as a leadership determinant
Crash-risk / convenience-yield channel: high carry co-moves with the price of crash-risk insurance and PREDICTS future crashes — the non-additive-drift caveat
Forced-liquidation / excess-volatility mechanism: mark-to-market losses on short futures before convergence trigger liquidation cascades, amplifying realized vol
pros: Built on genuinely high-quality, peer-reviewed microstructure scholarship (BIS / Management Science; Hasbrouck JF 1995) and current ETF-era data — not crypto-native numerology like S2F or Metcalfe

Supplies a rare, rigorous NEGATIVE result that protects a CMA from a real error: it proves the futures basis / funding 'yield' is NOT additive to expected spot return (high carry predicts crashes, not gains), directly disciplining carry-as-drift approaches

Directly informative for the volatility and tail cells of a CMA: documents excess futures volatility, forced-liquidation cascades, and a measurable crash-risk-insurance linkage — mechanisms that justify keeping the vol floor high
Falsifiable and refreshable: funding rates, the cross-rail wedge, and information shares are all computable in near-real-time from public/exchange data, so the regime read can be updated continuously
Illuminates the marginal-buyer/seller structure (trend-chasing leveraged longs vs. constrained arbitrageurs), which underpins BTC's rising equity/risk-asset correlation better than supply-only models
cons: Not a primary return model: this framework produces NO native long-horizon appreciation forecast for spot BTC — the appreciation number must be borrowed from another approach, so it can only constrain/adjust, not anchor, a CMA

The headline carry result is explicitly that carry does NOT predict positive spot returns (it predicts crashes), so naive practitioners who add 'basis yield' or 'funding income' to BTC's expected return are committing exactly the error the literature refutes — high abuse potential

Short, regime-unstable samples: perpetuals (2016+), spot ETFs (2024+), and the cross-rail wedge (2025-26, 386 obs) all post-date most of BTC's history; the segmentation wedge may compress sharply as CME moves to 24/7 trading and rails integrate, so today's ~2.6% is not a structural constant

Price-discovery findings are method- and period-dependent and contradictory: Hasbrouck IS studies variously crown CME futures (Kapar-Olmo), the spot market (Baur-Dimpfl; Corbet et al.), or 'no single price setter' — there is no settled answer to WHERE price is formed
Cross-asset correlation content is thin: the literature is essentially silent on BTC vs. gold/TIPS/value-equity correlations, so those CMA cells get almost no structural guidance from this approach
A cash-and-carry / basis-harvest STRATEGY return (a real ~5-15%/yr market-neutral yield) is a fund product, not a property of BTC the asset — conflating the two would mis-specify a long-only BTC CMA

new_approaches.rich_notes:
WHAT IT IS. This is a microstructure family that reads Bitcoin's derivatives complex as three distinct objects, deliberately separating them from approach #17's treatment of the dated-futures basis as a simple carry/yield input. (1) PERPETUAL FUNDING: the perp swap has no expiry; an 8-hour funding payment keeps it pinned to spot. Offshore base is ~0.01%/8hr (≈10.95%/yr), but in bull manias funding has spiked above 0.2%/8hr (>200% annualized). Funding is a near-real-time gauge of leveraged-long demand. (2) CROSS-RAIL WEDGE: Mallory (2026, arXiv:2605.29309) recovers an ETF-implied forward from put-call parity on IBIT options, maps ETF shares to BTC via BlackRock's daily holdings file, benchmarks against BRRNY, and compares the implied carry to matched CME-futures carry. Across 386 date-bucket obs the mean wedge is 2.58%, median 2.52%, SD 4.72% (annualized). She attributes it to 'friction resulting from inability to cross margin spot bitcoin and CME futures' — segmented collateral systems that 'do not recognize offsetting risk,' a clean limits-of-arbitrage result. (3) PRICE DISCOVERY: Hasbrouck (1995) information share and Gonzalo-Granger component share locate the efficient price. Findings are method/period-dependent — Kapar-Olmo (2019, daily) crown CME futures; Baur-Dimpfl and Corbet et al. crown spot; recent multi-market work (20 spot, 26 futures venues) finds CME futures lead with transaction size as the key determinant; post-ETF commentary describes discovery 'moving to Chicago' as CME underpins ETF hedging and moves toward 24/7 trading.

THE LOAD-BEARING RESULT (and the reason this is a distinct CMA entry). Schmeling, Schrimpf & Todorov, 'Crypto Carry' (BIS WP1087 2023; Management Science 2026), show crypto carry — the cash-and-carry return, long spot/short futures — reaches up to 40-60%/yr, varies strongly, and 'cannot be explained by observable fundamental factors.' Their interpretation: a 'highly volatile crypto convenience yield' from 'trend-chasing and attention by smaller investors seeking leveraged upside exposure… in boom periods,' plus 'the relative scarcity of arbitrage capital taking the other side.' The CMA-critical finding: carry is NOT a compensation for spot risk, and 'a high crypto carry predicts future price crashes and a rise in carry typically goes hand in hand with a rise in the price of crash risk insurance.' This is the non-additive-drift caveat: you cannot add the futures basis or funding 'yield' to BTC's expected spot return — if anything, an elevated basis is a bearish forward signal for spot. That directly refutes the common practitioner move of treating BTC's persistent contango as a structural tailwind.

HOW IT FEEDS A 10-15yr CMA. It does NOT produce a primary appreciation number; treating it as one is a category error. Its three contributions are: (a) a GUARDRAIL — forbid carry-additive drift; the basis/funding is a microstructure premium for leverage/insurance, not spot expected return; (b) a VOLATILITY argument — documented 'excess volatility of crypto futures relative to spot,' forced-liquidation cascades (short-futures mark-to-market losses before convergence), and the crash-risk-insurance linkage all argue for keeping the vol estimate at/above the realized ~57% floor rather than compressing it; (c) a CORRELATION-STRUCTURE story — the marginal buyer is a leveraged trend-chaser funded via perps, which mechanistically ties BTC to risk-on/liquidity regimes and supports a positive, possibly rising, equity correlation (realized 5y +0.56). On gold the framework is silent and supplies no co-movement mechanism, so it leaves BTC-gold at ~0.

FAILURE MODES / SKEPTICISM. (1) Regime instability: perpetuals date to ~2016, spot ETFs to 2024, the cross-rail wedge to 2025-26 — none spans a full BTC history, and CME's move to 24/7 plus rail integration could collapse the ~2.6% wedge, so it is not a structural constant. (2) Strategy-vs-asset conflation: the cash-and-carry basis harvest is a real market-neutral fund yield (~5-15%/yr historically), but that belongs to a delta-hedged STRATEGY, not to long-only BTC — importing it into a BTC asset CMA double-counts. (3) Price-discovery is unsettled and contradictory across studies; 'where price is formed' has no canonical answer. (4) Thin cross-asset content: the literature gives almost no guidance on gold/TIPS/value correlations.

ON-RECORD MULTI-YEAR FORECASTS PRODUCED THIS WAY: none. By construction this family publishes basis/funding/wedge levels and information shares, not multi-year BTC price targets. Its honest CMA footprint is a constraint layer, not a forecast — which is precisely its value: it is the one approach in the digest that actively PREVENTS an overstated appreciation by ruling out carry-additive drift, while reinforcing a high vol floor and a risk-on equity correlation.

issues: arXiv ID 2605.29309 looked malformed on first glance (2605 is not a standard YYMM since there is no month 25 — but it IS valid: 26=2026, 05=May; submitted May 28 2026), so the citation is correct. No error here, but it is the kind of thing a careless reader would flag — confirmed legitimate.

The Mallory wedge SD of '4.72%/yr' could NOT be independently confirmed from the abstract/landing page — only the mean (2.58%) and median (2.52%) and N=386 are verifiable from public-facing text. The SD and the 'SD ~4.7%' claim may be drawn from the body, but is presented as if equally sourced. Flag as partially-unverified, not wrong.

Carry magnitude is slightly overstated on the high end. The BIS abstract says carry 'sometimes exceeding 40% per annum' and base 'above 10% annually.' The deep-dive repeatedly says 'up to 40-60%/yr.' The 60% upper bound appears in the paper's figures/peaks but the headline/abstract number is 40%+. Citing '40-60%' as if it were the headline mildly inflates the documented magnitude.

BTC-gold correlation framing is stale/incomplete. The deep-dive asserts realized BTC-gold ~0 (full -0.01, 5y +0.04) and bounds the synthesized cell at 0.0 to +0.15. But 2026 realized data shows the rolling BTC-gold correlation has swung materially NEGATIVE in windows (cited as low as -0.88 early-2026; widely reported 'decoupling'). The synthesized band excludes negative outcomes that the realized series now exhibits. Since the framework supplies NO gold mechanism, holding ~0 as a long-run prior is defensible, but the band should acknowledge it can go negative, not just bound it at the bottom near zero.

Equity-correlation realized anchors (+0.56 growth, +0.37 value) are plausible and consistent with 2026 reporting (~+0.35 to +0.6 vs Nasdaq), BUT BTC-equity correlation is highly regime-unstable (reported swings -0.68 to +0.72 within 2026). Presenting +0.45 to +0.60 as the forward band understates how much it whipsaws; a wider band or explicit regime caveat would be more honest.

Price-discovery 'migrating toward CME/Chicago post-ETF' is presented with more confidence than the literature supports. The deep-dive's OWN con admits findings are contradictory (Kapar-Olmo=futures, Baur-Dimpfl/Corbet=spot), and the contradiction is largely a data-frequency artifact (daily->futures lead, intraday->spot lead). The 'moving to Chicago' claim leans on commentary, not a settled IS result. Internally the doc is honest about this in cons, so it is disclosed, not hidden.

Self-referential decay anchor: the synthesized 8-12% nominal is explicitly borrowed from OTHER approaches (the realized decay 142->65->17%/yr). This framework contributes NO appreciation number, which the doc states clearly. Not a defect, but means the headline appreciation figure cannot be 'verified' against this approach at all — it rides entirely on the cross-approach central case.
verdict.corrections: "Verdict: numbers are broadly REAL and CORRECTLY ATTRIBUTED. Verified against primary sources: (1) BIS WP1087 'Crypto Carry' (Schmeling/Schrimpf/Todorov, Apr 2023, rev Oct 2025; Management Science 2026, DOI 10.1287/mnsc.2024.05069) — confirms carry >40%/yr, base >10%/yr, NOT spot-risk compensation, and high carry PREDICTS CRASHES. The load-bearing non-additive-drift caveat is accurately represented. (2) Mallory arXiv:2605.29309 (May 28 2026) — confirms mean wedge 2.58%, median 2.52%, N=386, sign = CME richer than ETF rail, limits-of-arbitrage/cross-margin friction interpretation. (3) Perp funding math is exactly right: 0.01%/8hr x1095 = 10.95%/yr; 0.2%/8hr = 219% (>200%). (4) Hasbrouck 1995 JF DOI is canonical and correct. (5) Price-discovery contradiction (Kapar-Olmo vs Baur-Dimpfl/Corbet) is real and correctly characterized as frequency-dependent. CORRECTIONS NEEDED: (a) downgrade carry headline from '40-60%' to '40%+ (peaks ~60%)' to match the abstract; (b) mark the Mallory SD 4.72% as body-sourced/unconfirmed from public text; (c) widen/qualify the gold-correlation cell to admit realized has gone NEGATIVE in 2026 windows, not just ~0 — the 0.0-to-+0.15 band is too tight given current decoupling; (d) add a regime-instability caveat to the equity-correlation band (whipsaws -0.68 to +0.72). The synthesized 10-15yr figures are DEFENSIBLE precisely because this approach explicitly declines to anchor appreciation and instead acts as a constraint layer (forbids carry-additive drift, defends high vol floor, explains risk-on equity corr). That framing is honest and not hype — the doc does NOT inflate appreciation; if anything its unique value is preventing inflation. The vol band (55-65% vs realized ~57% floor) is well-supported and not overstated."
overstated_pros: Pro #1 'genuinely high-quality peer-reviewed scholarship' is fair, but it slightly oversells CURRENCY: the central Mallory wedge (~2.6%) rests on a single 2026 working paper with 386 date-bucket obs over a few months of IBIT-options history — thin and not yet peer-reviewed (arXiv preprint). Calling the wedge a documented structural object overstates the evidentiary weight of one unrefereed paper.

Pro #5 'illuminates the marginal-buyer structure better than supply-only models' — the marginal-trader (leveraged trend-chaser via perps) story is a plausible mechanism but the literature does NOT publish a BTC-equity correlation coefficient from it; the +0.45-0.60 cell is pure realized-data inheritance, not a structural output of this framework. The pro implies more causal/structural correlation guidance than the approach actually delivers (the doc's own con #5 admits cross-asset content is thin, partially contradicting pro #5).
missing_cons: No mention that the Mallory cross-rail wedge is an UNREFEREED arXiv preprint (May 2026) — every other load-bearing source is peer-reviewed, but the headline 2.6% number is not. This evidentiary asymmetry is not flagged.

Funding-rate base of ~11%/yr is an OFFSHORE/perp figure; post-ETF, a growing share of leveraged BTC exposure is intermediated via CME and ETF options where funding/basis dynamics differ. The doc uses the offshore perp base as if representative of the marginal trader, but the marginal trader is increasingly onshore/institutional — a composition shift that could undercut the 'leveraged trend-chaser' correlation story over a 10-15yr horizon.

The crash-prediction result is SHORT-HORIZON (carry predicts crashes over days-to-quarters). The doc imports it into a 10-15yr CMA as a vol-floor argument, but a multi-year average vol need not stay elevated just because intraday liquidation cascades exist — over 10-15yr, financialization/ETF maturation is a plausible vol-COMPRESSION force the doc underweights (it only argues against compression, citing current mechanics).

Survivorship/sample-period bias in the realized anchors: trailing-5y vol ~57%, equity corr +0.56, gold corr ~0 all come from a window dominated by 2021-2026 (post-COVID liquidity, ETF launch). Using these as forward 10-15yr priors embeds a specific-regime bias not disclosed as a con.

No discussion of funding-rate sign asymmetry: funding can go deeply NEGATIVE in bear markets (longs paid by shorts), which is itself a crash/capitulation signal. The doc only frames funding as a positive leveraged-long-demand proxy spiking to +200%, omitting the negative-funding regime that matters for the vol/tail read.

new_approaches.name: Convenience-Yield / Theory-of-Storage Commodity Valuation
new_approaches.description: Treats Bitcoin as a storable commodity and inverts the cost-of-carry / theory-of-storage identity to back out its implied convenience yield (cy) — the non-pecuniary benefit of holding the spot asset rather than a futures claim. From F(t,T) = S(t)·e^{(r + w − cy)(T−t)} (futures = spot grossed up by financing r plus storage w minus convenience yield cy), one solves cy = r + w − (1/(T−t))·ln(F/S). For BTC, physical storage w≈0, so cy is essentially the negative of the annualized futures basis adjusted for the risk-free rate. Estimates run ~2.35%/yr (Hilliard-Ngo, from option/jump-diffusion fitting) to ~5.4% (Kim, spot-vs-futures premium), with the holding benefit sourced to short-sale constraints (spot prices are 'downward sticky') and on-chain governance/voting rights (+~5.6% during active proposals). The structural valuation step embeds this cy in a Gibson-Schwartz (1990) two-factor stochastic-convenience-yield process: spot S follows GBM and cy mean-reverts (Ornstein-Uhlenbeck), jointly pricing the forward curve and options. As a CMA building block, cy is the closest thing a no-cashflow asset has to a 'dividend': expected return ≈ risk-free rate + risk premium − convenience yield, so a positive cy is a return DRAG (you forgo it by being long via derivatives) while telling you the spot embeds a real, if small, holding utility.
new_approaches.medium_explanation: This framework borrows the commodity theory of storage. The cost-of-carry identity says a futures price equals spot grossed up by financing and storage, minus a convenience yield — the intangible benefit of holding the physical asset now. For Bitcoin, storage is roughly zero, so the convenience yield is essentially the negative of the annualized futures basis net of the risk-free rate. Backing it out gives BTC's only quasi-'dividend': estimates of ~2.35%/yr (Hilliard-Ngo) to ~5.4% (Kim), attributed to short-sale constraints and governance/voting rights. The structural step plugs this into a Gibson-Schwartz two-factor model where the spot is geometric and the convenience yield mean-reverts, jointly pricing futures and options. For a 10-15yr BTC CMA this is sobering, not bullish: the convenience yield is small and, crucially, frequently NEGATIVE (an 'inconvenience yield' during stress — BTC traded at -95% annualized convenience during COVID). So this channel implies BTC behaves like a volatile industrial commodity with a modest, unstable carry — it cannot justify high appreciation, only a low-single-digit holding-utility component embedded in a high-vol price process.
key_drivers: Annualized futures-spot basis (the observable input): cy ≈ r + storage − (1/(T−t))·ln(F/S); for BTC storage≈0, so cy is mainly the negative of the basis net of the risk-free rate
Short-sale constraints in spot BTC markets — the primary documented source of positive convenience yield (Kim): hard-to-borrow spot makes prices 'downward sticky', creating a holding premium
On-chain governance / voting rights — holding spot (not a derivative) confers protocol-vote optionality; Kim finds the holding benefit rises ~+5.6% when an important network proposal is pending
Mean-reversion speed and long-run mean of the convenience yield in the Gibson-Schwartz OU process (κ, α) — governs how the carry evolves and how the forward curve is shaped over the horizon

Inventory / scarcity state: like industrial metals, BTC's convenience yield is more volatile and more often negative when 'inventory' (exchange balances / liquidity) is low or during crisis (theory-of-storage state dependence)
Jump intensity and jump size (Hilliard-Ngo): BTC's return process has significant jumps; the convenience-yield estimate is conditional on a jump-diffusion spot dynamic, not pure GBM

Funding/leverage demand: in crypto the basis is dominated by perpetual-funding and leverage demand (contango), so the 'convenience yield' partly reflects positioning/segmentation, not pure holding utility (BIS crypto-carry critique)
pros: Gives BTC a genuine, observable, market-priced quasi-dividend — the convenience yield is backed out of live futures/option prices, not asserted; it is the closest thing a cashflow-less asset has to a yield, and it plugs cleanly into a CMA as expected return ≈ rf + risk premium − cy

Theoretically rigorous and well-established: Gibson-Schwartz (1990) is a 1,000+-citation commodity-pricing standard, and Hilliard-Ngo show the jump-diffusion-plus-convenience-yield model significantly outperforms practitioner Black-Scholes on Deribit BTC options — so the commodity framing has real out-of-sample option-pricing support

Honest about magnitude: unlike scarcity/Metcalfe narratives, this framework produces a SMALL number (~2-5%), implicitly conceding BTC has no large structural carry — a useful discipline that argues AGAINST the 65-140% appreciation extrapolations

State-dependence is informative: the finding that BTC's convenience yield is more volatile and often negative in low-inventory/crisis regimes (like an industrial metal, unlike gold) is a direct, evidence-based rebuttal of the naive 'digital gold' thesis and helps set correlation/regime expectations

Decomposes the basis into economic primitives (financing, storage, convenience) rather than treating it as a black-box momentum/sentiment signal — more structural than the crypto-carry positioning family
cons: It is a valuation/relative-pricing tool, NOT a return forecaster: the convenience yield prices the forward curve and options consistently with spot, but says almost nothing about the spot's own expected drift (μ). A CMA needs the appreciation rate, which this framework treats as exogenous — so it cannot produce a 10-15yr appreciation number on its own

The estimated convenience yield is small AND frequently negative ('inconvenience yield'): full-sample mean ≈ −1.4%, COVID mean ≈ −9.5%, range −165% to +90% annualized (Aharon et al.). A 'dividend' that is often negative and wildly unstable is a poor structural building block and contradicts the 'positive holding benefit' framing

The basis is contaminated by leverage/funding demand and market segmentation, not pure holding utility: BIS crypto-carry work shows the BTC basis is dominated by perpetual-funding and arbitrage-capital constraints (contango from leverage demand), so what gets labeled 'convenience yield' is partly a positioning/financing artifact — backing out a structural holding benefit from it risks mislabeling noise

Estimates are fragile and disagree by ~2x across studies (2.35% vs 5.4%) depending on data window, exchange, and whether option-implied or futures-implied; the convenience yield is not a stable parameter

Silent on every other CMA cell: the literature publishes no appreciation, no annualized volatility figure, and no cross-asset correlations (growth/value equity, FI, TIPS, gold) — all distributional and correlation inputs must be imported from realized data

Theory-of-storage assumes meaningful 'inventory' and storage economics; BTC's storage cost is ~0 and 'inventory' (exchange balances) is a weak, manipulable analogue, so the commodity mapping is partly metaphorical and the convenience yield loses its classical interpretation

synthesized_outputs.appreciation_nominal: ~8-11%/yr nominal (JUDGMENT — the framework does not output drift, so this is anchored to the cross-approach central and the realized decay path, not to convenience yield). The convenience-yield channel's actual contribution is a small carry TERM, not a growth rate: a structural read says E[return] ≈ rf (~3.5%) + risk premium − convenience yield, and since BTC's convenience yield averages roughly ZERO-to-slightly-negative over a full cycle (−1.4% mean per Aharon et al.; +2.35% to +5.4% only in calm/constrained windows), it neither adds nor subtracts much. Stripped of the convenience-yield distraction, the forward appreciation must come from a maturing risk premium on a high-vol commodity-like asset, which the realized decay (142%→65%→17%/yr) pulls down to roughly 8-11%. I sit slightly above the very bottom because a persistent positive convenience yield in normal regimes signals genuine spot-holding demand (short-sale-constrained scarcity), a modest real tailwind.
synthesized_outputs.appreciation_real: ~5-8%/yr real (subtracting ~2.5-3% long-run US inflation). Judgment; the convenience yield is a nominal carry concept and offers no separate inflation-protection mechanism, so the real number is just the nominal estimate deflated.
synthesized_outputs.volatility: ~55-62%/yr (JUDGMENT). This is the framework where high vol is most defensible: Hilliard-Ngo show BTC needs a JUMP-diffusion (not GBM), and Aharon et al. show the convenience yield itself is extremely volatile and industrial-metal-like. Floor anchored AT realized trailing-5y ~57% (no compression below realized evidenced); band 55-62% reflecting the jump component that keeps tail risk elevated through the horizon.
synthesized_outputs.corr_growth_eq: +0.45 to +0.60 (JUDGMENT; framework silent). The theory-of-storage finding that BTC trades like an INDUSTRIAL commodity — convenience yield collapsing in low-inventory/crisis states — implies pro-cyclical, risk-on behavior, consistent with realized trailing-5y BTC-growth-equity ≈ 0.56. Industrial-commodity-like assets co-move with the cycle, so I keep this firmly positive.
synthesized_outputs.corr_value_eq: +0.25 to +0.40 (JUDGMENT). Below growth-equity correlation; BTC's commodity/risk-asset beta is shared with value equities only partially (realized 5y ≈ 0.37).
synthesized_outputs.corr_fi_nominal: +0.10 to +0.20 (JUDGMENT). The convenience-yield/basis is financing-rate sensitive (cost-of-carry includes rf, and the BTC basis is funding-driven per BIS), giving a mild positive linkage to rate-sensitive nominal bonds; realized 5y ≈ 0.19.
synthesized_outputs.corr_tips: +0.20 to +0.30 (JUDGMENT). Slightly above nominal FI via shared real-rate/liquidity sensitivity in the carry; realized 5y ≈ 0.30. No structural inflation-hedge mechanism in the convenience-yield channel, so I do not push it higher.
synthesized_outputs.corr_gold: ~0.0 to +0.10 (JUDGMENT). This framework provides the strongest evidence-based case for a LOW gold correlation: Aharon et al. show BTC's convenience yield behaves like an industrial metal, NOT like gold, whose convenience yield is far more stable. An industrial-commodity carry profile co-moves with the cycle (toward equities), not with gold's safe-haven/real-rate profile — so the theory-of-storage lens actively argues AGAINST 'digital gold' co-movement, consistent with realized BTC-gold ≈ 0 (full −0.01, 5y +0.045).
synthesized_outputs.notes: Convenience yield is a carry TERM, not a growth driver — the framework's honest CMA message is deflationary, not bullish: small/unstable/often-negative carry, high jump-driven vol, pro-cyclical (equity-like) correlations, and a LOW gold correlation that the industrial-metal evidence actively supports. Appreciation/vol/correlation cells are all judgment anchored to realized data because the literature is silent on them; only the convenience-yield magnitudes (2.35% / 5.4% / −1.4% mean) are source-published.

new_approaches.rich_notes:
METHODOLOGY. The approach imports the commodity theory of storage (Kaldor 1939, Working 1949, Brennan 1958; formalized in continuous time by Gibson-Schwartz 1990). The cost-of-carry identity is F(t,T) = S(t)·exp[(r + w − cy)(T−t)], where r is financing, w is storage, and cy is the convenience yield — the flow of non-pecuniary benefits from holding the physical asset rather than a forward claim. Inverting: cy = r + w − (1/(T−t))·ln(F/S). For Bitcoin storage w≈0, so the convenience yield is essentially the negative of the annualized futures basis adjusted for the risk-free rate. The structural valuation embeds cy in a two-factor stochastic process (Gibson-Schwartz): spot S follows geometric Brownian motion while cy follows a mean-reverting Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process dδ = κ(α−δ)dt + σ_δ dW, with the two innovations correlated. This jointly prices the entire forward curve and options. Hilliard-Ngo (2022) extend the spot to a JUMP-diffusion and show, on Deribit option data, that the jump-diffusion-with-convenience-yield model 'significantly outperforms Practitioner Black-Scholes,' concluding 'Bitcoin behaves more like a commodity than a currency.'

KEY RELATIONSHIPS & MAGNITUDES. Three studies pin the number, and they disagree by design because they use different instruments and windows: (1) Hilliard-Ngo estimate an average annual convenience yield ~2.35% from option/jump-diffusion fitting. (2) Kim (2022, FRL) finds the BTC spot trades at a 5.4% premium to futures — the convenience yield — sourced to short-sale constraints ('spot prices are downward sticky') and on-chain voting rights, with the holding benefit rising an additional +5.6% when an important network proposal is pending. (3) Aharon et al. (2023, COVID paper) compute cy directly from cost-of-carry and find it is frequently NEGATIVE: full-sample mean −1.4%, pre-COVID +1.6%, during-COVID −9.5%, with an astonishing range of −165% to +90% annualized. Critically, they show BTC's convenience yield is more volatile in low-inventory periods and behaves like an INDUSTRIAL metal, whereas gold's convenience yield is far more stable (mean −2.0%, range −26% to +16%).

WHY THIS IS DISTINCT, AND WHAT IT IMPLIES FOR A CMA. This is the only framework in the digest that gives BTC a genuine market-priced quasi-dividend. But as a CMA building block its honest message is deflationary, not bullish. The convenience yield prices the forward curve; it does NOT forecast spot drift. The CMA contribution is a small carry term in E[return] ≈ rf + risk premium − cy, and because cy averages roughly zero-to-slightly-negative over a full cycle, it neither powers nor explains the historical 65-140% appreciation. So this lens implicitly endorses a LOW, decaying appreciation (I synthesize ~8-11% nominal), a HIGH jump-driven volatility (~55-62% — the framework needs jumps, so vol-compression skepticism is well-grounded), and — most usefully — a LOW gold correlation: the industrial-metal carry profile co-moves with the cycle (toward equities, realized ~0.56), not with gold's safe-haven profile. The theory-of-storage evidence is thus an evidence-based REBUTTAL of 'digital gold,' aligning with realized BTC-gold ≈ 0.

FAILURE MODES & CRITIQUES (faithfully). First, it is a relative-pricing tool masquerading as valuation — it cannot output appreciation, which is exactly the cell a CMA most needs. Second, the 'convenience yield' is contaminated: the BIS 'Crypto carry' work (2023) argues the BTC basis is dominated by perpetual-funding/leverage demand and arbitrage-capital segmentation (contango from leverage demand), so backing out a structural 'holding benefit' from the basis risks relabeling a financing/positioning artifact as economic utility. Third, the number is unstable and often negative — a 'dividend' ranging −165% to +90% is not a usable structural parameter. Fourth, theory-of-storage presupposes meaningful inventory and storage economics; BTC's storage≈0 and 'inventory' (exchange balances) is a weak, gameable analogue, so the commodity mapping is partly metaphorical. Fifth, the literature is silent on volatility-as-a-statistic and on every cross-asset correlation, so the distributional half of the CMA must be borrowed wholesale from realized data.

ON-RECORD MULTI-YEAR FORECASTS. None. No author has used the convenience-yield/theory-of-storage framework to publish a multi-year BTC price or return forecast. Hilliard-Ngo, Kim, Gibson-Schwartz, and Aharon et al. are all relative-pricing/option-pricing/empirical papers, not capital-market-assumption documents. (Provenance note: the seed misattributed the Quantitative Finance paper to 'Hofmann, Maier & Reinerth'; the verified authors are Jimmy E. Hilliard and Julie T. D. Ngo, QF 22(11), 2079-2091.)

issues: MISATTRIBUTION (ironic, same class the doc congratulates itself for fixing): the COVID convenience-yield paper is cited as 'Aharon, Demir, Lau et al.' in 'International Review of Financial Analysis / PMC'. The ACTUAL paper is Arkorful, Chen, Gu & Liu (Xiamen/Hainan Univ.), 'What can we learn from the convenience yield of Bitcoin? Evidence from the COVID-19 crisis,' International Review of Economics & Finance, vol. 88 (2023), pp. 141-153, DOI 10.1016/j.iref.2023.06.029. Wrong authors, wrong journal name, and the link points to a generic PMC mirror rather than the IREF DOI. Every -1.4% / -9.5% / range / gold-contrast number in the doc traces to THIS paper, so the entire 'Aharon et al.' attribution chain (repeated ~10 times across pros/cons/drivers/notes) is mislabeled. The notes section explicitly brags about fixing the Hilliard-Ngo misattribution while leaving this larger one in place — a detection-gap failure.

VERIFIED CORRECT: Hilliard & Ngo (QF 22(11), 2079-2091, 2022), ~2.35% convenience yield, jump-diffusion beats Practitioner Black-Scholes, 'behaves more like a commodity than a currency' — all confirmed. The seed's 'Hofmann, Maier & Reinerth' was indeed wrong; the doc's correction to Hilliard-Ngo is right.

VERIFIED CORRECT: Kim (FRL 44, 2022), 5.4% spot-over-futures premium, sourced to short-sale constraints ('downward sticky') + voting rights — confirmed. The specific '+5.6% when a network proposal is pending' figure could NOT be independently verified from accessible sources (paywalled); the abstract only says voting-right value 'becomes more observable whenever a ballot [is pending]'. Treat the +5.6% as plausible-but-unverified, not as established.
VERIFIED CORRECT: Gibson-Schwartz (JF 45, 959-976, 1990), two-factor spot+OU-convenience-yield, ~1,150 citations — confirmed. 'Two-factor' / mean-reverting OU framing accurate.

VERIFIED CORRECT: BIS WP 1087 'Crypto carry' by Schmeling, Schrimpf & Todorov (2023). The doc's use is faithful: carry is large/volatile (BIS: averages >10%/yr, can exceed 40%), driven by trend-chaser leverage demand + limited arbitrage capital — supports the 'convenience yield is contaminated by funding/positioning' critique correctly.

OVERSTATED PRO / INTERNAL CONTRADICTION in synthesized appreciation: the doc nudges nominal appreciation 'slightly above the very bottom' (to 8-11%) justified by 'a persistent positive convenience yield in normal regimes [as] a modest real tailwind.' But the doc's OWN headline finding (from the same Arkorful paper) is that full-cycle cy mean is NEGATIVE (-1.4%) and the framework's honest message is 'deflationary, not bullish.' Citing a slightly-positive calm-window cy as an upward tailwind while the full-cycle mean is negative is selective and contradicts the doc's own framing. The upward nudge is unsupported by the very channel it invokes.

SYNTHESIZED APPRECIATION IS SMUGGLED, NOT DERIVED: the doc correctly states the convenience-yield framework outputs NO drift, then imports 8-11% from 'cross-approach central' + realized decay. Fine as a placeholder, but the 8-11% number has ZERO support from this framework — it is a borrowed cross-framework figure dressed in convenience-yield language. A reader could mistake it for a framework output. The decay path (142→65→17%/yr) extrapolated naively lands BELOW 8-11%; reaching 8-11% requires assuming decay ARRESTS ('maturing risk premium'), a mechanism asserted without evidence. The number is defensible only as a cross-framework anchor, NOT as anything this lens produces or even leans toward.
MINOR: range numbers rounded — doc says cy range '-165% to +90%' (actual -165.1% to +90.4%) and gold '-26% to +16%' (actual -26.2% to +16.4%). Rounding is fine and honest.
verdict.corrections: Fix the citation: replace 'Aharon, Demir, Lau et al.' / 'International Review of Financial Analysis / PMC' with 'Arkorful, Chen, Gu & Liu, International Review of Economics & Finance, vol. 88 (2023), pp. 141-153, DOI 10.1016/j.iref.2023.06.029' everywhere it appears (representative_sources entry, plus ~10 in-text 'Aharon et al.' mentions, plus the 'Provenance note' which currently only fixes Hilliard-Ngo). This is the SAME error class the doc flags as fixed — the detection gap is that only one of two misattributions was caught. Second: flag the Kim '+5.6% during governance proposals' figure as not-independently-verified (paywalled), or sourced to the specific table/page. Third: in synthesized_outputs.appreciation_nominal, drop or hedge the 'slightly above the very bottom because a persistent positive convenience yield... [is] a modest real tailwind' justification — it contradicts the doc's own negative full-cycle cy mean; the honest statement is that the convenience-yield channel gives NO directional signal on drift and 8-11% is purely a borrowed cross-framework anchor. Fourth: state explicitly that naive extrapolation of the decay path lands below 8-11% and that the floor relies on an unevidenced decay-arrest assumption.
missing_cons: The convenience-yield estimates from the three studies are not comparable: Hilliard-Ngo's 2.35% is option-implied under a JUMP-diffusion specification, Kim's 5.4% is a futures-basis premium, and Arkorful's -1.4% is a raw cost-of-carry mean — different instruments, windows, AND model assumptions. The doc presents them as a range ('2.35% to 5.4%') as if they measure the same object; they don't. The '2x disagreement' con understates this — it's not just fragility, it's apples-to-oranges.

Sign/direction confusion risk: under F=S·e^{(r+w-cy)(T-t)}, BTC futures historically trade in CONTANGO (F>S, large positive basis per BIS, >10%/yr), which mechanically implies a NEGATIVE convenience yield, not positive. Kim's 5.4% POSITIVE premium (spot over futures = backwardation) and the BIS large-positive-contango basis are in tension — they describe different regimes/instruments (Kim uses CME futures in a specific window). The doc never reconciles why one study finds spot-over-futures (positive cy) while the dominant market structure (perpetuals contango) implies negative cy. This is a material unresolved inconsistency the doc papers over.

Survivorship/regime selection in the realized anchors: the realized 5y correlations (BTC-growth 0.56, BTC-gold ~0, vol ~57%) all come from a single 2020-2025 window dominated by one macro regime (ZIRP→hiking→cuts). The doc treats these as structural for a 10-15yr horizon without noting regime-dependence — the same theory-of-storage state-dependence it invokes implies these correlations will themselves shift across the horizon.

No discussion of futures-market maturation eroding the convenience yield itself: as BTC spot-shorting becomes easier (ETF options, lending markets, borrow availability post-2024), Kim's short-sale-constraint source of positive cy should DECAY toward zero, pushing realized cy more negative — a forward-looking headwind the doc's 'persistent positive cy in normal regimes' assumption ignores.
overstated_pros: 'Persistent positive convenience yield in normal regimes signals genuine spot-holding demand... a modest real tailwind' — overstated and self-contradicting: full-cycle mean cy is NEGATIVE (-1.4%) per the doc's own source, so on a 10-15yr CMA horizon (which spans multiple regimes incl. stress) the expected carry contribution is slightly negative-to-zero, not a tailwind.

Pro #2 ('out-of-sample option-pricing support... commodity framing has real support') is accurate but oversells transferability: Hilliard-Ngo's result is that a jump-diffusion-with-cy beats Black-Scholes at PRICING OPTIONS — it says nothing about the cy being a usable CMA carry input or about spot drift. The doc elsewhere admits this, but the pro is phrased to imply broader validation than the paper delivers.

Pro #1 ('genuine, observable, market-priced quasi-dividend... plugs cleanly into a CMA') is undercut by the doc's own cons: a quantity that is often negative, ranges -165% to +90%, and is contaminated by funding/leverage (BIS) does NOT 'plug cleanly' into anything. The pro and con sections describe opposite realities; the pro is the overstated one.

new_approaches.name: Machine-Learning Forecasting & Empirical Asset Pricing (DL/Trees/On-Chain ML/Gu-Kelly-Xiu/HMM)
new_approaches.description: A family of nonparametric, nonlinear learned predictors applied to Bitcoin: deep sequence models (LSTM/GRU/CNN/Temporal Fusion Transformer), tree ensembles (random forest, XGBoost, LightGBM), on-chain-feature ML (active addresses, hashrate, NVT, exchange flows fed into classifiers), Gu-Kelly-Xiu-style empirical-asset-pricing ML that learns a flexible conditional expected-return function E[r|z] from a large characteristic/predictor set, and Bayesian (non-homogeneous) Hidden Markov regime-detection models that infer latent bull/bear/calm states. Unlike the parametric/linear approaches in the existing 20 (e.g. OLS factor model, GARCH), these learners impose almost no functional form and let nonlinear predictor interactions emerge. Crucially, they are NOT designed to produce a 10-15yr CMA: their documented edge is short-horizon (intraday-to-monthly) and directional. The honest CMA payload is a negative result: predictability is concentrated at short horizons and degenerates toward a random-walk-with-drift as the horizon lengthens, so a learned model gives no defensible decade-ahead appreciation number beyond the unconditional drift — and on-chain signal value is documented to decay post-ETF as the marginal buyer leaves the chain. To force a CMA you must fall back on the realized-decay baseline; ML adds regime/correlation structure, not a long-run level.
new_approaches.medium_explanation: These models learn a flexible mapping from predictors (technicals, macro factors, on-chain metrics, latent regimes) to next-period Bitcoin returns, letting nonlinear interactions emerge rather than imposing a line. Gu-Kelly-Xiu (2020) is the canonical empirical-asset-pricing version: trees and neural nets beat linear models, but the monthly out-of-sample R-squared is only ~0.3-0.4% in equities, with momentum, liquidity and volatility as dominant signals. For Bitcoin specifically, futures studies find ML directional accuracy near 56% intraday — barely above an ARIMA/coin-flip benchmark — and random forests that hit 87% in-sample collapse out-of-sample (overfitting). Bayesian Hidden Markov models add value by detecting bull/bear/calm regimes (predictors: momentum, VIX, Treasury yield), and TFT-style deep nets flag gold and the dollar as top macro drivers. The key implication for a 10-15yr CMA: edge is short-horizon and directional, decaying to random-walk-with-drift at long horizons. ML therefore cannot supply a decade appreciation level — only regime/correlation texture layered on the realized-decay baseline.
key_drivers: Predictor/feature set: technical (lagged returns, momentum, volatility), macro (VIX, US Treasury yield, USD index, gold, oil), and on-chain (active addresses, hashrate, NVT, exchange flows)
Model class and its inductive bias: tree ensembles (RF/XGBoost/LightGBM) for tabular feature interactions vs sequence DL (LSTM/GRU/TFT) for temporal structure vs Bayesian HMM for latent regimes
Nonlinear predictor interactions — the documented source of ML's edge over linear models (Gu-Kelly-Xiu)
Forecast horizon — the single most important driver of realized edge: predictability is concentrated intraday-to-monthly and decays toward random-walk at multi-year horizons
Latent regime state (bull/bear/calm) and the transition probabilities governing it (non-homogeneous HMM)
Training-window stationarity / regime stability — performance is highly sensitive to whether the test period resembles the training period
Sample size and signal-to-noise — DL needs large data; crypto is noise-dominated, amplifying overfitting
Structural breaks (ETF/institutionalization) that degrade on-chain feature informativeness as the marginal buyer leaves the chain
pros: Brutally honest about long-horizon limits: unlike S2F/Metcalfe/power-law, this family's own evidence says the edge is short-horizon and directional and degenerates to random-walk-with-drift at long horizons — which is the correct, conservative prior for a 10-15yr CMA (argues AGAINST extrapolating supra-decay returns)

Genuinely out-of-sample and statistically disciplined: Gu-Kelly-Xiu and crypto follow-ups use strict train/validation/test splits, SPA/MCS/Diebold-Mariano tests, and economic (not just statistical) performance metrics — a higher evidentiary bar than the in-sample R-squared bragging of scarcity models

Captures nonlinearity and regime structure that linear/parametric models miss: HMMs cleanly separate bull/bear/calm regimes, and trees/NNs surface real nonlinear interactions, giving useful texture for the correlation and volatility-clustering side of a CMA even when they fail on the level

Identifies which drivers actually matter empirically (momentum, liquidity, volatility, VIX, Treasury yield, gold, USD) rather than asserting a single narrative driver — useful for building defensible correlation views
Model-agnostic and refreshable: can ingest new features (on-chain, ETF-flow, macro) and be re-estimated as regimes shift, with explicit overfitting diagnostics
cons: Not a long-horizon model at all: the documented edge is intraday-to-monthly; at the decade horizon relevant to a CMA, learned predictors collapse to the unconditional random-walk-with-drift, so they supply NO independent appreciation level — the CMA still has to come from the realized-decay baseline

Severe overfitting / data-snooping risk in noise-dominated crypto data: random forests reaching 87% in-sample accuracy degrade to ~56% out-of-sample (barely above an ARIMA or coin-flip benchmark); with enough trials a beautiful backtest produces no real edge — the 'Training Set Delusion'

Tiny effective edge even when real: Gu-Kelly-Xiu's best monthly out-of-sample R-squared is ~0.4% in equities; for BTC, directional accuracy clusters near 50-56%, and transaction costs/non-stationarity routinely erase the gross edge

Non-stationarity and structural breaks break the models: crypto volatility, liquidity and behavior shift swiftly; ETF/institutionalization is documented to degrade on-chain feature informativeness (marginal buyer no longer touches the chain), so a model trained pre-ETF mis-specifies the post-ETF regime

Black-box / unstable feature importance: TFT calls gold the top driver, futures studies call SVM most robust, HMMs call momentum/VIX dominant — no consensus signal, and importances are sample-dependent, so the framework cannot be relied on to populate stable CMA correlations

Silent on equilibrium value: ML learns conditional means from history and has no anchor for a no-cashflow asset's fair value, so it cannot discipline whether BTC is over/undervalued at the horizon — it can only extrapolate the empirical drift it was trained on

cited_outputs.appreciation_nominal: n/a (source silent on a 10-15yr appreciation level). These models publish SHORT-horizon performance, not decade returns: Gu-Kelly-Xiu report monthly out-of-sample R-squared of ~0.33-0.40% (equities) and a neural-net long-short Sharpe of 1.35 value-weighted / 2.45 equal-weighted, plus a 0.77 S&P-timing Sharpe; BTC futures studies report ~56% directional accuracy (SVM most robust; random forest 87% in-sample collapsing out-of-sample). None is an annualized BTC CMA. The implicit long-horizon statement is that predictability decays to random-walk-with-drift, i.e. expected return collapses to the unconditional drift.

cited_outputs.volatility: n/a (source silent on a forward CMA vol). HMM/regime and ML-vol-prediction papers characterize BTC volatility as regime-switching and clustered (and warn ML vol forecasts are heavily overfit — 'Training Set Delusion'), but publish no single annualized 10-15yr figure.
cited_outputs.corr_growth_eq: n/a (source silent as a published CMA correlation). HMM/macro-ML papers identify VIX and US Treasury yield as dominant cross-asset predictors, implying a risk-asset linkage, but report no point correlation.

cited_outputs.notes: The framework's defining CMA contribution is a NEGATIVE result: rigorous out-of-sample ML finds only short-horizon, directional, economically-small edge that decays to random-walk-with-drift at long horizons. It therefore publishes performance metrics (R-squared, accuracy, Sharpe), not a decade appreciation/vol/correlation set. Any multi-year 'ML price target' in circulation is a practitioner extrapolation the academic horizon-decay evidence discredits.

synthesized_outputs.horizon: 10-15 years (forced onto the framework; ML supplies no native long-horizon output, so these are the realized-decay baseline plus ML-informed regime/correlation texture).
synthesized_outputs.appreciation_nominal: ~8-12%/yr nominal (judgment; the framework is silent on a decade level, so this is the realized-decay baseline, NOT an ML output). The honest ML lesson is that any learned long-horizon expectation collapses to the unconditional random-walk-with-drift, so the CMA must be the empirical drift after maturation. Realized appreciation decayed 142%->65%->17%/yr; extrapolating that decay, the forward drift sits in the high-single-to-low-double-digit range. ML explicitly argues AGAINST the supra-decay returns of S2F/power-law because its own out-of-sample evidence shows no exploitable long-horizon edge.
synthesized_outputs.appreciation_real: ~5-9%/yr real (subtracting ~2.5-3% long-run inflation). Pure baseline carry-through; ML supplies no scarcity tailwind and no fair-value anchor.
synthesized_outputs.volatility: ~55-60%/yr (judgment, anchored to realized trailing-5y ~57%). HMM/regime evidence supports clustered, regime-switching vol with fat tails rather than smooth decay; I hold the floor AT realized ~57% because the sub-2yr ETF sample does not yet evidence compression below realized, and ML vol forecasts are documented to be overfit (no credible case for stepping below the realized floor).
synthesized_outputs.corr_growth_eq: ~0.45-0.55 (judgment). The learned dominant predictors (VIX, Treasury yield, risk appetite) make BTC behave as a high-beta risk asset; consistent with realized trailing-5y 0.56 and rising with institutionalization. This is the most ML-supported of the correlations.
synthesized_outputs.corr_value_eq: ~0.25-0.35 (judgment; realized trailing-5y 0.37). BTC carries the duration/liquidity beta of growth more than value.
synthesized_outputs.corr_fi_nominal: ~0.10-0.20 (judgment; realized trailing-5y 0.19). HMM models flag Treasury yield as a regime predictor, supporting a modest positive rate/liquidity linkage rather than a hedge.
synthesized_outputs.corr_tips: ~0.20-0.30 (judgment; realized trailing-5y 0.30). Mild real-rate/liquidity sensitivity shared with other long-duration stores of value.
synthesized_outputs.corr_gold: ~0.05-0.15 (judgment). Köse et al.'s TFT flags gold as the top BTC feature, which would argue for a higher number, but feature importance is a learned dependence, not co-movement, and realized BTC-gold correlation is ~0 (full -0.01, 5y +0.045). I keep it at the low end and explicitly distinguish 'gold is a useful predictor of BTC direction' (plausible, learned) from 'BTC co-moves with gold' (not in the data). The digital-gold linkage is not empirically supported by realized correlation.
synthesized_outputs.notes: ML's genuine CMA contribution is texture, not level: it rejects long-horizon supra-decay extrapolation (forcing the appreciation back to the realized-decay baseline ~8-12% nominal), supports a high non-decaying vol floor via regime/fat-tail evidence, and — via learned predictor importance (VIX, Treasury yield, gold, USD) — supports a high equity correlation and a low, predictor-driven (not co-movement-driven) gold relationship. The single most defensible ML-anchored cell is corr_growth_eq ~0.45-0.55.

new_approaches.rich_notes:
METHODOLOGY. This family pools five learned-predictor strands that share a core property absent from the existing 20 approaches: they impose almost no functional form and let the data choose a nonlinear conditional-mean (or regime) function. (1) Gu-Kelly-Xiu (2020, RFS 33:2223-2273) is the canonical empirical-asset-pricing-via-ML template — estimate E[r|z] over a large characteristic set with penalized regressions, random forests, gradient-boosted trees and neural nets, then compare strictly out-of-sample. Their headline equities results: trees and neural nets dominate (monthly OOS R-squared ~0.33-0.40%, vs near-zero/negative for OLS), with momentum, liquidity and volatility the dominant signals; a NN-sorted long-short decile earns Sharpe 1.35 (VW) / 2.45 (EW), and NN S&P timing earns Sharpe 0.77. (2) Deep sequence models — Köse et al. (2025, J. Forecasting 44:1666-1698) run LSTM/GRU/CNN/TFT plus XGBoost/LightGBM/SVR on BTC vs global macro; the Temporal Fusion Transformer wins and ranks GOLD the single most relevant feature, USD index second. (3) Tree/SVM ensembles on microstructure — Akyildirim/Goncu/Sensoy (PMC8296834) test six ML models on CME BTC-futures mid-price direction at 5-60min: SVM most robust (~56% OOS), random forest 87% in-sample collapsing OOS (classic overfit), ARIMA ceiling ~56% — i.e. ML barely clears a naive benchmark. (4) On-chain-feature ML feeds active addresses, hashrate, NVT and exchange flows into classifiers. (5) Bayesian/non-homogeneous Hidden Markov regime models — Koki, Leonardos & Piliouras (2022, RIIBAF 59) find a 4-state NHHM gives the best one-step-ahead forecasts for BTC/ETH/XRP, with momentum, VIX and US Treasury yield the most common predictors, cleanly separating bull/bear/calm regimes.

KEY RELATIONSHIPS & CMA PAYLOAD. The shared, brutally honest message: documented edge is short-horizon and directional, and degenerates toward a random-walk-with-drift as the horizon lengthens. This is exactly the opposite of the S2F/Metcalfe/power-law/gold-parity family, which extrapolates supra-decay returns. For a 10-15yr CMA, the implication is a NEGATIVE result — ML supplies no defensible decade appreciation level beyond the unconditional drift, so the CMA defaults to the realized-decay baseline (~8-12% nominal). What ML DOES contribute is texture: regime structure (HMM bull/bear/calm, fat tails, vol clustering — supporting a high ~55-60% vol floor rather than smooth convergence to gold-like vol) and a learned cross-asset dependence set (VIX/Treasury-yield/USD/gold) that supports a high equity correlation (~0.45-0.55) and a modest, predictor-driven — not co-movement-driven — relationship to gold.

HISTORICAL FIT & FAILURE MODES. In-sample fit is often spectacular and almost entirely illusory: the 'Training Set Delusion' (Wang, Zeng, Li & Wang, 2025, SSRN 5797242) documents that BTC return/vol ML models are pervasively overfit; the broader literature applies SPA/MCS/Diebold-Mariano tests precisely because naive backtests are contaminated by data-snooping. Non-stationarity is fatal — crypto volatility, liquidity and news-response shift swiftly, so a model trained in one regime mis-specifies the next. The most important structural break is institutionalization: post-ETF, the marginal buyer no longer touches the chain, degrading on-chain feature informativeness; a pre-2024-trained on-chain-ML model is arguably mis-specified today. Novinsalari & Sensoy (2025, SSRN 5614913) find ML on BTC ETFs beats 50% accuracy and claim weak-form-EMH violations, but such edges are intraday/short-horizon and typically die to transaction costs — they do NOT scale to a decade view. Feature importance is unstable across studies (TFT says gold; futures study says SVM/microstructure; HMM says momentum/VIX), so the framework cannot reliably pin CMA correlations.

ON-RECORD MULTI-YEAR FORECASTS. Notably, this family produces essentially NO credible on-record multi-year point forecasts — which is itself the finding. Reputable academic ML work confines itself to short horizons (intraday to one-month) and reports R-squared/accuracy/Sharpe, not 10-15yr price targets. Where multi-year ML 'predictions' appear, they are practitioner/ainvest-style ($X by date) extrapolations of a short-horizon model run forward, which the academic literature's own horizon-decay result discredits. Gu-Kelly-Xiu is explicitly a measurement of conditional risk premia, not a long-run forecast. The honest CMA use of ML is therefore as a discipline that rejects long-horizon extrapolation and anchors to the empirical drift plus regime/correlation structure — not as a source of a decade appreciation number.

issues: AUTHORSHIP MISATTRIBUTION (only hard error): the futures microstructure paper 'Forecasting mid-price movement of Bitcoin futures using machine learning' (Annals of Operations Research, PMC8296834) is cited as 'Akyildirim, Goncu, Sensoy et al.' Verified actual authors are Erdinc Akyildirim, Oguzhan Cepni, Shaen Corbet, Gazi Salah Uddin. Goncu and Sensoy ARE genuine Akyildirim co-authors on OTHER crypto-ML papers, so this is a cross-citation bleed, not an invented source. The numbers attributed to it (SVM ~56% most robust, max 71%; RF 87% in-sample collapsing to ~56% OOS; ARIMA ceiling ~56%; beats random walk/ARIMA) are all CORRECT for this paper.

The EW Sharpe ~2.45 and monthly OOS R2 ~0.33-0.40% are the paper's standard headline figures (Table-level, the PDFs were binary-unreadable to the fetch tool) and match the canonical record; no contradiction found, but they rest on knowledge of the paper rather than a fresh table read.

FRAMING TENSION on the appreciation synthesis: the decay path is 142->65->17%/yr, and trailing-5y realized (the most recent, most relevant window) is ALREADY 17%. The synthesized 8-12% nominal sits BELOW the most recent realized print, so it is conservative, not hype. But the prose 'high-single-to-low-double-digit range' and 'extrapolating that decay' is slightly loose: a strict continuation of a 142->65->17 decay would argue for a forward number at or below 17% and trending lower, which 8-12% honors on the low side. INTERNAL-CONSISTENCY CHECK PASSED: every realized anchor in the synthesized column matches the scripted empirical_anchor.json exactly -- decay 1.422/0.6547/0.1697, trailing-5y vol 0.5745 (~57%), gold corr full -0.011 & 5y +0.045 (~0), growth_eq 5y 0.564, value_eq 0.367, fi_nom 0.192, tips 0.301.
