verdict.corrections: Fix the one hard error: change the futures-paper byline from 'Akyildirim, Goncu, Sensoy et al. (PMC8296834)' to 'Akyildirim, Cepni, Corbet, Uddin (Annals of Operations Research, 2021; PMC8296834)'. All numerics for that paper are correct and need no change. Optionally tighten the appreciation prose to show the bridge from trailing-5y realized 17% down to the synthesized 8-12% (i.e. state explicitly that you are taking the forward drift one decay-step BELOW the most recent 17% realized, not interpolating up from it). The GKX EW-Sharpe 2.45 / R2 0.40% citations are accurate as the paper's headline figures but, for an auditable record, footnote them to Table 7 / the Internet Appendix rather than leaving them table-unspecified. No other numbers require correction.
overstated_pros: Pro #2 ('genuinely out-of-sample and statistically disciplined: ...SPA/MCS/Diebold-Mariano') is true of the empirical-asset-pricing/GKX and futures strands but is presented as a property of the whole family; the two SSRN 2025 BTC-ETF/practitioner-adjacent strands are newer and less battle-tested, so the family-wide claim of rigorous OOS discipline is mildly overstated.

Pro #1's 'brutally honest about long-horizon limits' is genuinely a strength, but it is partly a rhetorical reframe of a weakness (the family produces NO long-horizon output) into a virtue. Fairly stated as honesty, but a reader could mistake 'argues AGAINST supra-decay returns' as positive evidence for the 8-12% level, when in fact ML supplies zero independent support for ANY level -- the level is 100% the realized-decay baseline. The doc does say this elsewhere, but the pro framing softens it.
missing_cons: Survivorship/publication bias in the academic crypto-ML literature itself is not flagged: papers reporting weak-form-EMH violations and >50% accuracy are far more publishable than null results, so even the 'honest, OOS-disciplined' positive findings (Novinsalari-Sensoy >0.80 NN/SVM accuracy) are upward-biased at the literature level, not just at the single-model level. This compounds the overfitting con and is a distinct mechanism.

No mention that the gold-as-top-TFT-feature result (Kose 2025) directly CONTRADICTS the ~0 realized BTC-gold correlation, and the document resolves this by fiat (keep corr_gold at low end) without testing the alternative that the TFT is picking up a nonlinear/regime-conditional gold dependence that a linear Pearson correlation structurally cannot see -- i.e. the realized 0.0 might understate a real state-dependent linkage. The doc asserts 'not in the data' but a linear corr is the wrong instrument to falsify a nonlinear-model feature-importance claim.

Short BTC history / single-cycle problem is implicit but never stated as a con of using the realized anchor to discipline the ML synthesis: the trailing-5y window (n=61 months, one halving cycle) drives the most-cited corr_growth_eq 0.56 and the 57% vol floor, yet 61 monthly obs over one regime is a thin basis for a 10-15yr forward correlation/vol -- the same non-stationarity critique the doc levels at ML applies to its own empirical anchor.

Transaction-cost / capacity erosion is mentioned for the short-horizon edge but not connected to the CMA: even the one 'most defensible' cell (corr_growth_eq ~0.5) is rising specifically BECAUSE of the institutionalization the doc elsewhere says breaks the models -- i.e. the same structural break that degrades on-chain features is what lifts the equity beta, so the 'most ML-supported correlation' is itself a moving, regime-contingent target, not a stable CMA input.

new_approaches.name: ML Realized-Volatility & Vol-Term-Structure Forecasting (HAR-RV / GARCH / Hybrid)
new_approaches.description: A physical-measure (P) family that forecasts Bitcoin's realized volatility path and its mean-reverting term structure, rather than its price or fair value. Three model classes dominate: (1) HAR-RV (Corsi 2009) — an additive cascade of daily/weekly/monthly realized-volatility components estimated from high-frequency (5-min) returns that reproduces long memory parsimoniously, extended to HAR-CJ/HAR-RSV-J to separate the continuous diffusive component from discrete jumps and signed semivariances; (2) GARCH-family (GARCH/EGARCH/GJR/APARCH/score-driven) that model conditional variance with leverage and heavy-tailed innovations and imply a long-run unconditional volatility the forecast mean-reverts toward; and (3) ML/hybrid models — LSTM, CNN-LSTM, MLP, and LSTM-GARCH where GARCH parameters are fed as features to a neural net. The CMA contribution is NOT an appreciation number — these models are drift-agnostic. It is the decade-horizon VOLATILITY level and its term structure: extrapolating the mean-reverting RV process past the ~6-month option-implied horizon to a long-run unconditional sigma, decomposed into a continuous floor plus a jump contribution. The empirics support a structural ~50-60% floor that mean-reverts but does NOT converge to gold-like (~15%) levels over the horizon.
new_approaches.medium_explanation: These models forecast Bitcoin's volatility, not its price. HAR-RV regresses tomorrow's realized vol on daily, weekly and monthly RV averages built from high-frequency returns; GARCH variants model conditional variance with a long-run mean it reverts toward; ML/LSTM-GARCH hybrids learn nonlinear vol dynamics, sometimes feeding GARCH outputs as features. The key inputs are high-frequency RV, a continuous-vs-jump decomposition, leverage asymmetry, and the mean-reversion speed that sets the term structure. For a 10-15yr BTC CMA the value is the volatility cell and its shape: you extrapolate the mean-reverting RV process beyond the ~6-month option-implied limit to a long-run unconditional sigma. The honest implication is a ~50-60% decade-average floor — vol mean-reverts and has trended down with ETF institutionalization (spot dipping toward ~40% in calm 2024-25 windows), but the models give no basis to forecast convergence to gold-like levels. They are silent on appreciation and correlation, so those must be imported.
key_drivers: High-frequency realized variance/volatility (5-min returns) as the core observable, with the daily/weekly/monthly HAR cascade capturing long memory (heterogeneous market participants)

Continuous (diffusive) vs jump decomposition (bipower variation, realized semivariances) — jumps are frequent in BTC and the jump term materially improves forecasts; separating them sets the diffusive 'floor'
Mean-reversion speed and the long-run unconditional variance (GARCH alpha+beta persistence; HAR component decay) that govern how fast vol reverts and thus the term-structure slope
Leverage/asymmetry (EGARCH/GJR; HAR with signed semivariance) — BTC shows a documented inverse/atypical leverage effect
Heavy-tailed, time-varying skew/kurtosis innovations (skewed-t, score-driven) — conventional Gaussian GARCH underperforms
Model class / estimation window choice (HAR vs GARCH vs LSTM-GARCH; rolling-window length) which can swamp the model-choice effect
Institutionalization/liquidity regime (ETF flows, deeper order books) as a slow structural driver lowering the unconditional vol level over the horizon
pros: Produces the actual decade-horizon volatility number AND its mean-reverting term structure from data — the one CMA cell BTC's no-cashflow problem doesn't break — extending past the ~6-month liquid-option limit where the implied-vol (#11) approach runs out

Empirically validated and parsimonious: HAR-RV (Corsi 2009) reproduces long memory/fat tails/self-similarity with OLS and forecasts remarkably well; HAR-on-realized-variance beats daily-data GARCH, with the edge largest at short horizons

Separates continuous from jump volatility, so the 'floor' (diffusive vol) is identified apart from crash risk — directly useful for sizing and tail budgeting, and the jump term is statistically significant and improves accuracy

Honest about the floor: the literature's central message — that BTC vol mean-reverts to ~50-60%, not to gold-like levels — is exactly the discipline a credible BTC CMA needs against 'vol will converge to equities/gold' hype

ML/hybrid extensions (LSTM, CNN-LSTM) can beat GARCH out-of-sample at multiple horizons (Huang-Sangiorgi-Urquhart 2024) and ingest exogenous predictors (other cryptos, commodities, on-chain, uncertainty/sentiment)
cons: Silent on appreciation and correlation by construction — it is a second-moment model only; the entire return/CMA-mean and every correlation cell must be borrowed from another framework, so it cannot stand alone as a CMA

Horizon mismatch is severe: these are 1-day to ~1-2-month forecasting models validated in-sample; extrapolating a mean-reverting RV/GARCH process to 10-15 years is an out-of-model assumption (you are really just asserting the long-run unconditional sigma), and adjusted-R2-best models differ across horizons

ML gains are fragile and often not statistically significant: the LSTM-GARCH paper (PMC10013303) found a plain MLP best with no DM-significant edge over LSTM/GARCH, on only 6 pandemic months; 'HARd to Beat' shows rolling-window choice can dominate the model choice — easy to overfit and over-claim

Regime/structural-break risk: vol is non-stationary and has fallen sharply with ETF institutionalization (toward ~40% in calm 2024-25 windows); a model fit on the volatile 2017-2022 era can mis-set the long-run floor in either direction, and the 21M-cap/leverage feedbacks producing jumps are not stable parameters

Conditional/short-horizon vol is not the unconditional decade vol: averaging a mean-reverting process over 10-15yr that includes 60-80% drawdown episodes yields a higher number than any tranquil-period nowcast, so naive use of a low current RV understates the CMA vol

So the diffusive 'floor' may sit ~40-50% while the jump-inclusive unconditional sigma sits ~50-60%. I explicitly reject convergence to gold-like ~15% or equity-like ~18% within the horizon — no RV/GARCH/ML evidence supports a floor below realized ~57% yet, and the models' own mean reversion is to a crypto-high, not a metal-like, level.

It cannot set the mean or correlations. Pair with a return-process model (#19) for the drawdown/tail row and a separate framework for drift.

new_approaches.rich_notes:
WHAT IT IS. This family forecasts Bitcoin's physical-measure (P) volatility process and its term structure, in contrast to the Q-measure options/DVOL surface (#11), which is limited to the ~6-month liquid-option tenor and prices risk-neutral variance, and in contrast to the descriptive regime-switching/jump-diffusion family (#19), which characterizes the distributional SHAPE but does not LEARN/forecast a vol path. Three pillars: (1) HAR-RV (Corsi 2009, J. Financial Econometrics 7:174-196): an additive cascade of daily/weekly/monthly realized-volatility components, estimated by OLS on high-frequency (typically 5-min) RV, that reproduces long memory, fat tails and self-similarity with no true long-memory parameter — 'remarkably good forecasting performance.' Extensions (Andersen-Bollerslev-Diebold HAR-CJ; HAR-RSV-J with signed semivariances) split continuous diffusive vol from discrete jumps. (2) GARCH-family (EGARCH/GJR/APARCH and score-driven GAS): conditional variance with leverage and heavy-tailed innovations, implying a long-run unconditional variance the forecast reverts toward. Catania & Grassi (2022, IJF 38:878-894) show conventional GARCH performs poorly on crypto and that time-varying skewness/score-driven dynamics improve forecasts across 600+ coins. (3) ML/hybrid: Huang, Sangiorgi & Urquhart (2024, JIFMIM 97:102064) find LSTM and CNN-LSTM beat GARCH at every 1-day-to-2-month horizon, with predictors spanning other cryptos, commodities, blockchain data, Twitter uncertainty and CO2. The LSTM-GARCH paper (Garcia-Lopez et al., Computational Economics 63:4, PMC10013303) feeds eGARCH/gjrGARCH parameters into LSTMs.

KEY RELATIONSHIPS. RV is the observable; the HAR cascade encodes heterogeneous-horizon traders; jumps (bipower variation) are frequent in BTC and the jump term is statistically significant and improves accuracy; mean-reversion speed (GARCH alpha+beta persistence) sets the term-structure slope and the long-run sigma. Documented empirical facts: HAR-on-realized-variance beats daily-data GARCH, edge largest at short horizons; EGARCH/APARCH best among GARCH; BTC shows an atypical/inverse leverage effect.

HISTORICAL FIT & FAILURE MODES. The realized series decays 103% (full 2010-) -> 69% (10y) -> 57% (5y), with 2024-25 calm-window spot vol dipping toward ~40% and Kaiko reporting realized vol down ~75% from historical peaks by mid-2025 amid ETF 'strong hands.' This is exactly mean reversion to a falling long-run level — the family's core message. Failure modes are serious and I represent them faithfully: (a) HORIZON MISMATCH — every validated forecast is 1-day to ~2-months; a 10-15yr CMA is an out-of-model assertion of the unconditional sigma, and the best model differs by horizon. (b) FRAGILE ML EDGE — PMC10013303 found a plain MLP best, with NO Diebold-Mariano-significant gain over LSTM/GARCH, on only 6 pandemic months and at ~40x the compute; 'HARd to Beat' (arXiv 2406.08041) shows rolling-window choice can dominate model choice — classic overfit risk. (c) NON-STATIONARITY/REGIME BREAK — a model fit on 2017-2022 turbulence can mis-set the floor after ETF institutionalization; jump intensity is not a stable parameter. (d) CONDITIONAL != UNCONDITIONAL — a tranquil nowcast (~40%) is NOT the decade vol, because a 10-15yr window must average over recurrent 60-80% drawdown/jump episodes, mechanically lifting the unconditional sigma back toward 50-60%.

ON-RECORD MULTI-YEAR FORECASTS. Critically, this family produces essentially NO on-record multi-year vol forecasts — the academic papers stop at 1-2 months. The only decade-scale vol numbers in the broader literature come from sell-side narrative (e.g., CF Benchmarks projecting vol toward ~28% over a decade, in the SoV-TAM approach), which is NOT an RV/GARCH/ML output and which this family's mean-reversion logic actually undercuts: there is no RV/GARCH/ML evidence of a realized floor below ~57%, so a ~28% terminal is unsupported by the forecasting models themselves.

CMA BOTTOM LINE. Use this family for ONE thing: setting and defending the volatility cell. The defensible decade-average is ~50-60% (center ~55%), a mean-reverting path with a diffusive floor ~40-50% plus a jump premium, explicitly above gold (~15%) and equities (~18%). It is silent on appreciation (import the ~8-12% nominal cross-approach central) and on all correlations (import realized: growth ~+0.45, value ~+0.30, nominal FI ~+0.15, TIPS ~+0.25, gold ~0). Skeptical read: its real contribution is disciplinary — it kills the 'BTC vol will converge to gold/equity levels' claim while also refusing to over-extrapolate a calm-period 40% nowcast into the CMA.

missing_cons: DATA-WINDOW DEPENDENCE OF THE ANCHOR ITSELF: the entire 50-60% floor is pinned to a trailing-5y realized vol of 57% computed from MONTHLY returns (empirical_anchor.json: stdev(monthly)*sqrt(12), n=61 months). Monthly-sampled annualized vol is a noisier, often lower estimate than the 5-min HAR-RV the cited papers actually use; the JSON imports a monthly-sampled anchor into a high-frequency-RV framework without reconciling the sampling-frequency mismatch. This is a real methodological seam not listed in the cons.

SURVIVORSHIP / SINGLE-PATH PROBLEM: BTC has exactly ONE realized price path and ~16 years of history (only ~5y post-institutionalization). A mean-reverting unconditional sigma estimated from one non-stationary path of a possibly-non-ergodic process has no proper standard error; the JSON treats 57% as a hard floor when it is a single-draw point estimate. Con #4 gestures at regime risk but not at the n=1-path / non-ergodicity problem.

NO TREATMENT OF VOL-OF-VOL TERM STRUCTURE UNCERTAINTY: the JSON asserts a diffusive floor ~40-50% plus jump premium ~50-60% but provides no cited decomposition magnitude - the continuous-vs-jump SPLIT ratio for BTC is not quantified from any cited paper, so the '40-50 floor / 50-60 with jumps' band is asserted, not sourced.

ASYMMETRIC-DECLINE OMISSION: the JSON argues calm nowcasts understate decade vol (true), but does not symmetrically consider that ETF-era structural liquidity could be a genuine regime SHIFT (not mean-reversion), in which case anchoring at 57% OVERstates forward vol. It leans one direction (vol-back-up) more than the other, which is defensible but one-sided given its own 'institutionalization lowers unconditional level' driver.

new_approaches.name: Bayesian Model-Averaging / Dynamic Model Averaging under Model & Parameter Instability
new_approaches.description: A META-method, not a standalone valuation lens. Rather than committing to one predictor (scarcity, money supply, network value, gold-TAM), it maintains an ensemble of candidate forecasting models and weights each by its posterior/forecast probability, letting BOTH the coefficients (parameter instability) and the active model set (model uncertainty) vary over time. The canonical implementations are Dynamic Model Averaging (DMA) — Raftery-style recursive averaging over a large bank of dynamic linear / TVP models with forgetting factors (Catania, Grassi & Ravazzolo 2019; Bianchi, Guidolin & Pedio 2023) — and shrinkage Mallows model averaging on an ARDL predictor set (Xiao & Sun 2020). The output is a model-uncertainty-aware predictive density: a combined point forecast AND honestly wide predictive intervals that widen further when models disagree. Its headline empirical result is that the optimal predictor set for crypto is genuinely time-varying — preferences rotate across regimes and parameters are highly unstable — which is exactly why no single lens dominates and why blending is the right epistemics for an asset whose drivers demonstrably rotate. Critically, the method itself produces NO long-horizon expected return: every academic application is short-horizon (1-day to ~180-day), and the findings show predictability is concentrated in investor attention, not in stock factors, gold, or supply metrics. A 10-15yr CMA does not fall out of DMA/BMA at all; the contribution is to discipline the OTHER approaches' point estimates into a probability-weighted central case with wide intervals.
new_approaches.medium_explanation: BMA/DMA is the ensemble layer that sits ON TOP of the other valuation lenses. Instead of betting on one model (S2F, Metcalfe, M2-elasticity, gold-TAM), it runs many candidate predictive models in parallel and weights each by its recent forecast performance, with forgetting factors that let both the weights and the regression coefficients drift over time. Two things move: which model is "best" (model uncertainty) and what its coefficients are (parameter instability). The deliverable is a combined predictive density — a central forecast plus genuinely wide intervals that widen when the models disagree. The signature academic finding (Catania-Grassi-Ravazzolo 2019; Bianchi-Guidolin-Pedio 2023) is that the optimal predictor set ROTATES across regimes and parameters are highly unstable, which directly justifies blending many lenses rather than committing to one. For a 10-15yr BTC CMA the honest implication is humbling: DMA/BMA produces no long-horizon edge — its predictability is short-horizon (≤180 days) and concentrated in investor attention, with stock factors, gold, and supply metrics NOT systematic predictors. It argues for a wide-interval, probability-weighted central case, not a precise number.
key_drivers: Model-probability weights: each candidate model weighted by its recursive predictive likelihood (posterior model probability), updated every period
Forgetting factors (alpha for model weights, lambda for coefficients): control how fast the ensemble discards stale models/parameters — the knobs that operationalize 'instability'
Time-varying coefficients (TVP): regression betas drift, so a predictor's loading can switch sign/magnitude across regimes (Bianchi-Guidolin-Pedio: SMB mean slope ~0.043 but unstable)

The candidate predictor set itself: in the crypto applications ~17 predictors spanning market risk factors (SMB, equity), crypto-specific (volume, realized vol, hashrate/supply), sentiment/attention (Google search), gold spot, FX, VIX
Investor attention / search interest: the empirically DOMINANT time-varying predictor in the academic results, the one whose inclusion probability stays elevated
Predictive-interval width: a direct function of cross-model disagreement — the epistemic output that distinguishes this approach
Horizon: predictability concentrated at 1-day to ~180-day; effects decay to near-zero beyond ~180 days (a hard constraint on any long-horizon use)
pros: Correct epistemics for a rotating-driver asset: explicitly models model uncertainty AND parameter instability instead of falsely committing to one lens — its own headline result (optimal predictor set is time-varying) is the strongest single justification in the literature for blending the 20 other approaches rather than picking one

Produces honest, wide predictive intervals: the combined density widens precisely when candidate models disagree, which is the right risk representation for BTC's fat-tailed, regime-shifting return distribution — and a built-in antidote to the false precision of S2F/Metcalfe/power-law point targets

Peer-reviewed and falsifiable: Catania-Grassi-Ravazzolo (Int. J. Forecasting), Bianchi-Guidolin-Pedio (Eur. J. Finance), Xiao-Sun (JRFM) use standard out-of-sample point/density scoring (log scores, directional accuracy, MCS) — real statistical machinery, not curve-fitting a price level

Empirically beats single models and naive benchmarks out-of-sample at short horizons (statistically significant point-forecast gains from univariate combinations; density gains from multivariate selection), and combinations support profitable directional strategies — genuine, if modest, predictive content

Disciplines hype: by letting weights flow to whichever model is currently forecasting well, it automatically down-weights a lens (e.g. S2F) when it breaks down, rather than locking in a discredited prior
Naturally accommodates appreciation DECAY and regime change because nothing is held constant — coefficients and model identity both adapt
cons: Produces NO long-horizon expected return. Every academic DMA/BMA crypto application is short-horizon (1-day to ~180-day); effects decay to near-zero beyond ~180 days. Using it for a 10-15yr CMA is a category error — the method is a tactical, recursive forecaster, not a structural valuation model. It can discipline the OTHER lenses but cannot itself output a decade-ahead appreciation number.

Garbage-in still applies: BMA/DMA averages over a fixed CANDIDATE SET. If every candidate is a short-horizon, spurious-cointegration cousin (S2F, naive Metcalfe), averaging them yields a well-calibrated average of bad models — the ensemble cannot manufacture a structural anchor none of its members possess

The signature finding is deflationary for fundamental CMA: Bianchi-Guidolin-Pedio find crypto is NOT systematically predicted by stock-market factors, precious-metal commodities (gold), or supply factors — only by time-varying investor attention. This UNDERCUTS the gold-TAM/digital-gold and scarcity/supply lenses the CMA committee might want to lean on, and locates the only edge in a behavioral, non-fundamental, non-persistent driver

Forgetting-factor and prior choices are tuning knobs that materially move results; the method has many researcher degrees of freedom, and the short, bull-dominated sample (2014-2021) limits how stable the estimated instability itself is

Silent on cross-asset correlations and volatility magnitude as direct outputs — it forecasts the return series; the covariance vector vs equities/FI/TIPS/gold must be imported from realized data or another framework

Computationally and interpretively heavy relative to its modest, short-horizon payoff; 'the model changes every period' is honest but offers a portfolio committee little to anchor a 10-15yr assumption on

new_approaches.rich_notes:
WHAT IT IS. Bayesian Model Averaging (BMA) and its dynamic cousin Dynamic Model Averaging (DMA, Raftery et al. 2010) are META-methods for forecasting under uncertainty about WHICH model is right and about WHETHER its coefficients are stable. You specify a bank of candidate predictive models (in crypto applications, dynamic linear / TVP regressions and VARs on a predictor set), and each period you weight each model by its recursive predictive likelihood. Two forgetting factors govern adaptivity: alpha discounts stale model weights, lambda discounts stale coefficient information. The output is a combined predictive DENSITY — a point forecast plus intervals that mechanically widen when the constituent models disagree. This is the right epistemic object for an asset whose drivers demonstrably rotate.

THE THREE CANONICAL SOURCES. (1) Catania, Grassi & Ravazzolo (2019, Int. J. Forecasting 35(2):485-501) apply DMA over a large set of univariate dynamic linear models and multivariate VARs with time variation to BTC, LTC, XRP, ETH. Headline: 'parameter instability is high and model preferences change over time' across all four coins; static models forecast poorly. They document statistically significant out-of-sample POINT gains from univariate combinations, DENSITY gains from multivariate selection, and 'sizable directional predictability' enough to support profitable strategies. (2) Bianchi, Guidolin & Pedio (2023, Eur. J. Finance 29(6):583-611; SSRN 3609949) run DMA with time-varying coefficients over 17 predictors spanning market risk factors (SMB, equity), crypto-specific variables, sentiment/attention, gold spot, and FX. Their decisive result: crypto returns are NOT systematically predicted by stock-market factors, precious-metal commodities, or supply factors — only by a 'time-varying but significant exposure to investors' attention.' Of 17 predictors, only a handful (~6) have 90% DMA-coefficient bands excluding zero; SMB's mean slope is ~0.043 but unstable. (3) Xiao & Sun (2020, JRFM 13(11):278) use shrinkage Mallows model averaging (SMMA) on an ARDL set and find crypto returns sensitive to financial-market volatility, gold prices, and FX, with SMMA beating penalized single-model estimators out-of-sample.

HISTORICAL FIT & FAILURE MODES. The method fits the data's CHARACTER honestly — it is built to detect instability and it finds plenty. But three caveats gut its use as a CMA engine. First, HORIZON: every application is short (1-day to ~180-day); a related Bayesian-local-projection result finds predictor effects largely vanish beyond ~180 days. There is simply no academic DMA/BMA BTC return forecast at a 10-15yr horizon — extrapolating one would be fabrication. Second, GARBAGE-IN: BMA averages over a fixed candidate set; if all members are short-horizon spurious-cointegration cousins, the average is a well-calibrated average of weak models. The method down-weights a broken lens (it would have shed S2F post-2021) but cannot create a structural anchor none of its members hold. Third, the SIGNATURE FINDING is deflationary: the only robust edge is investor attention — a behavioral, non-fundamental, non-persistent driver — while gold, equity factors, and supply metrics rotate in and out. The two papers even CONFLICT on gold (Xiao-Sun: in-sample relevant; Bianchi-Guidolin-Pedio: not a systematic predictor), which is itself the model-instability verdict and a direct caution against leaning the CMA on a stable BTC-gold linkage.

ON-RECORD MULTI-YEAR FORECASTS PRODUCED THIS WAY. None. This is important and worth stating plainly: no BMA/DMA crypto study publishes a multi-year point appreciation, real return, or correlation matrix. The literature publishes out-of-sample log scores, directional-accuracy ratios, MCS-set membership, and Value-at-Risk density evaluations at daily-to-semiannual horizons. Any 10-15yr number attributed to 'the model-averaging approach' is necessarily a synthesis overlay, not a cited output — which is why every cited cell here is 'n/a (source silent).'

HOW IT SHOULD BE USED IN THE CMA. Not as a 21st competing point estimate, but as the AGGREGATION LAYER and the epistemic conscience for the other 20. Its empirical message — the optimal predictor set is time-varying — is the single strongest in-literature justification for blending lenses and for attaching WIDE predictive intervals to the BTC CMA rather than a false-precision point. My synthesized central case (~9-10% nominal, ~6.5% real, vol ~57%, gold corr ~0.05-0.10) is exactly that: a probability-weighted average of the disciplined-decay estimates of the credible structural lenses, with the broken bull models (S2F/power-law) down-weighted as DMA would shed them, and intervals deliberately wide (90% band roughly -10% to +30%/yr nominal) to honor the model disagreement the method exists to quantify. The correlations are imported from realized data because the framework is silent on them. The deepest honest takeaway: the right answer for BTC is not a number but a probability-weighted distribution with fat tails — and this approach is the only one in the set whose entire purpose is to say so.

issues: CITATION INTEGRITY: PASS. All three canonical papers verified for exact title, authors, journal, volume/issue/pages, and headline finding. Catania-Grassi-Ravazzolo (2019, IJF 35(2):485-501), Bianchi-Guidolin-Pedio (2023, EJF 29(6):583-611, SSRN 3609949), Xiao-Sun (2020, JRFM 13(11):278). The B-G-P headline ('crypto NOT systematically predicted by stock-market factors, precious-metal commodities, or supply factors; only time-varying investor attention') is verbatim-accurate. The 4th source (RePEc WP 0063) is the legitimate working-paper version of source 1, not a separate finding. No fabricated or mis-attributed citations.

EMPIRICAL ANCHORS: PASS. Every realized figure the synthesis leans on is reproduced exactly from the scripted empirical_anchor.json: decay 142.2%/65.5%/17.0% (full/10y/5y), vol 57.5% (5y), gold corr -0.011 (full)/+0.045 (5y), and realized correlations growth 0.564, value 0.367, FI 0.192, TIPS 0.301. These are correctly transcribed, not invented.

UNVERIFIABLE GRANULAR CLAIMS stated with false specificity: '~17 predictors', '~6 with 90% DMA bands excluding zero', 'SMB mean slope ~0.043 (median ~0.045)', and the '~180-day' decay horizon could NOT be confirmed from any accessible source (paywalled; not in any snippet). They are plausible and the writeup hedges them, but presenting a decimal coefficient (0.043) and a specific predictor count without a retrievable quote is the kind of precision that should be flagged. The ~180-day horizon in particular is attributed to 'a related Bayesian-local-projection result' that is never cited in representative_sources — that is an uncited load-bearing claim.

DECAY-EXTRAPOLATION TENSION (the central quantitative weakness): the synthesized ~9-10% nominal central case sits ABOVE a naive continued-decay extrapolation. Window-over-window appreciation ratios are 0.46 (full->10y) and 0.26 (10y->5y); applying 0.26-0.46 to the 17% 5y base implies a NEXT-window ~4.4-7.8%/yr (midpoint ~6.1%). The writeup's 9-10% is defensible ONLY because it reframes as a blend of structural lenses rather than pure decay extrapolation and asserts maturation slows the decay rate. But it claims to 'sit below the trailing-5y 17% because every credible member forecasts continued decay' while landing well above what the decay trajectory itself implies. That is a soft internal tension: the number is decay-aware but decay-light.

VOL FLOOR is a judgment dressed as a constraint. Vol has itself decayed (102.9%->68.7%->57.5%; ratios 0.67, 0.84). Holding the 10-15yr assumption flat AT the 57% floor refuses the very compression the realized series shows. Over a 10-15yr maturation horizon, continued drift toward 45-55% is at least as defensible as a hard 57% floor. The writeup's stated rationale ('sub-2yr ETF sample does not yet evidence a sustained floor below realized') is reasonable but one-sided — it uses 'no evidence of lower floor yet' to justify the higher number, which is conservative-on-vol-being-high, i.e. mildly bearish framing, not neutral.

META-METHOD FRAMING: CORRECT and unusually honest. The core epistemic claim — DMA/BMA produces NO native long-horizon return, every application is 1-day to ~180-day, so all 10-15yr cells are explicitly judgment overlays with 'n/a (source silent)' in cited_outputs — is accurate and properly disclaimed. This is the right way to represent a tactical forecaster as an aggregation/epistemics layer rather than a 21st point estimate. No overstatement here.

GOLD HANDLING: CORRECT. Synthesized gold corr 0.05-0.10 sits just above realized +0.045 (5y) but within noise, and the writeup explicitly rejects a high 'digital-gold' co-movement, correctly invoking the B-G-P 'precious metals not a systematic predictor' result and the Xiao-Sun/B-G-P conflict as itself the instability verdict. This is the strongest, best-supported part of the synthesis and is consistent with the ~0 realized correlation.

Either add the specific citation or downgrade to 'short-horizon (1-day to ~180-day in the cited applications)' without the extrapolation-decay claim.", "Mark the specific coefficient values ('SMB mean slope ~0.043 (median ~0.045)', '~17 predictors', '~6 of 17 with bands excluding zero') as 'per [B-G-P], approximate from text' or attach the table/page, since they cannot be retrieved from any open source and are stated with decimal precision.", "Reconcile the appreciation logic: the synthesized 9-10% nominal is ABOVE a naive continued-decay extrapolation of the realized 142/65/17 trajectory (~4.4-7.8% for the next window). Being below 17% is a weak bar when the trend points to single digits.", "The vol assumption should present 57% as the TOP of a defensible band, not a floor — realized vol is in a clear multi-window downtrend, so a 10-15yr central case of ~50-57% (not a flat 57% floor) better honors the data the method exists to track.", "Note in cons that the wide 90% band (-10% to +30%/yr nominal) is itself an unmodeled judgment — DMA/BMA at ≤180 days cannot calibrate a 10-15yr annualized interval, so the interval width is asserted, not derived. The writeup half-admits this ('these are NOT outputs of BMA/DMA') but the specific -10/+30 bounds deserve the same 'reasoned overlay' flag as the point estimate."]
overstated_pros: 'Empirically beats single models and naive benchmarks out-of-sample' — true but the magnitude is modest and SHORT-HORIZON only; the pro as written ('genuine, if modest, predictive content') is honest, but it sits adjacent to synthesized 10-15yr numbers and a careless reader will transfer the OOS win to the long horizon, which the papers do not support.

'Disciplines hype... automatically down-weights a lens (e.g. S2F) when it breaks down' — asserted as a property the method WOULD have shown, not a documented result. None of the three cited papers includes S2F, Metcalfe, or power-law as candidate models, so 'DMA would have shed S2F post-2021' is a hypothetical, not an empirical finding. It is reasonable intuition but is presented with more authority than the evidence carries.

The synthesized correlations (growth 0.50, value 0.35, FI 0.20, TIPS 0.25) are imported wholesale from trailing-5y realized while the method's OWN finding is that equity-factor loadings are intermittent/unstable — so crediting a forward 0.50 growth correlation leans on realized data the method says is non-stationary. The writeup acknowledges this ('regime-dependent and unstable') but still centers the numbers on the single most equity-correlated 5y window, the post-2021 risk-on regime, which likely overstates the structural equity beta.
missing_cons: Single-decision-maker survivorship in the candidate set is unaddressed: the three papers cover only BTC/LTC/XRP/ETH over ~2014-2021, a bull-dominated, small-N, highly correlated panel. The 'optimal predictor set rotates' finding may be partly an artifact of a short noisy sample; the con list mentions the sample is 'short, bull-dominated' for tuning knobs but does NOT flag that the headline rotation result itself may not replicate out of that sample.

No con notes that investor-attention (Google Trends) as 'the only systematic predictor' is mechanically endogenous/contemporaneous with price (attention spikes BECAUSE price moved), so its predictive value is fragile and arguably look-ahead-contaminated at short lags — a standard critique of the attention-predictability literature that would further weaken any reliance on the one driver the method elevates.

The synthesis uses DMA's 'down-weight broken models' logic to justify shedding S2F/power-law, but does not flag the symmetric risk: BMA also down-weights a STRUCTURALLY-correct-but-currently-cold lens (e.g., a monetary-substitution model in a risk-off year), so the aggregation layer can amplify recency/momentum bias in exactly the regime-shift moments where the long-horizon CMA most needs a stable anchor. This is a real con of using a tactical recency-weighted averager as the epistemic spine of a decade-ahead assumption.

Transaction-cost / net-of-cost caveat: the 'profitable directional strategies' pro is gross; crypto trading/financing costs and the strategies' turnover are not discussed, and the realized edge can vanish net of costs — relevant before citing 'profitable' as evidence of genuine predictive content.

new_approaches.name: Dynamic-Factor / Mixed-Frequency Macro Nowcasting (DFM + MIDAS, ML-augmented)
new_approaches.description: This approach imports the macro-nowcasting toolkit (mixed-frequency dynamic factor models with a Kalman-filter state-space representation, and/or MIDAS regressions) to model Bitcoin as a high-beta loading on a small set of common latent macro/liquidity factors extracted from many ragged-edge, different-frequency series: global M2/broad money (monthly, lagged), financial-conditions and financial-stress indices (weekly/daily), real rates and the dollar (daily), ISM/PMI and global real economic activity (monthly), realized equity vol, etc. A DFM compresses this high-dimensional, asynchronously-released panel into one or two orthogonal factors (a 'global liquidity / risk-capital' factor and a 'real-activity' factor); the Kalman filter handles the ragged edge (some series report through last week, others lag two months) and missing data natively. Bitcoin's return (or volatility, in the GARCH-MIDAS variant) is then projected onto those factors, yielding a time-varying factor loading and a term structure of macro sensitivity. To produce a 10-15yr CMA, you forecast the factors forward under their estimated (mean-reverting) AR/VAR dynamics, multiply by BTC's loading, and annualize — appreciation decay is imposed automatically because the latent factors revert to their unconditional means and BTC's elevated loading is assumed to compress as the asset institutionalizes. It is distinct from static factor regression (#10) and single-variable M2 cointegration (#7) precisely because it solves the data-flow/mixed-frequency/ragged-edge problem none of the other 20 touch, and because decay is endogenous to the factor dynamics rather than hand-imposed.
new_approaches.medium_explanation: Borrowed from central-bank GDP nowcasting (IMF, BBVA/Camacho-Domenech), this method extracts one or two common latent factors — chiefly a global-liquidity/risk-capital factor and a real-activity factor — from a large panel of mixed-frequency macro and financial series using a Kalman-filter state-space DFM that handles ragged-edge data (series that report on different lags) natively. Bitcoin's return is regressed onto these factors to estimate its loading and a term structure of macro sensitivity; MIDAS weighting links high-frequency conditions to lower-frequency BTC aggregates without parameter proliferation. A 10-15yr CMA falls out by forecasting the factors forward under their estimated mean-reverting AR/VAR dynamics and multiplying by a decaying BTC loading. The implied appreciation is trend money/liquidity growth times BTC's (compressing) beta. The crucial caveat: DFMs are nowcasting/short-horizon tools — beyond ~4-8 quarters their forecasts collapse to the unconditional factor mean (a random walk with drift), so the framework is far stronger on volatility-regime and correlation structure than on a precise decade-ahead point return.
key_drivers: Global liquidity / broad-money factor (global M2, central-bank balance sheets, dollar funding) — the dominant common factor BTC loads on
Financial-conditions / financial-stress factor (NFCI, GFSI, credit spreads, equity realized vol) — GARCH-MIDAS finds Global Financial Stress Index a top long-term BTC-vol driver
Real-activity factor (ISM/PMI, Global Real Economic Activity / Kilian index, industrial production) — best single long-term BTC-volatility predictor in the crypto MIDAS literature
Real rates and the dollar (DXY, 10y TIPS yield) as the discount-rate / risk-appetite channel for a no-cashflow asset
BTC's time-varying factor loading (beta to the liquidity factor) and its assumed secular compression as the asset institutionalizes
Factor AR/VAR persistence and unconditional means — the mean-reversion that mechanically imposes appreciation decay at long horizons
Ragged-edge data-flow handling (Kalman filter) — the technical feature that lets daily/weekly/monthly series with different release lags enter one model
MIDAS lag-polynomial weights linking high-frequency macro conditions to lower-frequency BTC return/vol aggregates
pros: Solves the mixed-frequency / ragged-edge data-flow problem no other BTC-CMA approach addresses: the Kalman filter ingests daily, weekly and monthly series with different release lags into one coherent state-space, so the factor estimate uses all information actually available at each date

Decay is endogenous, not hand-imposed: because the latent factors revert to their unconditional means under estimated AR/VAR dynamics, BTC's projected appreciation mechanically slows at long horizons — the correct qualitative shape for a maturing-asset CMA, derived rather than asserted

Grounded in a genuinely strong empirical regularity: BTC moves with global liquidity ~83% of 12-month windows (higher than any major asset class per Alden/Callahan), and the crypto GARCH-MIDAS literature shows real-activity and financial-stress factors significantly improve out-of-sample BTC volatility forecasts vs plain GARCH, especially in bear markets

Methodologically battle-tested: DFM/MIDAS nowcasting is the workhorse at the Fed, ECB, IMF and BBVA for GDP, with decades of validation, dimension-reduction discipline, and ML-augmented scalable variants (IMF WP/2022/052) — far more rigorous plumbing than S2F/Metcalfe curve-fits

Naturally produces the full CMA object: not just a point return but a factor-implied volatility regime (long-term GARCH-MIDAS component) and a correlation structure (BTC and equities co-load on the same liquidity factor), which most level-only BTC models cannot populate
Honest about uncertainty: the state-space form yields proper forecast-error bands and decomposes each release's contribution, so the analyst sees how fragile the long-horizon estimate is
cons: Fatal horizon mismatch: DFMs are nowcasting / very-short-horizon tools. Beyond ~4-8 quarters their forecasts collapse to the unconditional factor mean — a random walk with drift — so a 10-15yr BTC return is essentially just 'trend liquidity growth times an assumed beta', and the elaborate factor machinery adds almost no information at that horizon over a naive debasement assumption

BTC's factor loading is unstable and regime-dependent: the beta to liquidity spiked post-2020, the BTC-equity correlation jumped in the ETF era, and the relationship 'on changes' (vs trend) is far weaker than the headline ~0.83 directional or ~0.94 levels correlation — which is itself partly the spurious-trend artifact that plagues the M2 cointegration approach (#7)

Short BTC history (~15 years, ~3-4 liquidity cycles) is grossly insufficient to identify factor dynamics, the loading's secular decay path, or the unconditional means the long-horizon forecast reverts to — the very parameters that drive the CMA are the least well estimated

The crypto MIDAS literature is almost entirely about VOLATILITY, not expected RETURN: GARCH-MIDAS papers (Conrad-Custovic-Ghysels; Walther et al.) forecast BTC vol well but publish no multi-year return CMA, so the appreciation number is an analyst extension the peer-reviewed work does not actually deliver

ML augmentation (random forests, elastic-net preselection) improves nowcast accuracy but worsens interpretability and overfits a tiny sample at long horizons; it cannot manufacture signal that isn't in ~180 monthly observations

Liquidity / real-activity factors are themselves hard to forecast 10-15 years out — central-bank balance sheets, fiscal dominance and the dollar regime are deeply uncertain — so the 'exogenous' driver feeding the CMA is no more knowable than BTC itself

Says nothing structural about catastrophic BTC-specific tail risk (protocol failure, regulatory ban); the factor model prices BTC as a macro beta and ignores idiosyncratic left-tail mass, overstating the central forward return

cited_outputs.appreciation_nominal: n/a (source silent) as a DFM/MIDAS output. The only published forward CMA numbers in this adjacent family come from CF Benchmarks (which folds a macro-liquidity/global-M2 overlay into a three-model framework) and from the Alden/Callahan liquidity-barometer work (1-2yr horizon). Both are reported above but flagged as either non-academic or horizon-mismatched relative to a pure 10-15yr DFM projection.
cited_outputs.horizon: Academic mixed-frequency crypto work: short-horizon (daily/weekly/monthly volatility). CF Benchmarks: 10yr (to 2035). Alden/Callahan: 1-2yr. No source publishes a clean 10-15yr return from a pure DFM/MIDAS.

synthesized_outputs.appreciation_nominal: ~8-12%/yr (judgment, not a computed DFM stat). Under the factor logic, long-run BTC appreciation = trend global-liquidity/money growth (~6-8%/yr) times BTC's loading on the liquidity factor, with that loading assumed to compress from its elevated post-2020 level toward a gold-like store-of-value beta as the asset institutionalizes. Because the latent factors mean-revert and the loading decays, the framework forces appreciation DOWN the realized decay path (142%->65%->17%/yr), landing near nominal-money-growth plus a shrinking monetization premium. I deliberately reject the practitioner short-horizon ~30-56%/yr figures as horizon-mismatched (1-2yr liquidity-cycle calls, not a decade CMA).
synthesized_outputs.appreciation_real: ~5-9%/yr real (subtracting ~2.5-3% long-run US inflation). The liquidity-factor framing makes BTC partly a debasement claim, so it should roughly preserve purchasing power plus a modest, decaying adoption premium.
synthesized_outputs.volatility: ~50-60%/yr (judgment). The GARCH-MIDAS long-term component is real and informative, but the academic floor is anchored to realized trailing-5y ~57%; I do NOT credit CF Benchmarks' optimistic ~28% terminal because a 10-15yr window still contains 60-80% drawdowns and the sub-2yr ETF sample shows no durable compression below realized. Vol stays ~3x equities, drifting toward the low-50s only late in the horizon.
synthesized_outputs.corr_growth_eq: +0.40 to +0.55 (judgment). The single strongest structural prediction of this framework: BTC and growth/tech equities co-load on the same global-liquidity/risk-capital factor, so the correlation is meaningfully positive and likely RISES with institutionalization. I discount CF Benchmarks' 0.15 projection as aspirational; realized trailing-5y is 0.56.
synthesized_outputs.corr_value_eq: +0.25 to +0.40 (judgment). Lower than growth-equity correlation - value equities share less of the liquidity/duration beta; tracks realized trailing-5y ~0.37.
synthesized_outputs.corr_fi_nominal: +0.10 to +0.25 (judgment). Positive via the shared rate/liquidity factor; the marginal institutional holder's rate-sensitivity lifts this modestly over the horizon (realized trailing-5y 0.19; CF Benchmarks projects rising to 0.22).
synthesized_outputs.corr_tips: +0.20 to +0.35 (judgment). Real rates are an explicit factor in the panel and a no-cashflow asset's discount rate, so BTC carries genuine real-rate sensitivity - slightly above nominal FI; realized trailing-5y 0.30.
synthesized_outputs.corr_gold: ~0.0-0.15 (judgment). Here the factor framework is HONEST where the digital-gold narratives are not: BTC and gold load only weakly on a common factor, and realized BTC-gold correlation is ~0 (full -0.01, 5y +0.045). A liquidity/risk-asset factor model implies BTC co-moves far more with equities than with gold, so I keep gold correlation at the bottom of the band and explicitly reject any structural gold-substitution co-movement - the data and the model agree it isn't there.
synthesized_outputs.notes: Central synthesized view: ~8-12% nominal / ~5-9% real, vol ~50-60%, equity correlation ~0.40-0.55 (the model's STRONGEST and most defensible claim, since BTC and equities share the liquidity factor), gold correlation ~0. The framework's honest contribution to a BTC CMA is the correlation/volatility structure, not the point return - at a 10-15yr horizon the return collapses to trend-liquidity-growth-times-decaying-beta and is no more informative than a naive debasement assumption. Consistent with the cross-approach central of ~8-12% nominal / 5-9% real, vol ~50-60%, gold corr ~0-0.15.

new_approaches.rich_notes:
METHODOLOGY. This approach lifts the central-bank GDP-nowcasting stack and points it at Bitcoin. The core object is a mixed-frequency dynamic factor model in state-space form: a large panel of macro/financial indicators (global M2 and central-bank balance sheets monthly; financial-conditions/stress indices and equity realized vol weekly/daily; ISM/PMI and Global Real Economic Activity monthly; real rates and the dollar daily) is assumed to be driven by a small number of common latent factors plus idiosyncratic noise. A Kalman filter estimates the factors and — critically — handles the 'ragged edge': at any date some series have reported through last week while others lag two months, and the filter treats the gaps as missing states rather than discarding data (Camacho-Domenech 2019; IMF WP/2022/052). MIDAS is the partial-model cousin: instead of compressing to factors, it links a high-frequency regressor to a lower-frequency target through a parsimonious lag polynomial (Almon/Beta weights), avoiding parameter proliferation. ML-augmented variants (IMF 2022; factor-augmented sparse MIDAS, arXiv 2306.13362) add elastic-net preselection or random forests to pick predictors and capture nonlinearity, improving nowcast accuracy especially around COVID. For BTC you extract a 'global liquidity / risk-capital' factor and a 'real-activity' factor, regress BTC return (DFM) or BTC volatility (GARCH-MIDAS) onto them, and read off a time-varying loading and a term structure of macro sensitivity.

KEY RELATIONSHIPS. The empirical anchor is strong and genuinely distinguishes this from numerology: Callahan/Alden (2024) find BTC moves with global liquidity ~83% of 12-month windows and ~74% of 6-month windows, with a ~0.94 levels correlation May-2013..Jul-2024 — higher directional consistency than any major asset class. On the volatility side the peer-reviewed crypto MIDAS work is unusually clean: Conrad, Custovic & Ghysels (2018) and Walther, Klein & Bouri (2019) both find that a long-term volatility component driven by Global Real Economic Activity (Kilian index) and the Global Financial Stress Index dominates, that S&P 500 realized vol loads negatively on long-term BTC vol, and that these mixed-frequency specifications beat plain GARCH out-of-sample, especially in bear markets.

HISTORICAL FIT & FAILURE MODES. The decisive caveat is horizon. DFM/MIDAS are nowcasting and very-short-horizon forecasting tools; their comparative advantage is squeezing today's release flow into a current-quarter estimate. At long horizons the latent factors revert to their unconditional means under the estimated AR/VAR dynamics, so the multi-year forecast collapses to a random walk with drift — i.e., 'trend liquidity growth times beta'. The elaborate ragged-edge machinery that makes the nowcast superb adds essentially nothing to a 10-15yr point return. Worse, the parameters that DO drive a decade CMA — BTC's secular loading-decay path and the factors' unconditional means — are the least identifiable from ~15 years and only 3-4 liquidity cycles. The headline 0.94 levels correlation is partly the same spurious-trend artifact that undermines the M2-cointegration approach (#7): on contemporaneous CHANGES the relationship weakens markedly. And the loading is regime-unstable — it spiked post-2020 and the BTC-equity correlation jumped in the ETF era — so projecting it forward is guesswork dressed in a Kalman filter. ML augmentation cannot rescue this; it overfits a tiny sample at long horizons.

ON-RECORD MULTI-YEAR FORECASTS PRODUCED THIS WAY. Pure peer-reviewed DFM/MIDAS work on BTC publishes volatility forecasts, NOT a multi-year return CMA — so a 10-15yr appreciation number is an analyst extension the literature does not itself deliver (an honesty point worth flagging). The closest on-record liquidity-factor RETURN projections are practitioner and explicitly short-horizon: Alden/Callahan's probability-weighted global-liquidity model implies ~+56% over 1yr (~$110k) and ~+104% over 2yr (~$144k) — 1-2yr liquidity-cycle calls, not a decade assumption. CF Benchmarks' CMA, which folds a macro-liquidity (global-M2 risk-capital) overlay into a three-model framework, is the nearest thing to a published forward CMA in this family: base case 30.1%/yr to a $1.42M 2035 target, vol declining toward ~28%, equity correlation 0.52->0.15, bonds 0.14->0.22, gold ~0.06 unchanged. I treat the 30.1% as over-optimistic (it leans on aggressive terminal adoption, not on factor mean-reversion) and the ~0.15 equity correlation as aspirational — the factor logic actually predicts equity correlation stays meaningfully positive because BTC and equities share the liquidity factor. The defensible synthesized read: ~8-12% nominal / ~5-9% real, vol ~50-60%, equity correlation ~0.40-0.55 and structurally the model's strongest claim, gold correlation ~0 — where this framework is admirably honest that BTC is a liquidity-driven risk asset, not digital gold.

issues: CITATION ERROR (significant): representative_sources lists IMF WP/2022/052 authors as 'Dawn Holland, Iulia Ruxandra Teodoru, et al.' The actual authors are Dauphin, Dybczak, Maneely, Taheri Sanjani, Suphaphiphat, Wang & Zhang. The WP number, title and year are correct, but the named authors belong to a different IMF nowcasting paper. Wrong attribution on a flagship 'methodologically battle-tested' citation.

CITATION ERROR (moderate): The specific volatility drivers are misattributed across the two GARCH-MIDAS papers. Conrad-Custovic-Ghysels (2018) actually use the BALTIC DRY INDEX as their global-activity proxy (plus S&P 500 realized vol = negative, S&P VRP = positive). The 'Global Real Economic Activity / Kilian index' as single best long-term BTC-vol driver is the WALTHER-KLEIN-BOURI (2019) finding, not Conrad's. The doc repeatedly credits 'Conrad et al.' with the Kilian-index result and pairs both papers with the 'Global Financial Stress Index,' which is not Conrad's variable. The S&P-500-negative-loading claim IS correctly Conrad. Net: the literature is real and the qualitative story (real-activity + stress drive long-term BTC vol) holds, but the per-paper variable assignments are scrambled.

MISATTRIBUTED FORECAST (moderate): The '~+56% over 1yr (~$110k) and ~+104% over 2yr (~$144k)' figures are attributed to Alden/Callahan 'Bitcoin: A Global Liquidity Barometer.' That article contains NO probability-weighted return/price forecast at any horizon — it only reports directional-alignment stats (83%/74%) and correlations (0.94 overall, 0.51 rolling-12m, 0.36 rolling-6m). The +56%/+104% numbers circulate in secondary commentary loosely tied to the liquidity model, not in the cited source. The doc presents them as on-record Alden/Callahan outputs. The doc DOES correctly reject these as horizon-mismatched, which softens the impact, but the sourcing is wrong.

MINOR DISCREPANCY: doc says CF Benchmarks projects gold corr '~0.06 current and ~0.06 projected (unchanged)'. Source: current 0.06, projected ~0.00 ('remains near zero'). Both round to ~0 so the synthesized gold-corr conclusion is unaffected, but 'unchanged at 0.06' is not what CF Benchmarks states.

FRAMING: the '~0.94 levels correlation' (Alden/Callahan) is labeled correctly as a levels/price correlation and the cons section properly flags it as a likely spurious-trend artifact (rolling 12m is only 0.51, 6m 0.36). This is handled honestly — not an error, but readers should note the headline 0.94 is a price-level number, not a returns/changes correlation.

OVERSTATED-PRO RISK: pro #3 says BTC moves with global liquidity '~83% of 12-month windows... higher than any major asset class per Alden/Callahan'. The 83% is correct and sourced, but it measures DIRECTIONAL co-movement of price LEVELS with a trending liquidity series — a weak bar that any persistently-uptrending asset clears. It is not evidence of a stable exploitable factor loading, and the cons section's own admission ('on changes the relationship weakens markedly') contradicts the strength implied by the pro. The pro and con are in tension; the pro reads stronger than the underlying statistic supports.
verdict.corrections: Fix the IMF WP/2022/052 author line to Dauphin, Dybczak, Maneely, Taheri Sanjani, Suphaphiphat, Wang & Zhang (2022). Split the GARCH-MIDAS driver claims correctly: attribute Baltic Dry Index + S&P-500-realized-vol(negative) + S&P-VRP(positive) to Conrad-Custovic-Ghysels (2018), and Global Real Economic Activity/Kilian index (single best long-term driver, bull & bear) to Walther-Klein-Bouri (2019); do not credit Conrad with the Kilian index or the Global Financial Stress Index. Re-source or down-rank the +56%/$110k 1yr and +104%/$144k 2yr figures — they are not in the cited Alden/Callahan barometer article (which publishes no return forecast); either cite the actual secondary source or drop them as 'unsourced practitioner round-trips.' Change the CF Benchmarks gold-corr projection from '~0.06 unchanged' to 'current 0.06 -> projected ~0.00 (near zero).' Otherwise the synthesized 10-15yr figures are defensible and well-anchored: every realized number cited (decay 142/65/17%/yr; 5y vol 0.5745~57%; gold corr -0.011 full / 0.045 5y; equity 0.564, value 0.367, FI 0.192, TIPS 0.301 trailing-5y) matches empirical_anchor.json exactly. The central calls (~8-12% nominal / 5-9% real, vol ~50-60%, equity corr 0.40-0.55, gold corr ~0) are reasoned, conservative relative to CF Benchmarks' 30.1%/28%/0.15, and the doc's headline honesty point — that at 10-15yr the DFM return collapses to trend-liquidity-growth x decaying-beta and adds little over a naive debasement assumption — is correct and well-argued.
overstated_pros: Pro #3's '83% of 12-month windows, higher than any major asset class' overstates a weak directional-levels statistic as if it were a stable exploitable factor loading; the doc's own cons concede the changes-based relationship is far weaker, so the pro reads stronger than the evidence (the 0.94 is a levels/spurious-trend number, rolling-12m is only 0.51).

Pro #2 ('decay is endogenous, not hand-imposed') is technically true within the model but oversells: the decay magnitude is driven entirely by the assumed loading-compression path and the factors' unconditional means, which the cons correctly note are the LEAST identifiable parameters from ~15yr/3-4 cycles. So 'endogenous' decay is really 'decay imposed via unidentifiable assumed parameters' — the pro and con #3 are in direct tension and the pro should be hedged.

Pro #5 ('naturally produces the full CMA object — vol regime + correlation structure') is the genuine strength, but the correlation/vol structure it 'produces' is largely just the realized trailing-5y empirical anchor re-labeled; the DFM machinery is not actually generating those numbers at the 10-15yr horizon (cons admit forecasts collapse to the mean), so the pro slightly overstates the model's marginal contribution over simply reporting realized stats.
missing_cons: No survivorship/look-back bias caveat: the entire 'BTC loads on global liquidity' regularity is fit over a single realized up-cycle history where both BTC and global liquidity trended up together; the framework has never been tested through a sustained multi-year liquidity-contraction regime, so the loading's behavior in the scenario that most matters for a CMA is pure extrapolation.

No mention that the global-liquidity factor itself has no agreed definition/series (Alden/Callahan's global-M2 proxy is one of several incompatible constructions); factor-model outputs are sensitive to which liquidity proxy is chosen, an additional researcher-degrees-of-freedom not flagged.

Identification circularity is understated: BTC's loading is estimated on the same short sample whose trend also defines the factor's unconditional mean, so the decay path and the terminal return are not independently identified — a sharper statement than the generic 'short history' con.

No treatment of the supply-side halving schedule, which every other BTC approach (S2F, cost-of-production, power-law) centers on; a pure macro-beta DFM ignores the programmatic supply shock entirely, which is a real omission for a 10-15yr BTC CMA, not just for tail risk.

Missing the point that if the decade return genuinely 'collapses to trend-liquidity-growth x beta and adds no information over a naive debasement assumption' (the doc's own honesty point), then this approach arguably should NOT be presented as a distinct CMA method at all at the 10-15yr horizon — it reduces to the M2/debasement approach (#7) it claims to be distinct from. The doc flags the horizon mismatch but doesn't draw the conclusion that its distinctness collapses precisely at the CMA horizon.

new_approaches.name: Implied-Equilibrium-Return Inversion (Black-Litterman / Risk-Parity / Kelly Back-Out)
new_approaches.description: This approach does not forecast Bitcoin's return from any external driver (scarcity, network, money supply, TAM). Instead it INVERTS a portfolio-optimization identity to solve for the expected return BTC must earn to rationalize an observed or chosen allocation weight, given its ~55% volatility. Three back-outs converge: (1) Black-Litterman reverse-optimization, Pi = lambda*Sigma*w, takes BTC's tiny global-market-cap weight (~0.3-0.5%) as the equilibrium holding and reverse-engineers the implied excess return that makes a CAPM-efficient market hold exactly that much; (2) inversion of return-agnostic risk-based weights (risk parity, max-diversification, Lopez de Prado's HRP), which set BTC's weight purely from the covariance matrix, then asks what return would make that weight ALSO mean-variance optimal; (3) growth-optimal Kelly, f*=(mu-r)/sigma^2, inverted off institutions' actual ~1-2% holdings to mu-r = f*sigma^2. Because BTC's huge variance is the denominator, a small rational weight implies only a modest excess return: a 1-2% Kelly weight at 55% vol implies just ~0.3-0.6%/yr of excess return; even a generous reverse-optimization rarely justifies more than mid-single-digit excess. The CMA is thus internally self-consistent and low, the mirror image of return-first models.
new_approaches.medium_explanation: Every return-forecasting model (S2F, Metcalfe, TAM) runs the optimizer FORWARD: assume a return, get a weight. This family runs it BACKWARD. Black & Litterman (1992) observed that market-cap weights, taken as a CAPM equilibrium, imply a unique vector of excess returns via Pi = lambda*Sigma*w (lambda~2.5-3 the market risk-aversion). Apply that to BTC's ~0.3-0.5% share of global investable assets and the implied excess return is tiny (<1%/yr). Kelly (1956)/Thorp give the same answer for a log-utility investor: f*=(mu-r)/sigma^2, so inverting a 1-2% holding at 55% vol gives mu-r = f*sigma^2 = only 0.3-0.6%/yr. HRP/risk-parity weights (Lopez de Prado 2016) are set without any return view at all; asking what return rationalizes them closes the loop. The implication for a 10-15yr CMA: if institutions hold BTC rationally at low weight, they are REVEALING a low expected excess return, not a triple-digit one. The denominator (sigma^2 ~ 0.30) is the killer.
key_drivers: Observed allocation weight to invert: BTC's global-market-cap weight (~0.3-0.5%) for Black-Litterman, or institutions' actual chosen holding (~1-2% satellite) for the Kelly back-out
BTC variance (sigma^2): at ~55% vol, sigma^2~0.30 is the dominant denominator that crushes the implied return; the single most important input
Risk-aversion coefficient lambda (~2.5-3.0) in BL reverse-optimization, Pi=lambda*Sigma*w; equals 1 for the pure Kelly/log-utility investor

Covariance structure / BTC's correlation to the rest of the portfolio: at tiny weights the CROSS-correlation term (lambda*corr*sigma_btc*sigma_port) can dominate the own-variance term, swinging implied excess return from <1% to ~6-8%
The risk-based weighting scheme being inverted (risk parity / max-diversification / HRP), all of which deliberately use NO return forecast
Equilibrium assumption: that the market portfolio is mean-variance efficient and current weights reflect collective rational expectations (the load-bearing premise)
Fractional-Kelly discounting (half-Kelly): institutions deliberately under-bet vs full Kelly, so inverting their actual weight understates the return they privately believe
pros: Self-consistent and assumption-light on the return side: it imposes no scarcity/network/TAM story and cannot be accused of return-extrapolation hype; the return falls out of an accounting identity given weight and vol

Correctly produces a LOW, decaying-style CMA: because BTC's enormous variance is the denominator, the framework structurally refuses to bless triple-digit forward returns, aligning with the realized appreciation-decay path (142->65->17%/yr) better than any forward-driver model

Revealed-preference logic is genuinely informative: if sophisticated institutions rationally hold only 1-2%, that holding ENCODES their expected return; reading it off is more honest than asserting a number
Black-Litterman's reverse-optimization is a peer-reviewed, widely-adopted institutional standard (Goldman, every major allocator), so the machinery is battle-tested, not crypto-native numerology

Naturally integrates the correlation CMA cells: the same covariance matrix that produces the implied return also produces the cross-asset correlations, so the outputs are internally coherent rather than bolted together
Falsifiable and stress-able: you can vary lambda, the weight, and the correlation assumptions and watch the implied return move, making the sensitivity transparent
cons: Circular / tautological: it assumes the market is in CAPM equilibrium and that current weights are RATIONAL, then 'discovers' the return that rationalizes them. If BTC is mispriced, under-owned due to mandate/career/custody frictions, or held for non-mean-variance reasons (speculation, ideology, convexity), the inverted return is meaningless. Black-Litterman itself only ever called Pi a NEUTRAL STARTING POINT to be overridden by views, not a forecast

Pathologically sensitive to the weight and correlation inputs: the own-variance back-out gives <1% excess (absurdly low for a 55%-vol asset nobody would hold for that), while adding a cross-correlation term to a 60/40 swings it to ~6-8%. The 'answer' is whatever you assume about BTC's correlation and the weight, so the precision is illusory

The near-zero own-variance result is economically nonsensical as a standalone CMA: no investor holds a 55%-vol, 70-80%-drawdown asset for 0.3-0.6%/yr of excess return, which exposes that institutions are NOT holding BTC as a mean-variance Kelly bet at all (they hold it as a convex option or debasement hedge), invalidating the inversion's premise

Risk-parity/HRP inversion is doubly indirect: those schemes were explicitly designed to AVOID return forecasts, so back-solving a return from them re-introduces exactly the estimation error they were built to dodge

Says nothing about the LEVEL or path of value, drawdowns, or tail risk; it is a one-equation identity, silent on volatility (which must be supplied as an input, not output) and on the survival/ruin question a 10-15yr holder faces
Fractional-Kelly and under-betting mean the observed weight systematically understates institutions' true expected return, so the inversion is biased low by an unknown amount

synthesized_outputs.appreciation_nominal: ~8-12%/yr nominal (JUDGMENT). The inversion's own pure own-variance answer (<1% excess => ~4-5% nominal) is economically absurd and tells us institutions are NOT holding BTC as a mean-variance Kelly bet. The defensible read: take the full reverse-optimization including BTC's ~0.3 correlation to the 60/40, which lifts implied excess to ~6-8%/yr, add a ~4% risk-free => ~10-12% nominal. I haircut slightly toward 8-10% to reflect fractional-Kelly under-betting biasing the observed weight low in the other direction. This lands squarely on the realized-decay extrapolation and the honest cross-approach central, by construction NOT a triple-digit number.
synthesized_outputs.appreciation_real: ~5-9%/yr real (subtract ~2.5-3% long-run inflation). Consistent with a maturing high-vol asset whose rational forward Sharpe is modest.
synthesized_outputs.volatility: ~55-60%/yr (JUDGMENT). This is the input that drives the whole inversion; anchored at realized trailing-5y ~57%, floor held there (no compression below realized yet evidenced). The framework is exquisitely sensitive to this number — halving it would quadruple the implied return.
synthesized_outputs.corr_growth_eq: ~0.45 (JUDGMENT). The cross-correlation term is what rescues the inversion from a near-zero answer, so this cell is load-bearing here; anchored to the post-ETF ~0.5 regime, partially mean-reverting over the horizon.

I anchor to the latter, haircut for fractional-Kelly under-betting, landing ~8-12%. The deepest critique to carry forward: the near-zero own-variance result is not a low-return forecast but a falsification of the premise — it reveals institutions do NOT size BTC as a Kelly/mean-variance bet, so the inversion's 'revealed' return should be read as a skeptical ceiling-check, not a believed point estimate.

new_approaches.rich_notes:
METHODOLOGY. This family is defined by direction of inference: it runs the portfolio optimizer BACKWARD. Forward models (S2F, Metcalfe, TAM, M2) posit a return and derive a weight or price; this family observes a weight and derives the return that rationalizes it. Three back-outs converge on the same identity for a single risky asset:

1) Black-Litterman reverse-optimization (Black & Litterman 1992 FAJ; Idzorek 2005). The implied equilibrium excess-return vector is Pi = lambda * Sigma * w_mkt, where lambda is market risk-aversion (typically 2.5-3.0, calibrated so the market portfolio's Sharpe is reasonable), Sigma the covariance matrix, w_mkt the market-cap weights. Black & Litterman's own framing: market-cap weights, under CAPM, ARE a statement of equilibrium expected returns; Pi is the 'neutral starting point.' Crucially, they NEVER claimed Pi is a forecast — it is the prior to be overridden by views. Repurposing it as a standalone BTC CMA is a use the authors did not endorse.

2) Kelly/growth-optimal back-out (Kelly 1956; MacLean-Thorp-Ziemba 2011). For a log-utility investor the optimal fraction is f* = (mu - r)/sigma^2, the lambda=1 special case of BL. Invert it: mu - r = f* * sigma^2. This is the cleanest statement of the family's punchline. At BTC's ~55% vol, sigma^2 ~ 0.30, so a rational 1-2% Kelly holding implies only ~0.3-0.6%/yr of excess return. Perrenod's 'Kelly Capital Growth Criterion for Bitcoin' (2024) computes the DISCRETE Kelly fraction from 4.5 block-years of monthly data: p=0.537, b=2.22 => f*=32.8% full-Kelly, 16.4% half-Kelly — but that inverts BTC's REALIZED (huge) return, not a forward one; run forward with a decayed mu it collapses toward a low single-digit weight.

3) Risk-parity / max-diversification / HRP inversion (Lopez de Prado 2016, JPM). HRP and risk-parity set weights purely from the covariance matrix with NO return input — the whole point of HRP (which beats mean-variance out-of-sample by dodging unstable return estimates). Inverting them asks: what return vector would make these risk-based weights ALSO mean-variance optimal? This closes the loop but is doubly indirect — re-introducing the very return estimate HRP was built to avoid.

KEY RELATIONSHIPS & THE CENTRAL NUANCE. The single most important and underappreciated point: the inverted return is wildly sensitive to whether you include BTC's correlation to the rest of the portfolio. The OWN-VARIANCE term (lambda*sigma^2*w) at a 0.3-2% weight gives <1%/yr excess — economically nonsensical, since nobody holds a 70-80%-drawdown asset for 0.5% of excess. But the CROSS-CORRELATION term (lambda*corr*sigma_btc*sigma_port*(1-w)) dominates at small weights: with corr~0.3 to a 12%-vol 60/40 and lambda=3, it alone contributes ~6%/yr, lifting total implied excess to ~6-8%. So the 'low self-consistent CMA' headline is really TWO different numbers: a near-zero figure that proves institutions are NOT Kelly-betting on BTC, and a mid-single-digit figure once you treat BTC as a correlated portfolio component. Both are below the realized level, which is the family's honest contribution to the appreciation-decay thesis.

GLOBAL-CAP WEIGHT. BTC market cap ~$2T against ~$500-600T of global investable assets (equities ~$110T, bonds ~$140T, gold ~$15-22T, real estate ~$330T) is ~0.3-0.4%; BTC is ~10% of (BTC+gold). Reverse-optimizing that weight with lambda=2.5-3 gives ~0.2-0.3%/yr implied excess — the starkest illustration that the market's revealed equilibrium return for BTC is tiny unless you lean entirely on the correlation channel.

HISTORICAL FIT / FAILURE MODES. The framework has no 'fit' in the predictive sense — it is an identity, true by construction given inputs. Its failure mode is the equilibrium/rationality premise: BTC is plausibly under-owned for mandate, custody, career-risk and regulatory reasons, and held by its actual owners for convexity/ideology/debasement-hedge reasons that are NOT mean-variance. If so, the observed weight encodes frictions, not a return belief, and the inversion is void. It is also silent on vol (an input) and on tail/ruin risk — a serious omission for a 70-80%-drawdown asset over 10-15yr.

ON-RECORD MULTI-YEAR FORECASTS. No major allocator has published a headline BTC 10-15yr CMA derived explicitly via reverse-optimization; the technique appears as the implicit logic behind right-sizing pieces (BlackRock's 1-2% sleeve, CoinShares' risk-budget). Perrenod's Kelly work is the most explicit public inversion but is backward-looking. This is itself telling: the inversion produces such a LOW return that no long-the-asset shop foregrounds it — the revealed-preference number is inconvenient for the bull case, which is exactly why it is a useful skeptical anchor for a CMA.

issues: BTC market cap input is stale-high. Doc uses ~$2T; actual May 2026 BTC mcap is ~$1.47-1.52T (CoinDesk/CoinMarketCap, 2026-05-29, BTC ~$73.5k). At $1.5T against $500-600T global investable, the global-cap weight is ~0.25-0.30%, BELOW the doc's stated 0.3-0.4% band. Since implied excess return scales linearly with the weight, the own-variance back-out is overstated by ~25-35%. Self-correcting toward an even lower number, but the input should be refreshed.

Internal contradiction in the volatility-sensitivity claim. synthesized_outputs.volatility states 'halving it would quadruple the implied return.' For the INVERSE direction the doc actually runs (mu-r = f*sigma^2 with f = OBSERVED/FIXED weight), halving sigma QUARTERS the implied return, it does not quadruple it. Quadrupling is the FORWARD relationship (f = (mu-r)/sigma^2, solve weight from return). The doc conflates the two directions on the single sentence that is supposed to demonstrate the framework's sensitivity. The magnitude of sensitivity (4x) is right; the SIGN/direction stated is backwards.

The ~8-12% synthesized nominal is NOT a clean output of the inversion the doc spends 90% of its text defending. The own-variance inversion (its 'native,' assumption-light result) yields <1% excess / ~4-5% nominal. The 8-12% comes ENTIRELY from (a) privileging the cross-correlation term and (b) two discretionary haircuts/add-backs (risk-free add, fractional-Kelly bias). The doc is admirably explicit that this is JUDGMENT, but the headline number is effectively a CAPM-beta estimate (BTC's equity-correlated risk premium), not a revealed-preference inversion. The 'self-consistent, assumption-light' pro does not actually support the 8-12% figure; it supports the ~4-5% figure the doc discards.

The cross-correlation term framing 'lambda*corr*sigma_btc*sigma_port*(1-w)' is an approximation, not the exact BL term. Exact BL implied return Pi_i = lambda*(Sigma*w)_i = lambda*[sigma_i^2*w_i + sum_{j!=i} corr_ij*sigma_i*sigma_j*w_j]. The cross term weights by the OTHER assets' weights (which sum to ~1-w), so using (1-w)*sigma_port as a single-sleeve proxy is defensible ONLY if the 60/40 sleeve is treated as one asset with vol sigma_port. The arithmetic (~6% at corr=0.3) checks out under that proxy, but the doc presents it as the identity rather than a one-asset reduction.

Equilibrium/rationality premise is even weaker than the doc concedes. The doc treats BTC's market-cap weight as a CAPM equilibrium holding, but a large and growing share of BTC float is held in ETFs, on exchanges, and by ideological/convex holders who are NOT mean-variance optimizers over a global portfolio. The 'market portfolio is MV-efficient' premise is load-bearing AND false for this specific asset, which the cons acknowledge but the synthesized 8-12% quietly relies on anyway.
