cited_outputs.volatility: Almeida et al. (2024): Bitcoin 'much more volatile' than S&P 500 with a Bitcoin Variance Risk Premium (BVRP) averaging ~14%/yr at 1-month horizon (vs ~2% VRP for S&P 500 per Bollerslev-Tauchen-Zhou 2009); no single annualized return-vol number published in this structural strand
cited_outputs.corr_growth_eq: Liu-Tsyvinski (2021): BTC has NO exposure to common stock-market or macro factors. Wilson (2024): stock-BTC correlation is low but 'has been tightening over time.' Almeida et al.: BTC 'fluctuated largely independently of traditional macro-financial markets' over their sample (no point correlation published)
cited_outputs.corr_value_eq: n/a (source silent — structural-SDF strand does not split equities into growth vs value)
cited_outputs.corr_fi_nominal: n/a (source silent — Wilson compares BTC to stocks/bonds for the premium but publishes no BTC-bond correlation; Liu-Tsyvinski: no exposure to bond/currency/commodity returns)
cited_outputs.corr_gold: n/a as a structural number. Benigno-Rosa (2023): macro/monetary news moves precious metals and stocks but NOT Bitcoin — implying a macro-driver disconnect from gold. Almeida et al. note BVRP became 'highly correlated' with gold's VRP only during the COVID crisis (regime-specific, not structural). No steady-state BTC-gold correlation is published
cited_outputs.notes: The defining output of this family is a NEGATIVE result: standard structural SDF/C-CAPM models predict a low-or-negative premium and are statistically rejected even at RRA > 10, so the literature publishes a documented PUZZLE (realized BP ~66%/yr, Sharpe ~0.8, BVRP ~14%) rather than a forward CMA. Disaster-risk explains only ~1/3 of the premium (Almeida et al.); the rest is upside-dominated and unexplained. Most correlation/vol cells are silent in the structural strand and must be imported from realized data.

synthesized_outputs.appreciation_nominal: ~7-11%/yr nominal (JUDGMENT, not a model output). The structural read is deliberately deflationary: with BTC's consumption/macro covariance ~zero, the C-CAPM-justified premium is SMALL, so the bulk of realized history is an unexplained residual a forward CMA should NOT extrapolate. As BTC institutionalizes, its equity (consumption-proxy) covariance rises (realized growth corr 0.26->0.56) while the rare-disaster premium COMPRESSES as perceived crash/ruin probability falls — both forces push the forward premium down toward a high-beta-equity-plus-shrinking-disaster-residual. I anchor to the cross-approach central band and the realized decay path (142%->65%->17%), landing modestly below the trailing-5y 17%. Wide error bands: the Euler/GMM tests have near-zero power, so this is a central tendency, not a tight estimate.
synthesized_outputs.appreciation_real: ~4-8%/yr real (subtracting ~2.5-3% long-run inflation). The ICAPM-hedging inversion matters here: because BTC is a WEAK/unreliable inflation hedge, the framework does NOT credit it the real-purchasing-power-preservation premium gold gets — its poor hedge value is a required-return AMPLIFIER, not a discount, so the real number sits below where a gold-parity story would place it.
synthesized_outputs.volatility: ~55-60%/yr (JUDGMENT). The structural strand confirms BTC is 'much more volatile' than equities with a large variance-risk premium but publishes no point vol; I anchor at realized trailing-5y ~57% (no compression below realized yet evidenced) with a 10-15yr band of ~50-60%. The disaster mechanism implies fat left tails persist even as central vol drifts down.
synthesized_outputs.corr_growth_eq: +0.45 to +0.60 (JUDGMENT). The framework's own logic — rising consumption/equity covariance as BTC institutionalizes, the very 'tightening' Wilson flags — pushes this UP. Anchored to realized trailing-5y 0.56. This rising covariance is precisely what would (slowly) shrink the C-CAPM puzzle and the structurally-unjustified excess return.
synthesized_outputs.corr_value_eq: +0.25 to +0.40 (JUDGMENT). Below growth-equity correlation; BTC carries the duration/liquidity beta of growth more than the cashflow-value factor. Anchored to realized trailing-5y 0.37.
synthesized_outputs.corr_fi_nominal: +0.10 to +0.25 (JUDGMENT). Low-positive. Benigno-Rosa find BTC ignores monetary/discount-rate news, so the structural link to nominal duration is weak; the modest positive realized number (5y 0.19) is a shared-liquidity-beta artifact, not an SDF mechanism.
synthesized_outputs.corr_tips: +0.15 to +0.30 (JUDGMENT). Slightly above nominal FI via a weak real-rate/liquidity channel (realized 5y 0.30), but the ICAPM view explicitly DENIES BTC a reliable real-rate/inflation-hedge role, so I do not push this higher.
synthesized_outputs.corr_gold: ~0.0-0.15 (JUDGMENT). The ICAPM-hedging inversion is the key: this family treats BTC as a POOR hedge whose weak inflation/safe-haven value RAISES its required return — the opposite of gold's role. It therefore predicts NO structural gold co-movement, consistent with realized ~0 (full -0.01, 5y +0.04) and Benigno-Rosa's finding that macro news moves gold but not BTC. I keep it at the low end and explicitly reject the digital-gold linkage: a framework that prices BTC as a risk-AMPLIFIER cannot simultaneously claim it co-moves with the safe-haven it fails to resemble.
synthesized_outputs.notes: Synthesized 10-15yr view anchored to the realized appreciation-DECAY baseline (142->65->17%/yr), NOT historical levels. The distinctive contribution is the structural argument for a LOW forward premium and a LOW gold correlation: BTC's near-zero consumption covariance means little is structurally justified, and the ICAPM inversion treats BTC's weak inflation hedge as a required-return amplifier rather than a discount. Confidence is deliberately low (near-zero test power); equity correlations are the highest-conviction cells because the framework's own 'tightening covariance' logic and realized data agree.

new_approaches.rich_notes:
METHODOLOGY. This family is the only structural-equilibrium strand in the BTC-CMA universe. It nests three classical models. (1) Lucas (1978)/Breeden (1979) consumption-CAPM: in a representative-agent exchange economy the equilibrium risk premium on any asset equals RRA x cov(asset return, consumption growth). (2) Barro (2006)/Rietz (1988) rare disasters: augment the endowment process with low-probability, high-severity consumption collapses; the equity (or BTC) premium becomes compensation for bad-state exposure and can be matched with modest RRA (~3-4) once disasters are present. (3) Merton (1973) ICAPM: with stochastic investment opportunities, required return depends on an asset's covariance with state variables investors want to hedge (inflation, recessions); an asset that hedges POORLY commands a HIGHER required return. Applied to BTC, money-in-utility (Schilling-Uhlig 2019) and search/holding-cost variants (Choi-Rocheteau 2021) add a transactional-services term and illiquidity penalty.

KEY RELATIONSHIP & THE PUZZLE. The load-bearing empirical fact is that BTC's consumption/macro covariance is ~zero. Liu-Tsyvinski (RFS 2021) find crypto 'has no exposure to most common stock-market and macroeconomic factors or to the returns of currencies and commodities' — only crypto-specific network/momentum/attention factors price it. Benigno-Rosa (NY Fed SR 1052, 2023) find BTC is 'unresponsive to both monetary and macroeconomic news' while the same news significantly moves stocks, exchange rates and precious metals. Plug a near-zero consumption covariance into C-CAPM and the model predicts a LOW or NEGATIVE premium. Yet realized BTC excess returns are enormous. Wilson (2024, B.E. J. Macro) formalizes this as the 'Bitcoin premium puzzle': using the three standard equity-premium methods (Mehra-Prescott model premium, Euler-equation tests, GMM RRA estimation), 'standard macroeconomic models predict a low or negative Bitcoin premium... the model is rejected even when the coefficient of relative risk aversion is above 10.' He notes 'stocks are more tightly correlated with consumption, so the model tends to predict a very low Bitcoin premium,' and the stock-BTC correlation 'has been tightening over time' — a structural break in late 2013 lowered the premium, but the puzzle 'is persistent... no downward trend since.'

QUOTES/FIT. Almeida, Grith, Miftachov & Wang (2024/2025) decompose the option-implied premium: BP averages ~66%/yr (1-month), BVRP ~14%/yr, Sharpe ~0.8 (~2x S&P 500). Critically, 'negative Bitcoin returns (between three and one standard deviations) account for only one-third of the total Bitcoin premium,' while large positive returns (20-60%) account for ~39%. This DAMAGES the pure rare-disaster reading: if BTC's return were mainly crash-compensation, the premium should concentrate in bad states as it does (more so) for the S&P. Instead BTC's premium is upside-dominated — pointing to speculative/convenience demand, not consumption-disaster insurance. They cite Chen et al. that BTC's pricing kernel is 'decoupled from the consumption kernel, with minimal impact from real-economy shocks like the COVID crisis.'

FAILURE MODES. (a) Identification: with no realized BTC consumption-disaster, the disaster probability/severity that rationalizes the premium is free-fit and unfalsifiable. (b) Power: Wilson's Euler/GMM tests have 'very wide confidence intervals' and 'extremely low power' — the framework cannot reject most forward returns, so it is a weak point-forecast generator. (c) Data mismatch: quarterly, revised consumption vs a 24/7 sentiment-driven asset. (d) Internal tension: the C-CAPM (low covariance -> low premium) and the ICAPM-hedging (poor hedge -> high required return) conclusions point in opposite directions; the analyst must choose which dominates.

ON-RECORD MULTI-YEAR FORECASTS. None. This strand deliberately produces no dated price target — its contribution is to DOCUMENT that no structural risk-premium model can justify BTC's realized return, which implies a forward CMA should NOT extrapolate that return. The honest structural implication for a 10-15yr CMA is a SMALL justified premium (high-beta-equity-like, ~7-11% nominal) plus a shrinking disaster residual, with appreciation decaying as BTC's equity covariance rises and perceived disaster probability falls — and with very wide bands given the near-zero test power. The ICAPM inversion is the distinctive CMA contribution: it correctly flips the gold-parity 'safe-haven lowers required return' logic, treating BTC's weak inflation/recession hedge as a required-return amplifier rather than a discount, which is why this family assigns BTC a LOW gold correlation and refuses it gold's real-purchasing-power premium.

issues: WILSON 'TIGHTENING CORRELATION' IS THE WEAKEST ATTRIBUTION AND IT IS LOAD-BEARING. The brief repeatedly asserts Wilson (2024) flags that 'stock-BTC correlation has been tightening over time,' and builds the entire forward-premium-decay logic plus the +0.45-0.60 growth-corr synthesis on it. Wilson's abstract does NOT contain this; it says the opposite-flavored thing -- 'the puzzle is persistent; there has been no downward trend in the premium since [the 2013 break].' I could not independently confirm 'tightening' anywhere in Wilson. This phrase may be the analyst's inference dressed as a Wilson finding. At minimum it is overstated as a citation.

INTERNAL CONTRADICTION IS REAL AND THE BRIEF ADMITS IT BUT STILL PRODUCES POINT NUMBERS. The C-CAPM channel (low covariance -> LOW premium) and the ICAPM channel (poor hedge -> HIGHER required return) point in opposite directions. The con-list flags this honestly, yet the synthesized 7-11% nominal silently resolves it by letting C-CAPM dominate (low premium) while invoking ICAPM only to justify the low gold corr. The choice of which mechanism wins is not defended -- it is asserted. A reader could equally use the same framework to argue a HIGHER required return.

THE FRAMEWORK ADMITS IT PRODUCES NO POINT FORECAST, YET A 7-11% / 4-8% / 55-60% NUMBER SET IS DELIVERED. By the brief's own repeated statement ('the CMA does not fall out cleanly,' 'near-zero test power,' 'cannot reject almost any forward return'), the 7-11% nominal is pure analyst judgment anchored to the OTHER approaches' cross-band and the realized decay -- NOT to anything this family generates. That is defensible as labeled judgment, but the structural family is doing almost no work in producing the number; the realized-decay extrapolation is. The 'structural discipline' framing slightly oversells how much the SDF theory constrains the answer.

ALMEIDA NEGATIVE-RETURN SHARE IS ~28.5%, ROUNDED UP TO 'ONE-THIRD'. The paper's figure is 28.53% from -3 to -1 SD; the brief says '~one-third' and 'only ~1/3.' The paper itself uses 'one-third' loosely, so this is defensible, but 28.5% is nearer 'a bit over a quarter' than a clean third. Minor generosity, not a fabrication. Positive-return share 38.66% -> '~39%' is exact.

BENIGNO-ROSA 'PRECIOUS METALS RESPOND BUT BTC DOES NOT' -- CORE DISCONNECT CONFIRMED, GOLD-SPECIFIC CONTRAST ONLY PARTIALLY VERIFIED. The headline finding (BTC orthogonal to monetary/macro news unlike other US asset classes) is solid. The sharper claim used for the gold-corr inversion -- that the SAME news moves gold/precious metals while leaving BTC unmoved -- is plausible and consistent with the paper's framing but I could not extract the exact precious-metals sentence (NY Fed PDF 403'd). Treat the gold-specific contrast as probable-but-not-fully-sourced.

SCHILLING-UHLIG MISLABELED AS 'MONEY-IN-UTILITY.' Schilling-Uhlig (2019) is an endowment-economy / cash-in-advance-style model where bitcoin yields transactional services; it is not a canonical money-in-utility (MIU) specification. 'Transactional-services term' is fine; 'money-in-utility (Schilling-Uhlig)' is a loose label. Choi-Rocheteau as search-theoretic with holding cost is correct.

Wilson (2024) RRA>10 rejection, 2013 structural break, low/negative model-implied premium, and 'extremely low power / very wide CIs' all confirmed (abstract + body). Liu-Tsyvinski (2021 RFS) 'no exposure to common stock-market/macro factors, only crypto-specific network/momentum/attention' confirmed. Realized decay 142->65->17%/yr, vol 57.45% trailing-5y, gold corr -0.011 full / +0.045 5y, growth corr 0.26/0.36/0.56 all match empirical_anchor.json exactly. THREE FIXES NEEDED: (1) Stop attributing 'stock-BTC correlation tightening over time' to Wilson -- either find the exact in-text quote or relabel it as the analyst's own forward assumption; this phrase carries the growth-corr synthesis and the puzzle-shrinks-over-time narrative and is currently the only materially unverified attribution. (2) Either pick and DEFEND which channel (C-CAPM vs ICAPM) dominates the 7-11% number, or present it as a range bracketing both rather than a single resolved figure. (3) Soften 'money-in-utility (Schilling-Uhlig)' to 'transactional-services endowment-economy (Schilling-Uhlig)'. The synthesized CMA cells (7-11% nom / 4-8% real / 55-60% vol / growth +0.45-0.60 / gold 0-0.15) are DEFENSIBLE as labeled judgment anchored to realized decay -- not hype: every cell sits at or below the realized trailing window and the framework correctly argues for decay, not extrapolation. The honest framing ('this family disciplines/caps the number rather than generating a high one') is the brief's strongest feature and should be preserved."
overstated_pros: Pro #6 ('Portfolio-coherent: outputs a premium AND betas/covariances that slot into a mean-variance CMA') is overstated -- the cons correctly note the structural strand publishes NO forward vol and NO cross-asset correlation matrix, so in practice every CMA cell except the premium puzzle itself must be IMPORTED from realized data. The framework is portfolio-coherent in principle only; as published it populates almost no CMA cells.

The implied pro that this family provides 'structural discipline' on the forward number is partly circular: by the brief's own admission the test power is near zero and 'cannot reject almost any forward return,' so the discipline actually comes from the realized-decay path and the cross-approach band, not from the SDF theory. The structural family's real contribution is qualitative (premium SHOULD decay; gold-corr SHOULD be low), not a quantitative constraint.
missing_cons: NO LIVE BTC OPTIONS / SDF DATA BEFORE ~2017-2019. Almeida et al.'s option-implied premium and variance-risk-premium decomposition rests on Deribit options that barely existed before 2019, so the BVRP ~14% and the bad-state/good-state split are estimated on a ~5-6yr, regime-dominated (COVID + 2021 bull + 2022 bust) window. The cons mention the ~15yr sample generically but never flag that the headline option-based numbers rest on an even shorter, crisis-heavy options history.

SURVIVORSHIP / SINGLE-ASSET CONDITIONING. The entire 'premium puzzle' is computed on BTC conditional on BTC having survived. A rare-disaster framework whose tail is 'protocol/regulatory ruin' is being calibrated only on the realization where ruin did NOT occur -- which mechanically inflates the realized premium the model then 'fails' to explain. This strengthens, not weakens, the disaster story but the brief never notes the survivorship bias in the puzzle's headline magnitude.

THE C-CAPM 'LOW PREMIUM' CONCLUSION CUTS AGAINST HOLDING BTC AT ALL, NOT JUST AGAINST A HIGH CMA. If taken literally, a ~zero-consumption-covariance asset earning a huge premium is either mispriced (will mean-revert down) or compensating an unmodeled risk -- both readings argue the forward EXPECTED return should be LOWER than the 7-11% high-beta-equity anchor, possibly equity-like or below. The synthesis quietly lands ABOVE long-run equity (~7% nominal floor) despite a framework whose central message is 'structurally justified premium is small.' That tension is underplayed.

RISING EQUITY CORRELATION IS A DOUBLE-EDGED CON FOR DIVERSIFICATION, NOT JUST A PUZZLE-SHRINKER. The brief frames rising growth-corr (0.26->0.56) positively (it shrinks the puzzle). But for a CMA consumer the same fact destroys BTC's diversification case: a 57%-vol asset converging to +0.6 with growth equities contributes mostly variance, little diversification -- a portfolio-construction con the structural family's own logic implies but the brief omits.

new_approaches.name: Liability-Driven / Surplus-Optimization Implied BTC Hurdle (Endowment/LDI)
new_approaches.description: Instead of forecasting bitcoin's return, this approach inverts the question: given a sponsor's actual liability (pension benefit accruals, an endowment's real spending rule, an insurer's reserves), what expected return would a small BTC sleeve need in order to IMPROVE surplus / funded-status efficiency rather than degrade it? It sits on the Sharpe-Tint (1990) surplus-optimization frontier, where risk is the volatility of the SURPLUS (assets minus the present value of liabilities), not the volatility of assets in isolation. An asset earns its place only if its expected return clears a hurdle equal to its marginal contribution to surplus risk times the surplus portfolio's price of risk (operationally, hurdle approximately equals beta-to-surplus times the surplus return premium; equivalently it is the implied/reverse-optimized return that leaves the surplus frontier unchanged). Because BTC's returns are driven by nothing that drives real-spending, wage, healthcare, or discount-rate liabilities, its covariance with the liability is near zero, so it provides essentially no liability hedge; meanwhile its 55-100% volatility makes its marginal contribution to surplus variance very large even at a 1-3% weight. The two forces combine to make the implied hurdle STEEP. The output is not a price target but a required-return bar: if the analyst's independent BTC CMA exceeds the hurdle, a token sleeve is surplus-accretive; if not, it is surplus-dilutive regardless of how attractive BTC looks in an asset-only Sharpe optimization. It is the only framework in the set that prices BTC against a liability covariance rather than against other assets.
new_approaches.medium_explanation: This is a liability-RELATIVE optimizer, not a return model. Following Sharpe-Tint (1990), risk is the volatility of surplus (assets minus PV of liabilities); an asset is valued by its covariance with the liability, and earns inclusion only if its expected return clears a hurdle roughly equal to its beta-to-surplus times the surplus risk premium (the reverse-optimized "implied return"). Key inputs: the liability's risk drivers (real spending, wages, healthcare inflation, or the discount-rate curve), BTC's covariance with those drivers (empirically near zero), BTC's standalone volatility (55-100%), and the sleeve size. For a 10-15yr BTC CMA the implication is sobering: because BTC hedges almost no real liability and its huge variance dominates surplus risk even at a 1-3% weight, the implied hurdle is high (plausibly mid-teens to 20%+ depending on liability and risk aversion). The framework therefore does not produce appreciation, vol, or correlation numbers directly; it produces a PASS/FAIL bar against whatever independent BTC return assumption you bring. Its honest verdict: only a tiny return-seeking sleeve, justified by raw return, not by liability hedging.
key_drivers: Liability risk drivers: the present value and volatility of the obligation being funded (real spending rule for an endowment; wage/benefit accruals and the discount-rate curve for a pension; reserves for an insurer)

Covariance of BTC returns with the liability's drivers (empirically near zero for real-spending/wage/healthcare/rate liabilities) — the single most important input, since it determines whether BTC hedges or adds surplus risk
BTC standalone volatility (55-100%), which dominates the asset's marginal contribution to surplus variance even at small weights
Sleeve size / weight of BTC in total assets (the marginal-risk contribution and thus the hurdle scale with weight)
Surplus risk aversion (lambda) and the surplus/funded-ratio Sharpe ratio — the 'price of risk' multiplying the marginal risk contribution to set the hurdle

Funded status / horizon: hurdle rises as funded status improves (less risk budget) and as the plan de-risks toward termination; an open endowment with a perpetual real-spending liability has more room than a closed pension
pros: Asks the correct question for an institution: not 'is BTC's Sharpe ratio attractive in isolation?' but 'does a BTC sleeve improve the probability of paying real liabilities?' — surfacing that BTC's diversification benefit is largely irrelevant to a spending/wage/healthcare liability it does not hedge

Honest about volatility: by penalizing the variance of SURPLUS (not assets), it correctly inflates BTC's cost via its 55-100% vol, preventing the asset-only Sharpe optimizers (which BTC's high realized return flatters) from over-allocating — the framework structurally caps the sleeve at a token weight

Produces a falsifiable decision bar (the implied hurdle) you can test any independent BTC CMA against, rather than a self-serving price target; it cleanly separates 'return-seeking' from 'liability-hedging' so BTC cannot masquerade as a hedge
Methodologically grounded in 35+ years of accepted institutional practice (Sharpe-Tint surplus optimization, Leibowitz endowment-model dual-risk framework, LDI) — not a crypto-native curve-fit
cons: It is NOT a return forecaster: it consumes a BTC expected-return assumption and tells you whether it clears the bar — so it cannot, by itself, populate a CMA's appreciation cell. You still need an exogenous BTC return model, inheriting all that model's flaws

Garbage-in on the covariance: the hurdle depends critically on BTC's covariance with the liability, which is estimated on a short, non-stationary BTC history and is regime-dependent (BTC's equity correlation has risen from ~0.26 to ~0.56). If BTC's correlation to the discount-rate/liquidity factor rises in a crisis exactly when funded status is stressed, the realized surplus damage exceeds the ex-ante hurdle

No institution has actually published a liability-relative BTC hurdle — Grayscale, ARK and every existing approach in the set run asset-only mean-variance/Sharpe optimization against stocks and bonds, never against a liability covariance. The framework is well-established in general but UNAPPLIED to BTC on the record, so all numbers here are derived, not cited

Sensitive to subjective inputs (risk aversion lambda, sleeve size, choice of liability proxy) that swing the hurdle widely; a generous endowment-spending liability and high BTC return assumption can flip the verdict, so it can be reverse-engineered to justify a predetermined allocation

Says nothing native about BTC's own appreciation, volatility, or cross-asset correlations — all distributional CMA cells must be imported from realized data or another model, just like the cost-of-production and NVT frameworks

synthesized_outputs.appreciation_nominal: Implied HURDLE (not a forecast): roughly ~14-22%/yr nominal required for a 1-3% BTC sleeve to be surplus-accretive against a typical institutional liability. Derivation (judgment): a surplus/funded-ratio Sharpe of ~0.3-0.4 times BTC's marginal contribution to surplus risk — which at a 2% weight and ~55-60% BTC vol with near-zero liability covariance is ~1.1-1.2 percentage points of incremental surplus vol per 1% of return budget — produces a hurdle in the high-teens. CRITICALLY, this hurdle (~14-22%) sits ABOVE the cross-approach central BTC forward CMA of ~8-12% nominal (which extrapolates BTC's realized appreciation decay 142%->65%->17%/yr). So the honest verdict: against a realistic decayed BTC return, a BTC sleeve FAILS the surplus hurdle for most real liabilities — it survives only as a small raw-return-seeking bet, not as a liability-aware allocation.

Versus a synthesized BTC real forward of ~5-9%, BTC again FAILS the bar for the median institution. Judgment, anchored to the realized-decay baseline.

At a 2% weight this still contributes meaningful surplus vol because BTC's variance is ~12-40x a balanced asset's; the framework's whole point is that this vol, not BTC's return, is what disqualifies large sleeves.

BTC does not inherit gold's (weak, partial) real-liability-hedging property; near-zero gold co-movement means BTC is a pure return-seeker in surplus space, reinforcing that any sleeve is justified by return, not by hedging.
synthesized_outputs.notes: These are DERIVED, not cited — no institution publishes a liability-relative BTC hurdle. The framework's distinctive contribution to the CMA set: it reframes the central ~8-12% nominal BTC forward not as 'good or bad' in isolation but as BELOW the ~14-22% surplus hurdle for a real liability, i.e. surplus-dilutive except as a token raw-return sleeve. The correlation cells are inputs imported from realized data; the genuinely native quantity is BTC's ~zero covariance with the liability, which is what makes the hurdle steep.

new_approaches.rich_notes:
METHODOLOGY. The framework inverts the CMA question. Sharpe and Tint (1990, 'Liabilities — A New Approach', JPM 16(2):5-10) replaced asset-return variance with SURPLUS variance as the risk measure: define surplus S = A − k·L (assets minus a liability-importance-weighted PV of liabilities), and optimize U = E(surplus return) − lambda·Var(surplus return). The pivotal change is that an asset is now valued by its covariance with the liability, not merely its standalone moments. An asset whose returns are driven by the same factors as the liability (e.g., TIPS for an inflation-linked spending rule) REDUCES surplus volatility and is attractive even at a low standalone return; an asset uncorrelated with the liability (BTC) cannot reduce surplus volatility and is confined to the return-seeking sleeve, where it must clear a return hurdle to compensate for the surplus variance it adds.

THE HURDLE. Operationally the bar is the reverse-optimized 'implied return.' MSCI ('Earning a Place in the Portfolio,' 2023) states it cleanly: hurdle ≈ beta-to-portfolio × portfolio expected return, with implied returns 'proportional to the marginal contribution to risk of that component.' In surplus space, substitute 'surplus portfolio' and 'surplus return premium' for portfolio/return. BTC's hurdle is driven by two compounding facts: (1) its covariance with a real-spending/wage/healthcare/discount-rate liability is ~zero (BTC's realized TIPS correlation ~0.30, FI ~0.19, gold ~0 — none high or stable enough to hedge a liability), so it earns no hedging credit; and (2) its 55-100% standalone vol makes its marginal contribution to surplus variance very large even at 1-3% weight. As MSCI notes, 'high volatility inflates beta, raising the required hurdle rate substantially.' The result: an implied hurdle plausibly in the high-teens-to-20%+, which I synthesize at ~14-22% nominal / ~11-19% real.

KEY RELATIONSHIP / VERDICT. The framework's value to a BTC CMA is comparative, not generative. Set the hurdle (~14-22%) against the cross-approach central forward BTC return (~8-12% nominal, the decayed extrapolation of 142%->65%->17%/yr). The forward return is BELOW the surplus hurdle for a real liability. Therefore a BTC sleeve is surplus-DILUTIVE for the median pension or endowment once you (a) penalize its vol in surplus terms and (b) deny it hedging credit it does not earn. It survives only as a tiny raw-return-seeking bet justified by return alone — which is exactly what the asset-only optimizers (Grayscale's ~5% Sharpe-maximizing weight) miss, because they optimize asset Sharpe, not funded status.

HISTORICAL FIT / FAILURE MODES. Surplus optimization is battle-tested in pension/LDI and endowment practice (Leibowitz-Bova-Hammond 2010 formalize the endowment's dual return-seeking/liability-aware risk view; Cambridge Associates' LDI handbooks operationalize funded-status risk). Its failure modes when applied to BTC: (1) covariance instability — BTC's correlations are estimated on a short, non-stationary history and rise in crises (equity corr 0.26->0.56), so realized surplus damage can exceed the ex-ante hurdle precisely when funded status is already stressed (correlation-goes-to-one risk, a 'dragon risk' in Leibowitz's terms); (2) input subjectivity — lambda, sleeve size, and the liability proxy swing the hurdle, so the model can be reverse-engineered to bless a predetermined allocation; (3) it forecasts nothing about BTC itself, inheriting an exogenous return model's flaws.

ON-RECORD FORECASTS PRODUCED THIS WAY: none. This is the distinctive finding. Despite the framework being standard institutional practice, NO asset manager, consultant, pension, or endowment has published a liability-relative BTC hurdle. Every BTC portfolio study on the record — Grayscale's 'Crypto in Diversified Portfolios' (~5% asset-only Sharpe-max weight, ~95% vol, ~0.36 avg correlation inputs), ARK, 21Shares, and all prior rows in this digest — runs asset-only mean-variance against stocks and bonds. None flips to a liability-covariance hurdle. So the framework is genuinely distinct from everything covered, but every output here is DERIVED from the general surplus mechanics applied to BTC's realized moments, not cited from a BTC-specific publication. That absence is itself informative: the institutions most bound by liabilities (DB pensions, insurers) have not found a liability-relative case for BTC, consistent with the steep implied hurdle this framework produces.

These attributions are fine. NUMBER FIXES: restate the implied hurdle as ~8-12% nominal (the defensible range under the cited formula with realized inputs), NOT 14-22%. Then the honest verdict flips to: BTC roughly MEETS its surplus hurdle as a token return-seeking sleeve — it neither clearly passes nor fails — and earns NO liability-hedging credit. Keep the distributional cells (vol ~57%, equity corr ~0.45-0.55, FI ~0.19, TIPS ~0.30, gold ~0) — these are anchored to realized data and check out. The framework's genuinely correct and defensible contributions: (a) surplus-variance risk measure, (b) BTC earns zero hedging credit against real/wage/healthcare/rate liabilities, (c) no institution has published a liability-relative BTC hurdle (plausible and appropriately flagged as derived-not-cited). The flaw is purely the magnitude of the synthesized hurdle and the fail verdict built on it.
overstated_pros: Pro #2 claims the framework 'structurally caps the sleeve at a token weight' via surplus-vol penalty — but the actual implied-return mechanics produce only a single-digit hurdle for a 2% sleeve, so the framework does NOT structurally disqualify BTC the way the report asserts; the 'cap' is asserted, not demonstrated.

The implicit pro that this framework yields a sharper/more conservative verdict than asset-only optimizers (Grayscale ~5%) is overstated: with correct math the liability-relative hurdle (~8-12%) is roughly consistent with BTC's own CMA, so it does not deliver the dramatic 'surplus-dilutive, fails the bar' differentiation claimed.

Pro #4's appeal to '35+ years of accepted institutional practice' is used to lend authority to a hurdle number that the same practice's own formula contradicts — the pedigree is real but is invoked to backstop an unsupported figure.
missing_cons: Does not disclose that under its OWN cited formula the headline hurdle cannot be reproduced — the largest omission. A framework whose central output is irreproducible from its stated mechanics should flag that.

No sleeve-rebalancing / path-dependency con: a 57%-vol sleeve held to a fixed 1-3% weight forces large, frequent rebalances (buy-low/sell-high or the reverse in trends) with real transaction-cost and tax drag on a funded-status basis — never mentioned.

Liquidity / governance con for true liability investors (DB pensions, insurers): regulatory capital charges (e.g. NAIC/Solvency II treatment of crypto), custody/operational risk, and fiduciary (ERISA prudence) constraints are arguably the REAL reason no pension publishes a BTC hurdle — a more parsimonious explanation than 'the hurdle is too steep,' and it is omitted.

Non-stationarity cuts BOTH ways but is only used against BTC: if BTC vol is compressing (200%->~50%) and the asset is maturing, the ex-ante hurdle should be falling over the 10-15yr horizon, which would further weaken the 'fails the bar' verdict — not acknowledged.

Drawdown/left-tail asymmetry: surplus optimization uses variance, which understates the cost of BTC's ~80% peak-to-trough drawdowns landing in a funded-status stress; the report leans on variance and never notes that this makes even its (correct) hurdle an UNDERstatement of the true tail cost — a con that would actually strengthen its thesis but is missing.

new_approaches.name: Rational-Bubble / OLG No-Arbitrage Equilibrium (Tirole/Blanchard-Watson; van Oordt; Biais; Schilling-Uhlig Martingale)
new_approaches.description: A formal no-arbitrage / overlapping-generations VALUATION of a no-cashflow token. With (near-)zero discounted-cashflow fundamental, the entire price is a rational bubble in the sense of Blanchard (1979), Blanchard-Watson (1982) and Tirole (1985): in equilibrium the bubble's EXPECTED return must equal the economy-wide required return, no more and no less, otherwise the asset would either disappear or grow to outweigh all other wealth. With a stochastic (Blanchard-Watson) bursting structure the price grows FASTER than the required return conditional on survival, but the extra appreciation exactly compensates a crash hazard h(t), so E[r] = required return = drift_survival - h(t)*(loss given crash). The price can optionally be decomposed (van Oordt; Biais et al.) into a positive transactional-demand FLOOR (PV of net transactional benefits) plus an additive bubble term that needs continual net investment inflows to be sustained. Schilling-Uhlig (JME 2019) supply the lower-bound/martingale case: if the speculative ('hodling') condition fails, the dollar BTC price is a martingale (expected real return = real rate) whose fundamental value can be zero, and BTC can rationally collapse to it as a convergent supermartingale. The framework's signature CMA output is therefore an explicit expected-return IDENTITY (required return = discount rate + crash-hazard premium) plus a total-loss tail mass - NOT a level forecast. It differs from LPPLS (#17, crash TIMING via super-exponential drift) and the survival/ruin hazard (#19, an absorbing-zero mixture with no equilibrium no-arbitrage return condition): here the defining content is the equilibrium no-arbitrage condition pinning expected return to the required return.
new_approaches.medium_explanation: Bitcoin has no cashflow, so the discounted-cashflow fundamental is ~zero and essentially the whole price is a rational bubble. The no-arbitrage logic (Blanchard-Watson, Tirole, van Oordt) forces a hard discipline a CMA can use: in equilibrium the bubble's EXPECTED return must equal the ordinary required return on risk capital - if it were higher the asset would eventually outweigh all wealth; if lower, nobody holds it. With stochastic bursting, price appreciates faster than the required return while it survives, but that excess exactly pays for a crash hazard, so unconditional E[r] = required return = discount rate + crash-hazard premium. Van Oordt adds a transactional-demand FLOOR (a PV of net transactional benefits) plus an additive bubble term needing ongoing net inflows; Biais et al. calibrate that only ~5% of BTC return variance is fundamental (95% extrinsic/sunspot) and that crash risk made up ~11pp of the early required return. Schilling-Uhlig bound it below: if the speculative condition fails, BTC is a martingale (expected real return = real rate) and can rationally go to zero. For a 10-15yr BTC CMA this implies a modest expected return (an equity-like required return plus a crash premium survivors collect, NOT the realized 142%/65% survivor trail) with a fat left tail.
key_drivers: Required return / discount rate on risk capital (rho) - the equilibrium anchor; the bubble's EXPECTED return is pinned to this, not to realized history (Blanchard-Watson, Tirole, van Oordt)

Crash hazard rate h(t) and loss-given-crash - the survival-conditioned appreciation is rho + h(t)*LGC; over a 10-15yr horizon cumulative crash/total-loss probability drives the tail mass and the gap between conditional and unconditional return

Transactional-demand floor: present value of net transactional benefits per coin (the non-bubble component); its level and growth set the lower bound below which negative bubbles are ruled out (van Oordt; Biais et al.)

Net investment INFLOWS required to sustain the bubble term - rises with new-coin issuance and required return, falls with growth in transactional demand; a Ponzi-equivalent aggregate-cashflow condition (van Oordt)

Extrinsic / sunspot volatility share - Biais et al. calibrate ~95% of return variance as non-fundamental, implying multiple equilibria and a coordination (sunspot) risk that can shift the asset off the positive-value equilibrium

Speculative ('hodling') condition (Schilling-Uhlig): whether buyers hold coins back expecting appreciation; if it fails, BTC is a martingale with expected real return = real rate and fundamental value can be zero

Dynamic-(in)efficiency / r-vs-g (Tirole): a deterministic bubble grows at the interest rate and can only persist if the interest rate does not exceed the economy's growth rate - a macro feasibility constraint on indefinite real appreciation
pros: Theoretically rigorous and internally consistent: it is the ONLY family that derives an explicit equilibrium expected-return IDENTITY (E[r] = required return = discount rate + crash-hazard premium) from first-principles no-arbitrage, rather than extrapolating a price curve - directly answering 'what return should a rational holder expect' for a no-cashflow asset

Honestly bounds the upside: the no-arbitrage condition proves a rational bubble CANNOT deliver above-required-return expected appreciation indefinitely (else it outgrows all wealth), which is exactly the discipline a 10-15yr CMA needs against S2F/power-law/Metcalfe over-extrapolation - van Oordt explicitly rebuts the 'BTC grows to outweigh all wealth' critique

Cleanly separates a defensible transactional-demand FLOOR from the speculative bubble term (van Oordt, Biais), so the CMA can be stress-tested by zeroing the bubble and seeing what utility-floor support remains

Empirically calibrated, not just theoretical: Biais et al. (JoF 2023) construct net-transactional-benefit indices and quantify fundamentals at ~5% of return variance and crash risk at ~11pp of early required return - rare hard numbers in this literature

Provides a principled left-tail / total-loss mechanism (Schilling-Uhlig supermartingale to zero; Biais multiple-equilibria sunspot shift) that justifies the crash-hazard haircut other CMA rows apply by hand-waving
Peer-reviewed, top-journal provenance (Econometrica, Journal of Finance, JME) with no asset-promoter conflict of interest - the opposite of the sell-side TAM pieces
cons: It is a POSITIVE (price-formation) theory, not a forecasting model: it pins expected return to an exogenous 'required return' it does not itself estimate, and it admits MULTIPLE equilibria and extrinsic volatility, so it yields a return IDENTITY and a tail structure but no unique point appreciation - any CMA number must be bolted on by choosing rho and h(t)

The required-return identity says BTC's expected return is ~ordinary risk-required return, which sits FAR below realized history (142/65/17%/yr) - but that realized history is the survivor path, so the framework essentially says past returns are uninformative about forward expected returns, an uncomfortable, hard-to-calibrate stance

Biais et al. find ~95% of return variance is extrinsic/sunspot - i.e. the model explicitly concedes that fundamentals explain almost nothing, so point forecasts inherit enormous uncertainty and the framework predicts perpetual high vol and crash risk rather than a clean expected return

Crash hazard h(t) and loss-given-crash are essentially free parameters with little out-of-sample anchor; the CMA's central tendency and tail are highly sensitive to them, and the literature does not pin a 10-15yr hazard

Schilling-Uhlig's stark result (fundamental value can be zero; BTC a martingale with expected real return = the real rate when speculation fails) implies a near-zero real expected return in the no-speculation case - a legitimate but extreme bound that, taken literally, would zero out most of the CMA

Tirole's r-vs-g feasibility condition implies an ever-growing real bubble is generically infeasible in a dynamically efficient economy (r > g), so indefinite real appreciation is theoretically constrained - useful as a ceiling but it makes the model agnostic-to-bearish, not a basis for a high CMA

Silent on cross-asset correlations entirely: the framework models BTC in isolation (or vs a single dollar/consumption numeraire), so all correlation cells must be imported from realized data - the model contributes nothing to the gold/equity/FI/TIPS correlation question

synthesized_outputs.appreciation_nominal: ~7-11%/yr nominal UNCONDITIONAL expected (judgment, center ~9%), with a much higher ~20-30%/yr survival-CONDITIONAL path. Construction strictly from the framework's identity: unconditional E[r] = required return = discount rate (risk-free ~4% + a sizable risk premium for a ~95%-extrinsic-vol asset, ~5-7%) ~ 9-11%; this already INCLUDES the crash-hazard compensation, so it is NOT additive on top. The survival-conditional appreciation is required return + h*LGC, which with a ~3-5%/yr crash-to-deep-drawdown hazard and large LGC lands ~20-30%/yr while it persists - reconciling with BTC's realized decaying survivor trail (142->65->17%/yr) as exactly that: a survivor path. I anchor the CMA-relevant UNCONDITIONAL number at ~8-10%, below the trailing-5y realized 17%, because the no-arbitrage condition caps expected return at the required return and forbids the indefinite above-required appreciation that level-extrapolation models assume.
synthesized_outputs.appreciation_real: ~5-8%/yr real unconditional (subtract ~2.5-3% inflation), center ~6%. The Schilling-Uhlig floor case (expected real return = real rate, ~1.5-2%) is the bear bound if the speculative condition weakens; my central ~6% assumes the speculative/store-of-value equilibrium persists and survivors are compensated for crash risk. The honest framing is a distribution: a ~6% real survivor-weighted mean sitting above a real-rate floor and below the conditional path.
synthesized_outputs.volatility: ~55-65%/yr (judgment). The framework predicts perpetual high, mostly-extrinsic volatility (Biais ~95% non-fundamental) plus discrete crash risk, so vol should NOT compress toward equities; I anchor at realized trailing-5y ~57% as the floor with upside to ~65% from sunspot/multiple-equilibria instability. Realized return distribution is fat-left-tailed, not Gaussian - the sigma understates downside.

synthesized_outputs.notes: The point estimate is the WRONG summary: the framework's honest output is a distribution - a survival path (~20-30%/yr conditional, decaying) carrying most of the probability mass, plus a non-trivial total-loss/deep-collapse tail (Schilling-Uhlig to zero; Biais sunspot shift) - whose probability-weighted mean is the ~8-10% nominal / ~6% real unconditional figure. Key discipline this approach imposes on the cross-approach central (~8-12% nom): it provides the THEORETICAL JUSTIFICATION for why forward expected return must sit near a risk-required return and far below realized survivor history, and why the left tail is fat - it is the rigorous backbone for the haircut other rows apply ad hoc.

new_approaches.rich_notes:
METHODOLOGY. This family treats BTC's price, in the limit of zero discounted-cashflow fundamental, as a rational bubble in the Blanchard (1979) / Blanchard-Watson (1982) / Tirole (1985 Econometrica) tradition, ported to crypto by van Oordt (2024), Biais et al. (JoF 2023), and bounded below by Schilling-Uhlig (JME 2019). The load-bearing result is a no-arbitrage IDENTITY: in equilibrium the expected return on a price that contains a rational bubble component must EQUAL the ordinary required return on risk capital - 'as is the case for all other financial assets' (van Oordt, verbatim). The intuition van Oordt spells out is the standard rebuttal to the 'BTC will outgrow all wealth' critique: if a single asset's bubble earned above the common required return, its share of total wealth would grow without bound in expectation, which cannot be an equilibrium; if below, no one holds it. Hence E[r] = required return, full stop. With a Blanchard-Watson stochastic structure, the price 'grows at a faster speed than the required return as long as the bubble persists, but there is a positive probability the bubble will burst. The expected return on such a stochastic bubble path still equals the required return because the higher rate of appreciation is counterbalanced by the downside risk' (van Oordt, verbatim). That is the explicit 'required return + crash hazard' decomposition: survival-conditional drift = rho + h*LGC, unconditional E[r] = rho.

KEY RELATIONSHIPS. Van Oordt decomposes price into a transactional-demand FLOOR (a baseline-equilibrium path = the PV-analogue of net transactional benefits, below which negative bubbles are ruled out by an assumption) plus an additive bubble term. Sustaining the bubble requires ongoing NET INVESTMENT INFLOWS that rise with new-coin issuance and the required return and the level of transactional demand, and fall with growth in transactional demand; for non-negative money growth, bubble participants earn 'Ponzi-scheme equivalent payoffs in the aggregate' even though each individual's expected return meets their required return - a striking, honest framing. Biais et al. build the empirical counterpart: BTC fundamental value = stream of net transactional benefits (which themselves depend on future prices, a fixed point), PLUS sunspots => multiple equilibria and extrinsic volatility. Their calibration is the most useful hard output: changes in fundamentals explain only 'around 5%' of BTC return variance (so ~95% is extrinsic/sunspot); required WEEKLY BTC returns start above 10%/week early in 2011-19 and DECAY to ~2%/week by sample end; crash risk contributes ~11 percentage points of the early required return, declining thereafter, and illiquidity (difficulty exchanging BTC) adds ~10pp early dropping to ~8pp. Schilling-Uhlig provide the floor/martingale: with two intrinsically worthless currencies, the fundamental pricing equation makes the dollar BTC price a MARTINGALE (Q_t = E_t[Q_{t+1}]); BTC must 'rise in expectation and earn a real interest' ONLY if the speculative ('hodling') condition holds; under their Assumption 3 (mutual impatience) the speculative condition fails, so the fundamental pricing equation applies and BTC's expected real return equals the real rate, with fundamental value possibly zero - and the price can be a convergent supermartingale falling toward that zero. Tirole supplies the macro feasibility ceiling: a deterministic bubble grows at the gross interest rate and can persist only in a dynamically inefficient economy (r <= g); with r > g indefinite real appreciation is generically infeasible.

HISTORICAL FIT & FAILURE MODES. Empirically the appeal is that the framework PREDICTS what we observe - extreme, largely non-fundamental volatility (Biais ~95% extrinsic), recurrent crashes, and a required return that decays - without needing scarcity numerology. Its honesty about the left tail (Schilling-Uhlig collapse-to-zero, Biais sunspot equilibrium shift) is a genuine strength versus single-path level models. The failure modes are real: it is positive not normative, so it yields an identity and a distribution but no unique point CMA; the required return and crash hazard are exogenous free parameters; multiplicity means the model cannot tell you WHICH equilibrium obtains; and it is silent on every cross-asset correlation (all imported from realized data). Its starkest implication - that forward EXPECTED return is just a risk-required return (~high single digits to low teens), far below realized survivor history - is exactly what makes it the rigorous backbone for the appreciation-decay haircut, and exactly why bulls dislike it.

ON-RECORD MULTI-YEAR FORECASTS. The academic papers deliberately publish NO dated multi-year BTC price/return forecast - that abstention is itself a stance (they hold expected return is the required return and the rest is sunspot). The only quantified on-record outputs are Biais et al.'s calibrated required-return path (>10%/week -> ~2%/week, with ~11pp early crash-risk and ~10pp early illiquidity contributions) over 2011-2019, and Schilling-Uhlig's martingale/real-rate floor. No gold-parity, S2F-style, or power-law multi-million target exists in this family - and that is precisely its disciplinary value for a 10-15yr CMA.

issues: Tirole (1985) Prop 1(c) — the r-vs-g feasibility/'ceiling' the deep-dive leans on (bubble persists only if r<=g, dynamically inefficient economy) — was shown to be INCORRECT as stated by a recent Econometric Society comment (arXiv 2507.12477, 'Comment on Asset Bubbles and Overlapping Generations', published 2026-05). A counterexample economy satisfies all assumptions yet has a unique bubbleless equilibrium. The deep-dive cites this as a settled macro feasibility constraint; it is contested. Doesn't sink the framework (the no-arb identity is independent) but the specific ceiling claim is overstated.

The synthesized ~8-10% nominal / ~6% real UNCONDITIONAL center is a judgment overlay the framework does NOT produce, and the write-up's own cons admit this ('any CMA number must be bolted on by choosing rho and h(t)'; 'the point estimate is the WRONG summary'). The number is internally honest but the framework gives no independent validation of 9% vs, say, 5% or 13% — it is rho (~4% rf + 5-7% premium) hand-picked. The decomposition 'unconditional already INCLUDES crash compensation, NOT additive' is correctly applied (avoids double-counting), but the premium size is unanchored.

Mild internal tension between the Schilling-Uhlig floor and the chosen center. The deep-dive correctly flags S-U's no-speculation case (expected real return = real rate ~1.5-2%, fundamental value can be zero) as a 'bear bound,' then centers ~6% real assuming the speculative equilibrium persists. That is a defensible choice but it is an ASSUMPTION that the hodling/speculative condition holds for 10-15yr — exactly the condition S-U show can fail under mutual impatience. The center leans bullish relative to what the cited floor literature would support.

The crash-hazard survival-conditional path (~20-30%/yr 'while it persists') is presented as 'reconciling' the realized 142->65->17% decay as a survivor trail. This is a narrative fit, not a calibration — h(t) and LGC are admitted free parameters with 'no out-of-sample anchor' and 'the literature does not pin a 10-15yr hazard.' The 20-30% figure is illustrative, not derived; fine as long as it's not read as a forecast.

Biais required-return path is 2011-2019 weekly data; the decay to '2%/week' (~equiv to a very high annualized number, ~180%/yr if naively annualized, though it is a survival-conditional required return on a high-crash-risk asset) is from an EARLY, illiquid, small-cap regime. Using it to justify a forward 'decay' story is directionally sound but the levels are not transportable to a 2026 institutional/ETF-era BTC. The deep-dive uses it qualitatively (correct) but a careless reader could over-anchor.
verdict.corrections: "All falsifiable hard numbers verified verbatim against the Biais et al. (JoF 2023) working paper (TSE WP 973): 'required returns... start very high (above 10% per week), but then decline, to 2% at the end of the sample period'; 'Crash risk accounts for around 11 percentage points of the required return at the beginning of the sample period... decreases to close to zero'; 'the difficulty to exchange bitcoin against standard currency contributes almost 10 percentage points... drops to around eight percentage points'; '(around 5%) of the variance of bitcoin returns.' Attribution to Biais/Bisiere/Bouvard/Casamatta/Menkveld, JoF 78(2):967-1014, 2023 is correct. van Oordt (Tinbergen DP 24-050; SSRN 4913885; CEPR VoxEU 2024), Schilling-Uhlig (JME 2019, vol 106 pp16-26; NBER w24483 — martingale/mutual-impatience/no-speculation framing correct), Blanchard-Watson (NBER w945), and Tirole (Econometrica 53(6):1499-1528, 1985) citations are all real and correctly attributed. ONE correction: the deep-dive presents Tirole's r-vs-g feasibility ceiling as settled; flag that Tirole's Prop 1(c) has a published 2026 Econometric Society comment refuting it as stated — soften to 'a contested macro feasibility argument.' Realized anchors used in the synthesized correlations are credible: BTC-gold ~0 (independently confirmed near-zero since 2024), BTC-Nasdaq ~0.52 in 2025 (confirms the +0.40 to +0.55 growth-equity band; the ETF-era spike + partial-mean-reversion framing is reasonable). The synthesized ~55-65% vol floor anchored to trailing-5y ~57% is consistent with the framework's 'perpetual high mostly-extrinsic vol' prediction and is NOT hype — it correctly refuses equity-like vol compression. Net: numbers are real and correctly attributed; the framing is unusually honest (it is one of the few rows that ARGUES DOWN the appreciation rather than up). The only place it overreaches is asserting a single ~9% nominal center from a framework that yields only an identity — but the write-up itself repeatedly flags this, so it is disclosed overreach, not hidden hype."
overstated_pros: 'Empirically calibrated, not just theoretical' — overstated in transportability: the Biais calibration is 2011-2019, pre-ETF, dominated by an illiquid micro-cap regime; the hard numbers are real but their forward relevance to a 2026 institutional BTC is weak. The pro oversells how much the calibration constrains a 10-15yr CMA (it constrains the SHAPE/decay, not the level).

'Provides a principled left-tail / total-loss mechanism that justifies the crash-hazard haircut other rows apply by hand-waving' — partially overstated: Schilling-Uhlig's collapse-to-zero is a sunspot/coordination result with no estimated probability, and Biais' crash hazard is calibrated to the early sample only. The mechanism is principled but the MAGNITUDE of the tail is as hand-wavy here as elsewhere; the framework gives the existence of the tail, not its mass.

'The no-arbitrage condition proves a rational bubble CANNOT deliver above-required-return expected appreciation indefinitely' — correct as a theorem but the pro slightly overstates its bite for a FINITE 10-15yr horizon: the 'indefinitely / outgrows all wealth' argument is an infinite-horizon limit; over 10-15yr a bubble can and historically did run well above required return conditional on survival. The discipline is real but applies to the unconditional expectation, not the path, which the bull case cares about.
missing_cons: Survivorship in the FRAMEWORK SELECTION itself: this row treats BTC's non-collapse as the conditioning event, but offers no probability that the speculative equilibrium SURVIVES 10-15yr. The whole ~6% real center is conditional on the hodling equilibrium persisting — an unmodeled, unestimated survival probability that should be a headline caveat, not buried.

Numeraire / denomination risk omitted: Schilling-Uhlig's martingale and the entire 'expected real return = real rate' floor are stated against a stable-dollar numeraire. If the relevant CMA question is BTC vs a debased fiat (the actual bull thesis), the framework is silent — it cannot speak to the monetary-debasement channel that motivates most BTC allocations. This is a real blind spot, not just 'silent on correlations.'

No treatment of regime change from ETF/institutionalization: the framework is regime-invariant (infinite-horizon OLG), but the realized correlation spike (BTC-Nasdaq 0.23->0.52) shows the asset's beta is non-stationary. A CMA built on this row implicitly assumes the high-beta-risk-asset regime is structural; the framework cannot tell you whether the next 10-15yr looks like the speculative regime or a transactional-utility regime — the two give very different correlations and the row picks one.

Liquidity/issuance dynamics are stale: van Oordt's 'net inflows to sustain the bubble rise with new-coin issuance' — but BTC issuance is asymptotically zero (post-2140 ~0, halvings drive it down). The con-set never notes that the issuance term the model leans on is mechanically shrinking, which actually WEAKENS the inflow-requirement bear argument over a 10-15yr horizon. Missing nuance that cuts against the bearish framing.

new_approaches.name: Equation-of-Exchange Velocity Network-Utility Valuation (Burniske MV=PQ)
new_approaches.description: A bottom-up "absolute valuation" for a no-cashflow cryptoasset that solves the equation of exchange MV=PQ for the monetary base M = PQ/V, where PQ is the cryptonetwork's own on-chain economic THROUGHPUT (its "GDP" — price P of the provisioned digital resource times quantity Q, with speculative/exchange-shuttle volume stripped out), and V is velocity (annual turnover of the float). Dividing M by circulating supply (excluding hodled/bonded coins, which have velocity 0) yields a Current Utility Value (CUV) per token; the model then discounts a single FUTURE utility value back at a high crypto risk rate (Burniske 30-50%, ~3-5x equities) to get today's rational price. Distinct from #8 (QTM as a static identity backing a price out of an assumed aggregate transaction-volume scenario): here PQ is built up from the protocol's own modeled adoption S-curve and resource economics, and V is the explicit, decade-dynamic central lever rather than a single plugged number. Distinct from NVT (#3), a mean-reversion ratio that never solves for a fair M. A 10-15yr CMA falls out as forward return ≈ PQ-growth MINUS velocity drift: rising on-chain economic throughput pushes M up, while falling velocity (decade-low, HODL/ETF-driven) is itself a tailwind (lower V raises M for given PQ) — but both compress as the network matures, forcing appreciation decay.
new_approaches.medium_explanation: Burniske inverts the monetary identity MV=PQ to size the monetary base a cryptoeconomy needs: M = PQ/V. PQ is the network's "GDP" — the real on-chain transaction volume it settles (speculative exchange shuttling, ~30%+ of raw volume, is excluded). V is velocity, the float's annual turnover. Divide M by the circulating, non-hodled supply to get a Current Utility Value per coin; markets price the future, so you discount a chosen future-year utility value back at a steep 30-50% crypto discount rate. A 10-15yr BTC CMA emerges as expected return ≈ growth in real on-chain throughput (PQ) minus the drift in velocity, plus the decaying re-rating as a higher-adoption scenario becomes more probable. Two forces matter: PQ compounds as adoption rises but decelerates on an S-curve, and BTC velocity is at decade lows (>70% of supply dormant, ETF cold storage), which mechanically lifts M. The catch: velocity is empirically unstable and unforecastable, and the discount rate dominates the answer — so the framework is more disciplined story than reliable forecast.
key_drivers: Real on-chain economic throughput PQ (the cryptonetwork 'GDP') — modeled bottom-up from resource price P (e.g. declining unit cost) and quantity Q via TAM x adoption S-curve x penetration, NOT raw on-chain volume (30%+ is exchange shuttling/speculation and is stripped out)

Velocity V — the single most sensitive and central lever; turnover of the active float. Burniske derives BTC hybrid V~6.5 (2016) from ~54% hodlers + ~46% transactional, and a transactional V~14; forward V is the dominant unknown. Crucially, FALLING velocity (BTC at decade lows, >70% dormant) is a price TAILWIND under M=PQ/V
Hodl / dormant-coin fraction — coins held off-market (velocity 0) are removed from the float denominator, raising CUV per token; the SoV-vs-MoE tension lives inside the identity
Discount rate (30-50%, ~3-5x risky equities) applied to a single future utility value — economically the expected return; tiny changes swing the present price ~2x (30% vs 40%)

Adoption-scenario probability / target transaction-share state the market believes BTC will occupy — price re-rates as belief climbs toward a ceiling (a decaying, one-time re-rating, not a perpetual growth rate)
Circulating supply M_supply (near-deterministic 21M issuance schedule) — converts the required monetary base into a per-coin price
pros: Genuinely 'absolute' / bottom-up: unlike NVT (a ratio) or S2F (supply-only), it solves for a fair monetary base from the network's OWN modeled economic throughput, and forces an explicit, auditable adoption story (P, Q, V, discount rate) you can stress one lever at a time

Makes velocity an explicit, first-class lever and captures a mechanism the other models miss: BTC's decade-low, still-falling velocity (HODL + ETF cold storage, >70% dormant) is a structural PRICE TAILWIND under M=PQ/V (lower V raises the required base) — a real, observable dynamic

Naturally produces appreciation DECAY: PQ growth decelerates on an adoption S-curve and the scenario re-rating is a one-time climb toward a ceiling, so the framework does not assume constant high returns forever — the correct qualitative shape for a maturing-asset CMA

Grounded in standard monetary economics (equation of exchange) and refutable: Zochowski/Winton extended it (nth-order investors, Fair Token Value) and the arXiv 2024 paper tested it empirically, so it has a real critique-and-improvement literature rather than pure narrative
cons: Velocity is empirically UNSTABLE and unforecastable — the load-bearing input. The arXiv (2024) empirical test finds V 'fluctuates dramatically' across coins and time, historical fits are poor, and forward predictions diverge substantially from realized prices ('better at post-hoc explanation than genuine forecasting'). The whole CMA pivots on a parameter the data says you cannot pin down

Severe circularity and discount-rate dominance: the answer is essentially the analyst's chosen 30-50% discount rate (a 30% vs 40% rate ~doubles the price), and 'future market prices themselves depend on further future expectations' (Burniske concedes the infinite-recursion-of-expectations problem is unresolved)

PQ (the 'GDP') is badly contaminated and structurally leaking: raw on-chain volume overstates economic throughput ~3x (change outputs, self-spends, exchange shuttling), while real BTC activity increasingly migrates to Lightning/L2, exchange-internal ledgers and ETF custody that never touch the base chain — so the numerator is breaking exactly as institutionalization deepens

Conflates store-of-value and medium-of-exchange in one identity: the same falling velocity that boosts M as a 'tailwind' also signals BTC is NOT being used as a transactional network (the velocity 'problem' Zochowski debates) — so PQ-as-payments-GDP shrinks while the SoV reading dominates, and the framework cannot cleanly tell you which regime it is valuing

Burniske himself refuses to publish a BTC price target with it and disavowed his earlier (2015 ARK) ~$2,000/BTC equation-of-exchange estimate as methodologically flawed — the originator does not treat it as a reliable point-forecast engine
Silent on volatility and cross-asset correlations — it is a level/utility-value model, so every risk-and-correlation CMA cell must be imported from realized data or another framework
