new_approaches.rich_notes:
WHAT MAKES THIS DISTINCT. Unlike #5 (one-way terminal-share-of-gold sizing, gold's own return not a building block, no reversion anchor) and #6 (BTC-on-M2 elasticity), this family makes a cross-asset RATIO the forecast primitive and uses the comparator's OWN return as numeraire. The cleanest decomposition: E[BTC nominal return] = (1 + reversion of the BTC/gold ratio toward a fair band) x (1 + gold's own expected return) - 1. Gold's appreciation is thus an explicit input, and a mean-reversion/Z-score anchor (which #5/#6 lack) supplies the pull-back force.

THE FOUR SUB-MODELS, with on-record multi-year forecasts.
(1) BTC/gold ratio + Z-score (Bitcoin Magazine Pro / The Block / CCN): ratio measured in oz-gold-per-BTC. Jan-2026 ~17.6-20, down ~50% from ~40 in Dec-2024 as gold rallied to ~$5,100; bull markets >30-35, risk-off <20. WisdomTree's model-implied 'fair' ratio is ~21. A sub-2 Z-score flagged BTC cheap-vs-gold in Mar-2020 (BTC then +1,170% over the next year) and Nov-2022 (BTC +~150% over the next year). Scripted: ratio 17.6->21 over 12.5y + 5% gold = ~6.5%/yr BTC; 17.6->30 + 6% gold = ~10.6%/yr.
(2) WisdomTree hard-money basket — explicit on-record 2030 forecasts. Basket = global M2 x H (hard-money share of M2; gold historically 10% calm to >30% inflationary, median ~15%) x B (BTC's share of the gold+BTC basket; ~8% at snapshot, modeled rising to ~15% by 2030). Three M2 regimes: deflationary 3% -> BTC ~$120-135k / gold $3,000; base 5%, H~15%, B~15% -> BTC ~$250k / gold ~$4,000 by 2030; inflationary 7%, H toward 20%+, B faster -> BTC >$500k (~35% CAGR) / gold >$5,500. This JOINTLY forecasts gold, the signature feature.
(3) CoinShares four-pool TAM 2025 — on-record to 2039. Pools (May-2025): Global M2 $217.3T, CB FX reserves $18.2T, corporate treasuries $17.8T, gold $16.5T; total $269.8T (up ~21% from $170.3T in 2022). Per-pool capture rates run on a Verhulst S-curve over a fixed 2009-2039 horizon. Reference points: 1% of all pools -> ~$104k; 2% M2 + 5% gold -> $189k; 2% M2 + 20% gold -> $261k; and crucially the BASELINE (3.5% overall share) -> only ~$62k/BTC by 2039. Off ~$110k spot that baseline is a NEGATIVE ~-4%/yr return — the single most honest, least-cited number in the entire BTC-CMA literature, and it comes from a long-BTC issuer's own model. CoinShares flags pool overlap (gold inside CB reserves; treasuries inside M2) as overstating TAM.
(4) Doeswijk-Lam-Swinkels Global Market Portfolio (RAPS 2020) — the falsifiable bar. The invested global multi-asset market portfolio realized ~4.45% real / 11.2% vol (1960-2017). BTC added in 2017 would have weighed just 0.09% (HY bonds were 21x bigger). Today BTC (~$2.2T) is ~0.3-0.8% of ~$175-261T investable wealth. Scripted: BTC to 1% of a grown $330T portfolio in 12.5y = ~3.3%/yr; to 2% = ~9.2%/yr; to 0.5% = -2.3%/yr. This variant cannot be inflated by narrative — it pins BTC to its equilibrium weight in ALL wealth.

HISTORICAL FIT / FAILURE MODES. The reversion premise is the weak link: the BTC/gold ratio fell 50% in 2025 with NO mechanical pull-back, and with only 3-4 cycles the 'fair' band (21) is curve-fit, not structural. Deeper still — using a ratio as the primitive and gold's return as numeraire REQUIRES BTC and gold to be co-moving substitutes, yet realized BTC-gold correlation is ~0 (full -0.01, 5y +0.04). Dividing two near-uncorrelated assets does not produce a stable reverting ratio; the ratio's swings are mostly BTC's own equity-beta noise. The level-pinning (WisdomTree basket = M2 LEVEL x shares) reintroduces the same non-stationary trend-on-trend spuriousness that sinks #6. And provenance is conflicted: WisdomTree (BTCW) and CoinShares (BTC ETPs) are long-BTC issuers; their bullish scenarios are where the optimism hides.

THE PUNCHLINE FOR A 10-15YR CMA. Run to its own discipline, this family is far MORE humbling than gold-parity hype: ratio-reversion + gold return clusters ~6-11%/yr, market-portfolio-share to 1-2% gives ~3-9%/yr, and CoinShares' baseline is outright negative. Synthesized central ~7-11% nominal / ~4-8% real, vol ~50-60%, BTC-gold corr ~0.05-0.20 (I credit a small premium for shared debasement narrative but reject the high co-movement the ratio framing assumes). The framework's value is less as a point estimate than as a falsifiable discipline — and its honest verdict is that most of the gold-substitution upside is already in the price.

issues: WisdomTree inflationary 2030 BTC target is $475,000 in the actual source (Advisor Perspectives / Armchair Trader / Cryptonews), NOT '>$500k' as the doc states repeatedly (cited_outputs, key_drivers, rich_notes, cons). Gold inflationary is '>$7,000/oz' in source vs doc's '>$5,500'. The doc rounds the bull case UP, which is the opposite of the 'I deliberately discount marketing scenarios' posture it claims.

CoinShares total-TAM breakdown is unverified and likely inflated. Doc gives M2 $217.3T + CB reserves $18.2T + treasuries $17.8T + gold $16.5T = $269.8T 'total $269.8T (up ~21% from $170.3T in 2022)'. But $170.3T x 1.21 = ~$206T, not $269.8T. CoinShares' own page states ~21% growth over three years AND that BTC is '1.1% of monetary markets as of June 2025'. The $269.8T sum and the +21% claim are internally inconsistent; the per-pool figures could not be confirmed in the primary text.

Doeswijk variant mis-attributes provenance and uses contested figures. The doc claims BTC '~0.09% of all investable wealth in 2017' with 'HY bonds 21x bigger' and brands it 'peer-reviewed, externally-anchored.' The actual 2017 BTC application (Seeking Alpha/Nasdaq 'Bitcoin As An Asset Class') gives 0.03% and 'HY bonds >50x bigger.' Critically the Doeswijk-Lam-Swinkels RAPS 2020 / FAJ 2014 papers NEVER mention Bitcoin -- the BTC weight is a third-party blog application of the framework, not a peer-reviewed result. The 'rare empirical discipline / cannot be inflated by narrative' pro oversells a non-peer-reviewed estimate.
CoinShares $261k (2% M2 + 20% gold) is computed by the doc as ~7%/yr off $110k spot; actual is ~6.4%/yr over 2025-2039. Minor upward rounding, consistently in the bullish direction.

The doc's '21 fair ratio' is repeatedly attributed to 'WisdomTree model-implied fair ~21,' but WisdomTree's published model forecasts gold and BTC LEVELS, not a ratio target -- '21' is the doc's own derived implication (250k/4000 = 62.5x in 2030, or back-solved), not a number WisdomTree publishes as a 'fair ratio.' Presenting it as a source-published anchor overstates external grounding for the reversion premise (which the doc itself elsewhere debunks).

Pool double-counting is correctly flagged as a con but the doc still REPORTS the naive $269.8T sum as 'the TAM' in key_drivers and rich_notes without ever netting it down -- so the headline pie it cites is one it concedes is overstated, yet uses anyway to frame capture scenarios.
verdict.corrections: Fix WisdomTree inflationary BTC to $475,000 (gold >$7,000) everywhere; stop writing '>$500k.' Reconcile the CoinShares TAM: either use ~$206T (consistent with +21% off $170.3T and the published '1.1% of monetary markets' anchor) or cite the exact per-pool table from the CoinShares 2025 PDF with the as-of date -- do not assert $269.8T as 'up 21%' since those two are arithmetically incompatible. Re-label the Doeswijk variant: 0.03% (2017, per the actual application) with HY '>50x', and state explicitly that the BTC weight is a THIRD-PARTY blog application of the Doeswijk framework, not a peer-reviewed paper result -- the RAPS 2020 paper contains no Bitcoin. Soften the 'peer-reviewed falsifiable bar' pro accordingly. Attribute the '~21 fair ratio' as the doc's own back-solved implication of WisdomTree's 2030 levels, not a WT-published target. Net the four pools down for overlap before quoting any TAM headline, or drop the headline sum. Recompute the $261k case as ~6.4%/yr. The synthesized central (7-11% nominal / 4-8% real, vol 50-60%, gold corr 0.05-0.20) is defensible and NOT hype: it sits below trailing-5y realized 17%, brackets the 57% vol floor (with only mild compression), and the gold corr at 0.05-0.20 is generously above realized (-0.011 full / +0.045 5y) but the doc explicitly flags this as a credited debasement-narrative premium and rejects the high co-movement the ratio framing assumes -- that is honest, not overstated.
overstated_pros: 'Peer-reviewed, externally-anchored falsifiable bar that cannot be inflated by narrative' (Doeswijk) -- the BTC weight is a non-peer-reviewed blog application; the cited paper has no Bitcoin. Overstated.

'The ratio carries a genuine mean-reversion anchor with falsifiable Z-score bands' -- with only 3-4 cycles and the ratio falling 50% in 2025 with no pull-back (which the doc itself flags as the deepest flaw in cons), calling the anchor 'genuine' in pros is in tension with the doc's own verdict that a reverting ratio between two ~uncorrelated assets is not structurally stable. The pro overstates a force the doc elsewhere debunks.

'Decomposable and stress-testable... both publish full scenario tables' -- WisdomTree publishes scenario outputs but the H and B lever values are sparsely documented (median H~15%, B 8->15% are loosely sourced); 'audit the math' overstates the reproducibility of the published tables.
The '~21 fair ratio' as a WisdomTree-published mean-reversion anchor -- it is the doc's own derived number, lending false external authority to the reversion premise.
missing_cons: Survivorship/issuer-selection in the source set: BOTH numeric-forecast providers (WisdomTree=BTCW, CoinShares=BTC ETPs) are long-BTC issuers. The doc flags conflict of interest but does not note that there is NO independent (academic or short/neutral) cross-asset-ratio forecaster in the family -- the entire numeric backbone is two conflicted sellers, so the 'honest low number' is itself issuer-sourced.

The CoinShares baseline ($62k/2039, negative) is the LEAST-marketed scenario from its own model; the doc leans on it as the family's 'most honest number' but a sell-side issuer's de-emphasized downside case is not necessarily its true central view -- selection of which scenario to anchor on is the analyst smuggling in a regime view, the same critique the doc levels at the family.

Ratio mechanics under fixed BTC supply: BTC/gold oz-ratio rises mechanically as gold's above-ground stock grows ~1.5-2%/yr while BTC issuance falls -- part of any 'reversion to a higher ratio' is a supply artifact, not monetary substitution. Not addressed.

No treatment of the denominator instability: when gold itself is in a sharp rally (2025, gold to ~$5,100), the ratio falls for reasons unrelated to BTC's monetary thesis, so the 'BTC cheap vs gold' signal fires precisely when gold momentum is strongest -- a known whipsaw the Z-score backtest (n=2-3 events) cannot rule out as luck.

Liquidity/absorption realism: capturing 2% of $217T M2 or 20% of gold implies multi-trillion BTC inflows the doc never sizes against actual annual flow capacity -- the TAM is a stock target with no flow feasibility check.
Tax/custody/regulatory tail risk (confiscation, ETF unwind, protocol risk) entirely absent -- relevant to a 10-15yr hold and to the 70-80% drawdown survivability the doc flags but does not quantify.

new_approaches.name: Equity-Beta-Implied / Public-Proxy-Implied Expected Return (Levered Nasdaq, MSTR mNAV, Miner NAV)
new_approaches.description: This approach imports the equity building block Bitcoin structurally lacks (no cashflow, no CAPE, no dividend, no GDP growth) by treating BTC as a high-beta equity and rearranging CAPM: E[BTC] = Rf + beta x ERP, where beta is BTC's measured sensitivity to a growth-equity benchmark (Nasdaq-100). The historical realized beta is large — Sherwood/practitioners cite ~4.6 to the NDX over the past decade, with shorter-window rolling betas swinging from negative to far higher. The key methodological move is to DECAY that beta toward ~1.5-2.5 as institutionalization (ETFs, treasury vehicles, options) compresses BTC's leverage and idiosyncratic vol, then run the CAPM forward off a normalized equity return (Rf ~3.5-4.5%, ERP ~4-5%), landing a forward nominal CMA roughly in the low-double-digits (~8-16%, central ~10-12%). The estimate is cross-checked against BTC-proxy EQUITY quotes that the market actually prices: MSTR's mNAV premium (VanEck/Sigel: +112% premium, with the premium itself carrying a ~1.77 beta to BTC and embedding a market-implied terminal BTC price/quantity/discount-rate) and bitcoin-miner NAV premia/discounts. These proxies reveal an embedded forward expected return and the leverage/vol the equity market assigns to BTC. Distinct from factor-regression approaches (which estimate loadings to explain variance, never invert a dominant equity beta into a forward level) and from derivatives-implied forwards (which read the futures/options curve): here the source of the forward is the EQUITY market — either CAPM run on BTC's equity beta, or the prices of levered BTC equities.
new_approaches.medium_explanation: BTC has no cashflow, so the standard equity CMA blocks (CAPE, dividend yield, real GDP, buybacks) don't apply. This approach borrows the equity premium through beta. CAPM rearranged: E[BTC] = Rf + beta x ERP. BTC's realized beta to the Nasdaq-100 has been roughly 4.6 over the past decade (Sherwood), so naively E[BTC] = 4% + 4.6 x 5% ~ 27%/yr. But that beta is unstable (it went negative in 2025) and is structurally falling as ETFs, MSTR-style treasuries, and listed options institutionalize the asset. Decaying beta toward 1.5-2.5 lands the forward at ~11-16%; a further haircut for BTC's fat left tail / non-survivorship pushes the central case to ~8-12% nominal. The view is cross-checked against equities the market actually quotes on BTC: MSTR's +112% mNAV premium and miner NAV premia/discounts embed a market-implied forward BTC price, leverage, and vol. Implication for a 10-15yr CMA: a decaying-beta CAPM is one of the few frameworks that mechanically produces appreciation decay AND a high vol/high equity-correlation profile consistent with realized data.
key_drivers: BTC's measured beta to a growth-equity benchmark (Nasdaq-100 ~4.6 over the past decade; rolling betas range from negative to far higher) — the single most important and most unstable input

The beta-decay assumption: how fast institutionalization (spot ETFs, MSTR/treasury vehicles, listed options, deeper liquidity) compresses BTC's leverage and idiosyncratic vol toward a normalized 1.5-2.5
Equity risk premium (ERP) assumed for the growth-equity benchmark (~4-5%) and the risk-free rate (~3.5-4.5%) — the building blocks BTC borrows
MSTR mNAV premium (VanEck/Sigel: +112%) and its ~1.77 beta to BTC, which embeds a market-implied terminal BTC quantity, future BTC price, and discount rate
Bitcoin-miner equity NAV premia/discounts (MARA, RIOT, CLSK, CIFR) as a second equity-market read on embedded leverage and forward BTC expectations (now muddied by HPC/AI pivots)
MSTR/proxy realized volatility (~113%) vs BTC (~55%) — the equity vehicles reveal the leverage multiplier the market assigns
Regime instability of the beta itself (risk-on vs risk-off; the 2025 decoupling where BTC-NDX beta turned faintly negative)
pros: Solves the core BTC-CMA problem directly: it imports a defensible equity expected-return building block (Rf + ERP) that BTC otherwise lacks, instead of extrapolating price history or scarcity numerology — uniquely well-suited to a no-cashflow asset

A DECAYING-beta CAPM mechanically produces appreciation decay (the correct qualitative shape: 142->65->17%/yr realized) AND simultaneously delivers the high-vol, high-equity-correlation profile that matches realized data — internally consistent across multiple CMA cells, unlike scarcity/network models that are demand-blind and correlation-silent

It is cross-checked against PRICES the market actually quotes (MSTR mNAV, miner NAV) — a genuine market-implied forward, not just a modeler's assumption; VanEck explicitly decomposes the MSTR premium into terminal BTC quantity x future price x discount rate
Transparent and falsifiable: every lever (beta, decay path, ERP, Rf) is observable and stress-testable; the equity proxies are liquid and continuously re-priced
Honestly frames BTC as what the data says it is — a high-beta growth-equity proxy — rather than a safe-haven/digital-gold story the realized correlations (~0 to gold) contradict
cons: Beta is wildly unstable and regime-dependent: the same Sherwood data shows BTC's NDX beta swung from ~4.6 to faintly NEGATIVE within 2025. A forward CMA built on a number that flips sign is fragile, and the whole framework hinges on an unfalsifiable decay-path assumption (how fast 4.6 -> 1.5-2.5)

CAPM is the wrong null for a fat-tailed, non-normal, partly-bubble-driven asset: BTC violates CAPM's mean-variance/normality assumptions, has large idiosyncratic (non-systematic) risk that CAPM ignores, and its single-path realized beta cannot price catastrophic-failure tail mass — so the inverted expected return is overstated unless explicitly haircut

Circularity / reflexivity in the equity proxies: MSTR's +112% mNAV premium is itself a function of BTC price and sentiment (premium has ~1.77 beta to BTC), so 'reading a forward' off MSTR partly reads BTC's own price back to itself; miner NAVs are now contaminated by HPC/AI-datacenter pivots that decouple them from BTC entirely (JPMorgan miner re-rating)

ERP and Rf are themselves contested inputs (ERP 4-6% range), and applying a SINGLE equity ERP to an asset whose risk is mostly idiosyncratic and non-equity (regulatory, custody, protocol, liquidity) is a category stretch — the 'equity premium' BTC borrows may not be the right premium

The proxies are sell-side/long conflicted (VanEck runs BTC products; MSTR/miners are promoting their own premium) and the framework can be tuned to almost any answer by choosing the beta window and decay speed

synthesized_outputs.appreciation_nominal: ~9-13%/yr nominal, central ~11% (judgment). Derivation: run CAPM forward with a DECAYING beta. Early-horizon beta is high (realized ~4.6) but unstable; institutionalization (ETFs, MSTR-style treasuries, listed options, deeper liquidity) compresses it toward ~1.5-2.5 by the back half of a 10-15yr window. A terminal beta of ~1.8-2.2 with Rf ~3.75% and ERP ~4.5% gives ~12-14%; I then haircut ~1-3 pts for BTC's fat left tail / non-survivorship that single-path CAPM ignores, landing ~9-13%. This sits squarely inside the realized-decay extrapolation (142->65->17%/yr) and the honest cross-approach central of ~8-12%.
synthesized_outputs.appreciation_real: ~6-10%/yr real, central ~8% (subtracting ~2.5-3% long-run US inflation). Judgment.
synthesized_outputs.volatility: ~55-60%/yr (judgment). The equity-proxy read (BTC ~55%, MSTR ~113%) confirms BTC sits at the realized ~57% floor; beta compression lowers the multiplier on the vehicles but the underlying asset vol stays multiples of equities across the horizon. No credible compression below ~50% within 10-15yr.
synthesized_outputs.corr_growth_eq: +0.45 to +0.65, central ~0.55 (judgment). This is the framework's core claim and matches realized trailing-5y 0.56; I assume partial mean-reversion of the ETF-era spike but BTC stays moderately-to-strongly tied to growth/tech equities — the asset IS a levered NDX proxy in this model.
synthesized_outputs.corr_value_eq: +0.25 to +0.40, central ~0.33 (judgment; realized 5y 0.37). Lower than growth-equity beta; value shares less of BTC's liquidity/duration sensitivity.
synthesized_outputs.corr_fi_nominal: +0.10 to +0.25, central ~0.18 (judgment; realized 5y 0.19). Low-positive via shared liquidity/real-rate channel of the marginal institutional holder.
synthesized_outputs.corr_tips: +0.20 to +0.35, central ~0.28 (judgment; realized 5y 0.30). Slightly above nominal FI through the real-rate/liquidity channel.
synthesized_outputs.corr_gold: ~0.0-0.15, central ~0.05 (judgment). The framework treats BTC as a growth-equity proxy, NOT digital gold; realized BTC-gold correlation is ~0 (full -0.01, 5y +0.04) and fell post-ETF. I keep it low and explicitly reject the gold-substitute reading — this approach's whole logic is that BTC borrows the EQUITY premium, not gold's monetary premium.
synthesized_outputs.notes: Central case ~11% nominal / ~8% real, vol ~57%, equity corr ~0.55, gold corr ~0.05. The framework is unusually self-consistent across CMA cells (decaying beta -> appreciation decay + high vol + high equity corr all at once), but its forward number is only as good as the unfalsifiable beta-decay path. I deliberately anchor to the decayed-beta + tail-haircut result, NOT the undecayed ~4.6 beta that implies an indefensible ~27%/yr.

new_approaches.rich_notes:
METHODOLOGY. Two coupled mechanisms. (1) CAPM-inverted equity beta. BTC has no cashflow, so instead of building an expected return from CAPE/dividends/GDP, you borrow the equity premium through beta: E[BTC] = Rf + beta x ERP. The load-bearing input is BTC's beta to a growth-equity benchmark. Sherwood News reports BTC's beta to the Nasdaq-100 averaged ~4.6 over the past decade ('if the NDX rallied 1% in a week, BTC up ~4.6%'). Run naively (Rf 4%, ERP 5%) that yields ~27%/yr — far too high for a 10-15yr CMA and exactly the level the realized-decay anchor rejects. The methodological discipline is to DECAY beta toward 1.5-2.5 as institutionalization compresses BTC's leverage; a terminal beta ~2 lands ~14%, ~1.5 lands ~11.5%, and a left-tail haircut pushes the central case to ~8-12%. (2) Public-proxy / equity-market read. Rather than assume the beta, read it (and an embedded forward) off equities the market actually quotes on BTC. VanEck's Matthew Sigel ('Deconstructing Strategy', 2025) decomposes MSTR: a +112% mNAV premium to combined fair value of its BTC + software; the premium alone drives 96.56% of returns and 87.48% of vol and carries an 'approximate beta of 1.77 to BTC'; MSTR realized vol ~113% vs BTC ~55%. Critically Sigel states the premium reflects 'market expectations around Strategy's future Bitcoin holdings' decomposed into terminal BTC quantity x projected future BTC price x discount rate — i.e. the equity market is pricing an implied forward BTC view, which can be backed out. Bitcoin-miner equities (MARA, RIOT, CLSK, CIFR) give a second NAV-premium/discount read on embedded leverage.

KEY RELATIONSHIPS. The framework is internally consistent across CMA cells in a way scarcity/network models are not: a high-but-decaying beta simultaneously delivers (a) appreciation DECAY, (b) high realized vol (~55-60%), and (c) high, rising equity correlation (~0.55) — all matching the realized anchor (142->65->17%/yr; vol floor ~57%; equity corr rising; gold corr ~0). It explicitly frames BTC as a levered growth-equity proxy, NOT digital gold — consistent with the realized BTC-gold correlation of ~0 and the post-ETF >50% drop in that correlation.

HISTORICAL FIT & FAILURE MODES. The beta is the Achilles heel. Sherwood's own data shows it is NOT stable: from March to mid-October 2025 the weekly BTC-NDX beta was 'faintly negative,' then spiked again near $100k. A CMA built on a number that changes sign is fragile; the decay-path assumption is unfalsifiable ex-ante. CAPM is also the wrong null for a fat-tailed, non-normal asset with large idiosyncratic risk (regulatory, custody, protocol) that CAPM ignores — so the single-equity-ERP it borrows is a category stretch, and the single-path realized beta cannot price BTC's catastrophic left tail. The proxies add reflexivity: MSTR's premium has ~1.77 beta to BTC, so reading a 'forward' off MSTR partly reads BTC's own price back to itself; miner NAVs are now muddied by HPC/AI-datacenter pivots (JPMorgan's late-2025 miner re-rating upgraded CLSK/CIFR on HPC, cut MARA/RIOT), decoupling them from pure BTC exposure. The academic anchor (Sanhaji & Chevallier, Econometrics 2023) validates that BTC's systematic beta is real, time-varying, and best measured with high-frequency 'realized' betas — but the authors frame it as a RISK-tracking (variance-explaining) tool for portfolio risk dashboards, NOT a device to invert into a forward expected return. That is the honest boundary: the literature supports measuring BTC's equity beta; inverting a dominant, unstable beta into a 10-15yr forward level is the practitioner's leap, not an academically blessed result.

ON-RECORD MULTI-YEAR FORECASTS. No firm publishes a clean CAPM-inverted 10-15yr BTC CMA. The closest on-record artifacts are: (i) the implied forward embedded in VanEck's MSTR premium decomposition (terminal quantity x future price x discount rate), which is a market-implied forward but not annualized; and (ii) the mechanical CAPM range itself (~11.5-27%/yr depending on the beta assumed). My synthesized central ~11% nominal / ~8% real, vol ~55-60%, equity corr ~0.55, gold corr ~0.05 reflects a decayed-beta CAPM haircut for tail risk, deliberately anchored to the realized-decay path rather than to the undecayed ~4.6 beta that would imply an indefensible ~27%/yr.

issues: DATE/ATTRIBUTION ERROR (material): The Sherwood article ('Bitcoin reclaims status as hyper-leveraged play') is dated Nov 22, 2024, not 2025 as the entry's representative_sources claims. More importantly, the 'faintly negative beta' decoupling period it describes ran March-mid-October 2024, NOT 2025. The deep-dive repeatedly asserts 'the 2025 decoupling where BTC-NDX beta turned faintly negative' (cons #1, key_drivers #7, rich_notes). This mis-dates the single most-cited instability evidence by a full year. The 4.6 'past decade' beta itself is correctly quoted but is a trailing-decade figure anchored to late-2024, now ~18 months stale.

OVERSTATED VANECK DECOMPOSITION: The entry repeatedly states VanEck/Sigel 'explicitly decomposes the MSTR premium into terminal BTC quantity x future price x discount rate' (pros #3, key_drivers #4, description, medium_explanation). VanEck's actual piece lists FOUR qualitative premium drivers (future BTC-holding growth expectations, regulatory access constraints, recognition of Saylor leverage, speculation) and does NOT publish a three-factor quantity x price x discount-rate mathematical backout. The 'market-implied forward you can invert' is the practitioner's analytical gloss, not VanEck's stated method. rich_notes half-admits this ('which can be backed out') but the pros/key_drivers present it as VanEck's explicit output.

SELF-REFUTING ANCHOR: The entry's strongest claim of internal consistency ('decaying beta mechanically produces appreciation decay') is undercut by its own beta evidence. A beta that swung from +4.6 to negative within a single year is not 'decaying' along a smooth institutionalization path - it is regime-flipping. The framework cannot distinguish a structural decay (institutionalization) from cyclical risk-on/risk-off beta compression, yet the entire 10-15yr forward rests on assuming the former. The con acknowledges this but the synthesized ~11% still hard-codes a monotone decay path the data does not support.

CAPM-INVERSION IS NOT A PUBLISHED OUTPUT: cited_outputs honestly flags that no source publishes a CAPM-inverted 10-15yr BTC CMA and that the betas are variance-tracking tools (Sanhaji & Chevallier explicitly frame realized beta as a RISK dashboard, not a forward-return device). Good. But the synthesized ~9-13% is then presented with false precision (central 11%, real 8%) off an unfalsifiable terminal-beta (1.8-2.2) x assumed ERP (4.5%) x assumed Rf (3.75%) - three contestable point estimates multiplied, none of which the realized data constrains. The number is defensible only as a wide judgmental band, not a central tendency.

REALIZED-DECAY MISMATCH: The 142->65->17%/yr realized appreciation decay is extrapolating toward the high-teens-and-falling, yet the synthesized 11% nominal sits ABOVE a naive continuation of that decay (17% and dropping over 10-15yr would plausibly land below 11%). The entry claims 11% 'sits squarely inside' the realized decay, but a monotone-decaying series passing through 17% recently and projected 10-15yr forward arguably undershoots 11%. The CAPM floor (Rf+ERP via residual beta) is propping the number UP relative to pure decay extrapolation - a tension the entry doesn't surface.
verdict.corrections: "1) Fix the Sherwood date: article is Nov 2024, and the faintly-negative-beta decoupling was March-mid-October 2024 (not 2025). Either correct '2025' to '2024' throughout, or cite a genuinely 2025-dated source for any 2025 decoupling claim. 2) Soften the VanEck decomposition language from 'explicitly decomposes into terminal quantity x future price x discount rate' to 'VanEck attributes the premium to future BTC-accumulation expectations + leverage + regulatory access + speculation; a quantity x price x discount-rate forward can be inferred but is the analyst's construction, not VanEck's published backout.' 3) Present the synthesized appreciation as a band (~8-14%) without a load-bearing 'central 11%', since three multiplied unfalsifiable inputs cannot support 1-pt precision. 4) Add the tension that the CAPM residual-beta floor holds the forward ABOVE a pure realized-decay extrapolation; reconcile or flag. Numbers that DO verify and need no change: 4.6 NDX beta (past decade, per Sherwood), +112% mNAV premium, 1.77 premium-beta, MSTR ~113% vs BTC ~55% vol, 96.5%/87.5% return/vol attribution (VanEck), JPMorgan Cipher/CleanSpark up + MARA/Riot down on HPC (Nov 24 2025), and the BTC~0/low gold correlation framing (broadly supported)."
overstated_pros: Pro #3 ('cross-checked against PRICES the market actually quotes... VanEck explicitly decomposes the MSTR premium into terminal BTC quantity x future price x discount rate') - the 'explicitly decomposes' is overstated; VanEck gives qualitative drivers, not a published three-factor forward. The market-implied-forward is inferred by the practitioner.

Pro #2 ('a DECAYING-beta CAPM mechanically produces appreciation decay') - overstated as a virtue. The beta's documented sign-flip means the framework cannot tell structural decay from cyclical compression; 'mechanically produces decay' only if you ASSUME monotone decay, which is the very thing in question. It is internal consistency by construction, not by evidence.

Pro #4 ('transparent and falsifiable: every lever is observable and stress-testable') - half-overstated. The levers are observable but the load-bearing one (the forward decay PATH of beta over 10-15yr) is precisely the unfalsifiable ex-ante assumption the cons concede. 'Falsifiable' overstates it; only the inputs are observable, not the path.
missing_cons: No supply/halving or stock-flow channel and no demand-adoption channel at all - the framework is purely a CAPM/equity-beta read, so it structurally ignores BTC's own issuance schedule and net-flow dynamics that drive much of realized return. A pure equity-beta CMA can be 'right' on correlation while missing the level entirely.

Survivorship/peso-problem in the realized beta and the realized-decay anchor itself: 142->65->17% and the 4.6 beta are conditioned on BTC NOT having gone to zero. Inverting a survived-path beta into a forward double-counts the survivorship the tail-haircut is supposed to remove; the haircut is applied to an already-survivorship-biased input.

Denominator instability: a beta of 4.6 'to NDX' depends heavily on return frequency (weekly vs daily vs monthly) and window; the entry never states the measurement frequency, and beta estimates for fat-tailed assets are extremely frequency-sensitive. The single 4.6 figure is presented as if frequency-robust.

ERP regime risk omitted: the borrowed ERP (~4.5%) is applied as a constant over 10-15yr, but if equity ERP itself mean-reverts up (compressing equity returns) the BTC forward inherits that with ~2x leverage - the framework's downside is more convex than the symmetric tail-haircut implies.

No treatment of the basis between holding spot BTC and the equity proxies' actual investability/cost (MSTR premium decay, miner dilution, ETF fees) - the 'market-implied forward' read off MSTR is gross of the premium-mean-reversion drag that an investor in the proxy would actually eat.

new_approaches.name: Intra-Crypto Relative-Value (BTC Dominance / ETH-BTC Rotation Overlay)
new_approaches.description: This approach values BTC along the WITHIN-crypto relative-value axis that every TradFi-anchored model ignores: Bitcoin's share of the total digital-asset market cap (BTC dominance, "BTC.D") and the ETH/BTC ratio, treated as conditioning variables for BTC's forward return, volatility, and correlation profile. The thesis is reallocation-based: the crypto complex commands a roughly fixed pool of risk capital at any moment, and that capital rotates between BTC and "alts." Rising dominance means capital flowing INTO BTC's share (often a within-crypto flight-to-quality during stress, when alts bleed and BTC behaves as the complex's "safe" reserve); falling dominance means capital rotating OUT of BTC into ETH and alts ("altseason"), with the ETH/BTC ratio the canonical leading trigger (cross thresholds like ~0.035-0.040 confirm rotation out of BTC). Crucially this is a TIMING/SCENARIO CONDITIONER, not a level forecaster: it produces no native 10-15yr expected-return number. Crypto-native practitioners use it to map regimes (dominance >62% "alt winter," 57-62% consolidation, <55% "altseason confirmed," 50-52% institutional ETF "soft floor") and the arithmetic of share shifts ($2T BTC at 59% dominance; a drop to 50% mechanically rotates ~$300B into alts). For a CMA it contributes a conditioning insight rather than an appreciation point estimate: BTC's vol and equity/gold correlations shift with the dominance regime, an idiosyncratic, intra-complex risk axis no level model captures.
new_approaches.medium_explanation: BTC dominance is BTC market cap divided by total crypto market cap; the ETH/BTC ratio is its higher-resolution cousin. The mechanism is pure capital reallocation inside a roughly fixed risk-capital pool: when dominance rises, capital concentrates in BTC (a within-crypto flight-to-quality, common in stress); when it falls, capital rotates out of BTC into ETH/alts ("altseason"), with ETH/BTC the leading trigger. Thresholds are practitioner lore: >62% alt-winter, <55% altseason, a 50-52% ETF "soft floor." For a 10-15yr BTC CMA the honest implication is narrow. This framework forecasts BTC's SHARE of the complex, not the complex's dollar growth, so it yields no native appreciation rate; rising dominance is bearish for alts but not mechanically bullish for BTC's price. Its real CMA value is conditioning: BTC's realized volatility and its correlations to equities and gold shift with the dominance regime (BTC behaves more "reserve-like," lower beta, in high-dominance stress; more risk-on as dominance falls). Treat it as a regime overlay on appreciation/vol assumptions, never a standalone level forecast.
key_drivers: BTC dominance level and (more importantly) its trend/direction — declining-from-a-high sustained over weeks signals rotation OUT of BTC
ETH/BTC ratio as the canonical leading rotation trigger (thresholds ~0.028 alt-capitulation / 0.035-0.040 altseason ignition)
Altcoin Season Index — % of top-100 alts outperforming BTC over trailing 90 days (>75 altseason, <25 BTC season)
Fixed-risk-capital reallocation assumption — the load-bearing premise that crypto risk appetite is a roughly fixed pie that shifts between BTC and alts
Within-crypto flight-to-quality dynamic — BTC as the complex's reserve asset during stress, raising dominance
Institutional/ETF 'soft floor' on dominance (~50-52%) — spot-BTC-ETF holdings structurally anchor BTC's share, dampening the deep 2017/2021 dominance crashes (86%->38%)
Dominance regime as a conditioner of BTC's own volatility and cross-asset correlation (beta) profile
pros: Isolates a genuinely distinct, idiosyncratic risk axis — BTC's share of the crypto complex — that EVERY TradFi-anchored model (S2F, Metcalfe, M2, gold-parity, LTCMA) ignores entirely; it surfaces the within-crypto rotation risk a BTC holder actually bears

Honest about its own scope: the careful practitioner versions explicitly state direction/trend matters more than level and that it is a relative measure, not a BTC price predictor — it does not pretend to be a level model

Captures a real, observable market microstructure (flight-to-quality into BTC during crypto stress) that plausibly conditions BTC's volatility and downside beta — useful as a regime overlay on vol/correlation CMA cells

Cheap, transparent, real-time computable from public market-cap data; the ETF 'soft floor' insight is a genuine structural change worth encoding (future dominance crashes likely shallower than 2017/2021)
Forces a useful discipline: BTC's risk/return is partly endogenous to the alt complex, so a BTC CMA built in TradFi isolation is incomplete
cons: NOT a return model at all — it forecasts BTC's SHARE of the complex, not the complex's dollar size, so it yields ZERO native long-horizon appreciation number. Any 10-15yr CMA appreciation must be imported wholesale from another framework; this is a category error if used as a level forecaster

Pure tautology risk: dominance = BTC cap / total cap is an identity, and the 'rotation' narrative ('$300B flows to alts if dominance drops 9pts') is accounting arithmetic, not a behavioral law — capital need not be a fixed pie; the whole complex can inflate or deflate, breaking the zero-sum rotation premise

Almost no peer-reviewed support as a return predictor — it is practitioner/sentiment lore (Gate, Nexo, DEXTools, MEXC). Academic lead-lag/spillover work finds ETH, not BTC, is often the dominant volatility/liquidity transmitter and BTC a net RECEIVER, contradicting the 'BTC leads, alts follow' framing

Regime thresholds (55%, 62%, 0.035) are eyeballed from only ~2-3 cycles, prone to overfitting; the index/altcoin-set composition drifts (new tokens, stablecoins, ETH staking) making historical dominance levels non-comparable across regimes

Reflexive and unstable: dominance moves can be driven by alt-supply inflation (new token launches dilute BTC's share with no BTC flow at all), severing the rotation interpretation; ETF era may have permanently changed the dynamic, invalidating pre-2024 calibration

new_approaches.rich_notes:
WHAT IT IS. The BTC-dominance / ETH-BTC rotation overlay is the only approach in either list that treats BTC's SHARE of the digital-asset complex as a variable. BTC dominance = BTC market cap / total crypto market cap; the ETH/BTC ratio is the higher-frequency version of the same idea. The crypto-native thesis (Gate, Nexo, DEXTools, MEXC) is reallocation: the complex commands a roughly fixed pool of risk capital, and that capital rotates between BTC and "alts." Rising dominance = capital concentrating in BTC (a within-crypto flight-to-quality, typical of stress, when alts bleed and BTC acts as the complex's reserve). Falling dominance = capital rotating OUT of BTC into ETH/alts ("altseason"), with the ETH/BTC ratio the canonical leading trigger.

THE NUMBERS PRACTITIONERS PUBLISH are all SHARE/relative, never BTC appreciation. The seed Gate/MEXC piece (Jan 2026): total crypto ~$3.3T, BTC ~$2.0T at 59% dominance; "if dominance drops from 59% to 50%, $300 billion rotates into altcoins; to 45%, $460 billion." Regime thresholds: >62% "alt winter" (alts bleed 12-18mo); 57-62% consolidation; <55% "altseason confirmed"; <50% "peak euphoria"; a 50-52% institutional-ETF "soft floor." ETH/BTC bands: <0.028 alt capitulation, 0.030-0.040 transition, >0.040 altseason ignition (article notes ratio "critically low" ~0.031 in early 2026). Nexo's framing is the most honest: "direction matters more than the level," dominance is "a relative measure," and altseasons historically begin when dominance "drops meaningfully — typically below 55% — AFTER Bitcoin itself has already made strong gains."

ON-RECORD MULTI-YEAR FORECASTS PRODUCED THIS WAY: essentially none for BTC's level. The framework produces dominance-path and ALT scenario forecasts (Gate's 3 scenarios: 30% "winter" dominance >62% ETH $1,800-2,200; 50% "grind" dominance 52-54% ETH $3,500-4,200; 20% explosive altseason), but these are 6-18 month, alt-relative, and say nothing about a 10-15yr BTC appreciation rate. The honest characterization (consistent with the prompt's framing) is: a timing/scenario conditioner, not a level forecaster.

WHY IT IS NOT A LEVEL MODEL — the fatal limitation. Dominance is an identity (BTC cap / total cap). Forecasting it tells you nothing about the DOLLAR size of the complex, hence nothing about BTC's dollar return. Rising dominance is bearish for ALT relative returns but NOT mechanically bullish for BTC price — BTC can stagnate while its share rises (alts fall faster) or rally while dominance falls (alts rally more). The "$300B rotates" arithmetic is accounting, not a behavioral law: capital is not a fixed pie (the whole complex inflates/deflates), and dominance also moves purely from alt-SUPPLY inflation (new token launches dilute BTC's share with zero BTC flow), severing the rotation interpretation entirely.

HISTORICAL FIT & FAILURE MODES. The narrative fits 2017 (dominance 86%->38% over ~6 months as alts exploded) and 2021 cosmetically, but with only ~2-3 cycles the thresholds are eyeballed and overfit, and the altcoin set composition drifts (stablecoins, ETH staking, thousands of new tokens) so historical dominance levels are not comparable across regimes. The ETF era is a genuine structural break: spot-BTC-ETF holdings (~$60-73B) plausibly put a "soft floor" under dominance at ~50-52%, meaning future dominance crashes are likely shallower than 2017/2021 — a real and CMA-relevant insight, but one that simultaneously INVALIDATES the pre-2024 calibration the thresholds rest on.

ACADEMIC CHALLENGE. The peer-reviewed lead-lag/spillover literature partly CONTRADICTS the framework's "BTC leads, alts follow" premise. Sifat et al. (2019) document a fast-shifting, non-stable BTC-ETH lead-lag; connectedness studies (MDPI Risks 2025; PMC connectedness work) find ETH is frequently the DOMINANT transmitter of volatility/liquidity spillovers while BTC is a net RECEIVER — "a macro crypto asset that responds to systemic trends rather than initiating them." That undercuts the clean "rotation out of BTC into alts" mental model and shows the relationship is bidirectional and regime-dependent, not a reliable one-way rotation law.

CMA BOTTOM LINE. Contribute it as a REGIME OVERLAY on the volatility and correlation cells, not as an appreciation source. The legitimate insights: (1) BTC's vol/beta is regime-conditional — lower in high-dominance flight-to-quality phases (BTC as crypto reserve, alts carrying the tail) — which supports tilting BTC's vol assumption to the LOWER end of the realized ~50-58% band; (2) the ETF soft-floor means BTC retains complex share through stress, a marginal share-support argument; (3) the "flight-to-quality" is INTERNAL to crypto, explicitly NOT a BTC-vs-gold safe-haven claim, so it reinforces (does not raise) the ~0 BTC-gold correlation. Appreciation (~8-12% nominal / 5-9% real) must be imported wholesale from the realized-decay baseline — the framework produces no level number and pretending otherwise is a category error.

issues: ACADEMIC ATTRIBUTION IS OVERSTATED AS SETTLED. The doc claims peer-reviewed connectedness work finds 'ETH, not BTC, is often the dominant volatility/liquidity transmitter and BTC a net RECEIVER.' The literature is genuinely SPLIT, not one-directional. The very MDPI Risks 2025 family it cites contains both 'Ethereum is the most effective [return] transmitter' AND 'Bitcoin consistently acts as the dominant transmitter of shocks to Ethereum over an approximately three-day window.' Presenting the ETH-dominant read as the academic consensus that 'contradicts' the framework is selective. (The Sifat 2019 bidirectional-causality cite IS correctly attributed, however.)

8-12% NOMINAL APPRECIATION IS IMPORTED FROM AN UNVALIDATED BASELINE AND SITS UNCOMFORTABLY ABOVE THE REALIZED-DECAY TREND. The doc is admirably explicit that this is borrowed judgment, not a framework output. But anchoring to ~8-12% while the realized CAGR has decayed 142->65->17%/yr means the synthesized number is ABOVE the most recent realized print (17%) by design. The text waves at 'cross-approach central' to justify the middle of the band, which is circular when this approach contributes zero level signal. This is the single largest hype-risk surface, and it is only half-flagged.

DOMINANCE-CONDITIONAL VOL TILT IS ASSERTED, NOT EVIDENCED. The one genuine first-order contribution (tilt BTC vol to the LOW end of ~50-58% because dominance regimes condition vol) rests on practitioner intuition that high-dominance flight-to-quality lowers BTC vol. No realized vol-by-dominance-regime estimate is cited. Given the doc's own warning that thresholds come from only ~2-3 cycles and the ETF era invalidates pre-2024 calibration, the low-end vol tilt is the same overfit it criticizes elsewhere. The ~57% realized floor should arguably be the anchor with NO downward tilt.

ETF SOFT-FLOOR / HOLDINGS FIGURE IS STALE AND SELF-UNDERMINING. The ~$60-73B ETF holdings is a Nov-2025 peak (IBIT $72.8B); by Mar-Apr 2026 IBIT alone was ~$54B AUM at lower BTC prices. More importantly the doc correctly notes the soft-floor insight INVALIDATES the pre-2024 threshold calibration the whole framework rests on — yet still leans on those same thresholds (55/62/0.035) as 'regime' inputs. That is having it both ways.

INTERNAL-RESERVE -> ZERO-GOLD-CORRELATION IS A NON-SEQUITUR DRESSED AS INSIGHT. The claim that BTC's within-crypto 'reserve' role 'reinforces' the ~0 gold correlation is rhetorical, not mechanistic: an internal-to-crypto safe-haven role says nothing about external gold co-movement either way. Holding gold corr at realized ~0 is correct; attributing it to this framework adds false explanatory weight.
verdict.corrections: "1) Cited practitioner numbers are REAL and correctly attributed: verified against Gate/MEXC source - total ~$3.3T, BTC ~$2.0T, 59% dominance, $300B@50%/$460B@45%, ETH/BTC 0.028/0.030-0.040 bands, ETH $3,500-4,200 grind target, ETF ~$60.8B/IBIT $72.8B. The 2017 dominance crash is correctly stated (86.3%->38.69%; doc says 86->38). 2) Sifat et al. 2019 is correctly attributed (bidirectional, non-stable causality; 'intraday traders can barely exploit' price discovery). 3) Soften the academic framing from 'literature finds ETH dominant / BTC net receiver, contradicting the framework' to 'the connectedness literature is SPLIT - some studies find ETH the dominant transmitter, others find BTC dominant over ~3-day windows - so the clean BTC-leads-alts premise is unsupported in EITHER direction, which is a weaker but defensible point.' 4) For the vol cell, drop the low-end tilt or label it explicitly speculative: anchor at realized ~57% and state there is no cited realized vol-by-regime evidence. 5) Re-flag the 8-12% nominal more loudly as sitting ABOVE the last realized 17%/yr print; the framework provides no support for it and arguably the decay trend argues the band low end. 6) Update ETF holdings to note the figure is a late-2025 peak now lower. 7) Remove the implication that the internal-reserve role 'reinforces' zero gold correlation - state only that the framework is silent on gold."
overstated_pros: 'BTC as the complex's flight-to-quality reserve, lower vol in high-dominance stress' is presented as an established microstructure fact but is practitioner lore with no cited realized vol-by-regime measurement; the academic split on transmission direction actively undercuts the BTC-as-anchor framing.

'ETF soft floor is a genuine structural change worth encoding' is double-counted as a pro while the doc simultaneously admits it INVALIDATES the framework's only calibration - it cannot be both a clean encodable insight and a calibration-breaker.

'Honest about its own scope' is true of the careful Nexo version but is generously extended to the whole crypto-native genre; the seed Gate/MEXC piece's '$2T rotation that could ignite alt season' headline is exactly the level-ish hype the doc elsewhere says the framework avoids.
missing_cons: NO ACCOUNTING FOR THE FACT THAT DOMINANCE AND BTC RETURN CAN BE POSITIVELY CORRELATED IN PRACTICE (BTC-led bull runs raise both price AND dominance), which would make any 'overlay' double-count BTC's own beta rather than add an orthogonal axis - the claimed idiosyncrasy may be partly spurious.

STABLECOIN TREATMENT IS UNADDRESSED: BTC.D is usually computed including stablecoins in 'total cap,' so stablecoin mint/burn mechanically moves dominance with zero BTC OR alt flow - a measurement artifact stronger than the alt-supply-inflation con already listed.

SURVIVORSHIP / REGIME-COUNT: with only ~2-3 cycles and the ETF structural break, there is effectively ONE post-institutional regime of data - the overlay is being calibrated on n~=1 for the regime that matters for a 10-15yr CMA.

NO LIQUIDITY/REFLEXIVITY DOWNSIDE: in a true crypto-wide drawdown, the 'fixed pie rotates to BTC' assumption fails - the whole complex deflates and BTC's 'reserve' bid can evaporate simultaneously, the exact tail a CMA vol cell should capture; the doc's low-end vol tilt cuts against this risk.

new_approaches.name: Treasury-Company Reflexive Demand Channel (mNAV Flywheel + Convertible Vol-Arb Loop)
new_approaches.description: A Soros-reflexive forced-buyer/forced-seller FLOW channel that prices BTC off the marginal demand created by leveraged digital-asset-treasury (DAT) companies — chiefly Strategy/MSTR — rather than off scarcity, network, cashflow, or TAM. Mechanism: while a treasury company trades at mNAV>1x (enterprise value / BTC-NAV above one), it issues equity, 0%-coupon convertibles, and preferreds ABOVE the value of the BTC they buy; proceeds purchase BTC at 1.0x, raising BTC-per-share ("BTC yield") accretively and permanently removing float from circulating supply. The deeper plumbing is convertible volatility arbitrage: vol-arb desks buy the converts and short/delta-hedge the equity, and because MSTR's implied vol is extreme (~106 vs ~15 S&P, ~60 BTC), the embedded option is hugely valuable even at a 0% coupon — gamma-hedging into rallies adds a mechanical bid that reinforces the premium and recycles into more BTC buying. The loop is self-reinforcing UP and self-destructing DOWN: when the premium collapses toward/below 1x, accretive issuance halts, the gamma bid inverts to selling, vol-arb unwinds, and (with thin cash, no revolver, and a 2029-30 convertible maturity wall) the company may be forced to SELL BTC to service debt/preferreds — a built-in bearish-asymmetric regime flip concentrated in one entity (Strategy holds ~76% of all treasury-company BTC, ~4% of total supply). A 10-15yr CMA falls out as: expected BTC return ≈ (DAT net demand flow vs new issuance, decaying as the premium normalizes and the float-removal pace slows) minus the latent forced-selling overhang on the downside.
new_approaches.medium_explanation: This treats BTC's price as set by a reflexive demand FLOW, not a fundamental level. When a treasury company (Strategy/MSTR) trades above 1x mNAV, it sells equity/0%-converts/preferreds above BTC-NAV and buys BTC at par, lifting BTC-per-share accretively and pulling float out of circulation. The engine underneath is convertible vol-arb: desks buy the converts and delta-hedge the stock; MSTR's ~106 implied vol makes the embedded option valuable at a 0% coupon, and gamma-hedging into rallies adds a self-reinforcing bid. In 2026 Strategy bought ~3x what all miners produced, so BTC grew "dependent on the buying machine." The loop reverses violently below 1x: accretive issuance stops, the gamma bid flips to selling, and thin cash plus a 2029-30 maturity wall risks forced BTC sales. For a 10-15yr CMA this implies a decaying appreciation as the premium normalizes toward 1x and the marginal float-removal flow fades, plus a fat left-tail from concentrated forced de-grossing — net a high-single-digit central return with elevated, asymmetric volatility.
key_drivers: mNAV premium (enterprise value / BTC-NAV); accretive issuance is only possible above 1x — VanEck: peaked ~2.6-2.8x late-2024, compressed to ~1.2x by Mar-2026, ~1-in-3 DATs now below 1x
BTC-per-share growth ('BTC yield') — the accretion metric the flywheel optimizes; each above-NAV raise that buys BTC at par increases it

Convertible volatility arbitrage / gamma feedback: vol-arb desks buy 0%-coupon converts and delta-hedge MSTR; extreme implied vol (~106 vs ~15 S&P, ~60 BTC) makes the embedded option valuable at 0% coupon and creates a self-reinforcing bid into rallies
Net DAT demand flow vs new supply: Strategy bought ~171k BTC in the first ~4.5 months of 2026 vs ~62k mined (~3x miner issuance); JPMorgan projects ~$30B of 2026 buying
Capital-markets dependence with no revolver: funding is 100% equity/convert/preferred issuance; thin cash; ~$8.25B converts + ~$10.3B preferreds; maturity/redemption wall 2029-2030
Concentration in one entity: Strategy holds ~76% of all treasury-company BTC (~818k BTC, ~4% of total supply); the channel is effectively a single-name flow

Latent forced-selling overhang / regime flip: below-1x premium + debt service + MSCI-exclusion risk (JPM: up to $8.8B index-driven forced sales) can trigger BTC liquidation and a reflexive 'spiral of doom'
pros: Identifies a REAL, observable marginal-demand mechanism that no other approach in the set treats as a valuation channel — in 2026 a single treasury company's buying (~3x miner issuance) was visibly the dominant net flow supporting price, so the channel has genuine, dated price-impact evidence rather than only an in-sample fit

Honest about asymmetry: unlike scarcity/network/power-law models that are structurally bullish, this framework builds in a bearish regime flip (premium collapse → halted issuance → gamma-bid inversion → forced BTC selling), which correctly shapes the LEFT tail of a CMA rather than ignoring it

Mechanistically transparent and falsifiable in real time: mNAV, BTC-per-share, convertible terms, implied vol, and DAT net flows are all observable and refreshable, so the thesis can be marked against live data (VanEck, NYDIG, JPMorgan all publish the inputs)

Explains BTC's elevated, fat-tailed volatility better than a fundamental-level model: forced de-grossing and vol-arb unwinds are an explicit endogenous source of crash risk and vol clustering, matching the realized ~57% vol floor
cons: Reflexive and circular by construction: the premium that funds the buying depends on BTC's price, which depends on the buying — there is no fundamental anchor, so the channel can sustain ANY price on the way up and provides no equilibrium level, only a flow. It is a flow/timing mechanism masquerading as a valuation channel; deriving a 10-15yr level from it requires bolted-on assumptions about how the premium and flow decay

Single-entity concentration makes it fragile and non-diversifiable as a 'channel': ~76% of treasury BTC sits in one company with thin cash, no revolver, and a 2029-30 convertible/preferred wall. A CMA built on this is really a bet on one balance sheet surviving — Coinbase flags it as systemic risk; NYDIG's Cipolaro calls mNAV 'woefully deficient' for ignoring convert-refinancing and opco risk

The bid is self-limiting and decaying: as the premium normalizes toward 1x (already from ~2.7x to ~1.2x), accretive issuance slows and the marginal float-removal flow fades, so the very mechanism that drove past returns mechanically weakens — extrapolating its historical demand impulse overstates forward return

Vol-arb gamma support is symmetric and can violently invert: the same delta-hedging that bids the stock up sells it into weakness; below-1x, forced BTC selling and de-grossing can cascade ('spiral of doom', ~1-in-3 DATs already below NAV in 2026), so the channel injects crash risk it cannot itself arrest

Silent on cross-asset correlations and on a real appreciation rate — it produces a flow and a regime-flip risk, not native volatility or correlation numbers, all of which must be imported from realized data

new_approaches.rich_notes:
METHODOLOGY. This is a Soros-style reflexivity channel applied to BTC's MARGINAL DEMAND rather than its fundamental level. The unit of analysis is the leveraged digital-asset-treasury (DAT) company — overwhelmingly Strategy/MSTR. The load-bearing variable is mNAV (enterprise value ÷ BTC-NAV, where EV = common market cap + debt + preferred notional − cash; VanEck's definition). Above 1x, the firm issues equity, 0%-coupon convertibles, and preferreds at a premium and buys BTC at par, raising BTC-per-share ("BTC yield") accretively and permanently removing float. The CMA isn't a level but a flow: expected BTC return ≈ DAT net demand vs new issuance, scaled by how long the premium (and thus accretive issuance) persists, minus a latent forced-selling overhang on the downside.

THE PLUMBING (AMINA, VanEck). The deeper mechanism is convertible volatility arbitrage. Vol-arb desks buy MSTR's 0%-coupon converts and short/delta-hedge the equity; because MSTR's implied vol is extreme (~106 vs ~15 S&P, ~60 BTC), the embedded option is hugely valuable even at a 0% coupon — so MSTR raises ultra-cheap capital while the arb is profitable "regardless of direction." Gamma-hedging into rallies forces desks to BUY stock as it rises, a mechanical self-reinforcing bid that supports the premium and recycles into more BTC purchases. VanEck decomposes the premium into leverage + volatility + sentiment and notes MSTR "behaves like a call option on Bitcoin" via this recursive issue-and-buy loop. The premium has compressed from a ~2.6-2.8x late-2024 peak to ~1.2x by Mar-2026 (VanEck), i.e., a +112% premium to BTC+opco fair value — the tailwind is visibly fading.

HISTORICAL FIT / DEPENDENCY. The channel's strongest evidence is 2026 flow: Bloomberg ("Bitcoin Grows More Dependent on Michael Saylor's Buying Machine," 20-May-2026) reports Strategy bought ~171,238 BTC in the first ~4.5 months of 2026 vs ~62,000 mined network-wide — ~3x miner issuance — and that this single company "largely prevented a steeper fall" with BTC ~$77,500. Saylor's own framing: miners no longer set the price; "structured credit products now absorb every coin produced." Strategy holds ~818k BTC (~4% of total supply) and ~76% of ALL treasury-company BTC — so the "channel" is effectively a single-name flow.

FAILURE MODES (the honest core). (1) Circularity: the premium funds the buying, the buying lifts the price, the price lifts the premium — no fundamental anchor, so the channel can rationalize any price up and supplies no equilibrium level. (2) Self-limiting decay: as mNAV normalizes toward 1x, each raise removes less float; the very engine of past returns weakens. (3) Symmetric/inverting vol-arb: the gamma bid that levitates the stock sells into weakness; below 1x, accretive issuance halts and forced BTC selling can cascade. (4) Concentration + maturity wall: thin cash, no revolver, ~$8.25B converts + ~$10.3B preferreds, redemption wall 2029-2030 (Coinbase). NYDIG's Greg Cipolaro calls mNAV "woefully deficient" for ignoring convert-refinancing and opco risk. DL News ("spiral of doom," 2026): ~1-in-3 of 156 tracked DATs already below 1x mNAV, ~$112B BTC collectively; former-Goldman analyst Dom Kwok: if forced to sell shares at thin premiums, "Strategy could be forced to offload Bitcoin to cover its obligations." Coinbase explicitly flags the model as systemic risk; JPMorgan warned MSCI exclusion could trigger up to $8.8B of index-driven forced sales.

ON-RECORD MULTI-YEAR FORECASTS PRODUCED THIS WAY. The channel publishes FLOW forecasts, not appreciation CMAs. JPMorgan (Panigirtzoglou): Strategy on pace for ~$30B of BTC buying in 2026, exceeding the ~$22B bought in each of 2024 and 2025. Saylor's stated ambition is 5-7% of total BTC supply (from ~4% today). VanEck stops short of a price forecast, instead arguing — per Sigel — that BTC "already has a lot of reflexivity, so there's no need to add leverage on top of it," i.e., even the bullish house is skeptical of the DAT model's durability. No source converts the flow into a 10-15yr annualized BTC return; that synthesis is mine.

WHY DISTINCT / CMA IMPLICATION. None of the 20 existing approaches treats a reflexive institutional demand-flow (or its convertible-financing plumbing) as the valuation channel — the closest, the LPPLS bubble-hazard and LTCMA approaches, model crash timing and portfolio assumptions, not the forced-buyer/seller flow itself. For a 10-15yr BTC CMA, this channel's real value is in SHAPING THE DISTRIBUTION, not pinning a central return: it justifies holding vol at/above the ~57% realized floor (endogenous de-grossing), a fat left tail (concentrated forced selling at the 2029-30 wall), and a tightened equity correlation (the marginal buyer is a leveraged equity vehicle, so BTC is MORE equity-like and NOT more gold-like via this mechanism). My synthesized central return (~6-10% nominal / ~3-7% real) sits at the low end of the cross-approach band precisely because a premium-dependent flow cannot compound at historical rates and carries a genuine reflexive-unwind probability mass.

issues: DL News 'spiral of doom' source is dated August 2025, not 2026 as listed in representative_sources (year field says '2026'). Also the '~1-in-3 of 156' is attributed to Capriole Investments' tracking in the source, which the deep-dive does not name.

MSCI $8.8B framing risk: JPM's actual estimate is $2.8B from MSCI exclusion ALONE, and $8.8B ONLY if all other equity indices also follow. The deep-dive's con #2 and notes say 'JPM: up to $8.8B index-driven forced sales' — the 'up to' caveat makes it defensible, but the headline-grabbing $8.8B is the maximal cascade scenario, not the base MSCI case. A reader could mistake it for the direct MSCI impact.

Premium is treated as monotonically decaying when it is actually noisy/mean-reverting. Sources show mNAV at ~1.2x (Mar 2026) but also 'expanded to about 26%' (~1.26x) over a subsequent two-month window in the $30B-buying article. The synthesis's central case ('premium decays gracefully toward 1x') reifies a volatile, bouncing premium as a smooth glide path — the actual series oscillates, which if anything strengthens the vol/skew argument but weakens any clean 'decay' narrative used to pin a central return.

Over-claim in medium_explanation: 'In 2026 Strategy bought ~3x what all miners produced' and 'Strategy bought ~3x what all miners produced' state the 3x without the '~4.5 months YTD' qualifier that key_drivers includes. Read literally this implies a full-year 3x; the verified figure is 171,238 / 62,000 = 2.76x over a partial (YTD ~4.5mo) window. The raw numbers ARE disclosed elsewhere in the doc, so it's checkable, but the unqualified medium_explanation phrasing rounds up and drops the horizon.

Holdings figure (~818k BTC, ~4% supply) is correct as of May 3 2026 but already stale by the doc's own date window: by May 25 2026 Strategy held 843,738 BTC. Minor, and the ~4%/~76% concentration story is unaffected, but the precise 818k is a snapshot, not current.

STRC preferred carries an ~11.5% annualized dividend (verified). The deep-dive cites '~$10.3B preferreds' and 'thin cash, no revolver' but never quantifies the cash drag of servicing double-digit-yield perpetual preferreds — a material omission given the entire bearish thesis hinges on forced selling to meet obligations. The preferred dividend service cost is arguably a bigger near-term cash strain than the 2029-30 convert wall and is left silent.

new_approaches.name: Stablecoin-Float Liquidity-Onramp Demand Sink
new_approaches.description: Treats the aggregate dollar-stablecoin float (Tether/USDC/etc. market cap, ~$200-250bn by 2025) as the NARROW, crypto-native dollar-liquidity base and "dry powder" reservoir that gates marginal BTC buying. The practitioner instrument is the Stablecoin Supply Ratio (SSR = BTC market cap / stablecoin market cap): a low/falling SSR means stablecoin buying-power is large relative to BTC (bullish capacity to bid), a high SSR means it is exhausted. The macro/official-sector layer (BIS WP 1270; Richmond Fed EB 26-10) adds that reserve-backed stablecoins are now a marginal buyer of short-dated US Treasuries — a 2σ inflow cuts 3-month T-bill yields 2.5-3.5bp (5-8bp when bills are scarce) — and that their growth raises safe-asset demand and presses on r-star, linking the crypto liquidity base to the macro safe-asset complex. A 10-15yr BTC CMA is NOT a native output: you would have to forecast secular stablecoin-float growth, an assumed BTC "absorption" multiple per dollar of new float, and SSR mean-reversion. CRITICAL caveat the official-sector evidence establishes: causation empirically runs BTC→stablecoin flows (inflows FOLLOW large BTC up-moves with a multi-day lag; NY Fed), so the float is largely a coincident/lagging reflection of demand, not an exogenous demand sink — undercutting its use as a forward return driver.
new_approaches.medium_explanation: The thesis: BTC can only be bought with on-ramped dollars, and the dominant on-chain dollar is the stablecoin. Aggregate stablecoin market cap is therefore the crypto-native "dry powder" that caps how much marginal bidding can occur; the Stablecoin Supply Ratio (BTC cap / stablecoin cap) operationalizes it — low SSR = ample buying power, high SSR = exhausted. Official-sector work hardens the macro side: reserve-backed stablecoins are now a real marginal buyer of T-bills (a 2σ inflow cuts 3-month yields 2.5-3.5bp, 5-8bp when bills are scarce — BIS WP 1270), and their growth raises safe-asset demand and pressures r-star (Richmond Fed). To get a 10-15yr CMA you must forecast stablecoin-float growth, a BTC-absorption multiple per new dollar, and SSR mean-reversion — none native to the framework. The fatal empirical wrinkle (NY Fed): stablecoin inflows FOLLOW large BTC up-moves with a lag, so the float reflects demand rather than gating it. For a CMA this means stablecoins are a coincident liquidity barometer, not an independent appreciation engine; usable only for regime/timing, anchoring forward returns to BTC's realized appreciation decay.
key_drivers: Aggregate dollar-stablecoin market cap / float (~$200-250bn 2025) as the crypto-native dollar liquidity base and 'dry powder' reservoir
Stablecoin Supply Ratio (SSR = BTC mktcap / stablecoin mktcap) and its mean-reversion band — the proximate timing instrument
Net stablecoin minting/burning and exchange-deposit inflows (velocity toward exchange addresses signals rotation into BTC)
Short-dated US Treasury (T-bill) supply/scarcity — gates the macro safe-asset price impact (state-dependent: 2.5-3.5bp ample, 5-8bp scarce per BIS)
Reserve-backed vs crypto-backed stablecoin mix — reserve-backed raise Treasury/dollar demand and press r-star; crypto-backed reduce it (Richmond Fed)
Regulatory regime (GENIUS Act) mandating safe reserve backing — channels stablecoin growth into Treasury demand and legitimizes the float
Lag structure: BTC price up-moves LEAD stablecoin inflows by several days (NY Fed) — the float is largely a coincident/lagging mirror of demand, not exogenous
pros: Grounds BTC bidding in an observable, high-frequency, crypto-native quantity (stablecoin float / SSR) rather than price extrapolation or scarcity numerology — and the float is auditable on-chain in near-real-time

Has genuine official-sector empirical backing for the MACRO link: BIS WP 1270 establishes a causal, IV-identified, state-dependent effect of stablecoin flows on T-bill yields, and Richmond Fed gives a coherent general-equilibrium safe-asset/r-star channel — far more rigorous than S2F/Metcalfe
SSR is a falsifiable, mean-reverting timing tool with some ex-post record of bracketing buying-power extremes; ties BTC to a concrete on-ramp constraint (you cannot bid without on-ramped dollars)

Connects BTC to the broader dollar/safe-asset complex, giving a portfolio-coherent macro narrative (debasement on-ramp + Treasury demand) distinct from the broad-M2 barometer and the eurodollar-collateral channel
cons: Causation runs the WRONG way for a demand driver: NY Fed shows stablecoin inflows FOLLOW large BTC up-moves with a multi-day lag, so the float is a coincident/lagging mirror of demand, not an exogenous 'sink' that gates it — using it to forecast forward returns is largely circular

Not a return model at all: it yields no native expected appreciation, volatility, or correlation; any 10-15yr CMA is bolted-on (float-growth × absorption multiple × SSR drift), none of which the literature estimates

The macro evidence is about T-BILL YIELDS, not BTC price: BIS WP 1270 and Richmond Fed never forecast BTC return — the BTC-pricing leap is the approach's own, unsupported by the cited official-sector work

Structural leakage and regime change: stablecoins increasingly fund non-BTC uses (cross-border payments, DeFi, T-bill yield, ETFs that never touch on-chain dollars), so float ≠ BTC dry powder; the ETF/institutional marginal buyer often bypasses stablecoins entirely, breaking the gating link
Tiny calibration window (2021-2025) spanning few cycles; SSR 'bands' drift and the indicator is among the on-chain cohort with unstable out-of-sample performance
