synthesized_outputs.notes: Synthesized CMA treats the stablecoin float as a COINCIDENT liquidity-regime overlay, not an independent appreciation driver — because the official-sector evidence (NY Fed) shows BTC leads the float, not vice versa. Outputs therefore anchor to BTC's realized appreciation-decay baseline (~8-12% nominal, ~55-60% vol) rather than to any float-extrapolation, and correlations sit near realized trailing-5y values, with the equity correlation if anything reinforced (the float channel is risk-on) and gold held near zero (no mechanism).

new_approaches.rich_notes:
METHODOLOGY. The approach fuses two layers. (1) A practitioner micro-instrument: aggregate dollar-stablecoin market cap as crypto-native "dry powder," operationalized via the Stablecoin Supply Ratio (SSR = BTC market cap / stablecoin market cap, CryptoQuant/Glassnode). Low/falling SSR = abundant stablecoin buying-power relative to BTC (bullish capacity); high SSR = exhausted. The bull narrative: BTC can only be bid with on-ramped dollars, and the dominant on-chain dollar is the stablecoin, so the float is the binding capacity constraint; new minting and stablecoin flows to exchange-deposit addresses are read as a leading rotation signal. (2) An official-sector macro layer establishing that the float is now systemically large: BIS WP 1270 (Ahmed & Aldasoro, 2025) uses daily 2021-2025 data and an IV strategy to show a 2σ stablecoin inflow lowers 3-month T-bill yields 2.5-3.5bp, rising to 5-8bp during bill scarcity (RRP drain, debt-ceiling episodes), concentrated in short maturities; ~$200bn AUM by Mar-2025, ~$40bn of T-bills bought in 2024 (rivaling the largest government MMFs). Richmond Fed EB 26-10 (Azzimonti & Quadrini, 2026) adds a GE result: reserve-backed stablecoins raise safe-asset/dollar demand and press the natural rate r-star DOWN, while crypto-backed reduce Treasury demand; under GENIUS-Act-style reserve mandates the dollar is reinforced, not threatened.

KEY RELATIONSHIPS & HISTORICAL FIT. The "dry powder" pattern has visual support: 2020-2021 stablecoin supply grew ~$20bn→$120bn+ as BTC ran $10k→$69k; major BTC rallies have been preceded by float expansions. The SSR has bracketed buying-power extremes ex-post. BIS provides the cleanest causal evidence in the whole crypto-macro literature for the float→T-bill-yield link.

THE FATAL WRINKLE (faithfully represented). The NY Fed update (Anadu et al., 2025, Liberty Street; SSRN 5227592) directly tests the direction and finds capital flows INTO all stablecoins FOLLOW large BTC price increases (top-5% return days), measured over an ~8-day window — i.e., BTC up-moves LEAD stablecoin inflows, and riskier offshore/crypto-backed coins get the biggest inflows while US-based asset-backed coins' inflows are "barely statistically significant." This inverts the gating premise: the float largely MIRRORS demand with a lag rather than supplying exogenous demand. For a forward CMA this is decisive — a lagging coincident indicator cannot drive expected returns; it is at best a regime/timing overlay. Compounding this, the official-sector sources price T-BILLS, never BTC: the leap from "stablecoins move bill yields" to "stablecoins set BTC's 10-15yr return" is entirely the approach's own and is unsupported by the cited work.

FAILURE MODES. (a) Reverse causality / circularity (NY Fed). (b) Leakage: stablecoins increasingly fund cross-border payments, DeFi collateral, T-bill yield-harvesting and (post-2024) sit beside ETF rails where the marginal institutional BTC buyer uses cash equities plumbing that never touches an on-chain dollar — so float ≠ BTC dry powder, and the gap is widening. (c) Tiny window (2021-2025), few cycles, drifting SSR bands, unstable out-of-sample like the broader on-chain-indicator cohort. (d) Mis-specification risk: total float conflates demand-sink and store-of-yield uses.

ON-RECORD MULTI-YEAR FORECASTS. None of the official-sector sources produce a multi-year BTC price/return forecast via this channel — by design, they forecast yields and dollar demand, not BTC. Practitioner SSR commentary is explicitly a timing/mean-reversion signal, not an annualized CMA. So unlike S2F ($288k-$500k+) or power-law ($1M+), this family has produced NO credible on-record multi-year BTC appreciation forecast — which is itself informative: its proponents treat it as a liquidity barometer, not a return engine. Synthesized CMA therefore anchors to the realized-decay baseline (~8-12% nominal, vol ~55-60%, equity corr ~0.45-0.55, gold corr ~0-0.15), treating the stablecoin float as a coincident liquidity-regime overlay rather than an independent appreciation driver.

issues: BIS magnitude has a minor internal inconsistency in the literature itself: the BIS abstract headline is 2.5-3.5bp for a 2sigma inflow on 3M yields, but one search summary of the paper body cites '2-2.5bp within 10 days.' The JSON uses 2.5-3.5bp (the abstract figure), which is the correct/defensible number, but the spread reflects horizon-dependence the JSON does not flag. Not an error, just under-specified.

The 'asymmetry' fact (stablecoin OUTFLOWS raise yields 2-3x as much as inflows lower them) appears in the BIS abstract and is materially relevant to a downside-risk framing, but the JSON omits it entirely. For a CMA this is a meaningful missing con: the channel is asymmetric and more dangerous on the downside (deleveraging/redemption spirals) than the modest upside it credits.

NY Fed '~8-day window' in rich_notes is more precise than the published blog, which says 'days following' large BTC moves. The SSRN working-paper version may specify a window, but as cited (the Liberty Street blog) the 8-day figure is not clearly on-record. Low-stakes but slightly overstated precision.

Realized decay figures (142->65->17%/yr full/10y/5y) are the user's own pipeline output and could not be independently recomputed here. Public sources show 5yr CAGR ~150-155% and 10yr ~84% on differently-dated windows; the JSON's much lower numbers imply a recent post-drawdown snapshot (BTC ~$80k late-2025). Direction (steep decay) is corroborated; the exact levels depend on the user's as-of date and are not externally verifiable in this check.

The synthesized ~8-12% nominal is anchored to a 'cross-approach central' band that is asserted, not derived within this card. Its defensibility rests entirely on the external cross-approach synthesis the reader must trust; within the four corners of THIS framework the honest output is genuinely n/a, which the card admits but then overrides with judgment.
verdict.corrections: "No hard factual corrections required - all four cited official-sector sources (BIS WP 1270, Richmond Fed EB 26-10, NY Fed Liberty Street 2025) are real, correctly authored, correctly dated, and their headline numbers (2.5-3.5bp / 5-8bp scarce, IV identification, daily 2021-2025, ~$200bn AUM, $40bn T-bills 2024, reserve-backed-raise / crypto-backed-reduce Treasury demand, r-star down, BTC-up-moves-LEAD-inflows) are accurately attributed. The framing is unusually honest: it explicitly labels every BTC return/vol/correlation cell as 'n/a (source silent)' for the cited literature and flags the reverse-causality (NY Fed) as fatal. Two soft fixes: (1) add the BIS outflow asymmetry (outflows raise yields ~2-3x more than inflows lower them) as a downside con, since it sharpens the redemption-spiral risk; (2) soften the NY Fed '8-day window' to 'days following' unless sourcing the SSRN version, and note the BIS effect is horizon-dependent (smaller at <=10 days) rather than a single point estimate."
overstated_pros: Pro #2 ('genuine official-sector empirical backing... far more rigorous than S2F/Metcalfe') is true but rhetorically smuggles credibility from the T-BILL-yield result onto the BTC-CMA use-case. The rigor attaches to a finding the card itself concedes does not price BTC. The card does flag this in cons, but the pro is written to make the framework sound more return-relevant than its own cons admit.

Pro #3 ('SSR is a falsifiable, mean-reverting timing tool with some ex-post record of bracketing buying-power extremes') overstates the out-of-sample track record. The card's own con #5 admits the calibration window is 2021-2025, SSR bands drift, and out-of-sample performance is unstable - so 'falsifiable timing tool' is fair but 'ex-post record of bracketing extremes' is closer to curve-fit pattern-matching on <2 cycles than a validated signal.

Pro #1's claim that the float is 'auditable on-chain in near-real-time' is true for supply but elides that the BTC-RELEVANT subset (dollars actually destined to bid BTC vs DeFi/payments/yield) is NOT cleanly observable - the very leakage con #4 raises. So the auditable quantity is not the decision-relevant quantity.
missing_cons: Downside asymmetry (BIS abstract): stablecoin OUTFLOWS move bill yields ~2-3x more than equal inflows - the macro channel is convex to the downside, implying redemption/deleveraging episodes hit harder than accumulation helps. Absent from the cons, yet directly relevant to a 10-15yr risk distribution.

Stablecoin idiosyncratic/credit risk: a major reserve-backed issuer (Tether/USDC) de-peg or reserve-quality shock is an exogenous tail that would simultaneously crater the 'dry powder' AND force BTC selling - a left-tail the SSR framing cannot see because it treats float as a clean dollar proxy.

Reflexivity within the indicator: because BTC up-moves CAUSE float growth (NY Fed), a low SSR reading is partly an artifact of a prior BTC rally, so 'ample buying power' can be a top signal as easily as a bottom signal - the timing tool can invert. The card notes reverse causality generally but does not draw out that it corrupts the SSR signal's polarity.

Regulatory/jurisdictional tail: GENIUS-Act-style mandates are credited as a pro (legitimize float), but the same regime can throttle offshore/crypto-backed coins (the ones NY Fed shows get the BIGGEST BTC-linked inflows), structurally shrinking the BTC-relevant float - a regulatory downside the card omits.

new_approaches.name: Structural Stock-Flow Demand-Clearing Engine (Inelastic-Supply Price-Multiplier)
new_approaches.description: A forward-simulating, bottom-up market-CLEARING model that solves each period for the equilibrium price where a perfectly inelastic (vertical) Bitcoin supply curve intersects a downward-sloping demand curve. Issuance is fixed by the halving schedule, so the only moving supply lever is the LIQUID float: total supply minus lost coins (~17%+) and HODLed/strategic-reserve coins (~40-50% already removed). Exogenous net demand enters two ways: a daily withdrawal flow (BTC/day moved from liquid supply into ETFs, treasuries, sovereign reserves, cold storage), which shifts the vertical supply line leftward, and a demand-shift multiplier (D / A', e.g. 10X-40X) scaling a constant-elasticity-of-substitution (CES) demand curve. Because the supply curve is vertical, modest withdrawals against a thinning float produce NONLINEAR, accelerating ('hyperbolic') price appreciation as liquid supply falls below ~1-2M BTC and the clearing point slides into the inelastic region of demand. The second-generation version (Rudd-Porter 18(10):570) replaces the static demand shift with an Epstein-Zin recursive-utility intertemporal-preference term and an explicit fiat-denominated withdrawal-sensitivity parameter (coins removed FALL as USD price rises), then Monte-Carlos over five inputs. A 10-15yr CMA falls out as the price path from spot to a horizon-year clearing price, with appreciation that DECAYS in BTC-withdrawal terms as the float thins (each remaining coin is dearer) but can spike in USD terms in supply-shock corners. Distinct from descriptive on-chain illiquid-supply gauges and from MV=PT: this endogenizes the clearing price from flow x supply-inelasticity.
new_approaches.medium_explanation: The model treats Bitcoin issuance as a vertical supply line and clears it against a CES demand curve each period. The only supply that matters is the LIQUID float (total minus lost coins and strategic-reserve HODLings). Two exogenous inputs drive price: a daily withdrawal flow (BTC/day pulled into ETFs/treasuries/sovereign reserves) that shifts the vertical line left, and a demand-shift multiplier (10X-40X) that scales demand. Because supply cannot respond to price, withdrawals against a thinning float push the clearing price up nonlinearly, going 'hyperbolic' once liquid supply falls below ~1-2M BTC. Key inputs: initial liquid supply, daily withdrawal rate, demand-shift parameter, CES elasticity, and (v2) a fiat withdrawal-sensitivity term that throttles coin removal as USD price rises. For a 10-15yr BTC CMA it implies a wide, scenario-dependent appreciation range whose central case (~mid-teens to ~40% nominal CAGR) sits far below BTC's ~100% historical CAGR but well above most cross-approach centrals — and it warns that volatility RISES, not falls, as scarcity binds, the opposite of the institutionalization-dampens-vol thesis.
key_drivers: Initial LIQUID float: total supply minus lost coins (~17%+) minus HODLed/strategic-reserve coins; authors estimate ~40-50% already removed from liquid supply, leaving the clearing-sensitive base near ~2M BTC at the 'hyperbolic' threshold
Daily withdrawal rate (BTC/day) from liquid supply into ETFs/corporate treasuries/sovereign reserves/cold storage — the left-shift of the vertical supply line (scenarios span 0 to 4000 BTC/day)
Demand-shift multiplier (D / A', e.g. 10X, 20X, 30X, 40X over the horizon) scaling the CES demand curve — captures institutional/sovereign adoption and credit-funded demand
CES demand elasticity (ε, ~ -2.10 conservative down to ~ -0.86 most-inelastic) — controls how fast the clearing price accelerates as the float thins
Perfectly inelastic (vertical) supply curve set by the fixed halving issuance schedule — the structural 'price-multiplier' premise
Fiat-denominated withdrawal sensitivity (v2): coins withdrawn per day FALL as USD price rises, the built-in damping that produces appreciation DECAY rather than runaway hyperbola
Epstein-Zin recursive-utility intertemporal preference (v2) — separates risk aversion from elasticity of intertemporal substitution in the demand block
Lost-coin / HODL-wave estimates feeding the liquid-vs-illiquid split (acknowledged as highly uncertain)
pros: Genuinely endogenizes the clearing price from first-principles supply-demand intersection rather than extrapolating price history (S2F/power-law) or regressing on a single trend (Metcalfe/M2) — it is the only family here that SOLVES for price from flow x inelasticity

Peer-reviewed (JRFM, two papers 2025) with a transparent, fully parameterized and reproducible model (Analytica implementation + Figshare data posted), so every lever (float, withdrawal, demand-shift, elasticity) is auditable and stress-testable

Correctly captures a real, observable structural fact: Bitcoin's supply is perfectly issuance-inelastic, so a demand/flow shock has nowhere to go but price — the CoinShares evidence (≈4500 BTC/day ETF demand vs ≈921 minted; OTC holdings -74%, exchange balances -29% since 2020) shows the float really is thinning

Naturally produces appreciation DECAY in the honest version: the v2 fiat-withdrawal-sensitivity term throttles BTC removed as USD price climbs, and the authors explicitly flag that a steady multi-thousand-coin daily drain 'may not continue as price increases' — the right qualitative shape for a maturing CMA

Triangulates within an order of magnitude of independent frameworks (MicroStrategy Bitcoin24, power-law, ARK) at the 2036 horizon, lending some convergent credibility to the central (not tail) scenarios

Makes a falsifiable, non-consensus VOLATILITY claim — that vol RISES as liquid supply falls below ~1-2M BTC (inelastic supply meeting inelastic demand), contradicting the institutionalization-lowers-vol narrative and giving a CMA a defensible high-vol floor
cons: Severe conflict of interest: co-author Dennis Porter runs Satoshi Action Education/Fund (board + employment) and Rudd consults for it — a Bitcoin-policy advocacy nonprofit lobbying US states/governments to ADOPT strategic Bitcoin reserves, which is precisely the 'sovereign withdrawal' input that drives the model's bullish output. The model assumes the outcome its authors lobby for.

The demand-shift multiplier D is set 'in an ad hoc way' by the authors' own admission — there is no empirical estimation of the demand curve, so the headline scenarios ($1M 2027, $2M 2027, $5M 2031) are assumption-driven, not derived; the authors caution explicitly 'against overinterpretation of the projections on the upper end'

'Hyperbolic' runaway price is conceded as possibly a 'first-generation model artefact' of the fixed-elasticity CES form — a model that produces multimillion-dollar tails because a vertical supply curve meets an inelastic demic curve is structurally rigged toward explosive output and may simply be mis-specified

Withdrawal-rate exogeneity is the load-bearing fiction: in reality net flows are price-RESPONSIVE (high prices entice lost/dormant coins and HODLers to sell, adding liquid supply), so the assumed steady multi-thousand-coin daily drain is the thing most likely to break exactly when the model says price accelerates

Calibrated only to the post-April-2024 halving with ~1-2 years of ETF data — no out-of-sample validation, tiny sample, and the liquid-supply / lost-coin estimates (~40-50% removed) are highly uncertain and could be wrong by a wide margin, which the authors acknowledge

Ignores Layer-2/Lightning, off-chain and custodial netting, and the demonetization-of-other-assets channel by construction — the float and demand measures are partial, and ETF/custodial concentration can hold coins that are economically liquid but appear 'withdrawn'
Says little directly about cross-asset CORRELATIONS — it is a price-path/clearing model, not a distributional CMA, so correlations to equities/FI/TIPS/gold must be imported from realized data

synthesized_outputs.appreciation_nominal: ~9-14%/yr nominal (JUDGMENT, not a model output). The model's own honest core — the v2 fiat-withdrawal-sensitivity term that throttles coin removal as USD price rises — is exactly the appreciation-DECAY mechanism a credible 10-15yr CMA needs, and the authors themselves flag that the multi-thousand-coin daily drain 'may not continue as price increases.' Stripping their lobbying-aligned demand-shift assumptions (D=20-40X is asserted, not estimated) and their disowned hyperbolic tails, and anchoring to BTC's realized decay (142%->65%->17%/yr over full/10y/5y), the clearing logic with a price-responsive (not exogenous) float lands near low-double-digits. I sit modestly above the cross-approach central (~8-12%) because the inelastic-float mechanism is real and the float genuinely is thinning, but well below their 40.2% headline.
synthesized_outputs.appreciation_real: ~6-11%/yr real (subtract ~2.5-3% long-run inflation). The model is intrinsically a relative-purchasing-power story (BTC vs USD), so a debasement tailwind is baked in, but most of it should already be in the nominal figure.
synthesized_outputs.volatility: ~55-65%/yr (JUDGMENT). This is the one place I lean ABOVE the standard ~50-60% CMA band: the model makes a specific, mechanism-based prediction that vol RISES as liquid supply falls below ~1-2M BTC (inelastic supply meeting inelastic demand), which argues against compression toward equities/gold vol. Floor anchored at realized trailing-5y ~57%; top of band reflects the model's supply-shock-induced spikes.

synthesized_outputs.corr_fi_nominal: ~0.10-0.20 (JUDGMENT; model silent). Low-positive via shared liquidity/real-rate sensitivity of the marginal institutional buyer; realized trailing-5y 0.19.

The framework frames BTC as demonetizing other stores of value (gold included), which a naive reading would push higher — but a flow-clearing model gives NO mechanism forcing gold co-movement, and realized BTC-gold correlation is ~0 (full -0.01, 5y +0.045). I hold it at the bottom of the band; the demonetization narrative is a sizing claim, not a measured correlation.
synthesized_outputs.notes: Central tension: the model's structure is the most economically coherent of the BTC families (it actually clears a market), but its published outputs are inflated by (a) exogenous, price-insensitive withdrawal assumptions, (b) an ad-hoc demand multiplier, and (c) a CES form prone to hyperbolic artefacts — all aligned with the authors' advocacy interest. The synthesized CMA keeps the inelastic-float MECHANISM and the decay logic while discarding the asserted demand path.

new_approaches.rich_notes:
METHODOLOGY. Rudd & Porter (JRFM 2025, two papers) build a discrete, forward-simulating market-CLEARING engine. Each period they intersect a perfectly inelastic (vertical) supply curve — fixed by the halving issuance schedule — with a constant-elasticity-of-substitution (CES) demand curve, and read off the equilibrium clearing price. The innovation vs descriptive on-chain gauges is that supply is the LIQUID float, not total coins: they net out lost coins (~17%+ via HODL waves, plus Satoshi's stash) and strategic-reserve/long-term HODLings, estimating ~40-50% of total supply already removed from liquid circulation. Two exogenous inputs move the system: a daily WITHDRAWAL rate (BTC/day pulled from liquid supply into ETFs, treasuries, sovereign reserves, cold storage), which shifts the vertical line leftward, and a DEMAND-SHIFT multiplier D/A' (10X-40X over the horizon) scaling the CES curve. Paper 1 (18(2):66, Jan 2025) calibrates to the April-2024 halving (ε about -2.10, L_Min=0.04, T*=8yr logistic) and a Dec-2024 $102k recalibration. Paper 2 (18(10):570, Oct 2025) upgrades the demand block with Epstein-Zin recursive utility (separating risk aversion from intertemporal substitution) and a FIAT-denominated withdrawal-sensitivity term (coins removed per day fall as USD price rises), then Monte-Carlos across five variables (demand level, intertemporal preference, withdrawal sensitivity, initial liquid supply, daily withdrawal).

KEY RELATIONSHIP. Because supply is vertical, price acceleration is nonlinear: as the float thins, the clearing point slides into the inelastic region of demand and small withdrawals move price a lot. The papers state 'hyperbolic' appreciation appears once liquid supply falls below ~1-2M BTC; the v2 Monte Carlo finds such paths 'relatively rare,' concentrated where liquid supply is near/below 2M and withdrawal sensitivity is low.

ON-RECORD MULTI-YEAR FORECASTS (produced THIS way). Paper 1: conservative path reaches $1M by ~June 2028 at 4000 BTC/day (autumn 2028 at 2000/day); a 10X demand shift with ZERO withdrawals still yields >$600k; CAGR tops 40.2% (2000 BTC/day + 30X demand). Bull scenario: $1M early 2027, $2M late 2027, $5M early 2031. Paper 2: 50% probability BTC > $5.17M and 75% > $4.81M by April 2036, with a stated range from 'low single millions to low tens of millions.' The authors cite BTC's 13yr historical CAGR (99.5%) for context and a v2 bull 2036 CAGR of 43.6% (D=40, 2000 BTC/day). They triangulate to MicroStrategy Bitcoin24 (baseline CAGR 29.2%, bull 37.5%, $13M by 2045) and a power-law 2036 fit (~$2.1M), claiming surprising convergence near $2-3M for 2036.

HISTORICAL FIT / FAILURE MODES. The model is calibrated, not validated out-of-sample — only ~1-2 years of post-halving ETF data, with highly uncertain lost-coin/liquid-supply inputs. Five self-disclosed limitations: (1) fixed-elasticity CES 'may oversimplify'; the forecasts are 'only a narrow slice from the very large space of possible demand curves'; (2) reliance on uncertain lost-coin estimates; (3) no Layer-2/Lightning dynamics; (4) credit-funded demand shocks could spike D unpredictably; (5) — most damning — the hyperbolic growth 'may be an artefact of our first-generation model.' The demand multiplier D is set 'in an ad hoc way.' The deepest economic flaw is exogenous, price-insensitive withdrawal: in reality high prices entice dormant coins and HODLers back to market, ADDING liquid supply exactly when the model says price runs away — the assumed steady multi-thousand-coin drain is the input most likely to break.

CONFLICT OF INTEREST (load-bearing for skepticism). Co-author Dennis Porter is on the board of and employed by Satoshi Action Education/Fund, a 501(c)(3) that lobbies US state and federal governments to ADOPT strategic Bitcoin reserves; Rudd reports a consulting/advisory relationship with it. The 'sovereign/institutional withdrawal' input that drives the bullish output is precisely the policy outcome the authors advocate — the model assumes the result its authors lobby for. This does not invalidate the clearing MECHANISM (which is the most economically coherent of the BTC valuation families — it genuinely solves a market rather than regressing on a trend like S2F/Metcalfe/M2), but it means the published demand-path scenarios and price targets should be treated as advocacy-aligned, not neutral estimates.

CMA IMPLICATION. The honest, transferable content is the inelastic-float clearing mechanism plus the v2 decay term — keep those, discard the asserted demand path and disowned hyperbola. A credible 10-15yr extrapolation of BTC's realized decay (142->65->17%/yr) under price-responsive (not exogenous) flows lands appreciation near low-double-digits (synthesized ~9-14% nominal), modestly above the cross-approach central because the thinning-float mechanism is real (CoinShares: ~4500 BTC/day ETF demand vs ~921 minted; OTC -74%, exchange balances -29% since 2020). Uniquely, the model argues vol RISES with scarcity (supply-shock corners), supporting a high vol floor (~55-65%) rather than the institutionalization-compression view. It is silent on cross-asset correlations, which must be imported from realized data; the demonetization-of-gold framing is a sizing narrative, not a measured gold correlation (realized ~0).

issues: Elasticity mis-cited: the dossier says baseline CES elasticity is 'epsilon ~ -2.10 conservative down to ~ -0.86 most-inelastic.' Paper 1's actual baseline is epsilon = -2.301 (line: 'we set A = 75M and epsilon = -2.301'), and the most-inelastic option is epsilon = -0.86086 (confirmed). So -0.86 is right but -2.10 is wrong; the true baseline is -2.301. Minor but it's a hard number presented as the paper's.

The '75% chance > $4.81M by April 2036' figure is paired with '50% chance > $5.17M' as if both are headline Monte-Carlo outputs of paper 2. I directly confirmed the 50%/$5.17M figure from the RePEc abstract; the 75%/$4.81M appeared only in a secondary search snippet, not the primary abstract I pulled. It is very likely real (consistent shape) but is presented with more certainty than I could independently verify from the primary source. Logical oddity: 75% > $4.81M and 50% > $5.17M are mutually consistent (lower threshold, higher probability), so no contradiction, just incomplete primary confirmation.

CoinShares figures are attributed loosely. The dossier's '~4500 BTC/day ETF demand vs ~921 minted; OTC -74%, exchange balances -29% since 2020' blends near-correct numbers: ETF ~4500/day and ~900 minted are confirmed from Butterfill/CoinShares; exchange balances actually fell ~28% (Feb 2024), not 29%; the '921 minted' and 'OTC -74%' specifics I could not confirm from primary CoinShares text (921 is oddly precise for a figure usually quoted as ~900). These are not in the JRFM papers themselves -- they are a separate CoinShares source the dossier imports, which it does label correctly.

STALENESS / live-data refutation of the core mechanism: a May 2026 CoinDesk item shows US spot-BTC ETFs accumulated only ~4,500 BTC for ALL of 2026 YTD (not per day) and flipped to a record 9-day outflow streak / $2.8B withdrawn in late May 2026. This is direct, current evidence that the 'steady multi-thousand-coin-per-day exogenous withdrawal' is NOT holding -- the single most load-bearing input of the bullish scenarios. The dossier flags withdrawal-exogeneity as the key fiction in prose but does not cite that the drain has already empirically reversed as of the dossier's own date (2026-05), which would have sharpened the refutation considerably.

The synthesized 9-14% nominal / 6-11% real CAGR is labeled 'JUDGMENT, not a model output' but is then justified by 'anchoring to BTC's realized decay (142->65->17%/yr).' That decay series is asserted in the dossier and not independently reproduced here; if the 17%/yr trailing-5y figure is as-of a local-price window it is sensitive to endpoint. The synthesized central is internally defensible GIVEN that decay, but the whole chain rests on an un-sourced realized-stat triplet that should itself be scripted/verified, not taken as given (violates the scripted-analysis rule -- a number is being used as an anchor without a reproducible source in-dossier).

Conflict-of-interest framing is correct but arguably understated in ONE direction: the dossier treats COI as biasing the demand-PATH upward, which is right, but does not note that 'no external funding' is also declared -- the lobbying interest is structural (advocacy outcome = model input), not a paid-study relationship. The distinction matters for how an allocator should discount it; the dossier's 'the model assumes the result its authors lobby for' is fair and verbatim-supported.
verdict.corrections: Fix the baseline elasticity: change 'epsilon ~ -2.10 conservative' to 'epsilon = -2.301 baseline' (the -0.86086 most-inelastic option is correct as stated). Soften the CoinShares attribution to match the primary source: ETF demand '~4,500 BTC/day vs ~900 minted' and 'exchange balances ~-28% since 2020' (drop the over-precise '921' and verify the 'OTC -74%' against the original Butterfill report before keeping it). For paper 2's Monte Carlo, anchor on the primary-confirmed line '50% probability > $5.17M by April 2036' and treat '75% > $4.81M' as secondary unless re-confirmed from the paper body. Strengthen the central refutation by citing the LIVE reversal: as of the dossier's own date (May 2026), US spot-BTC ETFs had accumulated only ~4,500 BTC for the whole of 2026 YTD and entered a record multi-day outflow streak (~$2.8B), i.e. the exogenous steady-drain assumption has already empirically broken -- this is the cleanest available falsification of the load-bearing input and belongs in the cons, not just the abstract 'price-responsive flows' caveat. Finally, source the realized-decay triplet (142->65->17%/yr), the ~57% vol floor, and the ~0 gold correlation to a scripted calculation rather than asserting them, since the entire synthesized CMA is anchored to them. Everything else -- the 40.2% CAGR scenario, 99.5% 13yr historical CAGR, $1M/$2M/$5M bull dates, 43.6% D=40 2036 bull, hyperbolic-paths-rare-below-2M, the verbatim COI disclosure, the 'ad hoc' demand multiplier and 'withdrawal may not continue as price increases' admissions, the volatility-rises / power-law-breaks-down claim, lost-coin/HODL split (4M lost, 1.1M Satoshi, 3.5M HODL, ~17% 10yr-inactive), MSTR Bitcoin24 (29.2%/37.5%, $13M-2045, $2.4M-2036), power-law ~$2.1M-2036, and ARK $3.8M-by-2030 -- checks out verbatim against the primary papers and is correctly attributed.
overstated_pros: Pro #2 ('peer-reviewed, transparent, fully reproducible... every lever auditable and stress-testable') leans on the MDPI peer-review brand harder than warranted. JRFM is a fast-turnaround MDPI journal; the same paper concedes its central demand lever D is set 'in an ad hoc way' and the headline tails 'may be an artefact of our first-generation model.' Reproducible plumbing (Analytica + Figshare confirmed) does not make the KEY input estimated rather than asserted -- the pro overstates 'auditable' as if it implied 'empirically disciplined,' which the authors themselves deny.

Pro #5 ('triangulates within an order of magnitude of independent frameworks... convergent credibility') overstates independence. Two of the three triangulation points are MicroStrategy's own Bitcoin24 (an issuer actively levering up to buy BTC) and a power-law fit -- neither is an independent demand-side estimate, and the convergence is partly because Rudd & Porter tuned their D and withdrawal knobs to LAND near those targets (the paper literally back-solves: 'close to our model when parameterized with a 20X demand multiplier and ~2250 BTC/day'). Convergence achieved by free-parameter fitting is weak corroboration, and the pro presents it as stronger than it is.

Pro #6 / the volatility claim ('falsifiable, mechanism-based, defensible high-vol floor') is framed as a virtue but the underlying claim is qualitative only -- the paper states 'extreme volatility should be expected' with NO annualized number. Calling it a 'defensible high-vol floor' for a CMA dresses a directional assertion as a quantitative input; it is suggestive, not a floor.
missing_cons: The exogenous-withdrawal assumption has ALREADY empirically failed as of the dossier date: 2026 YTD net ETF accumulation collapsed to ~4,500 BTC total with a record outflow streak in May 2026. The dossier lists withdrawal-exogeneity as a theoretical fiction but omits that the real-world drain reversed -- the single strongest available refutation of the model's bullish engine is not cited.

Survivorship / regime-dependence of the realized anchors: the synthesized CMA leans on trailing-5y realized stats (vol ~57%, equity corr ~0.56, gold corr ~0) measured over a single, unusually favorable BTC regime (post-2020 ZIRP-to-ETF). The dossier imports these as forward inputs without flagging that BTC's cross-asset correlations are notoriously regime-unstable (it spiked toward equities in 2022 risk-off) -- a CMA con in its own right.

No treatment of miner economics as an endogenous supply response. The model calls supply 'perfectly inelastic,' but post-halving miner capitulation/HODL behavior and miner treasury sales are a real price-responsive liquid-supply source that the model assumes away; the dossier accepts the vertical-supply premise as 'a real, observable structural fact' (Pro #3) without noting miners do in fact sell into strength.

Reflexivity/leverage downside is asymmetric and under-weighted: the same credit-funded demand channel the dossier credits (MicroStrategy-style bond/equity-funded buying) is a forced-seller mechanism on the way down. The cons mention price-responsive selling adding supply but not the leverage-unwind / treasury-company-liquidation tail that would make the realized vol fatter on the LEFT side specifically.

21M-cap demonetization framing is asserted, never sized against a competing-store-of-value loss path (CBDCs, tokenized T-bills, gold ETFs, stablecoins absorbing the 'digital money' demand). The dossier notes the model ignores demonetization-of-other-assets by construction but does not flag the symmetric risk that BTC LOSES the store-of-value race -- only the upside demonetization narrative is entertained.

new_approaches.name: Square-Root Market-Impact Law (Metaorder Demand-to-Price Mechanism)
new_approaches.description: This approach is not a standalone price-target model but the microstructural ENGINE that converts net institutional demand into price, supplying the concavity that forces appreciation decay from first principles. It rests on the empirically near-universal square-root impact law: executing a metaorder (a single investor's cumulative net buy program) of size Q moves price by I(Q) = Y * sigma * (Q / V)^delta, with delta empirically pinned at ~1/2 and Y an order-unity prefactor (~0.5-1), sigma the volatility and V the traded volume over the same window. Donier & Bonart (2015) reconstructed >1 million metaorders on Bitcoin/USD and confirmed delta ~ 1/2 holds over four decades of order size, despite Bitcoin's quasi-absence of arbitrageurs/market-makers. The mechanism, derived in Donier-Bouchaud's latent-liquidity (LLOB) / Walrasian double-auction theory, is that liquidity vanishes (locally linearly) near the current price, so each marginal dollar of demand must dig progressively deeper into a thin book -> concave, sub-linear price response. To turn this into a CMA you bolt a demand path onto the engine: project cumulative net institutional inflow Q over 10-15yr, run it through I(Q) ~ sqrt(Q), and read off the price path. Because impact is concave, doubling cumulative demand raises price by only ~sqrt(2) (~41%), not 2x -> appreciation MECHANICALLY decays as the asset's cumulative absorbed demand and float grow. It is the rigorous, falsifiable substitute for the naive linear "Bitcoin multiplier" (BofA 118x; Apollo 106x) that practitioners use.
new_approaches.medium_explanation: The square-root law says a buy program of size Q moves price by roughly Y*sigma*sqrt(Q/V): impact is concave, not linear. Donier & Bonart (2015) confirmed the exponent delta ~ 1/2 on over a million Bitcoin metaorders, spanning four decades of order size. The mechanism (Toth et al. 2011; Donier-Bouchaud LLOB) is that real liquidity is latent and thins out near the current price, so each extra dollar of net demand digs deeper into a sparse book. For a 10-15yr BTC CMA this is the missing engine under every flow-based model: feed in projected cumulative net institutional inflow Q, and price scales as sqrt(Q). The key implication is automatic appreciation DECAY — once cumulative absorbed demand is large, doubling it lifts price only ~41%, so the headline 100x+ "Bitcoin multiplier" must shrink as the asset matures. This is the first-principles reason naive linear-flow targets (BofA 118x, Apollo 106x) overstate forward returns. It says nothing about volatility or cross-asset correlations directly; those are imported. It also assumes a forecastable demand path Q, which it cannot itself supply.
key_drivers: Cumulative net institutional demand Q over the horizon (the metaorder size) — the exogenous input the law converts to price; for a CMA this is the projected 10-15yr net inflow path, which the law itself does NOT forecast
Square-root exponent delta ~ 1/2 (empirically anchored on Bitcoin; Donier-Bonart) — the concavity parameter that forces appreciation decay
Order-unity prefactor Y (~0.5-1) calibrating impact magnitude per unit normalized flow
Volatility sigma — impact scales linearly in sigma, so higher BTC vol amplifies the price move per dollar of flow
Traded volume / liquidity V (the normalization) — deeper float and volume shrink impact; thinning liquid float (HODLing, ETF custody) raises it
Latent-liquidity profile shape near price (locally linear vanishing of supply/demand -> sqrt; the LLOB/Walrasian micro-foundation)
Permanent vs transient impact fraction (~2/3 of peak impact tends to persist; the rest decays) — determines how much of demand-driven price gain is durable vs mean-reverting
pros: Strongest empirical pedigree of any BTC valuation primitive: delta ~ 1/2 is confirmed across equities, futures, options AND Bitcoin (Donier-Bonart, >1M metaorders, four decades of size), with error bars below 0.01 in equity studies — a genuine near-universal law, not a curve fit to one BTC price history

Supplies appreciation DECAY from first principles: concavity (sqrt) means the marginal price response to cumulative demand falls automatically, so it is structurally the RIGHT shape for a maturing-asset CMA and a rigorous correction to the naive linear 100x+ 'Bitcoin multiplier'

Has a real micro-foundation (latent-liquidity / Walrasian double-auction theory; Donier-Bouchaud), not just a statistical regularity — it explains WHY impact is concave (liquidity vanishes near the price)

Falsifiable and refreshable: Y, sigma, V are estimable from order-book/volume data and the law can be re-tested as the market matures; it also yields a tradeable liquidity/crash-risk measure (Donier-Bouchaud 'Why Do Markets Crash?')

Mechanically distinct from and complementary to higher-level flow/demand-clearing CMAs — it is the engine underneath them, so it disciplines any flow-based price target that would otherwise assume linearity
cons: NOT a self-contained CMA: the law converts demand Q to price but cannot forecast Q. All the long-horizon return uncertainty is exiled into the projected cumulative-inflow path, which is exactly the hard, unmodeled part — the engine is rigorous, the fuel input is a guess

Calibrated and validated at intraday-to-daily metaorder horizons; extrapolating a single-metaorder impact law to a 10-15yr cumulative-demand 'super-metaorder' is a heroic stretch the original authors never endorsed — impact decay, liquidity replenishment and regime change over a decade are not captured by a static sqrt(Q)

Impact is largely TRANSIENT: only ~2/3 (and on Bitcoin, per Donier-Bonart, an 'uninformed' component leading to 'almost complete long-term decay') of peak impact persists, so naive use overstates the permanent price gain from a given flow — durable appreciation requires the demand to be 'informed'/persistent, an assumption the law cannot certify

Parameters drift: Y, sigma and especially V (liquid float) are non-stationary; ETF custody and HODLing shrink V (amplifying impact) while deeper institutional books raise it — the net is ambiguous and the law gives no law of motion for V

Silent on volatility-as-a-stat and on all cross-asset correlations (growth/value equity, FI, TIPS, gold) — every distributional and portfolio-construction cell must be imported from realized data; it populates at most the appreciation channel

Reflexivity/endogeneity: sigma and V are themselves functions of price and flow, so the 'exogenous Q in, price out' framing is circular over long horizons; the same critique (price drives the inputs) that dogs S2F/NVT applies once you leave the intraday regime

representative_sources.title: A Million Metaorder Analysis of Market Impact on the Bitcoin

representative_sources.author_firm: Bank of America (Francisco Blanco et al., as reported)
representative_sources.title: Bitcoin price-sensitivity multiplier: ~$93M moves price 1% (118x)

cited_outputs.appreciation_nominal: n/a (source silent on a CMA return). The impact-law literature publishes no annualized BTC appreciation. It yields only a demand-to-price map I(Q)~Y*sigma*sqrt(Q/V); practitioner LINEAR variants (BofA ~118x: ~$93M moves price 1%; Apollo ~106x) are the closest on-record numbers and are exactly what the concave law corrects downward.
cited_outputs.appreciation_real: n/a (source silent — no inflation adjustment; law is a nominal demand-to-price mechanism)
cited_outputs.volatility: n/a (source silent as an output — sigma is an INPUT to the impact formula, not a forecast. Note impact scales linearly in sigma)
cited_outputs.corr_growth_eq: n/a (source silent — microstructure impact law makes no cross-asset correlation statement)
cited_outputs.corr_gold: n/a (source silent — no digital-gold or cross-asset claim; the law is asset-agnostic and applies identically to gold, equities, options)
cited_outputs.notes: Cited, robust empirical facts (not CMA outputs): exponent delta ~ 1/2 on Bitcoin over four decades of metaorder size (Donier-Bonart 2015); delta ~0.5 with error <0.01 across equities/futures/options (Toth 2011; Bouchaud 2024); prefactor Y order-unity (~0.5-1); permanent impact ~2/3 of peak with a large transient/'uninformed' component that decays almost completely on Bitcoin. On-record forecast PRODUCED this way: Donier-Bouchaud (2015, PLOS ONE) used the same liquidity/impact framework to predict crash AMPLITUDE from order-book liquidity (Mt.Gox 2011-2014), an early-warning liquidity-risk measure — a downside, not an appreciation, forecast.

synthesized_outputs.appreciation_nominal: ~7-11%/yr (judgment; the law's contribution is the DECAY shape, not a level). Mechanics: price ~ sqrt(cumulative net demand Q). If real cumulative institutional/ETF demand into BTC compounds at a plausible maturing ~12-18%/yr over the horizon, the sqrt map roughly HALVES that to a ~6-9%/yr price-appreciation contribution from flow, before any debasement/monetization drift. Add a small permanent-monetization premium and haircut for the transient (~1/3+) component that decays, and a concave-impact-consistent forward sits in high single digits — squarely in line with the cross-approach central (~8-12% nom) and well BELOW the realized 142->65->17% path. The law's core message for the CMA: whatever linear-multiplier flow target you start from, apply sqrt and let the multiplier shrink as float/cumulative demand grow.
synthesized_outputs.appreciation_real: ~4-8%/yr real (subtract ~2.5-3% long-run inflation). Judgment; the law is silent, so this just deflates the nominal flow-driven estimate.
synthesized_outputs.volatility: ~50-60%/yr (judgment; imported, not a law output). Anchored to realized trailing-5y ~57%. The impact mechanism actually argues vol stays HIGH: thin latent liquidity makes price 'hypersensitive to small fluctuations' (Donier-Bouchaud), so I hold the floor at realized ~57% and do not credit compression to equity-like levels within the horizon.
synthesized_outputs.corr_growth_eq: +0.40 to +0.55 (judgment; imported from realized trailing-5y ~0.56). The impact law is correlation-agnostic, but the marginal-demand flows that drive BTC are risk-on/liquidity-sensitive, so co-movement with growth/tech equity stays moderately-to-strongly positive.
synthesized_outputs.corr_value_eq: +0.25 to +0.35 (judgment; realized trailing-5y ~0.37). Lower than growth; BTC carries the duration/liquidity beta value equities lack.
synthesized_outputs.corr_fi_nominal: +0.10 to +0.20 (judgment; realized trailing-5y ~0.19). Low-positive via shared liquidity/real-rate sensitivity of the marginal institutional buyer; no structural duration link.
synthesized_outputs.corr_tips: +0.20 to +0.30 (judgment; realized trailing-5y ~0.30). Slightly above nominal FI through the real-rate/liquidity channel.
synthesized_outputs.corr_gold: ~0.0-0.10 (judgment). The impact law is asset-agnostic and supplies NO digital-gold linkage — it applies identically to gold and BTC without forcing them to co-move. Realized BTC-gold correlation is ~0 (full -0.01, 5y +0.04). I keep it at the bottom of the band; this approach gives zero mechanism for a gold tie, which is an honest mark against any digital-gold narrative.
synthesized_outputs.notes: The synthesized appreciation is deliberately the DECAY extrapolation: the sqrt(Q) engine converts even an optimistic compounding-demand path into a high-single-digit forward return and guarantees the per-dollar 'Bitcoin multiplier' falls over time. All vol/correlation cells are imported from the realized scripted baseline because the law is silent on them.

new_approaches.rich_notes:
WHAT IT IS. The square-root impact law is the most empirically robust object in all of market microstructure, and it is the mechanical engine that sits UNDER every flow-based BTC CMA — distinct from a higher-level demand-clearing simulator, which decides Q; this law decides how Q maps to price. Execute a metaorder of net size Q and price moves by I(Q) = Y * sigma * (Q/V)^delta, with delta empirically ~1/2 (concave), Y order-unity (~0.5-1), sigma volatility, V volume over the matching window. The concavity is the whole point: impact is sub-linear, so the marginal price response to cumulative demand falls as Q grows.

BITCOIN EVIDENCE. Donier & Bonart (2015, arXiv:1412.4503; Market Microstructure & Liquidity) reconstructed >1,000,000 metaorders on Bitcoin/USD and found delta indistinguishable from 1/2 across four decades of order size — remarkable because Bitcoin in 2011-2014 had almost no arbitrageurs or designated market-makers, so the law cannot be an artifact of HFT. They further decompose order flow into 'informed' and 'uninformed' components, with the uninformed part leading to 'an almost complete long-term decay of impact.' This is the crucial caveat for a CMA: a large fraction of demand-driven price moves is TRANSIENT. Across other markets only ~2/3 of peak impact tends to persist (Bouchaud 2024).

MECHANISM. Toth et al. (2011, Phys. Rev. X, 'Anomalous price impact and the critical nature of liquidity') introduced the latent-liquidity / 'epsilon-intelligence' picture: most liquidity is hidden and vanishes locally linearly around the current price, so a metaorder must consume progressively deeper, sparser book -> sqrt impact. Donier & Bouchaud (2015, 'From Walras' auctioneer to continuous-time double auctions', J. Stat. Mech.) generalized this into a dynamic supply/demand theory, empirically confirming on Bitcoin that supply and demand vanish QUADRATICALLY near the clearing price, which 'makes prices hypersensitive to small fluctuations.' This is the rigorous antithesis of Kyle (1985), whose linear lambda (delta=1) the data decisively reject.

WHY IT BELONGS IN A BTC CMA. Practitioners already use a crude linear version: the 'Bitcoin multiplier.' Bank of America (2021) estimated ~$93M of net inflow moves BTC price ~1% (a 118x market-cap multiplier); Apollo Crypto (2024) computed ~106x from spot-ETF flows (with only ~30% flow/price correlation — itself a red flag). These linear multipliers are exactly what the square-root law CORRECTS: if price ~ sqrt(Q), the multiplier is not constant — it shrinks as cumulative absorbed demand and float grow. So the law is the first-principles reason a credible 10-15yr CMA must extrapolate BTC's appreciation DECAY rather than its level. Plug a compounding net-demand path into sqrt(Q) and even an aggressive demand CAGR is roughly halved into a high-single-digit price-appreciation contribution.

ON-RECORD FORECAST PRODUCED THIS WAY. The framework's one genuine ex-ante deliverable is a DOWNSIDE forecast, not an appreciation one: Donier & Bouchaud (2015, PLOS ONE, 'Why Do Markets Crash? Bitcoin Data Offers Unprecedented Insights') used Mt.Gox order-book liquidity (Dec-2011 to Jan-2014) to build three liquidity measures that predict the AMPLITUDE of a crash given a sell-imbalance — an early-warning liquidity-risk gauge. No multi-year BTC price target has ever been published from the pure impact law, which is honest: the authors never claimed it forecasts long-run returns.

FAILURE MODES / SKEPTICISM. (1) The law converts demand to price but cannot forecast demand — all the CMA uncertainty is exiled into the unmodeled cumulative-inflow path Q. (2) It is calibrated at intraday-to-daily metaorder horizons; treating a decade of net demand as one giant 'super-metaorder' under a static sqrt(Q) ignores liquidity replenishment, the transient/decaying component, and regime change — a stretch the authors did not endorse. (3) Permanent impact is only a fraction of peak (Donier-Bonart's 'almost complete decay' for uninformed flow), so durable appreciation needs the demand to be persistent/'informed', which the law cannot certify. (4) Inputs sigma and V are non-stationary and endogenous to price/flow, reintroducing the same reflexivity that dogs S2F/NVT once you leave the intraday regime — ETF custody/HODLing shrink liquid float V (amplifying impact) while deeper institutional books raise it, net ambiguous. (5) The law is asset-agnostic and silent on volatility-as-a-stat and on all cross-asset correlations, so every distributional/portfolio cell (vol, growth/value-eq, FI, TIPS, gold) must be imported from realized data — and it supplies NO digital-gold linkage whatsoever, applying identically to gold and BTC without forcing co-movement (consistent with realized BTC-gold corr ~0). NET: a rigorous engine, an honest decay mechanism, but not a self-contained CMA — best used to discipline (square-root-haircut) any flow-based appreciation estimate and to flag liquidity-driven crash risk.

issues: Year nit (minor): Donier-Bonart 'A Million Metaorder Analysis' first hit arXiv Dec 2014 (1412.4503), published in Market Microstructure & Liquidity 2015. The deep-dive labels it 2015 throughout. Defensible (published/revised year) but the underlying empirical work is 2014.

The synthesized appreciation (7-11% nom) is presented as if the sqrt LAW produces it, but the entire result is driven by an UNSTATED assumed demand CAGR (12-18%) that the law explicitly cannot forecast. The deep-dive is honest that Q is exogenous, yet still publishes a headline return band. That band is a judgment call dressed in the law's empirical prestige — the rigor of delta≈1/2 does NOT transfer to the 7-11% number. This is the single biggest framing risk and it is only partially flagged.

The g/2 'halving' heuristic (price-from-flow ≈ demand-CAGR / 2) silently assumes V (liquid float/volume) is FLAT over 10-15yr. The cons correctly note V is non-stationary and reflexive, but the headline arithmetic ignores V growth entirely. If V grows with the market (plausible), the Q/V normalization shrinks impact further and the flow contribution is LOWER than 6-9% — i.e., the synthesis may still be optimistic, not conservative, on its own logic.

Extrapolation from intraday/daily single-metaorder horizon to a decade-long 'super-metaorder' under a STATIC sqrt(Q) is acknowledged as 'heroic,' but the synthesized band is still computed as if that extrapolation holds. The cons disclaim the move and the synthesis then makes it anyway — mild internal tension.

'~2/3 of peak impact persists' is asserted as a cross-market regularity (Bouchaud 2024) and applied as a ~1/3 haircut, but Donier-Bonart's Bitcoin-specific finding is stronger: the uninformed component shows 'almost complete long-term decay.' On BTC specifically the durable fraction could be well below 2/3, which would push the flow-driven appreciation contribution lower than the stated band. The deep-dive cites both but anchors the haircut to the gentler equity number.
verdict.corrections: All seven primary citations were independently verified against the sources and are accurately attributed, including the exact practitioner numbers (BofA $93M moves price 1% = 118x; Apollo 106x from spot-ETF flows; 30.4% flow/price correlation). The two seemingly-conflicting micro-foundation claims ('liquidity vanishes locally linearly' from Toth/LLOB vs. 'supply and demand vanish quadratically near the clearing price' from Donier-Bouchaud 1506.03758) are NOT a contradiction: they describe different objects (marginal latent-order density vs. the integrated supply/demand curve); both attributions are faithful. The PLOS ONE crash paper is correctly characterized as a downside/crash-amplitude forecast, not an appreciation forecast. The g/2 decay arithmetic (12-18% demand CAGR -> 6-9% price contribution) is correct under a pure sqrt map with flat V. The 7-11% forward, by sitting well below the realized 142->65->17%/yr decay path, is directionally consistent with the 'decay shape' thesis. Overall: the EMPIRICAL spine (delta≈1/2, the law, the multipliers) is real and correctly cited; the SYNTHESIZED return band is defensible-but-soft judgment whose uncertainty is honestly exiled into the unforecastable Q — it is not hype, but it borrows more credibility from the law than the law actually lends to a level estimate.
overstated_pros: Pro #1 ('strongest empirical pedigree of any BTC valuation primitive,' error bars <0.01) conflates the law's robustness with the CMA's robustness. The <0.01 error bars are on the EXPONENT in equity studies, not on anything in the BTC return forecast. The forecast inherits none of that precision. The framing risks implying the 7-11% band is empirically tight when it is pure judgment.

Pro #2 ('supplies appreciation DECAY from first principles ... the RIGHT shape for a maturing-asset CMA') overstates: the law gives a concave map FROM demand TO price, but whether realized APPRECIATION decays depends entirely on the demand path Q, which the law cannot supply. Decay of the per-dollar multiplier is guaranteed; decay of the return is NOT — a sufficiently accelerating Q could keep returns flat or rising. The pro elides demand-side from price-multiplier decay.
missing_cons: No treatment of metaorder DIRECTIONALITY/netting over a decade: the law is calibrated on net buy programs that complete; over 10-15yr there are large two-sided flows (sell-offs, capitulations, miner distribution, FTX-style forced selling). A static sqrt(Q) on NET cumulative demand ignores that intervening drawdowns permanently reset the float and price base. The decay framing implicitly assumes monotone net accumulation.

No survivorship/regime caveat on the BTC calibration itself: Donier-Bonart's window is 2011-2014 Mt.Gox-era Bitcoin (one dominant venue, no ETFs, no derivatives depth). Applying a law calibrated on that microstructure to a 2026+ ETF/CME/options-dominated market is a calibration-transfer assumption the deep-dive does not flag — arguably as large a stretch as the horizon extrapolation it does flag.

The Apollo source itself notes the 30.4% flow/price correlation is weak and that flows explain only a fraction of cap changes — meaning the very 'linear multiplier' the law claims to 'correct downward' is itself poorly identified. If the linear baseline is noise, a sqrt-haircut of noise is still noise; the deep-dive treats the multipliers as a credible anchor to correct rather than as evidence that flow->price is weakly identified at all.

No mention that sigma (an INPUT that scales impact linearly) is itself forecast at the ~57% realized floor, so the appreciation channel and the volatility channel are NOT independent: the same thin-liquidity mechanism that justifies holding vol high also amplifies impact per dollar. The synthesis imports vol 'separately' but the law ties them together — a coupling the notes acknowledge for vol-stays-high but not for its effect on the return band.

new_approaches.name: On-Chain Supply-Distribution & Flow Microstructure (URPD, Liveliness/Dormancy, Reserve Risk, Illiquid/Exchange-Flow, Entity-Cohort, LTH/STH)
new_approaches.description: This family reads Bitcoin not from aggregate cost-basis scalars (Realized Price/MVRV/SOPR/Thermocap — covered in approach #9) but from the DISTRIBUTION and FLOW of supply across the UTXO set. Five methodologically separate lineages: (1) the URPD cost-basis histogram — bars of supply bucketed by the price at which each UTXO last moved, revealing concentration "walls" (support/resistance) and thin "air-pockets"; (2) age-weighted spend FLOW — Coin-Days-Destroyed, Average/Median Dormancy (Tu-Xue ASOL/MSOL), and Blummer's Liveliness/Dormancy (ratio of CDD to all coin-days created), distilled into Hauge's Reserve-Risk conviction oscillator (price ÷ cumulative HODL-bank opportunity cost); (3) spend-propensity FLOAT classification — Schultze-Kraft's liquid/illiquid supply (entity liquidity L = cumulative outflows/inflows; illiquid if L≲0.25) and Clemente/Woo's Illiquid-Supply-Shock ratio; (4) venue FLOW — CryptoQuant exchange reserve/netflow and Exchange-Whale-Ratio; (5) entity-clustered cohort behavior — Glassnode's Accumulation-Trend-Score and whale-cohort (1k+ BTC) accumulation/distribution, plus the 155-day LTH/STH split (cohort realized price + cohort MVRV). A 10–15yr CMA does NOT fall out: every metric is a short-horizon timing/positioning oscillator. To force a CMA you must assume the float/flow regime mean-reverts and that net structural demand against a shrinking liquid float compounds at some rate — i.e., a supply-squeeze narrative wearing CMA clothing, with a severe ETF-era degradation caveat as supply migrates off-chain into custody.
new_approaches.medium_explanation: The thesis: because issuance is fixed and falling, what matters for price is how the EXISTING stock is distributed and whether it is flowing toward "strong hands" (illiquid, dormant, accumulating cohorts) or back to "weak hands" (exchanges, liquid float). URPD locates the cost-basis walls price must climb through; CDD/Liveliness/Dormancy and Reserve Risk measure whether long-term holders are spending or accumulating conviction; liquid/illiquid supply and exchange netflow quantify the float actually for sale; the 155-day LTH/STH split separates seasoned-holder cost basis from speculative flow. A supply-shock CMA reasons: if illiquid supply keeps absorbing more than issuance while ETF/treasury demand persists, a shrinking sellable float forces price up. But these are timing tools, not return models — none publishes a multi-year appreciation, and the realized appreciation-decay path (142%→65%→17%/yr) must discipline any extrapolation. The load-bearing risk: ETF/custody migration (~1.3M BTC, ~7% of supply, in wrappers) breaks every on-chain flow signal, since the marginal buyer never touches the chain.
key_drivers: URPD cost-basis histogram shape: concentration 'walls' (supply clusters that act as support/resistance) vs thin 'air-pockets' price moves through quickly; ATH- vs percent-partitioned binning

Age-weighted spend flow: Coin-Days-Destroyed, Average/Median Spent-Output Lifespan (ASOL/MSOL, Tu-Xue), Blummer Liveliness/Dormancy (CDD ÷ all coin-days created) — measures whether old coins are moving (distribution) or sitting (HODL)
Reserve Risk oscillator = current price ÷ cumulative HODL-bank (opportunity cost of NOT selling, accumulated from coin-days); low = high conviction + low price = attractive entry
Spend-propensity float: entity liquidity L = cumulative outflows/inflows (illiquid L≲0.25 / liquid 0.25–0.75 / highly-liquid ≳0.75); Illiquid-Supply-Shock ratio = illiquid ÷ (liquid+highly-liquid)
Exchange reserve / netflow (inflow−outflow) and Exchange-Whale-Ratio (top-10 inflows ÷ total inflows) as proxies for sell-side pressure / supply available to market
Entity-clustered cohort behavior: Accumulation-Trend-Score (size-weighted balance change across wallet cohorts), whale-cohort (1k+ BTC) accumulation vs distribution
155-day LTH/STH split: cohort realized price (on-chain cost basis) and cohort MVRV — separates seasoned-holder conviction from short-term speculative flow
Structural demand sinks (spot ETFs, corporate treasuries, sovereign reserves) draining liquid float faster than issuance — the supply-squeeze premise
pros: Grounded in observable UTXO-ledger data (move-prices, coin-ages, entity-clustered flows), not a fitted curve or narrative — URPD, CDD and liquid/illiquid classification are accounting transforms, not regression assumptions

Captures information aggregate cost-basis scalars (#9) cannot: the DISTRIBUTION of cost basis (URPD walls/air-pockets) and the directional FLOW of supply (toward illiquid strong hands vs back to exchanges) — genuinely orthogonal microstructure detail useful for tail/path-of-return and support-level work

Reserve Risk and the illiquid-supply ratio have real ex-post discriminating power: Reserve Risk has historically marked cyclical undervaluation (low) and blow-off tops (high); rising illiquid supply has preceded several supply-squeeze rallies — leading rather than coincident signals

Cohort separation (155-day LTH/STH, whale Accumulation-Trend-Score) maps cleanly to behavioral reality — seasoned holders and whales drive supply availability differently from speculators — making it a behaviorally honest middleware
Exchange netflow/reserve gives a near-real-time read on sell-side pressure and the actually-tradeable float, a discipline pure-scarcity (S2F) and pure-price (power-law) models entirely lack

Unlike S2F/Metcalfe, the careful versions do NOT publish a single hard price target, so they are harder to weaponize into a spurious decade forecast — their reluctance to forecast long-horizon is itself a feature
cons: Not a return model — every metric is a short-horizon TIMING/positioning oscillator with no native long-horizon expected-return output; a 10–15yr CMA is entirely grafted on by the analyst via a supply-squeeze assumption, exactly the over-extrapolation the literature warns against

Reflexive/circular: URPD and the LTH/STH/Reserve-Risk cost bases are transforms of PAST PRICE (coins stamped at move-time price), and Reserve Risk's denominator (HODL-bank) is endogenous to the bull market — high prices manufacture the very 'conviction floor' the model treats as fundamental

Severe ETF-era degradation, metric-specific: ~1.3M BTC (~7% of supply) sit in ETF custody and trade off-chain; daily on-chain transactions fell ~500K (Dec-2023) to ~250K (2025) at NEW highs. Exchange-reserve depletion no longer cleanly means cold-storage demand; illiquid supply is contaminated by custodial consolidation; the marginal buyer never touches the chain — breaking flow signals

Documented in-sample failures: Clemente's Sept-2021 'Illiquid Supply Floor $39K, never below again' was breached to ~$16K in 2022; his $53–57K supply-imbalance targets were undershot. In 2024–25 Reserve Risk, MVRV-Z, Pi-Cycle and related top-indicators failed to mark the cycle — the calibration visibly decays each cycle

Exchange-flow noise: market makers, OTC desks and institutional custodians move large BTC for reasons unrelated to immediate buy/sell intent, so netflow 'does not predict price movements with certainty'; whale-ratio and netflow are easily misread

Tiny sample / curve-fit risk: thresholds (illiquid L≲0.25, Reserve-Risk bands, 155-day cutoff) are calibrated on 2–3 cycles with lookahead bias; academic work finds on-chain metrics add only ~12–18% forecasting improvement and have weak, unstable out-of-sample predictive power for returns

Produces NO volatility or cross-asset correlation output whatsoever — the entire framework is silent on every CMA covariance cell; vol and the correlation vector vs equities/gold/TIPS must be imported from realized data

synthesized_outputs.appreciation_nominal: ~9–13%/yr (judgment, not a computed stat). This family has no native return output, so the only honest extrapolation is: a shrinking liquid float against persistent ETF/treasury demand supports continued appreciation, but the supply-squeeze premise weakens as illiquid supply approaches a saturation ceiling and as off-chain custody makes the float signal unreadable. Extrapolating the realized decay one regime past trailing-5y 17%, and discounting the documented signal-degradation, lands low-double-digits. I deliberately sit near the cross-approach central (~8–12%) and BELOW scarcity/Metcalfe bulls — these flow metrics cannot manufacture their own appreciation and have repeatedly over-promised supply-squeeze upside (Clemente $39K floor → $16K).
synthesized_outputs.appreciation_real: ~6–10%/yr (nominal less ~3% CPI). Judgment; the supply-squeeze tailwind is a one-time, decaying float-depletion re-rating, not a sustainable real growth rate.
synthesized_outputs.volatility: ~55–60%/yr (judgment; framework silent). A genuinely shrinking, illiquid float can amplify squeezes AND air-pocket crashes (URPD thin zones), so vol stays high; floor held AT realized trailing-5y ~57% — the sub-2yr ETF sample does not yet evidence compression below realized. Multiples of equity/gold vol.
synthesized_outputs.corr_growth_eq: ~0.45–0.55 (judgment; framework silent, so I inherit the rising trailing-window equity beta — 5y growth-eq corr 0.56 — and hold it elevated, since the ETF/institutional flows that drive accumulation and illiquid-supply growth ARE the same risk-on flows driving growth equities; the off-chain migration that degrades these metrics also tightens the equity link).
synthesized_outputs.corr_value_eq: ~0.30–0.40 (judgment; below growth, tracking the anchor's value-eq corr ~0.37 at 5y).
synthesized_outputs.corr_fi_nominal: ~0.15–0.25 (judgment; modestly positive via shared liquidity/rate-cycle sensitivity of the marginal institutional holder).
synthesized_outputs.corr_tips: ~0.20–0.30 (judgment; slightly above nominal FI, real-rate sensitivity of a long-duration risk asset).
synthesized_outputs.corr_gold: ~0.05–0.15 (judgment). The framework is silent on gold and gives no mechanism forcing co-movement; realized BTC-gold corr is ~0 (-0.01 full / +0.045 5y). Internal-contradiction note: the illiquid-supply/HODL 'strong-hands store-of-value' narrative is often read as a digital-gold thesis, but the flow data supplies no gold linkage and the realized number is ~0 — so I hold it at the bottom of the band and reject the digital-gold reading.
synthesized_outputs.notes: All synthesized numbers are decay-disciplined JUDGMENT, not model outputs — the family produces no native CMA. Appreciation is anchored to the realized 142%→65%→17% decay path and deliberately haircut for (a) supply-squeeze over-promise (Clemente $39K floor falsified) and (b) ETF/custody migration breaking the float signal. Vol/correlations are inherited from realized trailing-5y because the framework is silent. Gold corr held at band bottom against the digital-gold reading the strong-hands narrative implies.

new_approaches.rich_notes:
METHODOLOGY. This approach is the DISTRIBUTION-and-FLOW counterpart to approach #9's aggregate cost-basis scalars. Where #9 collapses the UTXO set into single numbers (Realized Price, MVRV, SOPR, Thermocap), this family keeps the cross-section and the directional flow. Five distinct lineages, each with its own author and its own ETF-era failure mode:

(1) URPD (Renato Shirakashi, popularized by Glassnode). A histogram: each bar sums the BTC whose last-move price fell in that bucket (ATH-partitioned into 100 bins 0→ATH, or percent-partitioned ±2% steps around spot). It exposes "walls" (cost-basis concentration that acts as support/resistance) and "air-pockets" (thin zones price traverses fast). This is purely descriptive — a map of where holders are anchored.

(2) Age-weighted spend FLOW. Coin-Days-Destroyed weights each spent coin by its dormancy. Tu & Xue (2017, arXiv:1712.10287) formalize Average/Median Dormancy (ASOL/MSOL) and link CDD to traded-pool size via Little's Law — explicitly a turnover/velocity measure, NOT a price forecaster (the abstract makes no predictive claim). Tamas Blummer's Liveliness = ΣCDD / Σ(all coin-days ever created), a 0–1 ratio that trends up when old coins move (distribution) and down when they sit (HODL); Dormancy is its inverse cousin. Hans Hauge's Reserve Risk distills conviction into an oscillator: price ÷ cumulative "HODL-bank" (the running opportunity cost of holders choosing NOT to sell). Low Reserve Risk = high conviction + low price = historically attractive; high = blow-off top. It is a cyclical timing oscillator, self-described as such.

(3) Spend-propensity FLOAT. Rafael Schultze-Kraft (Glassnode CTO) classifies every entity by liquidity L = cumulative outflows/inflows: illiquid (L≲0.25), liquid (0.25–0.75), highly liquid (≳0.75). Will Clemente & Willy Woo's Illiquid-Supply-Shock ratio = illiquid ÷ (liquid+highly-liquid) models the probability of a supply squeeze. Glassnode reported illiquid supply ~3.2x liquid+highly-liquid in 2022 (~78% of supply illiquid).

(4) Venue FLOW. CryptoQuant exchange reserve (coins on exchange wallets) and netflow (inflow−outflow); rising inflow = sell pressure. Exchange-Whale-Ratio = top-10 inflows ÷ total inflows.

(5) Entity-cohort behavior. Glassnode's Accumulation-Trend-Score (size-weighted balance change across cohorts) and whale-cohort (1k+ BTC) accumulation/distribution; plus the 155-day LTH/STH split — coins become statistically unlikely to move after 155 dormant days, so cohort realized price and cohort MVRV separate seasoned-holder cost basis from speculative flow.

KEY RELATIONSHIPS. The unifying CMA story is the supply squeeze: fixed/falling issuance + supply flowing into illiquid/dormant/accumulating hands + structural ETF/treasury/sovereign demand ⇒ shrinking sellable float ⇒ upward price pressure. But this is a TIMING narrative, not a return model. No metric outputs a multi-year expected return, vol, or correlation.

ON-RECORD MULTI-YEAR FORECASTS produced this way. The honest record is poor. Will Clemente's Sept-2021 "Illiquid Supply Floor" model declared ~$39K a floor BTC "may never drop below again" — BTC bottomed near $16K in 2022, a clean falsification. His Aug-2021 supply-imbalance targets ($53–57K) also undershot. These are the clearest cases of converting a flow metric into a forward price claim, and they failed. The careful publishers (Glassnode docs, Tu-Xue) explicitly decline long-horizon forecasts.

HISTORICAL FIT & FAILURE MODES. Pre-2017 these signals tracked cycles well. Post-futures and especially post-ETF, fit decays. The 2024–25 cycle is the decisive test: Bitcoin Magazine and 21shares document that Reserve Risk, MVRV-Z, Pi-Cycle and the top-indicator cohort failed to mark the cycle, and on-chain transactions fell ~500K→250K/day AT new highs. Mechanism of degradation: ~1.3M BTC (~7% of supply) migrated into ETF custody trading off-chain; exchange-reserve depletion no longer cleanly signals cold-storage demand; illiquid supply is contaminated by custodial consolidation; the marginal buyer never pricestamps the chain. Exchange netflow is further muddied by MM/OTC/custodian movement unrelated to intent. Academic work (data-source-diversity studies) finds on-chain metrics add only ~12–18% forecasting improvement with weak, unstable out-of-sample power.

CMA BOTTOM LINE. Treat this family as path/tail/support-level color, not a CMA generator. My synthesized ~9–13% nominal / ~6–10% real is a decay-disciplined judgment anchored to realized 142%→65%→17%, deliberately below scarcity bulls because the float metrics are reflexive (built from past price), have over-promised squeezes, and are precisely the signals most broken by the off-chain ETF migration. Vol ~55–60% (squeeze + air-pocket two-sidedness). Gold corr ~0.05–0.15: the strong-hands/HODL framing reads as digital-gold but the data shows ~0 — the load-bearing contradiction, held at band bottom.
