synthesized_outputs.horizon: 10-15yr (2026-2041), to match the BTC CMA mandate
synthesized_outputs.appreciation_nominal: ~16-22%/yr nominal (judgment, not a model output). Reading the central log-regression line forward, ln(10)·a/t decay takes instantaneous appreciation from ~mid-30s%/yr (age ~17) toward low-20s%/yr by ~2040, giving a ~20-27% central-line CAGR over 2026-2041. I haircut BELOW that to ~16-22% for (a) the documented retrofitting/recalibration bias (the curve is re-fit DOWNWARD each time price breaks the lower band, so the un-recalibrated line systematically over-predicts), and (b) left-tail/failure mass the single-path fit ignores. This sits above the cross-approach central (~8-12%) because the model's decay, while real, is still anchored to an extrapolated trend line; it remains the DECAY read, far below BTC's realized 142%→65%→17% history.
synthesized_outputs.appreciation_real: ~13-19%/yr real (subtracting ~3-3.5% long-run US inflation). Judgment; the model is nominal-only.
synthesized_outputs.volatility: ~55-60%/yr (judgment; model silent on vol-as-stat). Anchored to realized trailing-5y ~57%; the corridor's ~0.5×-5× width is consistent with very wide dispersion but is not an annualized vol. I hold the floor AT realized ~57% — the sub-2yr ETF sample shows no compression below realized — keeping vol ~3x equities.
synthesized_outputs.corr_growth_eq: +0.40 to +0.60 (judgment; model silent). Anchored to realized trailing-5y ~0.56, which rose post-ETF; I assume partial mean-reversion of the institutional-era spike, leaving BTC moderately-to-strongly tied to growth/tech equities.
synthesized_outputs.corr_value_eq: +0.20 to +0.35 (judgment; realized 5y ~0.37). Lower than growth equities; BTC trades as a long-duration risk asset loosely linked to the value factor.
synthesized_outputs.corr_fi_nominal: +0.10 to +0.20 (judgment; realized 5y ~0.19). Low-positive via shared liquidity/real-rate sensitivity; not a duration asset.
synthesized_outputs.corr_tips: +0.20 to +0.30 (judgment; realized 5y ~0.30). Modestly above nominal FI through a shared real-rate/liquidity channel; noisy and regime-dependent.
synthesized_outputs.corr_gold: ~0.0-0.10 (judgment). The Rainbow chart makes NO gold claim, so this is pure realized-baseline extrapolation: BTC-gold co-movement is ~0 (full -0.01, 5y +0.045). I keep it at the bottom of the band and explicitly reject any digital-gold reading — a time-curve model supplies no mechanism forcing gold co-movement, and the data supplies none.
synthesized_outputs.notes: The model legitimately constrains only the SHAPE of appreciation (monotone decay), not its level, and is silent on all moments beyond the price corridor. I therefore take the nominal figure from the central-line derivative (haircut for retrofitting/tail), and import vol + every correlation wholesale from the realized scripted baseline (CoinMetrics monthly: 5y vol ~57%, corr growth ~0.56, value ~0.37, FI ~0.19, TIPS ~0.30, gold ~0). The synthesized nominal (~16-22%) is deliberately HIGHER than the cross-approach central (~8-12%) and flagged as such: it reflects a curve-extrapolation, not a fundamentals-based CMA, and should be down-weighted accordingly in any blend.

new_approaches.rich_notes:
PROVENANCE & FORM. The Rainbow chart is a layering of two 2014 bear-market artifacts: BitcoinTalk user Trolololo's logarithmic-regression curve (22 Oct 2014) and Reddit user azop's humorous straight-line "rainbow" sentiment overlay. Rohmeo at Blockchaincenter merged them into the modern curved chart in 2019 and shipped the recalibrated V2 on 21 Nov 2022 after BTC fell below the V1 lower boundary in the FTX collapse. The load-bearing functional form is a regression of log(price) on ln(time): Blockchaincenter's V1 is quoted as y=2.9065·ln(x)−19.493; Coin Bureau quotes a V2-style log10(price)=2.6521·ln(weeks since 2009)−18.163 with R²≈0.95. This is the crucial distinction from #5 (Santostasi/Burger power-law-in-time), where log-price is LINEAR in log-time (a fixed exponent n≈5.6). Here log-price is CONCAVE in log-time — the ln(time) regressor bends the trend down even on the log axis, so the implied appreciation decays faster and the "fair value" flattens harder at long horizons. Nine bands, evenly log-spaced (~0.5× to ~5× the central line, each ~2× wide), supply the dispersion view. Several aggregators (Bitcoin Magazine Pro, Bitbo) actually publish a power-law variant log10(price)=a·log10(days)+b rather than the ln(time) form — the ecosystem is not internally consistent about whether it is log-regression-on-time or power-law-on-time, which itself is a tell that the curve is chosen for visual fit, not theory.

DECAY MATH FOR THE CMA. Under log10 P = a·ln(t) − b, d(ln P)/dt = ln(10)·a/t. With a≈2.6521 and t in weeks, at BTC's age ~905 weeks (~17.4yr) this is ~0.0067/week ≈ ~35%/yr; pushing t forward 15 years (~+780 weeks) drops it to ~22%/yr. So the central line forecasts a decaying nominal CAGR roughly in the low-20s%-to-mid-30s% band over a 2026-2041 window — the model self-generates decay, which is its one genuine virtue for a forward CMA. I anchor SYNTHESIZED nominal BELOW that (~16-22%) for retrofitting bias and tail risk.

RETROFITTING — THE CENTRAL CRITIQUE. The honest objection is not that the curve fits poorly but that it is MOVED whenever it fails. BTC broke the lower band in 2022; rather than falsify the framework, the slope/intercept were re-fit downward (V2 in Nov-2022, a further "maturing market / lower volatility" tweak in 2023). Coin Bureau notes the post-2021 trendline shifted ~15% and lower bands were extended to capture deeper drawdowns, "introducing subjectivity." A fair-value line that is silently re-parameterized each time price escapes it is descriptive, not predictive, and structurally un-falsifiable. Layer on the generic semi-log critique: log-price vs ln(time) are both monotone trends, and the log axis compresses error so massively that almost any rising series looks "tight" — the R²≈0.95 is an axis artifact, the same spurious-trend trap that sinks naive S2F and Metcalfe. The model also ignores demand, adoption, ETF flows, macro, and regulation entirely; its creators concede it has "no scientific basis" and call it a "meme chart." It is lagging (closing-price only, 20-50% overshoot at extremes), single-path (no left-tail mass), and breaks its own bands in both directions.

ON-RECORD FORWARD FIGURES. The careful authors publish NO dated multi-year price target — by design. The only concrete numbers are spot band snapshots (LBank, April-2026): Fire Sale ~$56k, BUY ~$75k, Accumulate ~$97k, Still Cheap ~$126k, with bands extended one halving cycle forward as "expected band ranges, not price predictions." Crypto marketing has nonetheless weaponized the corridor into "$1M floor by ~2037"-style claims (the same hype attached to the power-law corridor), which the Rainbow authors explicitly disclaim. The contrast with S2F is instructive and the LBank "broken models" piece makes it: S2F made hard dated predictions ($100k by 2021-23, $288k by 2024, ~$500k by 2025-26) that failed catastrophically against a ~$126k Oct-2025 peak; the Rainbow chart "survives" precisely BECAUSE it refuses to predict and recalibrates — durability via un-falsifiability, not accuracy. For a 10-15yr institutional CMA this is the worst of both worlds: it offers a decaying-trend shape that is qualitatively right but a level that is an extrapolated, periodically-massaged curve with no economic anchor, no native volatility, and no cross-asset correlation. I treat it as a sanity-check on the DECAY shape of appreciation, not as a source for the level, and import all vol/correlation cells from realized data.

issues: RECALIBRATION DIRECTION IS BACKWARDS (material). The document's central retrofitting thesis asserts the curve was 're-fit DOWNWARD each time price breaks the lower band' and that 'the un-recalibrated line systematically over-predicts,' then HAIRCUTS the synthesized CMA (from ~20-27% central-line to ~16-22%) explicitly for this 'downward recalibration bias.' But the cited sources say the opposite: Coin Bureau states 'Blockchaincenter recalibrated the trendline UPWARD by approximately 12-18%' (downweighting the 2021 peak; extending LOWER bands deeper to catch drawdowns). An upward level shift + deeper lower bands means the historical line if anything UNDER-stated downside, not over-predicted it. The haircut direction and its stated justification are contradicted by the very source cited ('Coin Bureau notes the trendline shifted ~15%').

THE LOAD-BEARING FORMULA IS BROKEN AND INHERITED UNCRITICALLY. The Coin Bureau V2 form log10(price)=2.6521*ln(weeks since 2009)-18.163 is quoted accurately (verified on coinbureau.com), but it does NOT reproduce real BTC prices: at age 17.4yr (905 weeks) it yields ~$0.78, at age 10 ~$0.03. The intercept/units are garbled (the working V1 days-form a=2.9065,b=19.493 correctly gives ~$22k at age 10 and ~$910k at age 17.4). The document presents both as live fair-value formulas and even leans on the corridor for the $56k-$126k band snapshot, without flagging that the quoted V2 formula is non-functional. Decay-rate derivation survives (scale-invariant), but the 'fair value level' the formula supposedly produces does not.

SYNTHESIZED CAGR OVERSTATED RELATIVE TO ITS OWN 'DECAY' FRAMING. The document repeatedly frames ~16-22% as 'the DECAY read, far below BTC's realized 142->65->17%/yr history.' But the most-recent realized window (trailing-5y) is already 17%/yr — so 16-22% BRACKETS-TO-EXCEEDS the latest realized, it is NOT 'far below realized.' The 'far below' claim only holds against the stale full-window 142%, which the document elsewhere correctly disowns as micro-cap-era dominated. So the headline figure is presented as conservative decay while actually sitting at/above the current realized trend.

CENTRAL-LINE CAGR UNDERSTATED. Document says reading the central line forward gives a '~20-27% central-line CAGR over 2026-2041.' Integrating the stated a=2.6521 (weeks) form over 2026-2041 gives ~28.8%/yr; the V1 a=2.9065 (days) form gives ~32%/yr. The true central-line read is ~29-32%, not 20-27%. This makes the actual gap between the model's own central case and the synthesized 16-22% LARGER than disclosed (i.e., a bigger, more discretionary haircut than the text implies).

INTERNAL FORMULA INCONSISTENCY ACKNOWLEDGED BUT NOT RESOLVED. The document correctly notes the ecosystem mixes log-regression-on-ln(time) (Blockchaincenter/Coin Bureau) with power-law-on-log10(days) (Bitbo/BM Pro) and calls this 'a tell.' Good. But it then derives its CMA decay from ONE form (ln-time, 1/t decay) while citing R^2~0.95 and band snapshots that come from the OTHER/garbled parameterization. The decay shape it sells is form-dependent and the document does not reconcile which form actually generated the cited numbers.
verdict.corrections: "1) Fix the retrofitting direction: per Coin Bureau, the trendline was recalibrated UPWARD ~12-18% (2021-peak downweighted; lower bands extended deeper), not 're-fit downward.' Rewrite the haircut rationale accordingly. The legitimate 'un-falsifiable / moved-when-it-fails' critique still stands, but the claim 'the un-recalibrated line systematically over-predicts -> haircut down' is unsupported; if anything the upward level shift cuts the other way. Either drop the retrofitting-bias haircut or re-justify it on tail-risk grounds alone. NOTE the separable truth: V2 lowered the long-run GROWTH SLOPE (flatter) even as it shifted the LEVEL up; the document conflates these into a single 'downward' and should distinguish slope vs intercept. 2) Flag the Coin Bureau formula as non-reproducing (yields <$1 at present age); either substitute the working V1 days-form (a=2.9065, b=19.493, days since genesis, gives ~$910k at age 17.4) or explicitly mark the V2 weeks-form as a garbled/units-broken quote. Do not present it as a usable fair-value generator. 3) Correct the central-line forward CAGR to ~29-32%/yr (verified by integrating both forms over 2026-2041), not 20-27%. 4) Drop or qualify 'far below realized 142->65->17' — against the relevant recent (5y) realized 17%, the synthesized 16-22% is at/above, not below; only the disowned full-window 142% makes it look conservative. 5) Realized cells (vol ~57%, corr growth 0.56 / value 0.37 / FI 0.19 / TIPS 0.30 / gold ~0, decay 142->65->17) all verified correct against the scripted empirical_anchor.json and need no change. Provenance (Trolololo 22-Oct-2014 + azop Aug-2014, Rohmeo 2019, V2 21-Nov-2022 post-FTX) verified correct. LBank Apr-2026 band snapshot ($56k/$75k/$97k/$126k) and S2F-failure contrast verified correct."
overstated_pros: 'Encodes appreciation DECAY ... qualitatively correct shape' is oversold as a virtue: the decay is a mechanical artifact of regressing on ln(time) with no demand/adoption variable, so it would 'decay' identically for any monotone series. The document's own con list says exactly this; listing the decay-shape as a genuine pro while the synthesized level (16-22%) is then anchored ABOVE recent realized makes the 'decay' framing rhetorical rather than load-bearing.

'Parameter-light, transparent and falsifiable ... deviations from the band are observable in real time' — directly contradicted by the document's own (correct) retrofitting con: a line that is re-parameterized whenever price escapes it is precisely NOT falsifiable. Calling it falsifiable in pros and un-falsifiable in cons is an unreconciled internal contradiction.
'R^2~0.95 in-sample' cited as a pro/strength while the cons correctly call it an axis artifact. It should never appear in the pro column as evidence of quality.
'The single most widely cited ... crypto-native fair-value band' — true as influence, but cited adjacent to language implying analytical merit; influence != validity and the phrasing blurs them.
missing_cons: NO REAL (inflation-adjusted) ANCHOR YET A REAL FIGURE IS SYNTHESIZED: the model is nominal-USD-vs-calendar-time only, so the ~13-19% real figure is nominal-minus-assumed-CPI with zero model content; the model cannot speak to real returns at all, which deserves an explicit con (the document buries it as 'judgment').

HALVING / SUPPLY-SCHEDULE BLINDNESS: the chart treats time as continuous and ignores the 4-year halving supply shocks that the COMPETING crypto-native models (S2F, even the power-law variants) at least nominally encode. For a maturing-asset CMA, ignoring the programmatic issuance collapse is a substantive omission, not just 'no demand variable.'

DENOMINATOR/SURVIVORSHIP IS WORSE THAN STATED: it is fit to the single surviving path AND the early fit window is the 2010-2013 micro-cap era where a handful of prints dominate the log-fit; the slope is therefore hostage to ~$0.01-$1 prints, an extreme leverage point the document mentions for realized appreciation but not as a fragility of the regression coefficients themselves.

BAND-WIDTH IS NOT A RISK MODEL: the document says the ~0.5x-5x corridor is 'not annualized vol,' but does not state the stronger point that the band width is a fitting choice (number/spacing of bands is hand-set), so it cannot be used as ANY kind of calibrated dispersion input — it is decorative.

ETF/INSTITUTIONAL REGIME BREAK is acknowledged for correlations but NOT for the trend: post-ETF spot demand is a genuine structural break that a time-only curve cannot represent, so extrapolating a pre-ETF-fitted slope through a post-ETF regime is a specific extrapolation hazard beyond the generic 'ignores flows' point.

new_approaches.name: Liquidity-Risk & Higher-Moment Priced Factors (Amihud Illiquidity, Co-Skewness / Downside-Tail Beta)
new_approaches.description: This approach prices expected cryptocurrency returns as compensation for SPECIFIC priced risks absent from the canonical Liu-Tsyvinski-Wu market/size/momentum set: (1) an Amihud-illiquidity premium (Zhang-Li 2023) where illiquid coins earn higher subsequent returns, transmitted partly through a systematic liquidity beta; and (2) higher co-moments — a downside-tail beta / downside-risk premium (Zhang-Li-Xiong-Wang 2021, in the Ang-Chen-Xing lineage) and a skewness premium (Chen-Liu 2024, in the Harvey-Siddique lineage). The crypto evidence is notably idiosyncratic-skew-driven (opposite to equities, where SYSTEMATIC coskewness is priced), and most anomalies are concentrated in tiny, illiquid coins. No native long-horizon level forecast falls out: it is a cross-sectional/Fama-MacBeth pricing framework that estimates per-unit factor premia on a panel of coins. To build a 10-15yr BTC CMA you must (a) measure Bitcoin's own loadings on Amihud-illiquidity, downside beta and coskewness, (b) form a view on each factor's forward premium, and (c) recognize a microstructure-DECAY mechanism: as Bitcoin's float deepens (ETFs, custody, derivatives), its Amihud illiquidity collapses toward zero, so any illiquidity premium it earns SHRINKS over the horizon. Bitcoin sits at the large-cap, deep-float, left-skewed end of every sort — precisely where these premia are smallest or absent.
new_approaches.medium_explanation: This family explains the cross-section of crypto returns with priced risks beyond market/size/momentum: an Amihud-illiquidity premium (illiquid coins earn more), a downside-tail-beta premium (Ang-Chen-Xing lineage), and a skewness premium (Harvey-Siddique lineage). Crypto's striking result is that skewness predictability is IDIOSYNCRATIC, not systematic coskewness as in equities, and that most anomalies live in the smallest 30-70% of coins. Key inputs: each coin's Amihud measure, downside beta, and (co)skewness, run through Fama-MacBeth/portfolio sorts. The framework yields no native CMA level; you measure Bitcoin's own loadings, assume forward factor premia, and translate. For a 10-15yr BTC CMA the load-bearing mechanism is microstructure DECAY: as ETFs, custody and deep derivatives compress Bitcoin's Amihud illiquidity toward zero, any illiquidity premium it once earned shrinks. Bitcoin is the largest, most liquid, left-skewed coin — sitting at the low-premium end of every sort — so this lens implies BTC's risk-premium FROM these specific factors is small and falling, reinforcing the appreciation-decay path rather than a high level.
key_drivers: Amihud illiquidity measure (|return| / dollar volume) and its level/trend for each coin — Bitcoin's collapses toward zero as float deepens (ETFs, custody, derivatives), the core decay mechanism
Systematic liquidity beta (covariance of coin returns with market-wide liquidity shocks) — distinct from the liquidity LEVEL premium; the Pastor-Stambaugh-style risk channel

Downside beta / downside-tail beta (return covariance with the market conditional on down markets) — Ang-Chen-Xing lineage; in crypto the premium is positive but driven by limits-to-arbitrage, not pure risk aversion

Co-skewness (systematic skewness with the crypto market) vs idiosyncratic skewness — crypto predictability is IDIOSYNCRATIC (Chen-Liu), opposite to equities where systematic coskewness is priced (Harvey-Siddique +3.6%/yr)
Market capitalization / float depth — anomalies concentrate in the smallest 30-70% of coins and largely vanish value-weighted; Bitcoin sits at the large-cap, low-premium extreme
Limits-to-arbitrage / mispricing intensity — premia widen when coins are hard to trade and shrink as arbitrage capital and liquidity arrive (post-ETF institutionalization)
Sign of Bitcoin's own skew: large-cap coins are MORE left-skewed (negative skew) — under a negative-skewness-premium regime this argues for LOWER, not higher, BTC expected return
pros: Grounds expected return in genuinely priced, theory-backed risks (illiquidity, downside tail, skewness) with a 25-year equity pedigree (Amihud 2002; Harvey-Siddique 2000; Ang-Chen-Xing 2006), not price-extrapolation or scarcity numerology

Supplies a real, mechanistic reason for appreciation DECAY specific to Bitcoin: as float deepens and Amihud illiquidity collapses, the illiquidity premium BTC can earn mechanically shrinks — a microstructure story the scarcity/network models lack

Cross-sectionally robust evidence: positive illiquidity premium (~25bps/week, Fitz 2021; Zhang-Li 2023 negative liquidity-return relation), positive downside-risk premium and a skewness premium all documented across hundreds of coins with Fama-MacBeth and portfolio sorts

Honest about crypto's distinctiveness — identifies that idiosyncratic (not systematic) skewness drives crypto, separating it cleanly from the equity coskewness story and from the behavioral lottery-MAX demand family
Directly portfolio-relevant: speaks to liquidity and tail covariances that matter for sizing BTC against equities/FI/gold, even if the level forecast is weak
cons: The anomalies concentrate in tiny, illiquid coins and largely VANISH value-weighted or after excluding the smallest 30-70% (Cryptocurrency anomalies and economic constraints, 2024) — Bitcoin, the largest and most liquid coin, sits exactly where these premia are smallest or absent, so the framework gives BTC almost NO extra expected return

Not a level/CMA model: it estimates per-unit cross-sectional factor premia, not a long-horizon price path. Any 10-15yr appreciation number is an analyst-imposed factor-premium assumption, not a model output

Self-defeating decay: the illiquidity premium relies on illiquidity, but Bitcoin's Amihud measure is collapsing toward zero with ETFs/custody/derivatives — the very maturation that makes BTC investable destroys the premium this lens would credit it with

Sign confusion / regime instability: crypto's downside-risk premium is POSITIVE (opposite to the usual safe-haven intuition) and explained by limits-to-arbitrage; the skewness premium is NEGATIVE and idiosyncratic-driven — both are fragile, sample-dependent, and may not be true risk premia but mispricing that arbitrages away

Short, overlapping samples (2014-2024) spanning few regimes, severe non-standard-errors / researcher-degrees-of-freedom problems (documented for crypto anomalies), and survivorship in the coin panel — premia may be data-mined

Silent on macro correlations and on Bitcoin's volatility level — it characterizes WHICH risks are priced cross-sectionally, not BTC's standalone vol or its co-movement with equities/FI/TIPS/gold, all of which must be imported

cited_outputs.notes: These are CROSS-SECTIONAL factor premia estimated on a panel of hundreds of coins (Fama-MacBeth + portfolio sorts), NOT Bitcoin-level CMA outputs. The framework deliberately publishes no BTC appreciation/vol/correlation figures. Crucially, the documented premia concentrate in the smallest, most illiquid coins and largely vanish for the largest/most-liquid coin — i.e. for Bitcoin specifically — so even the qualitative sign of BTC's factor compensation is small/ambiguous. The equity-lineage magnitudes (Harvey-Siddique +3.6%/yr coskewness; Ang-Chen-Xing +6%/yr downside) are provided only as the theoretical pedigree, not as BTC numbers.

synthesized_outputs.appreciation_nominal: ~7-11%/yr nominal (JUDGMENT, not a model output). Reasoning: this lens credits BTC with expected return only to the extent it LOADS on priced illiquidity/downside/skew factors. But the evidence shows these premia concentrate in tiny, illiquid coins and largely vanish for the largest, most liquid coin — and Bitcoin's Amihud illiquidity is collapsing toward zero as ETFs/custody/derivatives deepen its float, so the illiquidity premium it can earn DECAYS over the horizon. As a large-cap, LEFT-skewed (negative-skew) asset under a negative-skewness-premium regime, BTC sits at the LOW-premium end of every sort. Net: a modest systematic risk premium plus residual liquidity/tail compensation, landing below the trailing-5y realized 17% and consistent with the cross-approach central (~8-12%). I anchor ~7-11%, toward the lower half because the specific premia this approach prices are exactly the ones Bitcoin is shedding.
synthesized_outputs.appreciation_real: ~4-8%/yr real (subtract ~2.5-3% long-run US inflation). Judgment; reflects a maturing mega-cap whose illiquidity-based excess return is decaying toward a small tail/liquidity-risk compensation.
synthesized_outputs.volatility: ~50-60%/yr (JUDGMENT; framework silent on standalone vol). Anchored to realized trailing-5y ~57% with the floor held AT realized — the deep-float/ETF maturation that compresses the illiquidity premium also gently lowers vol, but the sub-2yr ETF sample does not yet evidence a floor below ~57%. Stays multiples of equities/gold.
synthesized_outputs.corr_growth_eq: ~+0.45 to +0.60 (JUDGMENT). The framework is cross-sectional and silent on macro betas, so anchored to realized trailing-5y +0.56, which rises with institutionalization. Notably, as BTC's idiosyncratic/illiquidity premia decay it behaves MORE like a systematic high-beta risk asset, reinforcing a strong equity tie.
synthesized_outputs.corr_value_eq: ~+0.30 to +0.40 (JUDGMENT). Below growth-equity; tracks realized trailing-5y +0.37.
synthesized_outputs.corr_fi_nominal: ~+0.10 to +0.25 (JUDGMENT). Low-positive via shared liquidity/discount-rate sensitivity; realized trailing-5y +0.19, drifting up as the marginal holder institutionalizes.
synthesized_outputs.corr_tips: ~+0.20 to +0.35 (JUDGMENT). Slightly above nominal FI through a shared real-rate/liquidity channel; realized trailing-5y +0.30.
synthesized_outputs.corr_gold: ~0.0 to +0.10 (JUDGMENT). This within-crypto factor framework supplies NO gold mechanism, and realized BTC-gold correlation is ~0 (full -0.01, 5y +0.04). I hold the bottom of the 0.0-0.15 band and explicitly reject any digital-gold reading — nothing in liquidity/skew pricing forces gold co-movement.
synthesized_outputs.notes: All synthesized numbers are JUDGMENT anchored to the realized BTC baseline (trailing-5y nom 17%, vol 57%, corr growth +0.56 / value +0.37 / FI +0.19 / TIPS +0.30 / gold +0.04), because the approach produces no native level/vol/correlation. The distinctive contribution is DIRECTIONAL: the microstructure-decay mechanism (Bitcoin's Amihud illiquidity collapsing toward zero as float deepens) plus BTC's large-cap/left-skew position at the low-premium end of every sort jointly argue the forward nominal should sit BELOW recent realized and toward the lower half of the cross-approach central band — reinforcing appreciation decay. Use this lens to discipline other models downward, not to manufacture a bullish BTC number.

new_approaches.rich_notes:
METHODOLOGY. This family extends the canonical Liu-Tsyvinski-Wu three-factor (market/size/momentum) cross-section by adding SPECIFIC priced risks: (1) liquidity — Zhang & Li (2023, Int. J. Finance & Economics) use the Amihud (2002) measure (|return|/dollar volume) and find a negative liquidity-return relation (illiquid coins earn higher subsequent returns) via univariate/bivariate sorts and Fama-MacBeth, robust to alternative liquidity proxies; (2) downside risk — Zhang, Li, Xiong & Wang (2021, J. Banking & Finance 133) find a POSITIVE cross-sectional relation between downside beta (Ang-Chen-Xing lineage) and future returns; (3) skewness — Chen & Liu (2024, Int. Review of Financial Analysis) find a NEGATIVE skewness premium driven by IDIOSYNCRATIC skewness, explicitly contrasting with equities where SYSTEMATIC coskewness is priced (Harvey-Siddique 2000, coskewness premium ~3.6%/yr; Ang-Chen-Xing 2006, downside-beta premium ~6%/yr). The estimation object is per-unit factor premia on a coin panel; there is NO native asset-level CMA.

KEY RELATIONSHIPS & MAGNITUDES. Fitz (2021, USU) reexamines 372 coins (Sep-2014 to May-2021) and finds a significant illiquidity premium of ~25bps/week, robust to weighting and model specification; the broader literature reports ~0.61%/month raw and ~0.44%/month four-factor-alpha high-minus-low illiquidity spreads. Crypto distinctives: large-cap coins are MORE left-skewed, small-cap more right-skewed; the negative skewness-return relation holds regardless of volatility (unlike equities, where volatility moderates it); limits-to-arbitrage explains why asymmetric-risk premia exceed left-tail premia at high arbitrage cost.

THE LOAD-BEARING CRITIQUE (why BTC gets little from this lens). 'Cryptocurrency anomalies and economic constraints' (2024) and related work show size/volume/distress/illiquidity anomalies are 'concentrated in hard-to-trade assets' and 'critically depend on harvesting extreme returns on small, illiquid, and volatile coins' — coming SOLELY from the 30-70% smallest coins. For 13 of 14 anomalies the low-liquidity group earns the higher long-short return; mispricing intensifies 'when cryptocurrencies lose their asset liquidity.' Momentum is the exception (stronger in large/liquid coins). Bitcoin is the largest, most liquid, most left-skewed coin — the exact corner where illiquidity and idiosyncratic-skew premia are smallest or absent. This is the microstructure-DECAY mechanism made concrete: an Amihud-illiquidity premium requires illiquidity, but BTC's Amihud measure is collapsing toward zero with ETF/custody/derivatives float-deepening, so the premium BTC can earn shrinks toward nil over a 10-15yr horizon. Under a negative-skewness-premium regime, BTC's left skew argues for LOWER expected return, not higher.

HISTORICAL FIT & FAILURE MODES. Fit is genuinely cross-sectional and replicated across hundreds of coins, but: (a) it does not produce a level — any BTC appreciation figure is an imposed factor-premium view; (b) the signs are unstable and partly explained by limits-to-arbitrage/mispricing rather than true risk compensation, so they should arbitrage away as the market matures (which is the decay thesis); (c) samples are short (2014-2024), overlapping, survivorship-prone, and crypto anomalies suffer documented 'non-standard errors' (large researcher-degrees-of-freedom dispersion across reasonable methodological choices); (d) the contradictory illiquidity findings — some studies find NO illiquidity premium and that return predictability diminishes in high-liquidity coins — directly imply BTC's premium is near-zero. There is no separate volatility or cross-asset-correlation output; those must be imported from realized data (trailing-5y vol ~57%; equity corr ~0.56; gold corr ~0).

ON-RECORD MULTI-YEAR FORECASTS. None. Unlike S2F, Metcalfe, power-law, or gold-parity families, this academic literature publishes NO dated BTC price targets or multi-year appreciation forecasts produced via this method. It is descriptive cross-sectional asset pricing; the authors do not extrapolate a Bitcoin level. That absence is itself informative: practitioners have not weaponized liquidity/higher-moment pricing into hype targets, because the honest reading gives Bitcoin a SMALL and SHRINKING factor premium. The CMA contribution is therefore directional, not numeric — it supports the appreciation-DECAY thesis (forward nominal well below realized 17%, toward ~7-11%) and warns that the maturation making BTC institutionally investable simultaneously erodes the very illiquidity/idiosyncratic-skew compensation this lens would credit. Skeptical bottom line: this approach is best used to DISCIPLINE other models downward, not to manufacture a bullish BTC number.

issues: MATERIAL CITATION ERROR: The source attributes an illiquidity premium of '~25bps/week (Fitz 2021)' in both the pros array and rich_notes. The actual Fitz (2021, USU) paper reports the most-liquid-minus-least-liquid weekly return spread as 'about 172 basis points' per its own abstract. I could not find any '25bps/week' figure in Fitz; the headline number is ~172bps/week. The 25bps figure is unverifiable and conflicts with the paper's stated magnitude (possibly conflated with a per-quintile step or a risk-adjusted alpha, but not labeled as such). This is the one load-bearing numeric error.

The '~0.61%/month raw and ~0.44%/month four-factor-alpha high-minus-low illiquidity spread' figures are attributed only to 'the broader literature' with no specific paper. These are not pinned to a verifiable source, so they cannot be confirmed and should either be cited to a specific paper or flagged as illustrative.

Minor link/attribution slip: the Chen-Liu skewness paper's published ScienceDirect identifier is pii S1057521924005581, whereas the source's representative_sources lists the Chen-Liu link via SSRN 4869652 (correct) but the same numeric pii family (S1057521924001509) is the 'Cryptocurrency anomalies and economic constraints' paper. The SSRN link for Chen-Liu is correct; just note the two IRFA papers are distinct and should not share a pii.

Internal-consistency tension (not an error, but worth flagging): the synthesized nominal band is '~7-11%' yet the notes repeatedly say 'below realized 17%' and 'toward the lower half of the cross-approach central (~8-12%)'. 11% top of band is below 17% realized (fine), but the upper end (11%) sits at/above the cross-approach central midpoint while the prose argues for the LOWER half. The 7-11% band is defensible but the framing slightly undersells how aggressive even 11% is for a framework whose own logic says BTC's specific factor premia are near-zero and decaying.

The framework genuinely produces NO native level/vol/correlation, which the source states honestly. But that means ALL synthesized CMA numbers (appreciation, vol, every correlation) are pure judgment anchored to the realized baseline, not outputs of this approach. The synthesis is transparent about this, so it is not deceptive — but a reader could mistake the precision of the bands (e.g. '+0.45 to +0.60') for something the liquidity/skew literature supports, which it does not.

Do not let it overlap with the 'Cryptocurrency anomalies and economic constraints' pii (S1057521924001509)."]
missing_cons: No treatment of the negative-vs-positive-sign collision for BTC specifically: the framework simultaneously implies a NEGATIVE skewness premium (BTC is left-skewed -> should LOWER expected return) and a POSITIVE downside-beta premium (BTC has high downside beta -> should RAISE it). For Bitcoin specifically these two priced higher-moment channels push in OPPOSITE directions and could roughly cancel, leaving the factor contribution genuinely indeterminate in sign, not just 'small'. The cons mention sign instability generically but never confront that BTC's own loadings net out ambiguously.

Survivorship and delisting bias in the coin panel is mentioned once but understated: dead-coin survivorship in crypto cross-sections is severe and systematically inflates measured premia in the small/illiquid bucket — the exact bucket the load-bearing critique relies on. This cuts BOTH ways (it weakens the very evidence the source uses to argue BTC's premium is small), which is not acknowledged.

No discussion that Bitcoin's Amihud illiquidity was already near the cross-sectional minimum BEFORE ETFs (BTC was always the most-liquid coin). The 'decay toward zero' mechanism is presented as forward-looking, but for BTC the illiquidity premium was arguably ~0 throughout the sample — so there is little left to 'decay'. The decay narrative is more relevant to the broader altcoin universe than to BTC, slightly overstating the framework's marginal insight for a BTC-specific CMA.

Liu-Tsyvinski-Wu (the canonical 3-factor base this extends) is cited as 'Liu-Tsyvinski-Wu' but the seminal crypto-factor paper is Liu, Tsyvinski & Wu (2022, Journal of Finance, 'Common Risk Factors in Cryptocurrency') — worth pinning since the whole framework is positioned as an extension of it; its absence from representative_sources is a gap.
overstated_pros: Pro #3 states a 'positive illiquidity premium (~25bps/week, Fitz 2021)' as cross-sectionally robust evidence. As above, the 25bps magnitude is unverifiable/misattributed (Fitz's number is ~172bps/week), so the specific quantitative backing of this pro is overstated even though the directional finding (illiquid coins earn more) is real.

Pro #2 ('supplies a real, mechanistic reason for appreciation DECAY... as Amihud illiquidity collapses') is somewhat overstated for BTC specifically: Bitcoin was already the most-liquid coin with near-floor Amihud throughout the sample, so there is little BTC-specific illiquidity premium left to decay. The mechanism is real for the altcoin cross-section but marginal for a BTC standalone CMA — the pro implies more decay headroom than BTC actually had.

Pro #5 ('Directly portfolio-relevant: speaks to liquidity and tail covariances that matter for sizing BTC') overstates usability: the framework publishes no BTC vol, no cross-asset correlations, and the cons admit all of those must be imported. The pro claims portfolio relevance that the approach cannot actually deliver without grafting on a separate model.

new_approaches.name: Entropy-Pooling / Fully-Flexible-Probabilities Stress-View CMA Construction (Meucci)
new_approaches.description: A CMA *construction methodology*, not a forecasting model. Start from a "prior" panel of joint scenarios for the asset set (built from a historical/bootstrapped, deliberately non-normal, fat-tailed, skewed return panel, or a Monte-Carlo factor model), each scenario carrying a probability. The analyst then states forward VIEWS as linear constraints on those probabilities: views on expectations (or medians, for fat tails), volatilities, the full correlation matrix, skewness/kurtosis, quantiles/VaR, and tail co-dependence. Entropy Pooling (EP) finds the *posterior* probability vector that satisfies every view while staying as close as possible to the prior, by minimizing Kullback-Leibler relative entropy (Meucci 2008/2010). A confidence parameter c in [0,1] opinion-pools prior and full-confidence posterior, so views can be partially trusted; multiple users/views blend naturally. For Bitcoin this is uniquely suited: it lets you impose a decaying-appreciation view, a hard volatility *floor*, explicit left-tail (ruin) mass, AND a near-zero BTC-gold correlation simultaneously on a non-Gaussian prior, then read out a coherent, internally consistent CMA (mean, vol, full correlation matrix, tail measures) — something Black-Litterman cannot do because BL imposes only mean views under a Gaussian prior.
new_approaches.medium_explanation: Entropy Pooling treats CMA-setting as a measure-change problem. You build a large panel of joint scenarios for BTC plus the correlation set (typically a fat-tailed historical bootstrap, so skew and crash mass are already present), each with a probability. Forward beliefs enter as linear constraints on those probabilities: mean/median (appreciation), volatility (a floor), the whole correlation matrix, skew, kurtosis, VaR/quantiles, and tail co-dependence. EP solves for the posterior probabilities that satisfy all views with minimum Kullback-Leibler divergence from the prior, then a confidence c shrinks the result back toward the prior (Meucci 2008/2010). The output is a fully coherent distribution from which every CMA cell — appreciation (nominal/real), vol, each pairwise correlation, downside risk — is computed jointly, not bolted together. For a 10-15yr BTC CMA it is the natural engine: impose the realized appreciation-decay path (142%→65%→17% to ~8-12% forward), a ~50-60% vol floor, deliberate left-tail mass, and ~0 BTC-gold correlation, and let EP reconcile them. It generates nothing on its own — garbage views in, garbage CMA out.
key_drivers: Prior scenario panel: the choice and construction of the baseline joint distribution (historical bootstrap vs Monte-Carlo factor model; how much fat-tail/skew/crash mass is baked in) — EP cannot manufacture tail mass the prior lacks
View set: which moments are constrained (mean/median, volatility, full correlation matrix, skew, kurtosis, VaR quantiles, tail co-dependence) and the numerical targets imposed on each
Confidence parameter c in [0,1]: opinion-pooling weight that shrinks the full-confidence posterior back toward the prior, governing how aggressively views override history
Use of median/interquartile-range location and dispersion measures instead of mean/variance for fat-tailed, possibly infinite-variance BTC returns

View ordering / partitioning: with many simultaneous moment views the naive single-shot EP can be suboptimal, so the grouping and sequence of constraints (Sequential Entropy Pooling) materially affects the posterior
Effective Number of Scenarios (ENS): how much the views collapse the prior's diversity — a low ENS warns that the views are over-distorting the panel
pros: Strictly more general than Black-Litterman/BMA: BL imposes only mean views under a Gaussian prior, whereas EP accepts views on volatility, the entire correlation matrix, skew, kurtosis, quantiles/VaR and tail co-dependence on an arbitrary non-normal prior — exactly the moments that matter for a fat-tailed, skewed asset like BTC

Internally coherent by construction: every CMA cell (appreciation, vol, all pairwise correlations, downside risk) is read from one posterior distribution, so the inputs are guaranteed mutually consistent — you cannot accidentally specify an appreciation/vol/correlation triple that has no valid joint distribution

Minimal-distortion / least-spurious-structure property: KL-minimization changes the prior only as much as the views require, generalizing Bayesian updating (Caticha-Giffin), so unstated features of the fat-tailed prior (crash mass, skew) survive untouched

Confidence parameter c lets you down-weight speculative long-horizon BTC views toward the historical prior, and opinion-pooling cleanly blends multiple analysts/scenarios — ideal when BTC views are genuinely uncertain

No repricing needed and views can be inequalities/rankings, so it scales to large scenario panels and lax/qualitative beliefs ('decaying but still positive'); mature open-source implementations exist (Meucci MATLAB/R; fortitudo.tech Python; skfolio)
cons: Produces NO forecast of its own — it is a reconciliation engine, so the BTC appreciation/vol/correlation numbers are entirely the analyst's imposed views; it adds rigor and consistency but zero independent predictive content (garbage views in → coherent garbage CMA out). It cannot adjudicate the central question of *what* BTC's forward return is

Garbage-prior risk: EP cannot create tail/crash mass the prior panel lacks. A BTC prior bootstrapped only from the survivorship-biased 2010-2026 path embeds BTC's good luck and under-weights absorbing-zero ruin; the posterior inherits that optimism no matter how the views are set

View-conflict and order/partition dependence: imposing many moment views simultaneously (mean + vol floor + full correlation + skew + tails) can yield a posterior that satisfies constraints in a degenerate way (collapsing the effective number of scenarios). The need for Sequential Entropy Pooling (Vorobets) to get 'much better results for the same views' is itself an admission that the naive single-shot solution is fragile and grouping-dependent

Confidence c and the prior are subjective and unobservable; there is no market-implied or data-driven way to pin them for a no-cashflow asset, so two honest analysts can produce very different BTC CMAs from the same engine — false precision risk

Practitioner-only / not validated on crypto: there is no peer-reviewed application of EP to a 10-15yr Bitcoin CMA, no out-of-sample track record, and the method silently assumes the prior panel's dependence structure is a reasonable forward template — questionable across BTC's regime breaks (ETF era, institutionalization)

cited_outputs.notes: Critical: this approach produces no on-record BTC numbers because it is an engine, not a forecaster. The closest practitioner deployment (Vorobets/Fortitudo, skfolio) demonstrates EP on equity/bond/commodity panels, not a published 10-15yr BTC CMA. Any BTC figures below are SYNTHESIZED — they represent the views a disciplined EP build would be seeded with (decay-consistent mean, vol floor, ~0 gold correlation), reconciled on a fat-tailed historical prior.

synthesized_outputs.appreciation_nominal: ~8-12%/yr nominal (the appreciation VIEW I would impose, then let EP reconcile with the vol-floor and tail views). EP itself forecasts nothing; this anchors to BTC's realized appreciation decay (142%→65%→17% over full/10y/5y windows) extrapolated forward below the trailing-5y 17%, consistent with the honest cross-approach central. I would impose it as a *median* view, not a mean, because the fat-tailed prior's mean is distorted by upside outliers.

Anchored at realized trailing-5y ~57%; I would NOT let views push it below ~50% because the sub-2yr ETF sample does not yet evidence compression below realized, and EP cannot invent low-vol scenarios the fat-tailed prior lacks.
