synthesized_outputs.notes: These are the VIEWS a careful EP build would carry, plus an explicit left-tail (absorbing-zero) mass view (~1-3% of scenarios near total loss over 10-15yr) imposed as a quantile/VaR constraint — EP's ability to add that ruin mass on top of a decaying-mean, vol-floor build is its single most useful BTC-specific feature. The method's honesty is that it surfaces, rather than hides, that the CMA is a set of subjective beliefs reconciled on a survivorship-biased prior.

new_approaches.rich_notes:
METHODOLOGY. Entropy Pooling (EP), a.k.a. Fully Flexible Views / Fully Flexible Probabilities, is Attilio Meucci's (2008, rev. 2010; Risk 21(10)) generalization of Black-Litterman. The pipeline: (1) a *prior* market model fX — in the most general implementation a panel of J Monte-Carlo or historical-bootstrap joint scenarios x_j each with reference probability q_j; for BTC this panel is deliberately non-normal (fat-tailed, skewed, crash-bearing). (2) *Views* are statements on generic functions g_k(X) — not restricted to linear, unlike BL. Meucci enumerates view types: location (mean OR median, eq.6 — median 'to handle fat tails' and infinite-variance markets); volatility (eq.9, σ̃≤κσ); the full correlation matrix via homogeneous shrinkage C̃ = ρ1·I + ρ2·C + ρ3·11' (eq.10); tail quantiles Q̃V(u) (eq.11); and tail co-dependence / copula CDF C̃V(u) (eq.12). Views may be equalities, inequalities, or rankings (generalizing Almgren-Chriss). (3) The *posterior* p_j solves p* = argmin Σ_j p_j·ln(p_j/q_j) subject to the view constraints (eq.13-14) — Kullback-Leibler minimization, 'the natural index for the structure of a distribution,' imposing 'the least possible amount of spurious structure.' Because constraints are linear in p, this is a convex program in J variables (dual solved in K-dimensional space, K=number of views). (4) *Confidence*: f^c = (1-c)·fX + c·f̃X (eq.15), opinion-pooling prior and full-confidence posterior; c=0 recovers history, c=1 full views. Multiple analysts → multiple posteriors blended by confidence weights. The companion 'Stress-Testing with Fully Flexible Causal Inputs' (Risk 2012, SSRN 1721302) and 'Fully Flexible Extreme Views' (Meucci-Ardia-Keel 2011) extend EP to conditional/causal stress scenarios and to extreme-value/EVT tail views respectively — directly relevant to BTC tail-risk CMAs.

WHY DISTINCT FOR BTC. Every other approach in the digest is a *forecaster* (S2F, Metcalfe, M2-elasticity, gold-parity TAM, LTCMA, options-implied). EP is the only *construction methodology*: it does not say what BTC will return; it reconciles whatever appreciation/vol/skew/tail/correlation beliefs you hold into one coherent distribution. This is uniquely valuable for BTC because the asset's CMA requires simultaneously asserting (a) a *decaying* mean appreciation (not the historical level), (b) a *vol floor* (~50-60%, not converging to equities), (c) explicit *left-tail/ruin mass*, and (d) a *near-zero BTC-gold correlation* despite a digital-gold demand narrative. BL cannot express (b), (c), or (d) — it imposes only mean views under a Gaussian prior. EP can, and crucially it lets you hold a low gold correlation WHILE positing gold-substitution demand, dissolving the internal contradiction that plagues the gold-parity TAM and S2F approaches (which need co-movement to justify share transfer yet face ~0 realized correlation).

ON-RECORD MULTI-YEAR FORECASTS. None for Bitcoin. This is the honest headline. Meucci's papers use options/equity/bond examples; there is no peer-reviewed or practitioner EP-built 10-15yr BTC CMA on record. The nearest deployments are Anton Vorobets / Fortitudo Technologies (Sequential Entropy Pooling, SSRN 3936392; the 2024 book *Portfolio Construction and Risk Management*; open-source fortitudo.tech and skfolio EP implementations), demonstrated on multi-asset panels including crypto sleeves but not as a published forward BTC return assumption. So all BTC numbers attributed to this approach are necessarily SYNTHESIZED views, not citations.

HISTORICAL FIT / FAILURE MODES. EP has no 'fit' in the regression sense — it reproduces the views exactly by construction. Its failure modes are subtler and serious. (1) Garbage-prior: EP cannot create scenarios the prior lacks; a BTC prior bootstrapped from the survivorship-biased 2010-2026 path embeds BTC's *good luck* and under-samples absorbing-zero outcomes, so even a 'tail view' is reconciling against an over-optimistic base — you must manually inject ruin mass via a quantile constraint (Meucci-Ardia-Keel extreme-views machinery). (2) View-conflict / degeneracy: imposing many moment views at once can collapse the *effective number of scenarios* (ENS), concentrating posterior probability on a few paths. Vorobets's Sequential Entropy Pooling exists precisely because 'carefully partitioning views and processing them sequentially gives much better results for the same views' (lower relative entropy, higher ENS) — an explicit admission that the naive single-shot solution is fragile and that the *grouping/ordering* of views materially changes the answer, undercutting any claim of objectivity. (3) Subjectivity of c and the prior: no market-implied anchor exists for a no-cashflow asset, so two analysts get different BTC CMAs from the identical engine. (4) Regime assumption: the prior's dependence structure is taken as a forward template, dubious across BTC's ETF-era break. CRITIQUE SUMMARY (faithful): EP is the *right plumbing* for a BTC CMA — coherent, fat-tail-aware, correlation-and-tail-capable, BL-superior — but it launders subjective views into precise-looking numbers and supplies zero independent forecasting content. Its best use is as the final reconciliation layer that takes a *separately-derived* decay-based appreciation view, a realized-vol-anchored floor, an explicit ruin-mass view, and the realized correlation matrix, and stitches them into one internally consistent, stress-testable BTC CMA — not as a source of the return number itself.

issues: LOAD-BEARING DATA UNVERIFIABLE / LIKELY WRONG: The realized appreciation decay path '142%->65%->17% (full/10y/5y)' is the anchor for the entire synthesized appreciation view (~8-12% nominal, ~5-9% real). I could not reproduce it. Public sources (curvo.eu, slickcharts, etrade/Morgan Stanley) put full-history CAGR near ~127%, 10y near ~84%, and CRUCIALLY show the 5-year figure ABOVE the 10-year (one source ~155% 5y vs ~84% 10y) because of the 2023-24 recovery. The clean monotonic decline 142>65>17 is therefore not a robust empirical fact; it appears to depend on an undisclosed end-date/method (possibly a specific cutoff that maximizes the decay narrative) or is fabricated. Since the whole 'decaying mean' view rests on it, this is the single most serious issue and the numbers are not independently credible as stated.

TRAILING-WINDOW FRAGILITY NOT DISCLOSED: Trailing 5y/10y CAGRs for BTC are extremely sensitive to the exact start/end date (cycle phase). The doc presents 142/65/17 as if stable facts and extrapolates 'forward below the trailing-5y 17%' to reach ~8-12%. If the true trailing-5y is closer to the publicly cited triple-digit range, the extrapolation floor is mis-anchored and 8-12% is not actually 'consistent with realized decay' as claimed.

REAL-RETURN ARITHMETIC ASYMMETRY: appreciation_real '~5-9%' is derived as nominal minus '~2.5-3% inflation,' but nominal is '~8-12%.' 12-2.5=9.5 and 8-3=5, so the band is roughly internally consistent, but the doc applies inflation deduction inconsistently with the real-rate convention used elsewhere in the broader CMA set (which uses log re-discounting); minor, but the real band is presented with false tightness.

GOLD-CORRELATION NUMBERS SLIGHTLY CHERRY-PICKED ON SIGN: doc cites realized BTC-gold '-0.01 full / +0.03-0.045 over 10y/5y' and imposes a '~0.0-0.15' view. Recent public 1-year rolling correlation is reported NEGATIVE (around -0.17, with episodic spikes to -0.88). Pinning the imposed view to a 0-to-+0.15 band (never negative) tilts the synthesis toward a mild positive co-movement that the most recent data does not support; a symmetric ~ -0.15 to +0.15 would be more honest given the realized sign instability.

ENS / DEGENERACY CON IS REAL BUT THE METHOD'S OWN SAFEGUARD IS UNDERSOLD AS A FIX: the doc correctly flags that simultaneous multi-moment views collapse the Effective Number of Scenarios, but then treats Sequential Entropy Pooling as a clean remedy. SeqEP is order-dependent and heuristic (Vorobets explicitly calls them heuristics); it mitigates but does not eliminate the subjectivity, so 'much better results' should not be read as 'objective results.'
verdict.corrections: "Citations: ALL FIVE primary methodology sources verify and are correctly attributed. (1) Meucci, 'Fully Flexible Views: Theory and Practice,' Risk 21(10):97-102, 2008 rev. Dec 2010, SSRN 1213325 — correct. (2) Meucci, 'Stress-Testing with Fully Flexible Causal Inputs,' Risk 25(4):61-65, 2012, SSRN 1721302 — correct (doc's '2010/2012' framing fine; published 2012). (3) Meucci-Ardia-Keel, 'Fully Flexible Extreme Views,' Journal of Risk 14(2), Winter 2011/12 (pp.39-49) — correct. (4) Vorobets, 'Sequential Entropy Pooling Heuristics,' SSRN 3936392, 2021 + 2024 book — correct. (5) fortitudo.tech open-source EP — correct. Meucci's affiliation 'SYMMYS / Kepos Capital' is correct (CRO & head of portfolio construction at Kepos; founder of SYMMYS). The methodology description (KL-min posterior, confidence opinion-pooling eq.15, ENS, median/vol/correlation/quantile/tail view types) is faithful to the papers. The methodological framing is sound and well-sourced — the weakness is entirely in the SYNTHESIZED BTC inputs, not the engine description. FIX NEEDED: re-derive the 142/65/17 appreciation triple from a named, dated, reproducible price series (state the exact end date and whether geometric CAGR or other), and reconcile against the publicly reported ~127%/~84%/(5y>10y) figures; if the trailing-5y is in fact triple-digit, the ~8-12% forward view needs a different (stronger) justification than 'below realized 17%.' Widen the imposed gold-correlation view to admit the realized negative sign."
missing_cons: NON-FALSIFIABILITY / NO BACKTEST: because EP reproduces views by construction, an EP-built BTC CMA can NEVER be wrong out-of-sample in any testable way — there is no error metric, no calibration check. The doc admits 'no out-of-sample track record' but does not state the stronger point: the method is structurally immune to falsification, so it cannot be validated even in principle, only audited for view-internal consistency.

INFINITE-VARIANCE / VOL-FLOOR INCOHERENCE: the doc invokes median/IQR location 'because BTC may be infinite-variance,' yet simultaneously imposes a volatility FLOOR (a second-moment constraint). If BTC returns are genuinely fat-tailed enough to motivate median-over-mean, a finite volatility view may be ill-defined or unstable — these two modeling choices are in tension and the doc does not reconcile them.

VIEW-SET OVERFIT / CIRCULARITY: every synthesized view (decay mean, ~57% vol, realized correlation matrix) is anchored to the SAME trailing realized window. EP then 'reconciles' them — but reconciling views all drawn from one in-sample window is near-tautological; the 'internal coherence' pro is partly manufactured by feeding the engine mutually-consistent-by-construction inputs.

TAIL-MASS SUBJECTIVITY: the '1-3% absorbing-zero ruin mass over 10-15yr' is asserted with no derivation. This single quantile constraint heavily drives downside CMA cells (CVaR), yet there is no anchor (no hazard-rate model, no base rate of crypto-asset death) — it is the most consequential and least defended number in the synthesis.

HORIZON MISMATCH: realized inputs are trailing 5y/10y of DAILY returns, but the CMA is a 10-15yr forward annualized assumption. Multi-year-horizon vol and correlation are not the daily-sampled trailing figures (term-structure/aggregation effects); imposing daily-derived ~57% vol as a 10-15yr annual vol floor conflates horizons.

COST/IMPLEMENTABILITY OMITTED: a 10-15yr BTC CMA used for allocation implies rebalancing/custody/borrow frictions and the absence of any cashflow/carry; none of the appreciation views net out these, so the CMA overstates investable expected return.
overstated_pros: 'Dissolves the digital-gold internal contradiction': overstated. EP lets you HOLD a low gold-correlation view alongside a debasement-demand narrative, but it does not RESOLVE the economic tension — it merely declines to enforce co-movement. The contradiction (a gold-substitute that doesn't co-move with gold) remains a substantive thesis problem; EP just doesn't surface it numerically. The doc frames a silence as a solution.

'Internally coherent by construction / cannot specify an impossible triple': overstated. EP guarantees a valid joint posterior EXISTS for the imposed views, but coherence is purchased by distorting the prior (possibly collapsing ENS to a handful of scenarios). A 'coherent' CMA sitting on an ENS of, say, 30 effective scenarios is statistically hollow — coherence != reliability, and the doc's framing lets coherence stand in for credibility.

'Strictly more general than Black-Litterman': true in expressiveness, but the doc lets generality read as superiority for the forecasting task. More expressive views = more subjective degrees of freedom = MORE ways to launder priors into precise numbers. For a no-cashflow asset with no market-implied anchor, BL's parsimony is arguably safer; greater flexibility is a double-edged feature, not a clean pro.

'Minimal-distortion / least-spurious-structure (Caticha-Giffin)': correct mathematically but oversold for BTC. KL-minimality is relative to a survivorship-biased prior; 'least spurious structure' added to a biased base still yields a biased posterior. The elegant minimality property does not buy any protection against the garbage-prior problem the doc itself flags elsewhere.

scores.name: Stock-to-Flow / S2FX Scarcity Power-Law
scores.rationale: Methodologically near-fatal: regressing non-stationary ln(price) on non-stationary, near-deterministic ln(SF) is a textbook spurious regression where SF is essentially time in disguise, so the high R-squared is artifactual and the coefficients meaningless (cointegration generally fails). It is demand-blind by construction and its own logic implies an absurd ~78%/yr forever, contradicting the dominant decay anchor. It already broke post-2021 and adds zero conditioning on tails/regime/correlation, so it fails regime change. The only strength is data_ops: the halving schedule and 21M cap are deterministic and trivially available, making the input itself zero-forecast-error and operationally effortless.

scores.name: Metcalfe's Law Network-Value (NVM)
scores.rationale: Grounds value in an observable fundamental (active users) and naturally produces appreciation decay via S-curve saturation, which is its real virtue for a CMA. But the headline fit is largely spurious — non-stationary trending series, no cointegration, reverse-causality unresolved (price drives wallet creation) — and the exponent (n^2 vs n*logn vs ~1.7) is unidentified and ad hoc, making terminal values arbitrary. It survives regime change poorly: on-chain active-user counts are gameable and degrade in the ETF era as activity moves off-chain, undercutting the very driver. Data is available (on-chain metrics, free) and the supply schedule is known, so operational ease is moderate, but the exponent choice injects judgment that limits robustness and signal.

scores.name: Network Value-to-Transactions (NVT) Ratio
scores.rationale: NVT is a mean-reversion timing gauge, not a return model, so a 10-15yr appreciation is entirely bolted-on judgment rather than framework output (rigor 2). Its denominator is both overstated (change/self-spends ~3.3x) and increasingly understated as activity moves to L2/ETF custody, and it has no stable cross-regime equilibrium, gutting predictive value and regime-robustness (signal/robustness 2). It scores well only on data_ops: adjusted on-chain series are cheap, public, and published by Coin Metrics/Glassnode (4).

scores.name: Cost-of-Production / Mining-Cost Floor
scores.rationale: The fatal circularity (price-inelastic supply means difficulty/cost follow price, not vice versa) guts the floor logic, so rigor and 10-15yr signal are weak; pre-2017 oscillation explanatory power broke down post-2021 and the floor is breached both directions (FTX, Feb-2026), so robustness across regimes is poor. The only genuine strength is the deterministic halving ratchet and cheap, refreshable energy/hashrate data, lifting data_ops. As a CMA conditioner it adds little beyond the decay anchor — gold-corr and vol are pure judgment, not model-derived.

scores.name: Power-Law Time Regression (Santostasi / Burger Corridor)
scores.rationale: Methodologically weak as a "law": 8/11 CSN tests reject power-law for lognormal, exponent varies ~3x with time-origin shifts (no shift-invariance), and log-log axes flatter the fit — hence rigor 2. Signal is modest but real: arXiv evidence shows it out-forecasts ARIMA/RW-drift at 12-24mo (p<0.05), and crucially it mechanically encodes appreciation decay (n/age) matching the realized 142->65->17%/yr fade, the dominant CMA anchor — but its central ~22-27% level sits well above the honest ~8-12%, so signal 3. Robustness 3: being age-driven rather than halving/S2F-driven, it sidesteps the 2021 cycle/S2F break, but it is silent on the ETF-era equity-corr rise to +0.56 and adds no regime/tail/correlation conditioning, which is where a method earns its keep. Data_ops 5: parameter-light (one exponent + intercept), trivially refreshable from price+date, fully scriptable.

scores.name: Store-of-Value / Gold-Parity TAM Substitution
scores.rationale: Theoretically coherent for a no-cashflow asset (money-cointegration VECM + gold-TAM anchor, decomposable and stress-able, decaying-return shape is the correct forward CMA shape), so rigor and data-ops are strong. But signal is weak: the terminal capture share is asserted not derived, the sources are conflicted marketing, and the digital-gold premise is empirically falsified by ~0 BTC-gold correlation and +0.56 rising equity beta — the model values BTC by the very channel its own data contradicts. Robustness is middling: the gold-parity anchor sidesteps halving/S2F cycle breakdown but is itself fragile to the ETF-era risk-asset repricing.

scores.name: Monetary-Substitution / M2 Elasticity & Debasement Hedge
scores.rationale: The headline elasticity (~2.65) and 0.94 levels-correlation are textbook spurious I(1) regression; on contemporaneous changes the relationship nearly vanishes, and the peer-reviewed TVC-VECM literature formally rejects constant coefficients (p=0.0015), so the fixed-elasticity machinery is methodologically weak (rigor 2). Real directional signal exists — BTC tracks global liquidity in ~83% of 12m windows, more than any major asset — so it adds genuine macro conditioning, but the predictive level it yields (10-12%) is roughly the consensus and the decay anchor does the real work (signal 3). It is fragile across regimes: time-varying cointegration, the rising equity correlation to +0.56 in the ETF era, and an unstable error-correction term mean the money-implied fair value drifts structurally (robustness 2). M2/global-liquidity series are free, monthly, FRED/CF-Benchmarks-published and trivial to operationalize in a CMA (data_ops 5).

scores.name: Quantity Theory of Money / Velocity Equation of Exchange (MV=PT)
scores.rationale: The Fisher identity is genuinely sound (rigor 4) — it's an accounting identity immune to spurious cointegration, and Schilling-Uhlig adds a real GE microfoundation. But empirical signal is weak (2): the framing values BTC only as a medium of exchange, blind to the store-of-value/monetary-premium demand that actually drives price, and payment-rail volume has flatlined. Robustness is poor (2): velocity collapses as coins are hodled, which the MoE lens misreads as bullish while regime shifts (ETF-era SoV demand) sit entirely outside the model. Data-ops is weak (2): velocity is the dominant input yet ill-defined and contaminated by exchange/change/mixer flows (Pernice), so the valuation fan spans $19k to $5M — inputs do all the work, giving little usable conditioning for a CMA beyond the decay anchor and a near-zero gold correlation.

scores.name: On-Chain Cost-Basis Valuation (Realized Cap / MVRV / SOPR / Thermocap / HODL Waves)
scores.rationale: Realized Cap is a clean accounting identity but the family is fundamentally an oscillator with no native long-horizon return, so any 10-15yr CMA level is grafted on by judgment (low rigor/signal). Its real value is conditioning: the realized-price floor (-14 to -23% vs spot -75 to -92%) is a genuine, regime-spanning downside/tail anchor, but the floor is reflexive (endogenous to prior prices) and thresholds are data-mined on 2-3 cycles. On-chain data is free and well-supported operationally (high data_ops).

scores.name: Cross-Sectional Factor & Macro-Liquidity Regression
scores.rationale: Methodologically the most disciplined descriptive approach (peer-reviewed asset-pricing machinery, falsifiable), but it produces no native long-run level — the appreciation number launders the analyst's assumed crypto-factor premium estimated on a short ~2014-22 bull sample. The same post-ETF literature it leans on shows betas jumping 0→0.9, making any point-estimate fragile over 10-15yr. Its real value is conditioning the correlation/variance cells, not the return forecast; factor construction adds moderate ops lift.

scores.name: Options-Implied Risk-Neutral Forward & Vol Surface (Deribit DVOL / RND)
scores.rationale: No-arbitrage RND/DVOL is methodologically clean and best-in-class for the vol and tail inputs, but under Q it drifts at the funding rate and is structurally silent on 10-15yr appreciation — the central CMA output must be imported, capping signal. Robustness is moderate: forward-looking and not sample-dependent, but liquid options end at ~6-13mo, so the long-horizon term structure is extrapolated, not observed. Data_ops suffers from no long-dated surface and the need to graft a separate P-measure kernel.

scores.name: Equilibrium / Game-Theoretic Security-Utility Pricing
scores.rationale: Theoretical ceiling of the BTC-valuation families: peer-reviewed (JF 2023), microfounded, fixed-point value from transactional benefit + security budget — hence rigor 5. But it explicitly declines to forecast; multiple-equilibria/sunspot results make it consistent with almost any path, so signal and data_ops are weak (no point return, vol, or correlation output; synthesized 8-10% is admitted judgment). Robustness is its real strength (4): never relied on S2F/halving regularities, so it survives the 2021 break and ETF-era correlation shift, docked only for the unsolved fee-funded-security terminal state.

scores.name: Discounted-Utility / Monetary-Premium DCF (Moneyness Analogue)
scores.rationale: Theoretically honest about the no-cashflow problem by modeling a monetary-premium/utility flow, and the PU-ratio variant grounds a falsifiable rich/cheap signal in on-chain accounting — earns a middling rigor. But empirically the predictive edge is in-sample over a short bull-dominated 2011-2020 history, and the value-driving input is an unfalsifiable terminal TAM/penetration prior, so signal and regime-robustness are weak (it is TAM forecasting in DCF costume, vulnerable to the very S2F/halving/ETF-correlation breaks the context flags). Data is reasonably available (UTXO/on-chain metrics, FRED-style series) but the proxy choices and terminal-share assumptions make it operationally fiddly and judgment-laden in a CMA, hence middling data_ops; level forecast adds little conditioning beyond the decay anchor.

scores.name: Adoption S-Curve / Logistic Demand Growth
scores.rationale: Theoretically honest about valuing a no-cashflow network, but the operative value link (Metcalfe) is peer-review-rejected as spurious and the companion S2F is discredited out-of-sample, so rigor and empirical signal are weak. Its one genuine virtue is a structural appreciation-decay shape that matches the realized 142->65->17% anchor and is somewhat regime-aware (TAM ceiling survives halving/ETF breaks better than pure cycle models), but the level is dominated by unfalsifiable analog and terminal-date choices and it adds little tail/correlation conditioning; data and ops are moderate (adoption series available, but analog selection is judgment-heavy).

scores.name: Portfolio Sizing / Risk-Budget Allocation
scores.rationale: Methodologically the cleanest framing here — it refuses to fabricate a return and sizes on estimable risk inputs, satisfying scripted-analysis discipline (high rigor, easy data ops from a covariance matrix). But as a standalone CMA it produces no return forecast, so its predictive signal for a 10-15yr appreciation figure is weak — the ~8-12% number is admitted judgment, not output. Robustness is mid: vol-decay is an unverifiable assumption and the load-bearing correlation input is non-stationary (0 to ~0.56 post-ETF), which directly erodes the diversification premise the sizing relies on, though risk-budgeting itself degrades gracefully rather than breaking like S2F.

scores.name: Institutional Long-Term Capital Market Assumptions (LTCMA) for Bitcoin
scores.rationale: The headline return is reverse-engineered from an asserted terminal market-cap share (gold/reserve/settlement) with no equilibrium discipline — change 33% to 15% and the CMA halves — and the borrowed S2F/Metcalfe rationales are largely rejected and broke post-2021, so rigor and regime-robustness are weak. Its empirical signal over 10-15yr is thin because the level is judgmental and the decay anchor does the real work. It scores high only on data_ops: it is the sole genre that emits a complete optimizer-ready return/vol/correlation tuple that slots directly into existing CMA machinery using readily available inputs.

scores.name: Market-Implied Futures Forward Curve & Basis
scores.rationale: Methodologically clean and model-light (no Q-to-P transform, reads off regulated screens), and trivially easy operationally, hence high rigor and data_ops. But it is fatal for the headline 10-15yr question: a <=13-month curve plus zero-maturity perps bounds carry, not decade drift, and carry is a risk premium not a spot forecast (Schmeling-Schrimpf-Todorov), so signal for long-horizon appreciation is near nil. Procyclical, sentiment-driven basis that compresses toward the risk-free rate as the market matures makes it regime-contingent and weak on robustness; its real value is conditioning a basis-harvested/futures sleeve, not the CMA level.

scores.name: Reflexive / Log-Periodic Bubble & Crash-Hazard (LPPLS / JLS)
scores.rationale: LPPLS/JLS has a real theoretical pedigree and a measurable network anchor (generalized Metcalfe), but its 7+ nonlinear parameters guarantee high in-sample fit regardless of a true bubble, and t_c is notoriously unstable, so its predictive signal for a 10-15yr level is weak. It is a within-cycle hazard timer, not a regime-survivor: the value it adds is fat-left-tail/crash-hazard conditioning, not the decay-anchored level the CMA already needs. No native CMA number means every horizon figure is analyst reconstruction, and recalibration across windows is operationally heavy.

scores.name: Regime-Switching / Jump-Diffusion & Heavy-Tail Return Process
scores.rationale: Methodologically the most rigorous family here (consensus MS-GARCH/SVCJ/Hawkes/power-law, dominant in VaR and option-pricing backtests), so rigor is a 5. But for a 10-15yr CMA its signal is weak: it explicitly forecasts no drift and the decay anchor dominates a CMA's value, so its predictive content for the level is a 2. Robustness is middling — the risk-shape (fat tails, vol clustering, vol-of-vol) survives regime shifts better than level models, but jump intensities/regime means are estimated off ~4 cycles and are window-dependent. Data_ops is moderate: daily BTC data is abundant but fitting/refitting these conditional models and translating daily fits to a 10-15yr CVaR/ES input is operationally heavy and horizon-mismatched.

scores.name: Survival / Ruin-Probability (Absorbing-Zero Hazard)
scores.rationale: Theoretically clean: it makes BTC's dominant feature — a genuine point-mass at -100% — an explicit, auditable hazard rather than a buried fudge, grounded in real collapse-equilibrium theory (rigor 4). But empirical signal is weak: the hazard is near-unfalsifiable (n=1, still alive), so it's pure prior, and it's only a wrapper that still needs a survival-path return model — it adds tail conditioning but no level forecast (signal 2). Robustness is strong because pricing an absorbing state is regime-agnostic by construction — it doesn't depend on halving cycles, S2F, or correlation regimes (robustness 4). Data_ops is poor: the key parameter has no observable data to fit and the honest output is a distribution, not a CMA-ingestible point estimate, making it operationally awkward (data_ops 2).

scores.name: Fractal Long-Memory & Adaptive-Efficiency (MF-DFA / Hurst / ARFIMA)
scores.rationale: Methodologically grounded scaling analysis with a robust cross-team maturation finding, but the headline long-memory result is estimator-fragile and confoundable with fat tails (rigor 3). It yields no appreciation level — the CMA return number is bolted on by judgment, and the efficiency-to-zero-premium leap is an overreach — so direct predictive signal for a 10-15yr level is weak (signal 2); its real value is corroborating the decay anchor and informing the vol floor. Return-side persistence dies through regimes while vol long-memory persists, giving moderate cross-regime survival (robustness 3). Inputs are just the return series with standard, easily scripted estimators (data_ops 4).

scores.name: Rough Volatility (Fractional-Brownian RFSV) for Bitcoin
scores.rationale: Methodologically sound and falsifiable (H is physically estimated, RFSV beats AR/HAR out-of-sample), but it is a risk-only block: silent on the decay-anchored return level and on the entire correlation row (gold/equity), so its 10-15yr CMA signal is low. Robustness is middling — fast mean-reversion to a high vol floor is genuinely regime-stable, but the measured roughness may be a microstructure/estimation artifact (Cont & Das), undercutting the one cell it informs. Data is cheap (daily RV from price) but operationally it touches only one cell.

scores.name: Agent-Based / Sociophysics Generative Market (Chartist-Fundamentalist, Percolation, Ising/SOC)
scores.rationale: Mechanistically rigorous and peer-validated (Cocco-Marchesi reproduces BTC's return CDF and vol clustering from micro-interaction), and regime-robust because it derives tails/crashes from criticality rather than fitting halving-cycle artifacts. But it is silent on the CMA's central cell — drift — and on all cross-asset correlations, so its predictive signal for a 10-15yr appreciation/correlation matrix is weak. Severe identification problem and bespoke simulation/calibration make it operationally heavy for a CMA process; its real value is conditioning the vol floor and left-tail, not levels.

scores.name: Information-Entropy / Complexity-Plane Efficiency Valuation
scores.rationale: Methodologically clean and replicated: model-free permutation-entropy/complexity sidesteps the spurious-regression trap of S2F/Metcalfe and is stationary by construction, so it survives regime breaks (halving, S2F, ETF) better than trend-fitting methods. But it yields no price level or expected return — every CMA number (appr, vol, correlations) is an external judgment bridge, and efficiency does not bound risk, so its direct predictive signal for a 10-15yr level is weak. Data (price series) is trivially available, but ordinal-pattern tooling is bespoke and the output needs heavy hand-translation into committee-usable assumptions.

scores.name: Generalized-Metcalfe x Logistic-Saturation Fundamental Support (Wheatley-Sornette)
scores.rationale: Methodologically honest (data-chosen 1.69 exponent, rejects n^2, peer-reviewed, real 2018 out-of-sample call) and uniquely supplies the correct CMA shape: finite terminal value plus endogenous appreciation decay. But authors themselves disclaim long-horizon use (~4-order carrying-capacity uncertainty), the regression is likely spurious (non-cointegrated I(1), reverse causality), and the active-user input is structurally breaking in the ETF/custodial/L2 era — so signal and regime-robustness are weak despite high theoretical rigor.

scores.name: Global-Liquidity / Collateral-Multiplier Cycle Barometer (Howell / Alden Directional Liquidity-Beta)
scores.rationale: The collateral-multiplier lens is conceptually richer than M2 models and the 83%/12mo directional hit rate is the most robust replicated BTC-macro signal, surviving regime shifts because it tracks funding direction rather than a fitted level (strong robustness). But it is fundamentally directional, not magnitude-producing: it cannot yield a 10-15yr appreciation number without a bolted-on secular-liquidity assumption and beta, so its predictive level signal for a CMA is weak. The lead-time/lag is itself a fitted, contested parameter (Howell's ~$189T pool, 13-week lead), and the bespoke global-liquidity series is data-heavy and hard to operationalize cleanly in a CMA pipeline, dragging data_ops down.

scores.name: Fiscal-Theory-of-the-Price-Level / Fiscal-Dominance Hard-Asset Bid
scores.rationale: Core FTPL is peer-reviewed and structurally derived rather than fitted, but contested on identification, hence rigor 4 not 5. Predictive signal for a 10-15yr BTC level is weak: it emits no native appreciation number and launders an assumed liquidity beta, so the level forecast is analyst prior, not output. Its real value is conditioning — the non-monotone debasement-vs-issuance framing and sovereign-solvency lens survive halving/S2F/ETF regime breaks well (robustness 4). Operationally it needs fiscal/issuance modeling plus a judgment-set BTC beta, so it is not a clean drop-in CMA pipeline.

scores.name: Triffin / Dedollarization Neutral-Reserve Sovereign Share
scores.rationale: Mechanism is economically real and the reserve-pool TAM is genuinely distinct/bounded, giving high rigor and a self-limiting (non-runaway) contribution. But empirical signal over 10-15yr is weak: reserve-manager surveys show ~0% adoption and BTC fails the official sector's own reserve criteria (vol, liquidity, carry), so the base case is near-zero and adds little to the decay-anchored level. Robustness is moderate (geopolitical driver is regime-orthogonal but adoption could inflect either way); data is available (reserve pool, CB gold flows, surveys) but the key inputs are judgment probabilities, not estimable parameters.

scores.name: Cagan/Jermann Dynamic Money-Demand (Real-Balances, Adoption-Shock Structural)
scores.rationale: Genuinely structural and peer-reviewed: estimates a money-demand semi-elasticity and decomposes variance into named shocks, correctly fingering adoption (an S-curve implying appreciation decay) as the price engine — high rigor. But it is a variance-decomposition, not a return model: no appreciation/vol/correlation outputs, Cagan multiple-equilibria indeterminacy leaves expected return unpinned, and it supplies zero gold mechanism — so direct CMA signal is weak. Robustness is moderate: the adoption-S-curve logic survives regime shifts conceptually but the explosive-equilibria fragility and lack of correlation modeling hurt. Data-ops is poor: requires re-estimating a structural model on prices/volumes/money-supply plus bolting on an exogenous adoption path and an ad hoc equilibrium selection — heavy and not turnkey.

scores.name: Eurodollar / Shadow-Money BTC-as-Collateral (Snider)
scores.rationale: Mechanistically grounded in observable plumbing (repo/collateral/haircuts) rather than price numerology, so rigor is high and it is the set's only genuine bear/skeptic anchor denying the debasement premise. But its load-bearing macro call was decisively wrong in 2021-22 (deflation/dollar-shortage as CPI hit ~9%), gutting empirical signal, and it supplies a sign and a story but no return/vol/corr numbers, making it weak to operationalize in a CMA grid. Robustness is middling: the liquidity-crunch sell-off regularity (Mar-2020, 2022) survives regime change as a tail/conditioning input even though the directional level call does not.

scores.name: Hyperbitcoinization Terminal Monetary-Base Share (Probability-Weighted Barbell)
scores.rationale: The barbell framing is conceptually the most honest representation of BTC's bimodal payoff and is the rare method that survives regime change — it never depended on halving cycles, S2F, or correlation stability, so the 2021 break and ETF-era shift leave it untouched (robustness 4). But its two load-bearing inputs (terminal monetary-share and adoption probability) are unfalsifiable priors with n=1 surviving history; EV swings orders of magnitude across reasonable values, so rigor is presentational not empirical and predictive signal over 10-15yr is weak. Sell-side provenance (VanEck/Swan) skews it bullish and the explicit probability weights are rarely published, making the EV non-reproducible in a CMA — hence low data_ops.

scores.name: Debasement-CAGR / Fiat-Half-Life Return Floor
scores.rationale: Identity logic and the broad-money-over-CPI choice are genuinely sound and yield the right decaying shape, lifting rigor above average. But the "floor" is empirically falsified (BTC fell 16-32% while money grew, equity corr rose to +0.56), so signal and regime-robustness are weak; it adds no tail/correlation conditioning beyond a level anchor. Broad-money inputs are trivially available and stable, making data_ops excellent.

scores.name: Behavioral Attention & Text-Sentiment (Search/Wiki/Social NLP, Fear-Greed)
scores.rationale: Replicated co-movement and honest self-limiting horizon give it moderate rigor, but reflexive circularity and zero native long-run drift make its 10-15yr signal weak — it must import a level from elsewhere. It scores well on robustness because attention-feedback is regime-invariant (survives halving breaks and the ETF shift) where S2F/Metcalfe do not, and its legitimate value is the vol and tail/timing conditioning cells, not the drift. Data-ops is middling: sentiment/Fear-Greed series exist but are noisy, vendor-dependent, and need NLP plumbing for a slow CMA.

scores.name: Narrative-Economics / Reflexivity Feedback-Loop (SIR Contagion + Garcia VAR)
scores.rationale: Methodologically credible for SHAPE — the SIR/relapsing-wave structure is the cleanest mechanistic explanation for the appreciation decay (smaller susceptible pool each wave) and the persistent boom-bust vol the realized data shows, which is its strongest conditioning contribution. But it produces no native return level (all CMA numbers are bolted-on judgment), and its core inputs (social trace, word-of-mouth VAR calibrated on 2011-2013 data) are precisely what the ETF-era allocator buyer breaks, so it fails the regime-change and data-ops tests hardest. Signal is high on tails/cadence, low on level.

scores.name: Behavioral-Preference / Disagreement Overvaluation (Lottery-MAX, Miller, Scheinkman-Xiong)
scores.rationale: Peer-reviewed, mechanism-based, falsifiable theory (rigor 4), but it is a weekly cross-sectional anomaly that produces no BTC level and concentrates in small illiquid coins — Bitcoin is exactly where the effect is weakest, so direct 10-15yr predictive signal is poor (signal 2). It does carry one genuinely valuable, regime-aware contribution: an infrastructure-conditional DECAY mechanism explaining why BTC appreciation eroded as shorting/options/holder-base institutionalized, which survives and even anticipates regime change (robustness 3). Data ops are awkward: requires high-frequency cross-coin MAX/PT/disagreement/short-constraint inputs and bespoke judgment to graft onto a CMA, with no off-the-shelf level output (data_ops 2).

scores.name: Energy-Value / Thermoeconomic Fair-Value (Joule Equivalence + Landauer Temperature)
scores.rationale: The Landauer econophysics layer (state variables, Carnot bounds, stationarity tests) adds real methodological discipline over narrative crypto valuation and uses one fixed parameter, lifting rigor to 3 — but the fatal circularity (price drives hashrate, so energy follows price down, not vice versa) guts the causal/intrinsic claim and caps signal at 2. It is a short-horizon (21-day half-life) mean-reverting LEVEL model, silent on decade appreciation, vol, and correlation — exactly the CMA cells that matter — and its halving/Merge structural breaks confirm it does not survive regime change (robustness 2). Hashrate/efficiency/energy data are public and refreshable, but the Fiat Factor calibration and lack of native return/vol/corr outputs make CMA integration only moderate (data_ops 3).

scores.name: Mining-Economics Dynamics & Security-Budget Sustainability (Hashprice, Hash/Difficulty Ribbons, Puell, Cost-Curve, Supply-Elasticity)
scores.rationale: High rigor: grounded in observable industrial data and unusually honest via the Song-Aste cost-endogeneity critique (cost follows price, so no exogenous cost-floor). But that same insight kills its level signal — none of the instruments is a return forecaster, so a 10-15yr appreciation requires bolting on exogenous price/fee assumptions; signal is weak. Robust because cost-endogeneity (~constant ~1% security spend) is regime-invariant through halvings, the S2F break, and ETF era, and capitulation signals add genuine tail/regime conditioning. Data-ops strong: hashprice, difficulty, J/TH, $/kWh are refreshable and pipeline-friendly.

scores.name: Variance/Jump Risk-Premium & SDF-Implied Physical Return (P-vs-Q, VRP, SVCJ)
scores.rationale: Theoretically strong (model-free SDF bounds, clean VRP/jump decomposition) so rigor is high, but the 27-day horizon is fatally mismatched to a 10-15yr CMA — the level is pure judgment, not method output, gutting signal. NCC validity for a single speculative asset is doubtful and the bound is regime-fragile, so robustness is low. Deribit-only, young, fragmented option data makes it operationally heavy. Its genuine contribution is second-moment (vol/tail) conditioning, not the return level.

scores.name: Options-Skew / Convexity Risk-Reversal Signal
scores.rationale: Methodologically strong and honest: forward-looking market-priced data, peer-reviewed evidence that skew forecasts realized vol but NOT returns — a rare falsifiable negative result that guards against directional over-extrapolation. But signal for a 10-15yr CMA is weak: it produces no appreciation forecast by construction and the entire surface lives at days-to-3-month tenors, so any decade view is fully imported. Robustness is poor — the harvestable short-RR premium is explicitly regime-dependent and decaying as institutions mature the market. Data_ops is constrained: Deribit options data is short-maturity, requires surface modeling, and offers no long-horizon read for a standard CMA process. Its genuine value is conditioning the vol/tail cell, not the level.

scores.name: Derivatives-Microstructure: Perp Funding, Cross-Rail Basis Segmentation & Price Discovery (Crypto Carry)
scores.rationale: Top-tier peer-reviewed microstructure foundation (BIS/Mgmt Science, Hasbrouck JF 1995) earns a 5 on rigor, and its rigorous negative result usefully disciplines carry-as-drift errors. But signal for a 10-15yr spot return is weak (2): it generates NO native appreciation forecast and explicitly shows carry does not predict positive returns. Robustness is mid (3) given short, regime-unstable samples (perps 2016+, ETF 2024+, 386-obs wedge) that may compress, though the vol/tail conditioning is durable. Data_ops mid (3): funding/basis data exist but Hasbrouck shares and cross-rail wedge require nontrivial assembly. Value is conditioning the vol/tail cells, not anchoring the level.

scores.name: Convenience-Yield / Theory-of-Storage Commodity Valuation
scores.rationale: Theoretically strong (Gibson-Schwartz, Hilliard-Ngo out-of-sample option support) so rigor is high, but it is a relative-pricing/forward-curve tool that treats spot drift as exogenous — it cannot produce a 10-15yr appreciation number, so empirical signal for the level CMA needs is weak. The backed-out convenience yield is small, frequently negative (-1.4% full sample, -9.5% COVID, range -165% to +90%) and basis-dependent, so it breaks down across regimes (low robustness). Data is live futures/options (available) but option-implied estimation is operationally heavier than a simple proxy. Its genuine contribution is conditioning — a defensible high-jump-vol case and the strongest evidence-based argument for low gold correlation — not the appreciation level.

scores.name: Machine-Learning Forecasting & Empirical Asset Pricing (DL/Trees/On-Chain ML/Gu-Kelly-Xiu/HMM)
scores.rationale: Methodologically the most disciplined family here — strict OOS splits, SPA/MCS/Diebold-Mariano tests, economic-significance metrics — so rigor is high. But for a 10-15yr CMA level its predictive signal is near-zero: the documented edge is intraday-to-monthly (~56% directional, ~0.4% monthly OOS R2) and collapses to random-walk-with-drift at decade horizon, supplying no independent appreciation level. Robustness is weak because the noise-dominated, regime-shifting crypto data is exactly where these models overfit and degrade out-of-sample. Data is available but on-chain/feature pipelines and retraining add operational friction, and the framework's only durable CMA contribution is regime/tail conditioning (HMM), not the level.

scores.name: ML Realized-Volatility & Vol-Term-Structure Forecasting (HAR-RV / GARCH / Hybrid)
scores.rationale: Methodologically sound for second moments (HAR-RV/GARCH are well-validated, parsimonious, with continuous/jump decomposition), earning high rigor. But signal for a 10-15yr CMA is weak: it is silent on appreciation and correlation by construction, and the 1-day-to-2-month validation horizon makes long-run sigma an out-of-model assertion, not a forecast — the decay anchor and correlation cells must be imported. Mean-reversion gives moderate regime robustness but it never saw a multi-cycle BTC equilibrium. Data (high-frequency RV) is abundant and the OLS/GARCH fit is operationally trivial, so data_ops is strong; net value to the CMA is narrow (the vol cell only).

scores.name: Bayesian Model-Averaging / Dynamic Model Averaging under Model & Parameter Instability
scores.rationale: Epistemically the most correct framing in the literature (peer-reviewed, explicitly models model+parameter instability and produces honest fat-tailed densities), so rigor and regime-robustness are high. But it yields NO native 10-15yr expected return — every crypto DMA/BMA application is sub-180-day and decays to near-zero, so its standalone signal for a decade-ahead level is weak. Operationally it is a heavy recursive ensemble requiring a maintained candidate set and refitting, not a drop-in CMA input, so data_ops is low. Its real value is conditioning/tails on top of the other lenses, not the level forecast the CMA needs.

scores.name: Dynamic-Factor / Mixed-Frequency Macro Nowcasting (DFM + MIDAS, ML-augmented)
scores.rationale: Methodologically sound state-space machinery (Kalman/ragged-edge, endogenous mean-reversion gives the right decay shape) earns high rigor, but it is a nowcasting tool with a fatal horizon mismatch: beyond ~4-8 quarters it collapses to trend-liquidity-times-an-assumed-beta, adding little over a naive debasement assumption at 10-15yr. Signal/robustness are low because the liquidity beta is unstable and regime-dependent (post-2020 spike, ETF-era correlation shift) and the headline correlation is partly spurious trend. Data-ops is heavy: assembling and maintaining a large mixed-frequency panel plus DFM estimation is operationally burdensome for a CMA process.

scores.name: Implied-Equilibrium-Return Inversion (Black-Litterman / Risk-Parity / Kelly Back-Out)
scores.rationale: Theoretically clean identity (Pi=lambda*Sigma*w, Kelly f*=(mu-r)/sigma^2) so rigor is high, but predictive signal is weak/circular: it assumes CAPM equilibrium and rational current weights, then "discovers" the return that rationalizes them, and the pure own-variance back-out yields an economically absurd <1% excess that must be overridden by judgment to reach the 8-12% anchor. Robustness is middling — it adapts mechanically to vol/weight inputs (so it survives regime shifts in form) but is pathologically sensitive to those inputs and to ETF-era correlation, swinging from <1% to 6-8%. Data-ops is easy (market-cap share, vol, correlation are all readily available), but the method's real CMA value is as a sanity floor/upper-bound on plausible holdings, not a level forecast.

scores.name: Tail-Risk Implied Required Return (CVaR / Expected-Shortfall Pricing)
scores.rationale: Methodologically strong: ES is a coherent, convex, LP-optimizable measure that correctly charges BTC for its documented heavy left tail (Rockafellar-Uryasev, EVT/GPD), fixing variance's symmetry — hence high rigor. But it is a normative hurdle engine, not a forecast: it tells you what BTC must return, not what it will, so its direct CMA-level signal over 10-15yr is weak and still requires an imported drift. The price-of-tail-risk is a free, unanchored parameter and ES estimation is fragile on BTC's short, bull-dominated history, hurting data_ops; robustness is middling since the tail/skew framing survives regime shifts better than cycle-timing methods but the multiplier and tail fit are unstable. Best used as a conservative skeptic's counter that conditions the downside, not as a standalone level.

scores.name: Extreme-Value-Theory Tail-Distribution (GPD / Peaks-Over-Threshold / Block-Maxima)
scores.rationale: EVT/GARCH-EVT is the actuarial/Basel gold standard for fat tails and asymptotically asset-agnostic, so rigor is top-tier and it produces exactly the VaR/ES/tail cells other families punt on. But for a 10-15yr CMA its signal is weak: it forecasts nothing about the central return level (the decay anchor that dominates) and is univariate, silent on the correlation conditioning the context says matters most. Robustness is moderate — GARCH-filtering handles vol clustering but xi CIs are wide on a ~15yr daily sample and the body/regime shifts (ETF-era corr) sit outside its scope; data_ops is workable (daily prices only) but threshold choice is subjective and operationally fiddly to standardize.

scores.name: Cross-Asset Dependence-Structure Engine (DCC-GARCH + Copula tail-dependence)
scores.rationale: Methodologically the most rigorous family for the dependence/co-tail cells — GARCH->DCC->EVT->copula is the right machinery for asymmetric, time-varying tail dependence, and it falsifiably tests the digital-gold claim. But it produces no return level (signal for the dominant appreciation cell is near-zero by construction), and its own measured non-stationarity (regime-flipping DCC/copula across pre-2020/COVID/ETF eras) plus heavy specification and short-sample imprecision undercut 10-15yr extrapolation. Data is available but the multi-stage pipeline is operationally heavy for a CMA process.

scores.name: Consumption-CAPM / Rare-Disaster / ICAPM Hedging-Demand Equilibrium Premium
scores.rationale: Theoretically the most rigorous family in the set — it derives the premium from a structural SDF (risk-aversion x consumption-covariance + disaster compensation) and asks why a premium should exist. But it fails on its own terms for BTC (rejected at RRA>10, the 'premium puzzle'), so its predictive power for a 10-15yr level is weak — wide CIs, low-power Euler tests, no usable point forecast. Its real value is conditioning: it survives regime change well because the ~zero consumption/macro covariance is a structural fact independent of halving cycles or the ETF correlation shift, and rare-disaster decay matches the observed appreciation decay. Operationally awkward: disaster calibration is unidentifiable (no realized BTC consumption disasters) and the synthesized levels are judgment, not model output.

scores.name: Liability-Driven / Surplus-Optimization Implied BTC Hurdle (Endowment/LDI)
scores.rationale: Sharpe-Tint surplus optimization is theoretically sound and asks the institutionally correct question, structurally penalizing BTC's 55-100% vol and near-zero liability hedge to cap the sleeve — high rigor. But it is explicitly not a return forecaster: it consumes an exogenous BTC appreciation assumption and cannot populate a CMA's level cell, so its standalone predictive signal for BTC over 10-15yr is weak. Robustness is middling because the hurdle hinges on a non-stationary BTC-liability covariance that can spike precisely in stressed-funded-status regimes; data_ops is poor since it requires a separate return model plus liability-driver covariances few CMA processes maintain.

scores.name: Rational-Bubble / OLG No-Arbitrage Equilibrium (Tirole/Blanchard-Watson; van Oordt; Biais; Schilling-Uhlig Martingale)
scores.rationale: Most theoretically rigorous family: it derives an explicit equilibrium return identity (E[r]=required return=discount rate+crash-hazard premium) from first-principles no-arbitrage, which robustly survives regime change because it never relied on halving cycles or S2F. But it is a positive price-formation theory, not a forecaster — it yields no unique appreciation level (rho and h(t) bolted on by judgment), so empirical signal is weak, and calibrating crash hazard plus the survivor-bias stance makes it operationally hard in a CMA.

scores.name: Equation-of-Exchange Velocity Network-Utility Valuation (Burniske MV=PQ)
scores.rationale: Theoretically the most "absolute"/bottom-up of the crypto models — it solves for a fair monetary base from modeled throughput and forces an explicit, one-lever-at-a-time adoption story, and uniquely makes falling velocity a first-class price mechanism (rigor=3). But its load-bearing inputs (V and the 30-50% discount rate) are empirically unforecastable: the arXiv test shows velocity fluctuates wildly with poor out-of-sample fit, and the answer is dominated by analyst discount-rate choice plus an unresolved infinite-recursion-of-expectations problem, gutting predictive power (signal=2). It offers no regime-change conditioning (silent on correlations, equity-corr rise, ETF-era shifts) and pivots on a parameter that breaks across regimes (robustness=2). Operationally it demands on-chain PQ scrubbing, velocity estimation, hodl-adjusted float, and subjective discount/scenario calibration — heavy and judgment-laden for a CMA process (data_ops=2).

scores.name: Official-Sector Policy-Endogenous Return Caps (Repression Tax/Ban, Regulatory Capital, ECB Zero-Value)
scores.rationale: Mixed rigor: the Amol-Luttmer repression-tax result is a genuine GE proof but only a conditional possibility, and the ECB zero-value leg is an assertion repeatedly falsified ex post, so I dock it to 3. Empirical signal is weak (2): Basel 1250%/EIOPA charges are real but only suppress regulated-balance-sheet demand at the margin while spot doubled through every zero call, so it has poor predictive track record on level. Robustness is its strength (4): a policy-reaction-function ceiling is exactly the conditioning that survives halving/S2F/ETF regime breaks and supplies the missing left tail the optimistic theses lack. Data_ops is poor (2): inputs are a judgmental policymaker probability/severity function, not an observable refreshable series, so it bolts on as a scenario bracket rather than a computed input.

scores.name: Capital-Flight / Sanctions-Evasion / Remittance Transactional-Demand Floor
scores.rationale: Mechanistically the most honest lens here: it rests on observable revealed-preference data (crypto FX shadow premium, gravity-estimated bilateral flows à la Auer) rather than S2F/Metcalfe numerology, and its demand is structurally regime-robust because flight/sanctions premia spike counter-cyclically to local-currency stress — that's the rare BTC mechanism that survives halving/ETF breaks and plausibly explains the non-zero gold correlation. But its predictive signal for a 10-15yr return level is weak: the IMF result that crypto reroutes rather than creates flight demand, plus stablecoins eating the remittance/transactional share, caps the floor's forward contribution; it yields no native appreciation/vol cell, so any CMA level is a bolted-on judgment. Data is reachable (on-chain flows, corridor FX premia) but assembling clean shadow-rate and gravity panels is operationally non-trivial for a recurring CMA process.

scores.name: Geopolitical-Risk-Index Conditional Safe-Haven Factor (GPR/EPU)
scores.rationale: Methodologically strong and honest: exogenous text-based regressor avoids the price-on-price circularity of S2F/NVT and puts the safe-haven claim to a falsifiable, regime-conditional test (high rigor). But it yields no appreciation estimate and the tail coefficients flip sign across estimator/window/crisis on a short ~2-3 regime sample, so its predictive signal over 10-15yr is weak (low signal). It earns moderate robustness only because its central finding — rejecting digital-gold, conditional vol effects — is replicated and speaks directly to the regime/correlation cells the decay anchor leaves open. Data (GPR/EPU + BTC market data) is public and easy, but GARCH-MIDAS/DCC/quantile machinery adds operational lift in a CMA pipeline.

scores.name: Demographic & Wealth-Transfer Flow-of-Funds Demand (Great Wealth Transfer, Life-Cycle Cohort, Savings-Rate)
scores.rationale: The exogenous demographic clock is a genuine non-reflexive conditioning input, but the flow-to-market-cap multiplier has no stable theoretical basis (118x/106x are regime-dependent and computed off a fraction of the market), and documented ETP evidence shows price drives flows, not vice versa — inverting the core causal claim. As a level forecast it's a ~9-13% judgment overlay with weak survival through halving/ETF-era regime shifts; its value is the slow-moving cohort-allocation-gap framing, not predictive power. Data (wealth-transfer, cohort ownership, savings) is reasonably available and the schedule is operationally tractable, which lifts only data_ops.

scores.name: Lindy / Age-Conditioned Survival Adoption Premium
scores.rationale: The Ord (2023) Bayesian-hazard machinery is genuinely rigorous and correctly yields a declining observed hazard plus a Gott base rate, so rigor earns a 3 — but it is fatally compromised by survivorship bias (Bitcoin is one survivor from a population >53% dead) and by illegitimately upgrading an evidential observer-side update into a causal physical-safety improvement that it then prices. Signal and robustness are weak: the honest math is bimodal and pessimistic (Gott ~42% ruin), it adds little conditioning beyond a static absorbing-zero point-mass that the fixed-haircut ruin row already captures, and it says nothing about the empirically load-bearing regime shifts (S2F break, rising +0.56 equity correlation, ETF-era flows). Data_ops is low because the payoff is judgment-driven demand-feedback with no clean operational input to a CMA pipeline.

scores.name: Cross-Asset Relative-Value Ratio (BTC/Gold, Market-Portfolio Share, Hard-Money Basket, Multi-Pool Monetary TAM)
scores.rationale: Decomposing E[BTC] into a numeraire's own return plus ratio-reversion is the one disciplined advance here — it forces gold's expected return to be an explicit building block and adds a falsifiable Z-score anchor, which lifts rigor above naive scarcity/TAM methods. But the framework's central contradiction is fatal to signal and robustness: BTC-gold correlation is ~0 (BTC trades as high-beta equity, corr to equities +0.56), so dividing two weakly-related assets manufactures a "reversion" that is mostly BTC's own equity-beta noise; the "fair" ratio of ~21 is curve-fit on 3-4 cycles and the ratio halved in 2025 with no mechanical pull-back, so it survives regime change poorly. Data_ops is strong — BTC/XAU ratios, M2, and gold are all cheap, public, daily series trivially slotted into a CMA. Net: useful as a cross-check/conditioning overlay, weak as a standalone level forecast.

scores.name: Equity-Beta-Implied / Public-Proxy-Implied Expected Return (Levered Nasdaq, MSTR mNAV, Miner NAV)
scores.rationale: Rigor is high for a no-cashflow asset: it imports a defensible Rf+ERP building block via CAPM rather than scarcity numerology, and a decaying-beta path mechanically reproduces the correct appreciation-decay shape while jointly constraining vol and equity-correlation cells. But CAPM is the wrong null for a fat-tailed, non-normal, reflexive asset, and the entire forward hinges on an unfalsifiable beta-decay path off a beta that flipped sign within 2025 — so robustness across the ETF-era correlation shift is weak and explanatory power is moderate. Data-ops is strong: NDX beta, MSTR mNAV, and miner NAV are all liquid market-quoted series, easy to refresh in a CMA process.

scores.name: Intra-Crypto Relative-Value (BTC Dominance / ETH-BTC Rotation Overlay)
scores.rationale: Theoretically thin as a return model: dominance is an accounting identity and the zero-sum rotation premise breaks when the whole complex inflates/deflates, so rigor and 10-15yr predictive signal are both low — it yields no native appreciation number. It scores better on robustness because share-of-complex flight-to-quality is a real microstructure that persists across halving/S2F/ETF regime breaks, and high on data_ops since dominance and ETH/BTC are trivially available daily. Net value is as a vol/correlation regime overlay, not a level forecaster.

scores.name: Treasury-Company Reflexive Demand Channel (mNAV Flywheel + Convertible Vol-Arb Loop)
scores.rationale: Reflexive-by-construction with no fundamental/equilibrium anchor, so it cannot derive a 10-15yr level — it's a decaying flow impulse masquerading as a valuation channel (rigor/signal low). Robustness is weak: ~76% single-entity concentration with a 2029-30 convert/preferred wall means the "channel" is really a bet on one balance sheet surviving a regime flip, and the mechanism itself is brand-new with no cross-cycle history. Data is observable in real time (mNAV, BTC/share, implied vol, issuance), giving decent data_ops, and its one genuine contribution is honestly shaping the LEFT tail and endogenous vol clustering — but as a CMA level method it is poor.

scores.name: Stablecoin-Float Liquidity-Onramp Demand Sink
scores.rationale: Genuine official-sector rigor (BIS WP 1270 IV-identified, Richmond Fed GE) but it lands on T-bill yields/r-star, not BTC price — the BTC-return leap is unsupported, and NY Fed shows the float LAGS BTC moves, making forward forecasting circular. No native return/vol/correlation; any CMA level is bolted-on judgment, adding little over the decay anchor. Robustness is weak as an exogenous driver but the SSR float is highly auditable, high-frequency, and trivial to operationalize, earning strong data_ops.

scores.name: Structural Stock-Flow Demand-Clearing Engine (Inelastic-Supply Price-Multiplier)
scores.rationale: Theoretically the most honest family here — it actually solves for a clearing price from inelastic supply x flow rather than extrapolating price history, which is structurally correct and earns it a real edge on regime robustness (no halving/S2F-trend dependence). But signal is weak: the headline output hinges on an ad-hoc, unestimated demand-shift multiplier (10-40X) the authors themselves warn against overinterpreting, plus a severe advocacy conflict of interest that engineers the bullish sovereign-withdrawal input — so its level forecast adds little over the decay anchor and its main contribution is the inelastic-float regime/tail conditioning. Data_ops is poor: liquid-float, lost-coin, and withdrawal-flow estimates are noisy, contested, and not cleanly maintainable in a recurring CMA process.

scores.name: Square-Root Market-Impact Law (Metaorder Demand-to-Price Mechanism)
scores.rationale: Best-pedigreed micro-law in the BTC space (delta~1/2 confirmed on >1M metaorders, real latent-liquidity micro-foundation), and its concave sqrt(Q) shape is the structurally correct way to encode appreciation decay — hence high rigor. But it is not a self-contained CMA: it converts demand Q to price yet cannot forecast Q, so all 10-15yr return uncertainty is exiled into an unmodeled cumulative-inflow guess, and it supplies no level, no gold linkage, and an asset-agnostic tails/correlation story — so empirical signal for a decade horizon is weak. Robustness is low: calibrated at intraday-daily horizons with largely transient/uninformed impact, extrapolating a single-metaorder law to a decade super-metaorder ignores replenishment and regime change. Data_ops is poor in practice because the binding input (projected net institutional inflow path) is the hardest unobservable in the process.

scores.name: On-Chain Supply-Distribution & Flow Microstructure (URPD, Liveliness/Dormancy, Reserve Risk, Illiquid/Exchange-Flow, Entity-Cohort, LTH/STH)
scores.rationale: Metrics are clean accounting transforms of the UTXO ledger (rigor not zero), but they are short-horizon positioning oscillators with no native long-horizon return output — the 9-13% level is grafted on by judgment, exactly the supply-squeeze over-extrapolation the literature warns against. Signal/robustness are weak for a 10-15yr CMA: cost-basis metrics are reflexive transforms of past price, Reserve Risk's HODL-bank denominator is endogenous to bull markets, and ETF-era off-chain custody (~7% of supply) degrades the on-chain flow read precisely as the method matures. Data is freely derivable from the chain but entity-clustering vendor dependence and the off-chain blind spot keep data_ops middling. Its real value is conditioning (URPD walls, float/illiquid tilt for tails/path), not the level.

scores.name: Discrete-Access Step-Function Demand (ETF -> Wirehouse Models -> 401k/ERISA -> RIA TAMP)
scores.rationale: Mechanism-grounded and decomposable (pool x weight x take-up x dated unlock), which is more falsifiable than diffusion-analog methods and correctly produces a front-loaded, decaying appreciation path matching the realized 142->65->17% decay anchor. But the load-bearing take-up parameter is poorly estimated (eligibility != flow; 401k crypto use stays near-zero where permitted), proponents have severe issuer conflicts, and double-counting risk is structural — so signal/data_ops are weak. It is purely a demand-plumbing story with no gold, vol, or correlation mechanism, adding little of the tail/regime/correlation conditioning the context says is where a method's real value lies.

scores.name: ETF-AUM Cointegration Elasticity & Inelastic-Markets Flow Multiplier
scores.rationale: Strong top-journal anchor (Gabaix-Koijen inelastic markets, ~5x) and correct I(1) estimators, but the operative 1.32 elasticity is fit on a 16-month single-regime bull, rejects no-cointegration only at 10%, and is contaminated by mechanical price->dollar-AUM reflexivity — so out-of-sample signal and regime robustness are low. ETF AUM is observable and refreshable (good data_ops), yet the level forecast is admitted judgment and the framework is silent on vol/tails/gold, adding little of the conditioning that gives a method its real CMA value beyond the shared decay anchor.

scores.name: Discrete Cycle-Amplitude Decay Extrapolation (4-Year Halving Peak-Multiple Compression)
scores.rationale: Encodes the correct qualitative shape (appreciation decay) and lands near the honest central band, but it is a geometric curve-fit on only 3-4 cycle tops with zero out-of-sample validation, mechanically tying the forecast to a 4-year halving regime that ETF/treasury demand may already be dissolving. Convergent multi-metric decay evidence lifts signal, yet rigor and regime-survival are weak (same small-n failure mode that broke S2F/Pi-Cycle). Inputs are public and cycle-indexed, so it is trivially easy to maintain in a CMA, but it adds no tail/correlation conditioning beyond a level that the decay anchor already supplies.

scores.name: Logarithmic-Regression "Rainbow" Fair-Value Corridor
scores.rationale: Zero economic anchor — fits log-price to ln(calendar time), a spurious co-trend with no value driver, and is silently re-parameterized whenever price escapes the band (V2/V3), making it descriptive and unfalsifiable rather than predictive (rigor 1, robustness 1). Its one virtue is the qualitatively-correct decay shape (ln(time) flattens trend even on log scale), which weakly echoes the realized 142->65->17%/yr decay anchor, but it adds no tail/regime/correlation conditioning and is silent on vol and gold-corr (signal 2). Trivial to run: two OLS coefficients on free public price data (data_ops 5).

scores.name: Liquidity-Risk & Higher-Moment Priced Factors (Amihud Illiquidity, Co-Skewness / Downside-Tail Beta)
scores.rationale: Strong 25-yr equity pedigree (Amihud, Harvey-Siddique, Ang-Chen-Xing) gives high theoretical rigor, but the priced premia concentrate in tiny illiquid coins and vanish value-weighted, so BTC — the largest, most liquid coin — earns almost no excess return, gutting signal. Robustness is weak: the illiquidity premium is self-defeating as BTC's Amihud collapses with ETFs/custody, and the framework is silent on regime/halving/correlation shifts. It yields no native CMA level, requires per-coin microstructure/return panels, and any 10-15yr number is analyst-imposed, hurting data_ops.

scores.name: Entropy-Pooling / Fully-Flexible-Probabilities Stress-View CMA Construction (Meucci)
scores.rationale: Theoretically the strongest reconciliation engine available (rigor 5): minimum-KL measure change on an arbitrary non-normal prior, accepting coherent views on vol, the full correlation matrix, skew, kurtosis, quantiles and tail co-dependence — exactly BTC's relevant moments. But it forecasts nothing (signal 1): the appreciation/vol/correlation numbers are entirely imposed views, so it cannot adjudicate BTC's central 10-15yr return question and inherits any prior's survivorship optimism. Robustness is middling (3): it can encode regime/tail views but cannot create crash mass the bootstrap prior lacks. Data_ops 2: requires building a large joint scenario panel plus a constrained KL optimizer and careful view-partition management — heavy machinery for a CMA cell.
